items.name: KaVontae Turpin
items.headline: Cowboys ruled out KaVontae Turpin (ribs) for Week 7 against the Eagles.
items.analysis: Turpin’s absence will be felt most on special teams, with the team now forced to find a replacement on punt and kick returns. Otherwise, there is almost zero fantasy impact as the team’s WR4.

items.name: A.J. Terrell
items.headline: Falcons activated A.J. Terrell (groin) from injured reserve.
items.analysis: The Falcons have been attackable on the perimeter while playing most of the season without Terrell. Fellow cornerback C.J. Henderson is listed questionable for Week 7, but the reintegration of Terrell provides a much more difficult matchup for the injury-riddled 49ers.

items.name: Jonah Coleman
items.headline: Broncos activated Jonah Coleman (ankle) from injured reserve.
items.analysis: Coleman missed the minimum four games as he tended to an ankle injury suffered in Week 2. He led the team in snaps in that contest and could return to the primary rushing role considering the inefficient play of J.K. Dobbins in his absence, making him worthy of a start in fantasy circles in a plus matchup against the Cardinals in his first game back.

items.name: Lamar Jackson
items.headline: Ravens ruled out Lamar Jackson (ankle) for Week 7 against the Bengals.
items.analysis: Tyler Huntley will draw the start under center for the third straight game as Jackson continues to rehab a high-ankle sprain. Jackson reportedly took most of the first-team reps at practice Friday and was close to being able to play in Week 7, with the team ultimately siding with caution for their franchise quarterback. The Ravens enter a 15-game stretch in which they play three games starting in Week 8, which could have influenced their decision to hold Jackson out one more game. Expect him back for Week 8 against the Bills. His absence greatly influences the upside of the remaining skill position players considering Declan Doyle has halved his usage of play action and completely eliminated RPO with Huntley under center.

items.name: Dallas Goedert
items.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) was removed from the injury report Saturday and will play against the Cowboys in Week 7.
items.analysis: Goedert reportedly aggravated his previous knee injury but got back on the practice field for a full session Saturday before being removed from the injury report. He could be stepping into a massive target share with both DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks ruled out. Fantasy managers can start him as an upside TE1 in a great matchup against the Cowboys in Week 7.

items.name: Saquon Barkley
items.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is questionable for Week 7 against the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Although getting in a full practice Saturday, the Eagles head into Monday’s game against the Cowboys with Barkley listed as questionable following a two-game absence. Fantasy managers have a decision considering the Eagles play in Week 7’s final game on Monday Night Football, with no clear fall back options should he be unable to play. It would seem prudent to make alternate plans at the position.

items.name: DeVonta Smith
items.headline: Eagles ruled out DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) for Week 7 against the Cowboys.
items.analysis: The Eagles will be without their top two receivers but got good news Saturday with the removal of Dallas Goedert from the injury report. Saquon Barkley is listed as questionable and appears to be a true game-time decision. Considering the low involvement of the backfield in the pass game this season, Goedert stands to benefit the most from the absences at wide receiver. He can be started as an upside TE1 in a solid on-paper matchup against the Cowboys.

items.name: Jordan Mason
items.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Vikings plan to activate Jordan Mason (thumb) from injured reserve.
items.analysis: Mason came into the season as the presumed lead back in a timeshare with Aaron Jones, the latter of whom has performed as a true workhorse in Mason’s absence. Although it could take a week or two for Mason to fully regain the lead back role, his presence significantly mutes the potential of Jones. Expect a near-even split when the Vikings take on the Colts in Week 7.

items.name: Dylan Sampson
items.headline: Browns activated RB Dylan Sampson (knee) from injured reserve.
items.analysis: Sampson was limited in practice throughout the week and listed as questionable for Week 7 against the Titans. Now that he’s officially been activated from injured reserve, he’s likely to be Cleveland’s change-of-pace back behind Quinshon Judkins this week. Sampson is worth stashing on fantasy benches, but is truly just a desperation FLEX play coming off a knee injury that’s sidelined him since Week 1.

items.name: Brian Thomas
items.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that several teams believe the Jaguars could trade WR Brian Thomas Jr.
items.analysis: Appearing on ESPN Saturday morning, Fowler, citing Thomas’ zero catches over the last two weeks, said something has to give in this situation. According to several teams the NFL Insider talked to, Thomas could be traded over the next few weeks. Fowler listed the Chiefs and Steelers as potentially interested teams and was emphatic that there will be suitors for Thomas. If you have Thomas in fantasy, it’s hard to imagine his value getting worse with a change of scenery. The Jaguars would appear content to roll with Parker Washington, Jakobi Meyers and Travis Hunter as their top receivers in the event of a Thomas trade.

items.name: Sam LaPorta
items.headline: The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones reports “it’s more likely than not” that the Lions work out an extension with TE Sam LaPorta before free agency.
items.analysis: According to one of Jones’ sources, Lions GM Brad Holmes “does not like losing his draft picks, especially high ones.” A second-rounder in 2023, LaPorta made waves earlier this week when he expressed frustration with his lack of a contract extension on the Pardon My Take podcast. While those frustrations persist, the 25-year-old tight end clarified some of his comments to local Detroit media Friday, reiterating his desire to stay with the Lions long-term. Jones notes that other extensions the Lions have handed out have taken some time to get done. He also cautions that the team shouldn’t wait too long to sign LaPorta as the Raiders are unlikely to waste time making Brock Bowers the highest-paid tight end in football when he becomes extension-eligible after the season.

items.name: Jonathan Taylor
items.headline: The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones reports the Colts aren’t discussing a Jonathan Taylor trade yet.
items.analysis: Jones writes that his understanding is the Colts will wait a few weeks before deciding what to do with their star running back. Indianapolis decided to move on from GM Chris Ballard after a 2-4 start. The way things are trending, it’s easy to imagine the Colts still on the outside of the playoff race in a few weeks. At that point interim GM Ed Dodds could look to recoup draft assets the team lost in previous trades. According to Jones, moving Taylor “would be the most expedient route” to acquiring a high draft pick. Citing sources, Jones lists the Giants and Vikings as potential suitors if Taylor is made available on the trade market. Taylor signed a two-year extension with the Colts in August that hasn’t even kicked in yet.

items.name: Lamar Jackson
items.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Ravens QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) is “50/50" to play against the Bengals in Week 7.
items.analysis: Appearing on ESPN Saturday morning, Fowler said the Ravens are “hopeful” that Jackson can play against the Bengals. He added that the team isn’t “overly optimistic” because, according to a source, Jackson is “50/50" to play in Week 7. If Jackson can’t go, Tyler Huntley will get the start and fantasy managers will need a backup plan this week. At this point, it’s unlikely we receive more clarity on the situation before inactives are released Sunday morning.

items.name: Sam LaPorta
items.headline: Sam LaPorta said he wants to continue playing for the Lions long-term.
items.analysis: Earlier this week, LaPorta expressed frustration in an interview about his contract negotiations stalling in-season. The Athletic’s Colton Pouncy asked him a few follow-up questions today on the matter today, and LaPorta made clear that he hopes to remain a Lion long-term and is excited about the prospect of raising a family in Detroit. LaPorta seemed extremely earnest, saying he felt bad about his comments potentially causing a distraction for his team, but he knows his teammates care for him and want him to be happy and compensated. He handled the issue well and appears to be ready to play hard for a lucrative contract extension, which is good news for fantasy managers. LaPorta is a locked-in TE1 against the Packers this week.

items.name: Jevón Holland
items.headline: Jevón Holland (concussion) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Texans.
items.analysis: Holland, the Giants’ starting free safety, and Tyler Nubin (neck), the Giants’ starting strong safety, are both questionable to play. Meanwhile, starting perimeter CB Greg Newsome (concussion) has been ruled out. Expect the Texans’ passing offense to stay hot this week.

items.name: Rashid Shaheed
items.headline: Rashid Shaheed (hip) is not on the Seahawks’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Chiefs.
items.analysis: The Seahawks’ sporadic producer will be on the field against the Chiefs this week. Shaheed has been involved as a receiver and as a rusher, scoring touchdowns in consecutive weeks. He offers a low floor, but he makes for a viable FLEX starter this week.

items.name: CJ Donaldson
items.headline: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Donaldson is the third member of the Saints’ backfield committee. While he will get a few touches this week, he is not getting enough work for fantasy relevance.

items.name: Landon Dickerson
items.headline: Landon Dickerson (knee/pectoral) was limited on Friday.
items.analysis: Dickerson injured a pectoral muscle on Thursday, complicating his knee-related return from injured reserve. He is firmly in the questionable camp at this time. Eagles C Drew Kendall (knee) was upgraded to full participation.

items.name: Saquon Barkley
items.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) was limited on Friday.
items.analysis: We had really hoped to see Barkley practice in full today. He still has a chance to take the field when the Eagles face the Cowboys in Week 7’s Monday Night Football game, but he is inching toward a questionable designation right now. Upgrading to full tomorrow would increase his odds of playing.

items.name: Dontayvion Wicks
items.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) did not practice on Friday.
items.analysis: Wicks has been banged up for weeks, and the Philadelphia Inquirer’s Jeff McLane said Wicks might miss the Eagles’ Week 7 game against the Cowboys. Hopefully, he resumes practicing tomorrow. Stay tuned.

items.name: Dallas Goedert
items.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) did not practice on Friday.
items.analysis: Goedert is on the wrong side of questionable for the Eagles’ Week 7 Monday Night Football game against the Cowboys. The Philadelphia Inquirer’s Jeff McLane reports that as of Thursday, there was “optimism” about Goedert’s Week 7 availability. Hopefully, he resumes practicing tomorrow.

items.name: DeVonta Smith
items.headline: The Philadelphia Inquirer’s Jeff McLane said he got “the sense” that DeVonta Smith (hamstring) will not play in Week 7 against the Cowboys.
items.analysis: Like Thursday, Smith was sidelined for Friday’s practice. The Eagles have been managing his practice reps and pulled him out for multiple drives in their Week 6 loss to the Panthers. The Eagles face the Cowboys on Monday night, giving Smith an extra day to rest. Consider him highly questionable to play at this time. McLane adds that Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) could also sit out this week.

items.name: Kendal Daniels
items.headline: Kendal Daniels (neck) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the 49ers.
items.analysis: Daniels was taken off the field on a stretcher last week, but managed to practice in full to begin the week. Daniels, a rookie, has 23 tackles, three quarterback pressures and one sack this season.

items.name: A.J. Terrell
items.headline: A.J. Terrell (groin) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the 49ers.
items.analysis: Both Terrell and CB C.J. Henderson (groin) are questionable to play after practicing in full on Friday. Getting them back in the starting lineup would be very helpful for the Falcons’ defense.

items.name: Budda Baker
items.headline: Budda Baker (groin/illness) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
items.analysis: Baker practiced in a limited capacity on Friday, and the veteran safety is no stranger to playing through injuries. The Cardinals ruled out DL Walter Nolen (ankle) and S Andrew Wingard (knee). Cardinals CB Garrett Williams (knee) has been cleared to play.

items.name: Jonah Elliss
items.headline: Broncos ruled out Jonah Elliss (ankle) for Week 7 against the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Reporting from earlier this week indicates Ellis could be sidelined for a few weeks. Broncos S Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) was also ruled out this week.

items.name: Pat Surtain
items.headline: Pat Surtain (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Surtain never managed to practice in full this week. Keeping him sidelined until he is able to do so could make sense. The 4-2 Broncos are currently second in the AFC West. They face the 5-0 Chiefs in Week 8. Stay tuned.

items.name: Jonah Coleman
items.headline: Jonah Coleman (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Coleman practiced in full all week, but the Broncos could technically give him another week to rehab the ankle. If active, there are too many unknowns regarding Coleman’s potential workload to start him in the FLEX, but he must be rostered in 12-team leagues.

items.name: Tyler Badie
items.headline: Broncos ruled out Tyler Badie (thumb) for Week 7
items.analysis: Badie is likely headed toward a demotion with Jonah Coleman (ankle) inching toward a return. The latter player is questionable to play this week.

items.name: Jaylen Waddle
items.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) is not on the Broncos’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Cardinals.
items.analysis: Waddle upgraded to full on Friday after logging two limited sessions to begin the week. The Broncos’ No. 1 wide receiver has struggled to deliver usable stat lines with Bo Nix intent on checking down. The Cardinals’ pass defense could facilitate a bounce-back game for Waddle, but he remains a WR3/FLEX at this time.

items.name: Drew Lock
items.headline: Drew Lock (right elbow) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Chiefs.
items.analysis: The Seahawks’ backup quarterback is dealing with an injury in his throwing arm, so any calls for Sam Darnold’s benching will have to quiet down. Seahawks S Nick Emmanwori (hip), LB DeMarcus Lawrence (knee) and LB Uchenna Nwosu (hip) are questionable. The Seahawks ruled out Chazz Surratt (calf) and LB DrakeThomas (ankle).

items.name: DeeJay Dallas
items.headline: Vikings released RB Deejay Dallas.
items.analysis: He’ll likely find his way back to the practice squad — here or elsewhere — at some point this season. This move portends that Jordan Mason will be activated for Week 7.

items.name: Christian Kirk
items.headline: Christian Kirk (calf) is questionable for San Francisco’s Week 7 game against the Falcons.
items.analysis: He is, however, expected to be activated off injured reserve and play. We’ve heard worse desperation options than “most accomplished 49ers wideout on paper playing with Brock Purdy and George Kittle as Mike Evans sits.” Kirk probably factors in the WR3/WR4 calculus assuming he is indeed activated on Saturday.

items.name: Nick Bosa
items.headline: Nick Bosa (calf) will not play in San Francisco’s Week 7 game against the Falcons.
items.analysis: The 49ers keep projecting a rosy picture of Bosa returning to practice at some point, it keeps not happening. He’ll get the Week 8 bye to heal up. Bosa hasn’t played since Week 2. If only there were a reserve list that teams could place injured players on.

items.name: Zach Charbonnet
items.headline: Seahawks ruled out Zach Charbonnet (knee) for Week 7 against the Chiefs.
items.analysis: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald told reporters that Charbonnet has not suffered a setback. He just isn’t ready yet. Many teams might rush a player of his caliber back, now that he is practicing in full, but the Seahawks are smartly taking the long view with Charbonnet’s health. Emanuel Wilson will function as the team’s leading rusher while George Holani plays on passing downs.

items.name: Deebo Samuel
items.headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) won’t play in San Francisco’s Week 7 game against the Falcons.
items.analysis: Samuel hasn’t practiced since injuring his hamstring in the latter stages of Week 5’s win over the Seahawks. He’ll get the Week 8 bye to heal up. It does seem like there’s at least some chance he could get active for Week 9.

items.name: Mike Evans
items.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) will not play in San Francisco’s Week 7 game against the Falcons.
items.analysis: He didn’t practice all week and will get San Francisco’s Week 8 bye to recover. The 33-year-old’s absence will leave veterans Christian Kirk and Brandin Cooks along with youngsters Jacob Cowing and Jordan Watkins on the 49ers receiver depth chart for Sunday.

items.name: Tyler Guyton
items.headline: Tyler Guyton (calf) practiced in full on Friday.
items.analysis: This is great news for the Cowboys’ offense. Guyton, the starting left tackle, is practicing in full and still has another practice tomorrow. Expect him to be available for the Cowboys’ Monday Night Football game against the Eagles.

items.name: Trent Brown
items.headline: Trent Brown (wrist) is not on Houston’s final Week 7 injury report.
items.analysis: He’ll be good to go after back-to-back full sessions on Thursday and Friday. The 380-pound behemoth will likely continue to spend plenty of time on the injury report in his age-33 season.

items.name: Dalton Schultz
items.headline: Dalton Schultz (quad) is not on Houston’s final Week 7 injury report.
items.analysis: He’ll be good to go, but given how much Houston’s wideout usage has expanded of late, Schultz is probably just a passable TE2.

items.name: George Pickens
items.headline: GeorgePickens (shoulder) said he will play in Week 7 against the Eagles.
items.analysis: The Cowboys face the Eagles in Week 7’s Monday Night Football game, giving Pickens an extra day to recover. ESPN’s Todd Archer said yesterday that Pickens has been icing his shoulder in-game during the Cowboys’ last two games. He encouragingly practiced in full today. Start him as a WR2 as usual this week.

items.name: Matthew Golden
items.headline: Matthew Golden (shoulder) is not on the Packers’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Lions.
items.analysis: A few Packers got a little banged up against the Cowboys last week, including Golden, but the breakout second-year wide receiver is good to go. This game profiles as a fantasy-friendly shootout. Golden should be started as a high-end WR2 with solid upside.

items.name: Brock Bowers
items.headline: Brock Bowers (hamstring/calf) is not on Las Vegas’ final Week 7 injury report.
items.analysis: A Friday afternoon tradition unlike any other, Bowers was cleared after getting in two full sessions on Thursday and Friday. He can be played as an elite TE1, as usual.

items.name: Christian Watson
items.headline: Christian Watson (ankle) is not on the Packers’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Lions.
items.analysis: Watson remained limited through the first two practices this week. We do not yet know his Friday participation level, but he seems to be ready for action. Watson belongs in the WR1 tier against a Lions’ pass defense that has freely surrendered big plays this season.

items.name: Jordan Love
items.headline: Jordan Love (back) is not on the Packers’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Lions.
items.analysis: Love was limited on Wednesday before upgrading to full on Thursday. Packers coach Matt LaFleur told reporters that his starting quarterback was “pretty beat up” after the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys. Hopefully, he is feeling much better by now. This divisional showdown looks like one of the most fantasy-friendly game environments in Week 7. He’s a QB1.

items.name: Tremaine Edmunds
items.headline: The Athletic’s Dan Duggan reports Tremaine Edmunds (shoulder) will miss the remainder of the season.
items.analysis: Edmunds will presumably be placed on IR before Week 7’s game against the Texans. He managed a 52.0 PFF grade in 380 snaps over six games, recording two sacks and 50 combined tackles. Edmunds will enter year two of his three-year deal with the Giants in 2027, in what will be his age-29 season.

items.name: Theo Johnson
items.headline: Theo Johnson (neck) is doubtful for Week 7 against the Texans.
items.analysis: Johnson is not fantasy-relevant on his own, but he can help out the Giants’ offense in real life when he is available. Isaiah Likely is the Giants’ clear-cut TE1.

items.name: Andrew Thomas
items.headline: Andrew Thomas (groin) is not on the Giants’ final injury report for Week 7 against the Texans.
items.analysis: Thomas has played through injuries in multiple games this year. Giants RT Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) and backup OT Marcus Mbow (knee) both resumed practicing in a limited capacity on Thursday and are officially questionable to play this week. The Texans’ defense has underperformed this year. Perhaps this is a get-right matchup for them.

items.name: Brian Branch
items.headline: Brian Branch (Achilles) is questionable for Detroit’s Week 7 game against the Packers.
items.analysis: After three full sessions this week, Branch is expected to be activated off reserve/PUP and should have no snap count per DC Kelvin Sheppard. He can be welcomed back to IDP lineups.

items.name: Cade Mays
items.headline: Cade Mays (wrist) is questionable for Detroit’s Week 7 game against the Packers.
items.analysis: Questionable but fully expected to play after three full practices, Mays should add some more teeth to the Lions’ run game.

items.name: Cam Skattebo
items.headline: The Athletic’s Dan Duggan believes Cam Skattebo “will be back in the mix” in Week 7 against the Texans, likely in “some sort of timeshare with Tyrone Tracy and Devin Singletary.”
items.analysis: Sigh. Three-player backfields are generally fantasy-unfriendly situations, and this one is no different. Skattebo is a capable dual-threat player who has seemingly been limited by the significant ankle injury he suffered last year. The Giants could get him more involved in the passing game, but Tracy can contribute there as well, muddying that opportunity. Singletary would not be a contributor for many NFL teams, but lucky him, he’s a New York Giant. Skattebo and Tracy are viable FLEX options, though both are likely touchdown-dependent.

items.name: Rashod Bateman
items.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 7 injury report.
items.analysis: He practiced in full twice on Thursday and Friday. With Ja’Kobi Lane eating into his targets and the Bengals ever-vulnerable through the air by tight ends, Bateman is probably only a deep-league play in Week 7.

items.name: Travis Kelce
items.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle) is not on Kansas City’s final Week 7 injury report.
items.analysis: He’ll be a reliable TE1, even in a tough matchup against Seattle’s defense, as the Chiefs simply don’t have many other Trusted Mahomes Targets healthy for this one. It’s essentially just Kelce and Xavier Worthy healthy of Kansas City’s main targets.

items.name: Tyjae Spears
items.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 7 game against the Browns.
items.analysis: Spears has been active off a questionable line twice since Week 4. We’d imagine he’d get there again after a limited Friday session. The touch upside just isn’t there for him to be more than a deep-league FLEX play at this point.

items.name: Baker Mayfield
items.headline: Baker Mayfield (thumb) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Panthers.
items.analysis: Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles told reporters earlier today that Mayfield “looks like he’s ready to go” for this week’s game. Mayfield seemingly has solid odds of suiting up this week, but we must wait for an official ruling. Hopefully, that arrives tomorrow. If active, Mayfield will play with a protective plate on the back of his glove to help keep his recently dislocated thumb in place. He is a QB2 for the occasion, if active.

items.name: Calvin Ridley
items.headline: Calvin Ridley (hip) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 7 game against the Browns.
items.analysis: He didn’t practice Thursday or Friday, and we’d consider him on the pessimistic side of questionable. Not that you were thinking about playing him anyway.

items.name: Bucky Irving
items.headline: Bucky Irving (illness) is not on the Buccaneers’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Panthers.
items.analysis: As is typically the case with ill players, Irving is good to go for this week’s game. He upgraded to full participation today after getting a limited session in on Thursday. The Buccaneers’ No. 1 running back has been a volatile producer this season, yet even with last week’s flop, he still totaled 21 touches. That type of workload keeps him firmly in the RB2 ranks.

items.name: Ashton Dulin
items.headline: Ashton Dulin (hamstring) is not on Indianapolis’ final Week 7 injury report.
items.analysis: With Tyler Warren down, Dulin probably figures to join Keenan Allen and Josh Downs as one of Indianapolis’ three main receivers. He has some desperation play viability in deeper leagues.

items.name: Zonovan Knight
items.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Bam Knight will handle “a lot of work” on early downs with Jeremiyah Love (ankle) sidelined.
items.analysis: LaFleur simply does not believe that any one running back can handle a full-time role and remain healthy, so he employs a committee approach. Although Tyler Allgeier sits ahead of Knight on the depth chart, LaFleur said he views Allgeier as a reliable complementary running back who excels in pass protection and short-yardage. Knight will be the team’s lead rusher on early downs and can be started in the FLEX against the Broncos this week.

items.name: Tyler Allgeier
items.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Tyler Allgeier is “always” going to serve as a complementary running back.
items.analysis: LaFleur really laid it all out there at today’s press conference, saying Allgeier “is always going to complement that next guy” when the starter is out. He adds that Allgeier is “extremely smart” and can be trusted in pass protection and short-yardage situations on third down. While Allgeier “can” do what the Cardinals need him to do on first and second down, LaFleur said Bam Knight will take “a lot” of that work with Jeremiyah Love (ankle) sidelined. LaFleur closed by saying he does not think any of these running backs can hold up in a full-time role over the course of the season. Allgeier handled a hefty 19 touches in this complementary role last week. He can be started as a high-volume FLEX with touchdown-based upside against the Broncos.

items.name: Mike Washington Jr.
items.headline: Mike Washington (foot/back) is questionable for Las Vegas’ Week 7 game against the Rams.
items.analysis: Washington didn’t practice on Thursday and was not spotted at practice on Friday. It would seem that he’s a very tenuous questionable at this point. Dylan Laube would be next up for backup duties behind Ashton Jeanty if Washington were ruled out.

items.name: Trent McDuffie
items.headline: Trent McDuffie (groin) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Raiders.
items.analysis: McDuffie has not practiced since straining his groin in Week 6’s Thursday practice. Labeling him as questionable to play seems like a formality before a game-day inactive listing, but only the Rams’ staffers know for sure. The Rams ruled out LB Nate Landman (concussion). Practice squad LB Eric Kendricks will be promoted to the active roster for Week 7.

items.name: Puka Nacua
items.headline: Puka Nacua (calf) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Raiders.
items.analysis: The fact that Nacua is not practicing today is a bad sign for his Week 7 availability. Ever the injury-related optimist, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported earlier today that Nacua’s injury is “more minor than anything else,” though he quickly balanced the scales by then saying that he would not call Nacua’s quick trip to the imaging room “precautionary, because it’s not nothing.” If active, Nacua should be in fantasy football lineups because his talent and workload are almost unparalleled. Unfortunately, coach Sean McVay told reporters that Nacua felt that “he wasn’t able to have some of the power and full explosion.” Nacua is on the wrong side of questionable, and the Rams obviously do not want his injury to worsen.

items.name: Brashard Smith
items.headline: Brashard Smith (hamstring) won’t play in Kansas City’s Week 7 game against the Seahawks.
items.analysis: Did you remember he was on the roster? Funny what one little Kenneth Walker signing will do. Smith has one touch and six snaps in five games. Jadyn Ott will get RB3 duties in Week 7.

items.name: T.J. Hockenson
items.headline: T.J. Hockenson (concussion) is not on the Vikings’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Colts.
items.analysis: Hockenson suffered a concussion in Week 5 against the Saints and was able to heal up over the Vikings’ Week 6. He demonstrated a solid connection with Kyler Murray in Week 4, posting a 13/119 receiving line against the Dolphins. Hockenson can be treated as a TE1 this week against the Colts.

items.name: Rashee Rice
items.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) will not play in Kansas City’s Week 7 game against the Seahawks.
items.analysis: Rice didn’t practice all week despite Andy Reid’s optimistic spin that he’s a “quick healer.” It’s hard to make much sense of how available he’ll be for Week 8 at this point as Rice hasn’t practiced since before the team’s Week 5 bye. Xavier Worthy will again get a WR3-caliber workload as The Only Game In Town for the Chiefs wideouts.

items.name: Justin Jefferson
items.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Colts.
items.analysis: Coming off the Vikings’ Week 6 bye, Jefferson got in a limited session on Wednesday before returning to full participation on Thursday. The star wide receiver posted a 6/79/1 receiving line in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints. He should be treated as an elite WR1 against a Colts pass defense that will be without CB Sauce Gardner (calf).

items.name: Cole Kmet
items.headline: Bears coach Ben Johnson said Cole Kmet (knee) will miss the rest of the season.
items.analysis: Unfortunately it’s not much of a surprise based on the reporting or the carting. Sam Roush will take over as Chicago’s TE2 and likely have fringe TE2 value. Kmet will be in the final year of his four-year, $50 million extension in 2027. The 28-year-old will be a potential cap casualty with a $15.425 million cap figure and $10 million in savings on release without getting into post-June 1 cap machinations.

items.name: Jordan Mason
items.headline: Jordan Mason (thumb) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Colts.
items.analysis: Mason practiced in full all week. He seemingly has good odds of suiting up, but sometimes NFL teams will give players extra time off when they are returning from injured reserve. If Mason plays this weekend, he should be able to handle his normal lead-rushing role. In that case, he can be started as an RB2/FLEX.

items.name: Carson Beck
items.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Carson Beck is dealing with back spasms.
items.analysis: Beck left Thursday’s practice with back spasms and was listed as a DNP. Head coach Mike LaFleur said he was not overly concerned with the injury and that he doesn’t believe it will be anything long-term. Beck’s injury shouldn’t change his Week 7 availability, as he has been the emergency QB3 all season.

items.name: Lamar Jackson
items.headline: Lamar Jackson (ankle) said he’s “heading in the right direction” when asked if he’d play in Week 7.
items.analysis: Here’s what happened: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter spoke and said the team is still “working through” whether Jackson would play on Sunday, and then the team took the unusual step of having both Jackson and Tyler Huntley talk to the media. Jackson also said he doesn’t need to be 100% to play and clarified that he had a high-ankle sprain. There’s little doubt in our minds at this point that Jackson is headed for a questionable tag after a limited Friday session. Reading between the lines, the fact that Huntley spoke probably sets us up nicely for a rug pull, but Jackson-reliant fantasy managers will probably be waiting until inactives on Sunday before they know for sure.

items.name: Denzel Ward
items.headline: Denzel Ward (hand) was limited in Friday’s practice and is questionable for Cleveland’s Week 7 game against the Titans.
items.analysis: Ward popped up on the injury report today. Friday pop-up questionables are always tough to understand from the outside without any major reporting, but it stands to reason that Ward has a real chance to miss the game based on the listing. The Browns cleared Carson Schwesinger (ankle) from the report, so at least their star linebacker will be in there.

items.name: Denzel Boston
items.headline: Denzel Boston (foot) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 7 injury report.
items.analysis: He’ll be on the WR3 line in a good matchup against the Titans. Boston finally had a clunker last week against Baltimore, but he’s been remarkably consistent otherwise and should find easier footing against Tennessee’s rough back seven.

items.name: KC Concepcion
items.headline: KC Concepcion (calf/quad) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 7 injury report.
items.analysis: Concepcion should be treated as a PPR WR3/WR4 tweener this week in a good matchup against the Titans. With Denzel Boston also active, we likely won’t be seeing any major explosions here. Concepcion-reliant managers would accept any explosion at this point as he’s found it hard to crack 50 receiving yards so far.

items.name: Quinshon Judkins
items.headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 7 injury report.
items.analysis: He should carry his usual load in a good matchup against the Titans. That will put Judkins in the mid-to-low RB2 range this week, even with Dylan Sampson getting a chance to come back off injured reserve.

items.name: Jeremiyah Love
items.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will not play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
items.analysis: Things have been trending in this direction all week, but LaFleur officially confirmed on Friday that Love will miss a second straight game. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will likely split duties again in Week 7 after seeing a near 50/50 split in the touch distribution last week, with Allgeier’s 19 touches narrowly edging out Knight’s 17. Both Allgeier and Knight are fringe RB2/RB3 plays against a stout Broncos defense. In addition to Love the Cardinals also ruled out DT Walter Nolen III (ankle), S Andrew Wiggins (ankle), and OG Jo Gaines II (ankle).

items.name: Dylan Sampson
items.headline: Dylan Sampson (knee/IR) is questionable for Cleveland’s Week 7 game against the Titans.
items.analysis: If active, he will be a change-up back for Quinshon Judkins, who is not carrying a status this week. Coming off a long-term injury, it would be a real leap of faith to put Sampson in a FLEX role this week, even against the Titans.

items.name: Divine Deablo
items.headline: Divine Deablo (forearm) won’t play in Atlanta’s Week 7 game against the 49ers.
items.analysis: It’s a slight upgrade for Christian McCaffrey, not that you were thinking about not starting McCaffrey anyway. The Falcons also ruled out CB Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring) — neither player practiced this week.

items.name: Emeka Egbuka
items.headline: Buccaneers ruled out Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) for Week 7 against the Panthers.
items.analysis: Just minutes after head coach Todd Bowles said the team would list Egbuka as doubtful, the official injury report listed him as out, despite his limited participation in Friday’s practice. Egbuka was unable to clear concussion protocol in time to be active for this week, and will now set his sights on returning in Week 8 in time to face the Falcons.

items.name: Brian Robinson
items.headline: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) won’t play in Atlanta’s Week 7 game against the 49ers.
items.analysis: Bijan should get a larger-than-usual workload this week against San Francisco. The Falcons only have two running backs on the 53-man roster so it may be Khalil Herbert or Jam Miller filling in as (Bijan) Robinson’s backup on Sunday. Herbert seems like the logical choice.

items.name: Sauce Gardner
items.headline: Sauce Gardner (calf) will not play in Week 7 against the Vikings.
items.analysis: Gardner was never expected to play this week after it was announced on Monday that he would be week-to-week with his calf injury. His absence could be a good sign for Vikings pass-catchers this week in what should be a plus matchup against a Colts defense that ranks 14th in fantasy points allowed to receivers this season. In addition to Gardner, the Colts also ruled out WR Anthony Gould (concussion).

items.name: Tyler Warren
items.headline: Tyler Warren (groin) will not play in Week 7 against the Vikings.
items.analysis: Warren was a DNP throughout the week and has now been ruled out for this week’s game against the Vikings. This will be the second straight missed game for Warren, who first suffered the injury in last Friday’s practice. The Vikings have allowed the fewest fantasy points to opposing tight ends this season, meaning fantasy managers are best off avoiding Will Mallory and Mo Alie-Cox as streaming options this week.

items.name: Emeka Egbuka
items.headline: Buccaneers head coach said Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) will be doubtful for Week 7’s game against the Panthers.
items.analysis: Bowles said Egbuka remains in concussion protocol and initially said “I’d say he’s out [for Week 7], too,” before saying the second-year receiver would be listed as doubtful. Fantasy managers holding out hope that Egbuka will suit up for Sunday’s game against the Panthers should ensure their backup plan is in place, as players listed as doubtful seldom end up playing on game day. Assuming he’s out, Ted Hurst could be tasked with operating as the Bucs’ WR1. Hurst has caught 11-of-22 targets for 168 yards and one touchdown this season but wouldn’t be viewed as anything more than a WR3/FLEX play even with Baker Mayfield (thumb) back under center.

items.name: Baker Mayfield
items.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Baker Mayfield (thumb) “looks like he’s ready to go” for Week 7 against the Panthers.
items.analysis: Mayfield was a full participant in practice all week and should be removed from the team’s final injury report when it’s released later in the day. Mayfield is expected to wear a protective glove on his throwing hand, which should prevent injury to the thumb he dislocated in Week 3, and will be on the QB2 radar in what is a must-win game for the 1-5 Buccaneers. Hopefully he can improve on a rough start to the season in which he threw for 615-2-2 in his first three games while completing 63.5 percent of his passes.

items.name: Lamar Jackson
items.headline: Lamar Jackson (ankle) was spotted at practice on Friday.
items.analysis: This makes three straight practices for Jackson, who continues to trend in the right direction ahead of Week 7’s game against the Bengals. Jackson was listed as a limited participant in each of the first two practices to start the week and should have a good chance of suiting up, even if he’s only listed as a limited participant. We will provide an update on his official status when the team announces it, but this is yet another encouraging sign for the two-time MVP.

items.name: Josh Jacobs
items.headline: Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Josh Jacobs is on track to play in Week 7 against the Lions.
items.analysis: LaFleur said Jacobs’ Week 7 status depends on how he gets through Friday’s practice. The 28-year-old back has looked “great” in practice this week, per an earlier quote from OC Adam Stenavich, and seems to be trending toward a return after a six-week stay on the Commissioner’s Exempt List. At this point, we would be surprised if Jacobs didn’t play this week against the Lions, but it’s too early to assume he will see his normal workload in his first game back. Even if he doesn’t get a full assortment of touches, we would still expect Jacobs to get enough work to justify starting him at RB2.

items.name: David Montgomery
items.headline: NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson reports David Montgomery (groin) will not play in Week 7 against the Giants.
items.analysis: This will be the second game in a row that Montgomery has missed due to the groin injury he suffered in Week 5. Woody Marks, who totaled 17 touches in last week’s win over the Jaguars will again lead the Texans’ backfield. He has averaged 18.0 touches per game over the last two weeks and will be a volume-based RB2 with a chance at significant upside. Safeties Jalen Pitre (AC joint) and S Reed Blankenship (concussion) will also miss this week’s game against the Giants, putting the Texans down a handful of starters with one game left before their Week 8 bye.

items.name: Emeka Egbuka
items.headline: Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) was seen practicing on Friday.
items.analysis: Egbuka missed the first two practices of the week, but could have a shot at suiting up after appearing on the practice field Friday. Head coach Todd Bowles should give an update on Egbuka shortly after practice, so we’ll check back on his official status once we have word on his Week 7 availability. Whether or not he has a chance to play will largely depend on the team’s independent neurologists clearing him from the league’s concussion protocol.

items.name: Adonai Mitchell
items.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Adonai Mitchell (finger) will play in Week 7 against the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Mitchell has been sidelined since injuring his finger in preparation for the Jets’ Week 3 game against the Lions. It was incredibly unfortunate time for Mitchell and his fantasy managers, as his injury came just days after he went for 6-63-0 on 12 targets against the Packers. Mitchell’s return could complicate things for Omar Cooper’s fantasy managers after Cooper broke out for 6-103-1 against the Patriots last week. The Jets rank 13th in the league in plays run from 11-personnel (209) through the first six weeks of the season, which means both Mitchell and Cooper should see plenty of snaps. That said, neither player should be viewed as anything more than a WR3/FLEX play until we see how the target distribution looks with both players active.

items.name: Breece Hall
items.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) will be questionable for Week 7 against the Dolphins.
items.analysis: Glenn said Hall will be limited in Friday’s practice and that the team will “see how that goes” to close out the week. Hall has missed the last three games with his quad injury but the fact he is closing out the week with two-straight limited practices suggests he’ll be a true game-time decision entering Sunday. If he’s unable to play, Braelon Allen would again serve as the primary back in the Jets’ backfield and would be a fringe RB1/RB2 in what is shaping up to be a plus matchup against the lowly Dolphins.

items.name: Jaylen Wright
items.headline: Jaylen Wright (foot) will play in Week 7 against the Jets.
items.analysis: Wright has rushed 14 times for 28 scoreless yards this season and has yet to receive a target in the four games he has appeared in. Fellow running back Ollie Gordon has emerged as the unquestioned RB1 for the Dolphins since the team lost De’Von Achane (knee) in Week 3. Wright is well off the fantasy radar at this point.

items.name: Caleb Douglas
items.headline: Dolphins WR Caleb Douglas (ankle) will play in Week 7 against the Jets.
items.analysis: Douglas hasn’t played since Week 2 against the 49ers, but the rookie caught five passes for 94 yards in his pro debut against the Raiders and has been targeted on 16.4 percent of his routes. Stuck in a Dolphins offense that currently ranks 31st in scoring and passing yards, Douglas will be hard to trust as anything more than a fringe WR3/WR4 this week against a top-five Jets pass defense.

items.name: T.J. Watt
items.headline: T.J. Watt (calf) was removed from the Steelers’ Week 7 injury report and will play against the Saints.
items.analysis: Watt popped up on Thursday’s injury report with a calf injury and was listed as limited. On Friday, he was upgraded to a full participant in what was an estimated report, but he does not carry an injury status heading into the weekend. S DeShon Elliott (knee) is listed as questionable but was listed as a full participant throughout the week.

items.name: Alvin Kamara
items.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) was removed from the injury report for Week 7’s game against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Kamara was still listed as limited in Friday’s practice, but the Saints feel confident enough in his health to clear him for Week 7. Kamara found the end zone last week on a 31-yard reception, but has largely been inefficient with his touches this season. He seen 14 opportunities to Kendre Miller’s 30 over the last two weeks and will be hard to trust as anything more than a touchdown-dependent RB3 against the Steelers. The only players on the Saints carrying injury designations into the weekend are guard Cesar Ruiz (knee) and DL Nathan Sheperd (illness). Both are listed as questionable.

items.name: Puka Nacua
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Puka Nacua’s calf injury is not considered “a significant injury.”
items.analysis: As far as Nacua’s long-term status goes, this sounds like good news overall. However, Rapoport also noted that Nacua’s status for Sunday’s game against the Raiders could be “up in the air.” With Friday’s practice still to go, Nacua’s status will be one to look for later in the day, as will his designation entering the weekend. If he draws a questionable tag, fantasy managers should treat him as a true game-day decision and have a backup plan in place should be unable to play this week. Given the 4:25 PM EST start time for this game, Rams WR Konata Mumpfield could be on a short list of players worth stashing until we know more about Nacua’s availability.

items.name: Anthony Richardson
items.headline: FOX59’s Tyler Haughn reports Colts QB Anthony Richardson was charged with misdemeanor possession of marijuana earlier this week.
items.analysis: According to reports, Richardson was stopped on October 12th for having a registration on his car that had expired and was assigned to a different vehicle. The officer reported noticing the “odor of marijuana” coming from Richardson’s car, and the former first-round pick admitted to smoking in the car; a “small mason jar containing a substance believed to be marijuana and an opened bag of THC-infused gummies” were found in his vehicle during a search. Richardson is scheduled to have a bench trial on January 4th, 2027. While the NFL no longer suspends players for testing positive for THC, it’s possible Richardson faces some kind of penalty from the league with this being a legal issue.

items.name: Cole Kmet
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Cole Kmet will undergo additional tests on his knee after Week 7’s win over the Patriots.
items.analysis: Head coach Ben Johnson said after the game that Kmet’s injury didn’t look “very good,” breaking from his normal tendency to avoid talking about injuries. Kmet’s knee buckled from under him in the fourth quarter of Thursday’s game, and he had to be carted from the field after the play. This looked like a potential season-ender when it happened, but tests will confirm the severity of it in the near future. Kmet’s absence could open up more opportunities for Colston Loveland, who has caught 26 passes for 244 yards and two touchdowns this season.

items.name: Rico Dowdle
items.headline: Rico Dowdle (knee) is questionable for Week 7 against the Saints.
items.analysis: Dowdle was listed as limited throughout the week and will officially be questionable entering this week’s game with the Saints. This is a new injury he is dealing with but it doesn’t sound like he’s at serious risk of missing the game at this time. Dowdle played on just 17 percent of snaps in his return to action last week and saw 11 opportunities. He’ll profile as a low-end RB3 this week if active.

items.name: Anton Harrison
items.headline: Jaguars OL Anton Harrison was revealed to have a torn ACL, ending his season.
items.analysis: Surgeons discovered Harrison suffered a torn ACL while performing knee surgery on him Thursday. The 23-year-old lineman will now be placed on season-ending IR, with hopes of returning in time for training camp next season. Harrison allowed just 13 pressures and two sacks in five games this season, earning a PFF pass-blocking grade of 67.2. Walker Little, who took over in Harrison’s absence, started last week against the Texans and will assume the starting left tackle role going forward.

items.name: Rome Odunze
items.headline: Rome Odunze caught 4-of-5 targets for 69 yards in the Bears’ Week 7 win over the Patriots.
items.analysis: The yardage total goes down as Odunze’s second highest mark of the season as the third-year receiver was held out of the end zone for the seventh straight game to start the 2026 season. He did make three massive catches on third downs to help extend drives, making his mark felt more with quality than quantity. That doesn’t necessarily benefit fantasy managers that chased his big-play abilities this offseason as Odunze has largely been a fantasy dud outside of the Week 4 win over the Jets in which he returned 15.4 PPR points. He remains best left on fantasy benches ahead of another difficult test against the Seahawks in Week 8.

items.name: Colston Loveland
items.headline: Colston Loveland caught 7-of-12 targets for 69 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 7 win over the Patriots.
items.analysis: Loveland found himself dancing in the end zone for the second consecutive week when he muscled his way in for a score from 12 yards out in the third quarter. The team-leading 12 targets also came on only 33 Caleb Williams pass attempts, with no other player on the team recording more than five targets to their ledger. Furthermore, backup tight end Cole Kmet departed in the fourth quarter with an apparently serious knee injury as he had to be carted off the field, potentially setting Loveland up for more consistent volume moving forward. Loveland finally appears to be making good on his lofty draft capital from the summer after returning fantasy TE1 weeks in two straight games, something managers hope will continue in another difficult matchup on paper against the Seahawks on Monday Night Football in Week 8.

items.name: Luther Burden
items.headline: Luther Burden caught all four targets for 130 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 7 win over the Patriots, adding seven yards on one carry.
items.analysis: Burden erupted on the scene with a 58-yard, catch-and-run reception on a crosser in the first quarter to set up a four-yard score for D’Andre Swift. He would tack on another 24 yards and his touchdown late in the second quarter to push him over the century mark in yards on an improbable touchdown reception, taking a quick screen to the house on third-and-17 with only 14 seconds remaining before the break. Burden would largely fall victim to a more reserved offensive stance after the Bears pushed their lead to 13 points on their first possession of the second half, adding just one additional reception in the final 30 minutes of play. That matters not to fantasy managers that had been waiting for a marquee performance from a player they chased up draft boards this summer. Burden appears to be heating up now further removed from the offseason injury he carried into the start of the regular season and can continue to be started as an upside WR2 ahead of a difficult matchup against the Seahawks in Week 8.

items.name: D'Andre Swift
items.headline: D’Andre Swift rushed 22 times for 78 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 7 win over the Patriots, adding 12 yards on four receptions.
items.analysis: Swift shook off an early injury scare when he took a helmet directly to his knee to earn a season-high 26 opportunities in the absence of Kyle Monangai. This game had an entirely different feel than the previous game played without Monangai, during which Roschon Johnson was much more involved in a game the Bears held a 31-7 lead in the fourth quarter. The back-and-forth nature of Week 7 kept Swift on the field for more of the game, allowing him to return a legitimate RB1 performance on the backs of elite volume. Monangai could return as early as Week 8 considering the Bears now have 10 days until they play the Seahawks on Monday Night Football, potentially sending Swift back into the RB2 range in fantasy circles.

items.name: Caleb Williams
items.headline: Caleb Williams completed 22-of-33 passes for 308 yards and two touchdowns in the Bears’ 30-24, Week 7 win over the Patriots, adding 18 yards on five carries.
items.analysis: The enigmatic signal caller also took three sacks, the last of which almost placed the Bears in position to hand the keys to victory to the Patriots. Ben Johnson called a pass play on third-and-five with under two minutes to play in Patriots territory, placing another nod of support toward his franchise quarterback. Things turned dire when Williams took a sack that appeared to take the Bears out of field goal range in a six-point game, with veteran kicker Cairo Santos hitting a career-long 58-yard field goal to dispel the worries. That sequence of two plays displayed Johnson’s unrelenting trust in his players considering the 58-yard field goal was not only the longest of Santos’ 12-year career, but the third longest field goal in Soldier Field history. Either way, Williams and the Bears escaped with the victory and move to 5-2, now 1.5-games behind the Vikings for the division lead in the most competitive division in football. The Bears get a mini-bye ahead of a Week 8 meeting with the Seahawks on Monday Night Football, where Williams will remain a back-end QB1 in fantasy.

items.name: DeMario Douglas
items.headline: DeMario Douglas caught 3-of-4 targets for 23 yards in the Patriots’ Week 7 loss to the Bears.
items.analysis: The magic of the previous two games quickly evaporated for the diminutive slot receiver as Hunter Henry and Rhamondre Stevenson stepped into the primary security blanket role for Drake Maye, the latter of whom faced consistent pressure from the aggressive Dennis Allen Bears defense. Starting Douglas on a weekly basis is akin to reaching your hand into a brown paper bag found on the side of the road. It feels exhilarating at the time but you never know what you’re going to get.

items.name: A.J. Brown
items.headline: A.J. Brown caught 3-of-6 targets for 48 yards in the Patriots’ Week 7 loss to the Bears.
items.analysis: Brown has not yet clicked with his new team after going down with injury in Week 1 and spending the subsequent four games on injured reserve. He committed yet another drop against the Bears after three drops the week prior, this time on what would have been a long gain down the left sideline. Brown’s burst off the line and at the top of routes appears to remain hampered, something both the Patriots and Brown’s fantasy managers hope will remedy in short order. You can’t really sit Brown at this point, but fantasy managers have to be growing impatient of their first or second-round selection. Brown remains a teeth-gritting start ahead of a Week 8 matchup with the Dolphins.

items.name: Hunter Henry
items.headline: Hunter Henry caught all seven targets for 71 yards in the Patriots’ Week 7 loss to the Bears.
items.analysis: Henry operated as the clear safety blanket for quarterback Drake Maye, the latter of whom was under constant duress in the face of unrelenting pressure from Dennis Allen’s Bears defense. The team was largely unable to move the football on the ground and fell into an early hole, leading to Josh McDaniels utilizing the short passing game as an extension of the run. That’s where Henry made his presence felt, although it was rookie tight end Eli Raridon that caught the touchdown at the position. Week 7 goes down as the first game with more than a modest five targets for the veteran tight end, who has quickly become a difficult weekly start in a more crowded New England pass offense. Fantasy managers might want to consider alternatives when the Patriots face the downtrodden Dolphins in Week 8.

items.name: TreVeyon Henderson
items.headline: TreVeyon Henderson rushed three times for nine yards in the Patriots’ Week 7 loss to the Bears, adding 14 yards on two receptions.
items.analysis: Henderson continues to play second, or third, fiddle behind Rhamondre Stevenson when the Patriots are forced into “gotta have it” mode, with Stevenson the back most trusted in key situations. The Patriots fell into an early hole and were playing catch-up throughout against the Bears, something that could help to explain the lowly opportunity total for the back widely considered the more explosive of the two. Furthermore, the team continued to rotate Corey Kiner through the opportunity pecking order, placing another sizable dent in the weekly floor of Henderson. Although he could find more opportunities in a softer matchup in Week 8, he’ll be a difficult click to insert into fantasy lineups against the Dolphins.

items.name: Rhamondre Stevenson
items.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson rushed six times for 22 yards in the Patriots’ Week 7 loss to the Bears, adding 93 yards and a touchdown on five receptions.
items.analysis: Stevenson scored one of the more improbable touchdowns you will see late in the second quarter. After taking possession with just 14 seconds remaining on the clock, Drake Maye completed an 18-yard pass to A.J. Brown to place the ball near midfield with three seconds remaining before the half. Instead of heaving the ball deep on a Hail Mary, Maye dumped the ball off to Stevenson in the flat with blockers out front. Stevenson would do the rest on his way to a 48-yard score as time expired in the second frame on a score that never really should have happened. The six carries go down as a season-low for the veteran back, although 11 opportunities handily led the team. Stevenson has not seen more than 14 carries since Week 1 and is not finding paint frequently enough to remain a consistent RB2, making him a shaky weekly start moving forward. That holds true ahead of a Week 8 meeting with the Dolphins.

items.name: Drake Maye
items.headline: Drake Maye completed 24-of-31 passes for 321 yards, two touchdown, and one interception in the Patriots’ 30-24, Week 7 loss to the Bears, adding 26 yards and a touchdown on four carries.
items.analysis: Maye and the Patriots struggled to tame an unrelenting Chicago pass rush and were unable to move the football on the ground effectively, two cariables that led to an early deficit against the Bears. Their first half possessions went turnover on downs, three-and-out, three-and-out, touchdown, interception before a wild series to end the second quarter. Caleb Williams led a touchdown drive that left only 14 seconds on the clock. After an 18-yard completion to A.J. Brown, just three seconds remained with the ball near midfield. That’s when Maye dumped the ball off to Rhamondre Stevenson in the flat underneath deep prevent coverage, and Stevenson did the rest on a touchdown that never should have happened to bring the game to a one-possession game. Maye’s other touchdown toss was a beautiful bread-basket throw to rookie tight end Eli Raridon up the seam, adding a score on a grit-play rushing touchdown early in the second quarter. It goes down as Maye’s fourth consecutive QB1 fantasy performance after starting the season leading the league in turnovers through three weeks. The 4-3 Patriots get a mini-bye ahead of a divisional meeting against the Dolphins in Week 8, where Maye will remain an upside QB1.

items.name: Cole Kmet
items.headline: Cole Kmet (knee) was carted to the locker room in the fourth quarter of Week 7 against the Patriots.
items.analysis: Kmet was sandwiched by two defenders on a hit in the fourth quarter and remained down on the field. He immediately grabbed at his knee as he remained on the turf. The cart was summoned and he was taken to the locker room, giving a thumbs up to the crowd as he went. Fantasy managers in deep leagues will want to track his status in the coming days, but it did not look good. Kmet managed to catch all three targets for 28 yards prior to departing.

items.name: Dalton Schultz
items.headline: Dalton Schultz (quad) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Correcting a previous item, Schultz ended up practicing today. He was limited, as was Brevin Jordan (foot), who evidently picked up a new injury. Schultz’s return gives him a chance to face the Giants this week. Ideally, he will upgrade to full participation tomorrow, though it is possible he gets hit with the questionable tag if he remains limited.

items.name: Carson Beck
items.headline: Carson Beck (back) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: Beck appeared on the injury report last Friday, as a limited participant. He remained limited on Wednesday and was downgraded today. Beat reporters saw him at practice briefly, but he ended up going inside with a trainer. This could help preserve Jacoby Brissett’s job security. Stay tuned.

items.name: Rashid Shaheed
items.headline: Rashid Shaheed (hip) practiced in full on Thursday.
items.analysis: Shaheed will be good to go for the Seahawks’ Week 7 game against the Chiefs, barring a setback. Unfortunately, his terribly volatile performances keep him in the boom-bust FLEX tier despite four teams being on bye. For what it’s worth, this could be a fantasy-friendly game environment.

items.name: Jaylen Waddle
items.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: The Broncos’ big-name offseason acquisition has totaled more than 35 yards just once all year, and now he has a chest injury. Waddle is on track to play, and he faces a beatable Cardinals pass defense this week, but he can only be treated as a FLEX starter at this time.

items.name: Jonah Coleman
items.headline: Jonah Coleman (ankle) practiced in full on Thursday.
items.analysis: Coleman is trending toward returning for the Broncos’ Week 7 game against the Cardinals. His teammate, RB Tyler Badie (thumb), remains sidelined. Coleman makes for a risky start if active, but the Broncos’ coaching staff likes him. He should be rostered in 12-team formats.

items.name: Mike Washington Jr.
items.headline: Mike Washington (foot/back) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: Dang. This suggests Washington suffered one or both injuries yesterday in practice. He is firmly in the questionable camp and may have only a long shot at suiting up in Week 7 against the Rams. Without him, Ashton Jeanty should handle a solid workload. Dylan Laube could end up serving as the No. 2 running back.

items.name: Kyle Monangai
items.headline: Bears declared Kyle Monangai, LB T.J. Edwards, LB Jack Sanborn, OL Jordan McFadden, DT Jayden Loving, CB Nick McCloud and QB Case Keenum inactive for Week 7 against the Patriots.
items.analysis: D’Andre Swift will serve as the team’s top back, while Roschon Johnson rotates in behind him. Johnson’s Week 6 fumble could result in less playing time. The Bears face the Seahawks in Week 8. Monangai was unable to practice all week. Hopefully, he returns next week and can be on the field on game day. Keenum will serve as the emergency third quarterback today.

items.name: Christian Gonzalez
items.headline: Christian Gonzalez (illness) is active for Week 7 against the Bears.
items.analysis: Gonzalez is active, but it sounds like he is not feeling great. ESPN’s Mike Reiss writes that Gonzalez “will attempt to play through” his illness. The Patriots declared DT Joshua Farmer, QB Behren Morton, G/C Ben Brown (knee), CB Karon Prunty (hamstring), CB Channing Canada (hamstring) and CB Carlton Davis III (neck) inactive for Week 7 against the Bears. Davis serves as the team’s No. 2 perimeter cornerback. Prunty and Canada are Gonzalez and Davis’ primary backups. The Bears’ passing game should play productively tonight.

items.name: Brock Bowers
items.headline: Brock Bowers (hamstring/calf) practiced in full on Wednesday.
items.analysis: Phew. Seeing Bowers return to full participation today is heartening. The star tight end appeared on the injury report as a limited participant yesterday, leaving some questions as to when the injuries occured, and how severe they are. Ideall, he remains full tomorrow and can be started as an elite TE1 as usual against the Rams this week.

items.name: Trent McDuffie
items.headline: Trent McDuffie (groin) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: McDuffie, the Rams’ No. 1 cornerback, and LB Nate Landman (concussion) were both sidelined today. Both players are on the wrong side of questionable for the Rams’ Week 7 game against the Raiders.

items.name: Landon Dickerson
items.headline: Landon Dickerson (knee/pectoral) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Eagles C Drew Kendall (knee) was also limited. Both players were listed as questionable to play in Week 6 against the Panthers. Neither player was able to suit up. Beginning the week with limited sessions is promising. The Eagles face the Cowboys on Monday night.

items.name: Dallas Goedert
items.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: Goedert missed time with a knee injury earlier this year, but he was not on the injury report last week. This could just be a maintenance day, but it is worth keeping an eye on in the lead up to the Eagles’ Monday Night Football game against the Cowboys.

items.name: DeVonta Smith
items.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: The Eagles held Smith out for multiple drives in Week 6 against the Panthers, in his first game back from a multi-week hamstring injury. He was also dealing with a toe issue. The latter injury is now behind him, and we suspect that his day off today is just a veteran maintenance day. He should be good to go for the Eagles’ Week 7 game against the Cowboys on Monday night.

items.name: Dontayvion Wicks
items.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: Wicks swaps out his multi-week hamstring injury for an ankle injury. He managed to play through it in Week 6 against the Panthers after meeting with the training staff. We expect him to face the Cowboys on Monday night, but he is just a boom-bust FLEX.

items.name: Quenton Nelson
items.headline: ESPN’s Stephen Holder listed QuentonNelson and DeForest Buckner as potential trade options for the Colts.
items.analysis: Holder writes that “trade speculation is swirling” around Buckner and notes that Nelson is in the final year of his deal, potentially providing motivation for the Colts to move him. Neither player had much to say when asked about a potential trade, but per Holder, “it is widely expected that significant organizational changes might be coming after the eventual hire of a new general manager.” Stay tuned.

items.name: Jonathan Taylor
items.headline: ESPN’s Stephen Holder reports that several teams are interested in trading for Jonathan Taylor.
items.analysis:
According to Holder, multiple teams would be open to trading for Taylor, but it remains unclear whether the Colts are ready to be sellers before the trade deadline. Colts GM Chris Ballard was recently fired, and “it is widely expected that significant organizational changes might be coming” after the eventual hiring of a new general manager.
Seth McGowan
should be stashed on benches at this time.

items.name: Christian Gonzalez
items.headline: Christian Gonzalez (illness) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Bears. TNF
items.analysis: Gonzalez has evidently come down with an illness. The Patriots will announce their inactive list in less than an hour. They are already without CB2 Carlton Davis (neck) and their top perimeter backup CBs Karon Prunty (hamstring) and Channing Canada (hamstring), plus S Craig Woodson (shoulder) is questionable to play.

items.name: Christian Gonzalez
items.headline: Christian Gonzalez (illness) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Bears.
items.analysis: Gonzalez has evidently come down with an illness. The Patriots will announce their inactive list in less than an hour. They are already without CB2 Carlton Davis (neck) and their top perimeter backup CBs Karon Prunty (hamstring) and Channing Canada (hamstring), plus S Craig Woodson (shoulder) is questionable to play.

items.name: Puka Nacua
items.headline: Puka Nacua left practice early after suffering a calf injury on Thursday.
items.analysis: Brutal. The Rams lost Davante Adams to a hamstring tendon rupture in Week 6 against the Cardinals, and now they could be without Nacua in Week 7 against the Raiders. The Rams have handled star-player injuries smartly this season. Consider Nacua highly questionable to play, and seek out a backup plan. Konata Mumpfield would serve as the de facto No. 1 wide receiver if Nacua is unable to play.

items.name: Nick Bosa
items.headline: Nick Bosa (calf) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: The 49ers were optimistic about Bosa’s availability for Week 7 against the Falcons, but he is firmly on the wrong side of questionable. The 49ers go on bye in Week 8. Allowing him to fully heal and return in Week 9 for their game against the Raiders could make sense.

items.name: Mike Evans
items.headline: Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: NBC Sports’ Jennifer Lee Chan reported earlier this week that Evans is expected to “miss a little time,” making his two absences unsurprising. Evans has not been formally ruled out, and he is no stranger to playing through injury, but fantasy managers should expect him to miss the 49ers’ Week 7 game against the Falcons.

items.name: Christian Kirk
items.headline: Christian Kirk (calf) practiced in full on Thursday.
items.analysis: Kirk is on track to make his 2026 debut this week in the 49ers’ game against the Falcons. As strange as it sounds, Kirk has a chance to vault into the 49ers’ No. 1 wide receiver role with Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) expected to sit out this week. Kirk should be rostered in 12-team formats.

items.name: Brian Robinson
items.headline: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: The Falcons’ No. 2 running back was limited yesterday. This series of events suggests Robinson strained his hamstring on Wednesday, putting him on the wrong side of questionable for the Falcons’ Week 6 game against the 49ers. Bijan Robinson would handle a few extra touches in Robinson’s absence. The team does not have a third running back on the active roster.

items.name: Justin Jefferson
items.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) practiced in full on Thursday.
items.analysis: The Vikings’ No. 1 wide receiver posted a 6/79/1 receiving line in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints. He should be feeling even better at this point, coming off a Week 6 bye. The Colts will notably be without No. 1 cornerback Sauce Gardner (calf) this weekend, making life even easier on Jefferson.

items.name: T.J. Hockenson
items.headline: T.J. Hockenson (concussion) practiced in full on Thursday.
items.analysis: Hockenson did the same yesterday and can be safely expected to start in Week 7 against the Colts’ beatable defense. Hockenson has seemingly developed a strong connection with Kyler Murray and can be started as a fantasy football TE1 this week.

items.name: Christian Rozeboom
items.headline: Buccaneers placed Christian Rozeboom on injured reserve with a finger injury.
items.analysis: Rozeboom heads to injured reserve with five tackles and one quarterback pressure to his name. The Buccaneers correspondingly activated David Sills from injured reserve

items.name: Travis Kelce
items.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Kelce should be good to go for the Chiefs’ Week 7 game against the Seahawks. At 37 years old, he does not need to practice fully in order to play, though it would be nice to see him upgrade to full participation tomorrow. If active, he is a locked-in TE1.

items.name: Rashee Rice
items.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: Chiefs coach Andy Reid told reporters that Rice’s strain was only a “tweak” in his Week 4 post-game remarks. So much for that. The Chiefs will almost assuredly be without their No. 1 wide receiver against the Seahawks this week, leaving Xavier Worthy to handle the role.

items.name: Tyler Guyton
items.headline: Tyler Guyton (calf) was added to the injury report as a limited participant on Thursday.
items.analysis: The Cowboys’ left tackle played through a minor back issue earlier this month as well. He’s a little banged up at the moment. Whether this injury keeps him out remains to be seen. The Cowboys take on the division-rival Eagles on Monday night.

items.name: George Pickens
items.headline: George Pickens (shoulder) was added to the injury report as a limited participant on Thursday.
items.analysis: Reliable ESPN beat reporter Todd Archer notes that Pickens has had ice on his shoulder during the Cowboys’ last two games. He does not think that this injury threatens Pickens’ Week 7 availability. Thanks, Todd. Ideally, Pickens jumps back up to full participation tomorrow, and we head into Sunday carefree. Stay tuned.

items.name: Dalton Schultz
items.headline: Dalton Schultz (quad) did not practice on Thursday.
items.analysis: Schultz is unlikely to play in Week 7 against the Giants, and now Texans TE4 Brevin Jordan (foot) appears to have suffered an injury. Jordan was added to the injury report today as a limited participant. The injuries elevate TE2 Foster Moreau to the streaming ranks for Week 7.

items.name: Rashod Bateman
items.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) practiced in full on Thursday.
items.analysis: Bateman has been playing through this shoulder injury for a while, though he was forced to leave early last week. Bateman should now be expected to play, but he is only a boom-bust FLEX option with Ja’Kobi Lane now back in the lineup.

items.name: Dylan Sampson
items.headline: Dylan Sampson (knee) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: The Browns could get their receiving specialist back in the lineup this week, though it would be nice to see him practice fully tomorrow. Sampson injured his knee while returning a kickoff in Week 1 against the Jaguars and has been sidelined ever since.

items.name: Quinshon Judkins
items.headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: Yesterday, Browns coach Todd Monken said he was “optimistic” about Judkins’ Week 7 availability. He has a chance to face the Titans this week, after sitting out in Week 6 against the Ravens, but it would be great to resume practicing in full tomorrow. If active, Judkins could be limited to a run-centric role, with Sampson also technically being on track to play.

items.name: Jaylen Wright
items.headline: Jaylen Wright (foot) remained limited in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: Wright played through this listing ahead of Week 5, but it appears that he simply won’t shake it this year. It makes him hard to trust him as someone who could suddenly usurp the lead role from Ollie Gordon, but we’d be surprised if he didn’t play in Week 7.

items.name: Caleb Douglas
items.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) remained limited in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: That’s back-to-back limited sessions from Douglas as he attempts to come back from an injury suffered in Week 2. We’d bet on him getting to the questionable line at this point given the significant layoff, but he does have a real chance to play against the Jets in Week 7 and be a WR4/FLEX candidate.

items.name: Denzel Boston
items.headline: Denzel Boston (foot) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: The Browns’ rookie field-stretcher played through his foot injury last week against the Ravens, posting just a 1/15 receiving line. Ostensibly, the foot is bothering him, but he still has a chance to suit up in Week 7 against the Titans. Hopefully, Boston upgrades to full participation tomorrow.

items.name: Matthew Golden
items.headline: Matthew Golden (shoulder) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: Golden appears to just be being managed at this point as Packers coach Matt LaFleur said there were no concerns on him playing in Week 7 on Wednesday. Two limited sessions are often a starting point for a questionable listing, but we’d be surprised if it got that far with Golden. He’ll likely be cleared off the injury report on Friday.

items.name: Christian Watson
items.headline: Christian Watson (ankle) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: Watson appears to just be being managed at this point as Matt LaFleur said there are no concerns on him playing in Week 7. Two limited sessions are often a starting point for a questionable listing, but we’d be surprised if it got that far with Watson.

items.name: KC Concepcion
items.headline: KC Concepcion (calf/quad) was limited on Thursday.
items.analysis: The Browns’ short-area target earner is banged up, but he still has a chance to play in Week 7 against the Titans. Ideally, Concepcion will upgrade to full participation tomorrow. If he remains limited, he may end up being listed with a questionable tag. Stay tuned.

items.name: Jordan Love
items.headline: Jordan Love (back) practiced in full on Thursday.
items.analysis: It’s an upgrade from Wednesday’s limited session. Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Love was “pretty beat up” after Sunday night, but Love doesn’t appear to be in any danger of missing the game. He’ll likely be cleared off the injury report Friday.

items.name: Theo Johnson
items.headline: Giants TE Theo Johnson (neck) remained limited in Thursday’s practice.
items.analysis: Johnson looks to be on track to returning to the field after missing Week 6, though he’s not doing anything fantasy-interesting at this point as Isaiah Likely has taken over.

items.name: Calvin Ridley
items.headline: Calvin Ridley (hip) did not practice on Thursday.
