He played through the back injury last week and is part of a rough running back committee in the Saints backfield. Kamara is in the RB4 ranks for fantasy purposes. Also active is Chris Olave (illness). The Saints declared QB Zach Wilson, EDGE Anfernee Jennings, S Mike Reid, LB Kaden Elliss, DT Nathan Shepherd, and DT John Ridgeway inactive for Week 6 against the Giants.

items.name: Lamar Jackson
items.headline: Ravens declared QB Lamar Jackson, WR Elijah Sarratt, FS K’Von Wallace, C Cam Jurgens, OG Andrew Vorhees, TE Matthew Hibner, and DE Broderick Washington inactive for Week 6 against the Browns.
items.analysis: The Ravens didn’t have any players listed as questionable entering the weekend, so all of these players are either healthy scratches or were ruled out before Sunday. The Ravens will start Tyler Huntley for the second consecutive week as Jackson continues to recover from the ankle injury he suffered in Week 4 against the Titans.

items.name: Tyjae Spears
items.headline: Tyjae Spears is active for Tennessee’s Week 6 game against the Colts.
items.analysis: He was questionable after a full practice, but will play against the Colts as a reasonable-if-unexciting FLEX option. Inactive for the Titans are S Kevin Winston Jr., CB Alontae Taylor (coach’s decision), RB Nick Singleton, T Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, TE Kylen Granson, DL Jordan Elliott and DT Jackie Marshall.

items.name: Sean Tucker
items.headline: Bucs declared RB Sean Tucker, DL DeMonte Capehart, OG Luke Haggard, QB Baker Mayfield, CB Benjamin Morrison, G Billy Schrauth, and S Antoine Winfield Jr. inactive for Week 6 against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Tucker has stolen the occasional goal line carry from Bucky Irving this year, though he only has eight attempts in total. His absence will move Irving up a spot or two in the RB2 ranks.

items.name: Marquise Brown
items.headline: Eagles declared WR Hollywood Brown, RB Saquon Barkley, S Michael Carter II, EDGE A.J. Epenesa, EDGE Jalyx Hunt, and QB Joe Milton inactive for Week 6 against the Panthers.
items.analysis: Despite the Eagles’ absurdly lengthy injury report, they only had one player listed as questionable for Week 6. That was center Drew Kendall, who is active. Brown was dealing with an ankle issue earlier this week but was cleared from the injury report on Friday, making him a healthy scratch.

items.name: TreVeyon Henderson
items.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is active for Week 6 against the Jets.
items.analysis: As are A.J. Brown (ankle) and LT Will Campbell (knee). It’s a rare day where all the injury news went right for a team. We can’t imagine Henderson will be in large for a particularly big backup role behind Rhamondre Stevenson, but the fact that a player the Pats didn’t even really “need” for Week 6 is giving it a go suggests he is close to regular health. Henderson is a boom/bust FLEX option. Inactive for the Patriots are CB Carlton Davis, CB Karon Prunty, QB Behren Morton, CB Channing Canada, OT Dametrious Crownover and TE Tanner Arkin.

items.name: Tyler Warren
items.headline: Colts TE Tyler Warren is inactive for Indianapolis’ Week 6 game against the Titans.
items.analysis: Warren suffered a groin injury during Friday’s practice and was put on the questionable line; this is not great news for his chances of playing in Week 7’s game. Fantasy managers relying on Warren must immediately pivot elsewhere. Also inactive for the Colts are WR Ashton Dulin, LB Jaylon Carlies, QB Riley Leonard (third quarterback), and G Dalton Tucker.

items.name: Kenyon Sadiq
items.headline: Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) is active for Week 6 against the Patriots.
items.analysis: Sadiq made quick work of the league’s concussion protocol, for better or worse. With Omar Cooper Jr. also active vs. the Pats, Sadiq isn’t much more than a low-end TE2 prayer.

items.name: Omar Cooper
items.headline: Omar Cooper (ankle) is active for Week 6 against the Patriots.
items.analysis: Up for the first time since Week 1, Cooper should immediately slide in as the Jets’ No. 2 wideout with Adonai Mitchell (finger) still somehow on the shelf. He’s a dart throw WR4 for a contest where the Jets should be playing from behind. Joining Mitchell on the shelf for Gang Green are RB Breece Hall, CB Nahshon Wright, LG Dylan Parham, DT Jack Heflin and EDGE Joseph Ossai.

items.name: Quinshon Judkins
items.headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) will not play in Week 6 against the Ravens.
items.analysis: Judkins tested out his ankle in pregame warmups, with the team deciding afterward that he would not play in this AFC North battle with the Ravens. With backup Dylan Sampson still sidelined and Raheim Sanders (hip) on injured reserve, the Browns will look to Jaleel McLaughlin and the recently signed Audric Estime to lead their backfield in Week 6. This is looking like a backfield to avoid for this week, but McLaughlin could have some value in deeper leagues. The Browns also ruled QB Taylen Green, CB Noah Igbinoghene, DT Mike Hall Jr., C Parker Brailsford, OG Teven Jenkins, and DT Mason Graham inactive for this week.

items.name: Azeez Al-Shaair
items.headline: Azeez Al-Shaair left Houston’s Week 6 game against the Jaguars to be evaluated for a concussion.
items.analysis: The Jaguars have been able to impose their will on the Texans in the run game in the first half, and this won’t help matters. Al-Shaair left after Jacksonville scored their first touchdown in the second quarter and was spotted walking to the locker room. He returned towards the beginning of the second half.

items.name: A.J. Brown
items.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports A.J. Brown (ankle) is expected to play “a good amount” in Week 6 against the Jets.
items.analysis: Brown was activated from injured reserve this week and will suit up versus the Jets. It was reasonable to expect some sort of snap count in his first game back, but it sounds like Brown will be a full-go after looking great in practice this week. In desperate need of a true WR1 to step up, the Pats should pepper Brown with targets this week. He is back in the fantasy WR2 ranks after the lengthy absence.

items.name: Dan Quinn
items.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Commanders owner Josh Harris “would love” for Dan Quinn to remain the team’s head coach.
items.analysis: Garafolo says this as if Harris is simply a bystander watching Quinn bumble his way through another season. Garafolo did add that “anything is on the table” if the Commanders get blown out by the 49ers on national television on Monday. They are currently 7.5-point underdogs on most sportsbooks. With a bye week on deck after San Francisco, the Commanders could see Week 7 as the best time to pull the plug on Quinn.

items.name: Kellen Moore
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that “no change is imminent” at head coach for the Saints.
items.analysis: Saints owner Gayle Benson said earlier this week that the team’s 1-4 record is “not acceptable.” Rapoport noted that she came to practice in a “show of support” for Moore and company, though it felt equally like a show of force from the outside. Rapsheet also stressed several times that the team needs to start winning games. While a change at head coach might not happen next week, it does sound like Moore won’t survive the season if things don’t turn around soon.

items.name: Najee Harris
items.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Najee Harris is “set to start” for the Giants in Week 6 against the Saints.
items.analysis: Fowler was adding to a report from Jordan Raanan , who said Harris is “likely to have a larger role with Cam Skattebo downgraded but still part of the mix after the fumbles.” Skattebo has indeed struggled with fumbles, putting the ball on the ground four times this year. No running back has more fumbles, and Skattebo’s most recent blunder cost the Giants a shot at an overtime win versus the Commanders last week. They instead settled for a tie. Even if Skattebo winds up leading the team in carries this week, he was only valuable for fantasy managers because of his high-volume role. With that out the window, Skattebo is buried in the RB3 ranks for Week 6.

items.name: Rico Dowdle
items.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Rico Dowdle (toe) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Bucs.
items.analysis: Dowdle has been out since Week 2 because of the toe issue. In the meantime, Jaylen Warren has looked like one of the league’s most dynamic backs on the ground and through the air. While his gargantuan workload will return to normal with Dowdle back, Warren should still operate as the team’s unquestioned RB1. Dowdle is just a mid-range FLEX play for his first game back.

items.name: Joey Porter
items.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler Jr. (ankle) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Packers.
items.analysis: JPJ was downgraded to a limited participant in Friday before being hit with the questionable tag, causing some concern about his Week 6 availability. It looks like the light practice session may have been a precaution. The newly-minted Cowboys should be good to go versus Green Bay.

items.name: Tyler Warren
items.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Tyler Warren (groin) is a game-time decisions for Week 6 against the Titans.
items.analysis: Warren suffered the groin injury during Friday’s practice. He was added to the injury report and listed as questionable for Week 6. Of note, Warren also dealt with a groin injury late in training camp, though he was ready to go for Week 1 and had not appeared on the injury report again until this week. Even if he does suit up, Warren will be at far less than 100 percent. Expect Josh Downs and Keenan Allen to take on more work whether or not Warren is active.

items.name: Tyler Shough
items.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Tyler Shough has two broken bones in his non-throwing hand.
items.analysis: Both Shough and Kellen Moore have given non-answers when asked about the quarterback’s left hand. Per Schefter, the injury could take a couple of months to heal, but it will not cost him any playing time. Shough injured his hand versus the Falcons in Week 4 and wore a protective glove in Week 5. He is coming off his two worst games of the year, though we don’t suspect the hand is to blame. Things get much easier this week with the Giants on tap. Shough will get another shot at a QB1 finish in Week 6.

items.name: Joe Alt
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Joe Alt (neck) is expected to “ramp up” this week.
items.analysis: Pre Rapoport, Alt received good news after seeing a specialist for his neck injury earlier this week. Alt missed last week’s game with the issue and has already been ruled out for Week 6, but this is still a positive turn of events, all things considered. With a Week 7 bye on deck, Alt could be back as soon as the following week when the Bolts take on the Rams.

items.name: Pat Freiermuth
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Steelers are “optimistic” Pat Freiermuth (calf) will play in Week 6 against the Bucs.
items.analysis: Freiermuth was added to the injury report on Saturday. The team listed him as questionable for Week 6. A last-minute addition to the injury report is never a good sign, so we wouldn’t be surprised if his snaps are limited even if he is active. On the other hand, with Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman out, the Steelers may have no choice but to play a banged-up Muth more than expected. He will be a high-risk TE2 if active.

items.name: Kenyon Sadiq
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Patriots.
items.analysis: Sadiq left Week 5 with a concussion. He was upgraded to a full practice on Friday and seemingly cleared the league’s concussion protocol over the weekend. With Mason Taylor and Omar Cooper Jr. back for Week 6, there will likely be fewer targets to go around in a Jets offense that has regressed heavily over the past two weeks. Sadiq is a low-end TE2 for his date with New England.

items.name: Abdul Carter
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Abdul Carter (groin) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Saints.
items.analysis: Carter got in one limited practice to close the week before being listed as questionable. That would normally make him a coin-flip at best to play today, head coach John Harbaugh was optimistic about Carter’s health early in the week. He is good to go, as is left tackle Andrew Thomas, who is dealing with a groin injury. He has played through the groin issue several times already and will do so again versus the Saints.

items.name: Sean Tucker
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Sean Tucker (quad) is not expected to play in Week 6 against the Steelers.
items.analysis: Despite seeing just eight total carries this year, Tucker has two attempts inside the five compared to one for Bucky Irving. Though he isn’t leaving that many total carries behind, Tucker’s absence will still create some extra fantasy value for Irving, who is on the RB1/2 border for Week 6.

items.name: Alvin Kamara
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Alvin Kamara (back) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Giants.
items.analysis: Kamara played through the back issue last week, though he only saw five touches. He has fallen behind Kendre Miller in the pecking order for carries, and even CJ Donaldson is pushing him for work on passing downs. Kamara is barely an RB4 for Week 6.

items.name: Chris Olave
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Chris Olave (illness) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Giants.
items.analysis: There was reportedly a bug going around the Saints’ locker room last weekend, and Olave seems to have caught the tail end of it. He missed the first two practices of the week but was back on the field for Friday’s session. The team listed him as questionable for Week 6. Barring any further updates, we’re expecting business as usual for the star wideout. He remains entrenched in the WR1 mix for his date with the Giants.

items.name: Quinshon Judkins
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Quinshon Judkins (ankle) will work out pregame to determine his status for Week 6 against the Ravens.
items.analysis: Per Rapoport, there is optimism that linebacker Carson Schwesinger (ankle) will be able to play this week. Judkins logged a single limited practice on Friday before being listed as questionable. The fact that the Browns are even letting him test the groin injury in warmups suggests he will miss at most one game. If he doesn’t suit up, the Browns would be down to Jaleel McLaughlin and Audric Estime as their remaining options at running back. McLaughlin would be the better choice for fantasy managers, though this is largely a situation to avoid if possible.

items.name: TreVeyon Henderson
items.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is likely to play in Week 6 against the Jets.
items.analysis: The same is true of left tackle Will Campbell, who also went down with an ankle injury in Week 5. It’s a remarkable turnaround for Henderson, who was initially expected to miss multiple weeks with a high-ankle sprain. He was limited in practice throughout the week before being listed as questionable on Friday. We expect Henderson to be on a pitch count this week, but he’s still capable of breaking a long run on just a few touches. Henderson is a high-risk FLEX play for Week 6.

items.name: CJ Williams
items.headline: Jaguars declared WR CJ Williams, CB Montaric Brown, S Jalen Huskey, LS Ross Matiscik, DE Wesley Williams, and DT Albert Regis inactive for Week 6 against the Texans.
items.analysis: Jones was the only Jaguar with a questionable tag headed into this contest. Brown and Matiscik were ruled out earlier in the week and the rest are healthy scratches.

items.name: Marlin Klein
items.headline: Texans declared TE Marlin Klein, S Jalen Pitre, RB David Montgomery, DE Sebastian Harsh, IOL Febechi Nwaiwu, OT Braden Smith, and OT Nate Thomas inactive for Week 6 against the Jaguars.
items.analysis: Klein remains a healthy scratch. David Montgomery was ruled out on Friday after missing all three practices this week because of a groin injury. Woody Marks will handle the lion’s share of the backfield touches versus the Jags.

items.name: Christian Kirk
items.headline: Christian Kirk (calf) is questionable for Week 6 against the Commanders.
items.analysis: Kirk is a candidate to be activated from injured reserve ahead of Monday’s game against the Commanders. His status is worth tracking considering the absence of Deebo Samuel and general lack of depth at the position. Fantasy managers could be forced to wait until Week 7 for more fidelity considering the team plays in the final game of Week 6.

items.name: Mike Evans
items.headline: Mike Evans (ribs, Achilles) is questionable for Week 6 against the Commanders.
items.analysis: Evans was unable to practice through Friday but ultimately did enough to land a questionable tag with multiple injury designations. However likely it is that Evans continues to play through various ailments, fantasy managers could look to make alternate plans considering the timing of the 49ers’ game on Monday.

items.name: Deebo Samuel
items.headline: 49ers ruled out Deebo Samuel (hamstring) for Week 6 against the Commanders.
items.analysis: Samuel will be forced to miss Week 6 with a hamstring injury sustained in the team’s Week 5 win over the Seahawks, leaving the team extremely thin at wide receiver. They could get a small boost with Christian Kirk a candidate to be activated from injured reserve ahead of Monday’s game, although Mike Evans is also listed as questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: Cowboys ruled out KaVontae Turpin (ribs) for Week 7 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Turpin’s absence will be felt most on special teams, with the team now forced to find a replacement on punt and kick returns. Otherwise, there is almost zero fantasy impact as the team’s WR4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: KaVontae Turpin (ribs) is questionable to return to Week 6 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Turpin departed before the first offensive play run from scrimmage after sustaining a ribs injury on the opening kickoff. He was taken to the locker room for x-rays and is listed as questionable to return by the team.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: KaVonte Turpin failed to haul in his only target in Week 18.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Turpin ends the season with 26 catches on 38 targets for 396 yards and two touchdowns. He also added 16 carries for 82 rushing yards, but his primary value was as a kick returner. On the season, he had 69 kick returns for 1,814 yards, which leads the league as of the end of this game. That will be his primary role in 2026 as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: KaVontae Turpin caught his only target for an 86-yard touchdown in the Cowboy’s Week 17 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: It took all of one target for Turpin to make his mark felt in the win as he broke free of primary coverage and split the safeties deep down the middle for an 86-yard, catch-and-run score. Turpin continues to play behind Jalen Tolbert but his flashy touchdown demonstrates his big play ability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: Cowboys listed WR KaVontae Turpin (shoulder) as a full participant on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Turpin played through the same shoulder injury in Week 13’s win over the Chiefs. The Cowboys’ special teams ace has posted a meager 19-260-1 receiving line this season and isn’t on the fantasy radar for Week 14 against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: George Pickens (knee/calf) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 13 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: KaVontae Turpin was also cleared to play. Pickens was held out of practice on Monday but returned for a limited session on Tuesday. He was full-go today before being removed from the injury report entirely. Pickens has worked himself into a weekly WR1 ranking and is even threatening to overtake CeeDee Lamb. Both he and Lamb are elite fantasy options for Week 13.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: Cowboys WR KaVontae Turpin (shoulder/illness) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Turpin was a DNP on Monday. The shifty slot receiver/returner looks to be trending towards playing on a short week after taking three touches for a combined 52 yards on Sunday afternoon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: KaVontae Turpin caught his only target for 17 yards in Dallas’ Week 7 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Turpin played 20 snaps according to early PFF data, well behind Jalen Tolbert’s 33. But Turpin remains the preferred fantasy option here given that Tolbert is an elite sacrificial X receiver who almost never commands a target. Turpin is not a preferred FLEX target against the Broncos in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: Cowboys WR KaVontae Turpin (foot) is not on Dallas’ final Week 7 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Turpin’s return should leave your Ryan Flournoy shares in shambles. With CeeDee Lamb and Turpin back, Dallas will have its starting receivers from Week 1 healthy for the first time since Lamb left Week 3’s game against the Bears. Turpin should probably be approached cautiously in his first game since Week 4, but he does have real FLEX upside against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.headline: Cowboys WR KaVontae Turpin (foot) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kavontae-t.analysis: Cowboys RG Tyler Booker (ankle) also remained limited on Thursday. Both players are on track to play, though it would be nice to see them graduate to full participation on Friday. Turpin is unlikely to be fantasy relevant, earning targets behind WRs CeeDee Lamb (ankle) and George Pickens, plus TE Jake Ferguson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-terrel.headline: Falcons activated A.J. Terrell (groin) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-terrel.analysis: The Falcons have been attackable on the perimeter while playing most of the season without Terrell. Fellow cornerback C.J. Henderson is listed questionable for Week 7, but the reintegration of Terrell provides a much more difficult matchup for the injury-riddled 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-terrel.headline: A.J. Terrell (groin) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-terrel.analysis: Both Terrell and CB C.J. Henderson (groin) are questionable to play after practicing in full on Friday. Getting them back in the starting lineup would be very helpful for the Falcons’ defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-terrel.headline: Falcons activated A.J. Terrell’s (groin) 21-day practice window from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-terrel.analysis: Terrell was back on the practice field with his teammates today. He has a chance to face the 49ers and their banged-up wide receiver corps in Week 7. Terrell is a capable coverage defender. His return is a positive for the Falcons’ defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-terrel.headline: Falcons placed CB A.J. Terrell (groin) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-terrel.analysis: He’ll miss at least the next four games. CJ Henderson will take over at cornerback. The Falcons used Terrell’s roster spot to re-sign Zach Harrison to the active roster from their practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-terrel.headline: A.J. Terrell (shoulder) is active for Week 2 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-terrel.analysis: Chris Lindstrom cleared concussion protocol over the weekend and is also active. Inactive for the Falcons are QB Tua Tagovailoa, QB Michael Penix Jr., DB Billy Bowman Jr., DB Malcolm DeWalt IV, and OL Ethan Onianwa.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-terrel.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Chris Lindstrom (concussion) is expected to play in Week 2 against the
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-terrel.analysis: Atlanta is also going to have AJ Terrell (shoulder) available for Week 2. Both players were listed as questionable on Friday. It’s a good start for Atlanta, but what the team really needs is a healthy quarterback. Even third-stringer Cooper Rush is playing through a back injury, and the results were downright pitiful in Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-terrel.headline: Falcons restructured CB A.J. Terrell’s contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-terrel.analysis: According to KPRC2’s Aaron Wilson, the Falcons converted $12 million of Terrell’s salary for next season into a $12 million signing bonus, lowering his 2026 salary to $3 million. Terrell is under contract through the 2028 season and appeared in 15 games for the Falcons last season, totaling 68 tackles and 12 pass breakups while earning a PFF coverage grade of 57.3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-terrel.headline: Falcons removed CB A.J. Terrell (hamstring) from the injury report Saturday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-terrel.analysis: That puts Terrell in line to return from a two-game absence against one of the top teams in the AFC on Monday night. The Bills don’t necessarily have a top wide receiver for Terrell to shadow, although he is likely to see the most of second-year standout Keon Coleman on the perimeter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-terrel.headline: Falcons CB A.J. Terrell (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-terrel.analysis: Terrell has been sidelined since straining his hamstring in Week 2 against the Vikings. Falcons head coach Raheem Morris said he “feels really good” about Terrell’s status moving forward. Terrell has decent odds of suiting up for Week 6 against the Bills, with the game taking place on Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-terrel.headline: Falcons declared WR KhaDarel Hodge, CB A.J. Terrell, RB Nathan Carter, OL Jack Wilson, and DT Sam Roberts inactive for Week 4 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-terrel.analysis: Terrell was ruled out before the weekend, leaving the Falcons absent their top corner for a second-straight week. Outside of that, the Falcons appear to be in good shape to take on a Commanders team that injuries have decimated through the first month of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Broncos activated Jonah Coleman (ankle) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Coleman missed the minimum four games as he tended to an ankle injury suffered in Week 2. He led the team in snaps in that contest and could return to the primary rushing role considering the inefficient play of J.K. Dobbins in his absence, making him worthy of a start in fantasy circles in a plus matchup against the Cardinals in his first game back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Jonah Coleman (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Coleman practiced in full all week, but the Broncos could technically give him another week to rehab the ankle. If active, there are too many unknowns regarding Coleman’s potential workload to start him in the FLEX, but he must be rostered in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Jonah Coleman (ankle) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Coleman is trending toward returning for the Broncos’ Week 7 game against the Cardinals. His teammate, RB Tyler Badie (thumb), remains sidelined. Coleman makes for a risky start if active, but the Broncos’ coaching staff likes him. He should be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Broncos designated Jonah Coleman (ankle) to return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Coleman can return to practice this week and the team now has 21 days to bring him off injured reserve. He could be back on the field as soon as Sunday. With the Broncos’ offense struggling and two backs already seeing work in the backfield, it’s hard to imagine Coleman having much fantasy value in his first game back. He’s worth stashing in deeper leagues, but it might be a while before fantasy managers want him in their lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Broncos placed RB Jonah Coleman (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: That escalated quickly. Coleman was potentially in line to serve as the starter in Week 3 with both J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey nursing various injuries. Coleman missed practice throughout the week with an ankle injury that wasn’t revealed until Wednesday’s practice report, with the injury now taking the next four games, at minimum, from the talented rookie. Both Harvey and Dobbins have been cleared to play in Week 3, forming a backfield tandem in the wake of Coleman’s injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Jonah Coleman (ankle) won’t play in Denver’s Week 3 game against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: For sale: one large FAAB bid, never used.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Broncos RB Jonah Coleman (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: The burly rookie has not yet resumed practicing, while both RB J.K. Dobbins (hamstring) and RB RJ Harvey (hamstring) upgraded to full participation today. Coleman should remain stashed on fantasy football benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Broncos RB Jonah Coleman (ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: What a strange turn of events. Earlier this week, Coleman was viewed as the Broncos’ potential Week 3 starter. Now, RB J.K. Dobbins (hamstring) and RB RJ Harvey (hamstring) are both practicing in a limited capacity while Coleman works in the training room. The rookie running back remains a worthwhile stash, but he may be unable to play this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: Broncos RB J.K. Dobbins (hamstring) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: Hamstring cramps forced Dobbins out of the Broncos’ Week 2 game against the Jaguars. Follow-up reports on the issue have been positive, and it sounds like he has a real chance to play in Week 3 against the Rams, potentially as the leader of a banged-up committee. Keep an eye on his practice participation this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Jonah Coleman suffered a sprained ankle in Week 2 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-cole.analysis: RJ Harvey missed Week 2 with a hamstring injury and J.K. Dobbins left the game early with what was eventually called leg cramps. It’s unclear if any of the three Denver backs will be available for Week 3. Dobbins appears most likely to suit up, though nothing is guaranteed. Tyler Badie could ultimately be the team’s starting running back on Sunday. He should be stashed in most fantasy leagues in case all three starting options ahead of him are ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Ravens ruled out Lamar Jackson (ankle) for Week 7 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Tyler Huntley will draw the start under center for the third straight game as Jackson continues to rehab a high-ankle sprain. Jackson reportedly took most of the first-team reps at practice Friday and was close to being able to play in Week 7, with the team ultimately siding with caution for their franchise quarterback. The Ravens enter a 15-game stretch in which they play three games starting in Week 8, which could have influenced their decision to hold Jackson out one more game. Expect him back for Week 8 against the Bills. His absence greatly influences the upside of the remaining skill position players considering Declan Doyle has halved his usage of play action and completely eliminated RPO with Huntley under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Ravens QB Lamar Jackson (ankle) is “50/50" to play against the Bengals in Week 7.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Appearing on ESPN Saturday morning, Fowler said the Ravens are “hopeful” that Jackson can play against the Bengals. He added that the team isn’t “overly optimistic” because, according to a source, Jackson is “50/50" to play in Week 7. If Jackson can’t go, Tyler Huntley will get the start and fantasy managers will need a backup plan this week. At this point, it’s unlikely we receive more clarity on the situation before inactives are released Sunday morning.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Lamar Jackson (ankle) said he’s “heading in the right direction” when asked if he’d play in Week 7.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Here’s what happened: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter spoke and said the team is still “working through” whether Jackson would play on Sunday, and then the team took the unusual step of having both Jackson and Tyler Huntley talk to the media. Jackson also said he doesn’t need to be 100% to play and clarified that he had a high-ankle sprain. Jackson officially draw a questionable tag after a limited Friday session. Reading between the lines, the fact that Huntley spoke probably sets us up nicely for a rug pull, but Jackson-reliant fantasy managers will probably be waiting until inactives on Sunday before they know for sure.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Lamar Jackson (ankle) was spotted at practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: This makes three straight practices for Jackson, who continues to trend in the right direction ahead of Week 7’s game against the Bengals. Jackson was listed as a limited participant in each of the first two practices to start the week and should have a good chance of suiting up, even if he’s only listed as a limited participant. We will provide an update on his official status when the team announces it, but this is yet another encouraging sign for the two-time MVP.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Lamar Jackson (ankle) practiced on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: After a weird limited session on Wednesday where he wasn’t out in front of the media, Jackson practiced today in full view of reporters, who noted that he was not favoring his ankle at all. Jackson’s injury has always felt tenuous, but even if Wednesday was sort of an aberration, he has to at least be considered to be moving towards playing. Friday’s status will tell the rest of the story. He was officially limited again today. We expect him to at least be questionable after practicing the first two days of the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson (ankle) got in “a little bit of limited work” during Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Jackson was not spotted during the portion of practice open to the media but apparently participated in some capacity later in the session. It’s a step in the right direction, but Jackson likely still has several hurdles to clear before returning to action. Despite Minter’s comments, we expect Jackson to miss another week. Tyler Huntley will draw the start versus Cincinnati if Jackson is ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Lamar Jackson (ankle) was not seen at the start of Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Jackson will go down as a DNP when the Ravens drop their first official injury report of the week. He hasn’t practiced since suffering an ankle injury in Week 4. Head coach Jesse Minter insisted earlier this week that Jackson was making progress, but we doubt it’s enough to get him back on the field for Week 7. Tyler Huntley appears to be the favorite to start against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Lamark Jackson (ankle) could “potentially” practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: When asked if Jackson’s ankle has improved over the last two weeks, Minter offered up a resounding “yes.” Jackson missed a second straight game in Week 6’s loss to the Browns, despite reports earlier in the week that said he nearly played in Week 5 against the Falcons. We’ve seen injuries linger in the past for Jackson, whose team fell to 4-2 on the season and is now preparing to face another division rival in the Bengals next week. Jackson, who is considered day-to-day, did not get on the practice field in any capacity last week, so even a few limited sessions would be an upgrade as far as his Week 7 availability is concerned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Ravens declared QB Lamar Jackson, WR Elijah Sarratt, FS K’Von Wallace, C Cam Jurgens, OG Andrew Vorhees, TE Matthew Hibner, and DE Broderick Washington inactive for Week 6 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: The Ravens didn’t have any players listed as questionable entering the weekend, so all of these players are either healthy scratches or were ruled out before Sunday. The Ravens will start Tyler Huntley for the second consecutive week as Jackson continues to recover from the ankle injury he suffered in Week 4 against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.headline: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson (ankle) will not play in Week 6 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/lamar-jack.analysis: Jackson will miss a second straight game with his ankle injury despite reports at the beginning of the week that said he had a “realistic” chance to play in Week 6. It was also reported after the team’s overtime win against the Falcons that Lamar was “closer than people realized” to playing in Week 5. Jackson and the Ravens will now set their sights on having him ready to go in Week 7 at home against the Bengals, while Tyler Huntley will draw the start this week against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) was removed from the injury report Saturday and will play against the Cowboys in Week 7.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert reportedly aggravated his previous knee injury but got back on the practice field for a full session Saturday before being removed from the injury report. He could be stepping into a massive target share with both DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks ruled out. Fantasy managers can start him as an upside TE1 in a great matchup against the Cowboys in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert is on the wrong side of questionable for the Eagles’ Week 7 Monday Night Football game against the Cowboys. The Philadelphia Inquirer’s Jeff McLane reports that as of Thursday, there was “optimism” about Goedert’s Week 7 availability. Hopefully, he resumes practicing tomorrow.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert missed time with a knee injury earlier this year, but he was not on the injury report last week. This could just be a maintenance day, but it is worth keeping an eye on in the lead up to the Eagles’ Monday Night Football game against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert caught 6-of-8 targets for 61 yards in the Eagles’ Week 6 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Early in the game, when Tanner McKee was struggling to get anything going, he seemed locked onto Goedert. When the Panthers were up by multiple scores and the defense seemed to allow some more space in the secondary, McKee felt more confident in taking shots down the field to his receivers, which meant Goedert was quiet in the second half. Still, he was second on the team in targets, receptions, and receiving yards and will be a low-end TE1 against the Cowboys next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert caught 6-of-9 targets for 38 yards in the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert returned to the lineup after missing three games with a knee injury. Already without Saquon Barkley and DeVonta Smith, Goedert was immediately thrust into a high-usage role. He led the team in targets and catches, though much of his looks were simply check-downs. Even if that’s his role going forward, Goedert should catch enough passes to sustain borderline TE1 numbers until DeVonta Smith returns. He gets a date with the Panthers in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) is not on Philadelphia’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert got in a full session on Friday and is cleared. With DeVonta Smith down, he has some TE1 potential against the Jaguars on volume. He’s always been one of Jalen Hurts’ favorite red zone targets, and Saquon Barkley being down may lead the Eagles to throw more once the field condenses.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: Goedert’s return cannot come soon enough. DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Hollywood Brown (ankle) remain sidelined, and Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) got hurt in today’s practice. If Goedert can play this week, he will vault right back into the TE1 tier.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) returned to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: It’s Goedert’s first practice since going down with a knee injury in Week 2. Even a limited session today puts him on track to suit up for Philly’s Week 5 game against the Jags. With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) unlikely to play, Goedert could be in line for a large role right away. He will be on the TE1/2 border for Week 5 if he is cleared for action.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 4 game against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: He didn’t practice all week and will again be replaced by the combination of Zach Ertz and Johnny Mundt in Week 4. Neither of those players are particularly appealing options, though Ertz has enough of a history of success and the Eagles are bereft enough of targets to make him a viable TE2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.headline: Dallas Goedert (knee) remained sidelined at Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dallas-goe.analysis: That leaves Goedert extremely likely to miss his second consecutive contest when the Eagles host the Rams this Sunday. Zach Ertz was Goedert’s feel-good Week 3 fill-in, but Ertz’s 38 percent snap share ended up producing one catch on two targets. With this entire offense looking rather sluggish at the moment, Ertz does not have TE2 streamer appeal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is questionable for Week 7 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Although getting in a full practice Saturday, the Eagles head into Monday’s game against the Cowboys with Barkley listed as questionable following a two-game absence. Fantasy managers have a decision considering the Eagles play in Week 7’s final game on Monday Night Football, with no clear fall back options should he be unable to play. It would seem prudent to make alternate plans at the position.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) was limited on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: We had really hoped to see Barkley practice in full today. He still has a chance to take the field when the Eagles face the Cowboys in Week 7’s Monday Night Football game, but he is inching toward a questionable designation right now. Upgrading to full tomorrow would increase his odds of playing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Barkley has been sidelined since straining his hamstring in the Eagles’ Week 4 loss to the division-rival Giants. He is now on track to make his triumphant return against the division-rival Cowboys in Week 7’s Monday Night Football game. The Eagles threw the ball at an 84 percent rate in neutral situations with Tanner McKee at the helm last week. Barkley’s expected return will allow them to run the ball more often, though they will likely remain a pass-first offense. Although Barkley’s rushing workload may decrease, his passing game involvement could get a serious boost, benefiting him in the box score. Barkley was officially limited today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is expected to return to practice today and “is in line to play Monday against the Cowboys.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Barkley will unfortunately return to a team without Jalen Hurts, but the Eagles’ offense is otherwise getting healthier ahead of a must-win matchup with the Cowboys. Barkley has been out since Week 4 because of the hamstring issue. Even in his first game back, we would expect Barkley to get the lion’s share of the backfield touches against a Dallas defense that is giving up the 10th-most fantasy points to running backs. Barkley would be, at worst, an RB2 for his Week 7 return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: The Athletic’s Zach Berman believes trading Saquon Barkley “could be a tougher debate” for the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: GM Howie Roseman has seen some quick turnarounds and loves to deal. Should the Eagles continue to spiral, they will certainly be willing to trade players like CB Riq Woolen and TE Dallas Goedert on expiring contracts. But Berman frames it as a real question on “aging stars who might be part of their 2027 plans” like Barkley and Zack Baun. Barkley, still sidelined with a hamstring injury, could be a home-run swing for some team as the trade deadline nears. ESPN’s Ben Solak suggested a trade to the Texans in his Tuesday column, also adding the Seahawks, Packers and Vikings as potential fits.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Eagles ruled out RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring) for Week 6 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: It was pretty clear that this was where things were headed when Barkley was unable to practice on Wednesday and Thursday. We do not yet know Barkley’s official Friday practice participation level, but he was not seen practicing during the portion of practice open to the media. Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele and practice squad player Jaydon Blue will likely split touches this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Barkley is firmly on the wrong side of questionable for his team’s Week 6 game against the Panthers, potentially leaving Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele and practice squad player Jaydon Blue to split touches. Hopefully, reports clarify whether Pierce would handle a sizable workload as the de facto starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Technically, a limited session is possible, but we expect to see Barkley listed as a non-participant since he skipped warmups. Barkley still has a chance to face the Panthers this week, but ideally, he would be out there right now, beginning his ramp-up period. Eagles RBs Dameon Pierce and Carson Steelers are on the active roster, while RB Jaydon Blue currently sits on the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni said he’s “hopeful” he will receive offensive reinforcements in Week 6 when asked about Saquon Barkley’s (hamstring) status.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: Sirianni was asked about both Barkley and DeVonta Smith, who is also dealing with a hamstring injury. Sirianni didn’t commit to either player practicing this week, but we’ll see how things look on Wednesday when the Eagles release their first injury report. Philly suddenly finds itself in desperate need of help at running back after Tank Bigsby (core) was placed on IR last week and Will Shipley (foot) was diagnosed with a partial tear in his plantar fascia that’s expected to sideline him for several weeks. If Barkley is unable to play in Week 6, Dameon Pierce and Jaydon Blue would be next in line to lead the Eagles’ banged up backfield.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) has been ruled out for Week 5 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/saquon-bar.analysis: With Barkley ruled out and Tank Bigsby (core) on injured reserve, the Eagles will officially go with Will Shipley and Dameon Pierce as their top two backs. Shipley feels like a safe bet to serve as the team’s primary pass-catching back, but whether or not he sees the majority of rush attempts is to be determined. It wouldn’t be surprising if Pierce, who profiles as more of an early-down grinder than Shipley, leads the Eagles’ backfield in carries this week, but fantasy managers shouldn’t rush to add him to their lineups. Shipley will likely fall somewhere in the RB2 rankings this week, while Pierce is nothing more than a stash at the end of fantasy benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: Eagles ruled out DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) for Week 7 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: The Eagles will be without their top two receivers but got good news Saturday with the removal of Dallas Goedert from the injury report. Saquon Barkley is listed as questionable and appears to be a true game-time decision. Considering the low involvement of the backfield in the pass game this season, Goedert stands to benefit the most from the absences at wide receiver. He can be started as an upside TE1 in a solid on-paper matchup against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: The Philadelphia Inquirer’s Jeff McLane said he got “the sense” that DeVonta Smith (hamstring) will not play in Week 7 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Like Thursday, Smith was sidelined for Friday’s practice. The Eagles have been managing his practice reps and pulled him out for multiple drives in their Week 6 loss to the Panthers. The Eagles face the Cowboys on Monday night, giving Smith an extra day to rest. Consider him highly questionable to play at this time. McLane adds that Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) could also sit out this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: The Eagles held Smith out for multiple drives in Week 6 against the Panthers, in his first game back from a multi-week hamstring injury. He was also dealing with a toe issue. The latter injury is now behind him, and we suspect that his day off today is just a veteran maintenance day. He should be good to go for the Eagles’ Week 7 game against the Cowboys on Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith caught 7-of-14 targets for 75 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 6 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Smith was easily the focal point of the passing attack after coming back from injury. He saw the most targets of anybody on the team by six, but many of them were not catchable. However, Tanner McKee kept taking shots down the field, and he made a beautiful pass to Smith in the end zone for a touchdown. The game itself might not be pretty when McKee is under center, but it seems like Smith is going to see the volume to continue producing solid fantasy value. He’s a low-end WR2 in a good matchup against the Cowboys next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring/toe) is not on the final injury report for Week 6 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Smith sat out on Wednesday, but practiced in a limited capacity on Thursday before upgrading to full on Friday. Smith told media members earlier today that he is “good,” and that the toe injury is not an issue. Jalen Hurts (blood clot) is out indefinitely, so Smith will be working with pocket-passing backup Tanner McKee. The Panthers are currently without both of their starting perimeter cornerbacks. It might be a bit uncomfortable, but Smith is a WR2 in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring/toe) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo said he is “still hearing optimism he’ll play Sunday. We’ll see.” Given his follow-up comment, it doesn’t seem like he shares the organization’s optimism. If active, Smith would be catching passes thrown by backup Tanner McKee. Jalen Hurts is sidelined indefinitely by a blood clot. McKee, a pocket passer, could lock onto Smith, keeping him in the WR2 tier if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: Devonta Smith (hamstring/toe) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Smith was already reported to be working off to the side on Wednesday, but he now adds a toe injury to his existing hamstring injury on the official practice report. Given he is not practicing yet and a new injury is added to his designation, Smith is currently trending in the wrong direction for Week 6 against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: Devonta Smith (hamstring) was seen working off to the side on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Smith could end up being listed as a limited participant, but this will likely result in a DNP. That said, the fact that he is out there working with the training staff is a good sign. Smith attempted to play through his hamstring injury back in Week 3, posting a 6/65 receiving line before apparently suffering a re-injury. He has not played since, but has a chance to suit up in Week 6 against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports DeVonta Smith (hamstring) has “a shot” to return for Week 6’s game against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Smith hasn’t been seen on the practice field since Week 3 ended, so to say the practice week matters would perhaps be underselling it. Expect Smith to play if he practices at all, though, as the veteran often has suited up with little practice time in the past.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.headline: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 5 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devonta-sm.analysis: Smith hasn’t looked anywhere close to playing since popping up on the injury report ahead of Week 5, not practicing a single session yet. His status for Week 6 remains murky at best. Makai Lemon and Dontyavion Wicks (if healthy) will get a targets boost in what looks to be a very thin offense at the moment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Vikings plan to activate Jordan Mason (thumb) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason came into the season as the presumed lead back in a timeshare with Aaron Jones, the latter of whom has performed as a true workhorse in Mason’s absence. Although it could take a week or two for Mason to fully regain the lead back role, his presence significantly mutes the potential of Jones. Expect a near-even split when the Vikings take on the Colts in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Jordan Mason (thumb) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason practiced in full all week. He seemingly has good odds of suiting up, but sometimes NFL teams will give players extra time off when they are returning from injured reserve. If Mason plays this weekend, he should be able to handle his normal lead-rushing role. In that case, he can be started as an RB2/FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Jordan Mason (thumb) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason is firmly on track to play in Week 7 against the Colts. He should tentatively be expected to lead the backfield in carries right away, with Aaron Jones potentially settling into a 1B role. The Colts’ defense is not an imposing unit, so both running backs are FLEX-viable this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Vikings designated Jordan Mason (thumb/IR) to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: His 21-day practice window will open; most of the reporting is that the Vikings expect him to play in Week 7. Assuming that’s the case, we expect to see him hit the ground running on the Wednesday practice report with at least a limited session and perhaps a full.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: The Athletic’s Alec Lewis believes the Vikings could target a running back with ‘home-run burst’ in a move for the trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Lewis connects the Vikings to Chargers backs Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal as well as Tennessee’s Tony Pollard, Tampa Bay’s Kenneth Gainwell, and Arizona’s Tyler Allgeier. These are just whispers at the moment, but any kind of costly trade acquisition would cut into the playing time and fantasy value of Jordan Mason and Aaron Jones. The Vikings have clearly already been shuffling depth pieces around so we believe there could be more urgency there as the trade deadline gets closer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Vikings “hope” to get Jordan Mason (thumb) back from injured reserve for Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Late last week, Fowler’s colleague, Kevin Seifert, reported that Mason is expected to return in Week 7 as well. Add him if he is available. Mason is not involved much as a receiver, but his expected rushing workload makes him a reliable FLEX with RB2 upside.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: ESPN’s Kevin Seifert reports Jordan Mason (thumb/IR) is expected to return for Minnesota’s Week 7 game.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: The Vikings play the Saints this week, then go on bye in Week 6, so Aaron Jones has one more massive workload week ahead of him against New Orleans before the backfield heads back to a split. Mason looked good in the early going and, if he was cut loose in a shallow league, makes a worthwhile pickup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Vikings placed RB Jordan Mason on injured reserve with a thumb injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: That escalated quickly. On Monday, Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said Mason’s “sore thumb” was being evaluated. Apparently, it had sustained a small fracture, which has now been “fixed,” ostensibly surgically, given O’Connell’s phrasing. Short-term injured reserve placement requires players to miss four games, but the Vikings are on bye in Week 6, so Mason will be eligible to return in Week 7. Mason led the backfield with 15 carries in Week 1, so his absence provides RB Aaron Jones with a touch-count boost. Veteran RB DeeJay Dallas operated as the RB3. Rookie RB Demond Claiborne was inactive last week, but should be active in Week 2 against the Lions. Speculatively stashing him could be worthwhile.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell said Jordan Mason has a sore thumb and is being evaluated.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason didn’t appear to have any issues in Week 1’s win, but adrenaline does carry athletes at times. We’ll likely get an update on this on Wednesday at the latest — we’d consider Mason likely to play in Week 2’s game against the Bears at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.headline: Jordan Mason rushed 15 times for 59 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 1 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-mas.analysis: Mason led the team in carries but only rushed three more times than Aaron Jones, who also found the end zone. Both backs also ran nine routes each, though Jones was targeted once while Mason did not see a look in the passing game. Mason’s lack of a role through the air will limit his weekly ceiling, but a floor of double-digit carries isn’t half bad. He will sit in the RB3 ranks for his Week 2 date with the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Browns activated RB Dylan Sampson (knee) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: Sampson was limited in practice throughout the week and listed as questionable for Week 7 against the Titans. Now that he’s officially been activated from injured reserve, he’s likely to be Cleveland’s change-of-pace back behind Quinshon Judkins this week. Sampson is worth stashing on fantasy benches, but is truly just a desperation FLEX play coming off a knee injury that’s sidelined him since Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Dylan Sampson (knee/IR) is questionable for Cleveland’s Week 7 game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: If active, he will be a change-up back for Quinshon Judkins, who is not carrying a status this week. Coming off a long-term injury, it would be a real leap of faith to put Sampson in a FLEX role this week, even against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Dylan Sampson (knee) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: The Browns could get their receiving specialist back in the lineup this week, though it would be nice to see him practice fully tomorrow. Sampson injured his knee while returning a kickoff in Week 1 against the Jaguars and has been sidelined ever since.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Dylan Sampson (knee) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: Browns coach Todd Monken indicated earlier today that Sampson has a chance to return from injured reserve in time to face the Titans on Sunday. The Browns’ skill position corps is banged up and could use an explosive player. Sampson might end up warranting FLEX treatment right off the bat, if he is active this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Browns head coach Todd Monken said he’s “optimistic” Quinshon Judkins (ankle) will play in Week 7 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: Monken sounded like Judkins and Dylan Sampson will be active and ready to go against Tennessee. Judkins had been the locked-in lead back for Cleveland before his Week 5 ankle injury, seeing 71 percent of the team’s designed rushing attempts. The potential return of Sampson, a good pass catcher, could complicate things for Judkins’ involvement in the pass game going forward. Judkins will be a touchdown-dependent flex play against a Titans defense allowing the NFL’s ninth lowest rushing success rate in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Dylan Sampson (knee) won’t play in Cleveland’s Week 6 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: Sampson practiced each of the last two days, but it was too little, too late, for Week 6. He stands a chance at returning in Week 7. As long as Quinshon Judkins is relatively healthy, Sampson won’t have standalone value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Dylan Sampson (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: This is at least some positive momentum towards being activated and helping the Browns out on Sunday, though even if Sampson was activated he’d likely be in a committee. We’ll see what Friday brings, but unless it’s a full session, we’d be surprised if Sampson was more than a sketchy questionable for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Dylan Sampson (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: The Browns opened Sampson’s practice window today, so it’s a bit odd to see him sit out of the session entirely. They were likely giving Sampson the option to suit up even though he may not be fully ready to return. With Quinshon Judkins injured and Raheim Sanders on IR, the Browns are clearly desperate at running back. If Sampson doesn’t play on Sunday, the backfield will be split between Jaleel McLaughlin and Audric Estime. This is likely a fantasy situation to avoid at all costs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: Judkins suffered a potentially serious ankle injury in Week 5 and could miss Week 6 against the Ravens if he’s unable to practice in the next couple days. That could leave Jaleel McLaughlin as the Browns’ lead back against Baltimore. Dylan Sampson (knee) could also suit up if he’s able to practice after a four-week stint on IR.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.headline: Browns RB Dylan Sampson (knee) is designated to return and eligible to return to practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dylan-samp.analysis: Sampson was placed on injured reserve in mid-September with a knee injury. His return could be an immediate factor in the Browns backfield with Quinshon Judkins likely out with an ankle injury. Sampson could compete for backfield touches with Jaleel McLaughlin in Week 6 against the Ravens if he’s active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that several teams believe the Jaguars could trade WR Brian Thomas Jr.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.analysis: Appearing on ESPN Saturday morning, Fowler, citing Thomas’ zero catches over the last two weeks, said something has to give in this situation. According to several teams the NFL Insider talked to, Thomas could be traded over the next few weeks. Fowler listed the Chiefs and Steelers as potentially interested teams and was emphatic that there will be suitors for Thomas. If you have Thomas in fantasy, it’s hard to imagine his value getting worse with a change of scenery. The Jaguars would appear content to roll with Parker Washington, Jakobi Meyers and Travis Hunter as their top receivers in the event of a Thomas trade.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes it could make long-term sense for the Commanders to acquire Brian Thomas, Jr.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.analysis: Shipley mentions the Commanders and Rams as wideout-desperate teams who might be interested in trading for Thomas before the NFL’s trade deadline. The Jaguars have apparently soured on the one-time burgeoning star in recent weeks; against the Texans in Week 6, Thomas ran a pass route on just 28 percent of the Jags’ drop backs and saw two targets. The Commanders, meanwhile, lost Terry McLaurin to a potentially long-term knee injury on Monday night. Thomas, per Shipley, “is not a trade that would make a ton of sense for a Commanders team that might be losing a ton of games and needs their picks to rebuild ... but it would make sense for a general manager who needs to keep his job to give his quarterback a familiar and talented target. Daniels was Thomas’ quarterback during their final seasons at LSU, and the connection between the two could go a long-way toward solving some of Washington’s long-term issues at the wide receiver position.” BTJ’s fantasy prospects would get a big boost if he were to land in Washington in the coming weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.headline: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said “Guys have to step up and make plays” when asked about benching Brian Thomas Jr. for the second half of Week 6’s loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.analysis: Coen benched Thomas for the entire second half after he had one drop and two non-catches in the first against Houston. It sure seems like the runway for Thomas is running out in Jacksonville. A potential trade is the only fantasy salvation coming for the third-year receiver as he looks buried here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.headline: Brian Thomas Jr. failed to catch either of his two targets in Jacksonville’s Week 6 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.analysis: That’s three games with three or fewer targets and Thomas Jr. has put up back-to-back bagels in London, apparently distraught over the local cuisine. He absolutely does not have to be rostered in most fantasy leagues through Jacksonville’s Week 7 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.headline: Brian Thomas Jr. failed to catch any of his three targets in the Jaguars’ Week 5 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.analysis: This game started with Jaguars defensive end Bryan Thomas Jr. getting ejected on the opening kickoff. He would go on to catch as many passes as his wide receiver doppelganger. BTJ nearly saved face with a late touchdown, but he failed to drag his back foot and stepped out of bounds for an incompletion. Josh Cameron, the team’s WR4, saw six targets. Thomas Jr. simply doesn’t have much of a role in this offense anymore. He will be the subject of trade speculation in the coming weeks. That seems to be his only path to meaningful fantasy production.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.headline: Brian Thomas Jr. caught 2-of-2 targets for 17 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 4 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.analysis: Though he was still No. 3 in wide receiver snaps agains the Bengals, Thomas saw more snaps this week than his 23-snap game against the Patriots last week. He out-snapped Josh Cameron 38-to-22 and caught Trevor Lawrence’s sole touchdown pass of the afternoon. Despite the score, Thomas’ lesser role relegates him to the WR3 spot in the Jaguars offense as he tied for fourth in targets against the Bengals. Thomas is a touchdown-dependent fantasy play and should be in the WR5 range for Week 5 against the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.headline: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said Brian Thomas Jr. played only 23 snaps in Week 3 because the Jaguars “were playing in a little bit more 12 and also some of the things that we had Josh [Cameron] on specifically were things that we felt good about him doing within a role that he has.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.analysis: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes that Cameron’s usage (23 snaps) could make it “stand[s] to reason Thomas could quickly become the fourth option instead” in a column that says he believes a “new start would be best for both parties.” It sounds like there’s a non-zero chance that Thomas is on the trade block at the deadline, as weird as that seems given how good the Jaguars have been on offense. Thomas isn’t necessarily someone who has to be rostered in shallow leagues given how things are trending.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.headline: Brian Thomas, Jr. caught his lone target for eight yards in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.analysis: After back-to-back 40-yard outings as the Jaguars’ No. 2 receiver, Thomas bottomed out on a low-volume day for the Jacksonville offense. Jakobi Meyers led the Jags with nine targets while Parker Washington saw five looks; both wideouts scored a touchdown against an overmatched Pats secondary. Thomas’ usage has been spotty even in two-receiver sets so far this season. That leaves him as an iffy flex play week to week. He could benefit from a potentially high-scoring game in Week 4 against the Bengals. In shallower leagues he should stay on the bench for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.headline: Brian Thomas Jr. caught 3-of-8 targets for 40 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 2 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.analysis: Thomas had a couple drops in this one and once again seemed not to be on the same page as Trevor Lawrence. Parker Washington led the Jaguars with a dozen targets and was clearly Lawrence’s preferred target. The highlight of Thomas’ day came on a 22-yard grab. BTJ’s downfield role in the Jacksonville offense means he will be a high variance weekly play in 12-team leagues. He some some flex appeal for Week 3 against a tough New England secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.headline: Jaguars WR Brian Thomas (shoulder) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/brian-thomas/0.analysis: Thomas missed a little time in Week 1 after landing on his injured shoulder, but was able to return. The Jaguars’ X-receiver could face Broncos CB Pat Surtain on the perimeter this week, but he should get a few chances to make big plays downfield. He remains a FLEX starter in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones reports “it’s more likely than not” that the Lions work out an extension with TE Sam LaPorta before free agency.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: According to one of Jones’ sources, Lions GM Brad Holmes “does not like losing his draft picks, especially high ones.” A second-rounder in 2023, LaPorta made waves earlier this week when he expressed frustration with his lack of a contract extension on the Pardon My Take podcast. While those frustrations persist, the 25-year-old tight end clarified some of his comments to local Detroit media Friday, reiterating his desire to stay with the Lions long-term. Jones notes that other extensions the Lions have handed out have taken some time to get done. He also cautions that the team shouldn’t wait too long to sign LaPorta as the Raiders are unlikely to waste time making Brock Bowers the highest-paid tight end in football when he becomes extension-eligible after the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta said he wants to continue playing for the Lions long-term.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: Earlier this week, LaPorta expressed frustration in an interview about his contract negotiations stalling in-season. The Athletic’s Colton Pouncy asked him a few follow-up questions today on the matter today, and LaPorta made clear that he hopes to remain a Lion long-term and is excited about the prospect of raising a family in Detroit. LaPorta seemed extremely earnest, saying he felt bad about his comments potentially causing a distraction for his team, but he knows his teammates care for him and want him to be happy and compensated. He handled the issue well and appears to be ready to play hard for a lucrative contract extension, which is good news for fantasy managers. LaPorta is a locked-in TE1 against the Packers this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 5-of-5 targets for 88 yards and one touchdown in the Lions’ Week 5 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: LaPorta got involved on the Lions’ third drive, making a clutch 12-yard grab on 4th-and-3 while suffering what the officials deemed an unnecessarily rough hit by LB Mack Wilson at the end of the play. He chipped in two catch-and-run plays on the following drive. The first being an 11-yard play that was controversially ruled down in front of the sticks. Coach Dan Campbell called his number on the next play, resulting in an effortless 38-yard touchdown down the right side of the field. LaPorta tacked on an eight-yard catch and a 19-yard catch in the second half as the Lions cruised to a blowout win. He goes on bye next week but returns to the TE1 ranks in Week 7 against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 8-of-13 targets for 84 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 4 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: LaPorta was the primary beneficiary against the single-high-heavy Panthers, which was interesting considering both of Carolina’s top two corners were absent from this game. The 13 targets were easily a season high for the veteran tight end, primarily the result of 52 Jared Goff pass attempts in what would become a negative game script. LaPorta routinely found space behind the linebackers as the primary outlet through pressure for Goff, and while it remains unlikely he repeats the lofty target totals, LaPorta’s red zone acumen keeps him a fantasy TE1 ahead of a very different matchup in the two-high-heavy Cardinals in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Sam LaPorta and the Lions “have broken off contract talks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: Rapoport did note that the Lions could make another push to sign LaPorta later this year, so the door isn’t entirely closed. LaPorta is set to become a free agent next offseason. The team could, however, place the franchise tag on him. He has gotten off to a quiet start with 14 catches for 144 yards and one score. LaPorta is currently on pace for a career-low in yards per game. He would still have plenty of suitors in free agency, even if the counting stats don’t improve this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 3-of-4 targets for 44 yards in the Lions’ Week 3 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: LaPorta was a secondary piece of the passing attack in this game, taking a backseat to Jhamyr Gibbs and Amon-Ra St. Brown. The two superstars combined for 16 targets while LaPorta and Jameson Williams were held to a combined eight looks. LaPorta has at least 44 yards in every game this year but no more than 52. With a solid floor established, all that’s left is for LaPorta to hit on a ceiling game. He remains a mid-range TE1 for Week 4 against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 6-of-7 targets for 52 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 2 loss to the Bills.
