https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: LaPorta combined with Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jahmyr Gibbs to be the primary targets for quarterback Jared Goff on a night where relentless pressure from the Bills forced the offense to primarily attack the intermediate areas of the field. That could be the norm for this offense moving forward considering the mounting injuries along their offensive line, which are likely to be felt the most against opponents with a legitimate pass rush. That may not be the case in Week 3 when the Lions host the Jets, a team that is likely to also utilize elevated rates of zone coverage. LaPorta has had stark man-zone splits throughout his career and could see less volume due to matchup. He’ll be a low-end TE1 against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Sam LaPorta caught 5-of-8 targets for 48 yards in the Lions’ Week 1 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: Week 1 was business as usual for LaPorta, who finished second on the team in catches and yards. After missing time in the offseason recovering from a season-ending back injury and later a minor hip issue, this goes down as a big win for the young tight end, even if fantasy managers aren’t thrilled with his score. LaPorta will project for TE1 numbers when the Lions take on the Ravens next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter said the Lions could sign TE Sam LaPorta to a contract extension early in the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: Schefter was exploring extension possibilities across the NFL with colleague Pat McAfee and noted that the Lions have a propensity for signing players to extensions in-season. The stud tight end spent the offseason rehabbing after undergoing back surgery. Perhaps the front office just wants to make sure LaPorta returns to his pre-injury form this month before signing him to a lucrative deal. He is scheduled to enter free agency next offseason. Signing him to a long-term deal makes sense. He is a locked-in TE1 this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.headline: Lions TE Sam LaPorta (hip) resumed practicing on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-laport.analysis: LaPorta’s hip issue no longer appears to be a concern. The 25-year-old has continued practicing as the week progresses. He was out there catching passes from QB Jared Goff during Friday’s scrimmage. LaPorta is a locked-in TE1, playing in what should be one of the NFL’s highest-scoring offenses this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones reports the Colts aren’t discussing a Jonathan Taylor trade yet.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Jones writes that his understanding is the Colts will wait a few weeks before deciding what to do with their star running back. Indianapolis decided to move on from GM Chris Ballard after a 2-4 start. The way things are trending, it’s easy to imagine the Colts still on the outside of the playoff race in a few weeks. At that point interim GM Ed Dodds could look to recoup draft assets the team lost in previous trades. According to Jones, moving Taylor “would be the most expedient route” to acquiring a high draft pick. Citing sources, Jones lists the Giants and Vikings as potential suitors if Taylor is made available on the trade market. Taylor signed a two-year extension with the Colts in August that hasn’t even kicked in yet.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: ESPN’s Stephen Holder reports that several teams are interested in trading for Jonathan Taylor.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis:
According to Holder, multiple teams would be open to trading for Taylor, but it remains unclear whether the Colts are ready to be sellers before the trade deadline. Colts GM Chris Ballard was recently fired, and “it is widely expected that significant organizational changes might be coming” after the eventual hiring of a new general manager.
Seth McGowan
should be stashed on benches at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: SNY TV’s Connor Hughes believes the Giants will likely try to trade for a running back, and Cam Skattebo is unlikely to return to his prior role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Hughes makes clear that he thinks Skattebo’s time as the clear-cut lead back is over, recapping coach John Harbaugh’s offseason attempts to acquire a bellcow, while noting that Skattebo is currently in the doghouse. Hughes believes Skattebo is a nice complementary player who can function as a physical change-of-pace option. The biggest issue the Giants face in replacing him is cost. He thinks a player like Jonathan Taylor will cost a Day 2 pick, at least, and he is not sure Taylor is worth that, given the Giants’ long-term plans for the 2027 draft capital they’ve accrued via various personnel moves. Trading away Kayvon Thibodeaux is an option, but doing so is challenging with Brian Burns (knee) out for the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: Jonathan Taylor rushed 21 times for 94 yards and a touchdown in the Colts’ Week 6 loss to the Titans, adding two receptions for 57 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Taylor also lost a fumble in the opening moments of the second half that set in motion a blown 13-0 lead against arguably the worst team in football. Taylor went into a whole crowd of Titans and did not emerge with the football. These things happen, but even the littlest things have a way of costing the Colts this season. Taylor is not the problem for Indy or fantasy managers, but Daniel Jones’ poor play is making it difficult for Indy to sustain drives, and for Taylor to live up to his high-end RB1 status. The blitz-happy Vikings are a dangerous Week 7 matchup in that regard.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: Jonathan Taylor rushed 15 times for 45 yards in the Colts’ Week 5 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Taylor added 37 receiving yards on three catches. As JJ Watt noted on the broadcast, the Steelers knew that the Colts love running off tackle, so they sent extra rushers and had their defensive ends bracket the tackles to force the Colts to run up the gut. It didn’t work out well for the Colts. Taylor had no running room all day and was stuffed inside the three-yard line three separate times. Things will likely be better next week against the Titans, but the Colts are going to need to fix their issues in the interior of their offensive line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: Jonathan Taylor rushed 20 times for 95 yards and two touchdowns in the Colts’ Week 4 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Playing in London, Taylor needed just 78 yards to overtake Travis Etienne as the league’s all-time leading rusher in international games. Taylor didn’t disappoint with his third multi-score effort of the season. Marcus Mariota left the game early and the Colts pulled away in the second half, allowing them to lean on the ground game. With the passing game struggling throughout the first month of football, expect the Colts to continue to build their offense around Taylor. He remains near the top of the RB1 ranks for his Week 5 matchup with the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: Jonathan Taylor rushed 23 times for 68 yards in the Colts’ Week 3 win over the Texans, adding two catches for four yards on three targets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: The Texans focused first and foremost on stuffing Taylor, and outside of a stretch in the middle of the second half when Azeez Al-Shaair was pulled off the field for injury, they mostly did just that. Taylor did have a 24-yard scamper pulled off the scoresheet by a holding call. He’ll be back in the RB1 ranks next week against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: Jonathan Taylor rushed 24 times for 92 yards and two touchdowns in the Colts’ Week 2 loss to the Chiefs, adding 40 yards on four receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Taylor’s one-cut rushing ability was on full display against the Chiefs while gashing Kansas City’s defense on outside zone runs. Both of his touchdown scampers came on such carries, the second of which knotted the game at 27 to eventually force overtime. Unfortunately for Taylor and the Colts, the two carries that mattered the most were stuffed for a combined negative-three yards following a 48-yard Laquon Treadwell reception in overtime, eventually forcing the Colts to kick a game-tying field goal. Patrick Mahomes would send Indianapolis to an 0-2 record on the following possession. Taylor gets a difficult matchup against one of the top defenses in the league in Week 3, but he will remain a locked-in RB1 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: Jonathan Taylor rushed 19 times for 98 yards and two touchdowns in the Colts’ Week 1 loss to the Ravens, adding three receptions for 23 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Taylor felt like the lone bright spot on Sunday for a Colts offense that struggled for much of the game. Taylor struggled at times on the ground, with nine of his 19 carries going for three or fewer yards, but he also broke free for five carries of 10-plus yards, with his longest run coming on a 21-yard burst in the third quarter. Taylor got the scoring started for the Colts in the first quarter when he plunged into the end zone for a one-yard score to give them the early lead, and found the end zone again in the second quarter on a three-yard score. Taylor was the only Colts running back to see a rush attempt in this one, and he saw four of the five running back targets. He’ll be firmly on the RB1 radar in next week’s game against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.headline: Colts signed Jonathan Taylor to a two-year, $44 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonathan-t.analysis: Taylor and GM Chris Ballard both talked about their desire to get a deal done earlier in training camp, and it didn’t take long for the two sides to reach an agreement. The deal includes $39 million guaranteed and has another $3 million for Taylor to earn via incentives. He was set to be a free agent next offseason but is now signed through the 2028 season. Taylor slowed down once Daniel Jones got injured last year. Even with the quiet finish, his season-long numbers look incredible. He ran for 1,585 yards and 18 touchdowns while setting career-highs in receptions (46) and receiving yards (378). Taylor is rightfully the fourth running back to be taken in most fantasy drafts this summer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jevon-holl.headline: Jevón Holland (concussion) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jevon-holl.analysis: Holland, the Giants’ starting free safety, and Tyler Nubin (neck), the Giants’ starting strong safety, are both questionable to play. Meanwhile, starting perimeter CB Greg Newsome (concussion) has been ruled out. Expect the Texans’ passing offense to stay hot this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jevon-holl.headline: Jevón Holland (concussion) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jevon-holl.analysis: Holland, the team’s top safety, and Greg Newsome (concussion), the team’s top cornerback, were both sidelined today. Giants LB Tremaine Edmunds (shoulder) was also sidelined. The Giants are tasked with containing a Texans’ passing offense that ties for the league lead in explosive pass plays this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jevon-holl.headline: Giants declared S Jevon Holland, CB Paulson Adebo, CB Cor’Dale Flott, DL Chauncey Golston, OT Jermaine Eleumunor, and TE Daniel Bellinger inactive for Week 9 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jevon-holl.analysis: Holland tested his knee out in pre-game warmups but wasn’t cleared to play. He will look to return in Week 10 against the Bears. The Giants are down multiple starters this week, making them a strong matchup for Mac Jones, who is a solid QB2 option in Superflex leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jevon-holl.headline: Giants declared S Jevón Holland, WR Jalin Hyatt, CB Paulson Adebo, T James Hudson III, DL Chauncey Golston, OL Evan Neal, and QB Jameis Winston inactive for Week 8 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jevon-holl.analysis: Holland continues to deal with a lingering knee injury. The absence of Holland and Adebo could make for a good matchup for Jalen Hurts and the Philly pass catchers. The Eagles have been far more pass heavy than usual in recent weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jevon-holl.headline: Giants downgraded S Jevon Holland (knee) to out for Week 8 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jevon-holl.analysis: Holland’s absence is big news for a Giants team also without cornerback Paulson Adebo. The fantasy upside of DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert continues to grow as Sunday approaches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jevon-holl.headline: Giants K Graham Gano (groin) is questionable to play in Week 8 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jevon-holl.analysis: Gano was designated to return from injured reserve earlier this week, and he promisingly practiced in full three times since then. Giants fill-in K Jude McAtamney converted just 2-of-4 extra point attempts last week. Getting Gano back would be a plus for the G-Men. The Giants will be getting back starting C John Michael Schmitz, who has been sidelined since the Giants faced the Eagles in Week 6. Giants S Jevon Holland (neck) is doubtful.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jevon-holl.headline: Giants EDGE Brian Burns (hip) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jevon-holl.analysis: Defensive backs Paulson Adebo and Jevon Holland were also held out of practice. The good news is that Burns, who has nine sacks this season, told reporters he fully expects to play on Sunday. Barring a surprise, the NFL’s sack-leader will be ready to face the Eagles by kickoff.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jevon-holl.headline: Giants agree to terms with S Jevon Holland, formerly of the Dolphins, on a three-year, $45 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jevon-holl.analysis: Holland will get $30 million guaranteed. The former second round pick out of Oregon is known for his physical play and should be an impactful addition to a revamped New York defense that last year allowed the ninth most yards and the 11th most points. Pro Football Focus graded the Giants coverage unit as the seventh worst in the NFL in 2024. Holland, 25, had five interceptions and 301 tackles over his four years in Miami.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jevon-holl.headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano reports that the Panthers will be “seeking big-name players in free agency,” particularly on defense.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jevon-holl.analysis: Graziano suggests the Panthers “might be one of the teams willing to spend big to lure defensive tackle Milton Williams away from the Super Bowl champion Eagles.” The Panthers will also attempt to bolster their edge rush and Graziano lists Saints defensive end Chase Young as an “intriguing option.” Adding Williams and Young to a defensive line featuring Derrick Brown and Jadeveon Clowney could help turn around Carolina’s dire 2024 defense. Safeties Jevon Holland and Camryn Bynum are also reportedly on the Panthers’ short list of preferred defenders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jevon-holl.headline: Dolphins are not expected to place the franchise tag on S Jevon Holland.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jevon-holl.analysis: Holland is on track to hit free agency as one of the top safeties on the market without a franchise tag. The Dolphins have seemingly declined to use the $19.6 million tag, a number that would have put Holland between Antoine Winfield Jr. and Derwin James among the highest paid safeties in the league. Instead, the Dolphins will have a chance to negotiate a long-term deal with Holland as he also tests free agent waters. Expect the 24-year-old to get a contract near the top of the market.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed (hip) is not on the Seahawks’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: The Seahawks’ sporadic producer will be on the field against the Chiefs this week. Shaheed has been involved as a receiver and as a rusher, scoring touchdowns in consecutive weeks. He offers a low floor, but he makes for a viable FLEX starter this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed (hip) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed will be good to go for the Seahawks’ Week 7 game against the Chiefs, barring a setback. Unfortunately, his terribly volatile performances keep him in the boom-bust FLEX tier despite four teams being on bye. For what it’s worth, this could be a fantasy-friendly game environment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed (hip) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed was heavily involved in the Seahawks’ high-volume passing game in Week 6. He seemingly came out of the week banged-up and will open this week as a limited practice participant. Shaheed competes with Cooper Kupp for the No. 2 pass-catching role on the team but is only a boom-or-bust option for deep leagues at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed caught 5-of-8 targets for 66 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 6 loss to the Broncos, adding two yards on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed’s eight targets were a product of 51 Sam Darnold pass attempts in a game the Seahawks could not find any room to run on the ground. He lost a fumble on a fluke play in the second quarter in which he rolled over the tackling defender, only for the defender’s knee to knock the football loose before Shaheed’s rear end touched the playing surface. he would fumble a punt return in the fourth quarter but easily had time to regain control before the ball was in real trouble. Shaheed remains the third option through the air for an offense typically not seeing this level of volume, making him a touchdown-or-bust fantasy option, for the time being. That doesn’t change ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Chiefs in Seattle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed caught 1-of-3 targets for 20 yards and rushed twice for 33 yards and a touchdown in the Seahawks’ Week 4 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: It wasn’t a ton of volume, but it was easily Shaheed’s biggest offensive day of the year. He took a pitch for a touchdown for his first score of 2026. He was once again not involved in the passing game, however, and he didn’t do much as a returner again, as well. Shaheed will be back in action — and should not be in lineups — against the 49ers in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed caught 2-of-3 targets for 14 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 3 loss to the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Once again, Shaheed didn’t make an impact, with his biggest play being a drop that resulted in a first down because of a questionable personal foul after the play. The 28-year-old also hasn’t made an impact on special teams, and while his big-play ability is almost assuredly still there, fantasy managers can’t count on it right now. A chance to get going comes in Week 4 versus the Chargers at home.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed caught 3-of-6 targets for 35 yards in the Seahawks’ Week 2 win over the Cardinals, adding one rush for four yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: The Seahawks tried to get Shaheed involved early on, but he largely made his presence felt on special teams, returning two kicks for 47 yards and three punts for 29 yards. Shaheed was unable to haul in his first target on the Seahawks’ second drive. He got open on a post route from the slot on the ensuing drive, and QB Drew Lock hit him for a 23-yard gain. He caught a four-yard pass in the flats immediately after that. Later, on the sixth drive, Lock fired a pass at Shaheed 34 yards downfield, but the coverage defender grazed the ball, altering the trajectory and leading to an incompletion that went off Shaheed’s fingertips. Shaheed also fumbled the second half’s opening kick return, but Seattle recovered it and advanced the ball 30 yards downfield. Shaheed remains a big-play-dependent FLEX against the Commanders next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Rashid Shaheed caught 1-of-3 targets for four yards in the Seahawks’ Week 1 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Shaheed caught multiple passes in 4-of-12 games as a Seahawk last year. He stayed the course in Week 1 with another single-catch outing. Shaheed simply can’t earn targets in an offense that revolves around getting Jaxon Smith-Njigba the ball at all levels. His versatility and elite skills on both punt and kick returns are valuable for the Seahawks in real life, but they don’t put fantasy points on the table. He is not on the FLEX menu headed into Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: The Athletic’s Andrew Destin believes WR Rashid Shaheed “could very well usurp” WR Cooper Kupp as the No. 2 receiving option.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Destin echoes what ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler forecasted late in June. It’s nice to know that training camp performances have not altered expectations. Whether Shaheed can be more than a big-play-based FLEX option remains to be seen, but his ADP is hardly prohibitive. Stashing him on benches in Weeks 1-2 while monitoring his usage is a fairly low-risk move, though he is not a priority add.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said WR Tory Horton’s (undisclosed) “injury isn’t a long-term thing.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashid-sha.analysis: Frankly, it is tough to trust this statement. The Seahawks kept things quiet almost all offseason about Horton’s season-ending shin injury. They do not have to disclose anything until Week 1 practices begin. Were he to miss time in the regular season, WR Rashid Shaheed might be able to earn an extra target or two, operating as the team’s uncontested field stretcher.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: Donaldson is the third member of the Saints’ backfield committee. While he will get a few touches this week, he is not getting enough work for fantasy relevance.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: The pass-protecting back looks likely to continue to mix in and limit snaps for the fantasy-valuable members of the backfield in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: A limited practice to start the week is usually maintenance. Donaldson looked good last week, running for 39 yards on six attempts, though he did commit one fumble. Donaldson is one of three backs seeing work for the Saints, and none of them have made a strong case to get more touches. Donaldson is a weak FLEX option for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson rushed six times for 39 yards and a fumble in the Saints’ Week 6 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: A messy Saints committee backfield had Donaldson get the second-most snaps among New Orleans running backs against the Giants. He and Alvin Kamara were the passing-down backs while Donaldson also had a 17-yard run, the longest run by a Saints running back on the day. His first-career touchdown was called back in the third quarter after he was ruled down just shy of the goal line. The 22-year-old rookie has had a surprisingly high utilization early in the season and will continue to be involved while Travis Etienne is out. Despite this, his fantasy impact will mainly be to dilute Kamara and Kendre Miller’s fantasy values. Donaldson should only be rostered in the deepest of leagues heading into Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: CJ Donaldson rushed four times for 13 yards in the Saints’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings, adding one catch for seven yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: Alvin Kamara entered this game with a back injury and played just eight snaps in the second half, freeing up some extra work for Donaldson. He led the team in snaps, but Kendre Miller was the top option between the tackles, seeing 10 carries, one of which went for a touchdown. Even if Kamara remains on the injury report for Week 6, Donaldson won’t crack the FLEX rankings versus the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: Kamara briefly left the Saints’ Week 4 game against the Falcons to deal with a knee injury. Today, he is sidelined by a back injury. It’s perhaps unsurprising for a 31-year-old player who has clearly lost a step at this point in his career. He is backed up by Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson. Either player can be stashed in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: Saints placed Travis Etienne on injured reserve with a hamstring injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: This is a tough break. The Saints’ high-priced free agent signee will be sidelined for at least four games. Their Week 8 bye makes him eligible to return in Week 9. Veteran RB Alvin Kamara is the next man up, followed by RB Kendre Miller. Both should be rostered in 12-team leagues. Kamara will likely get the first crack at the starting job, but he has struggled to play efficiently this season, and coach Kellen Moore gave RB CJ Donaldson the backfield’s first green zone touch last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: Saints RB Travis Etienne exited Week 3 against the Raiders after suffering an apparent hamstring injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: Etienne entered the game with a hamstring injury and appears to have aggravated it on an explosive run. The Saints’ starting running back broke off a 16-yard gain in the third quarter, setting up a Saints passing touchdown on the following play. Etienne could be seen grabbing at his left hamstring at the end of the run. He had mostly been limited to modest single-digit gains before that, rushing 13 times for 57 yards and catching 2-of-2 targets for 13 yards on the day. He seems highly unlikely to return. Etienne and the other veteran running backs notably ceded the first backfield touch inside the green zone to RB CJ Donaldson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: Saints RB Kendre Miller (back) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: The good news is that Miller was not listed with a knee injury after suffering a season-ending ACL tear in Week 7 last year. The bad news is that he evidently has a new injury, and the Saints have a fairly deep running back room right now. RBs Devin Neal, Audric Estime, Ty Chandler and CJ Donaldson are all vying for roster spots. Per Underhill, Neal is taking advantage of the extra reps. He could have the inside track to the RB3 role right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.headline: Saints signed Ohio State RB CJ Donaldson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-donalds.analysis: Donaldson (6’2”/230) burst on the scene as a true freshman at West Virginia, rushing for 87-526-6 in seven games before a leg injury ended his season. Donaldson was recruited as a three-star tight end before moving to RB during training camp and quickly cemented himself as the starter for the Mountaineers. He rushed for 421-2,058-30 in three seasons before transferring to Ohio State last season. With the Buckeyes, Donaldson managed just 96 carries in 13 games, rushing for 361 yards and 10 scores while averaging a paltry 3.8 YPC. Despite his prowess as a former tight end, Donaldson has never been much of a factor in the passing game, catching just 47 passes for 286 yards in four seasons. Despite his size, Donaldson struggled mightily after contact, posting a 2.99 yards after contact per attempt for his career, and averaging 2.92 YCO/ATT or less in each of his final three seasons. He totaled just 24 carries of 15 or more yards in his career, and may not have much to offer outside of a short-yardage/goal-line role. His larger body of work leaves much to be desired. He’ll need a strong camp if he hopes to stick on the end of a roster. The Saints also signed DT Keeshawn Silver.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.headline: Landon Dickerson (knee/pectoral) was limited on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.analysis: Dickerson injured a pectoral muscle on Thursday, complicating his knee-related return from injured reserve. He is firmly in the questionable camp at this time. Eagles C Drew Kendall (knee) was upgraded to full participation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.headline: Landon Dickerson (knee/pectoral) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.analysis: Eagles C Drew Kendall (knee) was also limited. Both players were listed as questionable to play in Week 6 against the Panthers. Neither player was able to suit up. Beginning the week with limited sessions is promising. The Eagles face the Cowboys on Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.headline: Drew Kendall (knee) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.analysis: Kendall, the Eagles’ starting center, and LG Landon Dickerson (knee) were both limited on Friday, resulting in questionable game tags. Dickerson remains on injured reserve. The team would need to activate him, if he is going to play. Eagles EDGE Jonathan Greenard (ankle) was cleared to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.headline: Drew Kendall (knee) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.analysis: The Eagles’ starting center now has a chance to play in Week 6 against the Panthers. Eagles LG Landon Dickerson (knee) was also limited again, as was EDGE Jonathan Greenard (ankle).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.headline: Eagles activated LG Landon Dickerson’s (knee) 21-day practice window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.analysis: The Eagles desperately need offensive line health. Dickerson’s return cannot come soon enough. New Eagles C Drew Kendall (knee) was not seen practicing today, though Dickerson has officially resumed practicing in some capacity, which is great news. He was seen taking the field with his teammates this afternoon. The Eagles also opened DB Jakorian Bennett, TE Grant Calcaterra and TE Eli Stowers’ (hamstring/quad) practice windows.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.headline: Eagles placed G Landon Dickerson (knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.analysis: It’s about the worst-case scenario for an offense with no shortage of change in 2026, with new offensive coordinator Sean Mannion now hit with a substantial blow to his front five. The news comes on the heels of a close Week 1 victory over the divisional rival Commanders, a game that played much closer than expected. Time will tell if Dickerson makes it back to previous form in what could be his final professional season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.headline: Eagles G Landon Dickerson told reporters he didn’t consider retiring this offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.analysis: Dickerson, a second-round pick in the 2021 NFL Draft, denied reports that he considered retirement this offseason. “I’m not sure where you guys got that from,” he said. Dickerson, who turns 28 in September, said he’s not really concerned about the toll playing takes on his body. He also admitted he “probably shouldn’t have went out and played” last season after needing meniscus surgery so close to the start of Week 1. Dickerson’s rethinking his approach to pushing through injuries as he has in the past.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.headline: Eagles and LG Landon Dickerson agreed to a reworked contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.analysis: Per ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, Dickerson was set to make $39 million over the next two seasons. That number is down to $36 million, though he can recoup the lost $3 million via 2027 incentives. Dickerson’s contract was previously set to expire in 2028. He is now only under contract through 2027. It’s a relatively minor pay cut for the veteran lineman, and hitting the open market a year earlier could ultimately work in his favor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo believes Landon Dickerson is “no certainty to return” to the Eagles in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.analysis: Dickerson is just 27, but struggled through a challenging season in 2025 with two missed games while struggling through several games with ankle and quad injuries. He didn’t look right from the jump. Lane Johnson is another retirement possibility for the Eagles, and The Philadelphia Inquirer’s Jeff McLane believes Johnson isn’t sure his body will hold up and he’s “not sure if he’s coming back or not.” The Eagles are set up for plenty of turnover on the offensive side of the ball this offseason and likely will need to target picks on the offensive line even if Dickerson and Johnson return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.headline: Eagles declared LB Nakobe Dean, S Marcus Epps, OLB Jaelan Phillips, RT Lane Johnson, LG Landon Dickerson, TE Dallas Goedert, and DT Jalen Carter inactive for Week 18 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/landon-dic.analysis: The Eagles are resting several of their banged-up starters ahead of a Week 18 showdown against the Commanders. The Eagles have already won the division while the Commanders are already eliminated, so this game will see many reserves play snaps. Expect the bulk of the Eagles’ inactive starters to be back for the playoffs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks has been banged up for weeks, and the Philadelphia Inquirer’s Jeff McLane said Wicks might miss the Eagles’ Week 7 game against the Cowboys. Hopefully, he resumes practicing tomorrow. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks swaps out his multi-week hamstring injury for an ankle injury. He managed to play through it in Week 6 against the Panthers after meeting with the training staff. We expect him to face the Cowboys on Monday night, but he is just a boom-bust FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks caught 2-of-4 targets for 24 yards in the Eagles’ Week 6 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks wasn’t much of a factor in this one. Tanner McKee seemed far more comfortable throwing to DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert, which left few targets for Wicks. Initial reports have Wicks playing on 40 of the team’s 64 snaps and running a route on 32 of their 52 dropbacks, which was actually fewer than Makai Lemon and only five more than Darius Cooper. Some of that could be because Wicks grabbed at his ankle and left the field after a tackle in the second half. He was able to return to the game later in the half, but he missed a few plays while being tended to by trainers. With McKee at quarterback, it’s hard to trust Wicks in fantasy, regardless of matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Apparently, Wicks’ day off on Thursday was only a rest day. The Eagles’ veteran wide receiver was limited on Wednesday and practiced fully today. Wicks played through the injury last week, posting a 5/63 receiving line with DeVonta Smith sidelined. Smith is back this week. Wicks is a boom-bust FLEX starter, catching passes thrown by backup Tanner McKee.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks played through the hamstring injury in Week 5 and may have made it worse. Downgrading to a DNP on Thursday is a bad sign. He is unlikely to play at this time, and if active, he would be prone to re-injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks suffered the hamstring injury in practice last week but played through the injury in the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jaguars. Also limited was Hollywood Brown (ankle). Brown has not played since suffering an ankle injury in Week 2 but has a chance to return this week. Expect Wicks to play in Week 6 while Brown is truly questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks caught 5-of-8 targets for 63 yards in the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: DeVonta Smith was out again this week, leaving the Eagles to spread his targets around to several role players. Wicks led the team’s wideouts in targets, but it was Dallas Goedert who paced the team. On the back of one long touchdown catch, Darius Cooper led the team in receiving yards. Wicks is good for the occasional big play but isn’t a consistent enough player to be a solid fantasy option. He will be a deep FLEX option for Week 6 versus the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) is not on Philadelphia’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: He only got in a limited session today, but apparently that was all the Eagles needed to see. He’ll still be a tough start against Jacksonville in what is projected to be a low-scoring game as Philadelphia’s passing offense looks to rebound from last week’s rough showing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) was added to the injury report on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks was listed as a limited participant today, indicating that he strained his hamstring during Thursday’s practice. With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) still sidelined, rookie WR Makai Lemon could be the de facto top receiver, though the team has struggled to use him effectively thus far. Hollywood Brown (ankle) also remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.headline: Dontayvion Wicks caught 3-of-5 targets for 18 yards in the Eagles’ Week 4 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dontayvion.analysis: Wicks was in theory the Eagles’ No. 1 receiver with DeVonta Smith (hamstring) sidelined, but in reality he does not really have a “scaleable” skill-set. It wasn’t surprising Wicks and Jalen Hurts failed to get anything going down the field with the Rams constantly in Hurts’ grill in rainy conditions. Smith seems to be looking at a multi-week absence, but Wicks will be hard-pressed to rise above WR4 status in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendal-dan.headline: Kendal Daniels (neck) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendal-dan.analysis: Daniels was taken off the field on a stretcher last week, but managed to practice in full to begin the week. Daniels, a rookie, has 23 tackles, three quarterback pressures and one sack this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendal-dan.headline: Kendal Daniels (neck) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendal-dan.analysis: Daniels was carted off the field on a stretcher in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears. It was a scary scene that paused the game for around fifteen minutes as Daniels’ neck was stabilized after he hit his head while attempting to make a tackle. Fortunately, the rookie appears to be okay as he appeared in practice as a full participant on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendal-dan.headline: Kendal Daniels was taken off the field on a stretcher in Week 6 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendal-dan.analysis: It was an ugly scene that saw the game paused for nearly fifteen minutes while medics tended to the rookie linebacker after he hit his head during a tackle attempt. It was unclear whether Daniels was able to move his extremities before exiting the field. We would expect Daniels to miss significant time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Budda Baker (groin/illness) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: Baker practiced in a limited capacity on Friday, and the veteran safety is no stranger to playing through injuries. The Cardinals ruled out DL Walter Nolen (ankle) and S Andrew Wingard (knee). Cardinals CB Garrett Williams (knee) has been cleared to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Budda Baker (groin/illness) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: Baker played through the groin injury in Week 6 but starts out this week not practicing due to both the groin injury and an illness. Also not practicing for the Cardinals defense were DL Walter Nolen (ankle), S Andrew Wingard (knee), and CB Garrett Williams (knee). Each player will likely need to practice in some capacity in order to play in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Budda Baker (groin) is active in Week 6 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: Baker and EDGE Zaven Collins (hip) were both added to the Cardinals’ injury report on Friday. Neither player practiced that day, but both are evidently good to go for this divisional showdown against the Rams (2-3). The Cardinals (1-4) are road underdogs, but this game should be a fantasy-friendly environment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Budda Baker (groin) is questionable for Arizona’s Week 6 game against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: It was a pop-up DNP for Baker on Friday after he had initially been listed as NIR-Rest on Wednesday. Ominous. Baker stands a real chance at missing Sunday’s game and throwing the Cardinals defense into (checking notes) further chaos against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Cardinals HC Jonathan Gannon said Budda Baker (concussion) will not play in Week 17 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: Baker entered the league’s concussion protocol earlier this week after going down in Week 16’s game against the Falcons. The star safety will miss at least one game due to his brain injury, with backup safety Kitan Crawford looking like the next man up to fill his role. In addition to Baker, the Cardinals also ruled out LT Paris Johnson (knee), and CB Kei’Tre Clark (knee) for Week 17.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Cardinals S Budda Baker entered the NFL’s concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: Baker was evaluated for a brain injury in Week 16 against the Falcons but re-entered the game, only to report concussion-like symptoms on Wednesday. Baker is likely to sit out this week against the Bengals, creating an even better matchup for Joe Burrow and the Bengals pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Cardinals S Budda Baker returned to Week 16 against the Falcons after being evaluated for a concussion.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: Baker remained down after making a tackle and took a minute to make his way to the sideline. After meeting with the training staff on the sideline, he jogged to the locker room for the concussion evaluation. After a short time, he was able to return to the game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Cardinals S Budda Baker (hamstring) is active for Week 10 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: Baker was limited through most of the week in practice but will suit up against Seattle after practicing in full on Friday. Cardinals declared OT Josh Fryar, OT Demontrey Jacobs, CB Will Johnson, CB Max Melton, DT Bilal Nichols, WR Xavier Weaver, and LB Mack Wilson inactive against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Cardinals CB Will Johnson (back/hip) will not play in Arizona’s Week 10 game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: Neither will (inhale): CB Max Melton (concussion), LB BJ Ojulari (knee), or LB Mack Wilson (ribs) — the good news is that Budda Baker (hamstring) upgraded to full today and has been removed from the injury report. Arizona’s defense looked good against the Cowboys on Monday night, but their cornerback depth will be tested against Jaxson Smith-Njigba and Rashid Shaheed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.headline: Cardinals trained were seen examining WR Michael Wilson (head) and S Budda Baker (shin) after the two players collided in practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/budda-bake.analysis: Per AZ Central Sports’ Theo Mackie, Baker appeared to pass his exam and attempted to resume practicing before DC Nick Rallis talked him out of it. Wilson left the field with training staffers and will undergo further examination.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-elli.headline: Broncos ruled out Jonah Elliss (ankle) for Week 7 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-elli.analysis: Reporting from earlier this week indicates Ellis could be sidelined for a few weeks. Broncos S Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) was also ruled out this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-elli.headline: Jonah Elliss (leg) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-elli.analysis: Elliss suffered a lower-leg injury on his right leg in Week 6. Broncos head coach Sean Payton said Wednesday that the injury is not season-ending, but did not rule out a stint on injured reserve. Either way, it sounds like Elliss will miss Week 7 and potentially more.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-elli.headline: Broncos ruled out CB Pat Surtain II (pec) for Week 11 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-elli.analysis: Surtain has been out since injuring his pec in Week 8. The Broncos will also be without LB Alex Singleton, who recently underwent a successful procedure to remove a tumor, and LB Jonah Elliss (hamstring). These are tough losses for a defense tasked with containing the Chiefs’ offense, but the unit as a whole remains strong.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-elli.headline: Broncos selected Utah EDGE Jonah Elliss with the No. 76 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-elli.analysis: Elliss (6’2/248) followed in the footsteps of his father, Luther, who also attended Utah and is a former first-round draft pick of the Detroit Lions. A former high school track athlete who ran a personal best 11.41s 100 meters, he saw consistent rotational snaps at LB as a true freshman before slotting into the starting lineup at EDGE in 2022. Elliss had a nondescript start after acclimating to the position change but finished strong, recording 18 of his 25 pressures and all three of his sacks over his last five games. He made the leap in 2023 by finishing second nationally with 12.0 sacks despite playing in just 10 games before sustaining a season-ending injury. Slightly undersized with a frenetic rush style, Elliss gets off the ball in a flash and attacks his opponents with expansive 10.5-inch hands so he can shed and make secondary effort plays. He is an unrelenting motor with a varied moveset but is likely ill-equipped for edge-setting duty against NFL-sized left tackles and needs to work on his counters. Elliss will likely see action on passing downs early on but could eventually work his way into a starting role if things break right.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.headline: Pat Surtain (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.analysis: Surtain never managed to practice in full this week. Keeping him sidelined until he is able to do so could make sense. The 4-2 Broncos are currently second in the AFC West. They face the 5-0 Chiefs in Week 8. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.headline: Pat Surtain (ankle) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.analysis: NFL on Prime’s James Palmer reported last week that Surtain was likely to return for the Broncos’ Week 8 game against the Chiefs, rather than face the Cardinals in Week 7. Given Surtain’s multi-week absence, and Palmer’s reporting, we expect to see Surtain listed as a limited participant on the final injury report. Whether he returns in time for the Cardinals’ game remains to be seen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.headline: NFL on Prime’s James Palmer reports that returning in Week 8 against the Chiefs is more likely for Pat Surtain (ankle) than in Week 7 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.analysis: Palmer also clarified that Surtain did not suffer a non-contact injury, as has been reported previously. Surtain apparently injured his ankle two plays before he exited the Broncos’ Week 5 game against the 49ers. The Broncos might be able to get by without Surtain next week, but getting him back before facing Patrick Mahomes would be huge.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.headline: Riley Moss (ribs) is questionable for the Broncos’ Week 6 game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.analysis: Moss missed Week 5 due to a rib injury but has a chance to return Thursday against the Seahawks after three straight limited practices this week. CB Patrick Surtain (ankle) and S Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) did not practice all week and were ruled out, as expected.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.headline: Broncos CB Patrick Surtain (ankle) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.analysis: Neither Surtain or Riley Moss (ribs) practiced on Wednesday. Head coach Sean Payton said the Broncos don’t anticipate placing Surtain on injured reserve. The injuries to both corners look to be shorter-term; Surtain is week-to-week while Moss’ return timeline is not disclosed yet. Both are on the wrong side of questionable for Week 5 against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Broncos CB Patrick Surtain (ankle) is “week-to-week” with one source bracing for him to miss “about two weeks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.analysis: It sounds like this is overall good news for the Broncos, but their defense will take a major short-term hit without one of the best corners in the league. The Broncos, who also lost Riley Moss to a rib injury against the 49ers, will probably have to change some things up next week against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Patrick Surtain’s ankle injury is not believed to be season-ending.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.analysis: According to Rapoport, there are no longer any concerns that this is an Achilles injury for Surtain, who left Week 4’s game against the 49ers with a non-contact injury. Surtain could be looking at a multi-week absence and will undergo an MRI soon to confirm the severity of his injury, but it sounds like he avoided anything too serious. In addition to Surtain, the Broncos are also evaluating the status of CB Riley Moss, who is dealing with a rib injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.headline: Broncos ruled out Pat Surtain (ankle) in Week 4 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.analysis: Surtain went down with a lower leg injury late in the second half and needed help getting to the Denver locker room. It was a non-contact injury. The Broncos also lost starting corner Riley Moss. Extended absences for Moss and Surtain would make the Broncos vulnerable to most opposing passing attacks, including the Chargers in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.headline: Pat Surtain exited Week 4 against the 49ers with an apparent leg injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.analysis: Surtain went down with a non-contact injury late in the second quarter and needed help getting the the Denver locker room. He was seen grabbing at his calf and foot area. Hopefully for the Broncos this injury is not a worst-case scenario for one of the NFL’s best cover corners. Brock Purdy and the Niners should have an easier time moving the ball if Surtain is sidelined for the remainder of this game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.headline: Broncos restructured CB Pat Surtain’s contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-surtai.analysis: He gets a $5 million raise this year and has a chance to make $5 million more next year if he makes the Pro Bowl or All-Pro teams. The “good player pay bump” is getting more and more common in NFL circles. Surtain has been on one of the two All-Pro teams in three of his first five seasons in the NFL, so there’s a good shot he makes it again this year if he stays healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-badi.headline: Broncos ruled out Tyler Badie (thumb) for Week 7
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-badi.analysis: Badie is likely headed toward a demotion with Jonah Coleman (ankle) inching toward a return. The latter player is questionable to play this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-badi.headline: Jonah Coleman (ankle) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-badi.analysis: Coleman is trending toward returning for the Broncos’ Week 7 game against the Cardinals. His teammate, RB Tyler Badie (thumb), remains sidelined. Coleman makes for a risky start if active, but the Broncos’ coaching staff likes him. He should be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-badi.headline: Tyler Badie (thumb) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-badi.analysis: Badie was a non-participant in practice with a thumb injury. With Jonah Coleman designated to return from injured reserve, Badie does not need to be rostered for fantasy purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-badi.headline: Tyler Badie had two rushes for seven yards in the Broncos’ Week 4 loss to the 49ers, adding two catches for 32 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-badi.analysis: Badie was again the team’s RB3 behind JK Dobbins and RJ Harvey. Harvey led the backfield with ten catches on ten targets while Dobbins had a team-leading 11 carries. Badie would be somewhat interesting in deeper leagues if Harvey were to miss more time this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-badi.headline: Tyler Badie had one rush for one yard in the Broncos’ Week 2 win against the Jaguars, adding two catches for 28 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-badi.analysis: Badie saw significant action in this one after JK Dobbins exited the contest with a hamstring injury. RJ Harvey was inactive with his own hamstring issue, leaving Badie in the Harvey role and rookie RB Jonah Coleman as the primary early-down option for OC Davis Webb. If Dobbins and Harvey are sidelined next week against the Rams, Badie would have some usefulness in deeper PPR formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-badi.headline: Broncos declared RB Tyler Badie, DT Tyler Onyedim, TE Dallen Bentley, OL Kage Casey, DL Jordan Jackson, and QB Sam Ehlinger inactive for Week 1 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-badi.analysis: Badie’s inclusion on the Week 1 inactives list means rookie Jonah Coleman gets the nod as the RB3 behind J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey. It remains unlikely Coleman contributes meaningful counting stats in his first professional appearance, but the fact he is now confirmed to be ahead of Badie is meaningful to his longterm upside in what should be one of the top rushing attacks in the league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-badi.headline: The Denver Post’s Luca Evans believes Tyler Badie and Jaleel McLaughlin are battling for one roster spot in training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-badi.analysis: Badie probably has the edge given his versatility on special teams and third-down work. McLaughlin’s path to a roster spot “looks dicey” per Evans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-badi.headline: Broncos re-signed exclusive rights free agent Tyler Badie to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-badi.analysis: That will make at least one more season of Badie cutting into RJ Harvey’s workload on third down. Badie played on 223 snaps in 2025 and the Broncos passed on 207 of them. Expect some catches, is what we’re saying.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-badi.headline: Broncos ruled out RB J.K. Dobbins (foot) for the AFC Championship Game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-badi.analysis: Dobbins is not yet ready to resume playing. He remained limited throughout all three practices this week after the Broncos opened his 21-day practice window on Monday. With Dobbins out, rookie RB RJ Harvey will again lead the backfield. He totaled 11 touches last week. Broncos RB Jaleel McLaughlin handled four and RB Tyler Badie had one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-badi.headline: Jaleel McLaughlin rushed six times for 41 yards in the Broncos’ Week 18 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-badi.analysis: McLaughlin also chipped in a 17-yard reception by forcing a missed tackle after securing a checkdown pass from QB Bo Nix before scampering down the right sideline. The rotational back ran very efficiently and even brought the ball into scoring position on the opening drive with a 10-yard gain from the Chargers’ 16-yard line. Fellow Broncos RB Tyler Badie rushed twice for minus-two yards and caught 2-of-2 targets for 28 yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) is not on the Broncos’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle upgraded to full on Friday after logging two limited sessions to begin the week. The Broncos’ No. 1 wide receiver has struggled to deliver usable stat lines with Bo Nix intent on checking down. The Cardinals’ pass defense could facilitate a bounce-back game for Waddle, but he remains a WR3/FLEX at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: The Broncos’ big-name offseason acquisition has totaled more than 35 yards just once all year, and now he has a chest injury. Waddle is on track to play, and he faces a beatable Cardinals pass defense this week, but he can only be treated as a FLEX starter at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (chest) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle briefly exited the Broncos’ Week 6 win over the Seahawks before returning to the game. He now pops up on the practice report as a limited participant on Wednesday with a chest injury. Waddle is not in jeopardy of missing time just yet, but his poor fantasy production to start the season makes him a volatile fantasy option for Week 7 against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (shoulder) returned to the game in the fourth quarter of Week 6 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle departed in the third quarter and was deemed questionable to return with a shoulder injury but made his way back to the field in the fourth quarter, catching two additional passes in the final frame. He ended with four receptions for 24 yards on seven targets and has quickly become a difficult weekly start in fantasy circles. An enticing matchup against the Cardinals in Week 7 is sure to give fantasy managers a hint of potential, but if he fails again to return a usable fantasy week, it might be time to reconsider entering him in weekly lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (shoulder) is questionable to return to Week 6 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle departed early in the third quarter and was quickly deemed questionable to return with a shoulder injury. It is unclear when the injury occurred. Waddle managed to catch just 2-of-5 targets for 15 yards prior to departing, keeping his usable weeks total at just two games through the first six weeks of the 2026 season. Fantasy managers that invested a fourth-round pick on the veteran wide receiver have got to begin to make alternate plans at wide receiver moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle caught 2-of-5 targets for 19 yards in the Broncos’ Week 5 win over the Chargers while adding a nine-yard rush.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Give some credit to the Chargers’ defense, but this was an ugly game for both passing attacks. Waddle has his second dud in three weeks, and doesn’t appear to have great chemistry with Bo Nix thus far. No one really does, to be fair, as no receiver caught more than four passes for Denver. Waddle is a volatile WR2, and that volatility becomes more, well, volatile for Week 6 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle caught 5-of-6 targets for 35 yards and a touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 4 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle was invisible for much of the game until a late red zone touchdown with the Broncos in up-tempo catch-up mode. It was his first touchdown reception as a Bronco. Waddle, who now has three down games in his first four contests as the Broncos’ nominal WR1, will probably struggle until Denver OC Davis Webb figures out how to maximize his personnel, including the struggling Bo Nix. Against the 49ers Waddle was targeted on a meager 16 percent of his routes. Hopefully that rate will rise in Week 5 against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle (foot) is not on the injury report for Week 4 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle gave folks a fright, sporting a walking boot after the Broncos’ Week 3 win over the Rams. He practiced in full all week, though, so there are no concerns about his availability. Waddle is a WR2 against the 49ers in what should be a fantasy-friendly game environment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: Jaylen Waddle is practicing in full for Week 4 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle was spotted in a boot after Week 3’s win over the Rams. DNVR’s Zac Stevens reported at the time that he was fine and can comfortably take a victory lap now that Payton has said he practiced in full. Waddle posted a dud in Week 3 with two catches for 10 yards, but he ripped off 138 yards the week before that. The production might come in peaks and valleys, but fantasy managers should hold the line and treat him like a WR2 for a potential shootout with the 49ers this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.headline: The Denver Post’s Sam Jane reports Broncos WR Jaylen Waddle is “fine” after he was spotted in a walking boot following the Broncos’ Week 3 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-wad.analysis: Waddle was spotted in a walking boot after the Broncos’ Sunday night win, prompting speculation over his status. Jane reports that Waddle is “fine” while beat reporter Zac Stevens said a source told him “there’s nothing wrong” with the 27-year-old wideout. The boot certainly could have been a precautionary measure but we will wait for Wednesday’s practice report to find out if Waddle is truly dealing with an injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Drew Lock (right elbow) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: The Seahawks’ backup quarterback is dealing with an injury in his throwing arm, so any calls for Sam Darnold’s benching will have to quiet down. Seahawks S Nick Emmanwori (hip), LB DeMarcus Lawrence (knee) and LB Uchenna Nwosu (hip) are questionable. The Seahawks ruled out Chazz Surratt (calf) and LB DrakeThomas (ankle).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Sam Darnold’s starting quarterback job is not in jeopardy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: The Seahawks’ head coach stood by his quarterback today, saying Darnold is “definitely part of the solution” to the offense’s recent struggles. Darnold returned somewhat quickly from a glute tendon strain a couple of weeks ago. One wonders if he is still rounding back into form following the early-season ailment. Backup Drew Lock played well in his stead, but the Seahawks believe their Super Bowl-winning quarterback should keep his job. That makes sense to us. He’s a QB2 next week against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said QB Sam Darnold (glute) will resume practicing, but won’t take every rep on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: This means Darnold will likely be listed as a limited participant today. The plan is to ramp him up as the week goes on, and Macdonald said the team would like to have a decision by Friday on whether Darnold will face the Commanders this week. The Seahawks’ quarterback has been sidelined since straining a glute tendon in Week 1. He will probably need to be treated as a QB2 with QB1 upside in his first game back, but his practice participation will clarify his readiness.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Seahawks QB Sam Darnold (glute) “has a chance” to play in Week 3 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: To be clear, Rapoport’s tone was controlled and cautionary here. Darnold can only be considered questionable, at best. The Seahawks’ quarterback “is healing faster than anyone had imagined,” but Rapoport adds that the team wants to be “cautious” with him. Backup QB Drew Lock should probably be viewed as the presumptive Week 3 starter at this time, but it sounds like Darnold can reasonably be expected to play in Week 4 at the latest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Seahawks HC Mike Macdonald said Sam Darnold (glute) is on track to practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: FOX Sports’ Megan Olivi reported on Sunday that the Seahawks “are aiming” to have Darnold play in Week 3 against the Commanders. It goes without saying that Darnold will need to get a few days of practice in if he hopes to suit up, making this a big week for the Seahawks’ QB1 as he looks to get back on the field. Darnold’s injury wasn’t as severe as the team initially feared when he exited in Week 1 against the Patriots, but with a game against the 0-2 Commanders on the horizon, it’s possible the team doesn’t look to rush him back to the field if he’s not close to 100 percent. His practice status will be worth monitoring throughout the week, but if he’s held out, Drew Lock will make at least one more start in what should be a plus matchup for fantasy managers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Drew Lock completed 19-of-26 passes for 235 yards and three touchdowns in the Seahawks’ 31-7, Week 2 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Lock looks great, and the Seahawks aren’t asking too much of him. The fill-in starter got things going with a perfectly placed 82-yard touchdown pass to Jaxon Smith-Njigba to cap the first drive. He linked up with Smith-Njigba for two more scores as the game progressed. At one point, Lock willingly took a hard hit as he stood tall against pressure before completing a pass to his No. 1 wide receiver along the sideline, which led to a successful field goal a few plays later. The Seahawks could get QB Sam Darnold (glute) back next week, but Lock warrants streaming QB1 consideration against the Commanders if he remains the starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: FOX Sports’ Megan Olivi reports that the Seahawks “are aiming” to have QB Sam Darnold (glute) play in Week 3 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Darnold’s rehab is reportedly progressing well, but coach Mike Macdonald acknowledged to Olivi that the team just has to wait and see how Darnold responds to treatment next week. His potential Week 3 return is no sure thing, and QB Drew Lock is filling in admirably thus far. Darnold’s practice participation should provide clues as to his availability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Week 4 is the “more likely” target for Sam Darnold (glute) to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Rapoport did note that Darnold is expected to practice in some capacity next week. It sounds like the team will use next week’s sessions to give him an extended ramp-up ahead of Week 4, though a Week 3 return isn’t out of the question. Drew Lock will start this week and probably next week as well. He is in the QB2 mix for Superflex leagues, though managers without a second quarterback spot don’t need to worry about Lock for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: Seahawks ruled out Sam Darnold (glute) for Week 2 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: The Seahawks will roll with QB Drew Lock as this week’s starter. He is backed up by QB Jalen Milroe. Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said he does not “anticipate” putting Darnold on injured reserve, so he should be back before Week 6. Lock can be treated as a volatile QB2 against the Cardinals this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.headline: NBC Sports’ Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio reports that Seahawks QB Sam Darnold (glute) could miss four to six weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/drew-lock/.analysis: Prior reports described Darnold’s injury as a hip issue, and the Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reported last week that Darnold had suffered an “unusual muscle strain.” Florio cites a report from FOX Sports’ Jay Glazer from earlier today, in which Glazer said Darnold actually suffered a glute tendon injury. Evidently, the injury is so unusual that, per Glazer, the team is gathering four second opinions to determine a course of action. Darnold is not expected to require surgery, but missing four-plus weeks could land him on injured reserve. The Seahawks will not be required to make that decision until late next week, though. Regardless, Glazer said QB Drew Lock will start next week against the Cardinals. He is a QB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deejay-dal.headline: Vikings released RB Deejay Dallas.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deejay-dal.analysis: He’ll likely find his way back to the practice squad — here or elsewhere — at some point this season. This move portends that Jordan Mason will be activated for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deejay-dal.headline: Demond Claiborne rushed three times for 12 yards in the Vikings’ Week 4 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deejay-dal.analysis: Claiborne was given chances to contribute on the Vikings’ seventh and 10th drives. The rookie was unable to maximize his touches and had a catch behind the line of scrimmage that he took back to the line, negated by a holding penalty. Claiborne’s best play was an eight-yard run off the right tackle. That said, he out-touched DeeJay Dallas, who bagged only a 10-yard checkdown on the opening drive.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deejay-dal.headline: DeeJay Dallas (toe) is active for Week 3 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deejay-dal.analysis: Dallas was the only Minnesota running back besides Aaron Jones to see a backfield touch last week with Jordan Mason sidelined with injury. Dallas wouldn’t hold fantasy value unless Jones gets dinged up. Vikings declared T Caleb Tiernan, DT Elijah Williams, CB Zemaiah Vaughn, S Jakobe Thomas, S Tavierre Thomas, and P Brett Thorson inactive against the Bucs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deejay-dal.headline: Vikings RB DeeJay Dallas (toe) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deejay-dal.analysis: Dallas and starting RB Aaron Jones (knee) both practiced in full on Friday. Jones will handle the majority of the backfield’s touches while Dallas takes a few carries and plays some on passing downs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deejay-dal.headline: Vikings RB Aaron Jones (knee) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deejay-dal.analysis: Jones, 31, injured his knee in Week 2 against the Bears and sat out yesterday’s practice. The fact that he is back today puts him on track to play. He will likely be listed as a limited participant, but a full session would be unsurprising. Jones is backed up by rookie RB Demond Claiborne, who would likely handle lead back duties if Jones were to miss time, and receiving specialist RB DeeJay Dallas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deejay-dal.headline: DeeJay Dallas (toe) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deejay-dal.analysis: Dallas should be fine by the time Sunday rolls around, but it’s worth noting given how thin the Vikings are at running back. Jordan Mason is on injured reserve and Aaron Jones came out of Week 2 with a knee injury. He did not practice today and his Week 3 availability is very much in question. Dallas and Demond Claiborne will split the Minnesota backfield if Jones is out. The toe injury could force Kevin O’Connell to give Claiborne a few more touches this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deejay-dal.headline: Aaron Jones (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deejay-dal.analysis: Jones tweaked his knee in the Vikings’ Week 2 win over the Bears. He ultimately played through the issue during the second half and racked up 23 carries for 105 yards. Head coach Kevin O’Connell said he was “pretty sore” after the game. ESPN’s Kevin Seifert added today that Jones playing in Week 3 is “not a sure thing.” Jones simply can’t handle that large of a workload at this point in his career, and the team will likely get DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne more involved this week, even if Jones is able to suit up. If he can’t, those two backs will likely split the backfield.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deejay-dal.headline: Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said he expects rookie RB Demond Claiborne to be active for Week 2 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deejay-dal.analysis: According to ESPN’s Kevin Seifert, Claiborne and RB DeeJay Dallas will also be “part of the group” that backs up starting RB Aaron Jones with RB Jordan Mason (thumb) on injured reserve. Dallas was active last week, while the team kept Claiborne, the rookie, inactive, so it stands to reason that Dallas could play more snaps than Claiborne. That said, some beat reporters viewed Claiborne favorably this summer. He can be stashed on benches in 12-team leagues to see how things shake out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deejay-dal.headline: Vikings placed RB Jordan Mason on injured reserve with a thumb injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deejay-dal.analysis: That escalated quickly. On Monday, Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said Mason’s “sore thumb” was being evaluated. Apparently, it had sustained a small fracture, which has now been “fixed,” ostensibly surgically, given O’Connell’s phrasing. Short-term injured reserve placement requires players to miss four games, but the Vikings are on bye in Week 6, so Mason will be eligible to return in Week 7. Mason led the backfield with 15 carries in Week 1, so his absence provides RB Aaron Jones with a touch-count boost. Veteran RB DeeJay Dallas operated as the RB3. Rookie RB Demond Claiborne was inactive last week, but should be active in Week 2 against the Lions. Speculatively stashing him could be worthwhile.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deejay-dal.headline: Jaguars released RB DeeJay Dallas.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deejay-dal.analysis: Dallas was the odd man out in the backfield after the signing of Chris Rodriguez, ultimately prompting his release. The team will move forward with Bhayshul Tuten, Rodriguez, and LeQuint Allen atop the depth chart entering the regular season. Also waived or released were LB Yasir Abdullah, QB Joey Aguilar, DT Tommy Akingbesote, DL T.J. Bollers, WR Brady Boyd, WR Chandler Brayboy, LB Amari Burney, OL Jerome Carvin, DE Quindarius Dunnigan, TE Patrick Herbert, CB Preston Hodge, DT Jalen Hunt, OL Ricky Lee, LB Jalen McLeod, OL Timothy McKay, CB Jabbar Muhammed, S Devin Neal Jr., OL Jimto Obidegwu, WR Trebor Peña, S Cam’Ron Silmon-Craig, RB J’Mari Taylor, S Trevian Thomas, WR Michael Wortham, OL Kilian Zierer, QB Carter Bradley, DT Kelvie Rose, CB Corey Ballentine, OL Geron Christian Jr., OL Chuma Edoga, WR Tim Jones, QB Nick Mullens, OL Sam Mustipher, LB Baylon Spector, and WR Austin Trammell.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Kirk (calf) is questionable for San Francisco’s Week 7 game against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: He is, however, expected to be activated off injured reserve and play. We’ve heard worse desperation options than “most accomplished 49ers wideout on paper playing with Brock Purdy and George Kittle as Mike Evans sits.” Kirk probably factors in the WR3/WR4 calculus assuming he is indeed activated on Saturday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Kirk (calf) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Kirk is on track to make his 2026 debut this week in the 49ers’ game against the Falcons. As strange as it sounds, Kirk has a chance to vault into the 49ers’ No. 1 wide receiver role with Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) expected to sit out this week. Kirk should be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Kirk (calf) was a full participant in Wednesday’s walkthrough practice.
