https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Kirk was limited all of last week but starts out this week listed as a full participant for the 49ers’ Wednesday walkthrough practice. He remains on injured reserve, but head coach Kyle Shanahan said Kirk is a “possibility” for Week 7. A full practice listing is a good start and Kirk could see WR3 volume immediately with Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel dealing with injuries.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said Christian Kirk is a “possibility” for Week 7.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Kirk has been on injured reserve with a calf injury but could return to the Niners’ injury-ravaged receivers room this Sunday against the pass-funnel Falcons defense. “He had two good practices (last week). It was just his first two practices of the year,” Shanahan said of Kirk, who last year had 239 yards and a touchdown in 13 regular season games for the Texans. “We were down on wideouts, so it was still something we discussed, but we decided to give it another week.” If Kirk returns and plays something close to a full complement of snaps against Atlanta, he could function as the team’s No. 1 receiver with Mike Evans (Achilles) seemingly unlikely to suit up. Kirk should be rostered in most 12-team leagues and all deeper formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Kirk (calf) won’t play in San Francisco’s Week 6 game against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: He won’t be activated off injured reserve for this one, but he did practice three times this week and he may be a consideration for Week 7’s game if things continue to trend in this direction. This means Brandin Cooks should operate as San Francisco’s No. 2 wideout assuming Mike Evans plays.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Kirk (calf) is questionable for Week 6 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Kirk is a candidate to be activated from injured reserve ahead of Monday’s game against the Commanders. His status is worth tracking considering the absence of Deebo Samuel and general lack of depth at the position. Fantasy managers could be forced to wait until Week 7 for more fidelity considering the team plays in the final game of Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Kirk (calf) was limited on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Kirk’s inability to practice fully despite his lengthy injured reserve stint suggests he might need another week or two to get ready for an NFL game. Still, the 49ers don’t face the Commanders until Monday night. If active, he could end up warranting FLEX treatment with Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) ailing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: 49ers designated Christian Kirk (calf/IR) to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: His 21-day window to practice before being activated begins today and he’ll be limited in practice. It would be surprising if Kirk were activated this week given the timing, but perhaps Week 7 will be a realistic target, assuming practice goes smoothly and there are no setbacks. He was limited in his first practice back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: 49ers placed Christian Kirk (calf) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: San Francisco also placed offensive lineman Austen Pleasants on injured reserve. Both players will miss at least four games to start the year. Kirk missed most of training camp with the calf issue. Mike Evans, De’Zhaun Stribling, and Deebo Samuel will start for the team in three-receiver sets. Even when Kirk comes back, he’s likely stuck as the WR4 on the depth chart.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: The Athletic’s Matt Barrows reports that “a Week 1 roster spot seems to be slipping away from” 49ers WR Christian Kirk (calf).
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Barrows’ phrasing leaves room for interpretation, but it seems as though he is suggesting Kirk could be a cut candidate. The veteran wide receiver was sidelined by a calf injury in the spring and reinjured it in the first practice of training camp. He should probably be avoided in fantasy drafts at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.headline: Nick Bosa (calf) will not play in San Francisco’s Week 7 game against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.analysis: The 49ers keep projecting a rosy picture of Bosa returning to practice at some point, it keeps not happening. He’ll get the Week 8 bye to heal up. Bosa hasn’t played since Week 2. If only there were a reserve list that teams could place injured players on.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.headline: Nick Bosa (calf) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.analysis: The 49ers were optimistic about Bosa’s availability for Week 7 against the Falcons, but he is firmly on the wrong side of questionable. The 49ers go on bye in Week 8. Allowing him to fully heal and return in Week 9 for their game against the Raiders could make sense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.headline: Nick Bosa (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.analysis: Kyle Shanahan told reporters he’s hopeful Bosa returns to practice tomorrow. The oft-injured pass-rusher hasn’t played since Week 2. Even if he does practice on Thursday, there’s no guarantee that will get him back on the field for Sunday’s game against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.headline: Nick Bosa (calf) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.analysis: Bosa is on the wrong side of questionable despite prior reports and coaching comments indicating he has a chance to face the Commanders on Monday night. For now, we expect Bosa to miss another week, though the extra day off could help him return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.headline: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said he’s “hoping Nick Bosa (calf) can go” in Week 6 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.analysis: Unfortunately, Bosa has not yet resumed practicing, though the 49ers have an extra day to let Bosa rehab. They face the Commanders in Week 6’s Monday Night Football game. Late last week, Bosa told reporters that it is “pretty darn likely” he plays in Week 6. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.headline: 49ers EDGE Nick Bosa (calf) said it is “pretty darn likely” he plays in Week 6 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.analysis: Bosa has missed two games since injuring his left calf in pre-practice warmups. He will miss his third game this weekend, but apparently the rehab progress is going well. The 49ers go on by in Week 8, and the team initially considered shutting him down until Week 9. Things are currently progressing well for the veteran pass rusher, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.headline: 49ers ruled out Nick Bosa (knee/calf) for Week 5 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.analysis: The 49ers will be without Bosa, FB Kyle Juszczyk (knee), DL James Thompson Jr. (ankle) and S Marques Sigle (ankle) for this divisional showdown, making life a little easier on their opponent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.headline: 49ers EDGE Nick Bosa (knee/calf) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.analysis: Bosa has yet to return to practice since injuring his calf two weeks ago in practice. He is listed with both knee and calf injuries and is seemingly not close to returning to in-game action. Bosa will need to practice before we can consider him ready to go for Week 5 or beyond.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.headline: 49ers LT Trent Williams (stinger) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.analysis: The 49ers will have their stud left tackle active on Sunday. 49ers LB Dre Greenlaw (quad bruise) is questionable to play. 49ers EDGE Nick Bosa (calf) and DL Mykel Williams (knee) have both been ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.headline: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan confirmed that EDGE Nick Bosa (calf) will miss multiple weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nick-bosa/.analysis: Bosa strained his calf while going through his pre-practice warm-up routine on Thursday. The team has not yet identified Bosa’s expected return timeline, but the 49ers’ pass rusher will be out for some time. The 49ers also ruled out EDGE Romello Height (hand) for Week 3 against the Cardinals as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Seahawks ruled out Zach Charbonnet (knee) for Week 7 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald told reporters that Charbonnet has not suffered a setback. He just isn’t ready yet. Many teams might rush a player of his caliber back, now that he is practicing in full, but the Seahawks are smartly taking the long view with Charbonnet’s health. Emanuel Wilson will function as the team’s leading rusher while George Holani plays on passing downs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Seahawks activated Zach Charbonnet (knee) from the reserve/physically unable to perform list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Charbonnet underwent ACL reconstruction after suffering his season-ending knee injury in the Seahawks’ Divisional Round win over the 49ers. He will make his 2026 debut in Week 7 against the Chiefs, facing his former teammate, Kenneth Walker. Charbonnet’s expected workload is unknown, though he could handle enough touches to be FLEX-viable. As long as he stays healthy, Charbonnet should advance to the RB2 ranks in the coming weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Zach Charbonnet (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Charbonnet was expected to get a full week of practice, so this is no surprise. He is listed as a full participant for the first time since returning to practice and is trending to be activated off the physically unable to perform list ahead of a Week 7 matchup against the Chiefs. With Jadarian Price on injured reserve, he is headed for a sizeable share of the Seahawks’ ambiguous backfield. Charbonnet is in the RB3 ranks if activated.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Mike Macdonald said Zach Charbonnet (knee) has a “good chance” to play in Week 7.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Finally, some good news for both Seahawks fans and fantasy managers, alike, after the Seattle run game has gotten off to a sluggish start to the 2026 season. Charbonnet has been on the physically unable to perform list through the first six weeks of the season but appears likely to make his return to the active roster for a marquee matchup against the Chiefs in a game some would consider a must-win for the suddenly reeling Seahawks. Macdonald added that the veteran back would get a full week of practice this week before any decision was made. Fantasy managers can add Charbonnet from waivers, if available.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Zach Charbonnet (knee) will be out for the Seahawks’ Week 6 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Charbonnet was already expected to miss Week 6, so no surprise here. The Seahawks also ruled out LB Drake Thomas and LB Chazz Surratt. There are no other players with injury designations heading into Seattle’s Thursday showdown against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Zach Charbonnet (knee) has a “legitimate chance” to play in Week 7 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Charbonnet’s return from ACL surgery has been going well. He is currently practicing with his teammates, though the quick turnaround time for this week’s Thursday Night Football game against the Broncos is too short for Charbonnet to properly ramp up. The Seahawks need a reliable player in the backfield and Charbonnet has coach Mike Macdonald’s trust. He will likely get all he can handle whenever he retakes the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said he does not plan to play Zach Charbonnet (knee) in Week 6 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: The Seahawks face the Broncos in Week 6’s Thursday Night Football game. Late last week, Macdonald acknowledged that the short turnaround time would make it difficult to ramp up Charbonnet as planned. The Seahawks are set to scale back the intensity at practice this week, which runs counter to the rehab plan. The Seahawks face the Chiefs in Week 7’s Sunday Night Football game. That seems like a plausible return date at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Seattle’s Week 6 Thursday Night Football game against the Broncos makes Zach Charbonnet’s (knee) ramp-up “tricky.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Charbonnet is on schedule in his rehab program and “will be ready to ramp up his work next week.” Unfortunately, the Seahawks will have scaled-down practices as they prepare for their Thursday Night Football game. It sounds like Charbonnet is close to returning, but team doctors might want to see how his knee responds to a full week or practicing before clearing him. A condensed practice week indeed makes that tricky. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Seahawks ruled out Zach Charbonnet (knee) for Week 5 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: We do not yet know Charbonnet’s Friday participation level, but he remained limited for the first two practices. The Seahawks are smartly bringing him along slowly despite mounting injuries at the position. He should be stashed in 12-team leagues, and could return to a sizable workload when healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.headline: Seahawks RB Zach Charbonnet (knee) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zach-charb.analysis: Charbonnet is starting to ramp up to a return from his torn ACL last season. The Seahawks opened up his practice window and he was limited on Wednesday. He is already ruled out for Week 5, but a Week 6 return is not out of the picture just yet.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) won’t play in San Francisco’s Week 7 game against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Samuel hasn’t practiced since injuring his hamstring in the latter stages of Week 5’s win over the Seahawks. He’ll get the Week 8 bye to heal up. It does seem like there’s at least some chance he could get active for Week 9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: Deebo Samuel (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Neither did Mike Evans, who is dealing with Achilles tendinitis. These absences shouldn’t come as much of a surprise. Evans is expected to miss Week 7 after aggravating his Achilles issue on Monday. Samuel is expected to miss “at least a couple of weeks” and has been sidelined for just one game so far. Jordan Watkins and Brandin Cooks are in line to start for the 49ers this week. What a time to be alive.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: 49ers ruled out Deebo Samuel (hamstring) for Week 6 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Samuel will be forced to miss Week 6 with a hamstring injury sustained in the team’s Week 5 win over the Seahawks, leaving the team extremely thin at wide receiver. They could get a small boost with Christian Kirk a candidate to be activated from injured reserve ahead of Monday’s game, although Mike Evans is also listed as questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said they’re going to hold off on placing Deebo Samuel (hamstring) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: The 49ers have a Week 8 bye and thus Samuel would stay on injured reserve an extra week. Reading between the lines, it sounds like Samuel has a chance to play in Week 9 if things go well. Shanahan added that Demarcus Robinson (ankle) could return for Week 9 as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said Deebo Samuel will miss “at least a couple of weeks” with the hamstring injury he suffered in Week 5’s win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Shanahan confirming this will be a multi-week absence isn’t surprising, but we still aren’t clear on just how much time he could miss. We’ll likely get a more specific timeline in the days ahead, but it sounds like we can safely assume Samuel will miss Week 6’s game against the Commanders and Week 7’s game against the Falcons. Jacob Cowing and Brandin Cooks could both be in line to see more work in the weeks ahead, with Cooks perhaps being the favorite to get the first crack at replacing Samuel. Cooks’ 11 routes run in the second half of Sunday’s game led all 49ers, including Mike Evans, and he found the end zone on a seven-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter to put the Niners ahead with just over 11 minutes left in regulation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said Deebo Samuel (hamstring) will have an MRI on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: The MRI will help determine the severity of Samuel’s injury, but the 30-year-old receiver is likely looking at a multi-week absence after he was quickly ruled out of Sunday’s game. Samuel has caught 16 passes for 206 yards and three touchdowns this season for the Niners while adding another 78 yards on nine carries. He seems unlikely to play in Week 6 against the Commanders, which means we could see an increased role for either Jacob Cowing or Brandin Cooks, who scored in Week 5’s win over the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: Deebo Samuel (hamstring) has been ruled out for the remainder of Week 5’s game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: That didn’t take long. Just moments after leaving the game, it was announced that Samuel had suffered a hamstring injury and would not return to the field. Shortly after being ruled out, Samuel was shown walking gingerly to the locker room with trainers. His day ends with a 2-21-0 line on three targets. Samuel also had two carries for four yards and a lost fumble, which came on the play he was injured on.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: Deebo Samuel exited in the third quarter of Week 5’s game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Samuel went down after being tripped up on a run play and remained down for an extended period of time after the play. It was hard to tell exactly what happened on the play, but Samuel was able to make his way to the sideline and could be seen sitting on the bench while being evaluated by trainers. We will provide an update on his status when we receive one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: Deebo Samuel caught 5-of-6 targets for 26 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 4 win against the Broncos, adding three rushes for 44 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Samuel was again a critically important part of the San Francisco offense. He scored his touchdown — his third of the year — on a well-designed red zone target from Brock Purdy. Looking far quicker and more fleet afoot than he did last year in Washington, Samuel has been a consistent flex option in 12-team leagues through Week 4. That should continue in Week 5, though the matchup is much tougher against the Seahawks secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.headline: Deebo Samuel caught zero passes for 80 receiving yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 3 win over the Cardinals. Yes, you read that correctly.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/deebo-samu.analysis: Samuel’s box score will looks strange to most, but that’s what happens when Kyle Shanahan tries out a hook-and-ladder play in the first quarter. Mike Evans caught a pass from Brock Purdy, lateraling the ball to Samuel, who sprinted 80 yards downfield for the score. Despite Evans (rib) leaving the game early, Samuel technically finishes with zero targets, though he did carry the ball twice for 14 rushing yards. With his final stat-line, he sets the record for most receiving yards without a reception in NFL history. Samuel will benefit if Evans misses time and would be in the high-end WR3 range for Week 4 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) will not play in San Francisco’s Week 7 game against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: He didn’t practice all week and will get San Francisco’s Week 8 bye to recover. The 33-year-old’s absence will leave veterans Christian Kirk and Brandin Cooks along with youngsters Jacob Cowing and Jordan Watkins on the 49ers receiver depth chart for Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: NBC Sports’ Jennifer Lee Chan reported earlier this week that Evans is expected to “miss a little time,” making his two absences unsurprising. Evans has not been formally ruled out, and he is no stranger to playing through injury, but fantasy managers should expect him to miss the 49ers’ Week 7 game against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Evans is already expected to miss “a little time” because of his Achilles tendinitis, so this isn’t a surprise. It’s safe to assume he’s out for at least Week 7, but the good news is that it’s not expected to be a long-term issue. Evans could be back as soon as Week 9 following the 49ers’ bye week. With Deebo Samuel all but ruled out for this week’s matchup with Atlanta, Brandin Cooks and Jordan Watkins are set for starting roles on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Deebo Samuel (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Neither did Mike Evans, who is dealing with Achilles tendinitis. These absences shouldn’t come as much of a surprise. Evans is expected to miss Week 7 after aggravating his Achilles issue on Monday. Samuel is expected to miss “at least a couple of weeks” and has been sidelined for just one game so far. Jordan Watkins and Brandin Cooks are in line to start for the 49ers this week. What a time to be alive.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: 49ers beat reporter Jennifer Lee Chan reports Mike Evans’ Achilles is intact but he is expected to “miss a little time.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Chan speculates that the window for his recovery could align with the team’s Week 8 bye week, meaning Evans would miss just one game with an aggravation of the Achilles injury that had him listed as questionable heading into Monday Night Football against the Commanders. All things considered, it’s solid news for Evans, the 49ers, and his fantasy managers. Expect a more concrete update from the team in the coming days as they limp into a Week 7 game against the Falcons down plentiful impact wide receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (Achilles) limped to the locker room in the second quarter of Week 6 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Evans came into the game with two injury designations, ribs and Achilles, ultimately suiting up. He limped to the locker room with the help of training staff and was seen in the tunnel pointing to his Achilles. The 33-year-old receiver has been on the injury report for much of the season, with the most recent ailment potentially proving to be too much to play through. Expect an update from the team after the half. Evans caught 3-of-5 targets for 94 yards prior to departing. 49ers beat reporter Jennifer Lee Chan reported after the game that Evans’ Achilles is intact but will “miss a little time.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (ribs, Achilles) is active for Week 6 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Evans will gut it out in Week 6 as fellow wide receiver Deebo Samuel is unable to go. Look for the bulk of the aerial offense to flow through Evans, George Kittle, and Christian McCaffrey, the three of whom handily led the team in route participation a week ago following Samuel’s departure. Inactive for the 49ers are QB Kurtis Rourke, DE Nick Bosa, WR Deebo Samuel, S Marques Sigle, LB Garret Wallow, OT Enrique Cruz Jr., and DT Naquan Jones.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Speaking on the Pat McAfee Show, Adam Schefter said “the 49ers are optimistic” Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) will play in Week 6 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Evans did not log a practice in the days leading up to Monday night’s game against the Commanders, but the team still listed him as questionable on Saturday. Schefter reports the Niners want to see how Evans looks during pregame warmups, but it sounds like they are somewhat hopeful he will be active for Monday’s game. Evans has caught 24 passes for 326 yards and three touchdowns this season and went for 7-113-1 on 10 targets in last week’s win over the Seahawks. He would be a must-start on Monday against Washington if he is active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (ribs, Achilles) is questionable for Week 6 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Evans was unable to practice through Friday but ultimately did enough to land a questionable tag with multiple injury designations. However likely it is that Evans continues to play through various ailments, fantasy managers could look to make alternate plans considering the timing of the 49ers’ game on Monday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.headline: Mike Evans (ribs/Achilles) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-evans.analysis: Even for an iron man like Evans, this is a little concerning. Frankly, we still expect Evans to play, but two missed practices due partially to Achilles “soreness” are less than ideal. The 49ers face the Commanders on Monday night. Making a backup plan is worthwhile at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-guyt.headline: Tyler Guyton (calf) practiced in full on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-guyt.analysis: This is great news for the Cowboys’ offense. Guyton, the starting left tackle, is practicing in full and still has another practice tomorrow. Expect him to be available for the Cowboys’ Monday Night Football game against the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-guyt.headline: Tyler Guyton (calf) was added to the injury report as a limited participant on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-guyt.analysis: The Cowboys’ left tackle played through a minor back issue earlier this month as well. He’s a little banged up at the moment. Whether this injury keeps him out remains to be seen. The Cowboys take on the division-rival Eagles on Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-guyt.headline: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said LT Tyler Guyton’s back injury is not considered serious.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-guyt.analysis: This is good news. Guyton was replaced by OT Broderick Jones for the Cowboys’ final possession in Week 5 against the Buccaneers. Guyton and the rest of the Cowboys have an extended time off to rest and rehab their injuries after playing on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-guyt.headline: Cowboys placed LT Tyler Guyton (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-guyt.analysis: Guyton’s season is over. The team signed DB Corey Ballentine from their practice squad to the 53-man roster in a corresponding move. Guyton suffered a high-ankle sprain in Week 12 and hasn’t played since. The team was likely holding out hope that he could return late in the year if they were still in the playoff hunt. Dallas was eliminated from postseason contention last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-guyt.headline: Cowboys T Tyler Guyton (ankle) will not play in Dallas’ Week 16 game against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-guyt.analysis: He hasn’t practiced or played since Week 12’s high-ankle sprain, so this will be his fourth-straight missed game. The Cowboys don’t necessarily have to shut him down, but they probably won’t bother trying to play him in Week 17 or 18 if there’s any question about his health now that they’re all but eliminated from the playoff picture.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-guyt.headline: Cowboys declared WR Jalen Tolbert, RB Jaydon Blue, T Tyler Guyton, DT Jay Toia, and DT Perrion Winfrey inactive for Week 15 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-guyt.analysis: Guyton continues his rehab from a high-ankle sprain suffered in Week 12, leaving Nate Thomas to draw another start. The Cowboys enter Sunday Night Football in desperate need of a win as they aim to keep their fading playoff hopes alive.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-guyt.headline: Cowboys T Tyler Guyton (ankle) won’t play in Dallas’ Week 15 game against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-guyt.analysis: Nate Thomas got the tackle work the last two weeks and should be set for another start against the Vikings defense in Week 15. Guyton has not played or practiced since suffering the dreaded high-ankle sprain in Dallas’ Week 12 win over the Eagles. The second-year tackle should be considered questionable for Week 16.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-guyt.headline: Cowboys LT Tyler Guyton (ankle) will not play in Week 14 against the Lions
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-guyt.analysis: Guyton went down with a high-ankle sprain in Week 12 and missed the following game on Thanksgiving. Nathan Thomas will continue to start at left tackle this week. Though he will be a clear weak point for the Cowboys, that shouldn’t stop their offensive machine from rolling versus Detroit. Trevon Diggs was not activated from injured reserve and is also out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-guyt.headline: Cowboys listed Tyler Guyton (ankle) as a DNP on Monday’s estimated practice report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-guyt.analysis: Guyton suffered a high-ankle sprain in Week 12’s win over the Eagles and was sidelined for Week 13’s game against the Chiefs. Given the nature of his injury, it seems unlikely that he would be ready to go with less than two weeks of recovery time. We’ll see if his status changes later in the week, but we could be looking at another start for Nate Thomas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-guyt.headline: Cowboys declared LT Tyler Guyton, RB Jaydon Blue, CB Caelen Carson, WR Jonathan Mingo, DT Jay Toia and DT Perrion Winfrey inactive for Week 13 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-guyt.analysis: The Cowboys are without their left tackle, who suffered a high-ankle sprain in Week 12 against the Eagles. He was unable to practice at all this week. Blue, the once exciting rookie running back, is only a mildly intriguing bench stash at this point. His explosive traits are not in doubt, but he seemingly has a way to go before the Cowboys trust him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-brow.headline: Trent Brown (wrist) is not on Houston’s final Week 7 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-brow.analysis: He’ll be good to go after back-to-back full sessions on Thursday and Friday. The 380-pound behemoth will likely continue to spend plenty of time on the injury report in his age-33 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-brow.headline: Trent Brown (wrist) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-brow.analysis: Brown was on the injury report because of the wrist injury several times earlier in the season. The team only listed him with a knee issue last week, and he was cleared from the injury report on Friday, but it’s likely that he’s been managing the wrist injury all season. Blake Fisher, his projected backup, also missed practice today, so this is at least a situation to monitor throughout the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-brow.headline: Texans RT Trent Brown (knee/wrist) is questionable for Week 3 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-brow.analysis: The Texans ruled out RG Ed Ingram (groin) and EDGE Jadevon Clowney (knee). The Colts’ defense has played unimpressively thus far, but hopefully Brown is able to play this week. Losing two offensive line starters is less than ideal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-brow.headline: Trent Brown (knee/wrist) did not practice Wednesdaay.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-brow.analysis: Ed Ingram remained sidelined with a groin injury. He did not play in Week 2. Brown had been playing through the wrist issue, but the knee injury is new. With Nico Collins banged up, the last thing Houston needs is another offensive line injury. Blake Fisher would take Brown’s spot at right tackle if he can’t suit up on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-brow.headline: Texans signed OT Trent Brown to a one-year contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-brow.analysis: Per ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the deal is worth “up to” $7 million. Brown was released by Houston at the end of training camp last year. The team kept him around on the practice squad and ultimately put him on the active roster during the second half of the season. He went on to make eight starts, including the playoffs, and received solid grades from Pro Football Focus. With fellow right tackle Tytus Howard traded to Cleveland, Brown is in line to take on that gig full-time for 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-brow.headline: Texans declared WR Nico Collins, T Trent Brown, RB Jawhar Jordan, QB Graham Mertz, and WR Justin Watson inactive for the Divisional Round against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-brow.analysis: Collins, who sustained a head injury in the Wild Card round against the Steelers, did not practice this week and was ruled out on Friday. It’s a massive blow to the Houston offense. Christian Kirk, who had 144 yards and a score last week against Pittsburgh, will profile as the team’s top receiver with Collins out. Brown tried to play but was unable to fight through an ankle injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-brow.headline: Texans RT Trent Brown (ankle/knee) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 17 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-brow.analysis: This is good news for the Texans’ offense. Brown’s 68.6 PFF offense grade ranks second among the Texans’ offensive line starters. Brown will help fend off the Chargers’ talented front-seven defenders as the Texans seek to secure a postseason appearance.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-brow.headline: Texans OT Trent Brown (ankle/knee) did not practice Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-brow.analysis: Brown left in Week 16 against the Raiders and now starts out the week not practicing. He is listed with ankle and knee issues and would be a notable loss if he cannot go Week 17 against the Chargers. With Aireontae Ersery (thumb) getting surgery, the Texans need healthy offensive tackles for their final playoff push. Brown still has a couple days to get a practice in and play on Saturday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-brow.headline: Texans T Aireontae Ersery (hand) left Houston’s Week 16 game against the Raiders and is questionable to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-brow.analysis: He left late in the fourth quarter and was replaced by Blake Fisher. Ersery has had a rough rookie year as Houston’s everydown left tackle, but given the depth on hand here, it would be a loss if he missed multiple weeks. Trent Brown also left the game at the two-minute warning, though he wasn’t given a designation before the end of the game. His status will be worth monitoring.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-brow.headline: Texans G Ed Ingram (knee) practiced in full on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-brow.analysis: After missing each of the last two games with a knee injury, Ingram looks likely to go on Thursday night. Ingram has posted back-to-back full practices this week. Tytus Howard (ankle/knee) and Trent Brown (hand/knee) were both limited participants on Monday and Tuesday and also look to be trending towards playing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz (quad) is not on Houston’s final Week 7 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: He’ll be good to go, but given how much Houston’s wideout usage has expanded of late, Schultz is probably just a passable TE2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz (quad) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Correcting a previous item, Schultz ended up practicing today. He was limited, as was Brevin Jordan (foot), who evidently picked up a new injury. Schultz’s return gives him a chance to face the Giants this week. Ideally, he will upgrade to full participation tomorrow, though it is possible he gets hit with the questionable tag if he remains limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz (quad) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Schultz is unlikely to play in Week 7 against the Giants, and now Texans TE4 Brevin Jordan (foot) appears to have suffered an injury. Jordan was added to the injury report today as a limited participant. The injuries elevate TE2 Foster Moreau to the streaming ranks for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz (quad) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Schultz never left the Texans’ Week 6 game against Jacksonville, but he was spotted with a limp after taking a knee to the leg. It’s possible the injury was worse than initially expected. If he were to miss Week 7, Foster Moreau, who scored twice last week, would be the next man up. Given that Schultz was barely putting up TE2 numbers as the starter, our hopes for Moreau as a streaming option would not be high.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz caught 3-of-4 targets for 30 yards in Houston’s Week 5 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: If you’re thinking all Dalton Schultz lines have started to blur together, you’re not wrong. He’s had eight catches for 69 yards since his Week 2 explosion against the Bengals. There’s not much upside here, but at least he’s providing a safe TE2 floor for those of you who get five points per TE reception.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz caught 2-of-2 targets for nine yards in Houston’s Week 4 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Not the most inspiring entry of #RevengeGame lore. Schultz was outgained by Cade Stover and Brevin Jordan. He’s trending towards TE2 usage with Nico Collins back in the lineup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz caught 3-of-3 targets for 30 yards in Houston’s Week 3 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Schultz told the CBS booth before the game that he “hopes to not have stat lines” like he had in Week 2, an anecdote they related as he had just one catch in the fourth quarter. Sounds like news that fantasy managers wish they had heard yesterday. He didn’t have a catch in the first half and yielded a red zone touchdown to spoiler Foster Moreau. Schultz has low-end TE1 status in a classic #RevengeGame against the Cowboys in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Texans ruled out WR Nico Collins (hamstring) for Week 3 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: Collins will miss his second consecutive game with yet another hamstring strain. Last week, the passing offense ran through TE Dalton Schultz, who earned 13 targets. Fellow Texans WR Xavier Hutchinson was next with eight targets, but he caught just three, making for a shaky FLEX option this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz caught 12-of-14 targets for 140 yards in Houston’s Week 2 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: An incredible PPR scam as the Texans had him as the main checkdown receiver while trailing for much of the game. Eight of the 12 catches came in the fourth quarter as C.J. Stroud tried in vain to push the rest of this offense anywhere. Don’t expect this much next week with Collins apparently questionable again, but Schultz clearly elevates in the pecking order and has TE1 appeal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.headline: Dalton Schultz caught 4-of-8 targets for 35 yards in Houston’s Week 1 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-sch.analysis: He did most of his work on the offense’s final drive, catching back-to-back targets for 26 yards. Schultz managed 52-of-79 snaps. If you were going to pick anyone in this offense besides David Montgomery and Nico Collins to return consistent fantasy value, it’s probably Schultz. It’s just, you know, there are not often three Texans worth starting in fantasy football. He’ll be a high-end TE2 against the Bengals in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: GeorgePickens (shoulder) said he will play in Week 7 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: The Cowboys face the Eagles in Week 7’s Monday Night Football game, giving Pickens an extra day to recover. ESPN’s Todd Archer said yesterday that Pickens has been icing his shoulder in-game during the Cowboys’ last two games. He encouragingly practiced in full today. Start him as a WR2 as usual this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens (shoulder) was added to the injury report as a limited participant on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Reliable ESPN beat reporter Todd Archer notes that Pickens has had ice on his shoulder during the Cowboys’ last two games. He does not think that this injury threatens Pickens’ Week 7 availability. Thanks, Todd. Ideally, Pickens jumps back up to full participation tomorrow, and we head into Sunday carefree. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens caught 6-of-11 targets for 73 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 6 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens was targeted just once in the first half as the Cowboys were held under 100 yards of total offense before the break. He would remain quiet through the third quarter, adding a single catch to his ledger on two additional targets before seeing eight looks in the final frame with the Cowboys in desperation mode. The 11 targets finished second on the team to CeeDee Lamb’s 18 while the 73 yards slightly edged the 70 of Lamb. Pickens remains an upside WR2 ahead of a divisional matchup against the inside-funnel Eagles’ secondary in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens caught 9-of-13 targets for 130 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 5 loss to the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens was the primary target throughout the game against the single-high-heavy Buccaneers, scoring a late fourth quarter touchdown to cap off his first impressive fantasy outing of the young season. Furthermore, fellow receiver CeeDee Lamb departed the game in the fourth quarter with a quad injury that he was unable to play through, potentially setting up Pickens for immense volume in a Week 6 meeting with the Packers at Lambeau. Fantasy managers have patiently watched as Lamb stole the show through the first four games of 2026, but it now appears as if Pickens will have his time to shine, pending the severity of Lamb’s soft tissue injury. Pickens is a WR2 with Lamb active and a surefire WR1 with Lamb out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens caught 2-of-3 targets for 75 yards in Dallas’ Week 4 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: He had a 53-yard mossing of Kamari Lassiter in the third quarter to set up a big Cowboys drive, and also wound up drawing two different penalties against Lassiter in the end zone to sustain a touchdown drive, one on fourth down. Pickens isn’t playing poorly, but the Cowboys simply are feeding CeeDee Lamb and it’s hard to argue with the results. Eventually the touchdown worm will turn and Pickens will be back on the WR2 line against the Bucs in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens caught 7-of-11 targets for 82 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 3 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens finally looked like the player we expected to see after his breakout 2025 campaign. While we’re still waiting for the first true explosive play from Pickens this season, he did manage to haul in all four targets he saw in the intermediate area of the field and picked up 19 yards on a third-and-10 on a drive that ended with a Jake Ferguson touchdown two plays later. Pickens would have had a much bigger day if not for a 20-yard reception that was called back due to a penalty, but fantasy managers won’t be upset with this performance. We’ll see if he can build on this week’s outing next week against the Texans, where he will be on the WR2 radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens caught 6-of-8 targets for 40 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 2 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: At some point, things will break in Pickens’ favor, but it was not to be in Sunday’s win over the Commanders, despite Dak Prescott throwing for 279-4-0 and having just five incompletions on the day. Pickens hasn’t generated any explosive plays yet, with his longest catch of the season coming on a 12-yard gain in the second quarter of today’s game. He’s still averaging 7.0 targets through the first two weeks of the season, so hopefully the big plays will follow soon. He should be treated as a high-end WR2 in next week’s game against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: George Pickens caught 3-of-6 targets for 28 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 1 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Pickens picked up two early receptions on the team’s first two possessions, contributing further by drawing a defensive pass interference penalty that would set up a CeeDee Lamb touchdown in the second quarter. An untimely drop on third down near the end of the first quarter halted any momentum he had in the box score as he would go on to notch a lone additional catch the rest of the game. The Cowboys managed only 52 offensive plays as they were dominated in both total offense and time of possession, while watching their defense allow the Giants to go 9-of-10 on third down. It is likely we see much more inspiring fantasy production the remainder of the season as Pickens plays out the year on the franchise tag. He enters a Week 2 home showdown against the Commanders as an upside WR2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: Cowboys WR George Pickens will officially play under the franchise tag for the 2026 season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: The July 15th deadline for franchise-tagged players to sign long-term deals came and went without Pickens signing a new deal. Cowboys executive vice president Steven Jones had said in April that “there won’t be negotiations on a long-term deal” with Pickens. The 25-year-old wide receiver showed up for mandatory minicamp and does not plan to hold out of training camp, either. He will play on a $27.3 million franchise tag and will either reach a contract extension after the season or enter unrestricted free agency in 2027. Pickens will be the WR2 across from CeeDee Lamb in 2026; both have ceilings in the fantasy WR1 range.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.headline: ESPN’s Ben Solak believes Dak Prescott could throw for 5,000 yards in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-pic.analysis: Solak’s prediction was among his bold predictions for the 2026 NFL season. Prescott having a shot at 5,000 yards, Solak said, would hinge on the Cowboys remaining a fast-paced offense in 2026. Last season the Cowboys led the league in play clock remaining at the snap and offensive plays per game, leading to 600 passes for Dak — a career high. The wideout duo of George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb won’t hurt matters for Prescott, who has eclipsed 4,500 passing yards three times in his NFL career. Pickens’ downfield ability was reflected in Prescott finishing sixth in deep ball accuracy last season. “The volume will be there for Prescott to not just lead the league in passing in 2026 but to once again challenge for the 5,000-yard milestone,” Solak said. Quarterbacks have thrown for more than 5,000 yards just 14 times in league history.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden (shoulder) is not on the Packers’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: A few Packers got a little banged up against the Cowboys last week, including Golden, but the breakout second-year wide receiver is good to go. This game profiles as a fantasy-friendly shootout. Golden should be started as a high-end WR2 with solid upside.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden (shoulder) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Golden appears to just be being managed at this point as Packers coach Matt LaFleur said there were no concerns on him playing in Week 7 on Wednesday. Two limited sessions are often a starting point for a questionable listing, but we’d be surprised if it got that far with Golden. He’ll likely be cleared off the injury report on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matt LaFleur said he has no concerns about Christian Watson’s ankle injury ahead of the Packers’ Week 7 game against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: The same is true of Matthew Golden, who is dealing with a shoulder issue. Both players were estimated as limited participants for Wednesday’s walkthrough. It doesn’t look like either wideout is at risk of missing the Packers’ upcoming shootout with Detroit. Watson is currently fifth in the league in receiving yards at 538. Golden is sixth at 501. Both players hold a spot in the WR1 ranks heading into Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: A limited session this early in the week is usually nothing to worry about. After racking up another 100-yard game on Sunday, this time on 13 targets, Golden could use a little rest at practice. He was working his way into the WR1 ranks already, and a shootout with the Lions all but guarantees him a spot in the top 12 this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden caught 6-of-13 targets for 104 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Golden took advantage of being the Green Bay receiver to mostly avoid Joey Porter Jr., although he did victimize the lockdown corner on a 37-yard reception in the first quarter. He would cash in on a touchdown eight plays later from nine yards out for his third score of the season. The speedy second-year receiver has now eclipsed 100 yards in half of his games while hitting 95 in one other, and is pacing for over 1,400 yards and eight touchdowns. That’s enough to have Golden in the conversation for one of the top values of fantasy drafts this summer. Golden will be an upside WR2 when the Packers take on the division rival Lions in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden caught 6-of-7 targets for 123 yards in the Packers’ Week 5 win over the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Golden’s 123 yards were his third new career high in just five games this season. In other words, his breakout year remains ongoing. Golden’s long gain was a soaring 50-yard deep shot over the middle of the field where the wideout had to go up and get it. Golden also contributed a 36-yard reception. Routinely providing 40-plus yard grabs while also doing some nice compiling, Golden has become not only a WR2 option, but a safe one at that. That will definitely include for Week 6 vs. the Cowboys’ leaky defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden caught 3-of-7 targets for 21 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 4 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Jordan Love couldn’t get the deep ball going in this game, resulting in Golden’s worst game of the season by catches and yards. For fantasy purposes, a two-yard score in the second quarter made the quiet day a non-issue. Golden still led the team in targets, tied with Tucker Kraft, so the usage was as strong as ever. He is working his way into the WR2 ranks ahead of his Week 5 matchup with the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden caught 5-of-12 targets for 100 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 3 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: It took Golden deep into the fourth quarter of Week 3 of his sophomore campaign to notch his first regular season touchdown, doing so by making a nice adjustment on a ball thrown behind him on a slant in the red zone. Golden leads the Packers with 30 targets through three games and should continue to bring weekly WR3 production, with upside for WR2 output, while operating as the X-type receiver in a Matt LaFleur offense. Increasing those chances is an offensive line that ranks as one of the worst units in the league that is paired with the absence of Josh Jacobs to bring zero run game support to Jordan Love and the Packers, making increased weekly pass volume something we’re likely to see carry forward in the immediate future. Golden is an upside WR2 ahead of a Week 4 matchup against the pass-funnel Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden caught 4-of-6 targets for 58 yards in the Packers’ Week 2 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: Golden ran a route on 32 of the team’s 34 dropbacks and was the target on a few deep passes that led to pass interference penalties. This was not an efficient passing day for the Packers’ offense, but it was nice to see Golden be such a huge part of it. With Jayden Reed (neck) getting hurt in this game and Tucker Kraft still not seemingly playing at 100 percent, Golden is the clear second target in this offense. He could be in for a big game against the Falcons in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.headline: Matthew Golden caught 6-of-12 targets for 97 yards in the Packers’ Week 1 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-go.analysis: As expected, Golden ran the bulk of the routes from an outside alignment and was much more involved compared to his rookie season. Christian Watson stole the show with 147 yards and two scores, but Golden comfortably led the team in targets. Four of his targets came on the Packers’ final drive while they were down by 17 points, but even his numbers before that were impressive. As the training camp reports indicated, Golden made massive strides during the offseason. Golden might not be the team’s target-leader every week, but he’s in the WR3 mix for the Packers’ Week 2 date with the Jets.

With outrageous usage in Klint Kubiak’s offense, Bowers has as much upside as any player in fantasy for now. He gets the Bills in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: The Packers held a walkthrough today, so Watson’s status is only an estimate from the team. The talented fifth-year receiver is already within 74 yards of setting a new career high in receiving while also being just one touchdown shy of a new high water mark, two achievements he will look to unlock when the Packers face off against the Lions in a potential shootout in Week 7. https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson caught 6-of-8 targets for 143 yards and two touchdowns.

Rather amazingly, the two-score effort was his seventh. This one came in true Watson fashion, as he found the end zone from 42 and 53 yards out. For the 42-yarder he ran right by the defense. For the 53-yarder, he high-pointed the ball off the defender’s helmet in the end zone. It was just that kind of day for the Packers, and it’s been just that kind of season for a wideout in Watson who continues to break out. Now firmly in the weekly WR1 mix, Watson has a potential Week 6 smash spot in the sorry Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson caught all three of his targets for 47 yards in the Packers’ Week 4 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: After scoring four touchdowns over the first three weeks, Watson finally cooled off with his first quiet game of the year. Jordan Love couldn’t get the deep ball going in this game and funneled the short targets to Tucker Kraft and Matthew Golden, leaving Watson without much to do. For a player known for having a low floor, 47 yards is a stunningly reasonable floor game. Watson is simply too good at picking up chunk gains to have the bottom truly fall out. He remains a boom/bust WR2 for his Week 5 date with the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson caught 7-of-10 targets for 96 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 3 loss to the Falcons.

Even better news for fantasy managers is the fact that we’re likely to see this sudden spike in pass volume continue forward given the current state of the Green Bay backfield and offensive line, meaning fantasy managers can continue to start Watson as a legitimate WR1 ahead of a road meeting with the pass-funnel Buccaneers in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Watson caught 4-of-11 targets for 41 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 2 win over the Jets.

While Watson and Jordan Love were inefficient in their connection, they did link up for some big catches, including a short fourth-quarter touchdown. Watson led the team in targets while running one fewer route than Matthew Golden. There is some concern that losing Jayden Reed (neck) to an injury may put even more attention on Watson, but this felt like an off-day for the offense. The ceiling remains really high for Watson this season, especially next week against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Watson got on the board early with an 81-yard bomb for a touchdown in the first quarter. He continued to gash the Vikings for big plays throughout the contest and even got in the end zone a second time on a short toss from Jordan Love just before halftime. Watson slowed down in the second half, but the damage was already done, at least for fantasy purposes. He won’t hit a career-long score every week, but the well-paid wideout certainly looked like a focal point of the Packers’ passing attack today. He will be in the WR2 mix when the Packers take on the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 23-of-41 passes for 276 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Packers’ 23-13, Week 6 win over the Cowboys, adding 12 yards and a touchdown on four carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Love isn’t typically a threat to punch in a touchdown with his legs, but the state of the backfield and flow of the game gave him that opportunity late in the second quarter, which he would cash in for his first rushing score since Week 11 of 2024. Fantasy managers shouldn’t get too excited about the touchdown on the ground considering running back Josh Jacobs is expected to be activated from the commissioner’s exempt list Monday. Even so, Love has now accounted for two touchdowns in all six games played through the first third of the season and has gone over 300 yards through the air in half his appearances to start the 2026 season, leaving plenty of meat on the bone for continued fantasy production as the Packers enter their most difficult stretch of the schedule. Love remains a locked-in QB1 ahead of a potential shootout against the division rival Lions in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 25-of-31 passes for 367 yards and two touchdowns in the Packers’ 31-7, Week 5 win over the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: With the Packers’ backs against the wall in a rivalry grudge match, Love had one of the best starts of his NFL life by simply cutting it loose. His 367 yards passing were the third most of his career, and accompanied by zero turnovers. He found each of Christian Watson, Matthew Golden and Tucker Kraft for at least one 46-yard gain, including a 53-yard touchdown to Watson. That does not include an earlier 42-yard scoring strike to Watson. Each score had serious air underneath them. This really was Love airing it out, something less competent quarterbacks had been struggling to do vs. the Bears’ vulnerable defense. We have seen this Love and Packers movie before — a step forward not followed by another move in the right direction — but neither Packers fans nor fantasy managers could have asked for more this afternoon. Love will have a good shot at keeping the good vibes going vs. the Cowboys’ struggling defense in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 22-of-30 passes for 197 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Packers’ 17-14, Week 4 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Green Bay entered this game in desperate need of a win. They got it, though it was not pretty. Kneel downs aside, the Packers had five drives that gained fewer than 10 yards. Love nearly threw the game away with an interception straight into the hands of Jacob Parris in the red zone with less than four minutes left on the clock. The Bucs could not score on the ensuing drive and Love got to kneel out the clock. The Packers’ offense still looked disjointed today. They simply found an opponent that wasn’t a threat to put more than a handful of points on the board. Love is slipping further back in the QB2 ranks as he prepares to take on the Bears in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 28-of-53 passes for 312 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Packers’ 35-14, Week 3 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Love was completely overrun by consistent pressure throughout on a night the Packers attempted 53 passes to just eight running back carries. The Atlanta defensive line took advantage of mounting injuries and ineffective play along the Green Bay offensive line to disrupt any offensive rhythm for the Packers. Love’s two touchdowns went to his top two options through the air in Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, the latter of whom notched the first regular season touchdown of his young career late in the fourth quarter. Matt LaFleur, Love, and the rest of the Packers have some significant work to do if they are to save their quickly sinking season. Love falls to a middling QB2 ahead of a road matchup with an aggressive Buccaneers defense in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 16-of-29 passes for 145 yards and two touchdowns in the Packers’ 20-17, Week 2 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: Love also ran in a touchdown in the fourth quarter, but it was called back because of a holding penalty. This game was played in a consistent drizzle, but the rain was not coming down hard enough to excuse why the Packers’ offense gained just 199 total yards. They committed 14 penalties and seemed incapable of making big plays, with just one play gaining at least 20 yards all day. Love took some deep shots down the field to Matthew Golden, but there weren’t many near misses to hang your hat on, and the offensive line didn’t hold up really well in pass protection. The good news is that the Packers will face a fairly mediocre Falcons defense in Week 3, so Love can be used in most fantasy leagues in that one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.headline: Jordan Love completed 21-of-42 passes for 387 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Packers’ 22-39, Week 1 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-lov.analysis: With Kyler Murray exiting this game early, the Packers appeared to be coasting to an easy win until the fourth quarter. Minnesota, however, slowly mounted a comeback that coincided with Love melting down. It started with a fumble that Minnesota took back to the one-yard line. Love got the ball back after a Jordan Mason touchdown and was immediately intercepted on his own side of the field, extinguishing any hope of a rebuttal from the Packers. Some garbage time production turned this into a strong fantasy outing from Love, but he will need to clear things up ahead of Week 2. Love will be in the QB2 mix versus the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tremaine-e.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Titans, Giants, and Raiders are “among teams” interested in trading for LB Tremaine Edmunds.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tremaine-e.analysis: Normally the “permission to seek trade” line leads to a release — Chicago Tribune’s Brad Biggs reported that he expected a release in his Friday column — but Edmunds appears to have a real market. Perhaps the Bears could manage a late-round swap out of this. The Titans and Raiders certainly make plenty of space as they have to use their cap space somehow.

The Bears could save $15 million by cutting him, though it would be in everyone’s best interest to find a trade partner. However, with his release looking increasingly likely, it may be hard to convince another team to give up draft capital for a player who is about to hit the open market. If that happens, Edmunds should still fetch a high-end contract for a linebacker. He led the Bears with 112 total tackles in 2025 despite missing four games. Edmunds also added four interceptions, nine pass breakups, and one sack to his ledger.

Edmunds has totaled 89 tackles, four interceptions, and one sack for the Bears this season and should be back in time to boost their defense by the playoffs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tremaine-e.headline: Bears placed LB Tremaine Edmunds (groin) on injured reserve.

Edwards was also ruled out for Week 12, boosting the rushing matchup for Jaylen Warren and Kenneth Gainwell for the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.headline: Darnell Mooney (neck) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.analysis: Mooney should be good to go this week, but he does not need to be on fantasy football rosters. Giants TE Theo Johnson (neck) was limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.headline: Giants declared TE Theo Johnson, CB Colton Hood, QB Jake Haener, S Tyler Nubin, OL Jermaine Eluemunor, and DL C.J. Okoye inactive for Week 6 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.analysis: Johnson was declared out heading into the weekend with a neck injury. Also out due to injury are Hood (concussion), Eluemunor (calf), and Nubin (neck). Expect to see more Thomas Fidone behind Isaiah Likely at the tight end position with Johnson out against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.headline: Theo Johnson (neck) will not play in New York’s Week 6 game against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.analysis: It’s Thomas Fidone hours in New York, marone.

https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.headline: Isaiah Likely (foot) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.analysis: Theo Johnson has a neck injury and was limited in practice. Both tight ends should be able to suit up on Sunday. Coming off a career-high in targets (13), Likely is looking more like a top-five fantasy tight end every week. He should be in every fantasy lineup for his Week 6 date with the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.headline: Giants TE Theo Johnson (shoulder) is practicing fully for Week 1 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.analysis: Johnson was seen practicing in a non-contact jersey last week, so today’s full session is positive. Unfortunately, Johnson’s path to fantasy football TE1 status is likely blocked by TE Isaiah Likely, so Johnson is not on the radar for most leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.headline: Theo Johnson (shoulder) participated in practice Tuesday wearing a non-contact jersey.
https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.analysis: John Harbaugh has said that Johnson “will be fine,” but we’re going to cover our bases on this one with the Giants keeping five tight ends. Johnson has a week and change to get healthy for Sunday Night Football in Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.headline: North Jersey’s Art Stapleton reports that Giants TE Isaiah Likely and TE Theo Johnson are currently the team’s top-two pass catchers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.analysis: This is the third positive report in as many months for Likely, who is set to handle TE1 duties for his new team. Johnson is slated for the TE2 role after posting a 45/528/5 receiving line in his second NFL season last year. Giants WR1 Malik Nabers recently underwent a clean-up procedure on his knee and field-stretching WR Darius Slayton is recovering from core muscle surgery. Nabers will retake the No. 1 pass-catching role when healthy. Slayton, 29, is on the downslope. Likely is in the low-end TE1 tier and could improve his stock through the spring and summer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.headline: The Athletic’s Dan Duggan reports TE Isaiah Likely is “expected to be a featured piece” of the Giants offense in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/theo-johnson/0.analysis: Likely followed former Ravens head coach John Harbaugh to New York in free agency, as expected, and signed a three year deal worth up to $47.5 million — a hefty deal considering Likely’s 2025 struggles in Baltimore. With the signing, the Giants “essentially swapped Likely in for Wan’Dale Robinson, signaling the shift in their offensive approach,” Duggan said (Robinson signed with the Titans). Likely will be “paired often” with TE Theo Johnson in a New York offense that should be among the league leaders in two tight end usage, just like Harbaugh’s Ravens, Duggan added. Likely, who should operate as a big slot receiver for Jaxson Dart, could have volume-based upside in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.headline: Andrew Thomas (groin) is not on the Giants’ final injury report for Week 7 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.analysis: Thomas has played through injuries in multiple games this year. Giants RT Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) and backup OT Marcus Mbow (knee) both resumed practicing in a limited capacity on Thursday and are officially questionable to play this week. The Texans’ defense has underperformed this year. Perhaps this is a get-right matchup for them.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.headline: Andrew Thomas (groin) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.analysis: Thomas, the team’s left tackle, RT Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) and backup OT Marcus Mbow (knee) are “all on the practice field participating to some degree in position drills during the media viewing period,” per USA Today’s Art Stapleton. This is good news for the Giants’ offense as a whole.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.headline: Andrew Thomas (groin) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.analysis: Thomas, the team’s left tackle, plus RT Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) and backup OT Marcus Mbow (knee) were all sidelined on Wednesday. Thomas played through a questionable tag last week. This unit is ailing. They face the Texans’ capable defensive line in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Abdul Carter (groin) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.analysis: Carter got in one limited practice to close the week before being listed as questionable. That would normally make him a coin-flip at best to play today, head coach John Harbaugh was optimistic about Carter’s health early in the week. He is good to go, as is left tackle Andrew Thomas, who is dealing with a groin injury. He has played through the groin issue several times already and will do so again versus the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.headline: Andrew Thomas (groin) is questionable for New York’s Week 6 game against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.analysis: This is a marked downgrade for Thomas, as he had been skipping plenty of practice days but at least had been cleared off the injury report on Fridays the last few weeks. John Harbaugh said Thomas was “basically full go” today, which seems sketchy in light of this listing. If we take the coach at his word, it seems likely that Thomas will play through this. Ditto Jermaine Eluemunor, who also is questionable after missing the first two days of practice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.headline: Andrew Thomas (groin) was seen working off to the side on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.analysis: Thomas, the Giants’ left tackle, RT Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) and EDGE Abdul Carter (calf) were all seen without jerseys, working on the side field with the training staff today. Expect to see all three listed as non-participants. Thomas has played through a couple of injuries this season, and seemingly has a good chance of suiting up in Week 6 against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.headline: Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.analysis: Eluemunor told reporters he felt his calf pop during Week 5 against the Commanders. He left the game and Marcus Mbow took his spot at right tackle. Head coach John Harbaugh called him day-to-day on Monday, so it’s at least not a long-term issue, though he still looks like a coin flip for Week 6. Left tackle Andrew Thomas did not practice, though that’s standard fare for him as he continues to play through a groin injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.headline: ESPN’s Jordan Raanan reports Giants RT Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) is feeling better post-game, but the team will have to see how he feels as the week progresses.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.analysis: According to Raanan, Eluemunor felt his calf pop and left today’s game against the Commanders. Fortunately, he was able to walk around on his own, which is a good sign. The Giants went to Marcus Mbow at right tackle in Eluemunor’s absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.headline: Andrew Thomas (groin) is not on New York’s final Week 4 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.analysis: Thomas is on the Terron Armstead plan — very limited practice reps, zero chance of him missing the game. He only got in a limited session on Friday after a pair of DNPs on Wednesday and Thursday. It does not actually seem to matter. Thomas will go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.headline: Giants RB Tyrone Tracy (knee) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andrew-tho.analysis: The Giants’ RB3 is seemingly on track to be active for Week 4 against the Cardinals. Unfortunately, Giants LT Andrew Thomas (groin) was not seen practicing during the portion of practice open to the media. He did not practice yesterday either and should currently be considered questionable to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Brian Branch (Achilles) is questionable for Detroit’s Week 7 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: After three full sessions this week, Branch is expected to be activated off reserve/PUP and should have no snap count per DC Kelvin Sheppard. He can be welcomed back to IDP lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Brian Branch (Achilles) is practicing in full ahead of Week 7’s game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: He seems likely to be activated off injured reserve after getting the Week 6 bye to get acclimated. Lions DC Kelvin Sheppard has said that Branch will not be on a snap count.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Lions ruled out C Cade Mays (wrist) for Week 5 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: Mays and S Brian Branch (Achilles) are not yet ready to return from their injuries. Starting CB Rock Ya-Sin (hamstring) has been ruled out as well, and DL Tyleik Williams (foot) is questionable to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Lions coach Dan Campbell said it will take a few weeks for S Brian Branch (Achilles) to ramp up before playing on game day.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: Branch has officially resumed practicing, but he has a 21-day practice window to bring himself up to speed. The team has handled Branch’s recovery responsibly thus far. He is unlikely to be rushed out there, no matter how poorly the Lions’ defense is playing. We do not expect him to face the Cardinals in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Lions S Brian Branch (Achilles) has a “really good chance” to return to practice next week, reports the Ringer’s Tom Pelissero.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: Branch is still on the PUP list after tearing his Achilles last season. Lions HC Dan Campbell said Branch was close to returning to practice on Friday, though he wouldn’t disclose when exactly the Lions will open the 21-day practice window for the 24-year-old safety. According to Pelissero, there’s a really good chance Branch returns to practice next week. He’ll undoubtedly help a Lions pass defense that has been torn to shreds in the first three weeks of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Lions head coach Dan Campbell said Brian Branch (Achilles) is “close” to returning to the field.
