https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: Campbell didn’t say when he expects Branch to return, but said the fourth-year safety “looks really good” as he continues to recover from a torn Achilles he suffered in Week 14 last season. The Lions haven’t opened Branch’s 21-day window for return, which will be the first sign that he’s nearing a comeback. Branch totaled 75 tackles, five TFLs, and 2.5 sacks for the Lions in 12 games last season and will be a welcome addition to a secondary that has allowed the most passing yards in the league through the first three weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Lions coach Dan Campbell said S Brian Branch (Achilles) “has a chance” to resume practicing sooner than S Kerby Joseph (knee), “but it won’t be this week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: Campbell spoke in a dejected tone when asked about the Lions’ safety duo returning to practice, particularly when discussing Joseph’s outlook. Campbell said Joseph did not suffer a setback, but stopped short of fully explaining the situation. It sounds like Joseph’s recovery stalled. The training staff was focused on strengthening Joseph’s knee, “but there was a little time there where we weren’t able to do everything we needed to do.” The Lions will not ask Joseph to play until he gets his knee as strong as it can possibly be, “and he feels comfortable.” Branch could return to practice in the coming weeks, but at this point, Joseph’s career status seems like it might be up in the air.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Lions place S Brian Branch on the reserve/physically unable to perform list with an Achilles injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: Branch ruptured an Achilles tendon in Week 14 last year. He is still recovering. The Lions also placed C Cade Mays (wrist) on the injured reserve/designated for return list due to his summer injury. Both players will be eligible to return after missing four games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Lions placed S Kerby Joseph on the active/PUP list with a knee injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: Just yesterday, Joseph implied via social media that he would avoid the physically unable to perform list. So much for that. Joseph dealt with a recurring knee issue for the entire 2025 season, which was first reported on at the end of July 2025, roughly three months after the Lions made him the NFL’s highest-paid safety. Given Joseph’s post, one imagines he has a chance to resume practicing relatively soon, but only time will tell. Branch suffered an Achilles tendon rupture in Week 14 last year. As of June 13th, Lions coach Dan Campbell said there was no timetable for his return. The Lions also placed TE Tyler Conklin on the physically unable to perform list.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.headline: Lions coach Dan Campbell told reporters there’s no timetable on S Brian Branch (Achilles) to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brian-bran.analysis: Campbell said that Branch hasn’t had any setbacks in his recovery from a torn Achilles, but wouldn’t put a timeline on the 24-year-old safety’s eventual return. Branch attended practice in a T-shirt and shorts on Thursday. Campbell jokingly set the timetable for Branch to return in December, just so the media would stop asking about it. Christian Izien and Chuck Clark continue to take the first-team safety reps for the Lions in practice with Branch and Kerby Joseph (knee) sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Cade Mays (wrist) is questionable for Detroit’s Week 7 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Questionable but fully expected to play after three full practices, Mays should add some more teeth to the Lions’ run game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions C Cade Mays (wrist) is practicing in full ahead of Week 7’s game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Mays seems likely to be activated off injured reserve ahead of the game given Dan Campbell’s public statements on the matter, him giving a presser today, and the trend to full sessions following the team’s Week 6 bye. It should be an upgrade for Detroit’s offensive line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions ruled out C Cade Mays (wrist) for Week 5 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Mays and S Brian Branch (Achilles) are not yet ready to return from their injuries. Starting CB Rock Ya-Sin (hamstring) has been ruled out as well, and DL Tyleik Williams (foot) is questionable to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions activated C Cade Mays’ (wrist) 21-day practice window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: This is a big deal for fantasy purposes. The Lions signed Mays to a three-year, $25 million contract this offseason, shoring up their center position with a reliable prime-age starter. Mays injured his wrist early in August, so he has not yet taken the field on game day with his new team. The Lions’ permissive defense continues to put the offense into pass-heavy game scripts. Getting Mays back on the field will fortify Jared Goff’s protection. He was limited on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions place S Brian Branch on the reserve/physically unable to perform list with an Achilles injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Branch ruptured an Achilles tendon in Week 14 last year. He is still recovering. The Lions also placed C Cade Mays (wrist) on the injured reserve/designated for return list due to his summer injury. Both players will be eligible to return after missing four games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions HC Dan Campbell said C Cade Mays (wrist) will miss a “significant amount of time.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: The Lions sought to upgrade at center this offseason and went out and signed Mays to a three-year, $25 million contract. Now, the 27-year-old lineman is expected to be sidelined for the next 8-10 weeks after fracturing a small bone in his wrist , per NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport. Campbell said that the injury is not believed to be season-ending, but it’s still a major blow to the offensive line. Former second-round pick Juice Scruggs came over in the David Montgomery trade and has played center before, so he will presumably get the first crack at taking over in Mays’ absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Lions agreed to terms with C Cade Mays, formerly of the Panthers, on a three-year, $25 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: A boost for Jahmyr Gibbs! Mays is a huge power-blocking 6-foot-6, 325-pound center and should help solidify a troubled interior line for the Lions. It allows them to leave Christian Mahogany and Tate Ratledge at guard and makes Juice Scruggs a depth piece.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Panthers OG Chandler Zavala (calf) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Zavala suffered the calf injury in Panthers’ Week 12 loss to the 49ers and starts out the week not practicing. Also out was C Cade Mays (ankle). Jake Curhan and Austin Corbett are in line to start for Zavala and Mays, respectively, if neither can play in Week 13.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Panthers re-signed C Cade Mays to a one-year, $3.3 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Mays was a restricted free agent, and the Panthers chose to tender him at the original round level. As a former sixth-round pick, Mays was then allowed to look for an offer as a free agent. The Panthers could then match that offer or let him walk in exchange for a sixth-round pick from his new team. With no takers on the open market, Mays returns for a camp battle with Austin Corbett for the starting center job this summer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.headline: Panthers selected Tennessee OG Cade Mays with the No. 199 overall pick in the 2022 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-mays/.analysis: Mays (6’5/311) was a top-25 overall recruit who started for two years at Georgia before transferring home to start his final two campaigns at Tennessee. Despite missing three games with a left foot injury in 2021, Mays earned second-team All-SEC honors for his work as the Vols’ right tackle. He has five-position versatility along with his four years of starting experience. Mays also impressed with a 75th-percentile relative athletic score during pre-draft testing. Mays’ play strength stands out on tape, both as a drive-blocker in the run game and when dropping the anchor in pass-pro. His biggest issue is a propensity to pop up and play high with a narrow base, gifting the leverage advantage to opponents while compromising his balance. Like Matt Slauson, Mays may need to iron out the kinks early in his career before entering a starting lineup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: The Athletic’s Dan Duggan believes Cam Skattebo “will be back in the mix” in Week 7 against the Texans, likely in “some sort of timeshare with Tyrone Tracy and Devin Singletary.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Sigh. Three-player backfields are generally fantasy-unfriendly situations, and this one is no different. Skattebo is a capable dual-threat player who has seemingly been limited by the significant ankle injury he suffered last year. The Giants could get him more involved in the passing game, but Tracy can contribute there as well, muddying that opportunity. Singletary would not be a contributor for many NFL teams, but lucky him, he’s a New York Giant. Skattebo and Tracy are viable FLEX options, though both are likely touchdown-dependent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: SNY TV’s Connor Hughes believes the Giants will likely try to trade for a running back, and Cam Skattebo is unlikely to return to his prior role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Hughes makes clear that he thinks Skattebo’s time as the clear-cut lead back is over, recapping coach John Harbaugh’s offseason attempts to acquire a bellcow, while noting that Skattebo is currently in the doghouse. Hughes believes Skattebo is a nice complementary player who can function as a physical change-of-pace option. The biggest issue the Giants face in replacing him is cost. He thinks a player like Jonathan Taylor will cost a Day 2 pick, at least, and he is not sure Taylor is worth that, given the Giants’ long-term plans for the 2027 draft capital they’ve accrued via various personnel moves. Trading away Kayvon Thibodeaux is an option, but doing so is challenging with Brian Burns (knee) out for the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Giants released Najee Harris.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: The move comes a couple days after Harris criticized the New York coaching staff for its handling of the backfield touch distribution. “It’s hard to get into a rhythm with one or two plays...if you’re getting a play here and then get taken out for a series, there’s nothing you could do,” Harris said after the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the Saints. “I’ve never been through none of this before.” Harris had 31 rushes for 99 scoreless yards before getting the boot. With Harris gone, Cam Skattebo could get another chance to see increased playing time after being all but benched last week. Tyrone Tracy, who led the team in rushing attempts against New Orleans, could be the de facto lead back for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Giants coach John Harbaugh, asked about the running back room, said carries are “earned” and told his players to “do something” in their opportunities and more will come.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Tyrone Tracy appeared to do the most with his opportunities last week, scoring the game’s only two touchdowns. Najee Harris was bottled up and Cam Skattebo was soft benched while Devin Singletary led the team in snaps while they were in comeback mode for most of the second half. By the letter of what he’s offering here, Tracy is probably the player who should get the majority of the snaps against the Texans. In actuality, we have no idea what will happen here and this quote doesn’t really help us. “I don’t like (rotating backs) either,” Harbaugh said per The Athletic’s Dan Duggan after the game. “One of those guys needs to step up. Somebody needs to step up and be the back. And none of those guys have done that yet.” We suspect we’ll be diving beat writer opinions ahead of Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo saw zero carries in the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Before the game, it was widely reported that the Giants would start Najee Harris with Skattebo dealing with fumbling issues to start the season. This was indeed the case as Skattebo saw zero touches and just six snaps on the day, last among all four Giants running backs. After the game, head coach John Harbaugh insisted the team did not bench Skattebo, but it’s hard to see this as anything else. Fantasy managers will be hoping Skattebo will be out of the dog house after no Giants running backs surpassed 20 yards rushing against a poor Saints run defense. He is cautiously in the RB3 ranks until further notice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Najee Harris is “set to start” for the Giants in Week 6 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Fowler was adding to a report from Jordan Raanan , who said Harris is “likely to have a larger role with Cam Skattebo downgraded but still part of the mix after the fumbles.” Skattebo has indeed struggled with fumbles, putting the ball on the ground four times this year. No running back has more fumbles, and Skattebo’s most recent blunder cost the Giants a shot at an overtime win versus the Commanders last week. They instead settled for a tie. Even if Skattebo winds up leading the team in carries this week, he was only valuable for fantasy managers because of his high-volume role. With that out the window, Skattebo is buried in the RB3 ranks for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Giants coach John Harbaugh said “We’ll see. We’ll find out,” when asked if the Giants have reached the point where he’ll make adjustments due to the team’s fumbling issues.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Giants beat writer Dan Duggan chimed in with “I would be very surprised if [Cam] Skattebo has the same RB1 workload on Sunday that he’s had in the first five games.” Skattebo has put the ball on the ground four times in the first five games. Najee Harris has one in 27 carries and Tyrone Tracy has added two. It sounds like Harris may start to be a significant thorn in the side of Skattebo-reliant managers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo rushed 13 times for 59 yards in the Giants’ Week 5 tie with the Commanders, adding two receptions for 12 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Skattebo rushed for just 12 yards on six carries in the first half as he and the Giants struggled on the ground for most of the day. He would come up with a few big runs in the second half, one of which resulted in a 19-yard gain in overtime as the Giants were attempting to drive into position for a game-winning field goal. Unfortunately for Skattebo, disaster struck later on the drive when he lost a fumble on the Commanders’ 24-yard line, which was recovered by Washington and ended any hopes of a Giants’ victory. Poor late-game clock management by the Commanders made Skattebo’s fumble a little less costly, as the two sides would end Sunday’s game in a tie, but it’s impossible to overstate how big a 4-1 start to the season would be for the Giants, who are playing in a struggling NFC East. Skattebo hasn’t rushed for more than 81 yards in any game this season and has only one touchdown to his name. His reliable volume continues to put him in fringe RB1/RB2 territory, but it’s been a disappointing start for the second-year back. He’ll look to turn things around next week against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Cam Skattebo’s shoulder injury is “not a concern.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Skattebo was cleared from the injury report on Friday, so he was never going to miss this game. The good news is that the Giants don’t have any plans to limit his workload. Playing in a rain-soaked matchup with the NFC East rival Commanders, Skattebo is expected to see “an extremely heavy workload”, according to Garafolo.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.headline: Cam Skattebo (shoulder) will play in Week 5 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-skatte.analysis: Skattebo was limited in Wednesday and Thursday’s practices but will be good to go in what he called a “slogfest” on Sunday against the Commanders. With rain and wind forecast for Sunday’s game, the Giants will likely lean heavily on Skattebo, who has rushed for 68-235-1 this season while averaging a subpar 3.5 YPC. Skattebo profiles as a volume-based RB2 against a defense that has been stout against the run out of the gate.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 7 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: He practiced in full twice on Thursday and Friday. With Ja’Kobi Lane eating into his targets and the Bengals ever-vulnerable through the air by tight ends, Bateman is probably only a deep-league play in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Bateman has been playing through this shoulder injury for a while, though he was forced to leave early last week. Bateman should now be expected to play, but he is only a boom-bust FLEX option with Ja’Kobi Lane now back in the lineup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Bateman left the Ravens’ Week 6 game against the Browns and did not return, though head coach Jesse Minter told reporters on Monday that he was going to be fine. Expect the team to manage his reps in practice this week with an eye on getting him ready for Sunday. Bateman has made a handful of splash plays this year, but his production is low-volume and high-variance. He will be a low-end FLEX option for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said there’s optimism that Rashod Bateman (shoulder) will “be fine.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Sounds like another week of managed reps in practice is ahead for Bateman, but he’ll likely have a reasonable chance to suit up in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) will not return in Week 6 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: We’re not quite sure when this injury occurred, but Bateman was dealing with a shoulder injury throughout the week. He was removed from the final injury report on Friday. Bateman’s day ends without a reception on one target.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Bateman was a surprise DNP on Thursday, but got in a full session today. He remains an uninspiring FLEX option against the Browns in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Bateman played through the shoulder injury last week. He was limited yesterday, but coach Jesse Minter said he wasn’t worried. Downgrading to a DNP is not a good sign. Meanwhile, Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is practicing fully this week and could hop right into WR2 duties for the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: We won’t know what Bateman’s injury is until the Ravens drop their first injury report of Week 6 later today, but head coach Jesse Minter wasn’t worried. He downplayed the issue and told reporters he expects Bateman to play this week. Barring a setback, Bateman will remain a deep-cut FLEX option for Week 6 versus the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman caught 5-of-6 targets for 62 yards in the Ravens’ Week 5 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Bateman had a relatively quiet game until notching 38 yards on three receptions on the team’s final possession of regulation, helping to spur an improbable comeback victory in overtime. The team took the ball with just over two minutes remaining down by eight, eventually driving the field and tacking on a two-point conversion to send the game to extra time. Bateman remains a shaky FLEX option for as long as Zay Flowers remains healthy. He won’t be worth starting in most leagues in a Week 6 meeting with the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) is not on Baltimore’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: He’ll play. It won’t matter for fantasy football players. Tyler Huntley seems much less likely to randomly connect with Bateman downfield than Lamar Jackson did, and even Jackson was barely doing it much.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashod-bat.analysis: Despite being listed as full, Bateman played in a red non-contact jersey per reporters. We suppose this technically qualifies as “fantasy football news” but Bateman isn’t a real threat to do much in Week 5, especially with Tyler Huntley likely under center for the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle) is not on Kansas City’s final Week 7 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: He’ll be a reliable TE1, even in a tough matchup against Seattle’s defense, as the Chiefs simply don’t have many other Trusted Mahomes Targets healthy for this one. It’s essentially just Kelce and Xavier Worthy healthy of Kansas City’s main targets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Kelce should be good to go for the Chiefs’ Week 7 game against the Seahawks. At 37 years old, he does not need to practice fully in order to play, though it would be nice to see him upgrade to full participation tomorrow. If active, he is a locked-in TE1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Kelce played through an ankle issue in Week 6, catching five passes for 53 yards. Despite not playing at full health, he was still second on the team in targets. Kelce starts out the week as a limited practice participant and it would be a surprise if he misses National Tight End Day this week against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce caught 5-of-6 targets for 53 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Kelce was in and out of the lineup in the first half while dealing with a lingering ankle issue. Though he clearly wasn’t 100 percent, Kelce was second on the team (behind Xavier Worthy) in targets and had a 24-yard catch and run reception in the second half. Kelce, who now has nine catches over his past three games, should see more looks from Patrick Mahomes for as long as Rashee Rice (hamstring) is sidelined. He’ll be a top-15 fantasy play in Week 7 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce caught 2-of-4 targets for 15 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 4 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Kelce was held in check throughout the entirety of this one and has been targeted just six times in his last two games. Were it not for an 11-yard score in last week’s win over the Dolphins, we would be looking at back-to-back disappointing fantasy weeks for the future Hall of Famer. Kelce and the Chiefs are now heading into their bye week. He could see an increase in targets with Rashee Rice (hamstring) and Tyquan Thornton (ankle) both at risk of missing multiple weeks, but Kelce now has three games on his 2026 ledger with five or fewer targets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce caught 2-of-2 targets for 59 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 3 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Both Kelce’s catches and targets were his fewest of the young season, though he made them count on an afternoon where Patrick Mahomes dropped back only 25 times. Kelce notched a 48-yard catch-and-run on the first offensive play of the game, then finished off the Chiefs’ last real drive with an 11-yard touchdown grab in the back of the end zone. Why he went so long between looks can be a question for another day. Sitting on 231 yards receiving through the Chiefs’ first three contests, Kelce will remain a strong TE1 for Week 4 in Vegas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce caught 9-of-11 targets for 101 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 2 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Kelce continues to do the bulk of his damage within 10 yards of the line of scrimmage while running a high percentage of hitch routes, but the volume of passing and inside-funnel matchup aided in him eclipsing 100 yards through the air for the first time since Week 8 of 2024. That game also happened to be an overtime win, meaning the only two times since Week 7 of 2023 in which Kelce has gone over 100 yards have gone to overtime. Even so, Kelce continues to be a solid outlet for quarterback Patrick Mahomes and should continue to see games of spiked volume when the Chiefs are pushed, as they were by the Colts. That is unlikely to be the case in Week 3 when the Chiefs travel to Miami to face the Dolphins, where Mahomes will be a shaky TE1 bet in fantasy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: Travis Kelce caught 3-of-5 targets for 71 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 1 win over the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Kelce passed Jason Witten to move into second on the all-time tight end receiving list with a 59-yard catch-and-run in the third quarter. Even so, the veteran tight end lacked any semblance of the burst that once made him a matchup nightmare, slow out of breaks while appearing to take multiple plays off that were not drawn up for him. His once-strong connection with quarterback Patrick Mahomes also looked off on the two incompletions directed his way, both bad misses. It will likely take time for the timing to resurface between the two and Kelce appears unlikely to command meaningful volume, leaving him as a middling TE2 ahead of a soft matchup against the Colts in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: The Kansas City Star’s Pete Sweeney reports that Chiefs TE Travis Kelce was not seen during the voluntary organized team activities viewing session on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Today’s session was voluntary and Kelce is entering his 13th NFL season. We would love it if he were there, but we are not worried about his absence. Kelce signed a three-year extension late in March and will once again man the TE1 spot in Kansas City this season. The Chiefs have another three-day OTA run from June 1-3. Mandatory minicamp goes from June 9-11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.headline: CBS Sports’ John Breech believes the Chiefs could pursue Kyle Pitts in a trade.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-kel.analysis: Kansas City, Breech said, “should be the first team to give them a call about making a possible deal” for Pitts, who is reportedly on the trade block, per ESPN’s Adam Schefter. “The Chiefs currently have two first-round picks heading into the draft and they would likely be able to get a deal done by sending just one of those to Atlanta.” Breech said dealing Pitts, entering his age-26 season, would free up some much-needed salary cap space for the Falcons and give them a first-round draft pick, which they do not have at the moment. Pitts, Breech said, would be the “heir apparent” to Travis Kelce, 36, who re-signed with the Chiefs last month after briefly considering retirement for a third straight offseason. Pitts in 2025 had 88 receptions for 928 yards and five touchdowns, a career season. KC last year ranked 11th in two tight end usage (28 percent).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 7 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears has been active off a questionable line twice since Week 4. We’d imagine he’d get there again after a limited Friday session. The touch upside just isn’t there for him to be more than a deep-league FLEX play at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears notched a one-yard carry and seven-yard reception in the Titans’ Week 6 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears’ two touches were a new season low, though he’s now been held to three or fewer in three of the past four weeks. The Titans have decided Tony Pollard is more of an every-down back than committee member, erasing what had been low-end FLEX status for his “1B” backfield partner. Despite his supposed contingency value, Spears is droppable if you find yourself in a roster crunch.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears is active for Tennessee’s Week 6 game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: He was questionable after a full practice, but will play against the Colts as a reasonable-if-unexciting FLEX option. Inactive for the Titans are S Kevin Winston Jr., CB Alontae Taylor (coach’s decision), RB Nick Singleton, T Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, TE Kylen Granson, DL Jordan Elliott and DT Jackie Marshall.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 6 game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears didn’t practice Thursday but was a full-go on Friday. He’ll be a sketchy FLEX option against the Colts in Week 6 assuming he plays; it sure does seem like he will after a full session.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: It was a surprising downgrade from Wednesday’s limited session, putting Spears’ status for Week 6 into real question. If he sits, we’re not entirely sure which Titans third-string back would get breather duties. Kalel Mullings, who was a practice squad activation, got the only non-Tony Pollard/Spears snap in Week 5. Nicholas Singleton and Michael Carter are also both on the active roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (knee) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: The Titans’ receiving specialist has been an injury report staple thus far, though he has previously been listed with an ankle issue. An early-week limited session puts him on track to play, though he is only relevant in PPR leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears rushed two times for zero yards, adding nine catches for 28 yards on nine targets, in Tennessee’s Week 5 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: He fumbled away one of his rushes, but with the Titans trailing for most of the second half, piled up nine catches as Cam Ward sought refuge from Houston’s pass rush. His final catch of the day — we’re not kidding — came as Ward threw it at him despite Spears having already crumpled to the ground. It lost six yards. Given the Colts likely won’t do this against the Titans next week, Spears is probably not going to keep lines like this going.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears rushed two times for seven yards in the Titans’ Week 4 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears also caught his lone target for what resulted in a one-yard loss. It was yet another underwhelming game for Spears, who has totaled a combined 40 yards from scrimmage in his last two games on eight touches. There’s nothing of fantasy value here. Spears can be left off the fantasy radar for Week 5’s game against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: Tyjae Spears (ankle) is active for Week 4 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears is good to go for Sunday’s game against the Ravens after entering the weekend listed as questionable. He has totaled 99 scoreless yards from scrimmage this season on 17 touches, and has caught four passes on the year. Spears shouldn’t be considered as anything more than a fringe RB3/RB4 against a stout Ravens defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Tyjae Spears (ankle) is expected to play in Week 4 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyjae-spea.analysis: Spears played through the ankle issue last week and there was no indication during this week’s practice that he suffered any sort of setback. He is good to go for Week 4, though fantasy managers can’t count on him for much. He touched the ball just three times last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield (thumb) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles told reporters earlier today that Mayfield “looks like he’s ready to go” for this week’s game. Mayfield seemingly has solid odds of suiting up this week, but we must wait for an official ruling. Hopefully, that arrives tomorrow. If active, Mayfield will play with a protective plate on the back of his glove to help keep his recently dislocated thumb in place. He is a QB2 for the occasion, if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Baker Mayfield (thumb) “looks like he’s ready to go” for Week 7 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield was a full participant in practice all week and should be removed from the team’s final injury report when it’s released later in the day. Mayfield is expected to wear a protective glove on his throwing hand, which should prevent injury to the thumb he dislocated in Week 3, and will be on the QB2 radar in what is a must-win game for the 1-5 Buccaneers. Hopefully he can improve on a rough start to the season in which he threw for 615-2-2 in his first three games while completing 63.5 percent of his passes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield said his injured thumb has “gotten to a place where it’s strong enough to play” in Week 7 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield has played through injuries regularly over the years. We expect him to be out there for the Buccaneers’ Week 7 game against the division rival Panthers. He is a QB2 for his first game back. A run-heavy game plan could be in the works as they ease him in. If his thumb really is good to go, though, this game could turn into a shootout. He practiced in full for the second time this week on Thursday, and told reporters that he will play with a protective plate on the back of his glove to help prevent re-injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield (thumb) practiced in full on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield going down as a full participant is a bit of a surprise given that it’s his first time practicing in any capacity since Week 3. Todd Bowles told reporters earlier this week that the team was preparing for Jalon Daniels to start. Now it looks like Mayfield may be the favorite to draw the start versus Carolina. This is ultimately a rather ambiguous situation, likely by Bowles’ design. Fantasy managers should have a backup plan in place if they are counting on either of the Bucs’ quarterbacks this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield (thumb) returned to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield hasn’t played since dislocating his thumb in Week 3. As of late last week, he hadn’t even thrown a football since suffering the injury. Todd Bowles told reporters on Monday that he’s preparing for Jalon Daniels to start, but Mayfield’s return to practice puts things up in the air. His practice statuses over the next few days will be telling. For now, fantasy managers should still plan on seeing Daniels under center, but this is a situation to monitor throughout the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said Baker Mayfield (thumb) is “supposed to practice Wednesday.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Bowles has already said that the team is preparing as if Jalon Daniels will start in Week 7, but the team will be evaluating Mayfield to see how he is progressing in his recovery from a dislocated thumb. Mayfield reportedly pushed to play last week after throwing on Monday, but his thumb swelled up, which factored into the decision to sit him in Week 6’s loss to the Steelers. Given Bowles’ comments about the team’s plans entering the week, it sounds like Mayfield is at risk of missing at least one more game, but we’ll see how his hand responds when he gets on the field on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said the team is planning as if Jalon Daniels will start in Week 7 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Bowles said this week will be an important evaluation week for Baker Mayfield, who is still rehabbing a dislocated thumb that has sidelined him since Week 3. Daniels hasn’t been overly impressive in his three starts this season, throwing for 501 yards, three touchdowns and five interceptions while also taking nine sacks. That said, he did manage to pull off a win over the Cowboys in Week 5 and had the Buccaneers in position to beat the Steelers in Week 6 before Pittsburgh erupted for 16 points in the fourth quarter to force overtime. We’ll see how things unfold throughout the week, but it sounds like Mayfield is at least one week away from returning. Daniels would be on the fantasy radar as a low-end QB2 if he gets the start against Carolina.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports there’s “optimism” Baker Mayfield (thumb) will return in Week 7 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Mayfield didn’t practice this week, but according to Buccaneers HC Todd Bowles he threw on Monday and was pushing to play before his “thumb swelled up on him.” It seems like Mayfield is trending in the right direction and that he could return against the Panthers in Week 7 if the swelling is no longer an issue. Jalon Daniels is starting for Tampa Bay again in Week 6 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: NFL on Prime’s James Palmer reports that Baker Mayfield threw on “Monday as he was pushing hard to play and the thumb swelled up on him.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles gets another tick in the obfuscation column. On Wednesday, Bowles told reporters that Mayfield has not resumed throwing yet. Today, Palmer tells us that Mayfield “was pushing hard to play,” and, perhaps briefly, resumed throwing on Monday. Apparently, his thumb reacted poorly. Palmer adds that Mayfield is “getting better,” but that does not necessarily mean he will be able to play next week. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.headline: Baker Mayfield (thumb) will not play in Tampa Bay’s Week 6 game against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/baker-mayf.analysis: It’ll be the Jalon Daniels show again. Mayfield did not practice at any point this week. Todd Bowles tried to tell us that it was too early to tell earlier today; it wasn’t. We’ll need to see Mayfield on the practice field next week before we think he has a real shot to play against the Panthers in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley (hip) is questionable for Tennessee’s Week 7 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: He didn’t practice Thursday or Friday, and we’d consider him on the pessimistic side of questionable. Not that you were thinking about playing him anyway.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley (hip) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Firmly off the fantasy radar when healthy, Ridley downgraded from a limited session on Wednesday and does not seem likely to play in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley (hip) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: The 31-year-old player has a hip injury. Ridley mostly runs cardio and game day and is not fantasy-relevant at this time. Were he to sit, Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike could get more playing time — which would be a positive outcome for the offense as a whole.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley caught 2-of-3 targets for 33 yards in Tennessee’s Week 5 loss to the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Is this doing anything for anybody? Ridley had a 23-yarder to open the game and vanished thereafter. He has not cracked more than two catches or three targets all year and does not need to be in fantasy consideration in the vast, vast majority of leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley failed to catch his only target in the Titans’ Week 3 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Ridley has been held without a catch in 2-of-3 games this year. He’s losing routes to Elic Ayomanor and not earning targets when on the field. He can be cut even in the deepest of leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley caught 2-of-2 targets for 35 yards in the Titans’ Week 2 loss to the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: The grabs were Ridley’s first two of the season. He also cost the Titans with a 15-yard personal foul penalty. Although it’s good to see Ridley’s Week 1 doughnut was something of an aberration, it’s not like he can be counted on for high-volume days going forward as the Titans sort out the rotation in their revamped skill corps. Despite his pedigree, Ridley can be safely left on 12-team league waiver wires.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Calvin Ridley was not targeted in the Titans’ Week 1 loss to the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Ridley’s 25 routes run were good for third-most among Titans receivers in Sunday’s loss, but the 31-year-old receiver went without a target despite his team trailing the entire game. Any hope that Ridley would improve on last year’s 17-303-0 performance will need to be put on hold for now, as Ridley and the Titans offense as a whole struggled mightily in the season opener.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll said the team’s downfield passing attack has to improve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Cam Ward’s preseason has been as bad or even worse than his rookie campaign. Ward in last week’s preseason game against Seattle completed eight of his 12 attempts for 69 yards. His average depth of target on completed passes this preseason sits at a meager 1.2 . Carnell Tate, meanwhile, has been targeted five times on his 23 preseason routes and does not have a reception to show for it. Daboll has been somewhat defensive this month when asked about Ward’s immense struggles after working on basic fundamentals with the second-year QB in the offseason. Ward, one of the most inaccurate passers in recent NFL history, is unlikely to support more than one fantasy-viable pass catcher in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: ESPN’s Turron Davenport reports that Titans OC Brian Daboll’s intent to improve on third down was a “key reason” for signing WR Wan’Dale Robinson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Davenport penned a lengthy piece detailing how OC Brian Daboll is focused on developing QB Cam Ward’s play on third down, in the red zone and in the two-minute drill. This is pretty straightforward. Those are all high-leverage situations, so harping on Ward’s performance there makes sense. Robinson played on all three drives in the Titans’ first preseason game while veteran Calvin Ridley was on the field for one. Rookie WR Carnell Tate was on the field for the first and third drives. A featured role on third downs could help Robinson return FLEX value — he’s certainly being paid like he is going to be featured.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.headline: Titans coach Robert Saleh said Calvin Ridley (leg) will participate in 7-on-7 drills on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/calvin-rid.analysis: Ridley suffered a broken fibula in Week 11 of the 2025 season and missed the remainder of the year. He hadn’t participated in any 7-on-7 or team drills up until this point, making today’s participation a major step in the right direction. Ridley agreed to a restructured deal to stay in Tennessee this offseason. He will tumble to third in the pecking order for targets now that Carnell Tate and Wan’Dale Robinson are both in the fold. That should still allow for the occasional splash play, but fantasy managers should look elsewhere for FLEX options.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Bucky Irving (illness) is not on the Buccaneers’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: As is typically the case with ill players, Irving is good to go for this week’s game. He upgraded to full participation today after getting a limited session in on Thursday. The Buccaneers’ No. 1 running back has been a volatile producer this season, yet even with last week’s flop, he still totaled 21 touches. That type of workload keeps him firmly in the RB2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Bucky Irving (illness) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: The Buccaneers’ No. 1 running back is on track to play in Week 7 against the Panthers. The offense is expected to be led by Baker Mayfield (thumb), who will play with a protective plate on his hand to prevent re-injury. Irving should be good to go this week and can be treated as a high-end RB2, as usual.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Bucky Irving (illness) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: Players missing time because of an illness this early in the weekend almost always get cleared to play by Sunday. We expect no difference from Irving. Coming off his third 20-touch game of the year, Irving remains a high-end RB2 for his Week 7 date with the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Bucky Irving rushed 19 times for 46 yards in the Bucs’ Week 6 loss to the Steelers, adding two catches for three yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: Irving was bottled up on nearly every attempt, with the Steelers’ defensive front simply winning the battle in the trenches far too often. On the bright side, Irving out-carried Kenneth Gainwell 19-2 and saw three targets to Gainwell’s one. The role was there. The production was not. That role was also bolstered by the absence of Sean Tucker, who missed today’s game with a quad injury. Irving will remain in the RB2 mix for Week 7 versus the Panthers, but Tampa Bay’s grizzly offensive environment will prevent him from cracking the RB1 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Sean Tucker (quad) is not expected to play in Week 6 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: Despite seeing just eight total carries this year, Tucker has two attempts inside the five compared to one for Bucky Irving. Though he isn’t leaving that many total carries behind, Tucker’s absence will still create some extra fantasy value for Irving, who is on the RB1/2 border for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: FOX Sports’ Greg Auman reports that Sean Tucker (quad) will be a pregame decision for Week 6 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: Tucker is officially listed as questionable. If he ends up being inactive, that is good news for Bucky Irving, who handled 23 touches last week, ceding seven to Kenny Gainwell and five to Tucker. Irving warrants borderline RB1/2 treatment at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Bucky Irvin rushed 21 times for 165 yards and a touchdown in the Buccaneers’ Week 5 win over the Cowboys, adding 10 yards and a touchdown on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: Irving cashed in on an early touchdown on the team’s first possession on a reception from quarterback Jalon Daniels on a leak to the right side of the formation, otherwise having a relatively quiet first half. Things would change in a hurry after the break as Irving ripped off a 72-yard explosive run on the first play from scrimmage in the third quarter. He would cash in on his second trip to paint on the following drive from one yard out before somewhat confusingly retreating to the sideline without his helmet the following two possessions. That raised speculation that his glute injury had flared up, a notion he would dispel in the fourth quarter as he helped to ice the game. This game goes down as his first 100-yard rushing game since Week 16 of his rookie season in 2024. Irving remains a volatile RB2 ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Bucky Irving rushed 16 times for 61 yards in the Bucs’ Week 4 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: A 16-touch outing isn’t bad for Irving, but the touches he did lose were extremely painful. Sean Tucker scored a goal line touchdown late in the second quarter and Kenneth Gainwell caught a touchdown from 10 yards out at the top of the fourth. Irving didn’t even see a target. It was his first game of the year without a catch. Irving remains the lead back for the Bucs, but a lack of high-value touches would cripple his fantasy value. He will be just inside the RB2 range for his Week 5 matchup with the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Bucky Irving (glute) is not on Tampa Bay’s final Week 4 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: He finally got in a full session on Friday after a pair of limited practices on Wednesday and Thursday. Irving will be hard to trust with Jalon Daniels under center in Week 4 but the volume should still be there to get him on the low-end RB2 line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.headline: Bucky Irving (glute) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bucky-irvi.analysis: The Buccaneers’ starting running back is on track to play, but consecutive limited sessions suggest this isn’t something that can simply be written off right now. Irving missed time in the fourth quarter last week with the injury. Earlier today, OC Zac Robinson indicated that the team would like to get RB2 Kenny Gainwell and RB3 Sean Tucker more involved. He cited game flow and poor production as the reasons for Gainwell’s minimal involvement. Neither aspect is guaranteed to change, and the game scripts have already been falling in Gainwell’s favor. Tucker’s range of outcomes might be wider. Regardless, Irving remains the starter and should play in Week 4 against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: Ashton Dulin (hamstring) is not on Indianapolis’ final Week 7 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: With Tyler Warren down, Dulin probably figures to join Keenan Allen and Josh Downs as one of Indianapolis’ three main receivers. He has some desperation play viability in deeper leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: Ashton Dulin (hamstring) won’t play in Indianapolis’ Week 5 game against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: After dealing with an ankle injury that sidelined him most of the first three weeks, Dulin picked up a hamstring injury and did not practice all week before being ruled out ahead of this game. Laquon Treadwell prayer starts remain on the fantasy football menu.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: Ashton Dulin (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: Dulin made his 2026 debut in Week 4 after missing the first three games of the year with an ankle injury. He’s now at risk of returning to the bench because of this hamstring injury. With Keenan Allen back at practice, Dulin’s role was going to decline either way. Laquon Treadwell would be the team’s No. 3 receiver if he is ruled out for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: Ashton Dulin caught 3-of-6 targets for 29 yards in the Colts’ Week 4
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: Dulin was active for the first time this year. His return could not have come at a better time with Keenan Allen ruled out over the weekend. Dulin took on a starting role and wound up leading the team in targets, tied with Laquon Treadwell. The Colts couldn’t get much going through the air and settled for spreading the ball around instead of peppering their top pass-catchers with targets. It’s hard to imagine them taking that approach again in Week 5. Even if they do, Dulin is more of a thorn in the sides of Tyler Warren and Josh Downs than a FLEX option in his own right.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: Ashton Dulin (ankle) will play in Week 4 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: With Keenan Allen ruled out and Alec Pierce on IR, Dulin is now in line to be the Colts’ No. 2 receiver in his season debut. The passing attack will run through Josh Downs, putting him comfortably inside the WR2 ranks. Inactive for the Colts are WR Keenan Allen, WR Darius Slayton, RB DJ Giddens, QB Riley Leonard, EDGE George Gumbs, and OG Dalton Tucker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: Colts WR Ashton Dulin (ankle) will not play in Indianapolis’ Week 3 game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: Laquon Treadwell prayer starts are officially on the menu for Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: Colts declared WR Ashton Dulin, LB Austin Ajiake, RB DJ Giddens, DE George Gumbs, QB Riley Leonard, and G Dalton Tucker inactive for Week 2 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: No real surprises here as the Colts look to snap the longest active losing streak in the league, having lost their previous eight games dating back to last season. Alec Pierce could see an increase in snaps and utilization after week of healthy practices.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: Alec Pierce (heel) is practicing in full for Week 2 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: The Athletic’s James Boyd noted that Pierce also had his wrist X-rayed after the game, though neither that nor the heel injury is a concern for him going forward. Ashton Dulin missed practice with a hamstring injury. Pierce was targeted six times in Week 1 despite having his snaps limited. He caught four passes for 61 yards. He will be a boom/bust WR3 for his Week 3 matchup with Kansas City.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: The Athletic’s James Boyd believes Ashton Dulin is the team’s third receiver “for now.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: He mentions Nick Westbrook-Ikhine and seventh-round pick Deion Burks as possible competition for the spot. We also (our speculation) wouldn’t rule out the Colts picking up one of the several as-of-yet unsigned free agents like Jauan Jennings, Deebo Samuel, or Stefon Diggs. Westbrook-Ikhine has flashed big touchdown upside in the past and would be the most fantasy-useful player in this group if he wins a role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.headline: Colts coach Shane Steichen said WR Ashton Dulin (hamstring) will “miss some time.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-dul.analysis: The Colts later placed Dulin on injured reserve. Dulin’s major fantasy football impact this year was mainly keeping Adonai Mitchell on the bench in Week 5, but this leaves the Colts thin behind their top three receivers and should keep their snap counts high in Week 13 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Bam Knight will handle “a lot of work” on early downs with Jeremiyah Love (ankle) sidelined.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: LaFleur simply does not believe that any one running back can handle a full-time role and remain healthy, so he employs a committee approach. Although Tyler Allgeier sits ahead of Knight on the depth chart, LaFleur said he views Allgeier as a reliable complementary running back who excels in pass protection and short-yardage. Knight will be the team’s lead rusher on early downs and can be started in the FLEX against the Broncos this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will not play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: Things have been trending in this direction all week, but LaFleur officially confirmed on Friday that Love will miss a second straight game. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will likely split duties again in Week 7 after seeing a near 50/50 split in the touch distribution last week, with Allgeier’s 19 touches narrowly edging out Knight’s 17. Both Allgeier and Knight are fringe RB2/RB3 plays against a stout Broncos defense. In addition to Love the Cardinals also ruled out DT Walter Nolen III (ankle), S Andrew Wiggins (ankle), and OG Jo Gaines II (ankle).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is not expected to play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: Love didn’t practice on Wednesday and Thursday after missing Week 6. It doesn’t sound like he will practice at all this week. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will split the backfield again this week. Allgeier out-carried Knight 18-15 last week, but Knight was far more effective, running for 80 yards in total. Allgeier posted just 38 yards. He still figures to be the lead runner this week, but Allgeier shine as a plug-and-play RB2 is waning headed into Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Bam Knight suffered from “full body cramps” for much of the second half of Arizona’s Week 6 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: The good news is that this shouldn’t exactly be expected to sideline Knight going forward after his 98-total yard effort against the Rams. Knight’s fantasy value is tenuous despite the big game, as he was outsnapped by Tyler Allgeier and Jeremiyah Love (ankle) could be back next week. But he did outplay Allgeier in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Bam Knight rushed 15 times for 80 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 6 win over the Rams, adding two receptions for 18 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: Knight seemingly earned more work as the game progressed by simply outplaying Allgeier, the team’s Week 6 starter. After a few unproductive Allgeier runs, the Cardinals got Knight involved as a receiver on the second drive, his first catch coming via a slant route and generating a first down. They gave him three carries on the third drive, culminating in a 31-yarder on a well-blocked run to the left. Allgeier subbed in for the red zone sequence on that drive, but the coaching staff gave Knight three red zone touches on the fifth drive, compared to just one for Allgeier. They gave Knight two more red zone touches on the seventh drive. Blocking failed him on the second one, and it may have resulted in a right hand or wrist injury. Knight trotted over to the medical staff after the play, and a trainer could be seen stabilizing Knight’s wrist while putting him through sideline testing. Knight did return to the game on the next drive, but this is worth keeping an eye on. If Jeremiyah Love (ankle) misses the Cardinals’ Week 7 game against the Broncos, and Knight’s apparent injury is a non-issue, Knight could end up getting the start next week. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Jeremiyah Love said he told Cardinals coaches that Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight were in better shape to play than he was in Week 4 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: Love engaged in a long, candid conversation with Cardinals beat reporters after the game today, saying his snaps are being managed because he currently is “not able to go out there and do spectacular plays every single time.” Love said this is probably going to be the “longest year” of his life, and his preseason ankle injury is not the only thing he is dealing with. Love said his body is sometimes just “tired,” and that he would “probably just hinder the team” if he took on more work in his current state. He rhetorically asked, “why not put somebody else out there that’s playing better?” For those wondering, the Cardinals don’t go on bye until Week 14. They face the fantasy-friendly Lions defense in Week 5, which could help Love get his confidence back with an efficient performance.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Cardinals re-signed RB Zonovan Knight to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: Useful depth last year for Arizona as the entire running back room got hurt, Knight now enters the 2026 season as no better than fourth on the depth chart for the Cardinals. He’s behind James Conner, Tyler Allgeier, and Trey Benson. Knight won’t be a priority in offseason Best Ball drafts and will only pick up steam if more injuries happen ahead of him in the pecking order.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Cardinals placed RB Zonovan Knight (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: The ankle injury suffered against the Texans in Week 15 will send the running back to season-ending IR. Knight had control of the lead role in the Cardinals backfield for the majority of the season after season-ending injuries to James Conner and Trey Benson left Arizona reliant on depth. The 24-year-old acquitted himself well with a 82/269/4 line on the ground, adding one receiving score on a 22/160 line through the air. He’ll be a restricted free agent this offseason. Knight showed enough to stick on a roster somewhere, even if he isn’t necessarily someone dynasty managers should build around.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Cardinals RB Bam Knight (ankle) is believed to have suffered “a bad sprain” in Week 15’s loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: Knight is expected to undergo an MRI on Monday to confirm the diagnosis, but the belief is that he did not break anything. Knight is highly unlikely to play in Week 16’s game against the Falcons, and depending on the severity of his injury, it wouldn’t be surprising if this proved to be season-ending. We’ll check back in with an update when the team provides one, but an already thin Cardinals backfield could be looking at Emari Demercado and Michael Carter as it’s top two options down the stretch.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.headline: Cardinals RB Zonovan Knight (ankle) left Arizona’s Week 15 game against the Texans and was ruled out.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zonovan-kn.analysis: He was carted off the field after being tackled on his first carry. Knight left with minus-2 rushing yards. Though they initially called him questionable, FOX’s sideline reporter Jen Hale described Knight as being “in a tremendous amount of pain.” Knight may be staring at a season-ending injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Tyler Allgeier is “always” going to serve as a complementary running back.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: LaFleur really laid it all out there at today’s press conference, saying Allgeier “is always going to complement that next guy” when the starter is out. He adds that Allgeier is “extremely smart” and can be trusted in pass protection and short-yardage situations on third down. While Allgeier “can” do what the Cardinals need him to do on first and second down, LaFleur said Bam Knight will take “a lot” of that work with Jeremiyah Love (ankle) sidelined. LaFleur closed by saying he does not think any of these running backs can hold up in a full-time role over the course of the season. Allgeier handled a hefty 19 touches in this complementary role last week. He can be started as a high-volume FLEX with touchdown-based upside against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will not play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: Things have been trending in this direction all week, but LaFleur officially confirmed on Friday that Love will miss a second straight game. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will likely split duties again in Week 7 after seeing a near 50/50 split in the touch distribution last week, with Allgeier’s 19 touches narrowly edging out Knight’s 17. Both Allgeier and Knight are fringe RB2/RB3 plays against a stout Broncos defense. In addition to Love the Cardinals also ruled out DT Walter Nolen III (ankle), S Andrew Wiggins (ankle), and OG Jo Gaines II (ankle).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is not expected to play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: Love didn’t practice on Wednesday and Thursday after missing Week 6. It doesn’t sound like he will practice at all this week. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will split the backfield again this week. Allgeier out-carried Knight 18-15 last week, but Knight was far more effective, running for 80 yards in total. Allgeier posted just 38 yards. He still figures to be the lead runner this week, but Allgeier shine as a plug-and-play RB2 is waning headed into Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: Tyler Allgeier rushed 18 times for 38 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 6 win over the Rams, adding one reception for 10 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: Allgeier got the start, but looked slow compared to his backfield mate Bam Knight today. It was an extremely disappointing showing and the Cardinals seemingly leaned on Knight more and more as the game progressed. Allgeier still totaled 19 touches, including 18 carries, but he was routinely stopped around the line of scrimmage and critically ceded red zone snaps to Knight. Knight may have injured his right hand or wrist late in the game, but he continued playing. With Jerermiyah Love (ankle) currently sidelined, Allgeier could end up being the lead back again next week against the Broncos. Keep an eye on the Cardinals’ injury report this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will not play in Week 6 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: The Cardinals officially ruled Love out for this Sunday’s game against the Rams after he was. DNP in practice all week. Head coach Matt LaFleur said Love is not considered a candidate to be placed on injured reserve at this time, but the fact that he even has to mention that is cause for some concern that Love could be looking at a multi-week absence. LaFleur also added that Love’s lack of involvement in the passing game is due to his inability to run routes on his injured ankle. His practice status will be one to monitor next week when the Cardinals begin preparing for the Broncos. Tyler Allgeier should be in line for a busy day against the Rams and will be a volume-based RB2 play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: Tyler Allgeier should be rostered in 10-team leagues. The Cardinals have downplayed Love’s ankle issues, but two missed practices are not a good sign. He still has a chance to suit up in Week 6 against the Rams, but he is currently on the wrong side of questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said he wasn’t sure about getting Jeremiyah Love more involved in the pass game because the team needs extra blocking.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: Asked about Love’s lack of route running — he has a 29 percent route participation rate on the season — LaFleur said the Cardinals’ pass blocking struggles often prevent Love from functioning as a pass catcher. “I wasn’t too confident in terms of getting into some of those ‘scat’ protections and stuff like that and five-man protections,” LaFleur said. “We wanted to have that extra body in there. There were a couple of times where I wanted to get him on some choice routes and stuff like that, but like I said I didn’t feel confident that we were going to be able to execute at the level that we needed to. But it is a good question.” Love, who has 13 targets and has been targeted on 21 percent of his pass routes, would need much more pass game involvement if he were to operate as an RB1 in fantasy leagues this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: Tyler Allgeier rushed three times for seven yards in the Cardinals’ Week 5 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: Allgeier was a non-factor, even with the Cardinals pulling Jeremiyah Love in the fourth quarter. Allgeier did not log a carry in the first quarter. He is nothing more than a bench stash moving forward. The Cardinals face the Rams in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love tweaked his other ankle in Week 4’s loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: It’s been an odd 24 hours for Love, who was quoted after Sunday’s game saying this is shaping up to be the “longest year” of his career while also adding that he’s “tired” and would be willing to pass off work to Tyler Allgeier or Bam Knight in the event that he doesn’t think he can do what is being asked of him. As for this latest injury, LaFleur said the ankle injury isn’t the same one Love injured in the preseason, meaning he now has two ankle injuries to manage for the rest of the season. The Cardinals’ backfield was already proving hard to predict, and the latest quote from Love, coupled with the injury news, doesn’t exactly instill more confidence in him going forward. He draws a plus Week 5 matchup against the Lions, but should be treated as a fringe RB2/RB3 for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.headline: Jeremiyah Love said he told Cardinals coaches that Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight were in better shape to play than he was in Week 4 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-allg.analysis: Love engaged in a long, candid conversation with Cardinals beat reporters after the game today, saying his snaps are being managed because he currently is “not able to go out there and do spectacular plays every single time.” Love said this is probably going to be the “longest year” of his life, and his preseason ankle injury is not the only thing he is dealing with. Love said his body is sometimes just “tired,” and that he would “probably just hinder the team” if he took on more work in his current state. He rhetorically asked, “why not put somebody else out there that’s playing better?” For those wondering, the Cardinals don’t go on bye until Week 14. They face the fantasy-friendly Lions defense in Week 5, which could help Love get his confidence back with an efficient performance.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington (foot/back) is questionable for Las Vegas’ Week 7 game against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Washington didn’t practice on Thursday and was not spotted at practice on Friday. It would seem that he’s a very tenuous questionable at this point. Dylan Laube would be next up for backup duties behind Ashton Jeanty if Washington were ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington (foot/back) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Dang. This suggests Washington suffered one or both injuries yesterday in practice. He is firmly in the questionable camp and may have only a long shot at suiting up in Week 7 against the Rams. Without him, Ashton Jeanty should handle a solid workload. Dylan Laube could end up serving as the No. 2 running back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington Jr. (foot/back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: In a semi-surprising twist of fate, the Raiders running back on the practice report with injuries is Washington, who was limited with foot and back injuries on Wednesday. Ashton Jeanty was not listed on the practice report. A limited practice indicates Washington is still trending to play Week 7, but with him appearing on the injury report and Jeanty off, any hopes for Washington achieving standalone fantasy value will have to wait.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington rushed nine times for 43 yards in the Raiders’ Week 6 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Washington’s nine carries were only one fewer than the 10 Ashton Jeanty saw on the night, but Washington was by far the more productive back. The rookie fourth-rounder averaged a solid 4.8 YPC in this one and ripped off an 18-yard run in the fourth quarter on a drive that ended with a Tre Tucker touchdown. Jeanty is dealing with a foot/ankle injury that is clearly limiting him on the field. Washington should continue to spell Jeanty in Week 7 against the Rams, but he doesn’t have much to offer fantasy managers as far as reliable production is concerned. He continues to be nothing more than a stash as long as Jeanty is active and on the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Mike Washington, Jr. had one rush for five yards in the Raiders’ Week 5 loss to the Patriots, adding one catch for five yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: It was odd usage for Washington, who had at least five carries in three of four games headed into Week 5. Even Ashton Jeanty being limited with his ankle and foot injuries did nothing to bolster Washington’s involvement in the Vegas offense. In fact, Dylan Laube was the team’s clear No. 2 back behind Jeanty on Sunday. Laube had four carries and three receptions and punched in a short touchdown in the second half of the blowout loss. It raises serious questions about what Washington’s workload might look like if Jeanty misses time this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Ashton Jeanty (ankle, foot) is active for Week 5 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Jeanty will play through his foot and ankle injuries against New England. It wouldn’t be surprising if he cedes some backfield work to a healthy and much more explosive Mike Washington, however. Jeanty should be considered a top-24 option this week while Washington is a desperation flex. Raiders declared WR Jalen Nailor, QB Aidan O’Connell, S Tristin McCollum, RB Roman Hemby, S Dalton Johnson, OL Trey Zuhn, and DT JJ Pegues inactive against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Ashton Jeanty (foot/ankle) is “hopeful” to play in Week 5 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Per Rapoport, Jeanty had a flare-up of plantar fasciitis last week to go along with his ankle injury. He added that Jeanty will work out before today’s game to see how he’s feeling. If he can’t go, Mike Washington Jr. would see the bulk of the backfield touches. Washington has been an explosive complement to Jeanty this year, averaging five yards per carry on 24 attempts. He would jump to the top of the RB2 ranks if Jeanty can’t go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Ashton Jeanty (foot/ankle) is questionable for Las Vegas’ Week 5 game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Kubiak didn’t get into real specifics about the injury when asked. Mike Washington just found his way into real contingency value and is a worthwhile stash/hedge anywhere he was dropped. Jeanty did not practice Friday after a limited session (and the addition of a foot tag) on Thurdsay, so this certainly doesn’t appear to be heading in the right direction. That said, we knew Jeanty would be managing something after the preseason ankle injury and the Raiders have given out rest days on Friday quite a bit already this year. Jeanty is likely something close to truly questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Ashton Jeanty (ankle/foot) was not spotted at Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Jeanty has been dealing with the ankle injury throughout the week, but the foot injury was added after Thursday’s practice. Jeanty was officially listed as limited on Thursday, but the Raiders’ RB1 was absent from the media portion of Friday’s practice. We will receive final word on his Week 5 availability soon, but rookie Mike Washington could be in line for a busy day against the Patriots if Jeanty is unable to go.
