https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Ashton Jeanty (ankle/foot) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Oh, dear. Jeanty was a full participant yesterday, listed only with an ankle injury. Today, he was downgraded to limited and the Raiders tacked on a foot injury. The second-year running back has played through the nagging ankle injury thus far and could play through the pain again this weekend, but this situation must be closely monitored. Backup RB Mike Washington must be rostered in all formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (groin) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie has not practiced since straining his groin in Week 6’s Thursday practice. Labeling him as questionable to play seems like a formality before a game-day inactive listing, but only the Rams’ staffers know for sure. The Rams ruled out LB Nate Landman (concussion). Practice squad LB Eric Kendricks will be promoted to the active roster for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (groin) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie, the Rams’ No. 1 cornerback, and LB Nate Landman (concussion) were both sidelined today. Both players are on the wrong side of questionable for the Rams’ Week 7 game against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (groin) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie injured his groin during last Thursday’s practice and did not play in Week 6 against the Cardinals. He starts out this week not practicing, putting him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 7. Also not practicing was LB Nate Landman (concussion). The Rams defense continues to lose players to injury; the Raiders face this defense in Week 7 and could see more fruitful fantasy performances than usual.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Rams declared CB Trent McDuffie, WR CJ Daniels, WR Tutu Atwell, QB Ty Simpson, DL Larrell Murchison and OL Bill Murray inactive for Week 6 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie injured his groin during Thursday’s practice and was unable to participate on Friday. Losing their top cornerback may not cost them the game, but it certainly makes it easier for Cardinals pass catchers to produce fantasy points. The Rams also activated OL Keagan Trost from injured reserve and promoted CB Cam Lampkin from the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Trent McDuffie (groin) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie reportedly injured his groin during Thursday’s practice, and is now questionable to play. Frankly, the Rams can probably get by without their No. 1 cornerback this week, though obviously it would be preferable to have him out there. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Rams signed CB Trent McDuffie to a four-year, $124 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: ESPN’s Adam Schefter was the first to report the deal, which includes $100 million in guaranteed money. The two-time All-Pro becomes the highest-paid corner in NFL history and will now be under contract through the 2030 season. The Rams traded a bevy picks to the Chiefs last week, including a 2026 first-rounder, to acquire McDuffie, who totaled 63 tackles, one interception, and seven pass breakups last season before a knee injury prematurely ended his season. The Rams hope McDuffie, who will turn 26 shortly after the start of next season, will prove to be the missing piece they need to make a deep postseason run in the limited time they have left with Matthew Stafford under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports the Rams have made “significant progress” on an extension for CB Trent McDuffie.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: Garafolo reports the team hopes to sign McDuffie to a deal “in the near future,” adding that he’ll likely become the highest-paid corner in the league when all is said and done. McDuffie, 25, was acquired by the Rams last week in exchange for a haul of picks that included the Rams 2026 first-round pick. The fourth-year corner totaled 63 tackles, one interception, and seven pass breakups in 13 games last season and was named a First-team All-Pro in 2023 and a Second-team All-Pro in 2024.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Rams acquired CB Trent McDuffie from the Chiefs in exchange for 2026 first, fifth, and sixth round draft picks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie, who has three interceptions over 56 NFL games, was a first-round pick of Kansas City in 2022 and was set to play on his fifth-year rookie option before being dealt to the Rams, who last season allowed the sixth lowest drop back EPA in the NFL. McDuffie, 25, finished the season on IR with a knee injury. He’ll likely sign a long term deal with the Rams. Shipping McDuffie to LA could suggest the Chiefs are finally ready to build via the draft, including, perhaps, improving the receiving room for Patrick Mahomes as he returns from a 2025 knee injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Chiefs GM Brett Veach said he’d like to have CB Trent McDuffie “back for the long-term.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: McDuffie is entering the fifth-year option season on his rookie contract and the Chiefs could chop down his cap number for 2026 with an extension. Forced to play outside more over the past few years, McDuffie finally managed to be left off an All-Pro team in 2025. He managed a 75.6 PFF grade — as opposed to 82.0 and 84.8 the two seasons before that — in 688 snaps with the Chiefs while dealing with a knee injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.headline: Chiefs placed CB Trent McDuffie (knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trent-mcdu.analysis: Fellow cornerback Jaylen Watson is joining him on injured reserve. With nothing left to play for, the Chiefs are packing it in for the year. McDuffie leads the team in pass breakups at six. Watson is one behind him. Down their top two corners, Kansas City will be an easy target for Bo Nix this week. Fantasy managers can feel free to fire Nix up as a QB1 one last time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Puka Nacua (calf) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: The fact that Nacua is not practicing today is a bad sign for his Week 7 availability. Ever the injury-related optimist, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported earlier today that Nacua’s injury is “more minor than anything else,” though he quickly balanced the scales by then saying that he would not call Nacua’s quick trip to the imaging room “precautionary, because it’s not nothing.” If active, Nacua should be in fantasy football lineups because his talent and workload are almost unparalleled. That said, he is on the wrong side of questionable, and the Rams obviously do not want his injury to worsen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Puka Nacua’s calf injury is not considered “a significant injury.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: As far as Nacua’s long-term status goes, this sounds like good news overall. However, Rapoport also noted that Nacua’s status for Sunday’s game against the Raiders could be “up in the air.” With Friday’s practice still to go, Nacua’s status will be one to look for later in the day, as will his designation entering the weekend. If he draws a questionable tag, fantasy managers should treat him as a true game-day decision and have a backup plan in place should be unable to play this week. Given the 4:25 PM EST start time for this game, Rams WR Konata Mumpfield could be on a short list of players worth stashing until we know more about Nacua’s availability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Puka Nacua left practice early after suffering a calf injury on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Brutal. The Rams lost Davante Adams to a hamstring tendon rupture in Week 6 against the Cardinals, and now they could be without Nacua in Week 7 against the Raiders. The Rams have handled star-player injuries smartly this season. Consider Nacua highly questionable to play, and seek out a backup plan. Konata Mumpfield would serve as the de facto No. 1 wide receiver if Nacua is unable to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Puka Nacua caught 6-of-7 targets for 80 yards in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: The Cardinals’ pass rush derailed the Rams’ offensive game plan early on, and Nacua was held without a target until just under 11 minutes remaining in the second quarter. Heartbreak struck on the Rams’ sixth drive. Nacua shook his coverage defender on a hitch-and-go and had no one between him and the end zone. Matthew Stafford let it rip, but was hit during the throw. Nacua dove for what should have been a 65-yard touchdown, but the pass fell incomplete. Nacua had another close call late in the game, dragging a defender for half of his downfield route, on what was ultimately flagged for DPI, but the defender’s unscrupulous tactic prevented Nacua from hauling in a 45-yarder at the Cardinals’ 10-yard line. Fortunately, Nacua and Stafford linked up for 42- and 16-yard gains on their lone touchdown-scoring drive at the end of the game, salvaging Nacua’s box score. He’s an elite WR1 against the Raiders next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Puka Nacua caught 17-of-24 targets for 138 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 5 loss to the Bills, adding nine yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Nacua operated as the primary option through the air for a Rams team that attempted more than 50 passes for the third straight game. The veteran alpha was mostly confined to short-area work, something that could be attributed to the groin injury that continues to have his name on the injury report in practice, but that would not keep Nacua from returning another elite WR1 performance. Nacua was also inches away from padding his stat line further after failing to come down with what would have been a 51-yard touchdown reception on the final play of the first half. Nacua and the Rams fall to 2-3 ahead of a Week 6 divisional showdown against the Cardinals, where he will remain one of the top fantasy assets in the league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Puka Nacua caught 9-of-12 targets for 125 yards in the Rams’ Week 4 win over the Eagles, adding a two-yard rushing touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Nacua’s rushing score came on a second quarter end-around. Out there for the first time since Week 1, Nacua did what he always seems to do when active and post a dominant statline. We say “active” rather than “healthy,” as FOX’s Erin Andrews confirmed during the broadcast Nacua is dealing with some sort of sports-hernia situation. That could make him something of a week-to-week proposition but hopefully the superstar wideout has found some way to manage the pain for the rest of the season. He has a Week 5 smash spot in the Bills’ shootout-prone defense. He will also have an extra day to get healthy with the game taking place on Monday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: FOX Sports’ Erin Andrews reports that Puka Nacua has been dealing with a “pre-hernia” injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Andrews broke the news while reporting from the sideline of the Rams’ Week 4 game against the Eagles. Signs have been pointing to this type of injury for a while now, with the Rams referring to Nacua’s nagging injury as both a hip and groin issue. Just over two minutes remain in the third quarter, and Nacua has only come off the field for a few plays thus far. It appears as though the team has handled the injury well, though one imagines re-injury risk is still a factor. That said, he is a WR1 whenever he is active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Rams “do not intend to limit” Puka Nacua’s workload in Week 4 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Looks like we’ve got ourselves an old-fashioned source-off here. Schefter says Nacua won’t be limited, while The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero said over the weekend that Nacua may be on “a stricter snap count than usual.” Even if his snaps are cut back, Nacua is one of the best per-route receivers in the NFL. He will get by for fantasy managers in whatever role the Rams give him. He is, at worst, a low-end WR1 for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Rams WR Puka Nacua (groin) may be on “stricter snap count than usual” in Week 4 against the Eagles, reports the Ringer’s Tom Pelissero.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Rams HC Sean McVay said Nacua, who has been dealing with a groin injury, is good to go after getting a full practice in on Friday. The coach also noted that they’re still working through Nacua’s snap count and now Pelissero reports that it could be stricter than usual. Fantasy managers should still treat Nacua as a high-end WR1 even in a difficult matchup against the Eagles in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Puka Nacua (groin) is “good to go” for Los Angeles’ Week 4 game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/puka-nacua.analysis: Nacua will return after getting in a Friday full practice and should be a WR1 play, even against the Eagles’ vaunted secondary. McVay noted that they are still working through how they will navigate his snap count, so Davante Adams should remain near the WR1 line this week as they reintegrate Nacua. But nobody is sitting Puka Nacua in a standard league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brashard-s.headline: Brashard Smith (hamstring) won’t play in Kansas City’s Week 7 game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brashard-s.analysis: Did you remember he was on the roster? Funny what one little Kenneth Walker signing will do. Smith has one touch and six snaps in five games. Jadyn Ott will get RB3 duties in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brashard-s.headline: Chiefs waived RB Emari Demercado.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brashard-s.analysis: Demercado’s departure leaves rookie RB Emmett Johnson and second-year RB Brashard Smith to back up starting RB Kenneth Walker. The Chiefs also waived DE Vincent Anthony, LB Kam Arnold, WR Andrew Armstrong, WR Wesley Bissainthe, DT Cole Brevard, WR Jason Brownlee, WR Jacob De Jesus, OT Ethan Driskell, WR Omari Evans, OT Chukwuebuka Godrick, LB Cam Jones, WR Xavier Loyd, S Tanner McCalister, DT Amari McNeill, C Pete Nygra, RB Jaydn Ott, DT Damon Payne, CB D’Arco Perkins-McAllister, TE Mason Pline, S DeShon Singleton, CB Melvin Smith, EDGE Tyreke Smith, OG Josh Thompson, CB Zelmar Vedder, TE Tre Watson and WR Jeff Weimer. The Chiefs released LB Cole Christiansen, CB Kaiir Elam, CB Kader Kohou and EDGE Emmanuel Ogbah. The Chiefs placed DT Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) on the reserve/physically unable to play list and WR Jimmy Holiday on injured reserve. The Chiefs also waived OG C.J. Hanson, QB Chris Oladokun and RB EJ Smith with injury designations.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brashard-s.headline: Emmet Johnson rushed seven times for 39 yards in the Chiefs’ preseason game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brashard-s.analysis: Johnson added two catches for 15 yards and had another chunk gain through the air called back because of a penalty. Kenneth Walker didn’t play in this contest, allowing Johnson to draw the start with some of KC’s first-team offense on the field. Johnson split reps with Emari Demercado over the team’s first three drives, then left the game for good. He looks like the team’s No. 2 back, though all three backs have been the next man up behind Walker at some point during the preseason. Johnson isn’t guaranteed the backup job, but he’s now the favorite, putting him in the mix as a late-round flyer in deeper fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brashard-s.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that Chiefs RB Emmett Johnson “is swiftly earning a role as an explosive, decisive runner.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brashard-s.analysis: Breer refers to RB Kenneth Walker as an “every-down” player, says RB Brashard Smith “has already shown he can be a weapon in space,” and notes RB Emari Demercado adds depth. Perhaps taking on a change-of-pace rushing role is in play for Johnson this season. The rookie back has pass-catching experience as well, but Smith and Demercado could offer more in that department at the moment. Johnson could be the next player up if Walker were to miss time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brashard-s.headline: The Athletic’s Jesse Newell believes there’s a chance that the Chiefs could “move on” from Brashard Smith.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brashard-s.analysis: Obviously Smith’s fantasy value took a huge hit with the addition of Kenneth Walker. But they also added Emari Demercado and moved up in the fifth round to draft Emmitt Johnson. Per Newell, “It all means Smith faces an important training camp. He’s a seventh-round pick, so the team doesn’t have a great amount invested in him if it does choose to move on.” Smith barely got a chance to run the ball last year, which was damning on its own considering how poor the running back room was, so it wouldn’t be surprising if he was a non-factor this year. He’s not a must-hold in dynasty formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brashard-s.headline: Chiefs general manager Brett Veach said the Chiefs plan to establish the run and rely on the defense early in the year.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brashard-s.analysis: Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes is currently rehabbing a season-ending knee injury, and although he has a chance to return in time for Week 1, it takes time for players to return to full strength. Enter new Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker, who Veach reminds us was the Super Bowl LX MVP. He adds that the team feels “real good” about the offensive line. Veach also indicates that the team intends to pass the ball more often as the season progresses, but if the run game is working, who’s to say they take the proverbial foot off the pedal? Walker warrants low-end RB1 treatment at this time. He is backed up by veteran RBs Brashard Smith and Emari Demercado, and fifth-round rookie RB Emmett Johnson. The depth chart order behind Walker will become clear in training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brashard-s.headline: Chiefs signed RB Emari Demercado, formerly of the Cardinals, to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brashard-s.analysis: The former Cardinals backup running back totaled a career-high 413 scrimmage yards last season, banking four half-PPR finishes as an RB3 or better. Demercado caught 50 passes during his three seasons in Arizona and could challenge second-year RB Brashard Smith for receiving work. At worst, he can rotate in as a decent rusher whenever RB Kenneth Walker III needs a breather.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brashard-s.headline: ESPN’s Nate Taylor reports the Chiefs are “expected” to have a new starting running back for the 2026 season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brashard-s.analysis: He drops this in a note about Kansas City’s lack of explosion in 2025, a year in which impending free agent Isiah Pacheco was not able to manage a single run of 20 or more yards. New OC Eric Bieniemy, per Taylor, “will be tasked with putting together the correct run-blocking scheme for the Chiefs.” With both Pacheco and Kareem Hunt impending free agents and only gadget back Brashard Smith under contract, this report is not much of a surprise. The Chiefs will likely contend for one of the better free agent backs in this class.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brashard-s.headline: Brashard Smith had 12 rushes for 56 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 18 loss against the Raiders, adding two catches for two yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brashard-s.analysis: It was only the second time Smith has seen more than four carries in a game this season. With Isiah Pacheco inactive, Smith easily led the KC backfield in touches while Kareem Hunt chipped in with breather back duty. Smith’s rookie season usage was curious considering both Pacheco and Hunt struggled to create yards or prove effective as pass catchers out of the backfield. Smith has just five games with more than three targets in 2025, averaging a healthy 7.5 yards per reception and scoring a touchdown. Smith will be an intriguing best bell draft pick in the coming months as the Kansas City backfield is in flux ahead of 2026. Hunt is a free agent, as is Pacheco. Smith likely won’t be anything close to a bell cow back based on how little interest Reid had in using him that way in 2025. but perhaps he has some head-of-committee runouts in his range of outcomes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brashard-s.headline: Brashard Smith caught 3-of-4 targets for five yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 17 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brashard-s.analysis: Smith did not carry the ball once for the second week in a row. He last saw more than three attempts in Week 7. He did, however, bring in a goal line touchdown toss from Chris Oladokun. It was the first career score for both players. Smith is good for a handful of catches every week, but his non-existent role on the ground will keep him off the fantasy radar for Week 18.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson (concussion) is not on the Vikings’ final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson suffered a concussion in Week 5 against the Saints and was able to heal up over the Vikings’ Week 6. He demonstrated a solid connection with Kyler Murray in Week 4, posting a 13/119 receiving line against the Dolphins. Hockenson can be treated as a TE1 this week against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson (concussion) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson did the same yesterday and can be safely expected to start in Week 7 against the Colts’ beatable defense. Hockenson has seemingly developed a strong connection with Kyler Murray and can be started as a fantasy football TE1 this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson (concussion) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson was ruled out in Week 5 against the Saints after suffering a concussion. The Vikings were on bye in Week 6. The extended absence gives Hockenson decent odds of practicing in full this week, and we expect that to be the case. An update will be provided if he is limited today. Hockenson developed a strong connection with Kyler Murray in Week 4, and warrants TE1 treatment in Week 7 against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson suffered a concussion in Week 5 against the Saints and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson was slammed into the ground on his first catch of the day. He got up slowly and was immediately checked out by the medical staff. Hockenson was eventually evaluated for a concussion and ruled out. With a bye week on deck for Week 6, Hockenson should be able to return for the team’s next game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson caught 13-of-13 targets for 119 yards in the Vikings’ Week 4 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: With just over two minutes left in the game, Hockenson took a knee at the Dolphins’ five-yard line, allowing Kyler Murray to seal the game with a trio of kneel-downs after that. Although Hockenson surrendered the touchdown, he still delivered a TE1-worthy stat line on the day. The veteran tight end served as Murray’s go-to receiver, regularly nabbing passes on short-to-intermediate slants and curls. Hockenson mostly dove forward for a couple of extra yards after catching passes, but he did manage to drag a defender on a 14-yard gain early in the fourth quarter. The Dolphins’ pass rush was very effective today, and Murray seemed to hone in on Hockenson as his primary pressure fix as the game progressed. Hockenson will be a borderline TE1/2 against the Saints in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson caught 2-of-4 targets for 11 yards in the Vikings’ Week 3 win against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Running a route on 29 of the team’s 37 drop backs, Hockenson was uninvolved in the offense even after Justin Jefferson exited the game with an ankle injury in the first half. Hockenson, who has nine grabs over the Vikings’ first three games, profiles as a low-floor weekly option in a Minnesota offense that has not passed at its usual volume early in the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson caught 3-of-4 targets for 29 yards in the Vikings’ Week 2 win over the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson more or less repeated his Week 1 statline, only this time on far less passing volume for the Vikings’ offense. Carson Wentz attempted just 20 throws as the Vikes went “survive and advance” mode in weather-addled Chicago. With Kyler Murray expected to return from his concussion in Week 3 in Tampa, perhaps Hockenson can post a higher-end TE2 statline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: T.J. Hockenson caught 4-of-5 targets for 36 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 1 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: Hockenson finished second on the team in targets, though his 17 percent target share isn’t much to write home about. He found paydirt late in the third quarter on a red zone strike from Carson Wentz over the middle of the field. Wentz was filling in for a concussed Kyler Murray, who will likely miss Week 2. Hockenson is more of a TE2 than a true TE1, but his strong Week 1 outing at least puts him on the border versus the Bears next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: Vikings restructured the contract of TE T.J. Hockenson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: The move saves $5 million against the cap for the Vikings in 2026, a franchise that is now scrambling to get under the salary cap following numerous high profile moves made the year prior. Hockenson is coming off the worst statistical season of his career following a devastating knee injury suffered in 2024. Now two years removed from the injury and playing with something to prove, the fantasy needle could be pointing up should he find more consistent quarterback play moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.headline: Vikings TE T.J. Hockenson (shoulder) won’t play in Minnesota’s Week 18 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-hocken.analysis: With Jordan Addison taking a major leap in 2024, Hockenson has slid into an uninteresting low-end TE1 stab over the past two years, generating 41/455/0 in 2024 and 51/438/3 in 2025. Cutting Hockenson would free up over $8.9 million in cap space for a team that’s currently up against it to get cap-compliant and The Athletic’s Alec Lewis pointed to Hockenson as one contract that could be reworked this offseason. His future with the Vikings is in some question entering 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) will not play in Kansas City’s Week 7 game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Rice didn’t practice all week despite Andy Reid’s optimistic spin that he’s a “quick healer.” It’s hard to make much sense of how available he’ll be for Week 8 at this point as Rice hasn’t practiced since before the team’s Week 5 bye. Xavier Worthy will again get a WR3-caliber workload as The Only Game In Town for the Chiefs wideouts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Chiefs coach Andy Reid told reporters that Rice’s strain was only a “tweak” in his Week 4 post-game remarks. So much for that. The Chiefs will almost assuredly be without their No. 1 wide receiver against the Seahawks this week, leaving Xavier Worthy to handle the role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Right tackle Jaylon Moore was also held out of practice with a concussion. Rice went down with the hamstring issue in Week 4. Even with a bye week to heal before Week 6, he wasn’t ready to return. A DNP today suggests he will miss at least one more game. Xavier Worthy led the Chiefs with seven catches for 73 yards in his absence last week. He would be in line for another high-usage game if Rice remains out for Week 7’s game against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Chiefs declared WR Rashee Rice, TE Jared Wiley, QB Garrett Nussmeier, DB Jadon Canady, DE Jack Pyburn, OT Diego Pounds, and OT Josh Simmons inactive for Week 6 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Rice did not come close to playing in this one and was ruled out on Friday. His status will be worth monitoring ahead of Week 7; Andy Reid called him a “quick healer” on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) won’t play in Kansas City’s Week 6 game against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: It seems like Xavier Worthy and Travis Kelce will be getting Only Game In Town treatment against the Chargers, with Cyrus Allen and Jalen Royals also in the mix at wideout now that Rice and Tyquan Thornton are both out. Andy Reid said Rice is “wanting to jump in on everything” and suggested he’s a “quick healer.” He has to be regarded as questionable for Week 7, but Reid’s words point to him having a chance to play in that one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Rice strained his hamstring in Week 4. Although Chiefs coach Andy Reid initially said Rice only “tweaked” it, The Athletic’s Mike Silver reported a few hours later that Rice could be out for several weeks. The fact that Rice remains sidelined for the first two practices following his team’s Week 5 bye is a bad sign. He is firmly on the wrong side of questionable for Week 6 against the Chargers. If he can get in a limited session tomorrow, that could put him on track to play in Week 7 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: Rice appeared to have a good chance at suiting up for Week 6 when Andy Reid spoke about it after Week 4’s win over the Raiders. Reid only said he “tweaked” his hammy. Even with a bye week to rest, it looks like Rice is now on the wrong side of questionable for Week 6. With Tyquan Thornton on IR, Xavier Worthy may be tasked with WR1 duties this week. He totaled four catches for 70 yards in his last outing and would be a solid FLEX play versus the Chargers if Rice can’t go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: The Athletic’s Mike Silver believes Rashee Rice (hamstring) could be out for several weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: After the game, Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Rice “tweaked” his hamstring, seemingly downplaying the severity of his injury. It’s possible Silver is speculating on how long Rice could be out given what we know about soft-tissue injuries. Rice didn’t return to the game on Sunday against the Raiders, but he could be seen working out on the sideline at various times and was also on the exercise bike. With the Chiefs now entering their bye week, it’s possible we won’t have more clarity on Rice’s potential absence until they return to prepare for Week 6 against the Chargers. We will check back in with any updates as the team provides them.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Chiefs downgraded WR Rashee Rice (hamstring) to doubtful to return in Week 4 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: The Chiefs aren’t formally ruling him out just yet, but Rice’s day is as good as done with this latest update. He continues to go through tests on the hamstring he injured in the first quarter of Sunday’s game and will likely be ruled out in the near future. If his day is done, Rice will finish with zero receptions on zero targets in just six offensive snaps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) is questionable to return in Week 4 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rashee-ric.analysis: This news comes from the team’s X account. Rice exited in the first quarter of Sunday’s game and eventually made his way to the locker room after initially refusing to leave the field. CBS Sports’ Tracy Wolfson reported that Rice was noticeably frustrated on the sideline, which isn’t an encouraging sign as far as his return for this game is concerned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: Coming off the Vikings’ Week 6 bye, Jefferson got in a limited session on Wednesday before returning to full participation on Thursday. The star wide receiver posted a 6/79/1 receiving line in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints. He should be treated as an elite WR1 against a Colts pass defense that will be without CB Sauce Gardner (calf).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: The Vikings’ No. 1 wide receiver posted a 6/79/1 receiving line in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints. He should be feeling even better at this point, coming off a Week 6 bye. The Colts will notably be without No. 1 cornerback Sauce Gardner (calf) this weekend, making life even easier on Jefferson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: This is just a maintenance day for the Vikings’ No. 1 wide receiver. Jefferson has an excellent matchup this week against the struggling Colts’ defense. The unit will likely be without No. 1 CB Sauce Gardner (calf), further enhancing Jefferson’s WR1 outlook for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson caught 6-of-7 targets for 79 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 5 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: Jefferson didn’t miss a beat after returning from a one-game absence due to an ankle injury. He made several spectacular grabs in this game, the most amazing of which was a toe-tapping catch in the back of the end zone with three defenders covering him. Even at less than full strength, Jefferson is simply one of the best receivers in the league. He will remain near the top of the WR1 ranks when the Vikings face the Colts after their bye week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) is active for Week 5 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: Jordan Addison is out. Jefferson would normally see plenty of targets anyway, but the absence of Addison all but guarantees that he will see one of the highest target shares in the league. Jefferson remains a top-end WR1 versus the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: ESPN’s Jeff Darlington reports Justin Jefferson (ankle) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: Jordan Addison, on the other hand, is not expected to suit up because of a hamstring issue. Even at less than full strength, Jefferson will dominate the targets for Minnesota, especially with Addison on ice. Barring a setback in warmups, Jefferson remains a top-half WR1 play for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Justin Jefferson will work out pregame to determine his status for Week 5 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: The same is true of Jordan Addison. Both Minnesota wideouts are currently listed as questionable for Week 5. Jefferson is from Louisiana and has already told reporters he plans to play in the homecoming game. We expect him to suit up, but fantasy managers should have a backup plan for him and Addison to be safe.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Justin Jefferson (ankle) plans to play in Week 5 against the Saints, but the team “has to see how he feels on Saturday.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: This is great news. We will not have to wait for the dreaded game-time decision call with Jefferson this time around. If active, Jefferson should be started as a WR1 against the Saints. He remained limited in practice all week. We will provide an update on the matter as soon as possible.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) is questionable for Minnesota’s Week 5 game against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: Jefferson practiced on Friday after limited sessions on Thursday and Wednesday. He also insisted that he plans to play when asked earlier this week. We think he’s on the optimistic side of questionable as he returns as close to LSU as he can in the league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-jef.analysis: The Vikings’ No. 1 wide receiver is on track to play in Week 5 against the Saints, but it would be really nice to see him practice in full tomorrow. Ideally, the full participation upgrade would have come today. Regardless, Jefferson is the type of veteran who does not need to practice fully in order to play. He is a WR1 if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-kmet/.headline: Bears coach Ben Johnson said Cole Kmet (knee) will miss the rest of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-kmet/.analysis: Unfortunately it’s not much of a surprise based on the reporting or the carting. Sam Roush will take over as Chicago’s TE2 and likely have fringe TE2 value. Kmet will be in the final year of his four-year, $50 million extension in 2027. The 28-year-old will be a potential cap casualty with a $15.425 million cap figure and $10 million in savings on release without getting into post-June 1 cap machinations.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-kmet/.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Cole Kmet will undergo additional tests on his knee after Week 7’s win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-kmet/.analysis: Head coach Ben Johnson said after the game that Kmet’s injury didn’t look “very good,” breaking from his normal tendency to avoid talking about injuries. Kmet’s knee buckled from under him in the fourth quarter of Thursday’s game, and he had to be carted from the field after the play. This looked like a potential season-ender when it happened, but tests will confirm the severity of it in the near future. Kmet’s absence could open up more opportunities for Colston Loveland, who has caught 26 passes for 244 yards and two touchdowns this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-kmet/.headline: Cole Kmet (knee) was carted to the locker room in the fourth quarter of Week 7 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-kmet/.analysis: Kmet was sandwiched by two defenders on a hit in the fourth quarter and remained down on the field. He immediately grabbed at his knee as he remained on the turf. The cart was summoned and he was taken to the locker room, giving a thumbs up to the crowd as he went. Fantasy managers in deep leagues will want to track his status in the coming days, but it did not look good. Kmet managed to catch all three targets for 28 yards prior to departing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-kmet/.headline: Cole Kmet caught both of his targets for 13 yards in the Bears’ Week 4 win against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-kmet/.analysis: Colston Loveland, meanwhile, led the Bears with nine targets in Tyson Bagent’s first start. Kmet has had solid route participation numbers thanks to the Bears’ heavy use of two tight end sets. Even so, he should be left on waiver wires unless or until Loveland misses time. Kmet now has four receptions on the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-kmet/.headline: Cole Kmet caught 2-of-3 targets for 35 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 1 win against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-kmet/.analysis: Colston Loveland, meanwhile, caught exactly zero passes as the Bears put up 59 points against a nonexistent Carolina defense. Kmet ran a route on 19 of Caleb Williams’ 39 drop backs against the Panthers and came down with one of Williams’ two touchdown tosses on the day. Kmet will have some fantasy value going forward as long as he has some route running involvement in the potent Chicago offense. He can be added in deeper leagues ahead of Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-kmet/.headline: Colston Loveland did not catch any of his three targets in the Bears’ Week 1 win against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-kmet/.analysis: The Bears broke scoring records in their Week 1 demolition of the Panthers but Loveland — leading the team in pass routes — was largely invisible. Caleb Williams missed a wide open Loveland in the middle of the field in the second half and nearly connected with his second-year tight end in the end zone. Cole Kmet, meanwhile, ran about half of the Bears’ routes and turned three targets into two catches for 35 yards and a score. Loveland is almost certain to bounce back in Week 2 against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-kmet/.headline: Cole Kmet caught 3-of-3 targets for 31 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Divisional round loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-kmet/.analysis: Kmet found himself on the receiving end of a miraculous fourth-down throw by Caleb Williams to keep the Bears’ season alive with 18 seconds left in the fourth quarter. Kmet’s score would force the game into overtime, but the Bears came up short in the extra frame after the Rams made the most of a Caleb Williams interception on the Bears’ only drive. Kmet’s numbers have now fallen off in back-to-back years. After going for 73-719-6 in 2023, the sixth-year vet saw his fewest targets (45), receptions (30), and receiving yards (347) since his rookie year this season, and found the end zone just twice. As far as his work as a pass-catcher is concerned, Kmet took a backseat to rookie Colston Loveland this season, and now looks expendable heading into this offseason despite signing a four-year contract extension in 2023. Per OverTheCap, the Bears can release Kmet for a dead cap hit of just $3.2 million if the team makes him a pre-June 1 cut. A post-June 1 cut would carry a $1.6 million dead cap hit. Kmet will turn 27 next season and could have plenty to offer another team as a starter should he become available.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-kmet/.headline: Bears TE Cole Kmet (ankle/knee) is questionable for Chicago’s Week 16 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-kmet/.analysis: He upgraded to a full practice on Thursday and would appear to be on the optimistic side of questionable after practicing all week. Kmet told reporters that he will play. Normally his presence is a sign to dial back expectations for Colston Loveland in fantasy, but it’s possible the Bears could use a ton of two tight-end looks in Week 16 with both Luther Burden and Rome Odunze ruled out. Loveland will be a playable low-end TE1, while Kmet is on the TE2 line at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-kmet/.headline: Cole Kmet (ankle/knee) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-kmet/.analysis: Kmet was limited yesterday as well. We fully expected him to suit up for Saturday’s game versus the Packers. With Rome Odunze and Luther Burden likely to miss Week 16, expect a heavy dose of 12-personnel from Chicago’s offense. That will keep Kmet on the edge of the TE2 ranks this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-kmet/.headline: Cole Kmet caught 2-of-4 targets for 28 yards in the Bears’ Week 15 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cole-kmet/.analysis: Kmet continues to be a thorn in Coleston Loveland’s side rather than a standalone fantasy option. The 26-year-old tight end hasn’t played ahead of his counterpart in about a month, but the three or so targets he gets every game is noteworthy. It’s just not enough for him to be on the fantasy radar in Week 16 against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Carson Beck is dealing with back spasms.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Beck left Thursday’s practice with back spasms and was listed as a DNP. Head coach Mike LaFleur said he was not overly concerned with the injury and that he doesn’t believe it will be anything long-term. Beck’s injury shouldn’t change his Week 7 availability, as he has been the emergency QB3 all season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Carson Beck (back) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Beck appeared on the injury report last Friday, as a limited participant. He remained limited on Wednesday and was downgraded today. Beat reporters saw him at practice briefly, but he ended up going inside with a trainer. This could help preserve Jacoby Brissett’s job security. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: ArizonaCardinals.com’s Darren Urban believes Carson Beck won’t start in the “immediate future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Cardinals fans appear to be pining for the team to bench Jacoby Brissett and start the rookie in the coming weeks as another season circles the drain for Arizona. Beck so far has been the Cards’ emergency third quarterback. Urban said there remains a “chance Beck is made the backup this week or next and allow him to come on in relief if the situation presents itself. I don’t see Beck starting in the immediate future, but it does feel his time grows closer, and if the offense continues to sputter, that would be understandable.” Brissett this season ranks 15th in passing yards. He’s thrown nine touchdowns to five interceptions and ranks 30th out of 37 qualifying QBs in adjusted yards per attempt. He won’t be a viable fantasy play this week against a tough Rams coverage unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals declared QB Carson Beck, S Dadrion Taylor-Demerson, OL Josh Fryar, DL Andrew Billings, and WR Reggie Virgil inactive for Week 3 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Beck continues to be the Cardinals’ third quarterback and will be a gameday inactive for Week 3 behind Jacoby Brissett and Gardner Minshew. Dadrion “Rabbit” Taylor-Demerson (back) was scratched on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Team reporter Darren Urban reports that Cardinals QB Carson Beck (ribs) is unlikely to play in Friday’s preseason game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: This is unfortunate. Beck looked great before injuring his ribs in the Hall of Fame game. Per Urban, Beck has been a very limited participant in practice ever since, which is costing him valuable reps. Only starting QB Jacoby Brissett will take first-team practice reps once the regular season begins. Beck practiced the week after the injury, “struggling much of the time,” and has sat out since then. The Cardinals have an extremely difficult schedule, so a rough record could bring Beck back onto the field at some point this year. Ideally, he would have spent all of August refining his play, though. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team re-draft leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said QB Carson Beck (rib) is unlikely to play in Saturday’s preseason game against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Beck is scheduled to resume throwing after practice today, though, so the Cardinals’ rookie is indeed on the mend. Beck looked good in his prior preseason action. Hopefully, he has a chance to return in time for his team’s final preseason game against the Packers next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals HC Mike LaFleur said he has ‘no concern’ over the rib injury that sidelined Carson Beck in Thursday’s preseason game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: LaFleur said Beck would have been well enough to throw if it were seven-on-seven drills, adding that the team “didn’t want to risk it” when it came to starting the rookie in Thursday’s preseason game. Beck already has some preseason experience under his belt. He threw for 188 yards and a touchdown in the Hall of Fame Game last week against the Panthers and will hopefully have a chance to suit up in next week’s preseason game against the Cowboys on Saturday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals ruled out QB Carson Beck (rib) for the team’s preseason Week 1 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: According to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, Beck suffered a rib injury in the Cardinals’ Hall of Fame game against the Panthers. Despite feeling “soreness,” he managed to practice this week. The Cardinals “decided to keep him out tonight as a precaution and to allow more time to heal.” This pours a little cold water on Beck’s moderate hype, but the reporting suggests that the injury is not overly concerning. Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett will start, and presumably be relieved by QB Kedon Slovis at some point. No word yet on QB Gardner Minshew’s potential involvement tonight.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals QB Carson Beck completed 15-of-19 passes for 188 yards and a touchdown in Thursday’s Hall-of-Fame Game against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: Beck played two-plus quarters. No offense to the Hall-of-Fame Game, but it’s not a contest we typically go into expecting highlights. The Cardinals’ No. 3 quarterback provided several of them, hitting Jalen Brooks for a 49-yard deep strike and Simi Fehoko for a five-yard end zone fade touchdown. In between were several smart in-rhythm completions, with Beck navigating the pocket well. 24-year-old Beck’s arm strength remains a massive question mark — even his Brooks completion drifted a bit toward the middle of the field — but his processing was on point against the Panthers’ second- and third-team defense. Although he was a highly polarizing pre-draft prospect, the fact that the rebuilding Cardinals were willing to use a Day 2 selection strongly suggests he will make late-season starts as the organization keeps an eye on the future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.headline: Cardinals announced QB Carson Beck will start Thursday’s Hall of Fame game.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-beck/00.analysis: It will be our first glimpse of Beck in an NFL uniform. Given the draft cost they paid for Beck, the 65th overall pick, it would behoove the Cardinals for him to be clearly better than everyone else out on the field Thursday and establish some sort of momentum to eventually get a starting role by the end of the season. We’ll see.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.headline: Denzel Ward (hand) was limited in Friday’s practice and is questionable for Cleveland’s Week 7 game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.analysis: Ward popped up on the injury report today. Friday pop-up questionables are always tough to understand from the outside without any major reporting, but it stands to reason that Ward has a real chance to miss the game based on the listing. The Browns cleared Carson Schwesinger (ankle) from the report, so at least their star linebacker will be in there.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.headline: Browns signed CB Denzel Ward to a two-year, $62.2 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.analysis: $52.3 million of the contract is guaranteed. It’s a huge payday for a 29-year-old cornerback, but Ward has been a stalwart for the Browns defense his entire career and hasn’t shown any real signs of aging just yet. He had two years remaining on his contract, so it’s likely that most of that guaranteed money just ties him to the Browns through 2027.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.headline: ESPN’s Daniel Oyefusi believes Browns CB Denzel Ward could be extended this offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.analysis: Browns beat writers have been very careful to say that they don’t know why Ward didn’t participate in mandatory minicamp — Todd Monken said nothing when asked about it — but it does have the whiff of a hold in situation. Ward has no guaranteed salary remaining on his deal entering his age-29 season, so it feels like a no-brainer for him to get some sort of adjustment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.headline: Browns general manager Andrew Berry said the team is not interested in trading CB Denzel Ward.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.analysis: Berry fielded questions after trading EDGE Myles Garrett to the Rams in exchange for EDGE Jared Verse, a 2027 first-round pick, a 2028 second-round pick and a 2029 third-round pick. Understandably, reporters wanted to know if Ward, whom the team drafted via the No. 4 overall pick in 2018, one year after the team drafted Garrett No. 1 overall, was also available for trade. Berry restructured both players’ contracts this offseason and told the media that Garrett was not on the trade block. He could be telling the truth here, but the fact remains that trading away a talented, yet aging, cornerback could net decent draft capital for a team that is seemingly attempting a speedy reset.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.headline: Browns restructured the contract of CB Denzel Ward, saving $2 million against the cap in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.analysis: The franchise converted a $2.5 million roster bonus into a signing bonus, saving $2 million against the cap in 2026 while adding $500,000 to his cap hit for each subsequent season. This comes a day after the Browns restructured the contract of quarterback Deshaun Watson. The rebuilding Browns remain unlikely to make major splashes in free agency but at least these moves give them options in the coming months.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.headline: Browns OG Wyatt Teller (calf) is inactive for Week 16 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.analysis: Teller was questionable entering the weekend but has been ruled out. Backup Teven Jenkins will start in his place. In addition to Teller, the Browns have also ruled out CB Denzel Ward, RB Dylan Sampson, DT Mike Hall Jr., WR Jamari Thrash, TE David Njoku, and DT Sam Kamara.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.headline: Browns CB Denzel Ward (calf) will not play in Cleveland’s Week 16 game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.analysis: He didn’t practice all week for the second-straight week and, again, carries some IR shutdown risk over the weekend ahead of Sunday’s game. If he remains active, Ward starts Week 17 firmly on the questionable line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.headline: Browns CB Denzel Ward (calf) won’t play in Cleveland’s Week 15 game against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.analysis: Ward did not practice at any point this week since suffering the injury in Week 14. He certainly could be a candidate for an IR shut down with the Browns eliminated from the playoffs. Ward has had the worst PFF coverage grade of his career so far in 2025, at 54.4 in 701 defensive snaps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.headline: Browns CB Denzel Ward (calf) left Cleveland’s Week 14 game against the Titans and did not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.analysis: Kevin Stefanski had no update on Ward’s status on Monday, but the rule-out was not encouraging. We’ll monitor his practice status, but we imagine he’s likely on the doubtful side of questionable for Week 15 at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.headline: Browns CB Denzel Ward (migraine) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-war.analysis: Ward was listed with a migraine on the Browns’ Wednesday injury report. It doesn’t seem like his migraine is tied to any concussion or head injury, so we would expect Ward to be able to recover and play in Week 13 against the 49ers. Also not practicing defensively for the Browns were DE Alex Wright (quad) and DT Adin Huntington (quad). Both Wright and Huntington are in jeopardy of missing Week 13, though practice reports later in the week will provide clarity.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (foot) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 7 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: He’ll be on the WR3 line in a good matchup against the Titans. Boston finally had a clunker last week against Baltimore, but he’s been remarkably consistent otherwise and should find easier footing against Tennessee’s rough back seven.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (foot) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: The Browns’ rookie field-stretcher played through his foot injury last week against the Ravens, posting just a 1/15 receiving line. Ostensibly, the foot is bothering him, but he still has a chance to suit up in Week 7 against the Titans. Hopefully, Boston upgrades to full participation tomorrow.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (foot) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: Boston played through the injury last week, catching just 1-of-5 targets for 15 yards. The foot injury could be bugging him. Fortunately, he did not appear to suffer any setbacks. Boston is a WR3/FLEX against the Titans in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston caught 1-of-5 targets for 15 yards in the Browns’ Week 6 win over the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: This was the worst game of Boston’s young career. After going for 40-plus yards in his first five games to start the season, the promising rookie was blanketed in coverage all afternoon and managed just one reception as a result. Boston may have had a chance at scoring were it not for a pass near the right side of the end zone sailing too far out of bounds for him to bring both feet down, but scoring opportunities were hard to come by in this one. Boston will be back on the fantasy radar as a WR3 next week against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (foot) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: He’ll be a usable WR3 against the Ravens this week. Boston has returned at least 41 yards in every start this year while hitting a deep gain seemingly weekly. The 22-year-old should be Cleveland’s No. 1 target again this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (foot) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: Of the (many) Browns in real danger of missing this week’s game against the Ravens, Boston seems to be in the best shape of actually playing. Still, it is two limited sessions in two tries and we wouldn’t be surprised if he wound up with a questionable tag on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston (foot) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: A limited practice to start the week is usually nothing more than maintenance. Boston should still be a safe bet to suit up on Sunday. The second-round rookie has already cemented himself as an impressive downfield threat with three touchdowns and three catches of 40+ yards. He’s managed several spike weeks despite the Browns’ up-and-down performances on offense. Health permitting, Boston will be a low-end WR3 for Week 6 versus Baltimore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston caught 3-of-7 targets for 47 yards and a touchdown in the Browns’ Week 5 loss to the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: Boston’s score was his third in five games as a pro. This one was a 29-yard strike down the left sideline where Boston won a 1-on-1 matchup with CB Brandon Stephens. Boston’s yardage totals are not popping off the page in this limited offense, but his play-making ability has been. He has also reached at least 40 yards all five times out, giving him a non-zero floor. The rookie second-rounder continues to press his WR3 case heading into Week 6 against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: Denzel Boston caught 4-of-7 targets for 89 yards in the Browns’ Week 4 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: Boston has now led the Browns in receiving in three of the team’s first four games, made more impressive by the fact that those were the first four contests of the youngster’s professional career. The second-round rookie continues to flash big play potential after catching his third pass of 46 yards or longer, this time unable to find the end zone after scoring twice in his first two games. Boston still has room to grow considering he has seen just 22 targets in the first month of the season, and could reward fantasy managers that invested late-round picks in his services handsomely in the second half of his rookie year. He’ll be an upside FLEX option against the Jets in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.headline: NFL on Prime’s James Palmer reports that the Browns “love” Denzel Boston, and he is viewed as a “possible future star.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/denzel-bos.analysis: What to do with this info? Stash Boston at the very least. Per Palmer, the Browns “felt he was a true pro from the day he walked into the building.” In the same pre-Thursday Night Football news dump, Palmer said that Harold Fannin is the team’s No. 3 pass catcher, despite Fannin leading the team in targets. This could indicate that the Browns plan to ramp up Boston’s offensive involvement as the season progresses.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: KC Concepcion (calf/quad) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 7 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: Concepcion should be treated as a PPR WR3/WR4 tweener this week in a good matchup against the Titans. With Denzel Boston also active, we likely won’t be seeing any major explosions here. Concepcion-reliant managers would accept any explosion at this point as he’s found it hard to crack 50 receiving yards so far.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: KC Concepcion (calf/quad) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: The Browns’ short-area target earner is banged up, but he still has a chance to play in Week 7 against the Titans. Ideally, Concepcion will upgrade to full participation tomorrow. If he remains limited, he may end up being listed with a questionable tag. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: KC Concepcion (calf/quad) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: The rookie wide receiver has been awfully banged up over the past two weeks. He suffered a concussion in Week 5, yet managed to play in Week 6. Unfortunately, he did not leave the contest unscathed, picking up two lower-body injuries. Hopefully, he resumes practicing fully tomorrow.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: KC Concepcion caught 4-of-6 targets for 37 yards in the Browns’ Week 6 win over the Ravens, adding two carries for two additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: Concepcion’s six targets led all Browns players, while his 37 receiving yards were good for second-most behind Jerry Jeudy. Concepcion’s biggest play of the game came on a 17-yard reception in the third quarter that helped set up the Browns’ first scoring drive of the afternoon. Concepcion had a red zone carry inside the Ravens’ 10-yard line that resulted in only a one-yard gain, but it’s always good to see his coaches trusting him in the valuable areas of the field. We are still waiting on his first breakout game, but the volume continues to be encouraging. Concepcion will be a fringe WR3/WR4 next week against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: Browns coach Todd Monken said KC Concepcion (concussion) has cleared protocol and will play in Cleveland’s Week 6 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: Concepcion will have some low-end WR3/FLEX appeal with four teams on bye in PPR leagues. He simply hasn’t been able to find much space with his opportunities so far, with two 25-yard catches and 16 other catches that went for just 99 yards in his first five weeks of action.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: KC Concepcion (concussion) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: He’s still in concussion protocol, but it looks like he’ll have at least some chance of clearing before Sunday’s game against the Ravens. Concepcion would struggle to be more than a FLEX option here even if healthy, so fantasy managers should probably look at alternatives this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: KC Concepcion (concussion) will practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: It’s a remarkable turn after Concepcion was knocked out cold on the field in Week 5 against the Jets. If Concepcion is able to practice in the coming days he should be active for Week 6 against the Ravens. The rookie leads the Cleveland offense with a 23 percent target per route rate, used primarily as a gadget player near the line of scrimmage. He would be a flex option in PPR formats if he suits up against Baltimore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: KC Concepcion suffered a concussion in the first quarter of the Browns’ Week 5 game against the Jets and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: Making a spinning first quarter grab, Concepcion took a high hit from Minkah Fitzpatrick, who was flagged for a personal foul. It was the kind of hit the NFL is trying to legislate out of the game, but it wasn’t necessarily dirty. It was extremely unfortunate, as Concepcion did appear to be briefly out cold. He thankfully made his way to his feet and to the locker room unassisted, but he was ruled out before even undergoing a formal evaluation. He will now be highly questionable for Week 6 against the Ravens. Concepcion’s loss will mean more routes for beleaguered Jerry Jeudy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: KC Concepcion caught 5-of-8 targets for 64 yards in the Browns’ Week 4 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: Concepcion continues to operate as the primary slot receiver for a Browns team clearly looking to their youth while phasing out veteran Jerry Jeudy, the latter of whom managed three receptions on three targets for 36 yards. Concepcion has yet to lead the team in receiving while working in a short area role, with this the first game thus far which he has gained more then 43 yards. He’ll be a difficult start in fantasy circles when the Browns take on the Jets in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Browns want Deshaun Watson to get KC Concepcion more involved.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kc-concepc.analysis: Concepcion ranks second on the team with 17 targets, but his chemistry with Watson remains a work in progress. The rookie wide receiver has turned a team-high 12 receptions into just 80 yards. Concepcion is FLEX-viable against the Steelers on Thursday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) is not on Cleveland’s final Week 7 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: He should carry his usual load in a good matchup against the Titans. That will put Judkins in the mid-to-low RB2 range this week, even with Dylan Sampson getting a chance to come back off injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: Yesterday, Browns coach Todd Monken said he was “optimistic” about Judkins’ Week 7 availability. He has a chance to face the Titans this week, after sitting out in Week 6 against the Ravens, but it would be great to resume practicing in full tomorrow. If active, Judkins could be limited to a run-centric role, with Sampson also technically being on track to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: Earlier today, Browns coach Todd Monken said he was “optimistic” about Judkins’ availability for Week 7 against the Titans. Today’s limited session puts him on track to play, though it would be nice to see him practice in full. If active, he would be a FLEX starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Browns head coach Todd Monken said he’s “optimistic” Quinshon Judkins (ankle) will play in Week 7 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: Monken sounded like Judkins and Dylan Sampson will be active and ready to go against Tennessee. Judkins had been the locked-in lead back for Cleveland before his Week 5 ankle injury, seeing 71 percent of the team’s designed rushing attempts. The potential return of Sampson, a good pass catcher, could complicate things for Judkins’ involvement in the pass game going forward. Judkins will be a touchdown-dependent flex play against a Titans defense allowing the NFL’s ninth lowest rushing success rate in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) will not play in Week 6 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: Judkins tested out his ankle in pregame warmups, with the team deciding afterward that he would not play in this AFC North battle with the Ravens. With backup Dylan Sampson still sidelined and Raheim Sanders (hip) on injured reserve, the Browns will look to Jaleel McLaughlin and the recently signed Audric Estime to lead their backfield in Week 6. This is looking like a backfield to avoid for this week, but McLaughlin could have some value in deeper leagues. The Browns also ruled QB Taylen Green, CB Noah Igbinoghene, DT Mike Hall Jr., C Parker Brailsford, OG Teven Jenkins, and DT Mason Graham inactive for this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Quinshon Judkins (ankle) will work out pregame to determine his status for Week 6 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: Per Rapoport, there is optimism that linebacker Carson Schwesinger (ankle) will be able to play this week. Judkins logged a single limited practice on Friday before being listed as questionable. The fact that the Browns are even letting him test the groin injury in warmups suggests he will miss at most one game. If he doesn’t suit up, the Browns would be down to Jaleel McLaughlin and Audric Estime as their remaining options at running back. McLaughlin would be the better choice for fantasy managers, though this is largely a situation to avoid if possible.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) is questionable for Cleveland’s Week 6 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: He only got in a limited session on Friday, leaving us to conclude this is likely a true questionable situation. The viability of Jaleel McLaughlin as a FLEX play will probably be determined by if Judkins is active or not. It’s also possible Judkins plays on a pitch count. He’ll be a shaky low-end RB2 if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) returned to practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: This is an improvement for Judkins, who was a DNP for the team’s first two practices this week. Head coach Todd Monken said earlier this week that Judkins was considered day-to-day, so we’ll see if he has a shot at playing when the team releases its final injury report in a couple of hours. It seems unlikely that Judkins will be fully removed from the injury report, meaning he’ll likely carry a questionable designation heading into the weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: It sure seems to be trending in the direction of Jaleel McLaughlin, Lead Back in Week 6 against the Ravens. We’ll see if Judkins can get back on the field or generate any kind of positive momentum on Friday, but we’d be surprised if he did better than a questionable listing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quinshon-j.analysis: Judkins suffered a potentially serious ankle injury in Week 5 and could miss Week 6 against the Ravens if he’s unable to practice in the next couple days. That could leave Jaleel McLaughlin as the Browns’ lead back against Baltimore. Dylan Sampson (knee) could also suit up if he’s able to practice after a four-week stint on IR.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will not play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: Things have been trending in this direction all week, but LaFleur officially confirmed on Friday that Love will miss a second straight game. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will likely split duties again in Week 7 after seeing a near 50/50 split in the touch distribution last week, with Allgeier’s 19 touches narrowly edging out Knight’s 17. Both Allgeier and Knight are fringe RB2/RB3 plays against a stout Broncos defense. In addition to Love the Cardinals also ruled out DT Walter Nolen III (ankle), S Andrew Wiggins (ankle), and OG Jo Gaines II (ankle).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is not expected to play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: Love didn’t practice on Wednesday and Thursday after missing Week 6. It doesn’t sound like he will practice at all this week. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will split the backfield again this week. Allgeier out-carried Knight 18-15 last week, but Knight was far more effective, running for 80 yards in total. Allgeier posted just 38 yards. He still figures to be the lead runner this week, but Allgeier shine as a plug-and-play RB2 is waning headed into Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: Love starts out not practicing for the second straight week due to an ankle injury. He missed Week 6 against the Rams and a DNP Wednesday puts him on the wrong side of questionable to play in Week 7 against the Broncos. Love will need to practice in some capacity to have a chance of playing this week, but Tyler Allgeier is back in the RB2 range if Love cannot go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Cardinals declared RB Jeremiyah Love, QB Carson Beck, S Andrew Wingard, S Wydett Williams, S Jerrick Reed and DL Andrew Billings inactive for Week 6 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: Tyler Allgeier is a volume-based RB2 with Love sidelined this week. The Cardinals are smartly giving Love time off to heal his injured ankles. Beck will again serve as the Cardinals’ emergency third quarterback. Wingard (knee) and his direct backup Williams (concussion) are both out, but Budda Baker (groin) and EDGE Zaven Collins (hip) are active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will not play in Week 6 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: The Cardinals officially ruled Love out for this Sunday’s game against the Rams after he was. DNP in practice all week. Head coach Matt LaFleur said Love is not considered a candidate to be placed on injured reserve at this time, but the fact that he even has to mention that is cause for some concern that Love could be looking at a multi-week absence. LaFleur also added that Love’s lack of involvement in the passing game is due to his inability to run routes on his injured ankle. His practice status will be one to monitor next week when the Cardinals begin preparing for the Broncos. Tyler Allgeier should be in line for a busy day against the Rams and will be a volume-based RB2 play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: Tyler Allgeier should be rostered in 10-team leagues. The Cardinals have downplayed Love’s ankle issues, but two missed practices are not a good sign. He still has a chance to suit up in Week 6 against the Rams, but he is currently on the wrong side of questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said Jeremiyah Love (ankle) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: The Cardinals are listing Love with just one ankle injury, but recent reports, including quotes from LaFleur, have said that Love is still managing the high-ankle sprain he suffered in the preseason and may have injured the other ankle in Week 4. LaFleur said the current plan is to “give it a little bit of rest and see as the week goes on.” Tyler Allgeier offers little standalone value, but he should be rostered in 12-team leagues.
