https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said he wasn’t sure about getting Jeremiyah Love more involved in the pass game because the team needs extra blocking.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: Asked about Love’s lack of route running — he has a 29 percent route participation rate on the season — LaFleur said the Cardinals’ pass blocking struggles often prevent Love from functioning as a pass catcher. “I wasn’t too confident in terms of getting into some of those ‘scat’ protections and stuff like that and five-man protections,” LaFleur said. “We wanted to have that extra body in there. There were a couple of times where I wanted to get him on some choice routes and stuff like that, but like I said I didn’t feel confident that we were going to be able to execute at the level that we needed to. But it is a good question.” Love, who has 13 targets and has been targeted on 21 percent of his pass routes, would need much more pass game involvement if he were to operate as an RB1 in fantasy leagues this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Jeremiyah Love rushed 12 times for 22 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 5 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: Love played extensively early in the game. He was the only Cardinals running back to record a carry in the first quarter. The Lions began running up the score in the second quarter, and Love was seemingly simply phased out as Jacoby Brissett repeatedly fired passes downfield. Later, in the fourth quarter, the camera suddenly showed Love standing on the sideline without his helmet. A reporter chimed in to say that Love had not received attention from the training staff, but noted that Love told her he is still managing the ankle injury he suffered in training camp. Reports also indicated that he tweaked his other ankle last week. Love’s weekly floor is sinking as his production becomes increasingly touchdown-dependent. That said, he should be in fantasy lineups as an RB2/3 against the Rams next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.headline: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is not on Arizona’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremiyah-.analysis: Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said “It’s a maintenance thing with ankles, you guys see the way he cuts...I don’t know what he’s totally feeling, only he knows...but he’s doing good.” Great, not cryptic at all, Mike. Love is a reasonable low-end RB2 if his ankles decide he wants to play his full allotment of the 50/50 split against the Lions in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.headline: Divine Deablo (forearm) won’t play in Atlanta’s Week 7 game against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.analysis: It’s a slight upgrade for Christian McCaffrey, not that you were thinking about not starting McCaffrey anyway. The Falcons also ruled out CB Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring) — neither player practiced this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.headline: Divine Deablo (forearm) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.analysis: Deablo suffered a forearm injury in Week 6 and opens Week 7 not practicing. Also not practicing was CB Billy Bowman (hamstring). Both will need to practice in some capacity to play in Week 7 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.headline: Falcons DE Samson Ebukam (hamstring) and LB Divine Deablo (hamstring) are questionable for Week 4 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.analysis: Ebukam and Deablo are the only two players listed on the Falcons’ injury report for their Week 4 divisional showdown agains the Saints on Monday Night Football. Ebukam returned to a full practice Saturday for the first time since injuring his hamstring in practice ahead of Week 3. The Falcons remain relatively healthy as they prepare to challenge the Saints for the division lead through the first month of play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.headline: Falcons placed LB Divine Deablo (forearm) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.analysis: Deablo suffered a fractured forearm in the team’s Week 7 loss to the 49ers and will now miss at least four games on injured reserve. His absence creates a significant hole in the interior for a defense allowing the second fewest yards per game this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.headline: Falcons ruled out EDGE Jalon Walker (groin) for Week 8 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/divine-dea.analysis: Falcons rookie slot DB Billy Bowman Jr. (hamstring) and LB Divine Deablo (forearm) have also been ruled out. None of the three practiced this week. On the plus side, LT Jake Matthews (ankle) will play. The defensive injuries soften up the Falcons’ interior, which benefits Dolphins RB De’Von Achane.

He’ll be a difficult start against the lockdown Houston defense in Week 3.

Whether that’s a start or as part of a committee remains in some limbo, but we’d be surprised if Jacobs wasn’t involved in Week 7.

Jacobs was reinstated by the league late last week and is eligible to play immediately, but whether or not he will be active next week is to be determined. We’ll see how this week unfolds, but it would be a bit surprising if Jacobs was inactive in a pivotal NFC North matcup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the NFL “could step back in and create a longer suspension” for Josh Jacobs if the video showing his altercation with a woman is released.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: Fowler is surprisingly saying the quiet part out loud here, though this has been the general consensus for fans and analysts for a while. Jacobs is scheduled to come off the NFL’s Commissioner Exempt list on Monday. The NFL is reportedly trying to get hold of the video, and Jacobs has sued to block its release. Fowler adds that the woman’s attorney said her client has not participated in the league’s investigation due to privacy concerns. If the video stays under wraps, Jacobs could be allowed to continue playing in the NFL.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Josh Jacobs is being removed from the NFL’s Commissioner Exempt list on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: According to Schefter, “the investigation will remain open for the NFL, so it reserves the right to add further discipline if and when warranted.” Yesterday, ESPN’s Rob Demovsky reported that the league is trying to get ahold of the video showing Jacobs’ altercation with a woman at his home. Jacobs is expected to be eligible to play in Week 7 against the Lions. The situation clearly remains in flux, but Jacobs can be stashed on fantasy football benches at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: ESPN’s Rob Demovsky reports that Josh Jacobs “has filed a civil suit seeking a permanent injunction restricting access to records from his May 23 altercation with a woman at his home.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: Demovsky notes that the NFL is trying to get the video of the altercation as part of its investigation. Jacobs is trying to prevent anyone from seeing it, citing everything from protecting the woman’s anonymity to future burglary prevention. We have no idea how this will play out, but Demovsky reported in late September that Judge Marc Hammer “denied the request by the victim in the Josh Jacobs case to have the records permanently sealed.” Jacobs is appealing this ruling. It is unclear when or if Jacobs will play in the NFL again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said he does not expect “an imminent return for Josh Jacobs.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: Jacob’s current time on the Commissioner’s Exempt List is expected to count as time served toward an eventual suspension. Rapoport added, “If they get to the point where it’s five games, six games, maybe eight games, that might be when you’re looking at a potential return for Josh Jacobs.” The NFL is currently trying to obtain video footage of the incident from the Hobart/Lawrence police department. The victim in Jacobs’ case requested that it be sealed by a judge for privacy reasons, but that request was denied. Now the NFL has filed a FOIA request to obtain it. It seems like they won’t make any decisions on Jacobs’ suspension until they have viewed the video, which could take several more weeks to resolve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: ESPN’s Rob Demovsky reports, “Judge Marc Hammer denied the request by the victim in the Josh Jacobs case to have the records permanently sealed.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: He added that the matter has been turned over to the Hobart/Lawrence police department, which is now in charge of determining whether or not the video will be released. Jacobs or the victim can then appeal that decision. The NFL has been adamant about getting the video before determining Jacobs’ pending suspension, and this increased the odds of that happening. Still, Jacobs could try to prevent that through the appeal process. Jacobs is believed to be facing a 4-6 game suspension, but the NFL can increase the length because of aggravating circumstances. This legal matter is inching toward a resolution, but a clash over the video would likely delay things even further.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Josh Jacobs could be facing a 4-6 game suspension after he pleaded no contest to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage to property.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: The league is reportedly pushing to get hold of the videotaped incident that took place between Jacobs and his ex-girlfriend, but the victim has filed a motion that states the disclosure of the tape would threaten her “privacy, dignity, security, and emotional well-being.” Fowler says this motion will make acquiring the tape “increasingly harder for the league,” but that a four-to-six-game suspension is believed to be in range for Jacobs, according to people Fowler has spoken with across the league. Jacobs remains on the commissioner’s exempt list and will not be active for Week 2’s game against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the NFL plans to interview Josh Jacobs before making a disciplinary ruling.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-jacob.analysis: According to Rapoport, the league is “trying all sorts of legal maneuvers” to get the video of the incident. The court has already barred the video from being released, so it’s unclear whether the league will be able to get it from Jacobs at all. For now, Jacobs remains on the Commissioner’s Exempt List. MarShawn Lloyd will start at running back until he is removed from the list and serves an impending suspension.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson reports David Montgomery (groin) will not play in Week 7 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: This will be the second game in a row that Montgomery has missed due to the groin injury he suffered in Week 5. Woody Marks, who totaled 17 touches in last week’s win over the Jaguars will again lead the Texans’ backfield. He has averaged 18.0 touches per game over the last two weeks and will be a volume-based RB2 with a chance at significant upside. Safeties Jalen Pitre (AC joint) and S Reed Blankenship (concussion) will also miss this week’s game against the Giants, putting the Texans down a handful of starters with one game left before their Week 8 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson reports that David Montgomery (groin) is not expected to play in Week 7 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: Like we said yesterday, Montgomery is still seemingly in the week-to-week camp. Woody Marks and Dare Ogunbowale will likely split backfield touches this week. The Texans used both Marks and Jawhar Jordan last week, but Jordan suffered an injured reserve-worthy injury. Marks should be in starting lineups, but he may be more of a FLEX than a reliable RB2. Ogunbowale is a low-floor PPR dart throw.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: David Montgomery (groin) was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: We were told early last week that Montgomery is week-to-week. Today’s absence suggests he is still week-to-week and will likely be ruled out again on Friday, though we do not know that for sure. We will provide an update before then if his status changes. In the meantime, Woody Marks will get the start again this week, potentially with less touch competition. Jawhar Jordan totaled 50 yards and a touchdown on seven total touches last week, but was surprisingly placed on injured reserve today. Dare Ogunbowale remains a receiving factor, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: Texans ruled out David Montgomery (groin) for Week 6 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: We already knew that Montgomery was considered week-to-week, so this is unsurprising. Woody Marks will start for however long Montgomery is sidelined. The Jaguars field one of the NFL’s best run defenses, but Marks ceded just one snap to Dare Ogunbowale last week. Theoretically, he should remain in a near-full-time role, elevating him to the RB2/FLEX tier despite the tough matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said David Montgomery will be week-to-week with the groin injury he suffered in Week 5 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: Ryans said Woody Marks “will carry the load” for the team while Montgomery is sidelined. It’s been a tough start to the season for Montgomery, who scored three times in Week 1 but has been locked out of the end zone ever since while averaging a career-low 3.5 yards per touch. Marks has been slightly more efficient than Montgomery this season, but the Texans’ running game as a whole has left much to be desired. Marks’ expected workload makes him worth a waiver wire claim where available, but fantasy managers shouldn’t expect anything more than RB3 levels of production at this time. The Texans will take on the Jaguars in London in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said David Montgomery (groin) may miss “some time.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: It sounds like Montgomery is in danger of missing both the Jaguars and Giants games before Houston’s Week 8 bye, assuming this is just a mild injury. Woody Marks will take over as Houston’s lead back for the time being and could be in for sizable role given how no other back received a snap or touch once Montgomery went down in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: David Montgomery (groin) will not return to Houston’s Week 5 game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: He finishes with five carries for 11 yards. Initially questionable to return in the second quarter, Montgomery was ruled out after halftime. This could open some major space for Woody Marks to have a strong role going forward. We’ll keep an eye out for updates after the game, but it doesn’t look good for Montgomery.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: David Montgomery (groin) is questionable to return to Houston’s Week 5 game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: He had five carries for 11 yards before leaving in the middle of the second quarter. Woody Marks will handle lead back duties for the moment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: David Montgomery rushed 10 times for 24 yards in Houston’s Week 4 loss against the Cowboys, adding zero receptions for 19 receiving yards on zero targets. Yes, really.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: The hook-and-ladder claims another box score. The Texans simply can’t run the ball. Woody Marks is a little faster at making something out of nothing, but it’s the same nothing for him. Montgomery should at least have game pace in his favor against the Titans in Week 5, but boy is it hard to trust him as more than a FLEX play right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.headline: David Montgomery rushed 11 times for 33 yards in Houston’s Week 3 loss to the Colts, adding two catches for 15 yards on his only two targets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/david-mont.analysis: The only official goal-line carry of the game went to Woody Marks in the two-minute drill. Montgomery added one of the dumbest-looking running back passes on first-and-goal in recent memory, though that play was bailed out as something like five different Colts committed DPI on Jaylin Noel in the end zone. Montgomery’s best play of the game was a minus-1 yard carry in his own end zone where he pulled out the entire stop/start arsenal to prevent a safety. It’s beginning to give RB3 vibes as we look ahead to Week 4’s game against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Adonai Mitchell (finger) will play in Week 7 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell has been sidelined since injuring his finger in preparation for the Jets’ Week 3 game against the Lions. It was incredibly unfortunate time for Mitchell and his fantasy managers, as his injury came just days after he went for 6-63-0 on 12 targets against the Packers. Mitchell’s return could complicate things for Omar Cooper’s fantasy managers after Cooper broke out for 6-103-1 against the Patriots last week. The Jets rank 13th in the league in plays run from 11-personnel (209) through the first six weeks of the season, which means both Mitchell and Cooper should see plenty of snaps. That said, neither player should be viewed as anything more than a WR3/FLEX play until we see how the target distribution looks with both players active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell (finger) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: It is too early to say whether Mitchell and his surgically repaired finger will be ready to face the Dolphins this week. He is a worthwhile bench stash, though. Mitchell played well early in the year, pre-injury and pre-breakout from rookie Omar Cooper. It is unclear whether Mitchell will return to the No. 2 wide receiver role or if he will be asked to unseat the youngster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell (finger) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell has missed the past four weeks with a finger injury that required a “small procedure” to fix. Though a limited practice today doesn’t guarantee he will be back for Week 7, it’s a big step in the right direction. Mitchell had nine catches for 123 yards in his first two appearances this year. If he’s able to return this week, he would at least earn a spot on the WR3/4 border versus the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell (finger) will not play in Week 6 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: It was reported earlier this week that Mitchell underwent a “small procedure” on the finger he injured in practice ahead of Week 3. Given that news, it doesn’t come as much of a surprise to learn that Mitchell will miss his fourth straight game with the injury. With rookie Omar Cooper Jr. set to play in his first game since Week 1, Mitchell could face additional competition for targets when he finally returns to the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Jets coach Aaron Glenn said Adonai Mitchell underwent a “small procedure” on his hand.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: As expected, he did not practice today. Per Glenn, Mitchell remains week to week. This explains the lengthy absence for Mitchell, who hasn’t played since injuring his finger in practice ahead of Week 3. According to Glenn, Mitchell is moving his fingers around well, which is hopefully a sign that he will be back soon. With Omar Cooper Jr.'s practice window now open, Mitchell could return to a rather crowded receiver room once he is healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell (finger) will not play in Week 5 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell will miss his third straight game with the finger injury he sustained in practice, ahead of Week 3’s game against the Lions. During Mitchell’s absence, Isaiah Williams has run 59 routes, the second-most of any Jets receiver, but has seen just five targets. Garrett Wilson is the only reliable receiver in this passing game, while rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq is a boom-or-bust option against a defense that has allowed the ninth-most fantasy points to tight ends this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Adonai Mitchell (finger) remains week to week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell will likely miss his third straight game with the finger issue. He suffered the injury just as he was coming on as the team’s clear No. 2 wideout behind Garrett Wilson. With Mitchell sidelined last week against the Bears, Isaiah Williams was second on the team in pass routes, saw three targets, and caught a 58-yard touchdown from Geno Smith. Williams will have some deep-league viability in Week 5 against a Browns defense allowing the most air yards in the NFL. Adonai was officially a non-participant on Wednesday’s injury report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Jets declared WR Adonai Mitchell, RB Breece Hall, CB Nahshon Wright, LB Kiko Mauigoa, DE Kingsley Enagbare, OL Dylan Parham, and TE Mason Taylor inactive for Week 4 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell will miss another game with his finger injury and Hall will be sidelined with a quad injury he sustained last week against the Lions. Garrett Wilson, with Mitchell out, should continue dominating air yards and targets in the balanced Jets offense. Braelon Allen will take over as New York’s lead back for now and should be in all fantasy lineups against a suspect Chicago run defense. Kenyon Sadiq has some streaming appeal with Mitchell out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell (finger) will not play in Week 4 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: Mitchell was a DNP in Wednesday’s and Thursday’s practices, so the team’s decision to rule him out on Friday doesn’t come as a surprise. Mitchell will now aim to return in Week 5 against the Browns. Rookie tight end Kenyon Sadiq, who saw a season-high eight targets last week in Mitchell’s absence, will be on the fantasy radar as a fringe TE1 with Mitchell again sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.headline: Adonai Mitchell (finger) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/adonai-mitchel.analysis: It’s trending in the wrong direction for Mitchell’s odds of playing in Week 4. We imagine he’ll get in at least a limited session Friday to see how natural it is for him to catch the football with his injured finger, but he looks headed for the questionable line — at best — against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) will be questionable for Week 7 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Glenn said Hall will be limited in Friday’s practice and that the team will “see how that goes” to close out the week. Hall has missed the last three games with his quad injury but the fact he is closing out the week with two-straight limited practices suggests he’ll be a true game-time decision entering Sunday. If he’s unable to play, Braelon Allen would again serve as the primary back in the Jets’ backfield and would be a fringe RB1/RB2 in what is shaping up to be a plus matchup against the lowly Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Breece Hall (quad) returned to practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Reporters on the scene said that Hall headed to the rehab area after reporters left the scene, so he’ll probably be given a limited session. Still, he moved well and likely at least has a chance to suit up for Week 7 after this update. Friday’s practice will be telling. It would be surprising if Hall doesn’t at least hit the questionable line as long as he practices on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Breece Hall (quad) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Head coach Aaron Glenn noted that Hall’s status will be evaluated throughout the week. Hall hasn’t played since injuring his quad in Week 3. If the Jets expected him to miss four games, they likely would have placed him on injured reserve. On the other hand, Adonai Mitchell just missed four games with a hand injury and was not placed on IR, so the team seemingly doesn’t have a great read on their players’ health. Hall will likely miss Week 7. Braelon Allen, in turn, is in line for a high-end RB2 ranking versus a weak Dolphins defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Breece Hall (quad) will not play in Week 6 against the Patriots
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Things have been trending in this direction for Hall all week. The 25-year-old back was a DNP on both Wednesday and Thursday, and will now miss a third straight game as a result of his injury. Braelon Allen will again lead the Jets’ backfield this week against the Patriots and has handled 44 of the Jets’ 48 running back opportunities since Week 4. Allen will be a volatile RB2 against a Patriots defense that ranks 18th against running backs in fantasy scoring this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: ESPN’s Rich Cimini reports that Breece Hall (quad) is working with trainers on the side field on Thursday, yet remains week-to-week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: This is a small but positive update. Hall typically works on his quad rehab program elsewhere or simply observes practice. Today’s return to the side field will still result in him being listed as a non-participant, but as Cimini says, this is measurable “progress” for the Jets’ top running back. Braelon Allen will undoubtedly get the start this week, but perhaps Hall has a chance to return in Week 7 against the Dolphins. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Jets coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) remains week-to-week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Hall will not practice today, and it sounds like he will not practice on Thursday or Friday either. Braelon Allen has played productively in his stead, most recently rushing 24 times for 116 yards and a touchdown against the Browns. Allen is a locked-in RB2 until Hall returns from his upper-leg injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Breece Hall (quad) will not play in Week 5 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Braelon Allen will once again be in line to lead the Jets’ backfield with Hall sidelined for a second consecutive week. Hall did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday and will presumably be a DNP again on Friday, now that he has been ruled out ahead of practice. Allen saw 100 percent of the Jets’ running back opportunities last week, rushing 14 times for 59 scoreless yards while adding two receptions for an additional eight yards on two targets. He’ll be a fringe RB1/RB2 in what should be another high-volume day for the third-year back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) is still “week to week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: It doesn’t look like Hall will practice this week as he recovers from the injury he sustained in Week 3. That would mean Braelon Allen, who saw all 14 running back rushes for New York in Week 4, will again function as the team’s workhorse in Week 5 against the Browns. Allen should still be considered a top-24 option despite the Jets’ immense offensive struggles last week against Chicago. The Browns’ defense is allowing the sixth-highest EPA per rush this season. Hall was officially a non-participant on Wednesday’s injury report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Jets declared WR Adonai Mitchell, RB Breece Hall, CB Nahshon Wright, LB Kiko Mauigoa, DE Kingsley Enagbare, OL Dylan Parham, and TE Mason Taylor inactive for Week 4 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Mitchell will miss another game with his finger injury and Hall will be sidelined with a quad injury he sustained last week against the Lions. Garrett Wilson, with Mitchell out, should continue dominating air yards and targets in the balanced Jets offense. Braelon Allen will take over as New York’s lead back for now and should be in all fantasy lineups against a suspect Chicago run defense. Kenyon Sadiq has some streaming appeal with Mitchell out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.headline: Breece Hall (quad) will not play in Week 4 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/breece-hal.analysis: Hall was initially mentioned as being week-to-week when he was diagnosed with his quad injury, so he was never really considered a candidate to play in Week 4 despite the team waiting until the end of the week to rule him out. With Hall out, the Jets will look to Braelon Allen to handle most of the backfield duties. Allen will profile as a solid RB2 candidate with a chance for more upside in what could be a high-volume day against the Bears. In addition to Hall, the Jets also ruled out OG Dylan Parham (knee), TE Mason Taylor (thumb), and LB Kiko Mauigoa (quad) for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (foot) will play in Week 7 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright has rushed 14 times for 28 scoreless yards this season and has yet to receive a target in the four games he has appeared in. Fellow running back Ollie Gordon has emerged as the unquestioned RB1 for the Dolphins since the team lost De’Von Achane (knee) in Week 3. Wright is well off the fantasy radar at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (foot) remained limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright played through this listing ahead of Week 5, but it appears that he simply won’t shake it this year. It makes him hard to trust him as someone who could suddenly usurp the lead role from Ollie Gordon, but we’d be surprised if he didn’t play in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (foot) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: The Dolphins’ speedy back will likely serve as a change-of-pace option behind Ollie Gordon, who has outplayed Wright since De’Von Achane’s season-ending knee injury. Wright does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright rushed six times for 11 yards in the Dolphins’ Week 5 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright entered the day questionable with a foot injury and wound up playing nine offensive snaps with special teams mixed in. The 23-year-old is the clear backup to Ollie Gordon for now, he is best left off fantasy rosters.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Dolphins RB Jaylen Wright (foot) is active for Week 5 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright had back-to-back limited practices to close out the week after seemingly reaggravating a foot injury. He is active against the Bengals and will backup Ollie Gordon for Week 5. The Dolphins declared WR Caleb Douglas (ankle), RB Kaytron Allen, CB Reese Taylor, EDGE Rob Beal Jr., G DJ Campbell, OT Chukwuebuka Godrick, and TE Justin Joly inactive for Week 5 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (foot) is questionable for Miami’s Week 5 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright was limited on Thursday and Friday after seemingly reinjuring his foot. He feels like a true wild card for Sunday. Ollie Gordon-reliant managers would benefit if Wright were ruled out, as it appears Kaytron Allen, who was just claimed on waivers today, would be the backup if Wright can’t go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright (foot) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: It’s unclear if this was related to the foot that was giving Wright problems earlier this year, but a mid-week downgrade is never great news for a player. Wright has a real chance to miss Week 5. We’ll probably have a better sign of how likely it is that he plays Friday morning if no national reporters pick up the story earlier than that.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Jaylen Wright rushed five times for seven yards in the Dolphins’ Week 4 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: The best thing we can say about Wright’s day is that he got the start. The Dolphins kept him out there for the first drive, giving him a chance to keep his position, but he was unable to do so. Ollie Gordon outplayed him as the game progressed, rushing nine times for 100 yards and one touchdown, while Wright was relegated to unproductive offensive snaps and five kick returns for 97 yards. Wright is a zero-floor FLEX against the Bengals next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: The South Florida Sun Sentinel’s David Furones reports that Dolphins RB Jaylen Wright is lining up with the first-team offense during pre-game warmups.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Dolphins RB Ollie Gordon is rotating in behind Wright, confirming Wright is the team’s current starter. That said, the Dolphins could still split the backfield workload almost evenly. We won’t know what the plan is until the game is underway. For now, Wright should be viewed as the slightly safer FLEX, though both running backs could get bottled up by the Vikings’ defense today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.headline: Dolphins RB Jaylen Wright (foot) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jaylen-wright/.analysis: Wright sits atop the Dolphins’ depth chart with De’Von Achane (knee) done for the year. He will likely split touches with new No. 2 running back Ollie Gordon in a very difficult matchup against the Vikings this week. Both players are worth rostering, but they are shaky FLEX starters this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Dolphins WR Caleb Douglas (ankle) will play in Week 7 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: Douglas hasn’t played since Week 2 against the 49ers, but the rookie caught five passes for 94 yards in his pro debut against the Raiders and has been targeted on 16.4 percent of his routes. Stuck in a Dolphins offense that currently ranks 31st in scoring and passing yards, Douglas will be hard to trust as anything more than a fringe WR3/WR4 this week against a top-five Jets pass defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) remained limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: That’s back-to-back limited sessions from Douglas as he attempts to come back from an injury suffered in Week 2. We’d bet on him getting to the questionable line at this point given the significant layoff, but he does have a real chance to play against the Jets in Week 7 and be a WR4/FLEX candidate.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: Douglas told reporters that he has finally progressed to being “day-to-day,” giving him a real chance to suit up in Week 7 against the Jets. Douglas should be added in 12-team formats. He played very well early on and will likely warrant FLEX consideration upon his return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) won’t play in Miami’s Week 5 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: Douglas has not practiced or played since Week 2. If only there were some sort of “injured reserve list” he could be placed on. Ah well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: Dolphins coach Jeff Halfey said Douglas is “doing better” but is not ready to practice yet. It sounds like the rookie will miss another week. Malik Washington will continue to operate as the Dolphins’ No. 1 receiver, putting him in the WR3 mix for Week 5. Fellow rookie Chris Bell has seen his role grow every week, but the fantasy numbers aren’t there to match. He was held without a catch on three targets in Week 4. Bell is a solid long-term stash but barely cracks the WR5 ranks for Miami’s matchup with the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said the team is taking it “one day at a time” with Caleb Douglas’ ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: It’s hard to know what to make of this, but Douglas has missed back-to-back games with his injury and could be at risk of missing a third straight game if he can’t get on the practice field ahead of Week 5’s game against the Bengals. Douglas did not practice at all last week, so even getting on the field in a limited capacity would be an improvement. His name will be one to keep an eye on when the Dolphins release their first injury report on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Dolphins declared WR Caleb Douglas, QB Brady Cook, CB Marcellas Dial, EDGE Rob Beal, OG DJ Campbell, OT Chukwuebuka Godrick and TE Justin Joly inactive for Week 4 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: The Dolphins will be without Douglas, one of their two talented rookie wide receivers, against the Vikings’ top-tier defense today. He is sidelined by an ankle injury. Joly, the Dolphins’ rookie tight end, is inactive after making his debut last week. Cook wil serve as the team’s emergency third quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) will not play in Week 4 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: Douglas will miss his second straight game with an ankle injury, paving the way for fellow rookie Chris Bell to build on his Week 3 performance in which he went for 4-67-0 on eight targets. Bell and all Dolphins pass-catchers will be tough for fantasy managers to trust as anything more than WR4s on the road against a Vikings defense that could give them fits all afternoon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: We expect to see Douglas listed with a second DNP next to his name today, putting him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 4 against the Vikings. Were he indeed to miss this week’s game, WRs Chris Bell (knee) and Malik Washington would benefit. Washington’s target volume is somewhat intriguing, but Bell looks like the far more talented player.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.headline: Caleb Douglas (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/caleb-doug.analysis: Douglas, who has shown flashes in limited action so far this season, did not suit up in Week 3 against the Chiefs and looks like a long shot for Week 4 against the Vikings. Douglas’ absence would be a potential boost for Malik Washington, who leads the Dolphins in targets and air yards through Week 3. Minnesota’s defense, while elite, has allowed the fourth most air yards this season and profiles as a pass-funnel.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-watt/5.headline: T.J. Watt (calf) was removed from the Steelers’ Week 7 injury report and will play against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-watt/5.analysis: Watt popped up on Thursday’s injury report with a calf injury and was listed as limited. On Friday, he was upgraded to a full participant in what was an estimated report, but he does not carry an injury status heading into the weekend. S DeShon Elliott (knee) is listed as questionable but was listed as a full participant throughout the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-watt/5.headline: T.J. Watt (calf) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-watt/5.analysis: It’s a new injury today that kept Watt to a limited session. We’re not overly concerned about it, and the fact that the Steelers are traveling overseas will likely keep practices lighter anyway. We expect the 32-year-old to suit up again on Sunday morning.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-watt/5.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport believes that the Steelers are likely to keep EDGE T.J. Watt and EDGE Alex Highsmith on the roster for 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-watt/5.analysis: Watt, 31, and Highsmith, 28, were the starting EDGE rushers last year. Their 24-year-old backup, LB Nick Herbig, signed a four-year, $100 million extension on Tuesday, prompting questions as to whether the Steelers could consider trading away one of their two veterans. Highsmith was not present at mandatory minicamp on Wednesday, but this was reportedly due to a stomach bug , not discontent over his backup’s big payday. Per Rapoport, Watt’s “enormous” contract, coupled with the amount of money the Steelers have invested elsewhere in their EDGE unit, means that they will probably “have a decision to make” in 2027.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-watt/5.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports “some teams could see Pittsburgh at least considering moving on” from T.J. Watt in 2027.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-watt/5.analysis: As Fowler notes, Steelers EDGE Nick Herbig is a free agent next offseason. Pittsburgh’s No. 3 pass-rusher is expected to be a hot name on the open market. The Steelers could work toward an extension for him before that happens, but they can’t realistically pay Watt, Herbig, and T.J. Watt top dollar. A Herbig extension might make Watt more valuable to the team as a trade asset. Still, it’s hard to believe the Steelers would trade one of the faces of their franchise at the tail end of his prime. How both he and Herbig play in 2026 will determine what GM Omar Khan does next offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-watt/5.headline: The Steelers and Saints will play in Paris for Week 7 of the 2026 season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-watt/5.analysis: The Saints will host the Steelers in a Paris matchup, the inaugural Paris game for the NFL at the Stade de France. The Saints did not play an international game in 2025 while the Steelers will play overseas for the second straight year, defeating the Vikings in Ireland last season. The game will be during Week 7 of the 2026 season, potentially meaning a bye for both teams before or after the game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-watt/5.headline: Steelers declared EDGE T.J. Watt active for Week 18 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-watt/5.analysis: Watt isn’t expected to get his usual amount of snaps, but the future Hall of Famer will be able to held as a pass-rusher in sub-packages in the winner-take-all game. The Steelers inactives for Week 18 will be WR Roman Wilson, QB Will Howard, RB Kaleb Johnson, CB Tre Flowers, LB Jeremiah Moon and OT Jack Driscoll.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-watt/5.headline: Steelers EDGE T.J. Watt (lung) said he “feels really good” and is “excited to play” against the Ravens in Week 18.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-watt/5.analysis: An interview with DC Teryl Austin foreshadowed that Watt may be kept to sub-package work this week, but anything the Steelers can get from him in a must-win AFC North title game will be appreciated. Watt missed Weeks 15-17 after undergoing surprise surgery to repair his lung following a dry needling. He has seven sacks in 13 games started this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-watt/5.headline: Steelers EDGE T.J. Watt (lung) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-watt/5.analysis: Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin previously said Watt needs to get in a week of full practices before being cleared. His limited participation is encouraging, but he is not yet guaranteed to suit up on game day, which means Watt may have played his last snap of the season already. The Steelers (9-7) and Ravens (8-8) are playing for a trip to the postseason on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-watt/5.headline: Steelers EDGE T.J. Watt (lung) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-watt/5.analysis: Watt was limited in practice last week but didn’t play on Sunday. Mike Tomlin previously said that Watt needs to get in a week of full practices before being cleared. His limited designation today means that he isn’t likely to suit up this week. Losing Watt will be a big blow to a Steelers defense that will need to keep Lamar Jackson in check to punch their ticket to the playoffs via an AFC North title.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-watt/5.headline: Steelers coach Mike Tomlin said he is “more optimistic than I have been in recent weeks” about LB T.J. Watt (lung) playing in Week 18.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/t-j-watt/5.analysis: That’s not to necessarily Watt has a good chance given the reporting we’ve already had that he’s a long shot, and the qualifier “in recent weeks” is holding up the optimism. We think Watt has a chance to play, but he’ll probably have to start practicing in full by Thursday for Tomlin to confidently plug him in for the AFC North championship on Sunday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) was removed from the injury report for Week 7’s game against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara was still listed as limited in Friday’s practice, but the Saints feel confident enough in his health to clear him for Week 7. Kamara found the end zone last week on a 31-yard reception, but has largely been inefficient with his touches this season. He seen 14 opportunities to Kendre Miller’s 30 over the last two weeks and will be hard to trust as anything more than a touchdown-dependent RB3 against the Steelers. The only players on the Saints carrying injury designations into the weekend are guard Cesar Ruiz (knee) and DL Nathan Sheperd (illness). Both are listed as questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: He’s played through this listing for a few weeks now, and though he’ll sometimes get dinged up in game, appears no worse for the wear. Kendre Miller feels like the more viable back in a normal game script right now, with Kamara playing more on passing downs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara has been playing through the back issue for several weeks. He is expected to do so again this week. Kamara is part of a three-back committee, and he isn’t the leader of the trio, but that didn’t stop him from finding the end zone on nine touches last week. With a limited receiving role to go along with his shrinking rushing workload, he’s barely in the RB3 mix for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara rushed seven times for 34 yards in the Saints’ Week 6 win over the Giants, adding two receptions for 35 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: The Saints deployed a committee backfield once again for Week 6. Kamara was the third running back into the game for the Saints, but was the only one to score a touchdown. He briefly went to the medical tent after falling on his hip in the first half but re-entered the game soon after. Kamara caught a swing pass from Tyler Shough and tip-toed away from the sideline to score from 17 yards out in the third quarter. With that catch, he became the sixth player in NFL history with 5,000 yards receiving and 5,000 yards rushing in his career. Despite the touchdown and milestone, Kamara was still third in running back snaps and is a touchdown-dependent FLEX play for Week 7 against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Saints declared RB Alvin Kamara (back) active for Week 6 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara is active after NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported he would be expected to play in Week 6. He played through the back injury last week and is part of a rough running back committee in the Saints backfield. Kamara is in the RB4 ranks for fantasy purposes. Also active is Chris Olave (illness). The Saints declared QB Zach Wilson, EDGE Anfernee Jennings, S Mike Reid, LB Kaden Elliss, DT Nathan Shepherd, and DT John Ridgeway inactive for Week 6 against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Alvin Kamara (back) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara played through the back issue last week, though he only saw five touches. He has fallen behind Kendre Miller in the pecking order for carries, and even CJ Donaldson is pushing him for work on passing downs. Kamara is barely an RB4 for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) is questionable for New Orleans’ Week 6 game against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara practiced each day this week, so it’s a bit surprising to see him here. Assuming no rough quotes or reports come out, we’d regard him as on the optimistic side of questionable. He’s a reasonable FLEX play against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara played through this injury in Week 5, and it doesn’t seem like he’s in any real danger of missing this one. It would be nice to see a full practice on Friday, but even if we don’t get that, Kamara should be a FLEX consideration for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: Kamara played through the back injury last week but only touched the ball five times. Kendre Miller rushed 10 times and CJ Donaldson led the team in snaps. The Saints are likely managing Kamara’s workload as he deals with this back issue. Kamara is not on the fantasy radar for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.headline: Alvin Kamara rushed three times for 12 yards in the Saints’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alvin-kama.analysis: He “added” two catches for -6 yards. Kamara rotated with Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson throughout the game. Donaldson ultimately led the backfield in snaps, while Miller’s 10 carries paced the team. Kamara only touched the ball once in the second half and spent long stretches of the final two quarters on the sidelines with his helmet off. The team was likely managing his reps while he played through a back injury. He was listed as questionable heading into today’s game. As part of a three-man committee, Kamara is barely an RB4 for his Week 6 date with the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.headline: FOX59’s Tyler Haughn reports Colts QB Anthony Richardson was charged with misdemeanor possession of marijuana earlier this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.analysis: According to reports, Richardson was stopped on October 12th for having a registration on his car that had expired and was assigned to a different vehicle. The officer reported noticing the “odor of marijuana” coming from Richardson’s car, and the former first-round pick admitted to smoking in the car; a “small mason jar containing a substance believed to be marijuana and an opened bag of THC-infused gummies” were found in his vehicle during a search. Richardson is scheduled to have a bench trial on January 4th, 2027. While the NFL no longer suspends players for testing positive for THC, it’s possible Richardson faces some kind of penalty from the league with this being a legal issue.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.headline: Colts HC Shane Steichen said Anthony Richardson (groin) will be good to go for Week 2 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.analysis: Richardson will be dressed to back up Daniel Jones in Sunday’s game against the Chiefs. Richardson tweaked his groin while lifting earlier this week, per head coach Shane Steichen, but he is good to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.headline: Anthony Richardson (groin) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.analysis: Perhaps the groin issue was just maintenance. Either way, Richardson is unlikely to be in line for any work in Week 2. The question here is simply if Richardson will back up Daniel Jones in Week 2 or if Riley Leonard will have to pick up the slack.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.headline: Anthony Richardson (groin) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.analysis: It’s unclear how Richardson picked up the groin injury after not playing a snap in Week 1. He earned the backup job during the summer but will now hand that over to Riley Leonard if he isn’t able to suit up this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.headline: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Anthony Richardson will serve as the team’s backup quarterback.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.analysis: Richardson spent training camp and the preseason battling it out with Riley Leonard for the backup gig. Given the arc of Richardson’s career, earning the backup gig is undoubtedly a win for the young passer. Richardson isn’t on the redraft fantasy radar, but dynasty managers can leave the light on for him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.headline: Colts general manager Chris Ballard said he expects Anthony Richardson, Jr. to remain with the team in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.analysis: Richardson is listed alongside Riley Leonard as the team’s QB2 for now. Either Leonard or Richardson — who struggled in the preseason — will serve as Daniel Jones’ backup this season. One of the most inaccurate passers in modern NFL history, Richardson would be a massive downgrade for all Indy pass catchers if he finds his way under center in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.headline: ESPN’s Stephen Holder reports that “signs continue to point to” the Colts keeping QB Anthony Richardson on the roster in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.analysis: Holder cites comments made by Colts assistant general manager Ed Dodds today. Dodds did not come right out and share the team’s plans, but when asked about Richardson’s status, he stressed the importance of having three quarterbacks on the roster. The Colts’ quarterback position group was so banged up last year that they brought Philip Rivers out of retirement. Recouping value for Richardson has its merits, but the Colts intend to compete this season. Keeping the quarterback room deep makes sense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.headline: Anthony Richardson completed 11-of-14 passes for 145 yards and an interception in Thursday’s preseason game against the Patriots, adding another six carries for 53 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.analysis: Richardson’s interception came on a play in which the ball bounced off his receiver’s hands and into a defender’s arms. The former No. 4 overall pick was mostly solid on Thursday, making quick and decisive throws to his receivers while going a perfect 6-for-6 on pass attempts of 10-plus air yards. Richardson also lost a fumble on a 10-yard scramble in the second quarter, but made up for it later on a one-yard touchdown run on a QB sneak. His days as a Colt are likely numbered. Richardson stringing together a nice preseason could draw the interest of several QB-needy teams before the start of the season and position him to eventually see the field sometime in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.headline: Colts announced Anthony Richardson will start Thursday’s preseason game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.analysis: Richardson and Riley Leonard will both play, while Daniel Jones will sit. Richardson’s trade request this offseason has gone nowhere, but the Colts appear to be giving him ample opportunity to showcase himself in the preseason as he will get the first half here and the second half next week against Atlanta, while Leonard picks up the other two halves. The Colts are likely hoping someone talks themselves into trading a low pick for Richardson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Colts QB Anthony Richardson must answer “real questions” as to how effective his eyesight is.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-ri.analysis: Rapoport adds that he “would not be surprised” if Richardson has played his last down as a Colt, and believes he could be traded or waived, seemingly soon. Richardson was recently seen taking third-team reps at practice, and Rapoport wonders whether Richardson can really see pass rushers on either side of him or the receivers running routes downfield. Richardson infamously injured his eye in a pre-game mishap with a resistance band last year, which Rapoport describes as “one of the most absurd and ridiculous injuries of all time.” He really didn’t hold back here. Back in May, The Athletic’s James Boyd used the “questions remain” line regarding Richardson’s eyesight as well, but follow-up reports have been difficult to come by. Richardson’s time as a Colt may be coming to a close, but finding a new team could be harder than expected if there is more to this eyesight story.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle (knee) is questionable for Week 7 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: Dowdle was listed as limited throughout the week and will officially be questionable entering this week’s game with the Saints. This is a new injury he is dealing with but it doesn’t sound like he’s at serious risk of missing the game at this time. Dowdle played on just 17 percent of snaps in his return to action last week and saw 11 opportunities. He’ll profile as a low-end RB3 this week if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: It’s a new injury that popped up on Wednesday, but with two limited sessions we’re not overly concerned about Dowdle missing Sunday morning’s Civil Unrest Bowl in Paris. He’ll be in the RB3/FLEX discussion.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle (toe) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: The Steelers will likely limit Dowdle’s reps for a few weeks as he manages the toe injury that cost him three games. He should be good to go for Sunday’s game by Friday. Dowdle saw 10 touches in his first game back and looked relatively explosive, running for 40 yards on seven attempts. He is in the RB3 mix for Week 7 versus the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle rushed seven times for 40 yards in the Steelers’ Week 6 win over the Bucs, adding three catches for nine yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: Dowdle was active for the first time since injuring his toe in Week 2. He initially formed a near 50-50 committee with Jaylen Warren, but the latter pulled away in the fourth quarter and overtime. Warren racked up four carries and one catch in overtime alone, bringing his touch total from 11 to 16. Dowdle saw a single carry in the extra frame. Dowdle’s role should grow in the coming weeks, but it’s clear that Warren is the top option in the backfield, leaving Dowdle as a low-end RB3 for Week 7 versus the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle (toe) is active for Week 6 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: Dowdle is back after missing three games with the toe issue. He will form a committee with Jaylen Warren, but the latter’s elite play last week likely earned him a larger split of the backfield in Week 6. Dowdle will primarily operate between the tackles, pushing him to the back of the RB3 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Rico Dowdle (toe) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: Dowdle has been out since Week 2 because of the toe issue. In the meantime, Jaylen Warren has looked like one of the league’s most dynamic backs on the ground and through the air. While his gargantuan workload will return to normal with Dowdle back, Warren should still operate as the team’s unquestioned RB1. Dowdle is just a mid-range FLEX play for his first game back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle (toe) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: Dowdle seemingly has a good chance to play. He was limited on Wednesday, but practiced in full on Thursday and Friday. However, Jaylen Warren has played extremely well with Dowdle sidelined and coach Mike McCarthy has said that Warren will remain a high-volume player. If active, Dowdle is a FLEX starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle (toe) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: It’s his first full practice since suffering the toe injury. Dowdle looks to be headed for hard-to-trust FLEX territory with Jaylen Warren crushing in his absence and Mike McCarthy (rightfully) saying that Warren deserves the lion’s share of the workload at the moment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Rico Dowdle (toe) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: Dowdle is expected to return to action this week after missing the past three games with a toe injury. Jaylen Warren has dominated the Steelers’ backfield in his absence and the results have been marvelous. He currently leads the team in rushing (410) and receiving yards (230). Even once healthy, Dowdle will likely struggle to force a 1B role in the backfield right away. He will be an RB4 for Week 6 if he’s given the green light.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said “there’s a number you’d like to continue to give [Jaylen Warren],” even after Rico Dowdle (toe) returns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rico-dowdl.analysis: “He’s produced, so it’s been heavy. It’d be great to get Rico back this week, too. ... Having him as a one-two punch was the vision of this offense, but Jaylen’s crushing it right now. He’s been awesome for us,” McCarthy continued. That’s a very telling “but.” Warren has to be regarded as the chair of a committee at this point rather than in a backfield split, and Dowdle probably doesn’t belong in the FLEX conversation coming off his injury until we see a good workload for him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.headline: Jaguars OL Anton Harrison was revealed to have a torn ACL, ending his season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.analysis: Surgeons discovered Harrison suffered a torn ACL while performing knee surgery on him Thursday. The 23-year-old lineman will now be placed on season-ending IR, with hopes of returning in time for training camp next season. Harrison allowed just 13 pressures and two sacks in five games this season, earning a PFF pass-blocking grade of 67.2. Walker Little, who took over in Harrison’s absence, started last week against the Texans and will assume the starting left tackle role going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.headline: Jaguars OL Anton Harrison will undergo knee surgery and will miss at least 3-5 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.analysis: He’s been placed on injured reserve. Harrison, who sustained the injury in Week 5 against the Eagles, could miss the rest of the season once doctors determine the severity of his knee injury, according to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport. Harrison had protected Trevor Lawrence’s blindside before the injury. His absence could be a problem for a Jacksonville offensive line that has the league’s third worst pass blocking win rate.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.headline: Anton Harrison was carted off the field with an apparent leg injury in the Jaguars’ Week 5 game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.analysis: Harrison went down with a non-contact injury in the third quarter. He rode the cart to the locker room. His day is likely over. Walker Little will take his spot at left tackle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.headline: Jaguars OT Cole Van Lanen (knee) was removed from the injury report for Week 1 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.analysis: Van Lanen should at least be active, although he is not guaranteed to start. The veteran blocker broke out last year, playing all across the line before settling in at left tackle. He suffered a knee injury in Week 18, which forced the coaching staff to get OT Anton Harrison for left tackle duties while penciling Van Lanen in at right tackle. The team also has capable OT Walker Little at the ready. Unfortunately, Harrison appeared on the injury report with a foot injury and was unable to practice on Friday. Hopefully, his sidelining was a precaution and he is not seriously injured. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.headline: Jaguars exercised the fifth-year option for RT Anton Harrison.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.analysis: Harrison was drafted with the No. 27 overall pick back in 2023 and has started all 48 games he’s appeared in since joining the team. He has spent his entire career at right tackle, allowing 10 sacks and 93 pressures in 48 regular-season games, and earned a PFF pass-blocking grade of 75.6 last season — his highest mark to date. Harrison will now be under contract with the Jaguars through the 2027 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.headline: Jaguars exercised RT Anton Harrison’s fifth-year option.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.analysis: Over The Cap projects Harrison’s option at $19 million, but in announcing they’d pick it up, Jaguars GM James Gladstone said they’ll have “deeper conversations” on a long-term extension. Harrison, 24, had his best season yet in 2025, registering a career-high 75.6 PFF pass block grade while protecting Trevor Lawrence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.headline: Jaguars RT Anton Harrison (illness) is active for Jacksonville’s Week 17 game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.analysis: He was questionable after being added to the report with an illness Sunday morning. The only other questionable Jaguars player was C Robert Hainsey (groin), who was scratched. Also inactive for the Jaguars are: CB Keith Taylor, RB Bhayshul Tuten (finger), OL Patrick Mekari (back), TE Hunter Long, DL Danny Striggow (ankle) and DT Maason Smith.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.headline: Jaguars RT Anton Harrison (illness) is questionable for Week 17 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.analysis: Harrison was added to the injury report on Sunday morning, likely after falling ill over the weekend. Players tend to play through illnesses, so this shouldn’t be an issue for the Jags. Cole Van Lanen will take his spot in the lineup if Harrison can’t go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.headline: Jaguars RT Anton Harrison (elbow) left Jacksonville’s Week 4 game against the 49ers and is questionable to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.analysis: He was injured in the second quarter and vacated the sideline quickly afterwards. Harrison was replaced by Chuma Edoga.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.headline: Jaguars T Anton Harrison (ankle) questionable to return against Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anton-harr.analysis: Harrison left in the second half of the Jaguars’ game against the Texans in Week 3 with an ankle injury. He is questionable to return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rome Odunze caught 4-of-5 targets for 69 yards in the Bears’ Week 7 win over the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The yardage total goes down as Odunze’s second highest mark of the season as the third-year receiver was held out of the end zone for the seventh straight game to start the 2026 season. He did make three massive catches on third downs to help extend drives, making his mark felt more with quality than quantity. That doesn’t necessarily benefit fantasy managers that chased his big play abilities this offseason as Odunze has largely been a fantasy dud outside of the Week four win over the Jets in which he returned 15.4 PPR points. He remains best left on fantasy benches ahead of another difficult test against the Seahawks in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rome Odunze caught 3-of-4 targets for 39 yards in the Bears’ Week 6 win against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Odunze, who led the Bears in pass routes on the day, was third in targets while Luther Burden and Colston Loveland had big days with Caleb Williams back under center. Odunze was seeing more targets and air yards with the Bears’ backups QBs under center, though he should remain a high-variance flex in Week 7 against the Patriots. Odunze leads the Chicago offense with a 35 percent air yards share this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rome Odunze caught 3-of-9 targets for 40 yards in the Bears’ Week 5 loss to the Packers, also losing a fumble.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Although the Bears were already losing 31-7, Odunze’s fourth quarter giveaway was an ill-advised decision on a fourth down catch-and-run where he had already secured a new set of downs. Odunze seemed to be extending the ball forward. Unnecessary. Like every Bears pass catcher, Odunze is treading fantasy water waiting for the return of Caleb Williams (hamstring). It appears that will be Week 6 against the Falcons, but Odunze’s returns have been uneven enough that not even Williams’ re-insertion under center will be enough to get Odunze above the mid-range WR3 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rome Odunze caught 6-of-7 targets for 94 yards in the Bears’ Week 4 win against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Tyson Bagent, making his first NFL start, locked on to his boundary wideout in the first half, hitting Odunze for a couple long gains, including a nicely-placed 37 yarder. Odunze was second on the team in targets behind Colston Loveland, who saw nine looks on the day. Odunze is leading the Bears offense in air yards and profiles as a high-variance weekly fantasy option in an offense that leans toward the run. Odunze will be a solid flex option in Week 5 against a Green Bay secondary that struggles against boundary receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rome Odunze caught 3-of-6 targets for 44 yards in the Bears’ Week 3 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Odunze continues to function as the deep threat in Ben Johnson’s offense, which spells trouble for his fantasy value in the immediate future considering the absence of Caleb Williams. Case Keenum got the start under center against the Eagles, and while he kept the offense on track through veteran savvy, his general lack of arm strength limited the offense to hefty rates of attacking the short-to-intermediate areas of the field. It is unclear whether Keenum or Tyson Bagent will draw the start in Week 4, but the decision could dictate whether Odunze can be inserted into fantasy rosters against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rome Odunze caught 3-of-4 targets for 43 yards in the Bears’ Week 2 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: It was Odunze’s second quiet statline in as many weeks to begin the season. The difference this time, of course, was the Bears scored only three points after dropping 59 on the Panthers in Week 1. They did attempt 35 passes, 26 of which came from Caleb Williams before he injured his hamstring midway through the fourth quarter. If Williams misses Week 3 against the Eagles as is currently looking likely, it would be difficult to jam Odunze into the WR3 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rome Odunze caught 2-of-3 targets for 52 yards in the Bears’ Week 1 win against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Odunze came down with an impressive 47-yard contested catch near the end zone in the first half. He was quiet from there on out. Running a route on about 60 percent of the Bears’ drop backs, Odunze may have been limited by the calf injury that kept him out of practice for much of last week. Odunze will continue as a high-variance downfield option in a run-first Chicago offense next week against the Vikings. He should be treated as nothing more than a WR3 option in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Rome Odunze (calf) is active for Week 1 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Odunze missed some practice time this week with the calf issue and was considered questionable headed into the weekend. He could see his snaps and routes limited if the calf is still bothering him. Odunze should be considered a high-variance flex option with a frightening floor against the Panthers. Bears declared QB Tyson Bagent, QB Miller Moss, S Xavier Woods, OT Ozzy Trapilo, DE Jamree Kromah, and OL Jordan McFadden inactive for the team’s season opener.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Rome Odunze (calf) is expected to play in Week 1 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Odunze was limited by the calf issue throughout the week before being listed as questionable on Friday. He will suit up today but might not be at full strength. Odunze will be a high-risk WR3 for his 2026 opener. To no one’s surprise, Colston Loveland trails only Trey McBride in the tight end rankings, while Luther Burden is a speculative WR2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bears elevated WR Kaden Davis for Week 1 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: This wouldn’t be news under normal circumstances but takes on additional meaning with Rome Odunze listed questionable for Week 1. It is of particular note that the Bears already have five wide receivers on the active roster and still chose to elevate another. While recent reports seemed to indicate a sense of optimism regarding Odunze’s potential availability, he could be on the wrong side of questionable given the recent transaction. Fantasy managers will want to confirm his status when the team releases its inactives 90 minutes prior to first kick. Luther Burden and Colston Loveland would be in line to benefit greatly should Odunze be unable to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: Luther Burden caught all four targets for 130 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 7 win over the Patriots, adding seven yards on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: Burden erupted on the scene with a 58-yard, catch-and-run reception on a crosser in the first quarter to set up a four-yard score for D’Andre Swift. He would tack on another 24 yards and his touchdown late in the second quarter to push him over the century mark in yards on an improbable touchdown reception, taking a quick screen to the house on third-and-17 with only 14 seconds remaining before the break. Burden would largely fall victim to a more reserved offensive stance after the Bears pushed their lead to 13 points on their first possession of the second half, adding just one additional reception in the final 30 minutes of play. That matters not to fantasy managers that had been waiting for a marquee performance from a player they chased up draft boards this summer. Burden appears to be heating up now further removed from the offseason injury he carried into the start of the regular season and can continue to be started as an upside WR2 ahead of a difficult matchup against the Seahawks in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: Luther Burden III caught all eight of his targets for 95 yards in the Bears’ Week 6 win against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: With Caleb Williams back from a hamstring injury, Burden led the Bears with eight targets and a season-high 95 yards, mostly on short over-the-middle passes from Williams. Burden’s long play was a 25-yard catch and run. That he ran a route on just 19 of the Bears’ 45 drop backs is something of a concern going forward. With that little route involvement, Burden will have to be hyper efficient if he’s going to be a WR2/3 in fantasy formats. He should remain in lineups next week against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: Luther Burden III caught 4-of-6 targets for 47 yards in the Bears’ Week 5 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: Burden “led” the Bears in receiving, but the fact that 47 yards was the team’s high-water mark tells you all you need to know about their offensive effectiveness this afternoon. Today was actually the first time in three games without Caleb Williams that Burden finished under 60 yards receiving, but he is still in dire need of his starting quarterback’s return. It appears that will be Week 6 against the Falcons, keeping Burden in the low-end WR2 mix despite his lack of spiked weeks through the season’s first five contests.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: Luther Burden III caught 4-of-6 targets for 63 yards in the Bears’ Week 4 win against the Jets, adding one rush for 11 yards.
