https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: It was a fine outing for Burden after he showed signs of life in Week 3’s win over the Eagles. Burden was second on the team in targets, trailing Rome Odunze’s seven looks from Tyson Bagent. He ran a few more pass routes than Kalif Raymond, who had two grabs for six yards. Chicago operating as a run-first team is going to necessarily limit Burden’s opportunities, but he should suffice as a WR3/4 in the coming weeks. That includes next week against a middling Green Bay secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: Luther Burden caught 7-of-11 targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 3 win over the Eagles, adding seven yards on one carry.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: Burden got the scoring started with a shovel-pass touchdown on the first possession of the game and continued to be the primary engine of the offense on a night the team was led by veteran journeyman Case Keenum. Head coach Ben Johnson handily outmatched his counterpart in Sean Mannion, keeping the offense in rhythm and unpredictable throughout. Burden should continue to improve upon his early-season returns for fantasy managers that chased him up draft boards this offseason, particularly once Caleb Williams returns to the starting roster in a few weeks. In the meantime, treat Burden as an upside WR2 ahead of a Week 4 meeting with the Jets in Chicago.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: Luther Burden caught 3-of-7 targets for 32 yards in the Bears’ Week 2 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: For the second straight week, Burden was out-produced by Kalif Raymond, who again led the receiver corps in production. D’Andre Swift “led” the entire team in receiving with five receptions for 54 scoreless yards. Burden is now sitting on eight catches for 95 yards through two weeks. It’s not the worst start anyone has ever seen, but fantasy managers were expecting better. It might not be coming in Week 3 if Caleb Williams’ hamstring injury costs him time against the Eagles, which seems highly likely. We are trying not to overreact to small-sample sizes, but Burden is definitely now more of a WR3 than WR2 heading into next Monday’s contest. That, of course, should still have him in most fantasy lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: Luther Burden caught all five of his targets for 63 yards in the Bears’ Week 1 win against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: Burden overcame a first quarter fumble on a bubble screen to finish second on the team in targets behind Kalif Raymond, who saw nine looks from Caleb Williams, just as everyone had predicted. While Burden’s 17 percent targets per route run was well below his 2025 rate, he should be more involved going forward in a Bears offense that might be trying to break the NFL’s single season scoring record, as head coach Ben Johnson mentioned in an August interview. Burden will be a top-30 PPR option next week against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: Bears elevated WR Kaden Davis for Week 1 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: This wouldn’t be news under normal circumstances but takes on additional meaning with Rome Odunze listed questionable for Week 1. It is of particular note that the Bears already have five wide receivers on the active roster and still chose to elevate another. While recent reports seemed to indicate a sense of optimism regarding Odunze’s potential availability, he could be on the wrong side of questionable given the recent transaction. Fantasy managers will want to confirm his status when the team releases its inactives 90 minutes prior to first kick. Luther Burden and Colston Loveland would be in line to benefit greatly should Odunze be unable to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: The Chicago Tribune’s Sean Hammond reports that Bears WR Rome Odunze exited practice early on Thursday after suffering an apparent leg injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: Per Hammond, Odunze “came up hobbling during an install period at the start of practice,” with what appeared to be a right leg injury. Apparently, Odunze “wasn’t overly concerned” and tried to continue practicing, but Bears trainers removed him from the field. That last bit is encouraging. Hopefully, Odunze’s Week 1 availability has not been jeopardized. Bears TE Colston Loveland and WR Luther Burden would benefit if Odunze cannot play. Odunze is backed up by WR Kalif Raymond.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.headline: Bears coach Ben Johnson said Luther Burden (hamstring) looks “100 percent.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luther-bur.analysis: This jives with what beat writers reported yesterday, but the coach saying it means we should probably expect Burden to be ready for Week 1. He’s a high-ceiling WR2/WR3 stab in drafts on an offense that Johnson has said wants to set the NFL scoring record.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: D’Andre Swift rushed 22 times for 78 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 7 win over the Patriots, adding 12 yards on four receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: Swift shook off an early injury scare when he took a helmet directly to his knee to earn a season-high 26 opportunities in the absence of Kyle Monangai. This game had an entirely different feel than the previous game played without Monangai, during which Roschon Johnson was much more involved in a game the Bears held at 31-7 lead in the fourth quarter. The back-and-forth nature of Week 7 kept Swift on the field for more of the game, allowing him to return a legitimate RB1 performance on the backs of elite volume. Monangai could return as early as Week 8 considering the Bears now have 10 days until they play the Seahawks on Monday Night Football, potentially sending Swift back into the RB2 range in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: Bears ruled out Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) for Week 7 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: Monangai will miss his third game in a row this week. Exactly two weeks ago, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported that Monangai’s turf toe injury would be an issue for 1-2 weeks. Technically, his statement remains accurate. This week’s Thursday Night Football game complicates things. If the Bears thought Monangai would miss four games, they likely would have put him on injured reserve, so he should, theoretically, be able to play in Week 8 against the Seahawks. Of course, nothing is guaranteed, and for those wondering, the Bears go on bye in Week 10. D’Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson have been splitting touches with Monangai sidelined. We do not yet know if Johnson will be punished for last week’s fumble though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: D’Andre Swift had 16 rushes for 44 yards and two touchdowns in the Bears’ Week 6 win against the Falcons, adding four catches for 26 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: Swift again dominated backfield touches for Chicago with Kyle Monangai sidelined with injuries to his toe and hand. Roschon Johnson had 13 carries, with most of those coming after the Bears had raced out to a big lead (before that lead dwindled in the fourth quarter). Both of Swift’s touchdowns came inside the ten yard line. Swift should be locked in for at least 15 touches in Week 7 against the Patriots if Monangai remains sidelined. His involvement in the pass game provides a nice weekly PPR floor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: Bears ruled out Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) for Week 6 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: Bears coach Ben Johnson said Monangai is “trending in the right direction,” but remains week-to-week. D’Andre Swift should handle a sizable workload with Monangai sidelined. Roschon Johnson may be able to catch a few passes, but he makes for a shaky FLEX bet. Monangai should be stashed safely on fantasy football benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: D’Andre Swift rushed nine times for 43 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 5 loss to the Packers, adding four receptions for 30 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: Swift was the only Bear to find the end zone in a throwaway performance where Tyson Bagent was benched for the fourth quarter. It was still a disappointing statline with Kyle Monangai (toe) on the shelf, but there just wasn’t much Swift could do with Bagent failing to threaten the Packers’ defense and the Bears’ D struggling mightily. Swift also lost a ton of passing-game work and targets to fill-in No. 2 RB Roschon Johnson. That’s a potentially disturbing development heading into Week 6 against the Falcons, with or without Monangai in the lineup. Thankfully, Caleb Williams (hamstring) should be back, shoring up Swift’s value in the RB10-14 range.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: D’Andre Swift (hip/knee) is not on Chicago’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: Despite an early-week DNP, Swift heads into the week in arguably a better position than he started it. We’re not sure how much workload he’ll handle with Kyle Monangai (foot) out, but it will certainly be a large majority of what the Bears do. Roschon Johnson figures to handle whatever Swift can’t, but isn’t a priority free agency pickup so much as a stash at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the “belief is that D’Andre Swift (hip/knee) should be able to go” in Week 5 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: We will get a better sense of Swift’s availability soon when the Bears release their final injury report of the week. After being a DNP in Wednesday’s practice, Swift was able to log a limited session on Thursday, which is a good sign for his availability with one practice left to go. Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe), who has yet to practice this week, could be at risk of missing Week 5, which could lead to a busy day for Swift, while Roschon Johnson would serve as the Bears’ RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: D’Andre Swift (hip/knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: It’s an upgrade from Wednesday’s DNP. Swift has been a constant presence on the midweek injury reports, but hasn’t seemed at any real risk of missing a game yet. We’d imagine he’s more likely than not to avoid a questionable tag again on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: D’Andre Swift (hip/knee) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: Swift nursed this knee injury last week, but was active on game day, as usual. Bears RB2 Kyle Monangai took on 30 carries, functioning as the team’s offensive centerpiece after Swift lost a fumble in the second half. Perhaps Swift’s hip injury, which he apparently picked up in-game, contributed to Monangai’s increased involvement. Monangai injured his right thumb and suffered a toe injury, though he is expected to play in Week 5 against the Packers. Swift’s participation level is worth watching closely this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.headline: Bears coach Ben Johnson said Kyle Monangai’s thumb injury is “not an issue.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dandre-swi.analysis: Johnson did add, “He had 30 carries, and he feels like he had 30 carries.” Monangai will play in Week 5 versus the Packers, but it doesn’t sound like he will double up D’Andre Swift in carries for the second week in a row. Expect a more even split of the work this week, with Swift potentially returning to his normal lead-back role. Even with fewer carries, Monangai is locked in as a fantasy RB3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams completed 22-of-33 passes for 308 yards and two touchdowns in the Bears’ 30-24, Week 7 win over the Patriots, adding 18 yards on five carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The enigmatic signal caller also took three sacks, the last of which almost placed the Bears in position to hand the keys to victory to the Patriots. Ben Johnson called a pass play on third-and-five with under two minutes to play in Patriots territory, placing another nod of support toward his franchise quarterback. Things turned dire when Williams took a sack that appeared to take the Bears out of field goal range in a six-point game, with veteran kicker Cairo Santos hitting a career-long 58-yard field goal to dispel the worries. That sequence of two plays displayed Johnson’s unrelenting trust in his players considering the 58-yard field goal was not only the longest of Santos’ 12-year career, but the third longest field goal in Soldier Field history. Either way, Williams and the Bears escaped with the victory and move to 5-2, now 1.5-games behind the Vikings for the division lead in the most competitive division in football. The Bears get a mini-bye ahead of a Week 8 meeting with the Seahawks on Monday Night Football, where Williams will remain a back-end QB1 in fantasy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams completed 30-of-36 attempts for 305 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 6 win against the Falcons, adding four rushes for three yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Williams was all the way back in this one, returning to action after three weeks on the sideline recovering from a hamstring injury. His only real miss of the day came on a ten yard throw to Colston Loveland that should have been an easy touchdown. Williams tormented the pass-funnel Atlanta defense with middle-of-the-field throws, along with typical out-of-structure passes to the sideline. It was an impressive outing against a Falcons defense giving up the league’s fifth lowest drop back success rate. Williams should remain in lineups in Week 7 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) is active for Week 6 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Williams will make his return to the starting lineup after being sidelined for a few weeks with a hamstring injury while the Bears declared RB Kyle Monangai, CB Tyrique Stevenson, LB T.J. Edwards, LB Keyshaun Elliott, OL Jordan McFadden, DL Jayden Loving, and QB Case Keenum inactive against Atlanta. Monongai’s absence should translate into another big workload for D’Andre Swift, facing a tough Falcons rush defense. Meanwhile, Tyson Bagent will serve as Williams’ backup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) will start in Week 6 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: This was expected to be the case but is now confirmed by sources close to the team. Williams returns after missing the previous three games as the Bears look to claw their way back into contention in a crowded NFC North division. Consider it a sizable boost for all Chicago pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) posted a video to social media indicating he will play in Week 6 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Normally, social media posts don’t count for much. However, earlier today, Bears coach Ben Johnson said that the Bears should have more clarity on Williams’ status by the end of the day, after the medical team put Williams through “the final stress tests” in his return-to-play program. We are inferring that Williams’ social media post suggests he passed the final medical testing, though we have not officially received word that this is indeed the case. For now, we tentatively expect Williams to play on Sunday. He can be treated as a mid-to-low QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Bears are smartly taking a conservative approach with their franchise quarterback. Williams had a limited practice session last week and practiced fully this week. Bears coach Ben Johnson told reporters that the team should have more clarity by the end of the day on whether Williams has passed his return-to-play plan’s final stress tests. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Bears’ QB1 is seemingly on track to make his return this week, when his team takes on the Falcons. When speaking to reporters after practice, though, Williams said he does not know if he is going to play yet, adding that he still has a number of tests and protocols to go through before he’s cleared. If active, Williams could end up running a little less frequently than he did early in the year, perhaps playing cautiously in his first game back. Regardless, Williams is a low-end QB1 if he is indeed active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) practiced in full Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Technically, Williams was estimated as a full participant ahead of the Bears’ Week 6 game against the Falcons. We’ll see if Williams, who has missed the past three games, practices in full on Thursday. Either way he’s likely to be under center against the pass-funnel Atlanta defense in Week 6. He should be in all lineups if he’s active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said “all signs point” to Caleb Williams (hamstring) returning in Week 6 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Head coach Ben Johnson said on Sunday that Williams would be “close” to suiting up for Week 6, and he reportedly had a good workout before Week 5’s game against the Packers. Williams has missed the last three games with the hamstring injury he suffered in Week 2, but the Bears have managed to go 2-1 over that span. Williams logged one limited practice last week, after being a DNP on Wednesday and Thursday. If he can get on the practice field multiple days this week, it would be a good sign for his availability for next week’s game against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bears declared QB Caleb Williams, RB Kyle Monangai, OT Ozzy Trapilo, LB Keyshaun Elliott, DT Jayden Loving and EDGE Jamree Kromah inactive for Week 5 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Why the Bears went through the dog and pony show of labeling Williams as “questionable” when everybody knew he would not be playing, nobody knows. Either way, Williams appears to have a strong chance of returning for Week 6 against the Falcons. Expect another run-heavy game plan, even without Monangai, in what should be the final game of the Tyson Bagent experience for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: DeMario Douglas caught 3-of-4 targets for 23 yards in the Patriots’ Week 7 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: The magic of the previous two games quickly evaporated for the diminutive slot receiver as Hunter Henry and Rhamondre Stevenson stepped into the primary security blanket role for Drake Maye, the latter of whom faced consistent pressure from the aggressive Dennis Allen Bears defense. Starting Douglas on a weekly basis is akin to reaching your hand into a brown paper bag found on the side of the road. It feels exhilarating at the time but you never know what you’re going to get.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: DeMario Douglas caught 7-of-8 targets for 86 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 6 win over the Jets, also losing a fumble.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Douglas followed up his best game of the season with another best game of the season, as well as the third most receiving yards of his career. His touchdown was a nine-yarder in the second quarter where the Jets’ defense simply afforded Drake Maye too much time. Things could not have been going better for “Pop” until his fourth quarter fumble at the end of a 39-yard catch-and-run. He was the victim of a classic “Peanut punch” from behind. Rather ominously, he was not targeted thereafter, though the Patriots were also in ball-control mode as they worked on draining the clock. That today’s effort came as A.J. Brown was returning from a five-week absence was promising, but the reality is that Douglas’ big box scores are likely to remain pop-up efforts rather predictable and/or weekly occurrences. He’s a shaky WR4 even with byes and injuries in full swing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: DeMario Douglas caught 4-of-5 targets for 65 yards and two touchdowns in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Douglas had his first two touchdown grabs of the season as Drake Maye sliced and diced a lifeless Vegas defense from start to finish. Douglas was wide open standing in the end zone by himself for his first score, and broke out of a bunch formation inside the ten yard line for his second score. Douglas has run significant routes in the New England offense since A.J. Brown (ankle) went down to injury. When Brown returns — perhaps this week — Douglas will take on a smaller role in the Pats pass game. He should remain on waiver wires in most formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: DeMario Douglas caught 1-of-5 targets for 38 yards in the Patriots’ Week 3 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Douglas was second on the team in targets behind only Mack Hollins, who saw nine looks from Drake Maye. Douglas got open and made a nice grab for his 38-yard gain — one of the only big plays for the struggling New England offense on Sunday. Though Douglas is playing a decent snap share, he should remain on waivers in most formats ahead of the Patriots’ Week 4 game against Buffalo.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports A.J. Brown (ankle) is expected to miss 6-8 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Schefter and other reporters previously called it a 4-6 week injury, which now seems unlikely. Schefter did add that Brown is moving “pretty well” and could come back on the faster side of his updated timeline. Still, it looks like Brown will miss at least half of the regular season. Romeo Doubs will operate as the team’s No. 1 receiver until he returns, though it will likely be a group effort to replace Browns’ production. Mack Hollins and Demario Douglas will also be more involved.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: DeMario Douglas caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Patriots’ Week 2 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Douglas made the first catch of the game for the Patriots, but was silent the rest of the day. The 25-year-old is a low-yardage slot receiver who tends to get schemed targets when he is on the field. Douglas tallied the third-most snaps of all Patriots wide receivers on the day but will find it hard to achieve fantasy relevancy in an offense that utilizes multiple receivers in several different ways. Second-year receiver Kyle Williams also saw a pair of targets, catching one for 10 yards. Neither Williams or Douglas are anything more than deep league dart throws for Week 3 against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports the “preliminary diagnosis” for A.J. Brown is a high-ankle sprain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Garafolo added, “MRI today after X-rays were negative.” That’s a good sign, but there is currently no timeline for Brown’s return. It will ultimately be a multi-week injury that could linger well into the season. Demario Douglas led the Pats with seven targets last night, though his looks are generally low-value check-downs. Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs will serve as the team’s primary outside receivers until Brown is healthy. Hollins led the Pats in receiving yards at a modest 51. Hollins is worth adding in deeper leagues, but it’s hard to imagine him putting up anything more than WR4 numbers while Brown is sidelined. Doubs should improve in Week 2 after failing to catch any of his three targets versus the Seahawks. He will get another shot at WR3 numbers against Pittsburgh next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: Demario Douglas caught 5-of-7 targets for 20 yards in the Patriots’ Week 1 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Seattle shut down the Patriots’ deep passing game, forcing Drake Maye to pepper Douglas with low-value check-downs. Douglas wound up leading the Pats in targets and catches. He finished fifth in receiving yards. With A.J. Brown banged up, Douglas could be in line for another smattering of targets next week versus the Steelers. Even with Brown out, Douglas would barely register as a PPR WR5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: A.J. Brown suffered an ankle injury in Week 1 against the Seahawks and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: A Seattle defender landed on Brown’s leg in the third quarter and the former Eagle clutched at his ankle as soon as he hit the ground. Brown eventually made his way off the field and limped to the locker room. He was listed as questionable for roughly a quarter, but the team has now ruled him out. The immediate worry will be that Brown suffered a dreaded high ankle sprain. That would sideline him for multiple weeks, though it’s too early to say much about the injury. Mack Hollins, Romeo Doubs, and Demario Douglas will all see some extra routes sans Brown.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.headline: The Boston Herald’s Andrew Callahan said the Patriots are “stretching DeMario Douglas’ usage and route tree more than in recent years.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demario-do.analysis: Douglas appears set to function as a mainstay of the New England passing attack in 2026 after the team used him in a rotational role in 2025. Douglas last season had a lowly 36 percent route rate and was targeted on just 20 percent of his pass routes. He was second among Pats pass catchers in yards per route run, trailing Stefon Diggs. Callahan said so far in training camp the Patriots have “featured every possible pairing” from the trio of Douglas, A.J. Brown, and Romeo Doubs, “at various times within two-back or two-tight end personnel, meaning Douglas is not always in the slot. Douglas is, however, the most consistently available of those three. The Patriots are stretching his usage and route tree more than in recent years.” Douglas could be worth monitoring in deeper fantasy formats this summer if he’s going to see a marked increase in playing time and involvement in Drake Maye’s passing attack.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown caught 3-of-6 targets for 48 yards in the Patriots’ Week 7 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown has not yet clicked with his new team after going down with injury in Week 1 and spending the subsequent four games on injured reserve. He committed yet another drop against the Bears after three drops the week prior, this time on what would have been a long gain down the left sideline. Brown’s burst off the line and at the top of routes appears to remain hampered, something the both the Patriots and Brown’s fantasy managers hope will remedy in short order. You can’t really sit Brown at this point, but fantasy managers have to be growing impatient of their first or second-round selection. Brown remains a teeth-gritting start ahead of a Week 8 matchup with the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown practiced in full on Friday. It is his first time doing so since returning from injured reserve last week. This is great news for his Week 7 outlook. The Bears field a beatable pass defense, setting up Brown for a bounce-back performance after last week’s disappointing showing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown spoke with the media today and there’s no reason to believe he’ll actually miss this game, but he was regarded as “limited” in both sessions this week and it’s fair to wonder if he’s 100 percent just yet after his drop-filled, rough Week 6. He’s best-treated as a WR2 this week — you’re still probably starting him regardless of what the ranking is.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown caught 3-of-10 targets for 27 yards in the Patriots’ Week 6 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Active for the first time since Week 1, Brown had an even more disastrous outing than that inefficient box score would indicate, as he was charged with at least three official drops and could end up with 4-5 when it is all said and done. One was a potential long score where the ball literally went through his hands. It was unbecoming of a highly-paid No. 1 wideout. Brown also looked stiff moving side to side, and might not be particularly close to 100 percent health returning from his high-ankle sprain. We assume things can only get better from here, but they absolutely have to in Thursday evening’s short-week potential shootout with the Bears’ leaky defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is active for Week 6 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: As are A.J. Brown (ankle) and LT Will Campbell (knee). It’s a rare day where all the injury news went right for a team. We can’t imagine Henderson will be in large for a particularly big backup role behind Rhamondre Stevenson, but the fact that a player the Pats didn’t even really “need” for Week 6 is giving it a go suggests he is close to regular health. Henderson is a boom/bust FLEX option. Inactive for the Patriots are CB Carlton Davis, CB Karon Prunty, QB Behren Morton, CB Channing Canada, OT Dametrious Crownover and TE Tanner Arkin.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports A.J. Brown (ankle) is expected to play “a good amount” in Week 6 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown was activated from injured reserve this week and will suit up versus the Jets. It was reasonable to expect some sort of snap count in his first game back, but it sounds like Brown will be a full-go after looking great in practice this week. In desperate need of a true WR1 to step up, the Pats should pepper Brown with targets this week. He is back in the fantasy WR2 ranks after the lengthy absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: Patriots activated A.J. Brown (ankle) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown makes his return from a four-game absence following a Week 1 injury to his ankle, reintegrating into an offense that has found their stride in recent weeks. After leading the league in turnovers through the first three games, quarterback Drake Maye has accounted for a league-leading eight touchdowns since Week 4. Although Brown could be on a snap count in his first game back, fantasy managers have to be feeling ecstatic to get their second round pick back on the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: ESPN’s Ian Rapoport reports the Patriots will likely activate WR A.J. Brown (ankle) to play against the Jets in Week 6.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown returned to practice this week after going on injured reserve with a high-ankle sprain. While nothing is official yet, it’s a great sign that Rapoport is anticipating a return for the 29-year-old wide receiver in Week 6 against the Jets. Brown may not play a full complement of snaps in his first game back, but is still essentially a must-start for fantasy managers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle) is questionable for New England’s Week 6 game against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said they’d make the decision on whether to activate him off injured reserve on Saturday, so at least Brown won’t be a game-time decision. Brown can be started with confidence if he’s active, though he’d potentially be in line for a pitch count to the point where he’d be more of a WR2 than a WR1 in his return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.headline: A.J. Brown (ankle) said his status for Week 6 against the Jets is “still up in the air.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/a-j-brown/.analysis: Brown was a limited participant on Wednesday. He is reportedly taking a “one step at a time” approach to his return. We’ll see how his ankle responds to Thursday’s limited practice “with full shoulder pads.” Per Brown, the team is not rushing him back and will keep the long haul in mind when deciding whether to activate him. The Patriots (3-2) are in second in the AFC East.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry caught all seven targets for 71 yards in the Patriots’ Week 7 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: Henry operated as the clear safety blanket for quarterback Drake Maye, the latter of whom was under constant duress in the face of unrelenting pressure from Dennis Allen’s Bears defense. The team was largely unable to move the football on the ground and fell into an early hole, leading to Josh McDaniels utilizing the short passing game as an extension of the run. That’s where Henry made his presence felt, although it was rookie right end Eli Raridon that caught the touchdown at the position. Week 7 goes down as the first game with more than a modest five targets for the veteran tight end, who has quickly become a difficult weekly start in a more crowded New England pass offense. Fantasy managers might want to consider alternatives when the Patriots face the downtrodden Dolphins in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry caught 4-of-5 targets for 48 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 6 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: It’s a fairly standard Henry box score, though the 48 yards were actually his second most of the season. The touchdown was his second, as well as second in as many weeks. Henry took advantage of a Jets communication breakdown near the goal line. By now we know Henry is a perfectly fine option if you find yourself in a streamer or second FLEX pinch, but he is not making a move on TE1 status heading into Week 7 against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Eli Raridon caught 5-of-5 targets for 57 yards in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: Raridon, who was out last week, was very much involved in the revived New England passing attack. Hunter Henry, meanwhile, had three grabs for 44 yards and a touchdown. The Patriots have used two tight end sets at a high rate when Raridon is healthy. Unless Henry misses time, Raridon should remain on waiver wires in most 12-team formats. He had been targeted on ten percent of his routes headed into Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry caught 3-of-4 targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: Henry was third on the team in targets and caught one of Drake Maye’s four touchdown tosses on the day. Henry has seen better involvement in the Pats offense of late; against the Bills in Week 4 he caught all five of his targets for 62 yards. The resurgence of the Patriots passing attack has made Henry viable as a streaming option. He’ll be in play next week against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry caught all five of his targets for 62 yards in the Patriots’ Week 4 win over the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: Henry always seems to produce against the Bills, so this was nothing new. The veteran played on 46 of the team’s 70 snaps and ran a route on 28 of their 43 dropbacks, the second most of any receiving option on the team. He also hauled in an 11-yard catch on 3rd and 10 to ice the game in the fourth quarter. With Eli Raridon (ankle) and Mack Hollins (calf) leaving this game with injuries, Henry could be on the TE1 fringe radar next week against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Eli Raridon (thigh) is active for Week 4 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: Raridon was questionable heading into the weekend, but he was able to get in three limited practice sessions this week, so he had been trending towards a return. He will back up Hunter Henry but could cut into Henry’s snaps enough to make Henry just a TE2 in deeper formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry caught 1-of-2 targets for five yards in the Patriots’ Week 3 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: With Eli Raridon sidelined, Henry still wasn’t part of the Patriots’ passing attack. Drake Maye threw one of his two picks on an end zone target to Henry. With seven catches through three games, Henry should remain on waiver wires ahead of the team’s Week 4 game against Buffalo.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry caught 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards in the Patriots’ Week 2 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: Henry was the Patriots’ primary tight end, leading all pass-catchers in targets on the day. He totaled 40 yards on three catches as part of a receiving-by-committee approach by the Drake Maye passing attack. His role is safe, despite Eli Raridon slowly taking on some more routes to open the season. Henry is a fantasy TE2 for Week 3 against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Hunter Henry caught all three of his targets for 26 yards in the Patriots’ Week 1 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: Henry was quiet in this contest, though the same can be said of basically every member of New England’s passing attack. Despite losing A.J. Brown to an ankle injury, Henry’s role didn’t change. He earned a measly nine percent target share and ceded a handful of routes to rookie tight end Eli Raridon, who scored on his only target of the day. Henry will remain in the TE2 ranks for Week 2, but another quiet day will raise red flags for fantasy managers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.headline: Mass Live’s Mark Daniels believes Patriots TE Hunter Henry “will be important” this year.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/hunter-hen.analysis: Daniels adds that third-round rookie TE Eli Raridon “looks the part,” but he believes Henry is “by far the team’s best tight end and once again will be a security blanket” for QB Drake Maye. Henry posted a 6/768/7 receiving line in 2025 and a 66/674/ receiving line in 2024. A similar stat line this year would be unsurprising.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson rushed three times for nine yards in the Patriots’ Week 7 loss to the Bears, adding 14 yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Henderson continues to play second, or third, fiddle behind Rhamondre Stevenson when the Patriots are forced into “gotta have it” mode, with Stevenson the back most trusted in key situations. The Patriots feel into an early hole and were playing catch-up throughout against the Bears, something that could help to explain the lowly opportunity total for the back widely considered the more explosive of the two. Furthermore, the team continued to rotate Corey Kiner through the opportunity pecking order, placing another sizable dent in the weekly floor of Henderson. Although he could find more opportunities in a softer matchup in Week 8, he’ll be a difficult click to insert into fantasy lineups against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is not on the final injury report for Week 7 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Henderson will be active for the Patriots’ Thursday Night Football game, but his usage is up in the air. Patriots coach Mike Vrabel got RB Corey Kiner going late last week after Henderson fumbled. The Patriots won’t simply discard their former second-round pick, so he remains FLEX-viable, but he may be playing with a very limited touch count.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) practiced in full on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: It’s been a stunningly quick recovery from what looked to be a high-ankle sprain that could sideline him. Henderson has practiced in full both days this week. We’re not concerned that he won’t play, but after fumble problems struck last week and Corey Kiner closed out the Jets in the fourth quarter, we do have slightly lowered expectations for his Thursday night stat line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson rushed seven times for 31 yards in the Patriots’ Week 6 win over the Jets, adding a nine-yard reception and losing a fumble.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Surprisingly active, Henderson was unsurprisingly disappointing. Although his lost third quarter fumble was his first of the season, it predictably landed him in the doghouse. He touched the ball just two times thereafter, and the Patriots decided to ride No. 3 running back Corey Kiner is closeout mode. Kiner took 11 carries in the final 16:30 of game time. We know Henderson has big-play ability, but now playing at less than 100 percent in a backfield that is beginning to look like a three-man ordeal, he’s not a particularly appealing RB3/FLEX heading into Thursday’s short-week date with the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is active for Week 6 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: As are A.J. Brown (ankle) and LT Will Campbell (knee). It’s a rare day where all the injury news went right for a team. We can’t imagine Henderson will be in large for a particularly big backup role behind Rhamondre Stevenson, but the fact that a player the Pats didn’t even really “need” for Week 6 is giving it a go suggests he is close to regular health. Henderson is a boom/bust FLEX option. Inactive for the Patriots are CB Carlton Davis, CB Karon Prunty, QB Behren Morton, CB Channing Canada, OT Dametrious Crownover and TE Tanner Arkin.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is likely to play in Week 6 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: The same is true of left tackle Will Campbell, who also went down with an ankle injury in Week 5. It’s a remarkable turnaround for Henderson, who was initially expected to miss multiple weeks with a high-ankle sprain. He was limited in practice throughout the week before being listed as questionable on Friday. We expect Henderson to be on a pitch count this week, but he’s still capable of breaking a long run on just a few touches. Henderson is a high-risk FLEX play for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: The Patriots’ No. 2 running back was limited all week after being diagnosed with a high-ankle sprain. He told reporters today that he was surprised he could practice this week, and is feeling “pretty good.” If active, he will be a FLEX starter, but Rhamondre Stevenson should lead the backfield in touches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Unlike yesterday, Henderson was spotted at the open portion of practice and appears to be making a real run to play in Week 6. If not for the report that he’d miss multiple weeks with a high-ankle sprain, this would be a pretty clear trend towards Henderson playing. As is, we’ll see what happens on Friday. It sure seems like he’ll hit the questionable line one way or another, but how it looks will be important as far as figuring out his Week 6 status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Henderson wasn’t spotted during the portion of practice open to the media but apparently got on the field at some point later in the session. It’s a truly stunning development for Henderson, given that it was reported this morning that he is expected to miss multiple weeks. We still expect him to sit for Week 6, but even that isn’t guaranteed at this point. Henderson would likely be on a relatively strict pitch count if he plays, but his presence would, at a minimum, be a thorn in the side of Rhamondre Stevenson’s fantasy backers. This is officially an injury report to keep a close eye on throughout the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) will miss multiple weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/treveyon-hende.analysis: Henderson suffered his latest ankle injury in Week 5 against the Raiders. Schefter said Henderson is “regarded as a quick healer, so the Patriots are hoping his return is sooner rather than later.” Still, he could be sidelined for the next few weeks, leaving Rhamondre Stevenson as the team’s clear lead back. Corey Kiner, meanwhile, appears to be in line as the Patriots’ RB2 after seeing seven touches last week against the Raiders. Kiner should be stashed in most 12-team fantasy leagues for now. Stevenson profiles as a top-12 play until Henderson returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson rushed six times for 22 yards in the Patriots’ Week 7 loss to the Bears, adding 93 yards and a touchdown on five receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson scored one of the more improbable touchdowns you will see late in the second quarter. After taking possession with just 14 second remaining on the clock, Drake Maye completed an 18-yard pass to A.J. Brown to place the ball near midfield with three seconds remaining before the half. Instead of heaving the ball deep on a Hail Mary, Maye dumped the ball off to Stevenson in the flat with blockers out front. Stevenson would do the rest on his way to a 48-yard score as time expired in the second frame on a score that never really should have happened. The six carries go down as a season-low for the veteran back, although 11 opportunities handily led the team. Stevenson has not seen more than 14 carries since Week 1 and is not finding paint frequently enough to remain a consistent RB2, making him a shaky weekly start moving forward. That holds true ahead of a Week 8 meeting with the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson rushed 14 times for 36 yards in the Patriots’ Week 6 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson was not targeted in the passing game. He didn’t make any big mistakes — that would be TreVeyon Henderson with his third quarter fumble — but like Hendo, Stevenson found himself mostly on the bench late as the Pats surprisingly rode No. 3 back Corey Kiner in closeout mode. Kiner received 11 carries in the game’s final 16:30. Speaking afterward, coach Mike Vrabel literally called it a hot-hand situation. The “hot hand” is something Stevenson rarely develops, so he can ill afford this backfield becoming a three-man committee. For now, Stevenson is still the Pats’ No. 1 running back. but things just got a little dicier heading into Thursday’s short-week matchup with the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson had 13 rushes for 64 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders, adding three catches for 21 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson was splitting the backfield workload with TreVeyon Henderson before Henderson sustained a potentially serious ankle injury in the second quarter and did not return. Stevenson was somewhat efficient with his opportunities, breaking a few tackles against a low-energy, low-effort Raiders defense. His touchdown came on a goal line carry in the first half. It was his second score of the year. Stevenson will be a top-12 fantasy option next week against the Jets if Henderson is sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) is expected to play in Week 5 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson already told reporters on Friday that he was “ready to go”, so this news item doesn’t come as much of a surprise. Stevenson will continue to operate as the Pats’ top option in high-leverage situations, though he could cede more work between the 20s to TreVeyon Henderson. Both backs are stuck as low-ceiling RB3 options this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) is questionable for New England’s Week 5 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson told Mike Reiss that he’s “ready to go” and that he just got “rolled up on” late in Week 4’s win over the Bills. We’d be surprised if he didn’t play on Sunday and he should be regarded on the optimistic side of questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson is on track to play in Week 5 against the Raiders. It would be great to see him upgrade to full participation tomorrow. Regardless, Stevenson should at least be available for FLEX-viable duties on game day, if not his normal RB2-worthy workload.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Patriots RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: This one is a surprise considering head coach Mike Vrabel said earlier Wednesday that Stevenson would not practice. Instead, the 28-year-old is listed as a limited participant on Wednesday’s official practice report. Stevenson seemingly tweaked his knee towards the end of Week 4 but he has a chance to play in Week 5 against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said Rhamondre Stevenson (leg) is not expected to practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson tweaked his knee or ankle on his last touch of Week 4. The game ended shortly after that, so we didn’t get an official update on his injury from the team. Vrabel told reporters there is a chance he plays in Week 5, but it sounds like the veteran is on the wrong side of questionable as of Wednesday. TreVeyon Henderson’s role was dwindling in recent weeks, but Stevenson’s absence will thrust him right back into a workhorse role. He would be a high-end RB2 if Stevenson is unable to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson rushed 13 times for 47 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 4 win over the Bills, adding 27 yards receiving on 3-of-5 targets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: Stevenson also hauled in a crucial two-point conversion catch on the late fourth-quarter drive that gave the Patriots the lead. Stevenson didn’t have any huge gains on the day, but he consistently gained yardage through the middle of the Bills’ defense and was the clear top option in the red zone. However, when the Patriots were trying to run out the clock, Stevenson got hit at the line of scrimmage and limped off the field with a knee injury. The game ended just two plays later, so this will have to be a situation fantasy managers monitor during the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.headline: Rhamondre Stevenson had seven rushes for 22 yards in the Patriots’ Week 3 loss to the Jaguars, adding three catches for 16 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rhamondre-.analysis: TreVeyon Henderson, meanwhile, had eight rushes for a meager 23 yards in the blowout loss to Jacksonville. Stevenson ran most of the pass routes out of the backfield and saw more targets than Henderson, as usual. It didn’t lead to much. Stevenson next week against the Bills will be a touchdown dependent RB3 option who should be kept on the bench in most fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 24-of-31 passes for 321 yards, two touchdown, and one interception in the Patriots’ 30-24, Week 7 loss to the Bears, adding 26 yards and a touchdown on four carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye and the Patriots struggled to tame an unrelenting Chicago pass rush and were unable to move the football on the ground effectively, two cariables that led to an early deficit against the Bears. Their first half possessions went turnover on downs, three-and-out, three-and-out, touchdown, interception before a wild series to end the second quarter. Caleb Williams led a touchdown drive that left only 14 seconds on the clock. After an 18-yard completion to A.J. Brown, just three seconds remained with the ball near midfield. That’s when Maye dumped the ball off to Rhamondre Stevenson in the flat underneath deep prevent coverage, and Stevenson did the rest on a touchdown that never should have happened to bring the game to a one-possession game. Maye’s other touchdown toss was a beautiful bread-basket throw to rookie tight end Eli Raridon up the seam, adding a score on a grit-play rushing touchdown early in the second quarter. It goes down as Maye’s fourth consecutive QB1 fantasy performance after starting the season leading the league in turnovers through three weeks. The 4-3 Patriots get a mini-bye ahead of a divisional meeting against the Dolphins in Week 8, where Maye will remain an upside QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 18-of-32 passes for 235 yards and three touchdowns in the Patriots’ 26-19, Week 6 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye added four carries for 24 yards rushing. The three-score passing effort was his third in as many weeks, while he is now up to 11 total touchdowns during his three-game hot streak. Good stuff, though it could have been much better. Maye lost No. 2 receiver Romeo Doubs to an early shoulder injury after he housed a 42-yard touchdown, while returning “No. 1" A.J. Brown had a nightmarish day with 4-5 drops, including several long gains and a potential score or two. Pop Douglas also lost a fumble at the end of a long catch-and-run. Unfortunate, but Maye is at least playing well enough again that those miscues merely held back his final box score instead of ruining it. He now has a likely short-week shootout in Thursday’s Bears road tilt.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 26-of-34 attempts for 374 yards and four touchdowns in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders, adding seven rushes for 25 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye had all day to operate in the pocket against a Raiders front seven that entered Week 5 with the league’s ninth highest pressure rate and fourth highest quick pressure rate. He attacked the Vegas secondary downfield from start to finish, hitting Kyle Williams and Pop Douglas for long touchdowns, and Williams for another long gain that put the Pats inside the five yard line. Maye’s rushing score came on a green scramble in the third quarter. Fully emerged from his early-season struggles, Maye is once again carving up opposing coverage units and causing fits with his scrambling ability. Maye, with eight total touchdowns over his past two outings, should be locked into lineups next week against a middling Jets secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 22-of-37 passes for 269 yards, three touchdowns, and one interception in a 29-26, Week 4 win over the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye also added 53 yards rushing on eight carries. This was easily the best game of Maye’s season. The Bills had pressure in his face often, but Maye was frequently able to evade pass rushers and pick up chunk gains with his legs. When he did have time to throw, he ripped off big passes downfield and could have even had a bigger day after a potential 40+ yard pass slipped through Romeo Doubs’ hands in the fourth quarter. Maye did wince and grab his right shoulder on one hit, so that will be something to watch during practice this week, but we don’t expect him to miss any time. The bad news is that Maye figures to be without Mack Hollins (calf) in Week 5, and A.J. Brown (ankle) is not yet ready to return, so Maye will play with limited options next week against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Bills declared CB Christian Benford, WR Skyler Bell, OL Jude Bowry, OL Ar’maj Reed-Adams, DL T.J. Sanders, OLB Mike Danna, and S Jalon Kilgore inactive for Week 4 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: No real surprises here. Benford was listed as questionable heading into the day, but he didn’t practice at all this week so he was never likely to play. Rookie Davison Igbinosun is likely to step into his spot opposite Maxwell Hairston, which makes the Bills young and inexperienced on the boundary. Perhaps Drake Maye could finally take advantage of that on the way to his first truly good fantasy game of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye (right shoulder) is practicing in full for Week 4 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: We are happy to see that the Patriots’ quarterback is practicing fully, but this is a new injury for Maye. He notably dealt with a throwing shoulder injury during the Patriots’ playoff run last season. His listing raises questions as to whether there might be a lingering issue. We expect a follow-up report on this in the coming days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: The Athletic’s Chad Graff believes Drake Maye’s confidence is “shot.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye, after another meltdown in Week 3 against the Jaguars, has now posted a negative drop back EPA in six dtraight outings dating back to last season. Against Jacksonville on Sunday he posted a meager 40 percent drop back success rate, the fifth lowest of the week. “What’s fallen apart with Maye looks like it’s between the ears as much as anything physical,” Graff said. “He looks like a quarterback whose confidence is shot.” Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel said this week that Maye needs to calm down if things are going to turn around. “We need to stop trying to choke the life out of every single play,” Vrabel said during his Monday radio appearance. “We need to relax.” Maye through Week 3 ranks 32nd in fantasy points per drop back, below the likes of Daniel Jones and Cam Ward. It will be tough to start Maye in Week 4 against Buffalo if there are other viable QB options on the waiver wire.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 14-of-29 attempts for 199 yards and two interceptions in the Patriots’ Week 3 loss to the Jaguars, adding four rushes for 18 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: He fumbled twice, losing one to the Jags defense. Maye was under duress and missing routine throws for most of this game. He also had a long touchdown throw and a rushing touchdown called back on penalties. Without A.J. Brown (ankle) in the lineup the Patriots have no one to threaten secondaries, allowing opposing defenses to stack the box, shut down the run game, and leave the Pats a one-dimensional offense. Though Maye’s rushing could keep him afloat as a top-12 quarterback in Week 4 against the Bills, he should be considered a shaky option for now. New England’s offensive line might be able to hold up against a Buffalo front seven that has struggled to pressure the passer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 14-of-22 passes for 208 yards and an interception in the Patriots’ 20-3, Week 2 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: It was a defensive slugfest for the Patriots and Steelers in Week 2, with neither team passing for a touchdown on the day. Maye added 17 rushing yards on four carries but took three sacks, including one in the red zone in the second quarter. His interception was a floater in Steelers territory in the third quarter, tossed right to Patrick Queen to end a drive. He ends the day with 44-percent of his passing yards coming on two third-quarter chunk plays to Romeo Doubs. Maye has had a rough start to the season, following up a three-interception Week 1 with a scoreless, one-interception Week 2. He faces another solid defense in the Jaguars for Week 3; Maye’s rushing upside keeps him in the low-end QB1 territory for next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.headline: Drake Maye completed 23-of-33 passes for 178 yards, a touchdown, and three interceptions in the Patriots’ 13-10, Week 1 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/drake-maye/000.analysis: Maye once again struggled with Seattle’s ironclad defense, routinely making poor decisions when attempting to push the ball downfield. His third, and worst, interception of the night came when he lobbed a pass off his back foot at Mack Hollins with under 30 seconds left. The throw fell well short of his target and Josh Jobe made a toe-tapping pick in the end zone. Maye only threw multiple interceptions once last year, including the postseason. That came in his Super Bowl loss to the Seahawks. His multi-pick total is already at one this year, again at the hands of Seattle. It’s a long season, but Maye did nothing to silence the “schedule merchant” claims tonight. He will look to rebound as a mid-range QB1 versus the Steelers next week. That could be without A.J. Brown, who left this game with an ankle injury and did not return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Bears declared Kyle Monangai, LB T.J. Edwards, LB Jack Sanborn, OL Jordan McFadden, DT Jayden Loving, CB Nick McCloud and QB Case Keenum inactive for Week 7 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: D’Andre Swift will serve as the team’s top back, while Roschon Johnson rotates in behind him. Johnson’s Week 6 fumble could result in less playing time. The Bears face the Seahawks in Week 8. Monangai was unable to practice all week. Hopefully, he returns next week and can be on the field on game day. Keenum will serve as the emergency third quarterback today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Bears ruled out Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) for Week 7 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: Monangai will miss his third game in a row this week. Exactly two weeks ago, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported that Monangai’s turf toe injury would be an issue for 1-2 weeks. Technically, his statement remains accurate. This week’s Thursday Night Football game complicates things. If the Bears thought Monangai would miss four games, they likely would have put him on injured reserve, so he should, theoretically, be able to play in Week 8 against the Seahawks. Of course, nothing is guaranteed, and for those wondering, the Bears go on bye in Week 10. D’Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson have been splitting touches with Monangai sidelined. We do not yet know if Johnson will be punished for last week’s fumble though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) did not practice on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: He hasn’t practiced yet this week and appears very unlikely to go on Thursday night. It would seem to be trending towards another week with Roschon Johnson as the backup runner for the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Bears ruled out Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) for Week 6 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: Bears coach Ben Johnson said Monangai is “trending in the right direction,” but remains week-to-week. D’Andre Swift should handle a sizable workload with Monangai sidelined. Roschon Johnson may be able to catch a few passes, but he makes for a shaky FLEX bet. Monangai should be stashed safely on fantasy football benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: Exactly one week ago, ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported that Monangai’s turf toe injury jeopardized his availability over the next 1-2 weeks. Unfortunately, he is on the wrong side of questionable at this time. Roschon Johnson could contribute on passing downs if Monangai cannot play, but D’Andre Swift will handle the majority of the backfield touches this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: Monangai missed Week 5 due to thumb and toe injuries; he did not practice all of last week and was estimated as a non-participant for the Bears’ Wednesday walk-through. A DNP listing after already missing a week is not a good sign for the 24-year-old’s availability. Starter D’Andre Swift (hip) was notably not on the injury report. Monangai will need to practice to have a chance to play but fantasy managers will need to start looking at backup Roschon Johnson as a potential fill-in for Week 6 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) will not play in Week 5 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: Monangai is currently in a walking boot and is considered week-to-week, per head coach Ben Johnson. Monangai reportedly consulted a specialist for his turf toe after the injury was revealed to be worse than initially expected, but he is not considered a candidate for injured reserve at this time. Backup Roschon Johnson will be elevated to RB2 duties for the foreseeable future, but we wouldn’t expect him to see the same volume as Monangai, who has averaged 15 carries/gm through the Bears’ first four games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the “belief is that D’Andre Swift (hip/knee) should be able to go” in Week 5 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: We will get a better sense of Swift’s availability soon when the Bears release their final injury report of the week. After being a DNP in Wednesday’s practice, Swift was able to log a limited session on Thursday, which is a good sign for his availability with one practice left to go. Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe), who has yet to practice this week, could be at risk of missing Week 5, which could lead to a busy day for Swift, while Roschon Johnson would serve as the Bears’ RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Kyle Monangai has a turf toe injury, “placing uncertainty around his availability over the next 1-2 weeks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: At the beginning of the week, Monangai’s thumb injury was the initial cause for concern. The team kept quiet about the toe issue until Wednesday’s injury report. Per Fowler, Monangai is hoping to play through the turf toe injury, but consecutive absences to begin the week put him on the wrong side of questionable. Given the Bears’ run-heavy tactics, RB3 Roschon Johnson is worth adding for running back-needy fantasy managers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.headline: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-monan.analysis: Ben Johnson has repeatedly said this is not an issue and that Monangai is “going to be okay,” but we’d sure like to see a Friday full session to prove that. As is, Monangai may be headed for a questionable listing for Week 5, even if the supposition will continue to be that he’ll play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Gonzalez (illness) is active for Week 7 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Gonzalez is active, but it sounds like he is not feeling great. ESPN’s Mike Reiss writes that Gonzalez “will attempt to play through” his illness. The Patriots declared DT Joshua Farmer, QB Behren Morton, G/C Ben Brown (knee), CB Karon Prunty (hamstring), CB Channing Canada (hamstring) and CB Carlton Davis III (neck) inactive for Week 7 against the Bears. Davis serves as the team’s No. 2 perimeter cornerback. Prunty and Canada are Gonzalez and Davis’ primary backups. The Bears’ passing game should play productively tonight.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Gonzalez (illness) is questionable to play in Week 7 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Gonzalez has evidently come down with an illness. The Patriots will announce their inactive list in less than an hour. They are already without CB2 Carlton Davis (neck) and their top perimeter backup CBs Karon Prunty (hamstring) and Channing Canada (hamstring), plus S Craig Woodson (shoulder) is questionable to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Gonzalez has not played since Week 3, but he returns in time to cover Garrett Wilson in a divisional showdown. Gonzalez primarily lines up on the perimeter, but he has taken 15 combined snaps in the slot and in the box. He could take a few reps on the inside this week, but perimeter CB2 Carlton Davis (neck) is out, so Gonzalez could be asked to simply stay out wide.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) said he is “ready” to play in Week 6 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Gonzalez told ESPN’s Mike Reiss that his shoulder is feeling “good” after sitting out in Weeks 4-5 to let it heal. This is an important game for the Patriots (3-2), who currently sit second in the AFC East, one spot ahead of the Jets (2-3). Gonzalez has traveled around the formation, at times covering the slot this season. This week, he will likely be tasked with covering Garrett Wilson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Patriots declared CB Christian Gonzalez, QB Behren Morton, OL Dametrious Crownover, CB Carlton Davis III, CB Karon Prunty, and CB Channing Cananda inactive for Week 5 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: New England’s injury-ravaged secondary could have a tough time slowing down the highly efficient Vegas passing offense today. The absence of Gonzalez and Davis should be a boon for both Tre Tucker and Brock Bowers. Kirk Cousins, who has 11 touchdowns to four interceptions this season, is a solid streaming option against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez will not play in New England’s Week 5 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: He has not practiced or played since Week 3. Nothing we’ve seen has suggested he’ll be a Saturday IR candidate, but it also wouldn’t necessarily be surprising if that happened. The Pats also ruled out fellow starting CB Carlton Davis (neck) for Week 5, leaving non-existent Raiders receivers with matchup upgrades. (Cody White is about to touch the end zone paint again.)

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Gonzalez and fellow starting perimeter CB Carlton Davis (neck) have missed each of the Patriots’ first two practices this week, putting them on the wrong side of questionable for Week 5 against the Raiders. Las Vegas lines up Brock Bowers as a wide receiver most of the time. Missing both starting coverage defenders would make life tough on the defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Gonzalez has been sidelined with a shoulder injury since last week, missing the Patriots’ Week 4 win over the Bills. Also not practicing were Carlton Davis (neck) and Karon Prunty (hamstring). We’ll see if any of these corners can practice enough to play for Week 5, but Raiders WR Tre Tucker is headed for a good matchup against a banged up Patriots secondary this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) will not play in New England’s Week 4 game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Gonzalez did not practice at any point this week after popping up on the injury report Wednesday; his status seems to be in doubt for Week 5 at this point as well. The Patriots also ruled out DT Christian Barmore. They’ll be without their best coverage player against the Bills, elevating the matchup for D.J. Moore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Back-to-back missed practices throw Gonzalez’s Week 4 status in real jeopardy. There are few players who mean as much to their defense as Gonzalez does, and if he is out against the Bills it will be open season for D.J. Moore and Khalil Shakir in what oddsmakers are predicting to be a shootout. Patriots DT Christian Barmore (shoulder) remained sidelined as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: ESPN’s Stephen Holder listed QuentonNelson and DeForest Buckner as potential trade options for the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Holder writes that “trade speculation is swirling” around Buckner and notes that Nelson is in the final year of his deal, potentially providing motivation for the Colts to move him. Neither player had much to say when asked about a potential trade, but per Holder, “it is widely expected that significant organizational changes might be coming after the eventual hire of a new general manager.” Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Jonathan Taylor said he would “definitely love to be a Colt for life,” as he enters the final year of his contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Taylor, 27, has totaled more than 320 offensive touches in each of the last two seasons. His current $14 million annual salary makes him the seventh-highest-paid running back in the league. Taylor has set multiple Colts records, operating as the centerpiece of Indianapolis’ offense for years. FOX 59’s Mike Chappell writes that it is “uncertain whether there’s a mutual desire to keep Taylor in Indy beyond 2025.” Multiple Colts stars, including DTs DeForest Buckner and Grover Stewart, OG Quenton Nelson and WR Josh Downs, are also entering the final year of their deal. Chappell believes owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon “might believe it’s more prudent to allow the upcoming season to run its course rather than reinvest in lucrative contracts.” Time will tell.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Colts LG Quenton Nelson returned to Week 2 against the Broncos after suffering an apparent leg injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Nelson was the downfield blocker on a delayed Tyler Warren screen pass when he was hurt. Broncos S Talanoa Hufanga went low on Nelson, which resulted in Nelson driving his quad-knee area into the diving Hufanga. Nelson immediately grabbed just above his knee as he went down. He then limped off the field under his own power and was seen talking to teammates with his helmet on, along the sideline. He returned on the following drive.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Colts LG Quenton Nelson (ankle) is questionable for Week 17 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Nelson was able to practice on Friday, though only in a limited capacity. He appears to be on the right side of questionable but will need to make it through pre-game warmups before being cleared. Tanor Bortolini would likely take his spot in the lineup if he is ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Colts listed OG Quenton Nelson (ankle) as questionable for Week 18 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Nelson was a limited participant in back-to-back practices to close out the week and should have a chance to suit up in what’s arguably the Colts’ biggest game of the season. In addition to Nelson, the Colts also listed center Ryan Kelly (ankle), cornerback Kenny Moore (back), and running back Zack Moss (forearm) as questionable heading into the weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Colts LG Quenton Nelson (toe) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Nelson missed practice last Wednesday and Thursday before being upgraded to a full session on Friday. He played through a questionable tag on Sunday. He will likely get a similar practice regimen this week. Left tackle Bernhard Raimann missed practice with a concussion.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Colts LG Quenton Nelson (toe) is questionable for Week 3 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Nelson did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday but was upgraded to a full session today. He played through the toe issue last week and should do the same versus Baltimore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Colts OL Quenton Nelson missed practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Nelson was present at Colts practice but was barefoot and did not go through any drills. The starting guard was battling through a toe injury last week but was able to suit up against the Texans. With starting center Ryan Kelly also not practicing, the Colts could be down two starting offensive linemen against the Ravens in Week 3. With Anthony Richardson (concussion) also hurt, the Ravens defense could be in for a big game on Sunday if the Colts can’t get healthy.
