https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Colts LG Quenton Nelson (toe) is active for Week 2 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Nelson wasn’t doing much in pre-game warmups, but we would assume he will be out there on Anthony Richardson’s blindside and not just active in an “emergency” capacity. Inactive for the Colts are CB JuJu Brents, DT Adetomiwa Adebawore, TE Drew Ogletree, QB Sam Ehlinger, OT Ryan Hayes, SS Isaiah Land and G/T Arlington Hambright.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.headline: Colts LG Quenton Nelson (toe) is questionable for Week 2 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quenton-ne.analysis: Nelson missed the first two practices of the week with the toe issue but was able to get in a limited session on Friday. He looks to be on the right side of questionable for Week 2, though we will need to see the Colts’ inactives on Sunday to be sure.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Buccaneers placed Christian Rozeboom on injured reserve with a finger injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Rozeboom heads to injured reserve with five tackles and one quarterback pressure to his name. The Buccaneers correspondingly activated David Sills from injured reserve

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Buccaneers signed LB Christian Rozeboom, formerly of the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Rozeboom totaled 122 tackles for the Panthers last season and started all 15 games he appeared in. The veteran linebacker has started 26 games over the last two seasons after being used primarily as a backup for the first three years of his career, and he becomes the second veteran linebacker to join the Buccaneers this offseason. Lavonte David, who is mulling retirement, could still return to play for the Bucs this season, but the team continues to strengthen it’s linebacking corps in the event David should choose to walk away from the game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Panthers CB Jaycee Horn (concussion) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Horn and LB Claudin Cherelus both did not practice due to concussions suffered in Week 12. It will be a tall task to pass protocol to play in Week 13. Also not practicing was LB Christian Rozeboom (hip/hamstring). The Panthers will enter Week 13 against the Rams banged up defensively.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Panthers agreed to terms with LB Christian Rozeboom, formerly of the Rams, on a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Rozeboom entered the league as a UDFA with the Chiefs but found a permanent home with the Rams in LA. He steadily earned more playing time, culminating in a breakout 2024 campaign. Rozeboom made 11 starts across 17 appearances and led the team with 135 combined tackles. He logged five TFLs, four pass breakups, and one interception. Rozeboom will compete for a starting role in Carolina during training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Rams agreed to terms with LB Christian Rozeboom.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Rozeboom has played in all 17 regular season games for the Rams over the last two seasons and started five games for them last year. The former UDFA wound up totaling a season-high 48 tackles and one interception for the Rams, and could be in line for a larger role this upcoming season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: The Athletic’s Jourdan Rodrigue says the Rams are not expected to tender restricted free agent LB Michael Hoecht.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Hoecht is a former undrafted free agent who caught on with the Rams ahead of the 2020 season. Through four seasons, Hoecht has carved out a nice career for himself, starting 26 of the 51 games he’s appeared in while also starting all 17 games last season. In what was essentially a contract year for Hoecht, the veteran linebacker totaled 81 tackles, six sacks, and seven TFLs — all career highs. In addition to Hoecht, the Rams are also expected to let linebacker Christian Rozeboom and defensive tackle Jonah Williams test the free agent market.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Rams tendered exclusive rights free agent DT Michael Hoecht.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: The team also tendered Shaun Jolly and Christian Rozeboom. All three will return to LA for the veteran minimum salary. Hoecht appeared in all 17 games for the Rams in 2022. Six of them were starts. He tallied 4.5 sacks and a forced fumble.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: South Dakota State LB Christian Rozeboom accepted an invite to the NFLPA Bowl.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Rozeboom is a small-school hero. He posted 100-plus tackles in all four seasons on campus. This past year, which included First-Team All-FCS honors, he added six TFL, two sacks, two interceptions, three forced fumbles and two recovered fumbles. The 6-foot-2, 225-pounder is known as a strong athlete. He’ll have to prove that to earn a Day 3 call.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Craig Haley of Athlon Sports lists South Dakota State senior LB Christian Rozeboom among the FCS players that could be drafted in 2020.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Rozeboom has been a very productive player over the last two seasons for the Jackrabbits -- and was solid his freshman year as well -- while being named an FCS All-American by several publications. As Haley notes, the 6-foot-2, 225-pound linebacker is a three-time All-MVFC first-teamer, and he leads all active FCS players in career tackles with 364. Haley also writes that he “plays with an edge,” and NFL teams will surely be watching Rozeboom to see if he can help their roster in 2020 and beyond.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alijah-ver.headline: Patriots placed Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alijah-ver.analysis: He’ll miss, at a minimum, Weeks 7-10 before being eligible to return in Week 12 after the Patriots return from their bye week. The Patriots will try to get by with Matt Pryor at guard for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alijah-ver.headline: Patriots ruled out Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) for Week 7 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alijah-ver.analysis: The Patriots will also be without RG Ben Brown (knee). The Bears’ defense is not an elite unit, but losing two starting guards is rough. Backups Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse will start instead. The Patriots listed RT Morgan Moses (foot) as questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alijah-ver.headline: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) and Ben Brown (knee) are unlikely to play on Thursday night.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alijah-ver.analysis: Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse stepped in for the two guards towards the end of last week’s offensive line apocalypse and would likely be in line to start in Week 7. Neither Vera-Tucker nor Brown practiced on Monday or Tuesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alijah-ver.headline: Patriots LG Alijah Vera-Tucker suffered a hamstring injury in New England’s Week 6 game against the Jets and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alijah-ver.analysis: It’s been a disastrous injury afternoon for the Pats, who have had 2-3 offensive linemen shuffling in and out of the game vs. Gang Green. Free agent addition Vera-Tucker has been off to a decent enough start this season but is mostly providing replacement-level snaps. Matt Pryor has been the next man up at left guard.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alijah-ver.headline: Patriots agreed to terms with OG Alijah Vera-Tucker, formerly of the Jets, on a three-year, $42 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alijah-ver.analysis: Vera-Tucker’s deal is worth “up to” $48 million. The former No. 14 overall pick played at every offensive line position other than center while on his rookie contract, though most of his reps have come at the two guard spots. He most recently started all 15 games of his 2024 campaign at right guard. Vera-Tucker was supposed to play out his fifth-year option with the Jets in 2025, but a torn tricep in practice just before Week 1 ended his season before it began. AVT has a lengthy injury history. He has only played more than seven games in two-of-five years. On the other hand, he has generally played well when healthy, and the Pats needed to keep adding talent to their offensive line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alijah-ver.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Jets RG Alijah Vera-Tucker (triceps) will undergo season-ending surgery.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alijah-ver.analysis: This confirms what both Schefter and the NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport had been reporting for the past day. AVT suffered the triceps injury during Tuesday’s practice and has been undergoing various tests to confirm the need for surgery ever since. Vera-Tucker was set to play 2025 on his fifth-year option but will now head to free agency after spending the entire season on injured reserve. Vera-Tucker has ended three of the past four seasons on injured reserve and has appeared in just 43-of-85 possible games since entering the league in 2021. Even with a checkered injury history, his play should earn him a healthy contract on the open market.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alijah-ver.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jets RG Alijah Vera-Tucker (triceps) is expected to miss the 2025 season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alijah-ver.analysis: This was expected after ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported the torn triceps yesterday. Vera-Tucker was seeking a second opinion to confirm that season-ending surgery was necessary. It appears as though that is the case. The Jets will place him on injured reserve once the news is official. The Jets will likely move center Joe Tippmann to AVT’s spot and replace Tippmann with Josh Myers. For a team built on establishing a ball-control ground game, an early offensive line injury is not what Jets fans wanted to see ahead of Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alijah-ver.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Jets RG Alijah Vera-Tucker suffered a torn triceps in Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alijah-ver.analysis: Per Schefter, AVT is getting a second opinion to confirm that season-ending surgery is necessary. Barring a surprise, Vera-Tucker appears to be done for the year. He should be placed on injured reserve later this week. Vera-Tucker was set to be an integral part of a Jets offensive line built for pounding the rock. Now they will be down a starting offensive lineman and a standout from training camp just days before the start of the season. Vera-Tucker was set to play on his fifth-year option in 2025, meaning he will be an unrestricted free agent next offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alijah-ver.headline: The Athletic’s Dianna Russini reports Jets RG Alijah Vera-Tucker “suffered a potentially serious [arm] injury and could miss significant time.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alijah-ver.analysis: Vera-Tucker’s 2025 season could be over before it begins after sustaining an arm injury days before the Jets’ Week 1 opener against the Steelers. Vera-Tucker missed much of the 2022 and 2023 seasons due to injuries before returning and playing 15 games for the Jets in 2024. The Athletic’s Zack Rosenblatt said Vera-Tucker “was a standout in camp, dominant in the run game and appeared to be finally fully healthy” headed into the regular season. His injury is a massive blow to the Jets offense, expected to be predicated on the run. Pro Football Focus graded Vera-Tucker as the 33rd best run blocking offensive lineman in the NFL last season out of 148 qualifying players. This news is certainly a blow to Breece Hall and Braelon Allen, and perhaps the whole New York offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alijah-ver.headline: Jets interim head coach Jeff Ulbrich said LG Alijah Vera-Tucker (ankle) has a chance to play in Week 15.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alijah-ver.analysis: Ulbrich said the team is hopeful Vera-Tucker can suit up this Sunday against the Jaguars in a meaningless game for both teams. Vera-Tucker could be an important addition to keep Aaron Rodgers upright and force feeding the ball to Garrett Wilson and Davante Adams against a terrible Jags defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek (calf) will not play in Pittsburgh’s Week 7 game against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Ruled out on Thursday before traveling, Skowronek probably has a real chance to get back in Week 8. With Marquez Valdes-Scantling now on the roster, Skowronek has likely lost whatever desperation fantasy value he might have had either way.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said Ben Skowronek (leg) has been ruled out for Week 6.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: We weren’t exactly worried about Skowronek siphoning many targets away, but with him out of the pecking order entirely Germie Bernard should be a wheels-up WR3 for Week 6 now that both Skowronek and Roman Wilson have been ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek has been ruled out for Week 5 against the Colts with a calf injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: There hasn’t been a lot of word on what happened to Skowronek. He went into the blue medical tent in the second quarter to have his leg looked at and then headed into the locker room. When the Steelers returned the kickoff to start the second half, Skowronek, who is a key special teamer, was not on the field. He was ruled out shortly after. With Michael Pittman Jr. already out, the Steelers are getting a little thin with their wide receiver depth.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Ben Skowronek caught his only target for 22 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 1 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: It was a play-action pass where Skowronek went against the flow of the defense and it almost operated like a screen, with Steelers receivers blocking downfield to create an easy crease for the 28-year-old receiver. Skowronek doesn’t need to be chased in fantasy leagues after only playing 10 of 53 snaps for the Steelers in this one. He’s operating more-or-less in a timeshare for Pittsburgh’s third receiver role with Roman Wilson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Steelers re-signed WR Ben Skowronek to a two-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Skowronek caught five passes for 69 yards with the Steelers last season while playing in a very limited role. Skowronek’s 46 routes run and five targets marked the second fewest amongst any receiver on the team in 2024. A good blocker and willing special teamer, Skowronek probably has an inside track to a roster spot even if what he does isn’t worthy of fantasy interest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Steelers WR Ben Skowronek (hip) is questionable to return to Week 16 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Skowronek was involved early, catching both targets for 25 yards, but departed early in the second quarter with a hip injury and was deemed questionable to return by the team. Already shorthanded at wide receiver due to the continued absence of George Pickens, it will be up to Calvin Austin, Van Jefferson, and Mike Williams to step up for a team fighting to clinch the AFC North against their great division rivals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Steelers elevated WR Ben Skowronek for Week 2 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: The team also elevated Skowronek in Week 1, but he wasn’t a factor against the Falcons and shouldn’t be one this week either. If anything, it’s likely not a good sign for the chances that rookie WR Roman Wilson makes his NFL debut this weekend. Skowronek will have most of his value of special teams this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Steelers elevated WR Ben Skowronek for Week 1 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Skowronek should fill a depth role on offense while contributing to special teams and is not in the fantasy discussion for Week 1 barring injury. The elevation likely has a lot to do with rookie Roman Wilson’s absence for Sunday for a team lacking in depth at the wide receiver position.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Steelers signed RB Boston Scott, formerly of the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Scott was let go by the Rams during final roster cutdowns and now lands with the Steelers. The veteran running back won’t be threatening for offensive snaps any time soon but could earn a look as a returner if somebody were to miss time with an injury. In addition to Scott, the Steelers also signed wide receivers Ben Skowronek and Brandon Johnson to the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.headline: Texans released Ben Skowronek.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ben-skowro.analysis: Skowronek signed with the Texans earlier this offseason after spending the first three years of his career with the Rams. The former seventh-round pick has caught 58 passes for 575 yards and one touchdown in his career and can be used both outside and in the slot. Skowronek also has valuable special teams experience and could find himself on another roster in the near future. The Texans also waived/released DT McTelvin Agim, LB Tarique Barnes, EDGE Solomon Byrd, WR Quintez Cephus, OG Dieter Eiselen, EDGE Malik Fisher, EDGE Ali Gaye, FB Troy Hairston, DT Marcus Harris, WR Johnny Johnson III, CB Troy Pride, RB J.J. Taylor, LB Max Tooley and OT Kilian Zierer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: SNY TV’s Connor Hughes believes the Giants will stick with J.J. McCarthy as the starter “for the foreseeable future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: According to Hughes, “this is the player they targeted and wanted” as their quarterback the minute Jaxson Dart (knee) got hurt. Hughes acknowledges that coach John Harbaugh could eventually bench McCarthy later in the year, but it will take more than a bad “game or two” for that to happen. In the meantime, the weekly fantasy football outlooks for Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely are more volatile than they were with Jameis Winston at the helm. Selling high could make sense. Hughes adds that McCarthy would have to play like a top-10 quarterback to make the coaching staff consider him for the starting role next season. That outcome seems highly unlikely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports J.J. McCarthy will start in Week 7 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: John Harbaugh is making the switch after a historic fourth quarter from “NINE”. McCarthy threw for 243 yards and a score in 11 minutes of action as the Giants mounted a frantic comeback against the Saints. Though he came up short in the end, McCarthy gave the Giants’ offense life after three dreadful quarters from James Winston. Now he’ll get the first snap versus a Houston defense that has been surprisingly ineffective this year. McCarthy is a high-risk QB2 for his first start as a Giant. He should at least be added in all Superflex formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: Giants coach John Harbaugh said they’re “working through that now” when asked which quarterback would start against the Texans in Week 7.
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: The fact that he has to think about it probably tips the hand that it will be J.J. McCarthy sooner or later — if not outright now. Jameis Winston was replaced by McCarthy in the fourth quarter yesterday and McCarthy showcased his deep arm and almost erased a large deficit by throwing for 243 yards on 21 attempts. If McCarthy did start against the Texans, he would likely be a bottom five superflex option on the Week 7 slate because of his established history as a starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said he “can’t answer that now” when asked about who his starting quarterback would be heading into Week 7 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: It’s the exact kind of answer we would expect from a coach who is just minutes removed from his team nearly completing a comeback victory. J.J. McCarthy stepped in for Jameis Winston in the fourth quarter and lit up the Saints for 243 yards and one touchdown in the fourth quarter, leading the Giants on three scoring drives and 17 unanswered points in a game that the Saints won 34-27. Whether it’s in Week 7 or a point later in the season, McCarthy feels like a lock to start multiple games for the Giants, who now sit at 3-2-1 on the season. The Jameis Winston Experience, while fun, is often short-lived, and his underwhelming performance on Sunday against the Saints (152-1-2) comes a week after Winston struggled for the entire first half against the Commanders before he turned it on in the second half. Harbaugh will likely announce his Week 7 starter in the coming days, but it wouldn’t be surprising to learn the team is handing McCarthy the keys for the remainder of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: J.J. McCarthy completed 11-of-21 passes for 243 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Giants’ 34-27, Week 6 loss to the Saints, adding two carries for 26 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: McCarthy’s first play of the game was a read-option where he kept the ball and rushed for a loss of two yards in the red zone. With the Giants down 24 points in the fourth quarter, McCarthy replaced a struggling Jameis Winston and started throwing several deep targets downfield. He threw an interception his first drive but led multiple successful drives late in the fourth quarter. Charlie Jones corralled a 49-yard pass away from a defender, making a near-interception into a long completion for McCarthy. Martin Emerson dropped an interception later in the drive before McCarthy connected with Isaiah Likely for a touchdown. He wound up leading the Giants in passing and rushing through just one quarter of play. Averaging 11.6 yards per attempt, McCarthy was one play away from leading a comeback against the Saints. Instead, we will wait to see if John Harbaugh will name the 23-year-old the starter for Week 7 against the Texans; he would be a fantasy QB2 if he starts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: According to ESPN’s Jordan Raanan, Giants coach John Harbaugh hinted that the Giants have “more in store for the J.J. McCarthy package.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: Who is asking for this? McCarthy was on the field for three plays in Week 5. They gained three yards, two of which came from McCarthy on a pair of rush attempts. After flaming out as a traditional quarterback in Minnesota, McCarthy is working his way toward becoming the next Taysom Hill. Jameis Winston remains the starter, but Harbaugh will use McCarthy as a change-of-pace option a few times each week. He could also take over as the starter if Winston struggles for an extended period of time, though we appear to be at least a few weeks away from that being a consideration.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: Giants declared RB Devin Singletary, S Ar’Darius Washington, CB Nikko Reed, DL Jihad Ward, OL J.C. Davis, TE Thomas Fidone, and DT Bobby Jamison-Travis as inactive for Week 4 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: This is the second-straight week that Singletary has been made a healthy scratch for the Giants. Najee Harris and Tyrone Tracy will serve as the backups to Cam Skattebo. It’s also worth noting that QB J.J. McCarthy, who was acquired from the Vikings earlier this week, is active for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: Giants coach John Harbaugh said the possibility of Jaxson Dart (knee) returning during the playoffs “may be a bit ambitious.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: Everyone but Harbaugh knew Dart wasn’t returning for the playoffs the moment his meniscus repair procedure was announced. Harbaugh, meanwhile, held out hope that his starting quarterback could return in time for a deep playoff run. Even he isn’t keeping that facade up anymore, though he noted that Dart’s surgery “went well.” Coming off an ugly win, Jameis Winston will make his second start of the year in Week 4. J.J. McCarthy will get a crack at the job when the Giants inevitably start losing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: SNY’s Connor Hughes believes the Giants could start JJ McCarthy in “the near future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: New York acquired McCarthy from the Vikings on Monday in exchange for a 2027 fifth round draft pick. Hughes spoke with NFL sources who said “the Giants do not give up a fifth-round pick unless they plan to play McCarthy in the near future.” Head coach John Harbaugh and the team’s coaching staff, per Hughes, see McCarthy as a starting-caliber quarterback despite his immense struggles in Minnesota last season. “The Giants welcomed the chance to add a player they view as a competitor, gritty, mobile, and who has all the tools to be a plus passer in the NFL,” Hughes said. With Jameis Winston playing worse than any QB in recent memory, McCarthy could be just a couple weeks away from taking over as New York’s starter. He would be a mild upgrade for Malik Nabers and the rest of the Giants pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.headline: Giants acquired QB J.J. McCarthy from the Vikings in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/j-j-mccarthy/0.analysis: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero was the first to report the trade. McCarthy landing with John Harbaugh’s Giants feels a bit too on-the-nose given his connection with Jim Harbaugh during his days at Michigan. McCarthy was at one point competing for the Vikings’ QB1 job in camp with Kyler Murray, but was knocked all the way down to QB3 on the Vikings’ depth chart when Carson Wentz took over for Murray in Week 1 and drew the start in Week 2. Assuming Jameis Winston doesn’t suddenly exceed expectations and lead an efficient passing attack, McCarthy will probably get a shot to start at some point when he gets up to speed with the offense. McCarthy has thrown for 1,632 yards, 11 touchdowns, and 12 interceptions in 10 career games while completing 57.6 percent of his passes. We’ll see if a change of scenery is all he needs to turn the corner and live up to the hype that made him the 10th overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Elijah Arroyo will undergo shoulder surgery and miss the rest of the 2026 season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.analysis: Arroyo will have multiple injured reserve stints on his NFL record by the time his third season begins next year. Arroyo has caught 16-of-26 targets for 196 yards and one touchdown in regular season play thus far in his career. The talented receiving tight end fell in the 2025 NFL Draft due to knee-related health concerns. Hopefully, a strong offseason propels him to career-best figures in 2027.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Elijah Arroyo (shoulder) is expected to miss time and it “could be an extended absence.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.analysis: Arroyo’s career hasn’t really got off the ground with AJ Barner as the obvious No. 1 in the Seahawks tight end room. The 50th overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft has just two targets this year and hasn’t been a fantasy factor yet.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.headline: Elijah Arroyo (shoulder) underwent further testing on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.analysis: No update yet on what was learned, and we may have to wait until next week’s first injury report to learn more. The Seahawks’ young tight end has faced multiple injuries in his short career. Hopefully, this one is not serious.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.headline: Elijah Arroyo (arm) was taken to the locker room in the second quarter of week 6 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.analysis: Arroyo was injured while trying to recover a Rashid Shaheed fumble in the second quarter and was promptly escorted to the locker room with trainers helping to stabilize his arm. It appeared to be a potential wrist or shoulder injury based on how the staff helped him off the field. The second-year tight end was not targeted prior to departing and appears to be on the wrong side of questionable to return to Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.headline: AJ Barner caught 1-of-1 targets for eight yards in the Seahawks’ Week 2 win over the Cardinals, adding one rush for one yard and one touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.analysis: Up 24-7 on 4th-and-goal with just over three minutes left in the game, the Seahawks started a fresh set of downs from the Cardinals’ three-yard line. Both RB George Holani and RB Emanuel Wilson were given chances to punch it in before Seahawks OC Brian Fleury dialed up a Tush Push play for Barner on 4th-and-goal. Barner jumped up and across the line, bringing his fantasy stat line from something unusable to something we can live with. He remains a boom-bust TE1 against the Commanders next week. Seahawks TE2 Elijah Arroyo nabbed a 17-yard pass on a post route, but that was it for him. So far, the Seahawks’ reported uptick in usage for the tight end position has not panned out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.headline: The Athletic’s Andrew Destin believes Seahawks TE AJ Barner “will likely see an uptick in production, as should backup TE Elijah Arroyo” this year.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.analysis: Destin notes that new Seahawks OC Brian Fleury served as the 49ers’ TE coach for four seasons “and is expected to feature the position prominently.” Aside from that, and an increase in shifts and motion, he thinks the offense is “going to look very similar” to last year. Barner underwent two offseason surgeries, one of which was to address a nagging ankle injury that Barner said he initially suffered during the 2024 Senior Bowl before the Seahawks drafted him. After turning in the PPR TE14 performance last season, Barner might have a shot to crack the position’s top 12.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.headline: Seahawks TE Elijah Arroyo caught 2-of-3 targets for 50 yards and one touchdown in Sunday’s preseason game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.analysis: Arroyo played three drives this evening, scoring from 36 yards out on the first one. Arroyo lined up in line on the left side, ran a route up the seam, shaking a safety along the way and easily hauled in the uncontested pass from tonight’s starting QB Drew Lock. Scoring against the Titans’ first-string defense is a plus, but playing while the rest of the Seahawks starters sat was not a great sign. Arroyo seems to be firmly behind TE AJ Barner on the depth chart right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler believes AJ Barner is an “ascending” player in the Seahawks offense.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.analysis: Fowlers said the team expects Barner to be more involved as a pass catcher in 2026 after recording 52 receptions for 519 yards and six touchdowns last season (while being targeted on 19 percent of his routes). Barner, following multiple offseason surgeries to clean up nagging injuries, is fully healthy and ready for a more prominent role in Seattle’s offense. New Seahawks offensive coordinator Brian Fleury, meanwhile, is expected to use plenty of two tight end sets in 2026, meaning TE Elijah Arroyo could see an increase in snaps and routes. Barner has a little bit of extra hidden upside as the Seahawks’ primary tush push option near the goal line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.headline: ESPN’s Brady Henderson reports TE Elijah Arroyo has been a standout through the first week of Seahawks training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.analysis: That apparently includes in both pad-less and padded practices. Henderson does add the same was true last summer before the then No. 50 overall pick went on to have a quiet rookie year. Arroyo dealt with knee issues after they were a red flag during his pre-draft process. Drafted in part to be an after-the-catch weapon, Arroyo could be left fighting for designed touches to begin the season. He is comfortably behind AJ Barner on both the depth chart and in average draft position. We’ll let you know if he keeps lighting up camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.headline: Seahawks TE Elijah Arroyo (undisclosed) resumed practicing at mandatory minicamp on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/elijah-arroyo/.analysis: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald revealed on Wednesday that Arroyo was working through something, but was expected to be ready for training camp. Getting back early, even in a limited capacity, is good to see. Arroyo’s past few years, both in college and in his NFL rookie season, have been slowed by knee issues. Fellow backup TE Eric Saubert resumed practicing as well. Hopefully, both players are practicing fully before long.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Chiefs placed Josh Simmons on injured reserve with a back injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: The Chiefs made head athletic trainer Rick Burkholder available to the media to explain the 2026 Simmons Saga today. On August 17th, the young left tackle reported calf discomfort in the same leg that he underwent a patellar tendon repair in 2024. Chiefs trainers discovered that a bulging, herniated disc in his lumbar spine was causing the lower-leg issue. According to Burkholder, offensive linemen occasionally deal with this type of disc issue, but Simmons’ issue was complicated because it was abnormally high up in the lumbar spine. Simmons consulted with a well-regarded spine specialist, who recommended rehabilitation instead of surgery. Imaging taken early in the rehab process showed improvement, so they stayed the course, but unfortunately, Simmons’ recovery has recently plateaued, leading to the injured reserve placement. Simmons will be eligible to return for the Chiefs’ Week 11 game against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Josh Simmons (back) won’t play in Kansas City’s Week 6 game against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: Simmons did actually practice this week, so he’s trending in the right direction, but Khalil Benson gets another start while Simmons tries to get past a bulging disc in his back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Josh Simmons (back) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: The Chiefs’ starting left tackle might need more time off, but his continued practice participation is good to see. The Chiefs take on the struggling Chargers this week, and may be able to get by alright without him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Josh Simmons (back) returned to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: Simmons has been held out of practice for roughly two months while dealing with a bulging disc in his lower back. Kansas City’s starting left tackle has yet to play a snap this year while dealing with the back injury. Head coach Andy Reid said the team will “ease him back in, but on a limited basis.” There is currently no timetable for when Simmons will return. Undrafted Khalil Benson has been serviceable as the team’s starting left tackle, but Simmons will ultimately be a notable upgrade whenever he returns to action. Benson is still expected to start this week versus the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Chiefs ruled out LT Josh Simmons (back) for Week 4 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: Earlier this week, Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Simmons is dealing with a bulging disc in his lower back. Brutal. On the plus side, CB Chamarri Conner (knee) will make his return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Josh Simmons is dealing with a bulging disc in his lower back.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: Simmons hasn’t played or practiced this year. Reid told reporters that he was making progress but will remain out of practice today. Kahlil Benson will presumably draw another start at left tackle in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Chiefs LT Josh Simmons (back) will not play in Kansas City’s Week 3 game against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: Kahlil Benson draws another start. Simmons has not been spotted at practice since the regular season started.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Chiefs declared OT Josh Simmons, S Chamarri Conner, TE Jared Wiley, QB Garrett Nussmeier, DT Bryson Eason, OT Diego Pounds, and DE Jack Pyburn inactive for Week 2 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: The Chiefs enter Week 2 relatively healthy as they look to start the season with consecutive victories. It will be interesting to see if the Chiefs carry forward a run-heavy attack after pounding the football on the ground in a Week 1 win over the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Chiefs ruled out LT Josh Simmons (back) for Week 2 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: Backup OT Kahlil Benson will start in Simmons’ stead. He did so last week and avoided major mistakes. The Chiefs also ruled out CB Chamarri Conner (knee).

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.headline: Josh Simmons (back) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-simmo.analysis: Simmons missed the Chiefs’ 2026 opener with the back issue and isn’t likely to suit up this week either. Kahlil Benson, a UDFA rookie, took his spot at left tackle in Week 1. Benson allowed three pressures and was penalized once, but he did not allow a sack and held his own in the run game. He will draw the start in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said the team is still determining “the best time” to schedule Davante Adams’ (hamstring) “cleanup” procedure.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Surgeries are sometimes delayed to help reduce swelling. Occasionally, new information is gathered during this time and/or during the surgery. Adams is currently expected to be sidelined for 6-10 weeks. Perhaps the wide return-to-play timeline is due to the fact that the surgeon has not yet fully assessed the injury. We tentatively expect the team to share an updated recovery timeline once Adams undergoes the procedure on his ruptured hamstring tendon. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said the Rams have not had discussions about bringing in a receiver with Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined for 6-10 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Earlier today, ESPN’s Dan Graziano reported that the Rams “will at least explore the possibility of trading for a wide receiver.” Obviously, McVay doesn’t want to tip off other wide receiver-needy NFL teams about their potential entrance into the trade market, and he has no reason to be honest with us. Acquiring a new wide receiver makes sense, and the Rams were aggressive players in the trade market last offseason. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano reports that the Rams “will at least explore the possibility of trading for a wide receiver.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams is set to undergo a procedure after rupturing his hamstring tendon in Week 6 against the Cardinals. He will be sidelined for 6-10 weeks. The Rams were already very thin at wide receiver and Puka Nacua has spent multiple weeks on the injury report as well. Acquiring a capable wide receiver makes sense, but as Graziano mentions, the Rams have already traded away a lot of their draft capital. Thus far, GM Les Snead has already given up their 2027 first- and third-round picks, and their 2028 second-round pick and their 2029 third-round pick. He notes that Rams QB Stetson Bennett played for Browns coach Todd Monken in college. Perhaps Monken would be interested in a reunion.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Davante Adams (hamstring) will miss 6-10 weeks with a ruptured tendon.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams had a non-contact injury at the end of Week 6’s loss to the Cardinals and unfortunately is as serious as it appeared. He’ll likely be placed on injured reserve ahead of Week 7. His absence will further focus targets on Puka Nacua and likely elevate Konata Mumpfield into a bigger role. Adams had put together a 30/480/4 line in his first six games of the season. Adams will reportedly have surgery to “clean” out the tendon, per NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, in hopes he can return around the team’s bye week, which is scheduled for Week 11. It’s a major blow for a Rams team that is already reeling at 2-4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Davante Adams 3-of-4 targets for 39 yards in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams appeared to injure his left knee while running a route in the red zone on the Rams’ final possession. He cut, turned upfield and quickly began limping his way to the back of the end zone, removing himself from the play while grabbing at the inside of his left knee. He subbed himself out after that. No word on his status, but we expect an update soon. Prior to that, the Cardinals’ pass rush made life tough on the Rams’ passing attack. Adams caught his first pass a minute and a half into the second quarter. Stafford was looking his way in the end zone later on the same drive, but Josh Sweat got to him for the strip-sack. Adams banked 16-yard receptions on the sixth and seventh drives, impressively getting wide open via a downfield out route on the second one. If Adams escaped with a minor injury, he would be a WR2 against the Raiders next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Davante Adams caught 5-of-7 targets for 51 yards and two touchdowns in the Rams’ Week 5 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams cashed in on a corner fade from four yards out in the second quarter and ran a beautiful route on a double move slant from five yards out for his second score in the fourth quarter, proving that he remains an elite red zone weapon for an offense that has now attempted 51 or more passes in three straight games. Adams is back to modest target rates following the Week 4 return of Puka Nacua but remains a weekly WR2 due to his red zone acumen, which remains true ahead of a much more forgiving matchup against the Cardinals in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Davante Adams caught 4-of-9 targets for 32 yards in the Rams’ Week 4 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams was the victim of a bad Matthew Stafford ball or two in rainy Philadelphia conditions, but he sadly immediately reverted to clear No. 2 wideout status with Puka Nacua back in the lineup. Nacua went off for 9/125. Adams now has seven catches for 58 scoreless yards in two games with Nacua in the lineup compared to 15/332/2 in two games without. Hopefully that trend normalizes a bit for a potential Week 5 shootout with the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Davante Adams caught 7-of-13 targets for 137 yards in the Rams’ Week 3 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Adams’ 137 yards combine with the 195 yards he erupted for in Week 2 to set a new high in receiving yards in consecutive games during his remarkable career. Even more stunning was the fact that he did so against one of the top corners in the league in Pat Surtain, who shadowed Adams for all but a handful of his routes, proving his ability to get open against top competition even in the later stages of his career. Puka Nacua missed both Week 2 and Week 3 and his injury timeline remains convoluted, at best. Adams will remains a top-tier WR1 should Nacua miss more time, and would be solid WR2 should Nacua return for a Week 4 meeting with the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: Sean McVay said Puka Nacua (groin) is “not making great progress.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: In a surprisingly candid interview with ESPN Los Angeles, McVay certainly did not sound optimistic that Nacua would play in Week 3. Nacua has already missed one practice this week and there’s been no indication that he will get back on the field over the next two days. Davante Adams racked up 195 yards and two scores with Nacua out in Week 2. It will be hard not to rank him as a WR1 once Nacua is ruled out. Terrance Ferguson operated as the team’s No. 2 receiver last week and will be in the TE1 mix without Nacua.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Rams WR Puka Nacua (groin) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/davante-ad.analysis: Sean McVay was unsure if Nacua would be able to play in Week 3 when asked about it on Tuesday. A DNP today suggests Nacua will need at least one more week of rest before returning to the lineup. Terrance Ferguson finished second on the Rams in targets last week with nine. He caught six passes for 54 yards and a score. No receiver outside of Davante Adams was targeted more than two times. Adams was utterly dominant, turning his 10 targets into 195 yards and two scores. Those are the only two major beneficiaries of Nacua’s likely absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.headline: Cam Jurgens (concussion) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.analysis: The Ravens acquired Jurgens from the Eagles two weeks ago, but he hasn’t made his Baltimore debut yet while he works through the league’s concussion protocol. A full practice today puts him on track to suit up in Week 7. His return will move rookie Vega Ioane back to right guard.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.headline: Cam Jurgens (concussion) will not play in Baltimore’s Week 6 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.analysis: Jurgens has now missed each of his first two weeks with the Ravens as he tries to shake a brain injury he suffered while with the Eagles. Vega Ioane will likely man center again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.headline: Cam Jurgens (concussion) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.analysis: Jurgens still has a chance to play, but we had hoped to see him upgrade to full participation. Ravens EDGE Mike Green (hamstring) was added to the injury report today as a limited participant. Ravens OG Andrew Vorhees (foot) joins him in the limited column. Ravens RT Roger Rosengarten (knee), LT Ronnie Stanley (rest/toe/ankle) and CB Marlon Humphrey (hamstring/calf) upgraded to full participation. Ravens OG John Simpson (groin) downgraded to a DNP.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.headline: Cam Jurgens (concussion) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.analysis: The Ravens’ new starting center is still recovering from his recent concussion, but he seemingly has a chance to face the Browns this week. Ravens EDGE Trey Hendrickson (finger) and S Kyle Hamilton (stinger) are practicing fully, while RT Roger Rosengarten (knee), OG John Simpson (groin), OG Andrew Vorhees (foot), LT Ronnie Stanley (rest/toe/ankle) and CB Marlon Humphrey (hamstring/calf) were limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.headline: Ravens C Cam Jurgens (concussion) won’t play in Baltimore’s Week 5 game against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.analysis: He didn’t practice all week after coming over from the Eagles. It’s likely to be Vega Ioane at center again as they try to get Jurgens healthy to man the pivot in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.headline: Ravens acquired Cam Jurgens and a 2027 seventh-round pick from the Eagles in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.analysis: The Ravens have sustained several interior offensive line injuries in recent weeks. Things got so bad that they did not have a healthy center on the active roster or practice squad after Week 3. Jurgens is currently in concussion protocol and may not suit up this week, but he will take over as the team’s starter once healthy. The Eagles, in turn, will move forward Drew Kendall at center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.headline: Eagles removed C Cam Jurgens (concussion) from the injury report ahead of Week 12 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.analysis: Jurgens departed the team’s Week 11 win over the Lions to be evaluated for a concussion. He increased his participation in each practice this week before drawing the questionable tag, ultimately removed from the injury report Saturday ahead of a matchup with the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.headline: Eagles C Cam Jurgens (concussion) is questionable to play in Week 12 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.analysis: Jurgens sat out Wednesday, was limited Thursday and practiced fully on Friday. He has not yet been cleared, but as long as he remains symptom-free, he is on track to play. The Eagles’ offense gets a boost with their reliable center on the field. Hopefully, he is good to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.headline: Eagles C Cam Jurgens (concussion) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.analysis: Jurgens is making progress in the NFL’s concussion protocol, but he has a ways to go before he can be viewed as more than questionable. Having their reliable center on the field would be great for a struggling Eagles offense as they take on the division-rival Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.headline: Eagles C Cam Jurgens (concussion) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cam-jurgen.analysis: Jurgens will likely miss Week 12 because of the brain injury. Right tackle Lane Johnson is also out this week. He is dealing with a Lisfranc injury and is expected to miss at least a month. Luckily for the Eagles, their banged-up line is facing Dallas’s bottom-tier pass-rush on Sunday. There are certainly worse matchups to be without two starters for.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Jordan Addison (hamstring) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison, well-rested coming off his team’s Week 6 bye, is ready to go. The Colts’ defense has played poorly, and they will likely be without top CB Sauce Gardner (calf). Addison can be a volatile producer at times, but he warrants WR3/FLEX treatment this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Vikings declared Jordan Addison (hamstring) inactive for Week 5 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison seemingly gave it a go this morning but wasn’t quite ready to play. The Vikings get a Week 6 bye, so Addison should be ready to go when they return to face the Colts in two weeks. Also inactive for the Vikings are OT Christian Darrisaw, S Jakobe Thomas, WR Odell Beckham, CB Chuck Demmings, DT Elijah Williams, and QB Max Brosmer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: ESPN’s Jeff Darlington reports Jordan Addison (hamstring) “isn’t likely to be active” for Week 5 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison got in two limited practices this week before being listed as questionable. He was considered a game-time decision as of this morning, but it sounds like the team is going to hold him out for at least one week. Justin Jefferson, on the other hand, is expected to suit up. The offense will run through him, per usual.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Justin Jefferson will work out pregame to determine his status for Week 5 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: The same is true of Jordan Addison. Both Minnesota wideouts are currently listed as questionable for Week 5. Jefferson is from Louisiana and has already told reporters he plans to play in the homecoming game. We expect him to suit up, but fantasy managers should have a backup plan for him and Addison to be safe.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Jordan Addison (hamstring) is questionable for Minnesota’s Week 5 game against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison practiced on Thursday and Friday after taking Wednesday off. We’d consider him on the optimistic side of questionable for Sunday’s game against New Orleans, but he will probably only be a WR3/FLEX play if Justin Jefferson (ankle) also returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Jordan Addison (hamstring) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: The Vikings’ No. 2 wide receiver sat out on Wednesday due to “a little hamstring soreness.” If he can get through today and tomorrow without aggravating the sore muscle, he should be able to play in Week 5 against the Saints. His WR3/FLEX viability is subject to Justin Jefferson’s (ankle) status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said Jordan Addison (hamstring) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: According to O’Connell, Addison has “a little hamstring soreness,” though it is “considered minor.” Keep an eye on this. Hamstring injuries can quickly become problematic at the wide receiver position. If active and practicing fully by the end of the week, Addison will be a WR3/FLEX against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Jordan Addison caught 4-of-6 targets for 52 yards in the Vikings’ Week 4 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison’s box score could have looked a little bit better, had his 21-yard gain on a curl route during the Vikings’ third drive not been erased by a penalty. Regardless, he played sidekick to T.J. Hockenson in this one. For his part, Addison maximized his opportunity, delivering the longest play of the game via a 27-yard catch on a crosser in which he barreled through multiple Dolphins defenders to generate extra yardage. The Vikings also gave him the ball on a jet sweep, but he lost one yard on it. Addison will be a WR3 against the Saints next week if Justin Jefferson (ankle) is still sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Jordan Addison caught 5-of-9 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in the Vikings’ Week 3 win against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: Addison dominated air yards and targets with Justin Jefferson sidelined with an ankle injury he sustained in the second quarter. His 41-yard touchdown grab from Kyler Murray was one of three downfield looks he got on the day; he nearly converted the other two as well. A non-factor in the Vikings’ first two games of the season, Addison should be locked into lineups if Jefferson misses any time with the ankle issue. If Jefferson returns for Week 4 against the Dolphins, Addison would figure to be flex-viable as long as Murray is under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.headline: Jordan Addison caught 2-of-5 targets for 21 yards in the Vikings’ Week 2 win over the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-add.analysis: It’s another disappointing statline for a wideout held without a catch in Week 1, though it was yet another game where we didn’t get to see the Vikings’ “real” offense. With Kyler Murray out with a concussion, Carson Wentz was fed to the wolves at rainy Soldier Field. Murray is expected back for Week 3 in Tampa, and with him, hopefully finally a useable statline for the Vikes’ talented No. 2 receiver.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis (right thumb) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: ESPN’s Marcel Louis-Jacques reports that Willis received treatment for his thumb injury on his right, throwing hand, though he did not share what exactly the injury is. Hopefully, it is nothing serious. If his ball placement is impacted, the Jets’ D/ST would benefit. Willis is a volatile QB2 against them this week. Willis underwent surgery on his left thumb in August 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said Malik “is our quarterback.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: “Malik needs to be better, but that’s not the headline -- we all need to be better ... everything in the pass game has to be better.. It’s the receivers, it’s the tight ends, it’s the protection,” Hafley continued. Willis is by all statistical measures one of the weakest quarterbacks in the league with his arm, but at least he’s skimping some superflex QB2 value with his legs. There’s not much reason for the Dolphins to bench him either way, as they have nobody they pressingly need to evaluate. Willis should return after the Week 6 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 15-of-27 passes for 137 yards, one touchdown, two interceptions and a fumble in the Dolphins’ 31-24, Week 5 loss to the Bengals, adding eight rushes for 74 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis had a poor passing day, finishing the first quarter completing 0-of-4 passes. He threw a pair of second quarter interceptions to Jordan Battle, the first coming off a tip and the second on a cross-body throw and poor decision. He also fumbled and recovered a snap in the two-minute drill while a potential third interception was dropped in the endzone in the second half. Willis recovered with a touchdown throw to Kevin Coleman in the fourth quarter but fumbled deep in the Dolphins’ own territory late in the game. He capped off his day with a quick goal-line rushing score at the end of the game but it was too little, too late. Between his decision-making and lack of ball security, Willis had a poor game but good fantasy production due to his rushing output. Willis is a fantasy QB2 heading into a Week 6 Dolphins bye week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 9-of-17 passes for 85 yards in the Dolphins’ 10-15, Week 4 loss to the Vikings, adding two rushes for 11 yards and one fumble lost.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis’ biggest plays of the day are the ones that didn’t count. Willis rolled out of the pocket, escaping pressure, on the Dolphins’ third drive and hit Chris Bell downfield for what could have been a 68-yard touchdown. Unfortunately, the officials determined that the tiniest edge of Bell’s right cleat grazed the sideline pre-catch, during the scramble drill, negating the play altogether. Heartbreaking. Willis also had a 10-yard scramble called back due to holding on the Dolphins’ fifth drive. He attempted a running fadeaway pass 25 yards downfield to Bell on 3rd-and-8 on the Dolphins’ ninth drive, but the catch was contested and ultimately fell incomplete. He is a QB2 against the Bengals next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said increasing Malik Willis’ designed run rate will be discussed game by game, “when we need him to.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Hafley’s full quote is fairly non-committal. The first-year head coach was asked whether Willis could receive more designed rushes with De’Von Achane (knee) out for the year. Hafley said the game planning in that regard will “go game by game,” and be employed “situationally when we need him to.” For those hoping that Willis will consistently be involved in the run game, those outings could come, but the occurrences could be volatile. Willis remains a QB2 at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 20-of-36 passes for 210 yards and an interception in the Dolphins’ 24-10, Week 3 loss to the Dolphins, adding nine carries for 56 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis also lost a fumble late in the second quarter. Willis made some of his best throws of the season this afternoon, though the two turnovers were also his first of the year. He also missed impressive rookie Chris Bell on what could have been a pair long-ish touchdowns. He was at least running more after combining for just eight carries between Weeks 1 and 2. That is going to remain a must, especially now with De’Von Achane being waylaid with a serious knee injury. That will further change the face of this undermanned offense, and make things even harder for Willis in this no-win setup. Despite his intriguing young wideouts, he will be difficult to trust as a superflex option vs. the Vikings’ blitz-happy defense in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis completed 14-of-23 passes for 197 yards and one touchdown in a 35-13, Week 2 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis was also held to just six yards on the ground as the 49ers’ defensive line was in his face all game long. 77 of Willis’ 197 passing yards came on one busted coverage pass to Ryan Miller in garbage time against defensive backups. There was a belief that Willis would provide fantasy value because of his talent as a runner, but the Dolphins offense has been so bad through two games that we’d find it hard to recommend playing Willis outside of the deepest two quarterback leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Dolphins Malik Willis (toe) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis practiced in full all week, so his toe injury should not be an issue against the 49ers. The Dolphins’ quarterback told reporters this week that he is focused on taking fewer sacks moving forward. As his team fell farther behind on the scoreboard last week, Willis began holding onto the ball for far too long. Getting the ball out quickly or throwing on the run could help.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Dolphins QB Malik Willis said he knows he must take fewer sacks in Week 2 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis stood in the pocket, holding onto the ball too long when trailing the Raiders in the second half last week. He is currently nursing a toe injury, though scrambling faster, or at least throwing on the run, might help him achieve his new goal. Checking down to explosive RB De’Von Achane would also be smart, but the South Florida Sun-Sentinel’s David Furones instead highlighted Willis’ strong connection with rookie WR Caleb Douglas in his article on the subject. Getting the ball out of his hands quickly to either player would be a smart move. Willis’ Dolphins will likely be trailing often in the second half. Developing go-to responses to this situation would help out all involved for fantasy purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.headline: Malik Willis (toe) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malik-will.analysis: Willis popped up on the Dolphins’ injury report with a toe injury, though he was a full practice participant. This indicates the issue is minor enough for the 27-year-old to keep practicing at full strength. Note down Willis’ toe issue, but expect him to be back out there for Week 2 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: Darnell Mooney (neck) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: Mooney should be good to go this week, but he does not need to be on fantasy football rosters. Giants TE Theo Johnson (neck) was limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: Malachi Fields caught 2-of-8 targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: Fields saw a season-high eight targets, but caught just two of those passes for 19 yards. The Giants passing game behind Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely isn’t productive for fantasy purposes. Darnell Mooney had a carry for 20 yards while Charlie Jones caught 2-of-3 passes for 66 yards. Fields is the best option past Nabers and Likely, but he can be left on fantasy benches for Week 7 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: Darnell Mooney (neck) is not on New York’s final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: Mooney turned seven targets into 14 yards last week and does not need to be trusted to do better this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: Darnell Mooney (neck) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: Mooney’s participation puts him on track to face the Saints in Week 6. He does not need to be in 12-team lineups, and his presence, unfortunately, keeps Malachi Fields from potentially playing in a full-time role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: Darnell Mooney (neck) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: He still has multiple practices left to improve his status. If Mooney were to miss time, Malachi Fields, who is tied with him for third on the team in targets, could see his role expand, though target volume could be limited behind Isaiah Likely and Malik Nabers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: Darnell Mooney caught 2-of-3 targets for 26 yards in the Giants’ Week 3 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: Mooney has exactly two catches in each of his first three games as a Giant. He has hit on a few chunk plays in New York but isn’t seeing enough targets to be a weekly fantasy option. He is not on the FLEX radar for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: Darnell Mooney caught 2-of-3 targets for 48 yards in the Giants’ Week 2 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: Mooney played well behind Malik Nabers and rookie Malachi Fields but was able to cash in on a 33-yard reception to pad his counting stats in the loss. Fantasy managers of Nabers will want to track his status closely in the coming week after the talented youngster briefly departed with a shoulder injury. An absence could thrust Mooney into a near every-down role against the Titans in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: Malachi Fields caught 2-of-4 targets for 25 yards in the Giants’ Week 1 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: The rookie wide receiver showcased a polished all-around skillset, reinforcing offseason reports that he had locked down the WR2 role opposite Malik Nabers. His 6'4, 220-pound frame was on full display as he was continually utilized as both a down-blocker and blocker in the second level on runs, something that should allow him to continue to operate as the clear-cut WR2 for the Giants throughout his rookie campaign. That said, the box scores highlights the obvious distinction that his snap rate — he led all Giants wideouts with 50 — won’t always translate to fantasy production while playing alongside Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely, the latter two of whom commanded 17 targets on 29 Jaxson Dart pass attempts. The good news is that he played well ahead of veterans Darnell Mooney and Odell Beckham Jr., with Mooney having 39 snaps and Beckham just 11. Fantasy managers are best off viewing Fields as a high-end stash at the end of benches for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: North Jersey’s Art Stapleton believes Giants WR Darnell Mooney and WR Calvin Austin “will get chances” to compete for targets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: This is not much of an endorsement. With Giants WR Malik Nabers (knee) and WR Darius Slayton (core muscle) sidelined by recent surgeries, Mooney and Austin are reportedly earning targets behind TE Isaiah Likely and TE Theo Johnson at organized team activities. Mooney ($10 million) and Austin ($4.5 million) signed one-year deals with the Giants in free agency. Nothing Stapleton “saw today would indicate that there’s no room” for free agent WR Odell Beckham Jr. in this wide receiver group. Avoiding the Giants’ healthy wide receivers in spring drafts is a prudent call.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.headline: Giants agreed to terms with WR Darnell Mooney, formerly of the Falcons, on a one-year, $10 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-mo.analysis: This one is a bit head-scratching. Mooney’s skillset seems to carry significant overlap with returning veteran Darius Slayton, the latter of whom recently signed a new three-year deal that ties him to the franchise through 2027. Mooney did play from the slot at a 41% frequency a season ago and the team saw Wan’Dale Robinson walk in free agency, although Mooney will have to compete with veteran holdover Isaiah Hodgins and recent signee Calvin Austin for snaps inside, if that is the vision from the team. The size of the contract seems to indicate he will have a legitimate role in the offense in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.headline: Carson Schwesinger (ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.analysis: This is probably just a maintenance day for the Browns’ linebacker. Schwesinger resumed practicing last Friday and ended up playing in Week 6 against the Ravens. We expect to see him resume practicing tomorrow. The Browns face the Titans in Week 7. Browns DT Mason Graham (knee/ankle) was limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Quinshon Judkins (ankle) will work out pregame to determine his status for Week 6 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.analysis: Per Rapoport, there is optimism that linebacker Carson Schwesinger (ankle) will be able to play this week. Judkins logged a single limited practice on Friday before being listed as questionable. The fact that the Browns are even letting him test the groin injury in warmups suggests he will miss at most one game. If he doesn’t suit up, the Browns would be down to Jaleel McLaughlin and Audric Estime as their remaining options at running back. McLaughlin would be the better choice for fantasy managers, though this is largely a situation to avoid if possible.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.headline: Carson Schwesinger (ankle) is questionable for Cleveland’s Week 6 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.analysis: Schwesinger played through a high-ankle sprain last year, so we anticipate he’s more likely to be active than not after returning to practice today. The second-year star linebacker will likely attempt to power through against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.headline: Carson Schwesinger (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.analysis: Mason Graham is expected to miss multiple weeks with an ankle injury of his own and Maliek Collins missed today’s practice with a foot injury. That’s three front-seven starters potentially out for Week 6. With Lamar Jackson still banged up, expect the Ravens to give Derrick Henry all the touches he can handle this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Browns LB Carson Schwesinger is dealing with a Grade 1 ankle sprain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.analysis: Schwesinger has not been ruled out for Week 6’s game against the Ravens, and attempted to play through the injury at one point. With a big AFC North matchup on tap for this week, it wouldn’t be surprising if the Browns gave Schwesinger every opportunity to play. His practice status will be one to keep an eye on throughout the week. The 2025 Defensive Rookie of the Year has totaled 43 tackles, one sack, and one forced fumble this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.headline: Carson Schwesinger was named Defensive Rookie of the Year.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.analysis: Schwesinger notched 156 total tackles, 67 solo tackles, 2.5 sacks, 11 TFLs, three pass breakups and two interceptions despite missing Week 18 with a high-ankle sprain. It was an extremely impressive season for the No. 33 overall pick in last year’s draft.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.headline: Browns LB Carson Schwesinger (quad/ankle) won’t play in Cleveland’s Week 18 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.analysis: Schewsinger battled through 16 games despite an ankle injury and looks to be the favorite to walk away with the defensive rookie of the year award after posting 156 tackles, 2.5 sacks, and two interceptions in his inaugural season. Bengals running backs could operate a little more freely than usual in Week 18.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.headline: Browns LB Carson Schwesinger (ankle) is questionable for Week 10 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.analysis: Schwesinger suffered a high-ankle sprain in Week 8’s loss to the Patriots. The rookie linebacker avoided landing on injured reserve, but only managed to get on the field for one practice this week. The questionable designation may be a bit too optimistic for Schwesinger this week, but he’s clearly trending toward a return and could be good to go for Week 11 if not this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports tests confirmed a high-ankle sprain for Browns LB Carson Schwesinger.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.analysis: Now that we have the diagnosis, it’s safe to assume the rookie second-rounder is likely looking at a multi-week absence. Schwesinger has stepped in to make an immediate impact for the Browns’ defense this season, leading the team with 64 tackles while also tallying one interception, one sack, and four TFLs. The Browns are now entering their Week 9 bye. If they believe Schwesinger, who will be reevaluated after the bye , can return inside of the four-game minimum he would be required to miss on injured reserve, it’s possible they opt to keep him on the roster in hopes of a return in 2-3 weeks. Regardless, his loss is a massive one for a defensive unit that has been among the league’s best despite their 2-6 record.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.headline: Browns placed LB Jeremiah Owusu-Koramoah (neck) on the reserve/PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carson-sch.analysis: Owusu-Kormaoah reported to Browns offseason activities last month, but didn’t practice with the team after suffering a serious neck injury in Week 8 against the Ravens last season. The Browns released a statement saying that they “will not make any predictions on Jeremiah’s football future at this time.” Landing on the reserve/PUP list means that Owusu-Koramoah will miss the entire 2025 season. Second-round pick Carson Schwesigner would seem to have a chance to compete for a starting role in his rookie season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-goede.headline: Luke Goedeke (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-goede.analysis: The Bucs’ right tackle has not missed a snap this year. If he were to miss Week 7, Justin Skule would likely be the next man up. Goedeke has been an impressive pass protector this year, allowing seven pressures and zero sacks on 259 pass-pro reps. Losing him would be a notable blow to the team’s line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-goede.headline: Buccaneers restructured Luke Goedeke’s contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-goede.analysis: The Bucs converted $20 million of Goedeke’s roster bonus into a signing bonus to clear $15.2 million in cap space for 2026. The fourth-year lineman signed a four-year, $90 million contract extension last offseason and appeared in 11 games last season after a foot injury sidelined him for multiple weeks. Goedeke earned a PFF blocking grade of 75.8 last season and did not allow a sack despite giving up 22 pressures.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-goede.headline: Buccaneers designated RT Luke Goedeke (foot) for return from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-goede.analysis: The Buccaneers will have 21 days to activate Goedeke from injured reserve, so he’s not a lock to be rushed back by Week 10 when the Bucs face the Patriots. Goedeke is one of a handful of key players along the Buccaneers’ offensive line who have missed most of this season, but those who have filled in have done so nicely for Baker Mayfield and company. Goedeke allowed five pressures on the 46 pass blocking snaps he appeared on this season and has allowed nine sacks over the last two years.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-goede.headline: Buccaneers placed RT Luke Goedeke (foot) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-goede.analysis: Goedeke is expected to return later this season. He will be eligible to do so after missing four games. It’s a brutal development for a Buccaneers offensive line that also lost RG Cody Mauch to a season-ending knee injury. Buccaneers LT Tristan Wirfs (knee) has not yet suited up on game day. He remains limited in practice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-goede.headline: Bucs LT Tristan Wirfs (knee) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-goede.analysis: Wirfs was limited for the first two practices of Week 2 before being downgraded to a DNP on Saturday. He was then ruled out. The late-week DNP was part of their plan for his rehab from the knee injury, but it also means a limited practice on Wednesday doesn’t necessarily put him on track to suit up. Right tackle Luke Goedeke also missed Wednesday’s practice with a foot issue that knocked him out of Week 2’s win over the Texans. Right guard Cody Mauch missed today’s practice as well. It’s a nightmare runout for this offensive line. The cluster of injuries makes Baker Mayfield and the rest of the Bucs’ fantasy options slightly worse bets for Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-goede.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Buccaneers RT Luke Goedeke (foot) is expected to miss “multiple weeks.”
