https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-goede.analysis: Goedeke came into Week 2’s game with a foot injury that he had barely practiced on, then aggravated it in-game and Charlie Heck took over at right tackle. Heck would appear to be the backup plan for the Buccaneers for the forseeable future while Goedeke is out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-goede.headline: Luke Goedeke (foot) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-goede.analysis: Nine days after getting an extension, Tampa’s stalwart right tackle pops up on the injury report with a new injury. Coach Todd Bowles said he is “hopeful” Goedeke can play, and Goedeke did play all 58 snaps on Sunday. His absence would be huge for a line already missing Tristan Wirfs against a fearsome Texans front on Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-goede.headline: Buccaneers signed RT Luke Goedeke to a four-year, $90 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-goede.analysis: Goedeke was selected in the second round of the 2022 NFL Draft by the Bucs, becoming a key part of the offensive line. He started all 30 games that he played over the last two seasons and finished 2024 with a 76.4 PFF run-blocking grade, No. 18 amongst offensive tackles. Entering the final year of his rookie deal, Goedeke now gets an extension done and the Bucs get to keep a key piece of the offensive line for the foreseeable future. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the deal is worth $90 million over four years, with $50 million guaranteed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-goede.headline: Bucs RT Luke Goedeke (concussion) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-goede.analysis: Center Graham Barton (hamstring) has been ruled out. Goedeke has been out for a few weeks with a concussion. Head coach Todd Bowles said he will play, “barring any setbacks.” Overall, the Bucs are getting healthy ahead of their divisional matchup with the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-goede.headline: Buccaneers ruled out Trey Palmer (concussion) for Week 5 against the Falcons
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/luke-goede.analysis: The Buccaneers are without their Nos. 3 (Jalen McMillan) and 4 (Palmer) WRs this week, condensing the passing tree to star wide receivers, Mike Evans and Chris Godwin. T Luke Goedeke (concussion) was also ruled out this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: Sean Tucker (quad) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: Tucker should be back after missing Week 6’s loss to the Steelers. He doesn’t offer much fantasy value of his own, but he does occasionally plunder goal-line work from Bucky Irving. Expect him to be a thorn in Irving’s side again this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: Bucs declared RB Sean Tucker, DL DeMonte Capehart, OG Luke Haggard, QB Baker Mayfield, CB Benjamin Morrison, G Billy Schrauth, and S Antoine Winfield Jr. inactive for Week 6 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: Tucker has stolen the occasional goal line carry from Bucky Irving this year, though he only has eight attempts in total. His absence will move Irving up a spot or two in the RB2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Sean Tucker (quad) is not expected to play in Week 6 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: Despite seeing just eight total carries this year, Tucker has two attempts inside the five compared to one for Bucky Irving. Though he isn’t leaving that many total carries behind, Tucker’s absence will still create some extra fantasy value for Irving, who is on the RB1/2 border for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: FOX Sports’ Greg Auman reports that Sean Tucker (quad) will be a pregame decision for Week 6 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: Tucker is officially listed as questionable. If he ends up being inactive, that is good news for Bucky Irving, who handled 23 touches last week, ceding seven to Kenny Gainwell and five to Tucker. Irving warrants borderline RB1/2 treatment at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: Sean Tucker (quad) returned to practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: Tucker missed Wednesday’s session with a quad issue. He previously missed one game due to a hamstring injury. Tucker should be good to go for Week 6, though we don’t expect much fantasy production from the Bucs’ RB3. He has eight carries and zero catches over the past two weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: Sean Tucker rushed three times for 10 yards in the Bucs’ Week 4 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: Bucs OC Zac Robinson talked about getting Tucker the ball more earlier this week. Tucker entered this game with zero touches on offense. Though his role was limited, Robinson subbed him in where it counts the most and Tucker punched in a goal line score in the first half. He still doesn’t have much standalone fantasy value, but Tucker reclaiming the goal line role he had last year would be brutal for Bucky Irving’s fantasy outlook. Tucker is, at best, a touchdown-based RB5 for Week 5 versus Dallas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: Buccaneers OC Zac Robinson said game flow and productivity have limited RB Kenny Gainwell’s usage.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: The Buccaneers are 0-3, so if trailing game scripts aren’t the ideal setup for a receiving specialist, we aren’t sure what is. Robinson said he would like to get Gainwell more involved, but also added that Gainwell has to earn those reps by being more productive. Robinson said he also wants to get RB3 Sean Tucker more involved during the same presser. It sounds like this backfield still belongs to starting RB Bucky Irving, who is dealing with a glute injury, but changes are at least being considered.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: Buccaneers OC Zac Robinson said he wants to get RB Sean Tucker going.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: Robinson described Tucker as being “special with the ball in his hands,” and said that it’s on the coaching staff to find spots to mix him in. Whether this impacts starting RB Bucky Irving basically comes down to how and when — and if — the Buccaneers get Tucker involved. Taking a few snaps away from RB2 Kenneth Gainwell would be no big deal. Utilizing Tucker in the red zone would be consequential for Irving. Hopefully, Robinson provides more insight before his team’s Week 4 game against the Packers. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: Sean Tucker (hamstring) is active for Week 2 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: Tucker was out last week with the hamstring issue. His return to the Tampa lineup could take a few touches away from Bucky Irving and/or Kenneth Gainwell. Last week against the Bengals, Irving out-carried Gainwell 8-5 and led the backfield with a 59 percent route share. Bucs declared CB Jacob Parrish, CB Ayden Garnes, DL Elijah Simmons, DL DeMonta Capehart, OL Billy Schrauth, and OL Luke Haggard inactive for Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.headline: Buccaneers RB Sean Tucker (hamstring) is practicing in full for Week 2 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-tucke.analysis: The Buccaneers should have their RB3 on hand against the Browns this weekend, though Tucker is not expected to contribute in a fantasy-relevant manner. He is just a deep-league bench stash at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Patriots ruled out Carlton Davis (neck) for Week 7 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: The Patriots will also be without their top-two backup CBs, Karon Prunty (hamstring) and Channing Canada (hamstring). The Patriots listed S Kevin Byard (chest), S Craig Woodson (shoulder) and LB Christian Elliss (chest) as questionable. This is good news for the Bears’ passing attack.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Patriots CB Carlton Davis (neck) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: It was an upgrade from an estimated Monday DNP. Davis has missed Week 2, Week 3, Week 5 and Week 6 to the neck listing so far. Perhaps he’ll try to give it a go on Thursday night, but we’d be surprised if he did better than a questionable tag on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: Gonzalez has not played since Week 3, but he returns in time to cover Garrett Wilson in a divisional showdown. Gonzalez primarily lines up on the perimeter, but he has taken 15 combined snaps in the slot and in the box. He could take a few reps on the inside this week, but perimeter CB2 Carlton Davis (neck) is out, so Gonzalez could be asked to simply stay out wide.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez will not play in New England’s Week 5 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: He has not practiced or played since Week 3. Nothing we’ve seen has suggested he’ll be a Saturday IR candidate, but it also wouldn’t necessarily be surprising if that happened. The Pats also ruled out fellow starting CB Carlton Davis (neck) for Week 5, leaving non-existent Raiders receivers with matchup upgrades. (Cody White is about to touch the end zone paint again.)

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: Gonzalez and fellow starting perimeter CB Carlton Davis (neck) have missed each of the Patriots’ first two practices this week, putting them on the wrong side of questionable for Week 5 against the Raiders. Las Vegas lines up Brock Bowers as a wide receiver most of the time. Missing both starting coverage defenders would make life tough on the defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Patriots CB Christian Gonzalez (shoulder) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: Gonzalez has been sidelined with a shoulder injury since last week, missing the Patriots’ Week 4 win over the Bills. Also not practicing were Carlton Davis (neck) and Karon Prunty (hamstring). We’ll see if any of these corners can practice enough to play for Week 5, but Raiders WR Tre Tucker is headed for a good matchup against a banged up Patriots secondary this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Patriots CB Carlton Davis (neck) is inactive for Week 2 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: Davis did not practice all week due to a neck injury and was officially ruled out on Saturday. The Patriots will look for reinforcements in the secondary for Week 2 against the Steelers. Also inactive for the Patriots are OT Dametrious Crownover, OT Walter Rouse, TE Tanner Arkin, DT Leonard Taylor, and QB Behren Morton.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Patriots downgraded CB Carlton Davis (neck) to out for Week 2 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: Davis was unable to practice all week with a neck injury and will ultimately be held out of the team’s Week 2 game against the Steelers. Pittsburgh will be without starting wide receiver Michael Pittman, so it will be interesting how the Patriots choose to deploy Christian Gonzalez. Gonzalez could find himself in shadow coverage of opposing alpha DK Metcalf.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Patriots CB Carlton Davis (neck) is questionable to play in Week 2 against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: Davis did not practice at all this week. He is seemingly a long shot to suit up. The Patriots also listed EDGE Dre’Mont Jones (foot) after three limited practices.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.headline: Patriots CB Carlton Davis (neck) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/carlton-da.analysis: Neck injuries are concerning. Davis is seemingly in jeopardy of missing his team’s Week 2 game against the Steelers. Hopefully, this is only a minor issue for the veteran cornerback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-jack.headline: Jonah Jackson (hip/quad) is not on the final injury report for Week 7 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-jack.analysis: This is great news. Jackson is one of the best guards in football. Bears LB T.J. Edwards (hamstring) is doubtful, Jack Sanborn (concussion) has been ruled out, and CB Tyrique Stevenson (hip) is questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-jack.headline: Jonah Jackson (hip/quad) was limited in Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-jack.analysis: Jackson left Sunday’s game with the injury, playing 64.9 percent of the snaps with Luke Newman spelling him. This is a good sign for his availability for Week 7 after Jackson did not practice on Monday, but he’s likely trending towards a questionable tag without a full listing on Wednesday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-jack.headline: Bears LG Joe Thuney (pectoral) is not on Chicago’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-jack.analysis: Nor are Darnell Wright (ankle) or Jonah Jackson (ankle), as all three got in two sessions after a Wednesday DNP. It seems like all three just got a maintenance day. The Bears line will be in good shape this week against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-jack.headline: Bears LG Joe Thuney (pectoral) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-jack.analysis: Bears RG Jonah Jackson (ankle) and RT Darnell Wright (ankle) also sat out. Starting LT Braxton Jones (knee) is currently on injured reserve. This unit is worth watching this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-jack.headline: Bears signed OG Jonah Jackson to a one-year contract extension through 2027.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-jack.analysis: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports that the Bears increased Jackson’s 2026 base salary guarantees to $7 million, with "$5.25 million more for injury.” He will also get “all $17.5 million he was slated to earn this season in the deal he [previously] signed with the Rams.” Sounds like a pretty hefty bag for a guy who played 267 snaps last year, but it’s not our money.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-jack.headline: Rams traded LG Jonah Jackson to the Bears in exchange for a 2025 sixth-round draft pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-jack.analysis: Jackson had been given permission to seek a trade after signing a three-year deal worth $51 million last offseason. Jackson started one game at center for the Rams after missing the first eight weeks of the regular season with a nagging shoulder injury. In Chicago, Jackson will join an offensive line graded by Pro Football Focus as last year’s eighth best pass blocking unit. He’ll rejoin Ben Johnson, who was Detroit’s offensive coordinator when Jackson played for the Lions in 2021. The Athletic’s Jourdan Rodrigue reports the Bears will take on Jackson’s salary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-jack.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Rams have given LG Jonah Jackson permission to seek a trade.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-jack.analysis: Jackson signed a three-year, $51 million contract with the Rams last offseason after spending the first four years of his career in Detroit. He suffered a shoulder injury before the season and re-aggravated it early in the year, causing him to miss roughly two months. Jackson started one game at center upon returning but was benched for the remainder of the season, save for a Week 18 start at right guard. The Rams can save $9 million in cap space by cutting him with a post-June 1 designation this offseason. Jackson, wanting to play out his current contract, is now searching for a team willing to foot the bill.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-jack.headline: Rams activated OL Jonah Jackson (shoulder) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-jack.analysis: He’ll likely be in the starting lineup as the Rams finally get some of their opening day offensive line back for Monday night’s matchup against the Dolphins. Jackson aggravated a shoulder injury in Week 2 and has been out for nearly two months. Jackson started out at center for the Rams, then moved to guard in Week 2 before leaving.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-jack.headline: Rams G Jonah Jackson (shoulder) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-jack.analysis: The Rams’ offensive line is quietly trending toward a midseason turnaround after operating as one of the league’s worst units early on. Hopefully, Jackson can stack another full practice on Saturday and suit up for the first time since Week 2. Fellow OL Steve Avila (knee) likewise practiced in full on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-jack.headline: Rams opened LG Jonah Jackson’s 21-day practice window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jonah-jack.analysis: In addition to Jackson, the Rams also opened the return window for center Steve Avila. Both players will be eligible to come off injured reserve at any time and would provide immediate boosts to an offensive line that’s ranked 31st in PFF pass-blocking grades and 15th in PFF run-blocking grades. Jackson has been on injured reserve since reaggravating a shoulder injury in Week 2 that he dealt with throughout training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.headline: AJ Dillon (ankle) returned to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.analysis: Dillon didn’t practice last week and was ruled out on Friday. He should be good for Week 7, barring a setback in practice. Dillon will back up Chuba Hubbard, though Trevor Etienne could also see a few snaps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.headline: AJ Dillon (ankle) will not play in Carolina’s Week 6 game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.analysis: He didn’t practice all week. With Jonathon Brooks also out, it seems likely that Trevor Etienne will be activated to serve as Chuba Hubbard’s main backup. Hubbard will project to get most of the volume here and has stumbled into high-end RB2 value this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.headline: Trevor Etienne (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.analysis: The Panthers’ backup running back is on track to return this week against the Eagles, while fellow backup A.J. Dillon (ankle) may need more time off. Dillon was unable to practice at all today. Etienne can be stashed in 12-team formats, though he may only qualify as FLEX-viable if he were to get a fill-in start at some point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.headline: AJ Dillon rushed four times for 16 yards in the Panthers’ Week 3 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.analysis: With Jonathon Brooks joining Trevor Etienne on injured reserve, Dillon was indeed the Panthers’ No. 2 back behind Chuba Hubbard. Good for him, though Pro Football Focus charted him with zero first half snaps. Were Hubbard to ever go down with injury, Dillion would form some sort of committee with a practice squad elevation or free agent addition.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.headline: ESPN’s Mike Kaye believes AJ Dillon could spell Chuba Hubbard on “obvious passing downs” in Week 3.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.analysis: Dillon will step into the main backup role for Week 3 after Jonathon Brooks (groin) wound up on injured reserve. There’s no real timeshare here; Hubbard will be the main back. But Dillon could cut into PPR point territory as Panthers OC Brad Idzik was described as “pleasantly surprised” by the veteran’s receiving ability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.headline: Panthers signed AJ Dillon, formerly of the Eagles, to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.analysis: Dillon missed all of the 2024 season while recovering from a neck injury he suffered late in the previous year. He returned in 2025 on a one-year deal with the Eagles. Dillon appeared in the first six games of the year but eventually fell off the game-day roster with Philly’s addition of Tank Bigsby. He finished the season with 12 carries for 60 yards. Dillon will be fighting for a roster spot in Carolina during training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.headline: Eagles declared RB A.J. Dillon, CB Mac McWilliams OL Drew Kendall TE Grant Calcaterra and QB Sam Howell inactive for Philadelphia’s Week 7 game against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.analysis: Will Shipley will assume second RB duties, with Tank Bigsby perhaps working in more on offense after the mini-bye. Active for the Eagles are OL Landon Dickerson (ankle) and DT Jalen Carter (heel), the latter of whom was questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.headline: Eagles listed Saquon Barkley (knee) as DNP on Monday’s estimated injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.analysis: It’s only an estimated report, but an estimated DNP is still concerning for Barkley, who has struggled on the ground to start the season. We’ll see if things change come Tuesday when the Eagles actually hold a practice, but this is clearly something worth monitoring until we receive word that Barkley is in the clear for Thursday night’s game against the Giants. If Barkley is unable to go, A.J. Dillon could be in line to handle early-down touches while Will Shipley mixes in on passing downs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.headline: Eagles RB Will Shipley (oblique) will not play in Philadelphia’s Week 2 game against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.analysis: Shipley didn’t practice all week with his “oblique” injury (reports are that he is dealing with fractured ribs) and is a candidate to be placed on injured reserve on Saturday. Tank Bigsby will take Shipley’s role in the offense, although it is possible that AJ Dillon gets more snaps as the Eagles figure out how they want to implement the newly-acquired Bigsby.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.headline: A.J. Dillon rushed five time for 27 yards and caught 3-of-3 targets for 27 yards in the Eagles’ preseason Week 1 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aj-dillon/.analysis: Dillon forced one missed tackle along the way. Reports have suggested that Dillon is playing well as a pass catcher, and his preseason showing reflected that. He appears to be in the hunt for the No. 2 job.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young (knee) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: It’s the first time we’ve seen Young o the injury report with this knee issue, though a full practice today is nothing to worry about. He will be good to go for his date with the Bucs. Young is currently the QB4 by fantasy points per game. Even if he does cool down this week, Young should be in most starting fantasy lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young completed 20-of-39 passes for 281 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers’ 25-14, Week 6 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: This game was never quite as easy as many thought it would be given Philadelphia’s injuries. Young looked pretty good, but he was often under pressure, and the Panthers continued to make things harder on themselves with 13 penalties for 149 yards. A few of those really killed the momentum on some Panthers drives. Still, Young made enough big throws and receivers were schemed open into space repeatedly throughout the day. We’d expect that to continue next week against a Bucs defense that might not be as talented as this Eagles one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young completed 29-of-41 passes for 329 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers’ Week 4 win over the Lions, adding three yards on three carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: The NFL’s passing leader through four weeks, pending Monday Night Football, took complete advantage of a defense still working to find their identity through the first month of play, leaning on his top option in Tetairoa McMillan throughout. Young now leads the league in passing and can only be caught by Tyler Shough on Monday Night Football, while only Kirk Cousins and Brock Purdy have more touchdown passes than Young’s nine. Even more impressive was the fact that he did what he did to the Lions without two of his top three receivers with both Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette out of action in Week 4. Young and the Panthers head to their Week 5 bye at 2-2 and alone atop the NFC South, soon to be joined by the winner on Monday night. He’ll be a legitimate QB1 when he returns to action against the Eagles in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Panthers QB Bryce Young (knee) is practicing in full for Week 4 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Young visited the blue medical tent a couple of times after taking a cleat to the knee in Week 3 against the Browns. He reportedly underwent imaging to assess the injury. We never received an official follow-up report, but he is practicing in full already, so the imaging evidently checked out just fine. After years of frustrating performances, Young is suddenly a low-end QB1 against an injury-impacted Lions pass defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Panthers coach Dave Canales said Bryce Young (leg) will undergo imaging “just to make sure” on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Canales didn’t want to get specific about Young’s status after he took a cleat to the leg, but deferred also to the idea of “other things.” It’s never incredible news to be looking down the barrel of imaging, but Young was able to return and play through the injury on Sunday and this has the feel of an “out of an abundance of concern” test for the 25-year-old quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young completed 26-of-48 passes for 291 yards, one touchdown and an interception in the Panthers’ 21-18, Week 3 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Young was also in and out of the blue tent with a “lower-body injury” head coach Dave Canales said was affecting the power on some of his throws. That does not include his game-sealing interception, which was a batted pass around the 0:10 mark as a timeout-less Panthers offense desperately drove for what would have been a game-tying field goal. It was a day of adversity on the road, as Young also lost Jalen Coker to a quad injury after the wideout entered the proceedings with an ankle issue. That was one reason Young was spreading the ball around to fantasy nonentities like Brycen Tremayne and Mitchell Evans. The Browns put the clamps on Tetairoa McMillan. Today was probably an inevitable correction to Young’s sizzling start, though the volume is still what fantasy managers are looking for. He has a bounce-back Week 4 spot in the defense-less Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young completed 23-of-36 passes for 287 yards and three touchdowns in the Panthers’ 34-3, Week 2 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Young got off to a slow start with just one touchdown on his first five drives. He found Xavier Legette for a 55-yard completion just before halftime, setting up an eventual strike to Darren Waller for six. Young rode the momentum into the third quarter and found Waller in the end zone once again coming out of halftime. That alone was enough to seal the game, and Young even got to take some time off in the fourth quarter. Young pushed the ball downfield with ease, just like he did in last week’s shootout with the Bears. While the passing volume may come down at some point, Young looks like a different quarterback in year four. He is moving up the QB2 ranks heading into his Week 3 date with the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Bryce Young completed 23-of-37 attempts for 361 yards, three touchdowns, and one interceptions in the Panthers’ Week 1 loss to the Bears, adding two rushes for ten yards and one touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: It was the fourth 300-yard outing of Young’s NFL career and it came in a wild back-and-forth affair with a Chicago offense that did whatever it wanted to against a pathetic Carolina defense. The Panthers had to abandon their run-heavy offense in the first half, leading to 44 Young drop backs. Young targeted Jalen Coker relentlessly and connected with Coker for two touchdowns — one of them in garbage time. Young, who was seven percent above his expected completion rate, made a handful of impressive throws under duress and found his way into the end zone on a short rush in the first half. Young will be a premiere streaming option in Week 2 against a middling Atlanta defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports that the Panthers will “likely” decide whether to offer QB Bryce Young an extension in the 2027 offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Young has two years remaining on his contract, but is currently eligible for an extension. According to Wolfe, Young needs to improve in three areas. First, Young must check down when it’s the responsible thing to do, in turn elevating his completion rate to the “high 60s, low 70s” range. Second, Young must be comfortable playing with tempo and diverse personnel formations, including WR Tetairoa McMillan lining up in the slot more often. Third, Young must play quickly and decisively. Whether he can accomplish these feats is up in the air. He’s a mid-to-low QB2 for fantasy purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.headline: Panthers owner David Tepper declined to say whether the front office offered QB Bryce Young an extension this offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bryce-youn.analysis: Reporters first asked whether Young had received an offer from the team. Tepper passed on answering. A reporter then asked what would prompt the team to offer Young an extension. Tepper initially declined to answer once again, before adding, “but look, success is success. And you know it when you see it.” Anything is possible, but given those remarks, it seems plausible that no offer was made. The Panthers picked up Young’s fifth-year team option in April, keeping the 25-year-old quarterback under contract through 2027. This could be a make-or-break year for him as the starter, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Dont’e Thornton (hamstring) has “got to go show us something” in the final week of his 21-day practice window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: This is rough. Currently on injured reserve, Thornton began practicing in Week 5, activating his 21-day practice window. The young wide receiver told reporters that he was “overly confident” in his hamstring and is “ready to play.” Two weeks later, the team has not yet officially removed him from injured reserve. Per Kubiak, Thornton “had a good first week, had a good second week,” but he still has to go “out there to practice to show us that he’s ready.” He’s been practicing in full for two weeks. The fact that the wide receiver-needy Raiders have not yet activated him is not encouraging. Thornton does not need to be stashed in 12-team leagues at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Dont’e Thornton Jr. (hamstring) is getting “closer” but won’t play in Las Vegas’ Week 6 game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: Thornton is in Week 2 of his 21-day window and figures to return in Week 7 or Week 8. Obviously there’s not much reason to trust him in fantasy at this time, but he may find a real role on Las Vegas’ depth chart.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders ruled out Dont’e Thornton (hamstring) for Week 5 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: The Raiders activated Thornton’s 21-day practice window this week. Despite the young wide receiver saying he feels “ready to play,” the team has determined that he needs more time. With Jalen Nailor (concussion) also ruled out, Cody White (ankle) and Malik Benson will round out three-wide receiver sets behind Tre Tucker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders WR Dont’e Thornton (hamstring) returned to practice and feels “ready to play.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: Thornton has been on injured reserve since late August, practicing in full for the first time on Wednesday. He told Raiders media that he is “overly confident” in his hamstring and is “ready to play.” With Jack Bech on injured reserve, there is room for the 23-year-old speedster to earn targets if he plays in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said it’s too early to say whether WR Dont’e Thornton Jr. (undisclosed) will resume practicing next week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: The lanky speedster was placed on injured reserve late in August. He is not exceptionally talented, but he can contribute meaningfully to an NFL offense. Getting him back would help keep safeties honest. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders placed WR Dont’e Thornton Jr. on the reserved/injured list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: Thornton has been dealing with an undisclosed injury that has prevented the wideout from practicing over the last month. The 23-year-old can return in four weeks, but there’s no timeline as to when the 2025 fourth-round pick will return to the Vegas lineup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders HC Klint Kubiak said Dont’e Thornton is still working his way back from an undisclosed injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: We still don’t know what Thornton is dealing with, but the second-year receiver hasn’t practiced since August 7th. Kubiak said earlier this month that he expected Thornton to return sometime during the preseason, but that didn’t come to fruition. Even if he’s able to make it back on the practice field ahead of Week 1, Thornton is unlikely to make any major contributions to the offense at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders HC Klint Kubiak said he expects Dont’e Thornton (undisclosed) to return at some point in the preseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: Thornton has missed nearly a whole week of practice, paving the way for Jack Bech and rookie Malik Benson to see more reps. Kubiak said Thornton has “been banged up a little bit” this training camp, but did not go into further detail on his situation. Thornton caught 10 passes for 135 scoreless yards last season after generating plenty of camp hype. He is not on the fantasy radar at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders WR Dont’e Thornton (undisclosed) missed his fourth straight practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: Thornton was at practice in street clothes Tuesday, missing his fourth straight. He left a training camp practice early last week and has not received a diagnosis or return timetable. Jack Bech, Jalen Nailor, and Tre Tucker are listed as the Raiders’ starting wide receivers on the team’s first unofficial depth chart of the preseason. Thornton is listed as Nailor’s backup but may be losing ground to Malik Benson as he misses time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.headline: Raiders WR Malik Benson operated as the team’s WR2 with WR Jalen Nailor and WR Dont’e Thornton “nicked up” on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/donte-thornton.analysis: The depth chart placement is a tad curious because it suggests Benson ran ahead of either WR Tre Tucker or WR Jack Bech. Benson has been rotating in with the first-team offense for more than a week, so this isn’t groundbreaking news, but one wonders if he can use the opportunity to make a compelling case for a starting role in three-wide receiver sets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-wilk.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports the Commander hired Steve Wilks “to work with the defensive coaches.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-wilk.analysis: Wilks won’t be with the Commanders on game days and the team will likely consider him an advisor. Per Garafolo, the decision to hire Wilks was made a month ago and he joined the staff last week. Wilks had been serving as a special assistant at Appalachian State. His last stint in the NFL was as the Jets’ defensive coordinator in 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-wilk.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports a court ruled that discrimination cases filed against the NFL by Brian Flores, Steve Wilks, and Ray Horton “now can proceed in open court.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-wilk.analysis: In the decision, the court writes that “an arbitration forum in which the defendant’s (NFL’s) own chief executive gets to decide the case would strip employees of their rights under the law,” while adding that “it is long overdue for the NFL to recognize this and finally provide a fair, neutral and transparent forum for these issues to be addressed.” Flores first filed a class-action lawsuit against the NFL, the Dolphins, Giants, and Broncos, for conducting “sham” interviews with him in 2022 to satisfy the league’s hiring rules. Wilks and Horton later add their names to the complaint and named the Cardinals and Titans. Should this head to open court, a trial would likely be set to take place where both sides will be heard before a jury ultimately decides if the league discriminated against Flores, Wilks, and Horton during various interview processes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-wilk.headline: Jets fired DC Steve Wilks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-wilk.analysis: A 48-20 loss to the Jaguars was the final straw for Wilks, whose defense entered the day ranked in the bottom five in EPA per play entering the day and had allowed six 30-plus point performances on the year. Another indictment of Wilks is the fact that his defense has yet to force an interception through the first 15 weeks of the season. Life got harder following this year’s trade deadline, when the Jets dealt stars Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams away for future draft picks, but Sunday’s loss to the Jaguars set a new low for the season. Wilks hasn’t spent more than one season with a team since his first stint with the Panthers, which lasted from 2012 to 2017. The long-time defensive coordinator who helped lead a top-five 49ers defense in 2023 could find a new home next offseason, but this latest stop left much to be desired. Defensive backs coach/passing game coordinator Chris Harris will takeover as interim DC for the final three weeks of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-wilk.headline: Jets hired former 49ers defensive coordinator Steve Wilks as their new defensive coordinator.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-wilk.analysis: The Jets interviewed Wilks on Wednesday and agreed to terms with him to be their new defensive coordinator. He last coached in the NFL as the 49ers’ defensive coordinator in 2023, spending time with the Panthers and Browns after becoming a one-and-done head coach with the Cardinals in 2018. He was also Missouri’s defensive coordinator in 2021 and served as a volunteer advisor for Charlotte in 2024. Newly hired Jets head coach Aaron Glenn will not be calling defensive plays, so Wilks’ role will be that of a play-caller to begin his Jets tenure.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-wilk.headline: FOX Sports’ Jordan Schultz reports the Jets are interviewing former 49ers DC Steve Wilks for their defensive coordinator vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-wilk.analysis: As Schultz notes, new head coach Aaron Glenn will not be calling plays on defense, putting extra emphasis on the defensive coordinator job in New York. Wilks last coached in 2024, serving as the 49ers’ defensive coordinator. He was fired after a single season despite San Francisco making the Super Bowl. Wilks also interviewed for defensive coordinator openings with the Colts and Falcons this offseason, though both positions have since been filled.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-wilk.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Falcons will interview former 49ers DC Steve Wilks for their defensive coordinator vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-wilk.analysis: Wilks has been coaching in some capacity for 20 years with his time in the NFL dating back as far as 2006. He most recently served as the 49ers’ defensive coordinator. Wilks held the gig for one year and was fired after the team’s Super Bowl loss to Kansas City. Atlanta is helmed by Raheem Morris, who also has some Shanahn routes. Morris coached under Mike Shanahan in Washington. The familiarity makes him a strong candidate to be the Falcons’ next defensive coordinator. Wilks also interviewed with the Colts for the same position.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-wilk.headline: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports the Colts will interview Steve Wilks for their defensive coordinator vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-wilk.analysis: Wilks and former Bengals defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo are both scheduled to meet with the Colts next week. Wilks served one season as the 49ers defensive coordinator in 2023 but has held countless positions around the league, with his first NFL role coming in 2006 as the Bears defensive backs coach. In his lone season with the 49ers, Wilks’ defense ranked third in points allowed and was eighth in yards allowed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-wilk.headline: 49ers fired defensive coordinator Steve Wilks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-wilk.analysis: Shanahan scheduled a surprise press conference to announce the news earlier today. The move comes as a bit of a surprise given how well San Francisco’s defense played in Wilks’ first and only season as the defensive coordinator. The 49ers finished the regular season ranked third in points allowed and 10th in EPA per play allowed. Shanahan also said he did not expect any moves within the coaching ranks as recently as Monday, though he noted that he hadn’t talked to any of his staff members about the matter yet. Though the 49ers’ defense arguably came up short in the Super Bowl, they held Patrick Mahomes to 19 points in regulation. Shanahan notably called a timeout late in overtime, seemingly to switch a defensive play called by Wilks. Even if Shanahan didn’t like Wilks’ calls on defense, the move feels more akin to making Wilks the scapegoat for the loss than anything else. San Francisco will now have to hire a third defensive coordinator in as many years. Wilks, who got multiple head coaching interviews during the playoffs, should be able to quickly land another job in the NFL.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-wilk.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports the Falcons have requested an interview with 49ers DC Steve Wilks regarding their head coaching vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-wilk.analysis: The Chargers put in a request to speak with Wilks earlier in the week, but they’ll now have competition as the Falcons have also thrown their hat into the ring. The long-time defensive coordinator joined the 49ers last offseason after being passed on for the Panthers’ head coaching gig despite a 6-6 record as their interim coach during the 2022 season. Wilks was one-and-done as a head coach with the Cardinals in 2018 but has received multiple endorsements across the league as a high-end head coaching candidate. It’s possible more teams target Wilks in the coming days as we’re still early into the coaching cycle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-wilk.headline: Chargers request to interview 49ers DC Steve Wilks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/steve-wilk.analysis: There is no shortage of vacant head coach positions this year, and there are few assistants more qualified than Wilks. In what seems like a yearly tradition, Wilks could be yet another San Francisco assistant to depart in the offseason for a head coaching job.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian Darrisaw (concussion) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Darrisaw suffered a concussion in Week 4 against the Dolphins and was unable to play in Week 5 against the Saints. The Vikings were on bye in Week 6, giving him more than two weeks to get ready for Week 7. We expect to see him practicing fully this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Vikings LT Christian Darrisaw (concussion) will not play in Minnesota’s Week 5 game against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: He did not practice all week with the concussion. Brian O’Neill is questionable. Ryan Van Demark will likely play left tackle for Darrisaw, while 2026 third-rounder Caleb Tiernan is the likely reserve if O’Neill can’t go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Vikings LT Christian Darrisaw (concussion) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Darrisaw is on the wrong side of questionable, having logged consecutive absences to begin Week 5. With Vikings LG Donovan Jackson (knee) out, Kyler Murray could be looking over his shoulder quite often against the Saints this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said LT Christian Darrisaw (concussion) will not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: O’Connell also said that RT Brian O’Neill (undisclosed) will be limited. The Vikings recently placed LG Donovan Jackson (knee) on injured reserve. The offensive line is very banged up at the moment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Vikings coach Kevin O’Connell said LT Christian Darrisaw cleared the NFL’s concussion protocol in Week 4 against the Dolphins, but later experienced symptoms.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Darrisaw was in and out of the Vikings’ Week 4 win over the Dolphins. Now, we know why. The Vikings’ left tackle will have to clear it in order for him to play in Week 5 against the Saints. Vikings LG Donovan Jackson was forced from the game with a knee injury. This line is ailing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Vikings LT Christian Darrisaw (knee) said he feels “the best” he has felt in two years.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Darrisaw suffered a multi-ligament tear in his left knee in October 2024 and struggled in his return last year. He told reporters today that he thinks he “turned the corner this offseason.” The Vikings plan to give him regular rest days during training camp and the regular season, but he believes he is on track to be a full-time player once again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Vikings restructured WR Justin Jefferson’s contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: This comes from NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero. In hopes of getting under the cap before the start of the new league year, the Vikings will restructure the deals of both Jefferson and LT Christian Darrisaw, likely by converting portions of their base salaries into guaranteed money. The Vikings rank last in the league in available cap space, per OverTheCap.com, and will likely restructure a few more deals in the coming days to get to a point where they have money to spend in free agency.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Vikings placed LT Christian Darrisaw (knee) on injured reserve
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Darrisaw tore his left ACL and MCL in October 2024. He retook the field for the first time in Week 3 this season, following the injury, but the knee continued to bother him. He allowed 18 quarterback pressures in 10 games this season. Hopefully, he can put the knee injury behind him with another offseason of rest and rehab.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Vikings C Ryan Kelly (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: As was Brian O’Neill (heel), both upgrades from a Wednesday DNP. Christian Darrisaw (knee) remains sidelined. Still, this is a good update for anyone considering playing a Viking against New York’s woeful defense on Sunday. Most of the offensive line is trending towards being up for this contest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Vikings LT Christian Darrisaw (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Darrisaw has been in and out of the lineup because of the knee issue this year. With the Vikings officially eliminated from the playoff hunt, he may have played his last snap of the season. Head coach Kevin O’Connell said both Justin Skule and Blake Brandel will get reps at left tackle in practice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.headline: Texans placed Jawhar Jordan on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.analysis: Jordan was elevated from the practice squad over the weekend and backed up Woody Marks on Sunday. He ran six times for 43 yards and a score. His 25-yard touchdown run was the Texans’ longest rush attempt of the season. The team hasn’t disclosed Jordan’s injury yet, but he will miss at least four games while on IR. Dare Ogunbowale will serve as Houston’s RB2 until David Montgomery is healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.headline: Jawhar Jordan rushed six times for 43 yards and a touchdown in Houston’s Week 6 win over the Jaguars, adding a seven-yard reception on his only target.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.analysis: Jordan had a huge cutback lane in the third quarter and took it 25 yards while breaking a Jarrian Jones tackle for his touchdown. He played just 14-of-63 snaps, but clearly brought more juice than Woody Marks in the run game and it wouldn’t be a total surprise if that total grew next week with David Montgomery (groin) expected to remain sidelined. Jordan is likely just a FLEX play against the Giants in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.headline: Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said Jawhar Jordan will be elevated off the practice squad to play against the Jaguars on Sunday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.analysis: Though he’s nominally the third back with David Montgomery out, the Texans tipped how they felt about Dare Ogunbowale as a running back by not using him a single time after Montgomery was ruled out against the Titans in Week 5. It seems likely that Jordan will be the main Woody Marks change-up in London, though given how poorly the Texans have ran the ball this year that probably doesn’t equate to much fantasy equity.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.headline: Texans RB Jawhar Jordan (ankle) was removed from the injury report and will play in the Divisional Round against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.analysis: Jordan practiced fully on Friday, which is a great sign. He was unable to play in the Wild Card Round after injuring his ankle in Week 18. We expect Jordan to handle No. 2 rushing duties behind starting RB Woody Marks, though Marks could ultimately dominate touches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.headline: Texans RB Jawhar Jordan (ankle) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.analysis: Two sessions would seemingly give him a real chance to suit up, though it’s unclear if the Texans would make him the No. 2 back ahead of Nick Chubb after Chubb’s output against the Steelers last Monday night. Jordan is probably trending towards a questionable tag on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.headline: Texans RB Jawhar Jordan (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.analysis: Jordan suffered an ankle injury in Week 18 which caused him to miss the Wild Card win over the Steelers. The 26-year-old played well in a reserve role and was the Texans’ RB2 in Week 18 with Nick Chubb a healthy scratch. A limited practice session early in the week indicates Jordan is trending to return in the Divisional Round against the Patriots, though the Texans may keep both Jordan and Chubb active behind Woody Marks if Jordan is not fully healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.headline: Texans ruled out RB Jawhar Jordan (ankle) for the Wildcard Round against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.analysis: Jordan injured his ankle in Week 18 and failed to practice all week, eventually ruled out with the ailment. That leaves very little depth behind starting rookie Woody Marks, who could find himself in a workhorse role for the team’s Wildcard matchup against the Steelers. Nick Chubb appears likely to operate as the primary change of pace option while Dare Ogunbowale could rotate in on obvious passing situations.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.headline: Texans RB Jawhar Jordan (ankle) did not practice Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.analysis: He looks incredibly unlikely to go based on the reporting that he suffered a high-ankle sprain in Week 18. Nick Chubb will probably be a pure fill-in back on a few downs for the Texans behind Woody Marks on Monday night, making Marks a high-volume play for DFS or Playoff Best Ball purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.headline: Texans RB Jawhar Jordan (ankle) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.analysis: NBC Sports Houston’s Aaron Wilson reported this morning that testing confirms Jordan suffered a high-ankle sprain in Week 18 against the Colts. He was unsurprisingly unable to practice on Thursday. The Texans face the Steelers on Monday. Veteran RB Nick Chubb would get his old job back as the team’s No. 2 rusher if Jordan cannot play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.headline: Jawhar Jordan rushed five times for three yards in the Texans’ Week 18 win over the Colts
https://www.nbcsports.com/jawhar-jordan/.analysis: The more noteworthy bit is that Jordan played ahead of Nick Chubb, who was a healthy scratch in Week 18. Jordan could wind up being Houston’s No. 2 back in the playoffs. He’s more of an outside zone specialist than someone the Texans trust all the time, but Jordan undoubtedly has more physical upside than Chubb at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/vita-vea/5.headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano believes Vita Vea could be traded before the NFL’s trade deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/vita-vea/5.analysis: With the Bucs’ 2026 season circling the drain, Vea, 31, could be dealt in the coming weeks to a contending team looking to beef up their defensive line for a second half run to the postseason. In coming to a contract compromise with Vea before the regular season, the Bucs “didn’t act as if he was part of their long-term future, and if teams come looking for a big, run-stuffing defensive tackle, Tampa would be silly not to listen,” Graziano said. Vea through Week 6 has a 17 percent pass rush win rate, which ranks 15th among defensive tackles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/vita-vea/5.headline: Buccaneers signed DT Vita Vea to a one-year, $30 million extension through 2027.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/vita-vea/5.analysis: Vea also gets a $6 million pay bump for the 2026 NFL season. He was previously set to make $18 million this year, bringing his new salary up to $24 million. NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reported last week that Vea was seeking an extension, placing him in the top defensive tackle tier, which currently sits around $38 million annually. It looks like the two sides compromised to get a deal done. Vea ranked in the top three on the team in quarterback pressures (51) and sacks (four) last year. Garafolo clarified in a follow-up segment that the $30 million extension includes this season’s pay increase. Vea will play for $24 million in 2027.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/vita-vea/5.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports that the Bills, Bears and 49ers are among the teams that have inquired about Bucs DT Vita Vea’s availability.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/vita-vea/5.analysis: Garafolo says that the Buccaneers remain steadfast in their position that Vea is not available. The team has also apparently kept the lines of communication open with Vea regarding a potential new deal, although “a deal is not imminent.” Vea is set to make roughly $18 million in the final year of his contract. Garafolo notes that the top of the defensive tackle market is now around $38 million annually, and Vea believes his production qualifies him for a contract extension in that tier.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/vita-vea/5.headline: Bucs GM Jason Licht said he has “no plans” to trade Vita Vea.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/vita-vea/5.analysis: Vea was looking for a new contract this offseason and the Bucs have not met his demands. In response, Vea requested a trade and is not currently participating in training camp. The team is calling it a back injury. We’re comfortable assuming it’s a bank issue. Vea can’t realistically hold out during the regular season, meaning he’s going to play football this year, one way or another. Whether that’s in Tampa and on his current contract remains to be seen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/vita-vea/5.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Buccaneers do not plan to trade Vita Vea.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/vita-vea/5.analysis: Fowler does acknowledge that Vea’s camp has “pretty heavy” trade interest and also notes that Vea has felt his contract has been outdated “for a long time.” Fowler adds that in his opinion it doesn’t seem like the Bucs really tried to reach an extension with Vea, at least as compared to how they acted with Baker Mayfield. It’s hard to make a trade with a team that doesn’t want to make a trade, so we’ll see how this unfolds but it’s far from certain that the Bucs will actually make good on Vea’s trade request.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/vita-vea/5.headline: Bucs head coach Todd Bowles said Vita Vea is out with a back injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/vita-vea/5.analysis: Vea this week requested a trade after contract talks with the Tampa front office stalled. That he’s now sidelined with a back injury could be another way of Vea “holding in” until he gets a new deal from the Bucs or the team works out a trade for the star nose tackle. Vea, who has earned two Pro Bowl honors and has been one of the league’s top nose tackle since entering the league in 2018, could fit with any number of contending teams if the Bucs are willing to trade him for draft capital.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/vita-vea/5.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Buccaneers NT Vita Vea has requested a trade.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/vita-vea/5.analysis: This comes on the heels of Vea’s absence from minicamp as the two sides were locked in negotiations. The evident impasse ultimately led to the eight-year veteran requesting a trade. Vea has earned two Pro Bowl honors and has been one of the league’s top nose tackle since entering the league for the Buccaneers with the team’s 2018 first-round selection. Losing Vea would be a significant hurdle for the Buccaneer to clear considering so much of what they are able to do defensively revolves around his ability to clog the middle of the defensive line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/vita-vea/5.headline: Fox Sports’ Greg Auman reports Buccaneers NT Vita Vea is present but not participating in minicamp amidst contract negotiations.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/vita-vea/5.analysis: Vea is due $17 million in the final year of his four-year contract, considerably lower than other top defensive big men around the league. It’s a situation to monitor as the season draws near, with the veteran nose tackle clearly looking for a new deal. Whether the saga carries into camp and the preseason remains to be seen, but it is possible Vea wants to put pen to paper before retaking the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/vita-vea/5.headline: Buccaneers declared RB Bucky Irving, WR Chris Godwin, OLB Haason Reddick, G Luke Haggard, CB Kindle Vildor, S Sebastian Castro and DL C.J. Brewer inactive for Week 8 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/vita-vea/5.analysis: The Buccaneers are without three of their top players this week. While Irving and Godwin continue to miss games, long-time No. 1 WR Mike Evans (collarbone/concussion) was recently placed on injured reserve. Rookie WR Emeka Egbuka will continue to operate as a fantasy WR1, while fellow rookie WR Tez Johnson can be started as a high-upside WR3/FLEX. Reddick’s absence is a plus for the Saints’ offense. His 27 quarterback pressures lead all Buccaneers defenders by three. Fortunately, DT Vita Vea (foot) is active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/vita-vea/5.headline: Buccaneers NT Vita Vea (foot) is questionable for Tampa Bay’s Week 8 game against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/vita-vea/5.analysis: He DNPed each of the final two practices of the week after not being listed on the report on Wednesday. It’s not great news for the Buccaneers that he didn’t find a limited status today, and we’d probably subjectively put him on the pessimistic side of questionable. Alvin Kamara could have a much easier task in Week 8 if Vea is ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Saints general manager Mickey Loomis said Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) won’t practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Loomis said Tyson is “improving” in his long rehab from a major preseason hamstring injury. Tyson, who traveled with the Saints to France for their Week 7 game against the Steelers, could still be a couple weeks away as the team takes a cautious approach to his recovery. In the meantime, Bryce Lance will operate as the Saints’ No. 2 wideout behind Chris Olave. Lance over the past two weeks has a 13 percent target share and a 20 percent air yards share in the pass-first New Orleans offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Saints head coach Kellen Moore said Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) traveled with the team to Paris for Week 7’s game against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: The Saints have not opened Tyson’s 21-day window for return, but the fact that he traveled with the team suggests his window could be opened later this week, which would allow him to begin practicing with the team. There’s some belief that Tyson could return in Week 9 after the Saints’ bye week, but the team hasn’t committed to a return date for him just yet. We wouldn’t expect Tyson to suit up this week against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: When asked if Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) could resume practicing for Week 6 against the Giants, Saints coach Kellen Moore said, “not right now.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Tyson was officially a non-participant to begin the week, as expected. Moore adds that Tyson is “progressing well,” and New Orleans Football’s Mike Triplett said there is “an expectation that he’ll return to practice soon.” Tyson should be rostered in 12-team formats, but fantasy managers must, unfortunately, remain patient.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is “weeks away from return.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: The Saints’ offense has managed just fine without Tyson, but it doesn’t sound like it will get a boost from the rookie first-rounder any time soon. According to Schefter, Tyson is “making progress and feeling good,” but the earliest we may see him is Week 7. That said, due to the Saints playing Week 7 in Paris, Schefter also notes that “the most logical” return date for Tyson could be Week 9 after the team’s bye week. Fantasy managers stashing Tyson will need to continue doing so for the next several weeks, and even when he’s active, it could take a few games for him to see a full assortment of snaps. We can expect Devaughn Vele to continue operating as the Saints’ WR2 behind Chris Olave until Tyson returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore said that “at the moment,” he does not expect WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) to begin practicing next week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Tyson is currently on injured reserve and will be eligible to join his teammates on the practice field next week. Moore added, “but we shall see” at the end of his statement, making it at least possible for Tyson to resume practicing in Week 5. For now, Week 6 could be more likely. Once activated from injured reserve, Tyson will have a 21-day window to continue rehabbing, if need be.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Saints placed Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Tyson has been dealing with hamstring issues since his senior season at Arizona State. The issue flared up during training camp and he is now expected to be sidelined for roughly two months, as of two weeks ago. With an international game in Week 7 and a bye the following week, a Week 9 return looks like the most likely outcome for the rookie. He could still put up strong fantasy numbers in the second half of the season, but it’s hard to justify holding him in leagues with shallow benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Saints WR Bryce Lance caught 2-of-4 targets for 28 yards in Friday’s preseason game against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Lance could have the inside track for the Saints’ short-term No. 3 wide receiver job with WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) sidelined, though WR Barion Brown will almost assuredly make the roster as a receiver and returner. Lance nearly added a decent, leaping downfield gain to his box score, but QB Spencer Rattler’s pass grazed off his fingertips along the sideline. Brown was not involved as a receiver today, but rushed twice for 19 yards and one touchdown, including an eight-yard jet sweep that got him into the end zone. He also returned one punt for four yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: New Orleans Football’s Mike Triplett believes the Saints might not need to sign a short-term replacement for WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring).
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Triplett was apparently surprised to see reporters wondering whether the Saints should bring a veteran receiver aboard. According to him, the Saints had nine legitimate wide receiver candidates to make the final roster, with rookie WRs Bryce Lance and Barion Brown leading the charge. Per Triplett, Lance “is coming on faster than anyone else,” though Brown notably surged early in camp. Lance does not play on special teams, which could make him an ideal No. 3 wide receiver. Triplett also believes the Saints should design a package of plays for the speedy Brown, who WR Chris Olave said is “basically the same player” as former Saints WR Rashid Shaheed. For deep league fantasy managers, Lance could be worth a late-round dart throw. Both players should be rostered in dynasty.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Saints WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is expected to miss roughly two months, reports NFL Insider Ian Rapoport.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: Tyson left practice last Thursday with a hamstring injury and sought opinions from multiple doctors over the weekend. Now he’s slated to miss roughly two months, according to Rapoport. It’s a tough blow for the 22-year-old receiver who also battled hamstring injuries during his college career. The Saints also drafted receivers Bryce Lance and Barion Brown, though Devaughn Vele could be first in line for additional targets while Tyson is out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.headline: Saints HC Kellen Moore said the team is “still in collection mode” regarding Jordyn Tyson’s hamstring injury
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordyn-tys.analysis: This comes a day after we learned that Tyson is seeking multiple opinions on the hamstring injury he suffered on Thursday. At some point, the Saints will have collected enough information to feel comfortable telling us about Tyson’s injury, but for now, we will continue to wait. The longer this goes on, the worse the news will feel. Hopefully this is something that will only sideline Tyson for a few weeks, but given his history of hamstring injuries, which slowed him during the pre-draft process, it wouldn’t be surprising if his absence extended into the regular season. Hopefully we’ll have a clear answer on his status soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-frankl.headline: NFL suspended Sam Franklin for one game.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-frankl.analysis: Franklin, who was seen spitting on a Raiders player late in the fourth quarter of the Bills’ Week 6 win, will not receive pay during his one-game suspension. Franklin will be able to appeal the NFL’s decision in the coming days. The Bills on are bye in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-frankl.headline: Bills re-signed S Sam Franklin Jr. to a three-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-frankl.analysis: According to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, Franklin can earn up to $7.5 million on his new deal, with $5 million coming in the first two years. Franklin is a career special-teams player who appeared on 329 special-teams snaps for the Bills last season, totaling 13 tackles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-frankl.headline: Broncos signed S Sam Franklin Jr., formerly of the Panthers, to a one-year, $1.5 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-frankl.analysis: The Broncos added former Saints interim head coach, and long-time special team coach, Darren Rizzi to their staff this offseason. He holds both the special teams coach and assistant head coach roles for Denver. The Denver Gazette’s Chris Tomasson reports that Rizzi is said to have “pushed” for Franklin’s signing this offseason, after watching Franklin dominate NFC South special teams play as a member of the Panthers. Franklin has totaled at least seven special teams tackles in each of the last four seasons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-frankl.headline: Panthers listed Jadeveon Clowney (shoulder) as doubtful for Week 7 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-frankl.analysis: Clowney was a DNP on Wednesday and Thursday but logged a limited session on Friday. The veteran pass rusher hasn’t played since Week 5 and will likely miss his second-straight game with the injury. In addition to Clowney, the Panthers also listed safety Sam Franklin Jr. and defensive tackle Jaden Crumedy as doubtful.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-frankl.headline: Panthers S Sam Franklin suffered a broken foot and is out indefinitely.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-frankl.analysis: Franklin is a special teams ace who re-signed with the Panthers this offseason. Head coach Dave Canales called the loss of Franking “a big hit” due to the value he’s provided on special teams over the years. There’s a belief that Franklin will return at some point in the season, but it sounds like this will be the last we hear from him in training camp. We’ll likely know more about the severity of his injury and how long he’s expected to be out in the coming days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-frankl.headline: Panthers re-signed S Sam Franklin to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-frankl.analysis: Franklin was brought back on a one-year deal last offseason after primarily playing special teams in 2022. Though he remained a special teams ace in 2023, Franklin also set a career-high in defensive snaps at 289. That, in turn, led to a high-water mark in tackles (30) as well. Franklin’s breakout season even involved a 99-yard pick-six against the Vikings in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-frankl.headline: Panthers signed Sam Franklin to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-frankl.analysis: Franklin was a restricted free agent this offseason. He will be able to enter the free agency portal but the Panthers will have the ability to match any offer from another franchise. The fourth-year pro has started only five games across his three-year NFL career. He will make the league minimum $2.627 million on the tender.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-frankl.headline: Draft Diamonds’ Damond Talbot writes that Temple senior LB Sam Franklin "[h]as extreme burst on a blitz or attacking the run.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sam-frankl.analysis: Talbot notes that the 6-foot-3, 210-pound Franklin "[p]lays hard, has a nonstop motor & plays with a little nasty.” The linebacker began his career with the Owls as a defensive back before shifting over to his current position. That experience in coverage shows, with Talbot writing that Franklin’s “coverage skills are something that stands out” on film. The senior finished the past season having registered 63 tackles (7.0 for loss), three sacks, an interception and a fumble forced. He should benefit from having had a full offseason of continued development at linebacker as he looks to blip onto the NFL radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: The Athletic’s Noah Furtado reports the Chargers will try to “simplify” the team’s offense in the coming weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Justin Herbert and the flailing Chargers skill position players have appeared almost comically confused about all the pre-snap motion OC Mike McDaniel uses. That came through in the team’s embarrassing Week 6 loss to the Chiefs when players were bumping into each other during pre-snap motion calls from Herbert. Head coach Jim Harbaugh acknowledged the team is considering narrowing the offensive playbook during their bye week. “Definitely looking at volume and where you can make it to where the players can understand,” Harbaugh said when asked about how Chargers players were adjusting to McDaniel’s complex offense. The Chargers have used pre-snap motion on 74 percent of their snaps, the fourth highest rate in the NFL. Last year they used motion on 56 percent of their snaps. Hopefully these adjustments lead to some production for the NFL’s worst offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert completed 22-of-37 attempts for 205 yards and one interception in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs, adding five rushes for 26 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Herbert’s hellish season continued unabated on Sunday against a Kansas City defense that swamped the beleaguered Bolts quarterback on seemingly every drop back. After throwing exactly one touchdown in each of his first five outings, Herbert didn’t have any against the Chiefs. He had a negative EPA per drop back and was 10 percent below his expected pass rate in the loss. Ladd McConkey was ruled out with a head injury in the first half, further complicating OC Mike McDaniel’s efforts to stop the bleeding for the LA offense. The team’s wideout injuries and the predictability of the offense means Herbert should be dropped in most one-QB fantasy formats ahead of the Chargers’ Week 7 bye week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter said the Chargers would not consider trading Justin Herbert.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Schefter reached out to the team after a league source told him the Chargers could get upwards of three first-round draft picks in exchange for Herbert. The Chargers source told Schefter the team has “never” discussed the idea of dealing Herbert, even as the Chargers start the season 0-5 and rank near the bottom in almost every offensive category. It would seem unlikely that the Chargers would consider trading Herbert even if they go all in on a rebuild following the 2026 season. Herbert, 28, who ranks 33rd out of 34 qualifying quarterbacks in EPA per drop back this year, is signed through the 2029 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert completed 14-of-24 passes for 121 yards with a touchdown and interception while rushing for 54 yards and losing a fumble in the Chargers’ 23-17, Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: Herbert was without his top wideouts, his top offensive lineman, and the fact he was able to put up even this type of statline is somewhat impressive, if you squint very hard. The 28-year-old quarterback was constantly under pressure, and was at his best when he was able to escape the pocket and use his underrated wheels. That being said, he could have had more turnovers than this, and his interception was an inexcusable throw right into the hands of the Broncos defender. Even if Herbert gets his weapons back, fantasy managers should be looking elsewhere in Week 6 in standard leagues with a tough matchup against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Rashawn Slater suffered a high ankle sprain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: The injury, sustained during the Bolts’ Week 4 loss to the Seahawks, will cost Slater between four and six weeks, Rapoport said. It’s yet another massive blow for the struggling Chargers offense. Through Week 4 the Chargers rank 30th in ESPN’s pass blocking win rate and fifth in run blocking win rate. Justin Herbert’s weekly prospects take a hit with the oft-injured Slate sidelined, as do the prospects of LA’s pass catchers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Justin Herbert completed 19-of-31 passes for 189 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions in the Chargers’ 30-23, Week 4 loss to the Seahawks while adding 40 yards on the ground on six attempts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.analysis: It really wasn’t this close. Herbert and Sam Darnold became the first quarterbacks since 1991 to throw interceptions on their first throws of their game. Things didn’t get less weird, nor less shaky for the now 0-4 Chargers. He threw both his picks to linebackers, and outside of a 26-yard scramble, there just wasn’t much there from a quarterback who had (much) loftier expectations coming into the year. His only touchdown was a flip to Kimani Vidal that left Los Angeles down two scores. There’s a lot of football left, but this is ugly. Herbert will try and get going in Week 5, but the Broncos make for a tough team to get that ship righted.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/justin-her.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Justin Herbert must “be better.”
