Harris was brought in to be a “significant contributor” to the Giants, according to ESPN’s Jordan Raanan. He looked the part in Friday’s preseason finale against the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/najee-harr.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler says he is expecting to see Najee Harris in the Giants’ final preseason game against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/najee-harr.analysis: This will be the first look we get at Harris since he suffered a torn Achilles in Week 3 last season. The 28-year-old vet signed a deal with the Giants less than two weeks ago, but could end up being a “significant contributor” to the Giants’ backfield, per ESPN’s Jordan Raanan. Whether or not Harris has any fantasy value as a standalone option with Cam Skattebo healthy is to be determined, but he could be the leader in the clubhouse to be the next man up should Skattebo ever miss time, making him an intriguing late-round pick in fantasy drafts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.headline: Dolphins signed Zane Gonzalez, formerly of the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.analysis: Gonzalez reportedly beat our Justin Tucker in a tryout for Miami and will sign with the team pending a physical. Gonzalez, a journeyman who has played for five teams since entering the NFL in 2017, will replace Riley Patterson, who has missed two of his seven field goal attempts in 2026. Gonzalez will not be a fantasy option in Miami.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.headline: Dolphins released K Zane Gonzalez.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.analysis: Gonzalez’s release seemingly bodes well for K Riley Patterson. The two veteran kickers were competing to replace K Jason Sanders, who signed with the Jets this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.headline: Dolphins agreed to terms with K Zane Gonzalez, formerly of the Falcons, on a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.analysis: Gonzalez converted 19 of his 22 field goal attempts and was 7-of-9 from 50-plus yards. The veteran kicker has spent the last two seasons with the Falcons and Commanders after injuries sidelined him for the previous two seasons. Gonzalez will likely face competition for the starting kicker job in Miami, but until they add somebody else, he’s the early favorite to replace Jason Sanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.headline: Zane Gonzalez converted a 43-yard field goal with no time remaining in the Falcons’ Week 15 win over the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.analysis: Gonzalez also connected on all of of his extra-point attempts. His 43-yarder with no time remaining just snuck inside of the post to give Atlanta the win. On the year, Gonzalez has made 11 of his 13 attempts, and he’s perfect on all 11 PATs. He’ll square off against the Cardinals in Week 16.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.headline: Zane Gonzalez converted 3-of-3 field goal attempts in the Falcons’ Week 12 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.analysis: Gonzalez hit a 56-yard field goal to open scoring and the Falcons never looked back. He nets a good fantasy scoring day, with three total field goals and an extra point. The Falcons were not in the red zone frequently against a solid Saints defense, leading to the longer field goals from Gonzalez. He will have similar opportunities against a decent Jets defense in Week 13.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.headline: Falcons signed K Zane Gonzalez, formerly of the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.analysis: Gonzalez is set to be the Falcons’ third kicker of the 2025 season after the team parted ways with John Parker Romo following his Week 9 meltdown against the Patriots. Parker Romo had replaced Younghoe Koo as the team’s starter. Gonzalez last season with Washington made five of his seven field goal attempts and all 19 of his extra point tries. Over six NFL seasons, Gonzalez has converted 80 percent of his field goal attempts. He won’t have much fantasy appeal in Week 10 against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.headline: Free agent K Eddy Pineiro worked out for the Bills on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.analysis: Fellow free agent kickers Zane Gonzalez and Greg Joseph also worked out for the Bills. Incumbent K Tyler Bass struggled last season and dealt with a pelvis injury in training camp. The Bills are likely just covering their bases, but Bass could be a risky fantasy pick at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.headline: Commanders signed K Matt Gay, formerly of the Colts, to a one-year contract worth $4.25 million.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.analysis: Gay will kick for his fourth team since entering the NFL in 2019. He was released by the Colts in early April after making 82 percent of his field goal tries over two seasons with Indy. Gay has been a solid kicker for much of his NFL career, though he has struggled from distance, converting just 61 percent of his field goal tries of more than 50 yards over six seasons. Attached to a high-powered Commanders offense, Gay could have fantasy upside in 2025. Washington had the league’s fourth most field-goal attempts (42) last season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.headline: Commanders released K Zane Gonzalez.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.analysis: The move comes less than two months after Washington re-signed Gonzalez following his 2024 late-season heroics. He converted five of his seven field goal attempts during six regular season games for the Commanders. Gonzalez, who has played for five teams since entering the NFL in 2017, will likely catch on with another team this summer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.headline: Commanders re-signed K Zane Gonzalez.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/zane-gonza.analysis: After being sidelined for the 2022 and 2023 seasons, Gonzalez caught on with the Commanders late in the 2024 campaign and ended up converting 5-of-7 field goals (71.4 percent) during six regular season games while also going 7-for-8 in the playoffs with one field goal of 50-plus yards. Gonzalez is unlikely to be handed the Commanders’ starting kicker job for next season, but will clearly have a chance to compete for it in camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Alec Pierce (heel) won’t practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Pierce, dealing with a heel injury since mid-September, will continue rehabbing and remain on injured reserve ahead of the Colts’ Week 7 game against the Vikings. Since Week 3, Keenan Allen leads the Colts with a 24 percent target share, while Josh Downs 17 percent of the team’s targets and 26 percent of the team’s air yards. Neither wideout is a great option in Week 7 against a marauding Minnesota defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Alec Pierce (heel) won’t practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Tom Pelissero’s report over the weekend was that Pierce was still weeks from returning, and unfortunately this very much aligns with that. Pierce is now eligible to return off injured reserve, but until we see him designated to return and practicing, it’s hard to believe he’s close to returning.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel) is still a few weeks away from a return to game action.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: No surprise here. Pierce shed his cast earlier this week, but there was also a report from the Athletic’s James Boyd that he “didn’t get the sense” Pierce was close to a return. Pelissero reports that Pierce isn’t expected to return to practice next week when he’s eligible. It’s difficult to justify holding Pierce in leagues without IR spots given the circumstances.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: The Athletic’s James Boyd reports Alec Pierce (heel) is no longer wearing a cast but is not close to a return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Boyd said he “didn’t get the sense” that Pierce is close to a return. Pierce went on injured reserve with a heel injury after Week 2 and wore a cast on his left ankle/heel while rehabbing. It’s a sign of progress for Pierce, who will have his first chance to come back in the Colts’ Week 7 game against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: Colts placed Alec Pierce (heel) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Pierce will be sidelined for at least four weeks after suffering the injury in Week 2 against Kansas City. Pierce had seen 19 percent of the Colts’ targets and 53 percent of the team’s air yards in Week 1 against the Ravens, resuming his role as a strictly-downfield pass catcher. With Pierce out, Josh Downs should have every chance to operate as the Colts’ No. 1 wideout while Tyler Warren sees a bump in targets. Laquon Treadwell is likely to take over as the team’s lone deep threat. Treadwell can be picked up in 14-team fantasy formats ahead of the Colts’ Week 3 matchup with the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel) will “attempt to rehab his injury rather than have surgery.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Pierce will most certainly be out for numerous games after appearing to re-injure the heel that he had offseason surgery on in Week 2. Rapoport’s wording seems to indicate that additional surgery has not yet been ruled out, but Pierce will attempt to rehab the issue in the interim. It’s a disaster of a scenario for a team that extended Pierce while allowing Michael Pittman to walk in the offseason. Josh Downs appears most likely to become the focal point of the offense through the air in Pierce’s absence after amassing seven catches on nine targets in the team’s overtime loss to the Chiefs. When, or if, Pierce returns to the active roster in 2026 remains to be seen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: Colts head coach Shane Steichen said Alec Pierce (heel) aggravated the injury that required surgery in March and the Colts are “still gathering information.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: X-rays came back negative last night but Pierce couldn’t put weight on it last night and left on crutches with a boot on. The fact that it was an aggravation is not promising. It sounds like Pierce could be looking at an extended absence. If true, Josh Downs will get some WR3 hype ahead of Week 3’s date against the Texans. If you were wondering why Laquon Treadwell was on the field deep in the game on Sunday night, Pierce’s injury is the reason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Colts WR Alec Pierce’s (heel) X-rays were negative.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Pierce evidently avoided suffering a fracture. He will undergo more testing tomorrow to determine the remaining specifics and the injury’s severity. Hopefully, the Colts’ field-stretching wide receiver is not sidelined for long, if at all. Pierce underwent surgery on his ankle/heel this offseason and spent almost the entire spring and summer rehabbing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel) is questionable to return to Week 2 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Pierce came up limping on a route on the final play of the first quarter and was escorted to the medical tent by the training staff. He appeared to be unable to put any weight on the injured leg. It’s obviously not what fantasy managers want to see after he missed most of the offseason program following surgery on the ankle and heel on the same leg in late March. He remained in the medical tent for about 10 minutes before being carted to the locker room. Pierce caught his lone target for 11 yards prior to departing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.headline: Colts WR Alec Pierce (heel) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/alec-pierc.analysis: Pierce’s Thursday absence appears to have been a rest day. The Colts reportedly plan to play Pierce more in Week 2 than they did in Week 1, when he played on 59 percent of the team’s snaps. He posted a 4/61 receiving line and can be viewed as a WR3/FLEX this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.headline: Ravens signed Jake Moody to the team’s practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.analysis: Moody could serve as competition for Tyler Loop after Loop’s early-season struggles. Loop has made ten of his 13 field goals attempts and all 16 of his extra points through Week 6. Moody — a career 78 percent kicker — competed with Loop for starting duties ahead of the regular season. Whoever ends up kicking for Baltimore will be fantasy relevant.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.headline: Ravens released K Jake Moody from their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.analysis: Moody is free to shop his services elsewhere as Tyler Loop’s 2-for-2 opening game appears to have marked him as safe for the moment. The Ravens used the practice squad spot on WR Gage Larvadain.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.headline: Ravens signed K Jake Moody to the team’s practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.analysis: It’s an interesting move after Tyler Loop, the team’s Week 1 starter, struggled in training camp and during the preseason. The journeyman Moody was most recently cut by the Commanders and would only be activated to the 53-man roster if Loop’s struggles continue into the regular season. Last year with Washington, Moody went 10-for-11 while going 2-for-2 on distances of 50-plus yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.headline: Commanders released K Jake Moody.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.analysis: NFL insider Jordan Schultz was the first to report the move. The former 49er was signed to a one-year deal earlier this offseason after a brief stint with Washington, in which he went 10-for-11 while going 2-for-2 on distances of 50-plus yards. Moody had been in a kicking competition with rookie UDFA Drew Stevens, who has outperformed Moody in camp. Moody was a third-round pick by the Niners in 2023 and has converted 78 percent of his field goals in his career and is 107-for-110 on his extra point tries.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.headline: Commanders re-signed K Jake Moody to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.analysis: Just days after the team opted not to tender Moody as a restricted free agent, they have now re-signed him for next season before the start of free agency kicks off next year. Moody was 18-of-20 on field goal attempts last season for the Bears and Commanders after going 1-for-3 in Week 1 for the 49ers. The former third-round pick only attempted two field goals from 50-plus yards last season, and will likely find himself in a kicking competition later this summer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.headline: Commanders did not tender restricted free agent K Jake Moody, making him a free agent.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.analysis: The 2023 third-rounder became a vagabond in 2025, playing for the 49ers, Bears, and Commanders. He’ll likely get another crack to win a starting job again in 2026 somewhere. He was 18-of-20 on field goal attempts for the Bears and Commanders after a Week 1 hail of misses had him released in San Francisco.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.headline: Jake Moody converted 1-of-2 field goal attempts in the Commanders’ Week 18 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.analysis: Moody missed a chip shot 24-yard field goal in Week 18, but subsequently made a 56-yard field goal later. He spent the 2025 season bouncing between the 49ers, Bears, and Commanders. The 49ers cut him after missing a pair of field goals in Week 1, after which he signed to the Bears’ practice squad. The Commanders signed him off the Bears’ practice squad after he made eight field goals in two games for Chicago. Moody spent the final six games of the season with the Commanders; it remains to be seen if he will return to Washington or sign elsewhere for next season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.headline: Commanders signed K Jake Moody, formerly of the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.analysis: A former third-round pick of the Niners back in 2023, Moody was waived by the 49ers for missing two kicks in Week 1’s win over the 49ers. The third-year kicker missed a whopping 10 kicks last season, but has gone 8-for-9 on his attempts in two games with the Bears, although he notably hasn’t attempted a field goal from 50-plus yards this season. Moody replaces Matt Gay, whose struggles primarily came from distances of 50-plus yards. If the goal is to find a kicker with more range, it seems unlikely that Moody will prove to be the difference-maker the Commanders are looking for. For his career, Moody is 6-for-12 on attempts from 50-plus yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.headline: Bears K Cairo Santos (thigh) is questionable for Chicago’s Week 8 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.analysis: He did get in full practices each of the last two days, which would seem to be an indication that the veteran kicker will be back against Baltimore. If not, Jake Moody will get another practice squad elevation and kick for the Bears in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.headline: Bears K Cairo Santos (thigh) will not play in Chicago’s Week 7 game against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-moody.analysis: It’s another Jake Moody week, for those of you in two-kicker leagues or contemplating a stream against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: Jordan Watkins caught his only target for 22 yards in the 49ers’ Week 6 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: Watkins drew the start in place of the injured Deebo Samuel but was unable to take advantage of the opportunity, with 23 of Brock Purdy’s 29 targets going to the team’s top three options in Christian McCaffrey, Mike Evans, and George Kittle. Evans departed at the end of the second quarter with an aggravation of his Achilles injury, something that appears likely to cost the veteran a Week 7 game against the Falcons. That could leave Watkins in line for a second consecutive start, although the upside remains modest. Fantasy managers are likely best leaving both Watkins and veteran Brandin Cooks on the waiver wire, the latter of whom caught 1-of-2 targets for 13 yards against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: KhaDarel Hodge (knee) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: This is a low blow, even for the subsation. Hodge began the year on San Francisco’s practice squad but was promoted to the active roster when De’Zhaun Stribling went down with an ankle injury. He wound up running 45 percent of the routes in Week 3 but was not targeted once. With Mike Evans also banged up, Jacob Cowing and Jordan Watkins could be in line for more work this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: Jordan Watkins caught both of his targets for 60 yards in the 49ers’ Week 3 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: Watkins saw increased opportunity with Mike Evans (rib) exiting in the second quarter. He caught a pair of long targets from Purdy despite KhaDarel Hodge and Jacob Cowing beating the 24-year-old in snaps. Watkins could certainly be on the fantasy radar if Evans misses an extended period of time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: 49ers declared RB Jordan James inactive for Week 1 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: James has officially lost the backup job to rookie RB Kaelon Black, who should be safely stashed on fantasy benches before kickoff. The 49ers also declared QB Kurtis Rourke, CB Ephesians Prysock, WR Jordan Watkins, LB Tatum Bethune and OT Enrique Cruz inactive for Week 1 against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: 49ers WR Deebo Samuel will take over “a portion” of the Z-receiver role, while also contributing as a “wide back.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: The Athletic’s Matt Barrows notes that at 30 years old, Samuel is “not going to be close to an every-down player.” 49ers WRs Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing are competing to be Samuel’s backup, though neither player will be reliable in fantasy. Samuel may also struggle to return FLEX value at this point in his career.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan said he is excited by the work WR Jordan Watkins and WR Jacob Cowing have been putting in this offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: Watkins drew positive reviews as a rookie last summer, but September ankle and calf injuries stunted his development, pushing him to the bottom of the depth chart. Cowing’s second NFL season was derailed by a recurring hamstring strain. The Athletic’s Matt Barrows listed him as a standout at Thursday’s practice, but he caught just four passes as a 2024 rookie. Expectations for him must be tempered. Watkins is worth monitoring for deep-league managers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: 49ers WR Jauan Jennings (ankle/ribs/shoulder) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: Jennings is very difficult to trust after last week’s meltdown. He was limited twice to begin the week, and we do not yet know his Friday participation level. At this point, the big-bodied wide receiver can only be viewed as a boom-bust WR4/FLEX option. If and when he resumes practicing in full consistently, we will be able to upgrade him to WR3 status. 49ers rookie WR Jordan Watkins (calf) is also expected to play this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said Jordan Watkins (calf) is expected to resume practicing this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: We were just thinking the 49ers wideout projections needed another variable to deal with. Watkins briefly wowed in training camp before dealing with a high-ankle sprain and later this calf issue. It’s possible he cuts into some veteran playing time if the 49ers wideout room remains unsettled, but he’s not someone to rush and pick up in re-draft leagues without seeing some real signs of fantasy life.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: 49ers ruled out QB Brock Purdy (toe) for Week 6 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: Purdy remained sidelined all week, as did WR Ricky Pearsall, who is dealing with a PCL sprain in his knee. Just eight days ago, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reported that Purdy is considered week-to-week, so the starting quarterback’s absence is hardly surprising. Hopefully, Purdy can remain setback-free and return for the 49ers’ Week 7 game against the Falcons, though that outcome should not be viewed as guaranteed. The 49ers also ruled out WR Jordan Watkins (calf), DL Kevin Givens (pectoral) and EDGE Yetur Gross-Matos (knee/hamstring).

https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.headline: 49ers QB Mac Jones (knee) is questionable for Week 4 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jordan-watkins.analysis: 49ers starting QB Brock Purdy (toe/left shoulder) has been cleared to play, so Jones has been put back into the No. 2 spot. He played admirably in his two starts, completing 53-of-80 passes for 563 yards, four touchdowns and one interception and rushing seven times for five yards despite aggravating a summer PCL sprain in Week 3. For fantasy managers in two-quarterback leagues with no one better to stash, he can be left on the bench this week to see how Purdy’s health holds up. For everyone else, he can be dropped. The 49ers also ruled out WR Jordan Watkins (calf) and DT CJ West (thumb). FB Kyle Juszczyk passed the NFL’s concussion protocol and will be active for Week 4 against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 5-of-8 targets for 69 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 6 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: Kittle got the scoring started with an 11-yard touchdown on a dime from Brock Purdy to the corner of the end zone, contributing to the offense steadily through a dominant first half before pushing his yardage totals with a 35-yard reception to start the third quarter. It was a tale of two halves for the San Francisco offense, who managed a staggering 303 yards of total offense in the first half and only 73 yards of total offense after the break, likely heavily influenced by the departure of Mike Evans at the end of the second quarter. Evens is expected to miss the team’s Week 8 contest against the Falcons, where Kittle could step into addition volume in his already-solid TE1 profile.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 5-of-6 targets for 24 yards in the 49ers’ Week 5 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: After three straight big weeks, Kittle finally came back down to earth in Sunday’s win over the Seahawks. His longest reception came on a 13-yard gain in the third quarter, but proved inconsequential after Deebo Samuel lost a fumble on the following play to end the drive. Kittle has been targeted 19 times over the last three weeks and has gone for 70-plus yards in three of his last four games. He should be primed for a bounce-back next week when the Niners play host to the Commanders on Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle (illness) is active for Week 5 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: It was reported earlier on Sunday that Kittle was dealing with an illness, but that he was still expecting to play. Kittle was not listed with the 49ers’ inactives when the team announced them 90 minutes before kickoff, meaning he is good to go and can be treated as a TE1 as usual.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 4-of-6 targets for 70 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 4 win against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: It was a quiet day for Kittle before a fourth quarter screen pass went for a 58-yard score that sealed the game for the Niners. Displaying explosiveness less than a year after tearing his Achilles tendon, Kittle outran the Broncos secondary for his second touchdown in as many weeks. His six looks from Brock Purdy was second most among Niners pass catcher, trailing only Mike Evans (eight targets). Kittle’s big play upside and his role in the red zone make him a potential matchup flipper in fantasy. He gets the Seahawks in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught 6-of-7 targets for 82 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers’ Week 3 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: Kittle saw a season-high seven targets in the 49ers’ win, becoming the team’s No. 1 pass-catcher after Mike Evans (rib) left the game. He caught a 10-yard touchdown at the start of the fourth quarter and later sealed the win with a 20-yard score with under two minutes left. Kittle seems to be all the way back from his Achilles tear, leading all 49ers offensive skill players in snaps, only trailing Brock Purdy and the offensive line. With Evans’ status in the air, Kittle is the team’s top receiver and is squarely in the fantasy TE1 conversation for Week 4 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: 49ers ruled out WR Demarcus Robinson (ankle) for Week 3 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: This was the expected outcome for Week 3. Reports on Robinson’s injury indicate this could be a multi-week issue. With WR1 Mike Evans (hip) questionable, WR Deebo Samuel and TE George Kittle could take on sizable workloads, though the team will likely still try to limit Kittle’s snap count.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: George Kittle caught all four of his targets for 80 yards and a touchdown in a Week 2 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: Kittle looked good in this one, finding space over the middle of the field and showing good burst after the catch. That’s important considering he’s still working his way back from last year’s Achilles injury. The veteran played just three fewer snaps than Mike Evans and was fourth on the team in routes run, just one behind Christian McCaffrey. His playing time will continue to increase as the year goes on, but he looks pretty close to the George Kittle we’ve gotten used to.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: 49ers TE George Kittle (Achilles) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: Kittle will likely remain on a snap count in Week 2, though his usage should continue steadily ticking upward. He can be started as a TE1 against the Dolphins’ fantasy-friendly defense this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: 49ers TE George Kittle (Achilles) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: Kittle’s continued limited participation is not concerning. The 49ers are likely just managing the veteran’s reps early in the year, coming off a season-ending injury. Kittle is a TE1 for the 49ers’ Week 2 game against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.headline: 49ers TE George Kittle (Achilles) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/george-kit.analysis: Kittle also started out last week as limited, so this seems to be regular practice management for the veteran. He appeared in Week 1 and was targeted five times. Expect Kittle to be back out there for Week 2 against the Dolphins, barring any setbacks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey rushed 16 times for 64 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers’ Week 6 win over the Commanders, adding 53 yards on nine receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: McCaffrey set a season high with 25 touches and 26 opportunities in a game played without Deebo Samuel and in which Mike Evans departed just before the half with an aggravation of his Achilles injury. The veteran workhorse back again proved how high his ceiling can be with such a robust role through the air. A second quarter fumble was his first lost fumble since 2024, a stretch spanning over 500 touches since he last lost a fumble. McCaffrey remains an elite RB1 despite a difficult matchup on the ground against the Falcons in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey rushed 11 times for 68 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 5 win over the Seahawks, adding three receptions for 15 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: McCaffrey’s lone touchdown came on an 11-yard touchdown run immediately after the 49ers had recovered a fumble by Emanuel Wilson. He hasn’t had the gaudy yardage totals we’re accustomed to seeing, but fantasy managers won’t be mad at this performance. While McCaffrey has yet to rush for 100 yards in a game this season, he’s gone for 80-plus yards from scrimmage in three of five games and has scored in four straight. He continues to be the only fantasy-relevant running back on the Niners and is set up to smash in Week 6 against the Commanders on Monday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey had 15 rushes for 52 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 4 win against the Broncos, adding three catches for 18 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Denver’s defense focused on slowing down McCaffrey and the Niners’ run game. That forced Brock Purdy and the offense into a more pass-heavy approach. CMC surprisingly was not all that involved in the passing attack against a Broncos defense that has been generous to pass catchers out of the backfield this season. He saved his fantasy day with a goal line plunge in the second half. Kaelon Black, meanwhile, saw six carries on the day. McCaffrey will be a top-5 option in Week 5 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: 49ers ruled out Kyle Juszczyk (knee) in Week 4 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: Juszczyk suffered what looked to be a serious knee injury in the fourth quarter and didn’t return to the game after being helped off the field. He would constitute an outsized loss for Kyle Shanahan’s offense, particularly his run game designs. A long-term absence for the trusted Shanny fullback could be something of a blow for Christian McCaffrey’s weekly prospects.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey rushed 15 times for 75 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 3 win over the Cardinals, adding four receptions for 41 yards
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: McCaffrey continued to run as the engine of the 49ers’ offense, turning 19 touches into 116 yards. He carried the ball frequently after the 49ers went up big in the first half and was a key receiver when the Cardinals attempted to stage a late-game comeback. McCaffrey scored his touchdown by jumping over a pile for a fourth-quarter goal-line score. He followed that up with a one-handed catch to keep a key drive alive late in the game. Though LT Trent Williams left with injury, McCaffrey is a big enough part of the receiving game to overcome any rushing inefficiency. He continues to be a fantasy RB1 for Week 4 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey rushed 10 times for 23 yards and two touchdowns in a Week 2 win over the Dolphins, adding four catches for 43 yards receiving.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: It was not an efficient day for the 49ers’ running backs, but Brock Purdy dissected the Dolphins enough that McCaffrey was set up for a couple of easy touchdown runs. His longest rush of the day was just five yards, so the team will be looking to get that sorted out ahead of Week 3’s game against the Cardinals. The positive news is that McCaffrey didn’t really split time with Kaelon Black as much before the end of the game. He remains a locked-in RB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: 49ers listed RB Christian McCaffrey, OT Trent Williams, LB Dre Greenlaw, and EDGE Nick Bosa as resting non-participants for Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: McCaffrey and Williams were listed as DNP simply for rest, while Bosa had a rest/knee designation and Greenlaw had a rest/Achilles designation. This is notable as the 49ers have several key veterans who have dealt with injuries throughout their career and practice reps will be managed for these players, especially coming off a Week 1 in Australia. McCaffrey reportedly dealt with cramps in the 49ers’ Week 1 win over the Rams; though he is not injured, his experiences with Achilles tendinitis will certainly lend to rest days throughout the season. We expect the 49ers to continue to rest veterans in practice throughout the season in an effort to remain healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan said Christian McCaffrey played through cramps in Week 1’s win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: McCaffrey’s usage was a bit underwhelming in the first half of Thursday’s win. The 30-year-old running back played on 20 offensive snaps to Kaelon Black’s, while Black’s seven rush attempts more than doubled the three carries we saw from CMC, who also saw six first-half targets. McCaffrey’s second-half usage saw a slight uptick, but it’s possible some of what we saw as it pertains to last night’s split was related to this cramping issue. McCaffrey was undoubtedly the more efficient of the two Niners backs in last night’s win, but Black was solid in his debut, rushing 14 times for 65 yards. McCaffrey should be positioned for a big Week 2 game next week against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey rushed 10 times for 68 yards in the 49ers’ Week 1 win over the Rams, adding five catches for 20 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: The man they call CMC was not a big part of the first-half attack, but saw plenty more touches over the final two quarters to turn what was looking like an ugly fantasy debut into a decent — although far from spectacular — outing for the 30-year-old veteran. It’s worth noting that Kaelon Black received 14 carries in the contest for 68 yards, and it’s likely that Black is going to be involved going forward in at least a somewhat similar capacity. McCaffrey should still get plenty of touches going forward, and should have a good day against the Dolphins in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.headline: Christian McCaffrey was not spotted at the early portion of Monday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/christian-.analysis: While most of us were asleep on Sunday night, the 49ers were already conducting a Monday afternoon practice in Australia. According to NBC Sports’ Matt Maiocco, McCaffrey was not seen taking part in drills during the early portion of practice. It’s possible this is by design as the Niners prepare for their season opener on Thursday against the Rams, so we won’t read too much into this just yet. McCaffrey missed some time during training camp due to “tightness,” but seemingly downplayed any idea of an injury when he later said the time off during camp was “the plan from the jump.” This is something to keep an eye on in the coming days, but for now, we’ll assume McCaffrey will be good to go for the season opener. According to Maiocco, DE Nick Bosa was also not spotted during the early portion of practice on Monday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 21-of-29 passes for 264 yards and one touchdown in the 49ers’ 23-17, Week 6 win over the Commanders, adding 28 yards on five carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Purdy and the 49ers absolutely dominated the first two quarters, gaining 303 yards of total offense on 41 plays before the break. The situation would alter course in a hurry after Purdy lost his top option through the air in the final minute of the second quarter as Mike Evans departed with an aggravation of the Achilles injury that had him listed as questionable entering the game. The team would go on to gain only 72 additional yards after the intermission, allowing the Commanders the ability to claw their way back into the game in the fourth quarter. Even so, Purdy now holds the NFL record for highest career passer rating after qualifying for the statistic with his 1,500th pass attempt in the win, which pushes the 49ers to a perfect 6-0 record ahead of a Week 7 meeting with the Falcons before their bye the following week. Purdy remains a surefire QB1 against the pass-funnel Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 19-of-29 passes for 189 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the 49ers’ 32-29, Week 5 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Purdy and the 49ers made the most of several short fields in this one. After an interception by Sam Darnold on the Seahawks’ first drive of the game, Purdy led a short 18-yard drive that he capped with a two-yard touchdown pass to Mike Evans to give the Niners an early lead. Purdy would orchestrate a long scoring drive in the fourth quarter, completing seven passes for 89 yards, with his final completion resulting in a seven-yard touchdown to Brandin Cooks. The Seahawks became the first team to sack Purdy this season, bringing him down three times in the backfield in the second half, but Purdy was able to evade pressure for the entire second half. Purdy and the Niners get a juicy Week 6 matchup next Monday against the Commanders, where he will profile as a solid QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 19-of-30 attempts for 218 yards and two touchdowns in the 49ers’ Week 4 win against the Broncos, adding ten rushes for 29 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Purdy’s ten rushing attempts were a season high, and the product of Denver’s secondary blanketing Niners pass catchers for much of the game. Injuries to both starting Broncos corners eventually loosened things up for Purdy and the 49ers. He connected with George Kittle on a fourth quarter screen pass that went for a 58-yard score — the biggest play of the game. Purdy, who now has 11 touchdown passes through four games, is a weekly top-10 fantasy play even on his less-than-efficient days. He gets a tough matchup against Seattle in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 15-of-27 passes for 297 yards and four touchdowns in the 49ers’ 36-30, Week 3 win over the Cardinals, adding two carries for 34 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: The 49ers offense had another fruitful fantasy day despite injuries haunting the team once again. Purdy showcased his mobility and athleticism, often making throws on the run and scrambling out of pressure. His first score was a completion to Mike Evans, who lateraled it to Deebo Samuel for the score. Purdy then threw a more traditional touchdown to Evans later in the first half, then threw two scores to George Kittle to seal the game in the second half. Despite losing Evans and LT Trent Williams by the third quarter, Purdy was still able to gash the Cardinals defense and surpass 300 total yards. Though the offense keeps losing pieces, Purdy in Kyle Shanahan’s scheme is a fantasy QB1 until further notice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 20-of-22 passes for 287 yards and two touchdowns in a 35-13, Week 2 win over the Cardinals, adding 30 yards rushing and a touchdown on the ground.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: The Dolphins’ defense didn’t put up much of a fight, but Purdy was tremendous in this one. He bought extra time in the pocket when he needed to, made plays with his legs if the opportunities were there, and found open receivers over the middle of the field all game long. He may find the going a little bit tougher next week against the Cardinals, but probably not much. The bigger question will be who else can step up in the receiver room with Demarcus Robinson leaving this game with an ankle injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Brock Purdy completed 25-of-34 passes for 205 yards with three touchdowns and one interception in the 49ers’ 27-7, Week 1 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Purdy also added 29 yards on his five attempts. The veteran signal-caller did throw a terrible interception, but outside of that pick he played exceptionally well; even if most of his completions were for short yardage. All three passing scores came to different players, with his best throw being a perfectly placed touchdown to Deebo Samuel between two Rams’ defenders to cement the blowout. Purdy will look to keep it going in Week 2, and gets a friendly matchup against the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that 49ers QB Brock Purdy said he is “prepared to use his mobility more this year if needed.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: The 49ers’ quarterback is not a straight-line burner, but he is more agile than he is given credit for. Purdy adds that he won’t constantly be looking for opportunities to run, however, he believes he can help the offense by scrambling for 10-12 yards from time to time. Purdy has racked up 113 carries over the past two NFL seasons, including the playoffs, proving himself an efficient scrambler with a 47.8 percent conversion rate that ranks first among quarterbacks with at least 50 attempts. He’s a borderline QB1/2. Scrambling more often could get him into the weekly low-end QB1 tier.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: 49ers added $300,000 in incentives to Mac Jones’ contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Jones, who could have started elsewhere this season if the Niners had found a trading partner, will now make $3.55 million in 2026, with another $2.25 million available in incentives. Jones will be a free agent after the 2026 season. The Niners reportedly wanted a first-round draft pick in exchange for Jones. The veteran threw for 2,151 yards, 13 touchdowns, and six interceptions last season over eight games as the Niners’ starter. Jones in 2025 was tenth in EPA per drop back, just behind Sam Darnold and Patrick Mahomes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: Vikings will face the 49ers in Mexico City on November 22.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: The Kyler Murray experiment should be well underway by late November as Kevin O’Connell and the Vikings look to recover from their failed dalliance with J.J. McCarthy as the team’s starting quarterback. Murray will lead a quietly loaded Minnesota offense against Kyle Shanahan’s EPA-maximizing Niners offense. The last time Brock Purdy faced the Vikings defense he threw for 319 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in a Week 2 2024 loss. Purdy took a season-high six sacks in that game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.headline: ESPN’s Field Yates reports Washington WR Denzel Boston is making a top-30 visit with the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brock-purd.analysis: Boston has a good chance of being on the draft board when the 49ers make their first round selection at No. 27 overall. Boston in his final collegiate season at Washington had 62 receptions for 881 receiving yards (14.2 yards per catch) and was tied for ninth in the FBS with 11 receiving touchdowns. Boston ranks 42nd in yards per route run among wideouts in the 2026 draft class. The big-bodied Boston would pair well with veteran Mike Evans, who signed with the Niners during free agency. With Evans, Boston, and George Kittle, Brock Purdy would have a range of excellent red zone options in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs caught 6-of-7 targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 6 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: While the end line looks good in the box score, the fact that Diggs continued to operate in a situational role following the departure of Terry McLaurin in the first quarter was somewhat concerning for the veteran receiver’s upside potential in McLaurin’s absence, although the fact that he came into the game listed as questionable with a hamstring injury could have influenced his snap rate. Either way, Diggs continues to produce when on the field, returning significant value for fantasy managers that invested a middle-round pick for his services this summer. Diggs will be an upside WR3 when the Commanders take on the division rival Eagles in Week 8 following their bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) is active for Week 6 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Diggs returns from a one-game absence due a hamstring injury. Although possible he sees his route participation curtailed, fantasy managers that made it this far are likely forced to ride with the veteran receiver in a solid schematic matchup against the zone-heavy 49ers. Inactive for the Commanders are QB Marcus Mariota, CB Fabian Moreau, CB Isaac Yiadom, OLB T.J. Magunranyanga, G Tanoa Togiai, and DE Charles Omenihu.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) is questionable for Week 6 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Diggs returned to the practice field Friday as a limited participant, following it with another practice with the same status a day later. The listed his as questionable for Monday Night Football against the 49ers as he attempts to return from a one-game absence due to a hamstring injury. Fantasy managers might be better off playing it safe considering the timing of the game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) was spotted at Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: After missing all of practice last week and being a DNP on Thursday, Diggs was back on the field Friday, which is a good sign for his Week 6 availability with one practice left to go in the week. The Commanders take on the 49ers on Monday Night Football this week and will likely announce Diggs’ availability sometime Saturday, but he could be on track to return in what is a must-win game for the 1-3-1 Commanders. Diggs has caught 18 passes for 170 yards and three touchdowns this season and would be in the mix as a fringe WR3/WR4 if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said he is hopeful Diggs will get some practice reps in later this week. Diggs missed Week 5 with the hamstring issue, and a DNP today puts him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 6, even if Quinn remains optimistic. Terry McLaurin and Chig Okonkwo led the team in receiving last week. McLaurin should pull away from Okonkwo as he puts more time between himself and the hamstring injury that previously knocked him out for a week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) will not play in Week 5 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Diggs did not practice this week and was ruled out by the team shortly after Friday’s practice concluded. His absence will give rookie Antonio Williams, who ran 30 routes last week, a chance to take on a bigger role. Williams tied for the team lead with eight targets in Week 4’s game against the Colts and could be treated as a desperation WR4/FLEX play. Fantasy managers considering Williams for their lineups may want to check the weather, as rain and wind are currently forecasted for the area, which could create a suboptimal environment for Washington’s passing game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) is not practicing on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Diggs was unable to get on the practice field this week and will likely be ruled out for Week 5’s game against the Giants in the next few hours. Rookie receiver Antonio Williams would again be in line for a busy day and could be the favorite to lead the team in targets this week, especially if Terry McLaurin (hamstring) also misses this week. McLaurin’s status remains wait and see after he was spotted on the practice field Friday after being a DNP on the first two days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: This runs contrary to media reporters that said he was participating. Welp. Diggs is officially in danger of missing Week 5 after two DNPs to start the week. Perhaps the Commanders deep wideouts will merit some desperation FLEX plays this week with Jayden Daniels under center. Or perhaps Diggs will turn it around enough on Friday to get a questionable tag.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) returned to practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Diggs was held out of Wednesday’s session because of the hamstring issue. Even a limited practice today puts him on track to suit up on Sunday. Terry McLaurin, on the other hand, looks likely to miss another week with a hamstring injury of his own. That will put Diggs in the WR1 seat for Week 5 against the Giants. Antonio Williams will continue to operate as the team’s No. 2 receiver.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/stefon-dig.analysis: Diggs didn’t appear to get hurt during the Commanders’ Week 4 loss to the Colts, but it looks like he felt something after the game. With Terry McLaurin also sidelined for today’s practice, Antonio Williams could be the Commanders’ No. 1 receiver in Week 5. He saw eight targets on Sunday, only one fewer than Diggs. The Commanders’ absurdly long injury report will be one to monitor as the week progresses.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Antonio Williams caught 3-of-4 targets for 50 yards in the Commanders’ Week 6 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: While the yardage total looks solid on paper, the fact that Williams had only four targets in a game in which veteran wide receiver Terry McLaurin departed in the first quarter and quarterback Jayden Daniels attempted 40 passes in concerning. Williams continues to flash big play upside through a multitude of injuries to teammates but has yet to fully take advantage of the increase in opportunity, something fantasy managers will hope corrects when the Commanders come out of their bye to face the Eagles in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Terry McLaurin (hamstring) will “most likely” be a game-time decision for Week 5 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: Keep it locked to Rotoworld, folks. Hopefully, we get word on McLaurin’s status on Saturday, but it appears as though we may have to wait until Sunday morning. Fowler adds that rookie WR Antonio Williams “could be a factor in the passing game regardless of whether McLaurin plays.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) will not play in Week 5 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: Diggs did not practice this week and was ruled out by the team shortly after Friday’s practice concluded. His absence will give rookie Antonio Williams, who ran 30 routes last week, a chance to take on a bigger role. Williams tied for the team lead with eight targets in Week 4’s game against the Colts and could be treated as a desperation WR4/FLEX play. Fantasy managers considering Williams for their lineups may want to check the weather, as rain and wind are currently forecasted for the area, which could create a suboptimal environment for Washington’s passing game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: Diggs didn’t appear to get hurt during the Commanders’ Week 4 loss to the Colts, but it looks like he felt something after the game. With Terry McLaurin also sidelined for today’s practice, Antonio Williams could be the Commanders’ No. 1 receiver in Week 5. He saw eight targets on Sunday, only one fewer than Diggs. The Commanders’ absurdly long injury report will be one to monitor as the week progresses.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Antonio Williams caught 3-of-8 targets for 21 yards in the Commanders’ Week 4 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: With Terry McLaurin out, Williams fully took over as the team’s No. 2 receiver. His eight targets were good for a 22 percent target share and he led the Commanders in routes. The bad news is that the offense struggled after Marcus Mariota went down with a knee injury. That happened in the first quarter, so Washington had a third-string quarterback under center for the majority of this game. If the role sticks, Williams could be a viable FLEX play once Jayden Daniels returns. The Commanders’ injury report will be one to watch heading into Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Antonio Williams caught 2-of-4 targets for 15 yards in the Commanders’ Week 3 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: The Commanders were able to put up an impressive 34 points — six of those coming on a pick six, but still — against the Seahawks, but Williams had little to do with it with a long gain of nine. The 2026 third-round pick has a chance to be a solid PPR play at some point, but Williams is much more of a dynasty option than a redraft one at this stage. He’ll likely be the third wideout for Washington in Week 4 against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Antonio Williams caught 3-of-3 targets for 24 yards in the Commanders’ Week 2 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: Williams tied Dyami Brown for the second-most routes run (24) by any Commanders receiver, but he saw one fewer target than he did in his rookie debut. The rookie receiver came up short on an opportunity for a wide-open touchdown pass to Terry McLaurin on a trick play, which was the closest he came to generating a big play in this one. All three of Williams’ targets came on the second-to-last drive of the game for the Commanders. There’s far too much target competition here to consider Williams a viable fantasy asset in Week 3’s game against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Jaylin Lane (groin) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: A limited session this early in the week shouldn’t stop Lane from suiting up on Sunday, but it’s worth noting. Lane split the WR4 role with Antonio Williams in Week 1. Williams stole the show with four catches for 64 yards and a score. If Lane can’t suit up this week, Williams could be in line for a larger role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: Antonio Williams caught 4-of-4 targets for 64 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 1 loss to the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: Williams’ 64 receiving yards were enough to lead all Commanders players in Sunday’s loss. The rookie third-rounder made his first catch late in the second quarter, picking up 16 yards to put the Commanders down on Philly’s one-yard line, which set up a rushing touchdown by Jacory Croskey-Merritt on the following play. He again came up big with a 33-yard reception in the fourth quarter to convert a third-and-14 that helped set up another Commanders touchdown, and on the team’s final drive of the game, Williams displayed good hands on a one-yard touchdown when he maintained control of a low, poorly thrown ball for the score. While Williams’ strong performance certainly warrants more opportunities, he shouldn’t be viewed as any more than the third receiver in Washington’s passing game. He’s an intriguing stash in deeper leagues, but there’s no reason to chase the points in next week’s game against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.headline: ESPN’s John Keim believes rookie WR Antonio Williams “will play early” for the Commanders this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/antonio-willia.analysis: Playing early is one thing. Pulling targets from Terry McLaurin, Stefon Diggs, and Chig Okonkwo is another. Williams has reportedly had a strong camp and will likely see most of his snaps come from the slot in his rookie season. The former Clemson Tiger caught 130 passes over his final two seasons, but it’s hard to imagine him offering much fantasy production, especially in the early part of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks caught 4-of-6 targets for 66 yards in the Commanders’ Week 6 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks stepped into an increased role in the offense following the first quarter injury to Terry McLaurin, the latter of whom appears to have suffered a significant knee injury. The six targets ranked third on the team behind tight end Chig Okonkwo and veteran wide receiver Stefon Diggs, but a late injury could immediately halt his momentum. Burks was injured on a contested ball in the end zone on fourth down with just over two minutes remaining in the fourth quarter and was escorted to the locker room by training staff. Fantasy managers interested in a potential waiver addition will want to track updates from the team regarding his health in the coming days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks caught 1-of-3 targets for 47 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 4 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks only catch of the day came on a double-move that saw him burn Sauce Gardner for a massive touchdown, though he may have simply been working back to the quarterback before realizing the throw was going over his head. Either way, Burks turned on the jets, tracked down the ball, and ran in the Commanders’ only touchdown of the day. Burks isn’t on the fantasy radar despite the long catch, but it’s nice to see him carving out a role in Washington.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks caught both of his targets for 13 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 3 win over the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: You heard that right, Treylon Burks plays for the Commanders. The former first-round pick hauled in just his third receiving touchdown of his career on a throw over the middle from Marcus Mariota. Burks has the size to be a red-zone threat, but despite the scoring play Sunday, he’s too far down the depth chart to be a fantasy consideration.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Last Man Standig’s Ben Standig reports that Commanders WR Treylon Burks (foot soreness) sat out Thursday’s “on-field work.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Commanders coach Dan Quinn also said the team doesn’t see the soreness as a long-term issue, but it is a disappointing follow-up to what was reportedly a strong showing for Burks at the first training camp practice. The Commanders have a very thin wide receiver corps, so every injury matters. Hopefully, Burks is back before long.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Commanders re-signed WR Treylon Burks to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks had a Catch Of The Year candidate on his lone touchdown catch last season, finishing with a 10/130/1 line in spot duty. He’s not likely to start out the year in the Commanders starting three-wide, but he’s a reasonable depth option and should have a good shot to win a roster spot.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks caught 2-of-4 targets for 12 yards in the Commanders’ Week 18 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks signed to the Commanders’ practice squad in October after the Titans released him. He finished his year with the Commanders totaling 10 receptions for 130 yards and a touchdown. Burks’ touchdown was a candidate for catch of the year, a highlight-reel five-yard grab with one hand in Week 13 against the Broncos. With Luke McCaffrey and Jaylin Lane out towards the end of the season, Burks became the team’s WR3, seeing a variety of targets as an outside receiver opposite Terry McLaurin. He is certainly an option to return to Washington next season, though he is likely to be a depth piece on whichever team employs him for 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks caught 1-of-4 targets for a five-yard touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 13 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks showed a glimpse at what made him a first-round pick for the Titans in the 2022 draft as he elevated over a defender for a one-handed touchdown in the third quarter. Unfortunately for him, that would go down as his only reception of the evening with the return of Terry McLaurin. He does not hold any fantasy value while playing behind McLaurin, Deebo Samuel, and Jaylin Lane.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Jaylin Lane (hip) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: In addition to Terry McLaurin, Noah Brown and Treylon Burks were also limited today. It’s tough to say which depth options will suit up this week. With Marcus Mariota expected to make another start, it’s a situation fantasy managers don’t need to get bogged down by. Deebo Samuel is the only game in town until McLaurin returns. Zach Ertz is also in the mix as a volume-based TE1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Commanders WR Treylon Burks (finger) will not play in Washington’s Week 11 game against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: He didn’t travel to Spain with the team. Burks led the team in receiving yards last week — even just reading that in words conveys the direness of the Commanders passing attack right now. Jaylin Lane will have more paths to WR5 success now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.headline: Treylon Burks caught 3-of-3 targets for 58 yards in the Commanders’ Week 10 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/treylon-bu.analysis: Burks astonishingly led the Commanders in receiving yards this week. His performance was highlighted by hauling in a deep, contested catch along the left sideline for 38 yards. Across two 2025 appearances, he has now caught 4-of-4 targets for 75 yards. Boasting tight end-esque size and athleticism, Burks is sauntering toward waiver wire consideration. Burks notably out-snapped Commanders rookie WR Jaylin Lane 21-15. Lane caught 1-of-1 targets for 41 yards. The Commanders face the Dolphins in Week 11.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo caught all seven targets for 69 yards in the Commanders’ Week 6 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Okonkwo was thrust into an increased role with the departure of lead wide receiver Terry McLaurin in the first quarter, operating as the primary option through the air for much of the game. Veteran wide receiver Stefon Diggs continued to operate in a situational role, making Okonkwo a priority start when the Commanders come out of their Week 7 bye to face the Eagles in Week 8.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Stefon Diggs (hamstring) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said he is hopeful Diggs will get some practice reps in later this week. Diggs missed Week 5 with the hamstring issue, and a DNP today puts him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 6, even if Quinn remains optimistic. Terry McLaurin and Chig Okonkwo led the team in receiving last week. McLaurin should pull away from Okonkwo as he puts more time between himself and the hamstring injury that previously knocked him out for a week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo caught 4-of-6 targets for 60 yards in the Commanders’ Week 5 tie with the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Okonkwo caught two passes on the Commander’s opening and immediately topped his previous best game of the season. He hauled in passes of 11 and 23 yards on back-to-back catches before Jacory Croskey-Merritt ended the drive with a 33-yard touchdown run. Okonkwo would come up with a 25-yard reception later in the second quarter on a drive that ended with a Drew Stevens field goal, but was targeted just one time in the second half. It was an overall nice outing for Okonkwo, but fantasy managers shouldn’t rush to add him to their lineups. He’ll be a boom-or-bust streaming option in Week 6 against the Niners.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) is not on the final injury report for Week 5 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Okonkwo got in a full practice on Friday after consecutive limited sessions. With Stefon Diggs (hamstring) out, Terry McLaurin (hamstring) questionable and Jayden Daniels (elbow) returning, Okonkwo could warrant top-12 positional treatment this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: With Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs both absent for a second day in a row on Thursday, Okonkwo could catch some desperation TE1 steam on Friday. He seems on track to play and Jayden Daniels should provide a more reliable passing floor than he had last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Okonwko returned to the lineup last week after missing a handful of games with the hamstring injury. His limited designation today is likely just maintenance. With Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs banged up, he should see more work in Week 5. Okonkwo is in the TE2 mix for Sunday’s game versus the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo caught 2-of-4 targets for five yards in the Commanders’ Week 4 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Okonkwo was back in action today after missing the last two games with a hamstring issue. With Marcus Mariota exiting this game early because of an injury, the passing attack was out of whack from the jump. There wasn’t much of a chance to reinstall Okonkwo into the mix this week. The hope is that he will earn more work with Jayden Daniels potentially back in the lineup in Week 5, but fantasy managers will need to see it to believe it with Okonkwo.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinnsaid Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) will play in Week 4 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: After missing the last two games with a hamstring injury, Okonkwo will suit up when the Commanders take on the Colts in London. The 27-year-old tight end caught 2-of-3 targets for 16 yards in the Commanders’ Week 1 loss to the Eagles and ran 22 routes before exiting late in the third quarter. He has the chance to turn into a meaningful contributor in Washington’s passing game, but fantasy managers shouldn’t rush to put him in their lineups until we get a better sense of his role over the next few weeks. In addition to Okonkwo, Quinn also said LB Frankie Luvu (groin) would return in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: That’s two limited practices in a row for Okonkwo, who has missed the last two weeks with the hamstring injury. It would be nice to see a full practice, but he’s at least trending in the right direction to hit the questionable line on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.headline: Commanders TE Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chig-okonk.analysis: Okonkwo was limited today after traveling with the team to London last night. Both signs are positive. Okonkwo has not played since injuring his hamstring in Week 1. If active, he will likely just be a boom-bust TE2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White rushed seven times for 27 yards in the Commanders’ Week 6 loss to the 49ers, adding 30 yards and a touchdown on four receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: The Commanders immediately found themselves in a negative game environment, managing just 17 offensive plays and 90 yards of total offense in the first half. While White found the end zone from nine yards out in the fourth quarter on an in-breaking route, the backfield split amongst White, Jeremy McNichols, and Austin Ekeler was troubling for fantasy managers looking to the former as a potential option with lead back Jacory Croskey-Merritt on injured reserve. White and the Commanders head to their bye week at a 1-4-1 record and some serious questions to answer, the least of which is the current state of their backfield.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Commanders ruled out RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) for Week 6 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: No surprise here. Croskey-Merritt has been dealing with a groin injury since the start of the season. This week he couldn’t practice and has since been officially ruled out for the Commanders’ Monday Night Football matchup against the 49ers. Croskey-Merritt will get a two-week break with Washington on bye in Week 7. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler figure to handle the majority of the backfield touches in his absence with White being the preferred fantasy option between the two.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: Croskey-Merritt has played through multiple injuries this year. We still think he has a chance to face the 49ers in Week 6’s Monday Night Football game. Rachaad White (shoulder) sported a red non-contact jersey for the first time this week, and was downgraded to limited today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Austin Ekeler (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: Ekeler and Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) are both ailing, though the latter player sat out entirely. Rachaad White (shoulder) and Jeremy McNichols (quad) are both practicing in full. Croskey-Merritt is the only fantasy-relevant Commanders running back at this time, assuming he is good to go on Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White rushed seven times for 18 yards in the Commanders’ Week 5 tie against the Giants, adding one reception for two additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: White continued to serve as the RB2 behind Jacory Croskey-Merritt and led the backfield with 11 snaps on third down. While his role remained largely the same, even with Austin Ekeler active, White offered nothing of fantasy value in this one. He saw only one target on the afternoon, and could continue to have his fantasy upside limited as long as Jayden Daniels is scrambling away from pressure rather than dumping it off to his checkdown options. Fantasy managers should avoid White in Week 6 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White (shoulder) will play in Week 5 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: In addition to White, the Commanders will also get RG Sam Cosmi back after missing the last two games with a concussion. White will likely return to his role as the team’s third-down/pass-catching back, but could be at risk of having Austin Ekeler eat into some of his workload. Fantasy managers hoping for White to return to the 10.3 touches/gm he was averaging before his injury may want to temper expectations and leave him on the bench while we wait to see how Ekeler is factored into the game plan.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White (shoulder) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: He looks to be on track to return to the backfield in Week 5. What percentage of carries that leaves him in a post-Ekeler world appears to be open to interpretation. We would not recommend starting him in any reasonably-sized league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: White injured his shoulder in Week 3. He did not practice once last week before being ruled out on Friday. A limited practice today puts him on track to suit up in Week 5. With Austin Ekeler now on the roster, White’s role as the team’s top back on passing situations could be at risk. Fantasy managers will want to leave him on the bench for another week, even if he is cleared to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White (shoulder) will not play in Washington’s Week 4 game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: He didn’t practice at any point this week after suffering a shoulder injury in Week 3. He has to be considered questionable for Week 5 at this point. ‘Bill’ Croskey-Merritt figures to shoulder the majority of the workload for the Commanders this week and is a reasonable FLEX play against the Colts. Freshly-signed Austin Ekeler figures to handle third-down work.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.headline: Rachaad White (shoulder) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/rachaad-wh.analysis: With two DNPs to start the week, White looks unlikely to suit up for Week 4 against the Colts. Austin Ekeler traveled with the team after signing with the team earlier this week, so he could ultimately take on White’s role. Backup running back Kayton Allen could also see more work, but Jacory Croskey-Merritt remains the clear lead back in Washington for now. He is on the RB2/3 border for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: Jayden Daniels completed 29-of-40 passes for 300 yards and two touchdowns in the Commanders’ 23-17, Week 6 loss to the 49ers, adding 10 yards on four carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: The Commanders gained just 90 yards of total offense and ran just 17 offensive plays in the first half, taking a 20-3 deficit into the break. Two quick touchdown drives to end the third quarter and begin the fourth quarter had the team in position to pull off an improbable comeback but two critical errors from Daniels sank that effort. The first error occurred on fourth down in the red zone with just over two minutes to play, when the team was late to break the huddle and ended up taking their first timeout down by six. They would fail to convert but would get the ball back with no timeouts and 52 seconds left. Daniels then committed an intentional grounding penalty from the San Francisco 28 with 16 seconds left, which incurred a loss of down and a 10-second runoff on the clock. The game would end on the following play. That now makes consecutive contests with late-game clock mismanagement that cost the Commanders potential wins. Rumors continue to swirl about a potential coaching change as the Commanders limp into their bye at a 1-4-1 record.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: Jayden Daniels completed 17-of-25 passes for 199 yards in the Commanders’ 27-27, Week 5 tie with the Giants, adding nine carries for 103 additional yards and two touchdowns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Daniels turned in one of the best games of his career on the ground on Sunday against the Giants.
