Daniels broke off an uncontested 38-yard touchdown run in the third quarter to put the Commanders up 19-6, and later broke free for a 26-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter to again extend the Commanders’ lead. Both runs came on scrambles where the Giants seemingly forgot Daniels was a threat to run at any moment, and Daniels made the most of his opportunities. With the Commanders in range for a game-winning field goal late in overtime, Daniels inexplicably took a sack with no timeouts left on what appeared to be an attempt to center the ball in time for the game-winning try. We’ll likely get an explanation from both Daniels and head coach Dan Quinn on that final play, but Washington snatched defeat from the jaws of victory to move to 1-3-1 on the season. Despite the late-game gaffe, Daniels looked on-point for most of the afternoon, but struggled at times against the blitz, as the Giants brought pressure in several key spots to force Daniels to get the ball out quick or throw it away. Daniels looked like the elite dual threat fantasy managers want to see, and will be firmly in the QB1 ranks in next week’s game against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports “there are doctors around the NFL who believe it’s a matter of when, not if, Jayden Daniels hurts his left elbow again.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Schefter immediately added the caveat that the “overwhelming opinion” among doctors was that playing with a brace was a viable option. Daniels reportedly contemplated surgery after dislocating his elbow for the second time in less than a year. He opted against it and missed two games. Daniels is now set to return for Week 5 against the Giants. The Commanders could scale back his rushing for the time being, but OC David Blough already dismissed the idea that the playbook would be limited because of Daniels’ elbow injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Jayden Daniels (elbow) is “not 100 percent” healthy yet.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Rapoport, typically cheery on the injury front, said that there are still “a lot of questions, going forward, for Jayden Daniels.” The bottom line is that Daniels is still rehabbing the elbow in his non-throwing arm. He should be able to throw and run effectively, putting him squarely in the QB1 tier, but re-injury risk remains a factor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said Jayden Daniels (elbow) will start in Week 5 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Daniels appeared to be close to playing in Week 4 against the Colts before ultimately being ruled out. His being upgraded to a full participant in Thursday’s practice suggested he was a virtual lock to start in Week 5, barring any unexpected setbacks. Daniels will wear a brace on his left arm for the rest of the season in hopes of avoiding a three-peat of his dislocated elbow. Daniels will be without Stefon Diggs (hamstring) for Sunday’s game, and rainy/windy conditions are currently in the forecast. We’ll conservatively project him as a mid-to-low-end QB1 in what could be less-than-ideal conditions on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: Commanders offensive coordinator David Blough said Jayden Daniels is a “full go” when asked if his elbow injury would create any limitations in the game plan.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Daniels is practicing in full and is expected to return to the lineup this week. He has suffered the same elbow dislocation twice in the past year, but his game-changing running ability is a big part of what makes Daniels a potential superstar quarterback. Blough might be more tactile with how he calls quarterback runs, but they will still be in the playbook this week. Daniels will be a low-end QB1 once he is officially cleared to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: ESPN’s John Keim reports Jayden Daniels (elbow) is expected to be a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo already reported that Daniels is expected to play in Week 5 and a full practice to open the week all but confirms his update. With Marcus Mariota also banged up, seventh-round rookie Athan Kaliakmanis would have been the next man up. He will back Daniels up as long as the latter doesn’t suffer any setbacks. The Commanders will likely dial back the designed runs for their franchise quarterback, but fantasy managers have to start him as a low-end QB1 as long as he’s on the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Jayden Daniels (elbow) is “on track” to start for the Commanders in Washington’s Week 5 game against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Washington will be trying to keep their season on the tracks after falling to 1-3 against the Colts while having to go to third-stringer Athan Kaliakmanis. It’s unsurprising that they’re rushing Daniels back. Even if you factor in an elevated chance of re-injury, Daniels probably clears the QB1 line for fantasy managers against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Marcus Mariota suffered a sprained MCL in the Commanders’ Week 4 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: The Commanders were forced to go to rookie seventh-rounder Athan Kaliakmanis after Mariota went down in yesterday’s game. Mariota sprained the MCL in the same knee during the preseason, and it would be surprising if Mariota was cleared in time for Week 5’s game against the Giants. If he’s unable to play, Kaliakmanis could make his first career start if Jayden Daniels (elbows) isn’t ready to return. Daniels traveled with the team to London for last week’s game and was limited in all three practices. He seemed close to playing against the Colts, and with the Commanders sitting at 1-3 and their season potentially on the line, it wouldn’t be surprising if he did suit up in a pivotal divisional matchup against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.headline: Commanders QB Jayden Daniels (elbow) could play in Week 5 against the Giants, reports Jonathan Jones of the Athletic.
https://www.nbcsports.com/jayden-daniels.analysis: Daniels practiced in a limited capacity this week, but will ultimately sit out the Week 4 matchup against the Colts. According to Jones, sources in Washington believe Daniels could return in Week 5 against the Giants if he gets in a full week of practice this week. While Daniels is going to play through the same elbow injury he had last year, offseason surgery hasn’t been ruled out. Marcus Mariota will continue to start under center for the Commanders in Daniels’ absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquez-va.headline: The Athletic’s Mike DeFabo reports Steelers are expected to sign Marquez Valdes-Scantling.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquez-va.analysis: Say it ain’t so, a former Rodgers favorite set to rejoin him during his twilight tour. Valdes-Scantling is reportedly set to sign to the Pittsburgh practice squad and could work his way to the active roster considering the absence of Michael Pittman, the latter of whom was moved to injured reserve Saturday. There likely won’t be any fantasy value to speak of.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquez-va.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquez-va.analysis: Johnston is on track to play, but this wide receiver corps is very banged up. KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring) and Brenen Thompson (quad) remained limited as well. Marquez Valdes-Scantling (ribs) upgraded to full.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquez-va.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquez-va.analysis: Johnston, KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring), Brenen Thompson (quad), and Marquez Valdes-Scantling (rib) were all limited Wednesday. Lambert-Smith currently has his practice window for return from IR open while the others are dealing with a varying level of ailments. Johnston is the best fantasy option out of this group, but he is only worth FLEX consideration in the deepest of leagues. With Ladd McConkey (foot) also limited, the Chargers have several “maybes” ahead of a Week 6 matchup against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquez-va.headline: Marquez Valdes-Scantling caught 2-of-3 targets for 22 yards in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquez-va.analysis: Valdes-Scantling finished second in receiving yards for the Chargers against the Broncos. That’s not great. The veteran wideout is going to get some opportunities because of the injuries, but that shouldn’t equate to a chance to help a fantasy roster. He’ll face the Chiefs in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquez-va.headline: Chargers signed WR Marquez Valdes-Scantling to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquez-va.analysis: Valdes-Scantling worked out with the Chargers earlier Tuesday and now signs with the team’s practice squad. The 31-year-old spent the offseason with the Cowboys and has been a journeyman since his first four seasons with the Packers, also spending time with the Chiefs, Bills, Saints, 49ers, and Steelers over his career. The Chargers add Valdes-Scantling as depth with Ladd McConkey dealing with a rib injury and KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring) heading to injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquez-va.headline: Free agent WR Marquez Valdes-Scantling is working out with the Chargers on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquez-va.analysis: He was cut by the Cowboys at the end of training camp and has been looking for his next opportunity. Valdes-Scantling’s appearance here probably doesn’t bode overly well for Ladd McConkey’s status for Week 2, though obviously that’s just trying to read the tea leaves.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquez-va.headline: Cowboys released Marquez Valdes-Scantling.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquez-va.analysis: Valdes-Scantling signed a one-year deal with the Cowboys this offseason. He barely garnered more than the veteran minimum and was clearly nothing more than a depth option for the team. With well over 100 career games across six teams to his name, MVS should still find a team willing to carry him on their practice squad in the coming days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquez-va.headline: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said WR Marquez Valdes-Scantling “is doing an awesome job,” and will contribute on special teams this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquez-va.analysis: Valdes-Scantling has logged only 78 special teams snaps in his career, with 49 of them coming in his 2018 rookie season. Schottenheimer said that Valdes-Scantling has the “speed to be a gunner,” so it sounds like he will not be returning punts and kicks. Don’t count on any return touchdowns appearing in his box score. The Fort Worth Star-Telegram’s Nick Harris adds that Valdes-Scantling caught two passes and dropped one on Tuesday. His hands have always been an issue. While he will help out QB Dak Prescott with a few big plays this season, Valdes-Scantling is unlikely to be a reliable fantasy contributor in his age-31 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquez-va.headline: Cowboys signed WR Marquez Valdes-Scantling, formerly of the Steelers, to a one-year, $1.26 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquez-va.analysis: The deal includes a $187,500 signing bonus and appears to simply be a depth move. MVS spent time with the 49ers and Steelers last season, catching 14 passes for 120 yards and a touchdown. The veteran speedster has bounced around to four different teams since parting ways with the Chiefs after the 2023 season and hasn’t caught more than 17 passes at any of his stops. He’ll likely be battling to earn a roster spot in camp and carries little fantasy value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquez-va.headline: Marquez Valdes-Scantling caught 3-of-5 targets for 26 yards in the Steelers’ Wildcard loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/marquez-va.analysis: Following Aaron Rodgers to Pittsburgh after a cacophony of whispers in Mike Tomlin’s ears and a failed second-year leap from Roman Wilson, Valdes-Scantling’s season ends with just 14 catches for 120 yards and one touchdown in split time between the 49ers and Steelers. It is difficult to imagine him sticking on an NFL roster with Rodgers expected to retire considering a myriad of mental errors on the field in 2025, regardless of his blocking ability or veteran status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-br.headline: Seahawks activated Anthony Bradford’s 21-day practice window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-br.analysis: Bradford was placed on injured reserve after Week 1, seeing his first step to a return processed with the activation of his 21-day practice window. Head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters Monday that the veteran guard has a “really good chance” to return for Sunday Night Football against the Chiefs in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-br.headline: Seahawks placed OG Anthony Bradford on injured reserve with a knee injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-br.analysis:
Bradford missed Week 2 and will now miss at least four more games with the knee injury. The Seahawks also signed S Rodney Thomas to the active roster and signed DT
Uso Seumalo and WR Malick Meiga to the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-br.headline: Seahawks OT Josh Jones (ankle) is out for Week 4 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-br.analysis: Jones did not practice all week with an ankle injury and is out for Thursday’s game against the Cardinals. He has played sparingly in the Seahawks’ three games as depth for the offensive line. OG Anthony Bradford (back) and LB Boye Mafe (toe) are both listed as questionable while S Nick Emmanwori (ankle) is doubtful for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-br.headline: Seahawks placed OL Anthony Bradford (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-br.analysis: He’ll be out until at least Week 18. Christian Haynes replaced Bradford, who has been a bit of a sieve this year, at guard. Bradford has 10 penalties and a 53.0 PFF pass block grade in 11 starts this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-br.headline: Seahawks OL Anthony Bradford (leg) exited Week 12 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-br.analysis: Bradford went down with an apparent leg injury in the first quarter of the Seahawks’ Week 12 game against the Cardinals. He was listed as doubtful to return. Rookie Christian Haynes entered the game for Bradford.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-br.headline: Seahawks signed No. 108 overall pick G Anthony Bradford to a four-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-br.analysis: Seattle now have seven of their 10 draft picks under contract as OTAs open around the league. Bradford is expected to serve as a depth piece behind presumed starting left guard Damien Lewis in the coming season, but the fourth-round rookie still has OTAs, camp, and the preseason to stake his claim to a starting role to begin 2023.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-br.headline: Seahawks selected LSU G Anthony Bradford with the No. 108 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-br.analysis: Bradford (6’4/337) was a 4-star recruit, and the 12th-ranked offensive guard in the 2019 recruiting class, from Muskegon, Michigan according to 247 Sports. Bradford has an exceedingly thick lower half, especially when compared to his average upper half, that should eventually lend itself to giving a good base for anchoring or driving defenders off the ball. For now, the LSU mauler is a raw athlete with good heft at about average height. His 92nd percentile 10-yard split time turned heads considering the amount of mass that he needs to move to get going. He has good sustain on his blocks as is active on the inside always looking for work. Whenever there is a body being thrown to the turf in the trenches, Bradford is usually on either side of the exchange. With his size, a coach will clamor to select Bradford. However, he will need development getting from block to block, because once he gets his hands on a defender, he can at least survive and at most get a pancake.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-br.headline: LSU received a verbal commitment from four-star 2019 T Anthony Bradford.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-br.analysis: Bradford (6'5/320) took official visits to both Tennessee and LSU this spring, though neither trip was widely reported. The Muskegon, Michigan, native is something of an old soul and does not maintain an active presence on social media. Nor does he own a cell phone. A big, long tackle prospect who shows plenty of moxie on his feet when moving laterally, Bradford could potentially play either guard or right tackle with the Tigers after he puts pen to paper. His upside position will likely come on the interior of the line, though. Rivals ranks him as the No. 186 overall prospect in the 2019 class.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-br.headline: LSU four-star 2019 verbal T commit Anthony Bradford was named the position group MVP at the Rivals 3 Stripe camp regional in Chicago over the weekend.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-br.analysis: “The way Bradford moves at [6-foot-5, 320 pounds] is remarkable, and he handled two smaller, quicker defensive ends with ease during the one-on-one session (in camp),” Helmholdt writes. While his size would seem more of a fit for the interior of the line, Helmholdt passes along that LSU plans on starting him out at right tackle. His athleticism makes that possible. On the Rivals rankings board for the 2019 cycle, Bradford ranks as the No. 186 overall prospect in the class.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-br.headline: LSU four-star 2019 verbal T commit Anthony Bradford won Big Man Bench honors after turning in 31 reps on the bench press at the Rivals100 Five-Star Challenge.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/anthony-br.analysis: Bradford (6'5/325) notched a career-best at the bar while taking part in the premiere camp in Atlanta on Thursday. His 31 reps rivaled what we saw from NFL-caliber offensive linemen at the combine in the winter. To wit, the only prospects in Indianapolis who would have topped his 31 hoists of the bar would have been Will Hernandez (37 reps), Quenton Nelson (35), Braden Smith (35) and Colby Gossett (32). That Bradford is already comparably in range with those players is impressive given that he has not yet even embarked on his senior year of high school. Rivals ranks Bradford as the No. 124 overall prospect in the 2019 class.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mazi-smith.headline: Packers signed DT Mazi Smith, formerly of the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mazi-smith.analysis: Smith, a former first-round pick by the Cowboys in 2023, appeared in one game for the Dolphins earlier this season and has appeared in just nine games since 2025. The 25-year-old lineman has tallied 57 tackles and two sacks in his career and wouldn’t be asked to serve as anything more than added depth for the Packers if he were elevated to the 53-man roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mazi-smith.headline: Dolphins signed RB Jarquez Hunter to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mazi-smith.analysis: Hunter was notably acquired for Tutu Atwell in the preseason but was released during final cuts. The Dolphins now bring him back as depth in the running back room. Also notably on the practice squad is former first-round defensive lineman Mazi Smith. The Dolphins rounded out the practice squad with RB Carlos Washington, WR Jalen Reagor, WR Will Sheppard, CB Ethan Bonner, DE Max Llewellyn, TE Tre Watson, OT Gottlieb Ayedze, DL Jordan Miller, EDGE Clelin Ferrell, EDGE Amari Gainer, EDGE Rodney McGraw, LB Liam Anderson, CB Jaylin Simpson, and S Major Burns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mazi-smith.headline: Jets waived DT Mazi Smith.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mazi-smith.analysis: Smith was one of the key pieces in the trade that sent Quinnen Williams to Dallas. The Jets declined his fifth-year option in April before eventually releasing him at final roster cuts. Smith graded as one of the worst defensive linemen in the league in 2025, per Pro Football Focus, and will likely be forced to settle for a depth role moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mazi-smith.headline: Jets declined DT Mazi Smith’s fifth-year team option.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mazi-smith.analysis: The Jets acquired Smith when they traded Quinnen Williams to Dallas. Smith only appeared in three games for Gang Green last year. He did not record any counting stats. Smith now enters a contract year with a lot to prove.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mazi-smith.headline: Cowboys acquired DT Quinnen Williams from the Jets for DT Mazi Smith, a 2026 second-round pick and a 2027 first-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mazi-smith.analysis: Williams is notably not Micah Parsons, but if for some reason you can’t have Parsons, he’s probably on the short list of defensive line stars in the league. He’s a star run defender — something we seem to recall the Cowboys needing — by virtue of splash plays. Williams has only one sack this year, but the Jets have not held many leads and Williams does have 23.5 sacks in his past seasons. The Jets star defender has 1.5 years remaining on a four-year, $96 million extension signed in 2023. So the Cowboys will make sure to have someone with an expiring contract distraction on the roster in 2026, as nature abhors a vacuum. The Jets are now a conceptual football team, the closest thing we’ve seen to one since the Sashi Brown Browns anyway. So from that standpoint, Mazi Smith, a theoretical defensive tackle, is a great addition.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mazi-smith.headline: The Athletic’s Jon Machota believe the Cowboys “still need to see more” from DT Mazi Smith for him to make the 53-man roster.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mazi-smith.analysis: Smith has played in both preseason games — the Cowboys have sat most of their starters — and he was still on the field in the second half against the Ravens on Saturday. The former first-round pick’s 2024 PFF grade was 208th among 220 interior defensive linemen and it sure doesn’t seem like the Cowboys feel he’s played any better in training camp. “For a defense that badly needs to improve at stopping the run, an outside addition might be a requirement before Week 1,” Machota adds.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mazi-smith.headline: Cowboys CB Trevon Diggs (foot) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mazi-smith.analysis: Defensive tackle Mazi Smith is listed as questionable. Diggs missed Wednesday’s practice but was back on the field by Thursday. He was a full participant in Friday’s session before being cleared. Diggs notched one interception and two pass breakups in Week 1 before he and the rest of the Dallas defense gave up 44 points to the Saints last week. He will look to get back on track versus Lamar Jackson on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mazi-smith.headline: Cowboys DT Mazi Smith suffered an allergic reaction at Friday’s practice and did not travel with the team to Las Vegas for Saturday’s preseason game.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mazi-smith.analysis: The Cowboys didn’t provide specifics about Smith’s status but said he will be reevaluated on Saturday morning. After his evaluation, the team also said they would update his status for Saturday’s game. It doesn’t sound like there’s too much to worry about here for Smith, who totaled 13 tackles and three TFLs for the team as a rookie last season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mazi-smith.headline: Michael Gehlken of the Dallas morning news Cowboys DT Mazi Smith is said to be “fine” after an MRI on his knee revealed no damage.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mazi-smith.analysis: Smith is reportedly dealing with tendinitis and discomfort in his knee and sat out the team’s practice on Tuesday. The rookie first-rounder is expected to be an immediate contributor along the defensive front this season, but this string of knee issues will need to be resolved before he takes to the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mazi-smith.headline: Cowboys signed No. 26 overall pick DT Mazi Smith to a four-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mazi-smith.analysis: The Cowboys signed their entire rookie class on Thursday ahead of rookie minicamp. Smith (6’3/323) has the ideal frame for a nose tackle and his bench press number of 34 shows his underlying power and his commitment to being a weight room warrior. Before the 2022 season, he was ranked No. 1 on Bruce Feldman’s Freaks List. While he is still very raw, Smith has a good sense of when to go low on offensive linemen, and when he needs to keep his head up to play the point of attack. His body leverage is rare, though his unrefined hand technique leaves much to be desired. With only two years of starting experience under his belt, he will probably improve his play leverage with additional reps. The lack of production at the college level probably has to do with being confined to the nose in Ann Arbor. However, 85 tackles in his two starting years show the potential to make an impact in every game. If he can learn how to pass rush, Smith can be a force for Dan Quinn’s defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kobie-turn.headline: Rams placed DL Kobie Turner (groin) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kobie-turn.analysis: It’s a tough injury for Turner, who is in the final year of his rookie contract and will miss at least four weeks. He’s been a mainstay of Los Angeles’ defense over his first three years with several high-hurry seasons and stellar run defense. The Rams interior defense has taken a big hit today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kobie-turn.headline: Rams selected Wake Forest DL Kobie Turner with the No. 89 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kobie-turn.analysis: Turner (6’2.5/293) was a walk-on at FCS-subdivision Richmond out of high school, where he redshirted, then played for four years before graduate transferring to Wake Forest in 2022. After walking on at Richmond and earning a scholarship, Turner racked up 16 sacks and 33.5 tackles for loss in four years against FCS competition. While the Combine snub is only average in size and weight, if not a bit of a tweener, he overcomes his lack of arm length by being active with his hands. He has a bit of a bowling ball tendency, where his aggression and activity in small spaces creates more havoc than any single skill or technique. His feet are his asset when it comes to play leverage, as his short shuttle time of 4.49 shows great change of direction in the interior. His evaluation relies on his production at a lower level of competition as he only held a reserve role at Wake Forest. However, his good work ethic and non-traditional path to the NFL will make for a good story and win the favor of a coach once he can get into camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/poona-ford.headline: Rams placed DT Poona Ford (biceps) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/poona-ford.analysis: It will end his season. Ford has been a find for the Rams the last two years as a premium run-stuffer. This injury will test their defensive line depth. The soon-to-be 31-year-old will be a release candidate after the season with an $11.08 million cap hit of which the Rams can save $9.25 million by cutting him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/poona-ford.headline: Rams agreed to terms with DT Poona Ford, formerly of the Chargers, on a three-year, $30 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/poona-ford.analysis: Per ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, the deal is technically worth just under $30 million and includes $17 million guaranteed. Ford began his career in Seattle before joining the Bills as a free agent in 2023. Buffalo only brought Ford to eight games and he signed a prove-it deal with the Chargers last offseason. Ford started all 17 games for LA and totaled eight TFLs with three sacks. He also batted five passes and intercepted one throw. Ford is primarily a run-stuffer, making him a perfect fit for a Rams roster suddenly loaded with young pass-rush talent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/poona-ford.headline: Chargers agreed to terms with DT Poona Ford, formerly of the Bills, on a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/poona-ford.analysis: Coming off back-to-back underwhelming campaigns, Ford missed a big chunk of 2023 with injury. He will be hoping for a “Harbaugh boost” under a coaching staff known for extreme discipline and focus on fundamentals. Although he has 11 career sacks from the interior, Ford’s job in L.A. will be stopping the run.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/poona-ford.headline: Bills declared CB Kaiir Elam, DT Poona Ford, S Damar Hamlin, OL Germain Ifedi, and OL Alec Anderson inactive for Week 3 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/poona-ford.analysis: While Kaiir Elam gets a lot of attention for being inactive since he was Buffalo’s first round pick last year; however, Poona Ford may be the bigger name. Ford was active for each of Buffalo’s first two games but will take a seat in Week 3 with the Bills choosing to activate DE Kingsley Jonathan instead. The choice signals that Buffalo is opting to go with an extra pass-rusher than they have the first two games. It signals how valuable Buffalo thinks getting pressure on Sam Howell will be; however, if the rain comes in the middle of the game, as expected, and this becomes a game about controlling the running games, the Bills could miss Ford.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/poona-ford.headline: Bills signed DT Poona Ford, formerly of the Seahawks, to a one-year, $3.25 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/poona-ford.analysis: Seattle adding Cameron Young in the draft apparently made them comfortable enough to not match this deal. Ford is coming off a rough year after being asked to work out of his comfort zone in different gaps. He’d had four straight years of PFF grades over 68.4 and was a good run defender prior to 2023. This looks like a solid bounceback pickup for Buffalo.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/poona-ford.headline: Seahawks signed DT Poona Ford to a two-year contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/poona-ford.analysis: Ford was an undrafted free agent in 2018 but quickly became one of the twitchier defensive tackles in the NFL. Now he’s paid like it. His deal is worth “close to $14 million” per NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero. With the extension, Poona and the Seahawks will dodge the restricted free agency tender. The Texas alum has tackle counts of 21, 32, and 40 over his first three seasons as a rotational interior lineman. Ford and Jarran Reed are a strong duo up front. Seattle was ninth in rushing EPA defense in 2020.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/poona-ford.headline: Seahawks DT Poona Ford (calf) said he expects to play on Sunday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/poona-ford.analysis: The player said he’d play, but coach Pete Carroll mentioned Ford would still be limited mid-week. Bryan Mone would start again if Ford’s soft tissue injury doesn’t heal in time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/poona-ford.headline: Seahawks DT Poona Ford (calf) is week to week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/poona-ford.analysis: Ford suffered a calf strain in Seattle’s season opener. He started and had two tackles before going down. Bryan Mone is Ford’s backup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/poona-ford.headline: Seahawks sign Texas DT Poona Ford.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/poona-ford.analysis: Ford (6’0/306) made 30 starts on the Longhorns’ defensive line, earning 2017 Big 12 Defensive Lineman of the Year and logging 20.5 career tackles for loss but only four sacks. Snubbed for a Combine invite, Ford tested as a sub-par athlete at Texans’ Pro Day. Ford won with leverage and power in the Big 12, but he seems likely to struggle to carry over that success into the NFL.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.headline: Commanders activated Jeremy McNichols (quad) off injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.analysis: He’ll likely be Washington’s third-string back tonight, but one thing that two years and five weeks of Dan Quinn being in charge have taught us is that no one ever expects that Jeremy McNichols takeover until it’s too late. The backfield mix in Washington is weak and anyone could emerge in a post-'Bill’ world.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.headline: Austin Ekeler (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.analysis: Ekeler and Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) are both ailing, though the latter player sat out entirely. Rachaad White (shoulder) and Jeremy McNichols (quad) are both practicing in full. Croskey-Merritt is the only fantasy-relevant Commanders running back at this time, assuming he is good to go on Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.headline: Commanders placed RB Jeremy McNichols (quad) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.analysis: McNichols will start the season sidelined with a linger quad injury he suffered in mid-August. Used primarily as a pass-catching back, McNichols could see playing time later this season if Rachaad White or Jacory Croskey-Merritt miss any time. He will miss at least the first four games of the season and should remain on waivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.headline: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Jeremy McNichols (quad) will be sidelined a few weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.analysis: McNichols probably is no higher than fourth on the depth chart in Washington behind ‘Bill,’ Rachaad White, and Kaytron Allen. Missing time due to injury doesn’t bode well for him making the initial 53-man roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.headline: Commanders RB Jeremy McNichols (quad) is out Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.analysis: This is the second straight practice McNichols has missed with the quad issue. He’s slated to function as Washington’s No. 3 back behind some combination of Rachaad White and Jacory Croskey-Merritt this season. McNichols was efficient in 2025, averaging five yards per carry on 44 rushes in Washington.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.headline: Last Man Standig’s Ben Standig reports that Commanders RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (soft tissue) sat out the team’s three-week organized team activities program.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.analysis: Whether Croskey-Merritt can participate in the Commanders’ three-day mandatory minicamp, from June 16-18, is unknown. That said, Standig believes RB coach Anthony Lynn’s “positivity is notable.” Lynn thinks the team can take Croskey-Merritt’s game “to another level and get him potentially in the lead role.” To do this, Croskey-Merritt must take on more responsibility in the passing game this summer. Lynn adds that the young back’s “hands are very good, his movement skills are very good, and there’s no reason why he couldn’t win routes.” The staff is happy with its new-look backfield, but Standing writes that RBs Rachaad White, Jeremy McNichols and Jerome Ford “are not high-volume playmaking threats,” like “Bill” is, and rookie RB Allen is still getting up to speed. Once Croskey-Merritt arrives, he must prove that he can meaningfully contribute as a receiver and as a pass protector. Doing so would unlock a fantasy-friendly role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.headline: Commanders re-signed RB Jeremy McNichols to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.analysis: McNichols is the third running back to sign with Washington in recent days. The 30-year-old vet has been used sparingly over the last two seasons with the Commanders, but has totaled 705 yards from scrimmage and five touchdowns on 133 touches. McNichols would likely have a camp battle with Jerome Ford to play on passing downs on the current depth chart, meaning he could be in some risk of starting off the year on the practice squad. But after playing 34 games with the Commanders the last two years, we think it’s clear the current administration thinks highly of him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.headline: Jeremy McNichols rushed one time for three yards in the Commanders’ Week 18 win over the Eagles, adding one reception for eight yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.analysis: McNichols spent the season as the Commanders’ pass-catching back after Austin Ekeler tore his Achilles at the beginning of the season. He broke several tackles on a Beast Mode-esque 60-yard touchdown run in Week 3; that run was his only rushing touchdown and accounted for 27 percent of his rushing yards for the season. McNichols totaled 44 carries for 221 yards and a touchdown on the ground but often saw more passing-down snaps than rushing snaps, adding 25 receptions for 196 yards through the air. He will be a free agent heading into the offseason and could find a home as a pass-catching depth piece for a team’s backfield.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.headline: Jacorey Croskey-Merritt rushed 18 times for 96 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 15 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.analysis: He wasn’t targeted in the passing game. With Chris Rodriguez unavailable due to a grain injury, Croskey-Merritt was the bellcow for the Commanders. He outrushed Jeremy McNichols by 91 yards (nine attempts for five yards) and McNichols also lost a fumble. The rookie tailback reached 90 yards for the first time since Week 5, and it seems likely he’ll see a similar amount of touches in Week 16 against the Eagles if Rodriguez can’t get healthy for that matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.headline: Jeremy McNichols rushed four times for 13 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 loss to the Dolphins, adding two catches for 16 tards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jeremy-mcn.analysis: McNichols led the Washington backs in catches but finished third on the team in rush attempts. He has a minor role through the air and doesn’t see much work on the ground. McNichols is more of a thorn in the side of the other Washington backs than a standalone fantasy asset. He is not worth holding onto through the team’s Week 12 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/trey-amos/0000.headline: Commanders activated CB Trey Amos (fibula) from injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/trey-amos/0000.analysis: He’ll immediately step in as a starting corner after a long rehab from a broken fibula suffered last November. The Commanders are desperate for better outside cornerback play and will be hoping their 2025 second-rounder can provide it in a hurry.

https://www.nbcsports.com/trey-amos/0000.headline: Commanders CB Trey Amos (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 5 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/trey-amos/0000.analysis: Amos has not yet played in 2026, and appears to be truly questionable this week. The Commanders need all the help they can get on defense, but holding him out another week could be the smart move for his long-term health.

https://www.nbcsports.com/trey-amos/0000.headline: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said he has “no updates” on when Trey Amos (fibula) will return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/trey-amos/0000.analysis: The Commanders placed Amos on injured reserve at the end of camp, which will require him to miss at least the first four games of the season. Quinn said Amos’ “speed and on-field work” have been encouraging as of late, but declined to comment on when the 2025 second-rounder could return. The Commanders’ secondary has struggled through the first two weeks of the season, allowing a league-high seven touchdown passes while also ranking 25th in yards per attempt allowed. We’ll have a better sense of when Amos could be in line to return once the team opens his return window.

https://www.nbcsports.com/trey-amos/0000.headline: ESPN’s John Keim believes the Commanders could draft LSU CB Mansoor Delane in the 2026 NFL Draft’s first round.
https://www.nbcsports.com/trey-amos/0000.analysis: Keim lists the team’s No. 2 need as “a cornerback with length.” Delane stands 6'/187. His arms measured 30" at the NFL Scouting Combine. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn spent the 2010, 2013 and 2014 seasons with the Seahawks under former head coach Pete Carroll, who eagerly drafted cornerbacks standing at least 6' with arms measuring at least 32". We have no way of knowing if Quinn values arm length like Carroll used to, but Delane is generating first-round buzz. The Commanders signed former Lions CB Amik Robertson in free agency. He is expected to man the slot. CBs Trey Amos and Mike Sainristil are currently expected to start on the perimeter. Drafting Delane in the first round could mean he is allowed to compete for a starting role on the outside.

https://www.nbcsports.com/trey-amos/0000.headline: Commanders coach Dan Quinn said Trey Amos (fibula) will “miss some significant time.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/trey-amos/0000.analysis: Considering how little is left of the NFL season and Washington’s placement in the standings, this is likely a season-ender. Amos had a 58.8 PFF coverage grade in 511 snaps during his first 10 games of the season, but looked rough the last two weeks as he allowed 138 yards and a touchdown while allowing 8-of-8 completions in coverage. He’ll likely head to IR in the coming days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/trey-amos/0000.headline: Commanders DT Daron Payne was ejected from Week 10 against the Lions after committing an unnecessary roughness penalty.
https://www.nbcsports.com/trey-amos/0000.analysis: Payne was flagged after a hard-fought 13-yard touchdown run made by Lions RB Jahmyr Gibbs. Payne can be clearly seen punching Lions WR Amon-Ra St. Brown on the left side of his facemask. Astonishingly, Commanders DT Javon Kinlaw was not ejected after striking a referee in the forehead, though he was penalized, after Payne was ejected. The Commanders also may have lost CB Trey Amos, who entered the game with a hip injury, and required two trainers’ assistance to leave the field after injuring his ankle on the play. Amos is currently questionable to return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/trey-amos/0000.headline: Commanders declared WR Terry McLaurin, QB Jayden Daniels, LB Kain Medrano, OT Trent Scott, OT George Fant and DE Jalyn Holmes inactive for Week 10 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/trey-amos/0000.analysis: Facing the Lions without McLaurin and Daniels gives the Commanders long odds of pulling off the upset. Fortunately, they have a capable backup quarterback in Marcus Mariota, and lead rusher, RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (tooth) was medically cleared on Friday. The defense will have CB Trey Amos on hand. The rookie cornerback injured his hip last week against the Seahawks. He practiced fully on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/trey-amos/0000.headline: Commanders selected Ole Miss CB Trey Amos with the No. 61 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/trey-amos/0000.analysis: Amos (6’1/195) worked his way up to the SEC spending three seasons with Louisiana, where he allowed a sub-40% completion rate in each campaign, before getting the call up to Alabama in 2023. He assumed a reserve role with the tide, starting just one of 14 games despite a respectable 76.9 PFF defensive grade. Amos transferred to Ole Miss and ran with his new opportunity, logging career highs with 841 snaps, 13 PBU, 3 interceptions and a 54.5 NFL passer rating allowed. The First Team All-SEC performer also posted a strong 81.3 run defense grade and produced an exceptional 28.6% forced incompletion rate. He ran an 88th% 40-yard dash with a solid 8.37 RAS, though his 4.36s shuttle (36th%) wasn’t great. Amos is pretty balanced in terms of his versatility on the field, having demonstrated effectiveness in both zone and man. He is rarely stressed downfield thanks to a smooth backpedal and is savvy on third downs, sitting on routes and not getting run off the sticks. If there’s a prevailing critique it probably stems from his tendency in zone to sag off receivers on in-breaking routes, preferring to read the quarterback. Amos flashed the tools to become a weekly starting cornerback and has one of the higher floors of this CB group.

https://www.nbcsports.com/trey-amos/0000.headline: Beat reporter Nick Underhill reports that head coach Kellen Moore and many of the Saints’ “top people” are expected to attend Ole Miss QB Jaxson Dart’s Pro Day on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/trey-amos/0000.analysis: Although Derek Carr’s hefty contract is somewhat prohibitive, drafting a promising quarterback prospect is perhaps the most prudent option for Moore, who undoubtedly plans to craft his offense around a talented youngster at some point. Dart has generated some first-round buzz, it would be shocking if the Saints took him No. 9 overall. Underhill notes that the Saints will likely take a look at CB Trey Amos on Friday as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/trey-amos/0000.headline: Louisiana-Lafayette received a verbal commitment from three-star 2020 ATH Trey Amos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/trey-amos/0000.analysis: Amos plays both cornerback and quarterback for his high school and led them to a state finals appearance. He also won the high school state championship for long jump. The uber-athletic player will likely player cornerback at the next level. He’s the 92nd-ranked athlete in the 2020 recruiting cycle and 50th-ranked prospect from the state of Louisiana.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Commanders placed Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: He’ll miss at least the next four weeks. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler figure to get the majority of the work from Weeks 6-9. The Commanders also brought Jeremy McNichols off injured reserve and signed him to the active roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Commanders ruled out RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) for Week 6 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: No surprise here. Croskey-Merritt has been dealing with a groin injury since the start of the season. This week he couldn’t practice and has since been officially ruled out for the Commanders’ Monday Night Football matchup against the 49ers. Croskey-Merritt will get a two-week break with Washington on bye in Week 7. Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler figure to handle the majority of the backfield touches in his absence with White being the preferred fantasy option between the two.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Commanders beat writer Ben Standig reports RB Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) isn’t expected to play in Week 6 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: Croskey-Merritt has dealt with a groin injury all season despite playing in the Commanders’ first five games. He missed multiple practices this week and will now get two weeks off with missing the game against the 49ers ahead of Washington’s bye week. For now, expect Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler to handle the majority of the backfield touches for the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: Croskey-Merritt has played through multiple injuries this year. We still think he has a chance to face the 49ers in Week 6’s Monday Night Football game. Rachaad White (shoulder) sported a red non-contact jersey for the first time this week, and was downgraded to limited today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Austin Ekeler (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: Ekeler and Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) are both ailing, though the latter player sat out entirely. Rachaad White (shoulder) and Jeremy McNichols (quad) are both practicing in full. Croskey-Merritt is the only fantasy-relevant Commanders running back at this time, assuming he is good to go on Monday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: Croskey-Merritt has played through soft tissue injuries for weeks now. He played through a groin injury last week, and the same issue is still bothering him today. Regardless, Croskey-Merritt still has a chance to play this week and today’s absence could actually benefit the starting running back. The Commanders face the 49ers on Monday night, so Croskey-Merritt has extra time to rest and rehab. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed 11 times for 82 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 5 tie with the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: Croskey-Merritt’s 82 rushing yards set a new season high. Nearly half of his yards came in the first quarter when “Bill” broke free for a 33-yard touchdown to give the Commanders a 7-0 lead on their opening drive. On the final play of the third quarter, Croskey-Merritt would rip off a 22-yard run on a drive that eventually ended on a 26-yard touchdown run by Jayden Daniels. JCM continues to be the unquestioned leader in Washington’s backfield, but he remains a touchdown-dependent fantasy option due to his lack of receiving upside. He’ll be a boom-or-bust RB2 in next week’s game against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) is not on the final injury report for Week 5 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: Croskey-Merritt logged two limited sessions to begin the week before upgrading to full on Friday. He should be good to go for this normal weekly role. Unfortunately, his workloads have varied, so he is more of an upside FLEX starter than he is an RB2. That said, Jayden Daniels (elbow) is returning this week, which should give the offense an efficiency boost.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: He remains on track to play, but the workload he’ll get remains more uncertain after the Commanders re-divvied carries in England last Sunday. Croskey-Merritt would make for a shaky FLEX play in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.headline: Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacory-cro.analysis: A limited session to start the week is usually a non-issue, but JCM’s role was already suspect before getting banged up. He ran nine times in Week 4. Austin Ekeler, Kaytron Allen, and Craig Reynolds all combined for nine attempts. Rachaad White is also back at practice, giving the team another option beyond Bill. With health and workload concerns, JCM is barely an RB3 headed into Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.headline: Patriots placed Romeo Doubs (shoulder) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.analysis: Doubs was ruled out in the third quarter of Week 6’s win over the Jets and will now miss at least the next four games. With the Patriots’ bye not coming until Week 11, the earliest Doubs will be able to return to the field will be in Week 12 against the Chargers. Doubs has caught 14 passes for 261 yards and three touchdowns this season and has been targeted more than four times in just one game. Doubs can be dropped in leagues that don’t allow players to be stashed on IR.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.headline: Romeo Doubs injured his shoulder in the Patriots’ Week 6 game against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.analysis: Initially deemed questionable, Doubs was ruled out in the third quarter. Doubs landed hard on his shoulder on his first target, which just happened to be a 42-yard touchdown where he broke free along the back line of the defense. Most unfortunate, though he at least tallied the score first. Doubs was evaluated in the blue tent before heading to the locker room. It’s bad news for the Pats and fantasy managers, but at least comes as A.J. Brown is back in the lineup for the first time in five weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.headline: Romeo Doubs caught 1-of-3 targets for 16 yards in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.analysis: Drake Maye carved up the Vegas secondary to the tune of 376 yards and four touchdowns, with almost none of it going to be nominal No. 1 wideout. Doubs, who last week against the Bills had 58 yards and two touchdowns, nearly came down with a short touchdown grab in the third quarter on a nice touch throw from Maye. The potential return of A.J. Brown (ankle) in Week 6 against the Jets could limit Doubs’ targets going forward. With Maye cooking, Doubs remains a potential flex option in 14-team formats going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.headline: Romeo Doubs caught 6-of-9 targets for 58 yards and two touchdowns in the Patriots’ Week 4 win over the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.analysis: Doubs simply beat Bills cornerback Maxwell Hairston all game long. He seemed to be open at will and almost had a bigger day when he failed to haul in a 40+ yard pass that went off his hands on a diving attempt in the fourth quarter. With Mack Hollins (calf) getting hurt in the first half, Doubs played on 47 of the team’s 70 snaps and ran a route on 30 of their 43 dropbacks, the most of any receiver on the team. It seems that Doubs is finally starting to click with Drake Maye, and now that Hollins is out and A.J. Brown (ankle) is still not ready to come back, Doubs could be in for a big role against the Raiders next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.headline: Romeo Doubs caught 3-of-4 targets for 49 yards in the Patriots’ Week 3 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.analysis: Doubs was again an every-down player and finished second behind Mack Hollins in receiving yards. Doubs continues to be an afterthought in the New England offense, even with A.J. Brown out with a severe ankle injury. Through three games Doubs now has just six catches in the low-wattage Pats offense. He’ll be a deep league option in Week 4 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports A.J. Brown (ankle) is expected to miss 6-8 weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.analysis: Schefter and other reporters previously called it a 4-6 week injury, which now seems unlikely. Schefter did add that Brown is moving “pretty well” and could come back on the faster side of his updated timeline. Still, it looks like Brown will miss at least half of the regular season. Romeo Doubs will operate as the team’s No. 1 receiver until he returns, though it will likely be a group effort to replace Browns’ production. Mack Hollins and Demario Douglas will also be more involved.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.headline: Romeo Doubs caught 3-of-4 targets for 96 yards in the Patriots’ Week 2 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.analysis: Doubs followed up a rough Week 1 with a productive Week 2, leading the Patriots wideouts in targets, receptions, and yards. With A.J. Brown out, Doubs started and tallied the second-most snaps among Pats wide receivers for the day. The bulk of his yardage came from a pair of third-quarter chunk gains, catching a 29-yard pass early in the quarter and breaking free for a 63-yard gain later in the quarter. Between Drake Maye’s early season struggles and a spread-the-wealth approach in the passing game, the Patriots receivers’ ceilings are capped. Doubs looks like the best pass-catching option and will be firmly in the WR4 ranks for Week 3 against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Patriots WR A.J. Brown (ankle) will miss at least four weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.analysis: NFL insider Jordan Schultz puts Brown’s return timeline between 3 and 6 weeks. Both reports make Brown a candidate to be placed on short-term injured reserve. The rest of the Patriots’ wide receiver corps failed to step up in Week 1. Newcomer WR Romeo Doubs will undoubtedly be given a chance to earn his hefty contract in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports the “preliminary diagnosis” for A.J. Brown is a high-ankle sprain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.analysis: Garafolo added, “MRI today after X-rays were negative.” That’s a good sign, but there is currently no timeline for Brown’s return. It will ultimately be a multi-week injury that could linger well into the season. Demario Douglas led the Pats with seven targets last night, though his looks are generally low-value check-downs. Mack Hollins and Romeo Doubs will serve as the team’s primary outside receivers until Brown is healthy. Hollins led the Pats in receiving yards at a modest 51. Hollins is worth adding in deeper leagues, but it’s hard to imagine him putting up anything more than WR4 numbers while Brown is sidelined. Doubs should improve in Week 2 after failing to catch any of his three targets versus the Seahawks. He will get another shot at WR3 numbers against Pittsburgh next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.headline: Romeo Doubs failed to catch any of his three targets in the Patriots’ Week 1 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/romeo-doub.analysis: Doubs was blanketed in coverage all night. He failed to climb the ladder and win a jump ball early in the fourth quarter, resulting in a deflected ball turning into an interception. Later in the quarter, Doubs turned his eyes upfield before securing the pass and let the ball slip out of his hands for a drop. Drake Maye was intercepted on the next play. By any measure, this was a catastrophic debut for a player who signed a four-year, $68 million contract in the offseason. The good news for Doubs is that the team will likely be counting on him to step up next week. A.J. Brown left this game with an ankle injury and did not return. If he isn’t available for Week 2 versus the Steelers, Doubs will get one more chance at a WR3 fantasy ranking.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.headline: Giants coach John Harbaugh, asked about the running back room, said carries are “earned” and told his players to “do something” in their opportunities and more will come.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.analysis: Tyrone Tracy appeared to do the most with his opportunities last week, scoring the game’s only two touchdowns. Najee Harris was bottled up and Cam Skattebo was soft benched while Devin Singletary led the team in snaps while they were in comeback mode for most of the second half. By the letter of what he’s offering here, Tracy is probably the player who should get the majority of the snaps against the Texans. In actuality, we have no idea what will happen here and this quote doesn’t really help us. “I don’t like (rotating backs) either,” Harbaugh said per The Athletic’s Dan Duggan after the game. “One of those guys needs to step up. Somebody needs to step up and be the back. And none of those guys have done that yet.” We suspect we’ll be diving beat writer opinions ahead of Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.headline: Tyrone Tracy rushed six times for 18 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the Saints, adding two receptions for 27 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.analysis: With Cam Skattebo facing a soft benching due to fumbling issues, Tracy saw the second-most running back snaps in a pass-happy game script. He opened scoring with a 17-yard catch-and-run in the first quarter and followed it up with a five-yard rushing score in the fourth quarter. The Giants backfield remains murky after Skattebo saw zero touches and no Giants back rushed for over 20 yards. Tracy is worth rostering as a potential FLEX play for Week 7 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.headline: Tyrone Tracy (knee) is not on New York’s final Week 4 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.analysis: Tracy upgraded to a full practice session, but looks to have lost most of his backup work to Najee Harris at this point. Tracy does not need to be kept in shallow leagues, but at least he’s good to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.headline: Giants RB Tyrone Tracy (knee) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.analysis: The Giants’ RB3 is seemingly on track to be active for Week 4 against the Cardinals. Unfortunately, Giants LT Andrew Thomas (groin) was not seen practicing during the portion of practice open to the media. He did not practice yesterday either and should currently be considered questionable to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.headline: Giants RB Tyrone Tracy (knee) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.analysis: The Giants’ backup is not presently fantasy-relevant, and a knee injury certainly won’t improve his stock, though coach John Harbaugh said he is only “day-to-day.” Giants LT Andrew Thomas (groin) was also sidelined, but he played through it last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.headline: Giants RB Tyrone Tracy (illness) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.analysis: Tracy should be good to go for Week 2 sideline duties, though RB Najee Harris could leapfrog him on the depth chart at some point. Tracy does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues after being benched for a fumble in Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.headline: Tyrone Tracy (illness) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.analysis: Tracy has the flu, according to head coach John Harbaugh. He said the hope is that Tracy is back for tomorrow’s practice. Tracy was demoted from the RB2 role in Week 1 after losing a fumble on his second carry of the night. He did not play a snap on offense after the turnover. The missed practice time this week could be reason enough for the Giants to make him inactive in favor of Najee Harris on Sunday. Either way, Tracy is not worth stashing even in deep fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.headline: Cam Skattebo rushed 18 times for 81 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 1 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.analysis: Although Skattebo was not targeted in the pass game, his 18 carries handily led the team. Furthermore, presumed backup Tyrone Tracy lost a fumble on one of his two carries, resulting in Devin Singletary taking over primary backup duties for the remainder of the game. Those two variables should keep Skattebo’s weekly volume high after showing no ill effects of the devastating ankle injury suffered in 2025. His touchdown now gives him eight total scores in nine professional appearances despite only six of those being starts, a rate that will keep Skattebo in the weekly borderline RB1 discussion moving forward. Tracy managed just two snaps to Singletary’s 25, leaving Singletary as the primary backup for the moment. It’s possible Najee Harris gets into this discussion after being a healthy scratch in Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.headline: Tyrone Tracy Jr., Najee Harris and Devin Singletary are all listed as co-No. 2 backs on New York’s unofficial Week 1 depth chart.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.analysis: We can’t endorse relying on anyone in this backfield as a surefire bellcow in the event that Cam Skattebo gets hurt or is ineffective enough to lose playing time. It seems like it will be hard to rely on Tracy to have a major role this year with Harris in town.

https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.headline: Giants announced RB Tyrone Tracy was evaluated for concussion, but was cleared.
https://www.nbcsports.com/tyrone-tracy/0.analysis: Tracy left Friday’s preseason game against the Jets with an apparent injury in the second quarter. The Giants announced Tracy was evaluated for a concussion, but was able to clear concussion protocol. Before leaving the game, Tracy had 37 yards and a touchdown on four carries. He doesn’t carry much standalone fantasy value in a crowded Giants backfield that also includes Cam Skattebo, Najee Harris and Devin Singletary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-manni.headline: Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni said OC Sean Mannion will continue to call plays.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-manni.analysis: Mannion is in his first year as the Eagles’ offensive coordinator and has struggled to turn around an offense that ranked 19th in scoring and 24th in total yards last season. The loss of Jalen Hurts (blood clots) will only further complicate life for Mannion and the Eagles, who rank 28th in points scored through six games this season. While Sirianni did say “everything’s on the table” to fix the offense, it doesn’t sound like any dramatic changes are coming just yet.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-manni.headline: Eagles OC Sean Mannion told reporters the Tush Push will continue to be part of the offense.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-manni.analysis: No surprise here as the Tush Push has been an extremely effective play for the Eagles over the years. Mannion, Philadelphia’s third OC in the last three years, is sure to change things with the offense. When it comes to the Tush Push, however, that’s one area that doesn’t need to be fixed. QB Jalen Hurts should continue to be the main beneficiary of the short touchdowns the Tush Push provides.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-manni.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo called Raiders interim offensive coordinator Greg Olson a “name to watch” for the Eagles’ quarterbacks coach position.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-manni.analysis: Scot Loeffler is currently Philly’s quarterbacks coach, but it’s possible the Eagles let him go, allowing new OC Sean Mannion to pick his replacement. In a similar vein, Olson should be let go by the Raiders once they land Klint Kubiak as their next head coach. Mannion previously played under Olson in Seattle. Per Garafolo’s sources, Mannion would be interested in reuniting with his coach in Philly.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-manni.headline: Eagles hired Sean Mannion as their new offensive coordinator.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-manni.analysis: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero believes “a schematic shift coming to Philly,” noting that Mannion played under Rams head coach Sean McVay and Vikings head coach Kevin O’Connell before serving as quarterbacks coach for the Packers under head coach Matt LaFleur. All three coaches use play action, shifts and motion far more than the Eagles did under former OC Kevin Patullo. Mannion will reportedly call plays for the offense. Pelissero’s belief is reasonable and bodes positively for a more fantasy-friendly environment in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-manni.headline: Eagles interviewed Packers quarterbacks coach Sean Mannion for their offensive coordinator vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-manni.analysis: Entering its third week, the Eagles offensive coordinator search is taking on an eau de Browns and they are responding by adding even more candidates to the pool. Mannion, 33, a former NFL backup quarterback, has no play calling experience and has only coached for two seasons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-manni.headline: Packers hired DeMarcus Covington, formerly of the Patriots, as their DL coach.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-manni.analysis: Covington spent last season as the Patriots’ defensive coordinator but first joined their staff in 2017 as a coaching assistant. He was promoted to their DL coach in 2020 and served in that role until 2023. It was reported earlier that Covington, who interviewed earlier this month for the Bengals’ defensive coordinator vacancy, was not expected to return to the Patriots after they went out and hired Mike Vrabel as head coach. Now, he’ll have a chance to start over in Green Bay. In addition to Covington, the Packers also hired former quarterback Sean Mannion as their quarterbacks coach.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-manni.headline: Seahawks elevated QB Sean Mannion for Week 15 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-manni.analysis: The quarterback elevated comes with starter Geno Smith questionable with a groin injury, potentially signaling that Smith is not expected to be available for the team’s game against the Eagles. The Seahawks could still render Mannion inactive to be used as their emergency quarterback, so keep an eye on the inactives list 90 minutes prior to kickoff.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-manni.headline: Vikings released QB Sean Mannion.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-manni.analysis: When the Vikings traded for Nick Mullens, the writing was on the wall for Mannion and sophomore Kellen Mond. Both were cut Tuesday. Mannion has made three NFL starts since entering the league in 2015 and is 0-3 with a pitiful 5.2 YPA average. He’s not a capable fill-in starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-manni.headline: Vikings acquired QB Nick Mullens from the Raiders in exchange for a conditional 2024 seventh-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-manni.analysis: Perhaps the Vikings are less than thrilled with the performance of Kirk Cousins’ backups this preseason. Sean Mannion has completed 66% of his attempts for a meager 5.3 yards per attempt. Sophomore Kellen Mond has been erratic in two appearances, completing 55.5% of his throws for two touchdowns and two picks. Mond also wasn’t picked by the new Minnesota regime. Mullens, with a career 64.7% completion rate and 26 touchdown passes over 20 appearances, should be the favorite to open the season as Cousins’ No. 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-manni.headline: Vikings re-signed QB Sean Mannion to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/sean-manni.analysis: A favorite of former Vikings head coach Mike Zimmer, Mannion will play a fourth season as Minnesota’s backup with the team’s new coaching staff. Mannion has completed 60.9 percent of his passes and thrown one touchdown and three interceptions in his six NFL seasons. He could once again be ahead of 2021 third-round pick QB Kellen Mond on the Vikings depth chart.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tredavious.headline: Bills signed CB Tre’Davious White to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tredavious.analysis: The 31-year-old will be the latest veteran-as-practice-squadder bit corner in Buffalo’s beleaguered room. He has a storied history with the organization and is clearly still a very smart player.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tredavious.headline: Bills declared WR Curtis Samuel, NCB Taron Johnson, S Jordan Hancock, LB Shaq Thompson. T Chase Lundt, DT Ed Oliver, and DE Landon Jackson inactive for Week 2 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tredavious.analysis: We already knew Oliver was missing this week with an ankle injury but there had been hope that Johnson (quad) would suit up. Those are two big losses for this Bills defense heading into a showdown with a Jets offense that seemed live in week one. The good news is that Tre’Davious White (groin) will make his season debut across from Christian Bedford.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tredavious.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Bills CB Tre’Davious White (groin) will be active for Week 2 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tredavious.analysis: White missed Week 1 with the groin issue and was listed as questionable for Week 2 after three limited practices. He may be worked in slowly for his first game of 2025, but White will make his return to Buffalo later today after spending last year with the Rams and Ravens. White could replace sixth-round rookie Dorian Strong in the lineup. Strong started in Week 1 but may be better deployed as a reserve cornerback for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tredavious.headline: Bills CB Taron Johnson (quad) is questionable to play in Week 2 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tredavious.analysis: The Bills’ talented slot cornerback suffered a quad injury in Week 1. He logged just two limited sessions in practice this week. The Bills have also listed CB Tre’Davious White (groin), backup S Jordan Hancock and LB Shaq Thompson (hamstring/hand) as questionable for Week 2. Star DT Ed Oliver is expected to miss multiple weeks after injuring his ankle in practice this week. The Jets’ capable skill position players are primed for a solid outing in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tredavious.headline: Bills CB Tre’Davious White (groin) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tredavious.analysis: White did not practice last week and was listed as doubtful on Friday. As expected, he was ruled out before kickoff. It looks like the veteran corner is nearing a return after getting in a limited session to open the week. White will likely take over as Buffalo’s CB2 once healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tredavious.headline: Bills CB Christian Benford (groin) is off Buffalo’s final Week 1 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tredavious.analysis: He practiced in full on Thursday and Friday and should be good to go against the Ravens on Sunday. Tre’Davious White (groin) was not so fortunate, being listed as doubtful after three straight DNPs. Benford is a good starter, but the Bills CB2 spot threatens to be an exploitable fantasy matchup in the early season with White unable to stay on the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tredavious.headline: Bills CB Christian Benford (groin) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tredavious.analysis: Bills CB Tre’Davious White was limited by a groin strain as well. That makes both of the Bills’ starting perimeter cornerbacks who are now questionable to play in Week 1 against the Ravens. Zay Flowers and Rashod Bateman could have fruitful outings if neither coverage defender can go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tredavious.headline: Bills GM Brandon Beane said Tre’Davious White (leg) will play again this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tredavious.analysis: He didn’t rule him out of Week 1, though that seems aggressive. Buffalo will be relying on pieces like Dorian Strong or Ja’Marcus Ingram to fill out the Week 1 depth chart at outside corner next to Christian Benford while White heals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tredavious.headline: Bills CB Tre’Davious White left practice early on Thursday after suffering an apparent leg injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tredavious.analysis: White reportedly hopped on one leg, over to Bills’ trainers, before being carted to the locker room. No word on the injury’s specifics yet. Fellow CB Christian Benford exited practice early as well, though he later said he is okay and “just needed some rest.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tredavious.headline: Bills signed CB Tre’Davious White, formerly of the Ravens, to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tredavious.analysis: Tom Pelissero reports the contract is worth “up to” $6.8 million. White, now 30 years old, returns to the team that drafted him in the 2017 NFL Draft’s first round. White was a force to be reckoned with early in his career, but a 2021 ACL tear and a 2023 Achilles tendon rupture have reduced his play quality. He finished 2024 with a career-low 54.8 PFF coverage grade. White will now compete for the Bills’ No. 2 perimeter role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.headline: Rams placed K Blake Grupe (knee) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.analysis: He’ll miss at least the next four weeks. The Rams will reshuffle the kicker deck again in Week 7, keep refreshing the page over the next few days to learn who it will be.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reports that Blake Grupe suffered a knee injury in their Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.analysis: Bringing back Harrison Mevis, whom the Rams waived five days ago, is one option, but it is unclear whether either side wants a reunion. The Rams might want to bring a few special teams contributors aboard while they’re at it. Grupe was injured during a tackle attempt because yet another return had scooted right past the Rams’ special teams coverage unit. The Rams rank outside the top 25 in average kick return yards allowed and average punt return yards allowed. Minimizing kicker tackling attempts in the future is probably a good call.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.headline: Blake Grupe is doubtful to return in Week 6 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.analysis: Grupe will be credited with tackling Cardinals returner Devin Duvernay because he technically knocked Duvernay out of bounds, but the engagement proved costly. Duvernay got behind the Rams’ punt coverage, and Grupe valiantly lowered his shoulder in an attempt to bring Duvernay down. Duvernay responded in kind and sent Grupe tumbling to the ground before jogging out of bounds. Grupe struggled to get up and was eventually helped off the field. Rams P Ethan Evans is the emergency kicker. Grupe was later ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.headline: Rams signed K Blake Grupe off the Jets practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.analysis: Going 5-for-9 on the season will get you replaced in the modern NFL, as Thiccer Kicker Harrison Mevis is learning. It’s not totally fair, one of those was blocked, but clearly the Rams were not happy with how things were trending. Grupe is a worthwhile pickup in leagues that still use kickers. He went 11-for-11 for the Colts last year after being released by the Saints at midseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.headline: Jets signed K Jason Sanders to their active roster.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.analysis: Sanders somehow won the kicking job over Blake Grupe despite Grupe being on the active roster and Sanders falling to the practice squad. Sure. Well, anyway, Grupe is being waived. Sanders will continue to kick for the Jets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.headline: Jets HC Aaron Glenn said Jason Sanders will serve as the team’s kicker in Week 1 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.analysis: This is notable because Sanders is currently on the Jets’ practice squad while veteran kicker Blake Grupe is on the 53-man roster. Fantasy managers expecting Grupe to contribute to their Week 1 lineups will want to make sure they find a replacement. Sanders certainly makes for a viable option after he converted 37-of-41 field goal attempts last season while going 12-of-14 from distances of 50-plus yards.
