https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.headline: Jets claimed K Blake Grupe off waivers from the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.analysis: Jason Sanders, who had won the Jets kicker competition, is instead released to make way for Grupe. As we wrote about Sanders a few days ago: Winning the Jets kicker competition is not an endorsement that provides many fantasy points. Grupe will probably be stuck in the 20s in weekly ranks in most of the Jets games this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.headline: Colts released K Blake Grupe.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.analysis: Grupe, who had a “90% make rate in camp” per Mike Garafolo, has a chance to come aboard late and win a different kicking job. Spencer Shrader will kick for the Colts this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.headline: The Indianapolis Star’s Nathan Brown reports Blake Grupe “has the clear statistical lead” in the Colts’ kicking competition.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.analysis: Grupe is competing with Spencer Schrader for the Colts’ starting gig, and through a week of training camp, Grupe has been more accurate. Brown said the team is evaluating other factors as well, including ball flight and pre-practice kicks from Grupe and Schrader. The Colts in 2025 tied for tenth in team field goal attempts. That sort of opportunity will make Grupe or Schrader fantasy viable in 2026 as long as Daniel Jones is healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.headline: Colts signed K Blake Grupe to a one-year, $1.4 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/blake-grup.analysis: Grupe appeared in only five games for the Colts in 2025 but went a perfect 11-for-11 with the team. He was signed in December after making only 18 of 26 attempts with the Saints to start the year. His efforts to end the season earn him a chance to prove his worth on the modest deal. Spencer Shrader remains under team control, setting up a potential kicker battle in camp and preseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said Tank Dell (knee) will play in Week 7 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: Dell will make his long-awaited return next week against the Giants. By the time he takes the field in Week 7, Dell will have been more than 22 months removed from his last regular-season game, which came in Week 16 of the 2024 season. Dell suffered a torn ACL, LCL, and MCL, along with a dislocated knee, in that game against the Chiefs and has been on a long road to recovery. He’ll join a crowded receiver room that recently acquired Marvin Harrison Jr., and Jaylin Noel has posted a solid 17-334-2 line through the first six weeks of the season and topped 100 yards in Sunday’s win over the Jaguars. Targets could be hard to come by for Dell, but his return next week is an impressive feat on its own given the injury he had to work through.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Texans ruled out Tank Dell (knee) for Week 6 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: The Texans depart for London tonight to face the Jaguars on Sunday, and Dell will remain in Texas. He is currently practicing in full, but the team has not yet cleared him for game-day activities. Dell does not need to be stashed in 12-team leagues at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Tank Dell (knee) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: The Texans are facing the Jaguars in London this week. If Dell travels, that would indicate that Dell has a chance to play for the first time since suffering a multi-ligament tear in 2024. He would be a low-floor FLEX if he is active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Tank Dell (knee) won’t play in Houston’s Week 5 game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: He did not practice on Friday and was ruled out. The Texans reportedly pushed hard on Dell in full pads on Thursday’s practice despite the questionable listing, it seems his body did not react as they’d hoped. This leaves Jaylin Noel in a potential FLEX-useful spot against a rough Titans secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Tank Dell (knee) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: The diminutive wide receiver remains limited through two practices. In most situations, that would put him on track to play. In this case, Dell might need to consistently practice fully before the Texans let him go out there on game day. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Tank Dell (knee) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: It is unclear when Dell will take the field on game day, but he is officially participating in his 21-day practice window. His range of potential outcomes is quite wide. Stashing him on fantasy benches is a reasonable move at this time, though he is not guaranteed to be a fantasy contributor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said Tank Dell (knee/IR) will have his practice window opened.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: Dell has missed the mandatory four games on injured reserve, but may be a week-to-week proposition at this point. None of the Texans secondary receivers have really hit the bar of fantasy interesting — partially because none of them gets full playing time — and we’d be skeptical that Dell would hit that either early in his return. But he could grow into a bigger role as the season plays out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Texans agreed to terms with WR Tank Dell on a one-year, $1.7 million contract restructure.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: The deal includes $1 million in guarantees while saving the franchise almost $2 million against the cap. Dell is reportedly nearing a return from the devastating knee injury suffered in Week 16 of the 2024 season but will begin 2026 on the physically unable to perform list, meaning he will miss the first four games of the regular season. The contract restructure hints at a potential “prove it” year for Dell, giving the team options following 2026 pending health.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Texans GM Nick Caserio said Tank Dell (knee) is “close” but “not quite there.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: He was already placed on injured reserve, so he’ll miss the first four games of the season. Reading between the lines it sounds like Dell has a chance to miss more than just the first four games of the season. Kayshon Boutte and Dalton Schultz will battle for the role of lead secondary target behind Nico Collins while Dell is sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.headline: Texans placed WR Tank Dell on injured reserve, designated to return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tank-dell/.analysis: The designation to return means that Dell is expected to contribute in some capacity this season, although he appears a ways off still. With Jaylin Noel still nursing an injury after experiencing a setback and Jayden Higgins lost for the season, recent acquisition Kayshon Boutte has all the runway to operate as the WR2 opposite Nico Collins to start the season. Xavier Hutchinson should also see an uptick in opportunities while tight end Dalton Schultz should see a significant boost in weekly volume.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.headline: Bills S C.J. Gardner-Johnson has been suspended one game for an act of unsportsmanlike conduct in Week 6’s game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.analysis: Gardner-Johnson was caught on tape spitting at/in the direction of Raiders TE Brock Bowers after the two were seen jawing at one another after a play. Gardner-Johnson will be suspended without pay when the Bills return from their bye to play the Ravens in Week 8. He has tallied 25 tackles, two pass breakups, and one interception this season while earning a PFF grade of 55.2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.headline: C.J. Gardner-Johnson was ejected in the second quarter of the Bills’ Week 6 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.analysis: Instant replay showed Gardner-Johnson spitting in the direction of Brock Bowers and other Raiders players after he was seen jawing with Bowers after a play. The veteran defensive back was flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct and immediately disqualified from the game, and will likely be facing a fine and suspension later in the week. The 28-year-old DB has started all five games he has appeared in this season, and entered the day with 25 tackles, two pass breakups, and one interception.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Bills S C.J. Gardner-Johnson has a calf strain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.analysis: Gardner-Johnson was carted off with a scary-looking injury that appeared to be near his Achilles. It looks as if he’s avoided the worst-case scenario, though we still wouldn’t be surprised if he missed a lot of time. The team should have further updates soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.headline: Bills S C.J. Gardner-Johnson (leg) was carted to the locker room on Saturday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.analysis: Gardner-Johnson appeared to suffer a non-contact lower leg injury. He went down on the practice field and grabbed at his leg near his Achilles. The 28-year-old safety couldn’t put any pressure on his right leg as he was helped off the field. Gardner-Johnson had a towel over his head as he was carted to the locker room. Buffalo lacks safety depth behind Gardner-Johnson as fifth-round rookie Jalon Kilgore could be next up if this injury indeed turns out to be significant.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.headline: Bills signed S C.J. Gardner-Johnson, formerly of the Bears, to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.analysis: Gardner-Johnson can make up to $6 million this year. The 28-year-old safety allowed a career-high 71.4 percent catch rate playing for both the Texans and Bears last season. He also forced four incompletions, intercepted two passes, recorded 51 solo tackles and notched three TFLs. He may help fill former Bills CB Taron Johnson’s vacated slot cornerback role. The Bills traded Johnson to the Raiders on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.headline: Bears signed CB C.J. Gardner-Johnson, formerly of the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.analysis: Gardner-Johnson will reunite with Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen, who coached him in New Orleans from 2019 to 2021. The mercurial cornerback will join a Chicago defense that has allowed the NFL’s fourth highest drop back success rate and the second highest completion rate over expected this season. Look for Gardner-Johnson, who has 18 interceptions over 77 NFL games, to primarily play slot corner in Chicago.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.headline: Ravens released C.J. Gardner-Johnson from their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.analysis: The 27-year-old safety asked for his release after the Ravens traded for Alohi Gilman.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.headline: Ravens signed S C.J. Gardner-Johnson to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.analysis: The Texans released Gardner-Johnson after Week 3 and much came out about him freelancing, blowing assignments, and complaining about his role. The Ravens defense is at a juncture where they’d probably take that if it came with some competent NFL-level play, too.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.headline: Texans released S C.J. Gardner-Johnson.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.analysis: What was your favorite moment of the Gardner-Johnson era in Houston? He did play 96 percent of the snaps for the Texans in three weeks, so it’s a loss. NBC’s Aaron Wilson reports there was “friction behind the scenes” behind the release, with Gardner-Johnson “complaining about his role, wanting to blitz more, per league sources, and even communicating that he wanted to be traded.” M.J. Stewart will take over at safety for the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.headline: Texans restructured S C.J. Gardner-Johnson’s contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-gardne.analysis: According to KPRC2’s Aaron Wilson, the Texans are converting $7.75 million of Gardner-Johnson’s base salary into a $6.58 million signing bonus that will free up just over $3.086 million in cap space. Gardner-Johnson is in the second year of a three-year deal he originally signed with the Eagles in 2024, but can be released with no dead cap hit if the team opts to move on from him at the end of this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Colts coach Shane Steichen said Daniel Jones will remain the team’s starting quarterback against the Vikings in Week 7.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Jones has yet to crack 270 yards or throw multiple touchdowns in a start. He’s also thrown six interceptions and is completing a career-worst 59.6 percent of his passes. It is not an uncommon observation to say that he is struggling to drive the ball on his throws. While the Colts are not going away from Jones now, that does not necessarily mean he will remain the starter all year if he continues to play like this. Given what the Vikings have been up to this year, we’d be surprised if Jones escaped the bottom five of quarterback fantasy points this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Daniel Jones completed 22-of-42 passes for 269 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in the Colts’ 26-20, Week 6 loss to the Titans, adding three carries for 30 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: This one is going to leave a mark. The Colts led 13-0 at halftime but couldn’t get anything going after the break, where they committed two turnovers and Jones provided just 116 yards passing. His third quarter pick came only moments after a lost Jonathan Taylor fumble. It went right to Titans corner Cor’Dale Flott. Jones was not helped by some shaky hands from default No. 1 receiver Josh Downs, but he simply was not standing and delivering. Jones is really struggling to drive the ball this season, and he’s contributing far less than usual with his legs. In other words, he looks like a 29-year-old coming off a torn achilles’ tendon. There is little reason to expect things to get better in the near term, very much including Week 7 against Brian Flores’ ferocious Vikings defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Daniel Jones (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: A full practice today means Jones will play through the issue in Week 6, but it’s never a good sign to see a starting quarterback unexpectedly pop up on the injury report. Jones has also struggled mightily this year, so the last thing he needs is a lingering ankle issue, even if it’s a minor one. Needless to say, we aren’t itching to get Jones in our fantasy lineups in a low-scoring affair with the Titans. He is buried at the back of the QB2 ranks for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Daniel Jones completed 24-of-44 passes for 267 yards in the Colts’ 34-22, Week 5 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: The 267 yards aren’t a terrible total for Jones, but the Colts’ offense was not effective for most of the game. They were stuffed inside the Steelers’ three-yard line at least four times during the game, and the only touchdown they scored was on a one-yard sneak to tight end Tyler Warren. Even on that play, Warren was stuffed short of the end zone and had to be pushed in from behind. Jones was unable to connect with any receivers down the field and overthrew a few deep shots on the day. The Steelers spent a lot of energy trying to corral Jonathan Taylor, and you’d assume other defenses will deploy the same strategy, which means Jones is going to need to start to make them pay. Things should get easier next week against the winless Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Daniel Jones completed 19-of-34 passes for 143 yards and an interception in the Colts’ 30-13, Week 4 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Jones was disastrously inaccurate in the first half, making even routine catches absurdly difficult for his banged-up receiver room. He also began the game by losing the football after his left tackle was pushed into him, resulting in a fumble. He eventually got the grain on the tracks with back-to-back scoring drives to close the first half. Daniels settled in after the break, though the Colts mostly leaned on Jonathan Taylor, who scored twice, to salt away the game. Jones is averaging a dismal 188.5 yards per game with just three scores to his name. He is barely in the QB2 mix for Indy’s Week 5 game versus the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Daniel Jones completed 24-of-36 passes for 235 yards, one touchdown and one interception in Indianapolis’ 19-17, Week 3 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: He added three fumbles, two of which were recovered by the Texans on Will Anderson Jr. strip sacks. It wasn’t pretty, and expectations should be held in check for the Colts passing game given the lack of relevant options, but Jones held on to help snap Indianapolis’ nine-game losing streak dating back to last season. His most impressive play was probably a middle-of-field ball to Laquon Treadwell that put the Colts in field-goal range for Spencer Shrader’s go-ahead kick with less than 30 seconds remaining. The Colts have a better matchup next week against the Commanders, but Jones would be tough to trust as more than a bottom-rung superflex QB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Daniel Jones completed 22-of-31 passes for 210 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Colts’ 33-30, Week 2 loss to the Chiefs, adding 10 yards on three carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Jones lost one of his top receivers at the end of the first quarter when Alec Pierce departed with a heel injury. He was largely unable to attack downfield following Pierce’s departure. That would all change on the team’s lone possession of overtime when Jones hit Laquon Treadwell for a 48-yard shot on the first play following a Chiefs field goal, but the team would be unable to punch their ticket to a win while settling for a field goal of their own. The team could be forced to play possession ball moving forward considering the short-area nature of the remaining pass-catchers, pending the status of Pierce. That spells trouble against the vaunted Houston defense in Week 3, where Jones will be a fringe QB2 while potentially down his field-stretching option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Daniel Jones completed 19-of-31 passes for 166 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Colts’ 41-23, Week 1 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Jones and the Colts got off to a strong start in this one. The Colts came out of the gate attempting seven straight passes, with Jones going 5-for-7 on the drive for 59 yards. Jonathan Taylor would cap the opening drive with a one-yard touchdown to give the Colts an early lead, but Jones and company struggled to get things going after that. He would muster just 29 passing yards for the remainder of the first half and was baited by Ravens LB Roquan Smith into throwing an interception on the Colts’ second possession. Jones would orchestrate a scoring drive early in the fourth quarter, connecting on passes of 14 and 23 yards to Alec Pierce before eventually finding Tyler Warren for a nine-yard score. Things won’t get any easier for Jones and the Colts next week as they travel to Kansas City to take on the Chiefs. Jones shouldn’t be trusted as anything more than a mid to low-end QB2 in that matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: Colts announced Anthony Richardson will start Thursday’s preseason game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Richardson and Riley Leonard will both play, while Daniel Jones will sit. Richardson’s trade request this offseason has gone nowhere, but the Colts appear to be giving him ample opportunity to showcase himself in the preseason as he will get the first half here and the second half next week against Atlanta, while Leonard picks up the other two halves. The Colts are likely hoping someone talks themselves into trading a low pick for Richardson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.headline: The Indy Star’s Joel A. Erickson reports that QB Riley Leonard and QB Anthony Richardson will play in the Colts’ preseason Week 1 game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/daniel-jon.analysis: Colts coach Shane Steichen did not indicate who will start the game, nor did he rule out QB Daniel Jones (Achilles). Per Erickson, holding Jones out would be unsurprising. Richardson was recently seen working with the third-team offense, so Leonard could have the inside track to start on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Broncos coach Sean Payton said he has not considered removing Bo Nix from the starting job.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: “He is going to become the byproduct of all the finer things that get improved. The improved play from our offensive line; the more efficient we are relative to downs; running the football. That’s our job as coaches here,” Payton said. Nix has been one of the worst quarterbacks in the league through six starts and Jay Glazer passed along word yesterday that Payton changed the terminology that OC Davis Webb had put in this offseason back to what it was last season, which apparently did not help Nix out. He’ll be hard to trust even with a slapdash Cardinals defense on tap for Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 17-of-27 passes for 107 yards in the Broncos’ 17-14, Week 6 win over the Seahawks, adding two yards on four carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Broncos managed just 168 yards of total offense on a night their defense carried them to victory in overtime. Nine of the Broncos’ 11 possessions, excluding the two kneel downs to end each half, ended in punts on drives that lasted five plays or fewer. Two second quarter touchdown drives had the Broncos playing with a lead for much of the game but they were otherwise unable to move the football with any consistency. An overtime interception by nickel corner Ja’Quan McMillian allowed for a game-winning, 53-yard field goal from kicker Will Lutz after the Broncos again failed to gain a first down. The win sends Denver to 4-2 while averaging only 18.7 points per game through six weeks. The team gets a scheduling gift with the Cardinals on deck in Week 7, although Nix cannot be treated as a starter-worthy fantasy asset outside of the deepest leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 16-of-127 passes for 123 yards with a touchdown in the Broncos’ 23-17, Week 5 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Nix also added 10 yards on the ground on his four carries. He once again wasn’t able to get the ball downfield, with a long passing gain of 34 yards on a busted coverage. He was at least able to find Courtland Sutton for a short touchdown, but this was an ugly day for both signal-callers. Nix is no more than a QB2 for a matchup against the tough Seattle defense in Week 6, and it’s worth noting that game takes place Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 25-of-42 attempts for 214 yards and one touchdown in the Broncos’ Week 4 loss to the 49ers, adding two rushes for ten yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Nix’s play — including missing easy intermediate throws in the first half — left Broncos offensive coordinator Davis Webb without answers, a common theme so far this season. His lone touchdown came on a garbage time score to Jaylen Waddle. Nix was in check-down mode throughout the game against the Niners, finishing with a 4.9 aDOT. He was 5 percent under his expected completion rate, targeting his running backs 12 times. Until Webb and Sean Payton figure out the offense, Nix will be a superflex-only fantasy option without much of a weekly ceiling. He gets the Chargers in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 17-of-34 passes for 186 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Broncos’ 30-26, Week 3 win over the Rams, adding seven yards and a touchdown on four carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Broncos were shut out in the first half amidst consistent struggles from Nix, who, for his part, turned in solid production in a third quarter that saw the Broncos knot the game at 16 through two touchdowns and successful two-point conversions. Nix and the Broncos would struggle to move the football again in the fourth quarter but a pick-six from safety Talanoa Hufanga gave them the lead with under five minutes to play. Stafford returned blows to send the Rams to a three-point lead before Nix’s game-winning score from one yard out. That final drive was aided by three key penalties to go against the Rams, the final of which was questionable, to put it kindly. Josh Wallace appeared to intercept Nix for the second time in the fourth quarter but a defensive pass interference penalty was called, giving the Broncos renewed life. Hufanga would intercept Stafford for a second time in the fourth quarter, this time in the end zone, to seal the victory for the Broncos as time expired. Nix and offensive coordinator Davis Webb have not looked good through three games despite the team’s 2-1 record, and will need to clean things up ahead of another NFC West showdown against the 49ers in Week 4. Nix is currently nothing more than a middling QB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 22-of-31 attempts for 288 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Broncos’ Week 2 win against the Jaguars, adding five rushes for eight yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: It was an uneven day for Nix, who missed some routine throws and threw a bad pick in the end zone while targeting Courtland Sutton. He targeted Jaylen Waddle heavily and connected with Waddle for a 49-yard gain in the first half, regularly attacking the Jaguars secondary downfield. After taking far too many sacks in Week 1 against the Chiefs, Nix was not sacked against a solid Jaguars pass rush on Sunday. Nix’s lack of early-season rushing success has dinged his fantasy prospects a bit. He’s a fine superflex option for Week 3 against the Rams, however.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix called the Broncos’ Week 1 offensive performance “pretty pitiful.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Nix during his postgame presser defended offensive play caller Davis Webb, who took over for head coach Sean Payton this offseason. “The players did not make it easy on [Webb] today,” said Nix, who completed 17-of-28 passes for 131 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in Monday night’s loss to Kansas City. “Pretty pitiful, actually.” Denver had the league’s second lowest drop back EPA of Week 1; only the Falcons were worse. Nix, meanwhile, ranked 28th out of 32 qualifying QBs in Week 1 accuracy. “We called exactly what we prepared for and what we wanted to get to and we just didn’t execute,” Nix said. “Then we were behind.” Webb and the Broncos will look to bounce back in Week 2 against a tough Jaguars defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Bo Nix completed 17-of-28 passes for 131 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Broncos’ 31-10, Week 1 loss to the Chiefs, adding two yards on three carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Nix and the rest of the Denver offense struggled throughout against Steve Spagnuolo’s Kansas City defense, gaining fewer yards as a team (176) than opposing running back Kenneth Walker (191). Things seemed to be clicking early after the Broncos were able to knot the game at seven in the first quarter, but quickly fell apart under unrelenting pressure. The poor offensive showing is sure to draw criticism in the media considering it was the first game called by first-time offensive coordinator Davis Webb after head coach Sean Payton relinquished play calling duties this offseason. Whether that setup continues remains to be seen and we wouldn’t be shocked if Webb failed to make it through the first six weeks still calling plays. The Broncos hold the league’s most difficult schedule through the first six weeks, with games against Jaguars, Rams, 49ers, Chargers, and Seahawks on the immediate horizon. Nix could regain form against the pass-funnel Jaguars in Week 2, where he will be a back-end QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Broncos QB Bo Nix completed 6-of-9 passes for 76 yards and one touchdown in Friday’s preseason game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Nix looked mobile and eager to chuck it downfield. He even had a few overthrows, which we suppose is a good thing for a quarterback who spent the offseason rehabbing an ankle injury. The Broncos quarterback linked up with new WR Jaylen Waddle for a 35-yard gain down the seam and targeted WR Courtland Sutton a couple of times along the sideline. He found tonight’s starting RB RJ Harvey speeding down the right side of the field on a wheel route, and linked up with the second-year running back for a 21-yard touchdown to conclude the first drive. New OC Davis Webb regularly dialed up play action, which is great for fantasy purposes. Nix looks like a low-end QB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Broncos coach Sean Payton believes Bo Nix’s movement is “back to where it was” before his broken ankle.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Payton said Nix’s health “looks really good.” Payton’s words come a week after Nix pledged to keep running this season despite his unfortunate injury. Considered something of a finished product upon being the No. 12 overall pick of the 2024 Draft, Nix took a decent sophomore step forward, and now has the best supporting cast of his career entering Year 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalon-dani.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said the team is planning as if Jalon Daniels will start in Week 7 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalon-dani.analysis: Bowles said this week will be an important evaluation week for Baker Mayfield, who is still rehabbing a dislocated thumb that has sidelined him since Week 3. Daniels hasn’t been overly impressive in his three starts this season, throwing for 501 yards, three touchdowns and five interceptions while also taking nine sacks. That said, he did manage to pull off a win over the Cowboys in Week 5 and had the Buccaneers in position to beat the Steelers in Week 6 before Pittsburgh erupted for 16 points in the fourth quarter to force overtime. We’ll see how things unfold throughout the week, but it sounds like Mayfield is at least one week away from returning. Daniels would be on the fantasy radar as a low-end QB2 if he gets the start against Carolina.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalon-dani.headline: Jalon Daniels completed 22-of-43 passes for 164 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the Bucs’ 26-19, Week 6 overtime loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalon-dani.analysis: Daniels added 39 yards on the ground but lost a grand total of 42 yards via five sacks. Despite making a handful of big plays, Daniels’ down-to-down inaccuracy was the storyline of this game. He routinely threw passes behind Emeka Egbuka, who only caught seven passes despite seeing a whopping 16 targets on the day. Daniels also overthrew Egbuka on a long touchdown pass that could have changed the course of this game. Baker Mayfield hasn’t resumed throwing yet, meaning Daniels will likely get at least one more start. Averaging just 167 passing yards and one passing touchdown per game, Daniels will be a low-end QB2 for his Week 7 matchup versus Carolina.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalon-dani.headline: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said it’s “too early to tell” if Baker Mayfield (thumb) will be able to play in Week 7 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalon-dani.analysis: Mayfield has already been ruled out for Week 6’s game against the Steelers. After being a DNP in practice all week, Mayfield could still be another week away from returning. It was reported on Wednesday that he is still unable to grip/throw a football, so this will be a situation to keep an eye on when the Bucs begin prepping for next week’s game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalon-dani.headline: Baker Mayfield (thumb) did not practice Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalon-dani.analysis: Mayfield will be ruled out for Week 6 tomorrow. Having not thrown a football since his Week 3 thumb injury, he’s also unlikely to suit up for next week’s game against the Panthers. Jalon Daniels will draw at least one more start versus the Steelers this week. His rushing production will keep him in the QB2 ranks for Sunday’s game, but a lack of passing numbers makes him a weak fantasy option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalon-dani.headline: Bucs coach Todd Bowles said Baker Mayfield (thumb) has not resumed throwing yet.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalon-dani.analysis: Mayfield did not practice today and is a safe bet to miss Week 6 as he continues to work his way back from the dislocated thumb he suffered in Week 3. The fact that he can’t even throw a football right now, let alone participate in practice, suggests Mayfield could be out beyond just Week 6. Jalon Daniels will start on Sunday versus the Steelers. Daniels has been held well under 200 passing yards in both of his starts, but he does at least have 78 rushing yards in those contests. His output as a runner will keep him in the QB2 mix for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalon-dani.headline: Baker Mayfield (thumb) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalon-dani.analysis: Mayfield is unlikely to suit up this week against the Steelers, leaving Jalon Daniels to get another start for Tampa. Daniel last week in a win over Dallas completed 19-of-25 passes for 189 yards and one touchdown, rushing for 23 yards. Daniels ranked tenth in EPA per drop back on the week and 11th in drop back success rate. His rushing makes Daniels a viable superflex option this week against the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalon-dani.headline: Jalon Daniels completed 19-of-25 passes for 189 yards and one touchdown in the Buccaneers’ 24-16, Week 5 win over the Cowboys, adding 23 yards on seven carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalon-dani.analysis: Daniels watched from the sideline as the Cowboys took the opening possession for quick touchdown drive, responding in splendid fashion by piecing together the longest Buccaneers drive since 2007 to knot the game at seven at the start of the second quarter. A last-minute Brandon Aubrey field goal at the end of the first half sent the Buccaneers to the break down by three but two early touchdowns after the break gave the Buccaneers a lead they would not relinquish. Running back Bucky Irving broke free for a 72-yard gain on the first play of the third quarter and Emeka Egbuka would punch it in on a 14-yard rush the following play. A Dak Prescott interception on the subsequent possession gave the ball right back to Daniels and the Buccaneers. Another explosive play, this time a 64-yard, catch-and-run dime to Tez Johnson got them immediately back into scoring position. Daniels picks up his first professional win in his second career start while the Buccaneers improve to 1-4, miraculously only 1.5-games back of the division lead. Daniels will be a shaky QB2 when the Bucs host the Steelers in Week 6, assuming he gets at least one more start for the injured Baker Mayfield.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalon-dani.headline: Jalon Daniels completed 19-of-27 passes for 148 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in the Bucs’ 17-14, Week 4 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalon-dani.analysis: Daniels added 55 yards on the ground. It was a long day for the UDFA rookie. The Bucs had five drives in the first half. They went three-and-out twice. Daniels was intercepted twice. And Sean Tucker punched in a short score. Daniels started to find his rhythm in the second half and tossed his first career touchdown to Kenneth Gainwell on an impressive scramble drill. In the end, the Packers dialed up the blitz and forced a near-interception on fourth down to get the ball back inside the two-minute warning. Daniels’ rushing will keep him in the QB2 mix for Week 5 versus the Cowboys, but he will need to play better to keep the job beyond that game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalon-dani.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports an MRI revealed no ligament or tendon damage to Baker Mayfield’s dislocated thumb.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalon-dani.analysis: In addition to a clean report on his ligaments and tendons, the MRI also revealed no fracture. This is as good of news as the Buccaneers could have hoped for, as Mayfield’s absence is expected to be on the shorter end compared to what it could have been had the MRI revealed more damage. Head coach Todd Bowles said Mayfield is looking at a minimum three-week absence, which would put him in line to return for Week 7 against the Panthers if all goes well. Rookie UDFA Jalon Daniels, who went 0-for-3 passing with an interception against the Vikings, will draw the start in the Buccaneers’ Week 4 game against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalon-dani.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Baker Mayfield could miss 2-4 weeks with his thumb injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalon-dani.analysis: This is the “best-case” scenario, according to Rap. Mayfield will undergo an MRI to confirm the severity of his injury and could miss more time if an MRI reveals “significantly torn ligaments in his thumb,” per Rap. The Buccaneers will now pivot to rookie UDFA Jalon Daniels as their starter after Daniels won the backup job in camp. Daniels threw for 9,282 yards, 67 touchdowns, and 31 interceptions in six seasons at Kansas while also rushing for over 1,400 yards and another 23 scores. All Buccaneers pass-catchers will receive a significant downgrade heading into Week 4’s game against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.headline: Dan Patrick of The Dan Patrick Show said a source familiar with the Colts’ GM situation told him the team’s “first call will be/has been to Peyton Manning.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.analysis: Patrick isn’t a reporter we go to often here, but he’s a well-connected veteran in the industry. According to Patrick, his source said the call with Manning will not only be to get the names of potential candidates for the GM vacancy but also to “explore whether or not Peyton would be interested in being a general manager for the Colts as the entry point that would include ownership interest in the Colts.” Mannings’ connection to the Colts doesn’t need to be explained to anyone, but it’s far too early to say whether Manning has any interest in the role. Long-time GM Chris Ballard was recently relieved of his duties, and the Colts will likely speak to several candidates to fill the role in the offseason. Manning has not been involved in any football front office roles since retiring after the 2015 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.headline: Peyton Manning has been elected to the Pro Football Hall-of-Fame.
https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.analysis: The absolutely loaded 2021 class also includes Calvin Johnson. Alongside fantasy legends Manning and Megatron, DB Charles Woodson, S John Lynch, OG Alan Faneca, WR Drew Pearson, executive Bill Nunn and coach Tom Flores will also be enshrined. One of the greatest players in league history, Manning also helped fundamentally change the way the game is played his hyper-accurate, precision passing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.headline: Bleacher Report’s Kalyn Kahler reports Peyton Manning has had “offers to run teams.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.analysis: Since retiring in 2016, Manning has bounced from organization to organization informally taking notes on how teams are operated, particularly with scouting. There have been a few reports of Manning having offers to be a general manager, although the future Hall of Fame quarterback denies that a written offer has never been presented. It’s clear that Manning has some degree of interest in an executive role, but it’s unclear if he’ll actually accept a position at any point in the near future. People around Manning believe he’d be better as a general manager than as a television analyst because of how much he likes being hands on. He will likely have offers to go in either direction for the next decade. In the meantime, Manning has commercials to film.

https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.headline: Peyton Manning is 0-5 in Foxboro in his career, with 15 interceptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.analysis: If you own Ty Law in IDP leagues, be sure to start him, as he owns seven of those picks. We really don’t expect Manning to continue to struggle this badly against New England, but neither will he have his best game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.headline: Coach Tony Dungy wants to see his starting offense get more time together in Saturday’s preseason game.
https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.analysis: Quarterback Peyton Manning, wide receiver Marvin Harrison, running back Edgerrin James and the No. 1 offense are slated for a heavier workload, perhaps playing a good way into the second quarter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.headline: Peyton Manning said Tuesday night on Letterman that he’d be willing to defer money to help the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.analysis: Consider the place he’s saying it, but Manning was quoted saying, ''I want to be a Colt for life, and so they’ll start doing that probably maybe next year, the year after. . . . You do what you can to help build the team around you, to keep some of the good players and get some new young players.’'

https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.headline: When asked about how much his starters will play in week 17, coach Tony Dungy said, “They’ll all play.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.analysis: We doubt they’ll play much. A scheduling oddity has them facing the Broncos, their most likely playoff opponent, at the end of the season for the second straight year. The Broncos punked the Colts late last season before getting embarrased in the playoffs. It could happen again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.headline: Colts owner Jim Irsay reiterated his faith that the Colts will re-sign Peyton Manning, making him the highest paid player in the league.
https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.analysis: Manning is an unrestricted free agent, but there doesn’t appear to be any chance of this deal not getting done. The team could also franchise him, but that would cost $18.4 million against the cap this season, so a long-term deal would make more sense. Marvin Harrison and Edgerrin James are both free agents after this season. Keeping all 3 may prove difficult.

https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.headline: The Colts deadline to get Peyton Manning signed to a long-term deal is today.
https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.analysis: Colts fans everywhere should be crossing their fingers because their team’s depth will seriously suffer if a deal is not reached. Manning is currently the Colts franchise player.

https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.headline: Peyton Manning signed a contract today that will make him the highest-paid player in NFL history.
https://www.nbcsports.com/peyton-manning.analysis: The contract is worth $99.2 million over seven years, including a $34.5 million signing bonus. Manning’s per-year average salary will be $14.17 million, the highest ever by far. The deal helps Indianapolis’ salary cap flexibility this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-dodds/0.headline: Colts assistant GM Ed Dodds will lead the team’s personnel department for the remainder of the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-dodds/0.analysis: With the Colts sitting on a 2-4 record and the trade deadline 22 days away, Dodds could be involved in some key roster decisions over the next three weeks. Dodds was hired as the Colts’ vice president of player personnel in 2017 and has been a candidate for several GM openings over the last few offseasons. Depending on how things go the rest of the way, it’s possible Dodds earns a chance to be promoted to the Colts GM position next offseason after the team fired Chris Ballard earlier in the day.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-dodds/0.headline: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports the Titans will interview Colts assistant GM Ed Dodds a second time for their general manager vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-dodds/0.analysis: Dodds is one of five names (so far) the Titans have been linked to via second interview, including Chiefs assistant GM Mike Borgonzi, Bucs assistant GM John Spytek, Bears assistant GM Ian Cunningham, and Bills executive Terrance Gray. Where is Ruston Webster when you need him? Dodds has been interviewed several times over the past few years, including multiple interviews with the Raiders last year and single interviews with the Panthers and Chargers. Dodds has been the Colts assistant GM to Chris Ballard since 2018 and has also worked for the Seahawks and Raiders as he climbed the ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-dodds/0.headline: Titans requested an interview with Colts assistant general manager Ed Dodds for the team’s general manager vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-dodds/0.analysis: The Titans, fresh off firing former GM Ran Carthon after two years at the helm, will talk with Dodds, who has been discussed as a potential replacement for Colts GM Chris Ballard. Dodds — who is reportedly close with Colts owner Jim Irsay — would appear to be more likely to stay in Indy before bailing to an undesirable job in the Titans front office.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-dodds/0.headline: The Athletic’s Tashan Reed reports the Raiders had second interviews with three different general manager candidates.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-dodds/0.analysis: According to Reed, the Raiders held second interviews with interim GM Champ Kelly, former Chargers GM Tom Telesco, and Colts assistant GM Ed Dodds. Reed also adds that owner Mark Davis “expressed hesitation” about hiring a rookie GM and head coach, which could tilt the job in Telesco’s favor. Telesco last served as the Chargers’ GM from 2013 through 2023 and was fired last December when the team also opted to cut ties with coach Brandon Staley.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-dodds/0.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Colts assistant GM Ed Dodds met with the Raiders and will meet with the Panthers and Chargers for their GM vacancies.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-dodds/0.analysis: Dodds has been with the Colts since 2018 and has a busy schedule of general manager interviews for this hiring cycle. Schefter reports that Dodds has interviewed with the Raiders and plans to meet with the Panthers and Chargers as well. The three teams are looking to fill their general manager vacancies with different appeals to all three jobs. Dodds is in demand as a potential new general manager this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-dodds/0.headline: The Raiders requested interviews with 49ers assistant GM Adam Peters and Colts assistant GM Ed Dodds for their GM vacancy, according to multiple reports.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-dodds/0.analysis: ESPN’s Adam Schefter broke the news on Peters, who has also been targeted by the Commanders as a potential GM candidate. NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero broke the news on Dodds, who has been with the Colts since 2018. The Colts have appeared in the playoffs only twice since Dodds was hired, but he makes for a tough evaluation given owner Jim Irsay’s involvement in roster decisions and Irsay’s relationship with GM Chris Ballard. The Raiders have several decisions to make in the coming days, as they’ll also be deciding whether to promote interim head coach Antonio Pierce to head coach or hire another candidate from outside. Dodds and Peters are only two candidates in a GM search that is expected to include a few more candidates before a decision is made.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-dodds/0.headline: Dale Lolley of DK PGH Sports reports that the Steelers want to talk to Colts assistant GM Ed Dodds and Titans VP of Player Personnel Ryan Cowden about their soon-to-be vacant GM position.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-dodds/0.analysis: Steelers GM Kevin Colbert will retire after the 2022 NFL Draft, though reportedly may stay on in some role after the season as support. This is the first we’ve heard of real candidates to replace him. Dodds was a hot name in each of the last two offseasons and withdrew his name from consideration for the Bears job in January.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-dodds/0.headline: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports Colts assistant GM Ed Dodds has withdrawn his name from consideration for the Bears’ general-manage vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-dodds/0.analysis: Dodds is also in the mix for the Raiders’ GM gig, so perhaps he’s more interested in that one or likes where he is with the Colts. He’s already passed up multiple jobs in the last couple years to stay with Indianapolis. Other executives known to interview for the Bears’ GM job are Glenn Cook, Kwesi Adofo-Mensah, Jeff Ireland, Monti Ossenfort, Joe Schoen, and Eliot Wolf.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-dodds/0.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Raiders requested an interview with Patriots director of player personnel Dave Ziegler for their GM job.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-dodds/0.analysis: The Raiders currently have Mike Mayock as their GM but this points to the end of his tenure in Las Vegas. After a tumultuous season off the field, the Raiders may be cleaning house this offseason. Head coach Jon Gruden resigned earlier this year. Interim head coach Rich Bisaccia led Vegas to the playoffs and the team is conducting head coaching interviews anyway. Mayock might be the next to go. Ziegler was a candidate to land the GM gig in Denver last year but chose to stay in New England instead. He took over as director of player personnel for Nick Caserio after the latter left for Houston. The Raiders also put in a request in interview Colts executive Ed Dodds.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-dodds/0.headline: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports the Bears have requested an interview with Colts assistant general manager Ed Dodds for the team’s GM opening.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ed-dodds/0.analysis: The Bears are also interested in Colts defensive coordinator Matt Eberflus for their head coaching vacancy. Dodd was a favorite to land the Browns’ general manager position in 2020, but stayed with the Colts because he had “unfinished business.” He’ll have a strong chance to being the Bears’ next GM if he wants the gig.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ja’Kobi Lane caught 4-of-5 targets for 40 yards in the Ravens’ Week 6 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Lane was immediately involved in the offense after missing the previous four weeks with a wrist injury. The rookie third-rounder caught two of his four passes on the Ravens’ opening drive that ended with a short touchdown pass to Josh Cuevas and ran 22 routes on the day. Zay Flowers (34) and Devontez Walker (26) both ran more routes than Lane on the afternoon, but Lane has been targeted on 21.1 percent of his routes in limited action this season. Fantasy managers shouldn’t be looking to start him in Week 7 against the Bengals, but the early volume is encouraging for a player who was hyped up throughout training camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Ravens WR Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is “good to go” and should be activated for Week 6 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: While nothing is official yet, Lane practiced in full all week, which is another good sign for his availability against the Browns this weekend. Lane was one of the most impressive rookies this offseason and preseason. Rashod Bateman isn’t on the injury report, but missed practice during the week with a shoulder. Lane could conceivably operate as the second option in the Ravens passing game behind Zay Flowers as early as this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is questionable for Baltimore’s Week 6 game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Lane practiced in full all week, lending credence to the idea that he’ll be activated. Ravens coach Jesse Minter stopped short of saying Lane would play when given a chance, saying they’d “figure that out,” but said he had a great week of practice.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Bateman played through the shoulder injury last week. He was limited yesterday, but coach Jesse Minter said he wasn’t worried. Downgrading to a DNP is not a good sign. Meanwhile, Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is practicing fully this week and could hop right into WR2 duties for the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Earlier today, NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reported that Lane has “a shot” to face the Browns in Week 6. His full participation furthers that notion. The talented rookie drew rave reports all summer before suffering an unfortunate wrist fracture in Week 1. While he makes for a dicey FLEX if Tyler Huntley is under center, Lane should at least be safely stashed on fantasy football benches in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) has “a shot” to play in Week 6.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said Lane, who injured his wrist in the season opener against the Colts, will return to practice this week and could suit up this weekend against the Browns. Lane had impressed Ravens coaches and beat writers through training camp and in Week 1 he caught one of three targets for 11 yards before exiting with the wrist injury. Lane’s return to the Baltimore lineup could limit snaps and routes for Rashod Bateman Devontez Walker. Lane should be picked up in 14-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ravens placed WR Ja’Kobi Lane on injured reserve with a wrist injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Lane underwent surgery to address a fracture in his wrist and will now miss at least four games on short-term injured reserve. He will be eligible to return in Week 6. Ravens No. 1 WR Zay Flowers (hamstring) is also nursing an injury. Theoretically, fellow rookie WR Elijah Sarratt should be active in Week 2 against the Saints, though it is unclear if he would have a meaningful role if Flowers plays.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Ravens WR Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) is expected to undergo surgery “in the coming days.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Lane fractured his wrist in the Ravens’ Week 1 victory over the Colts, catching one pass for 11 yards in his rookie debut. The 22-year-old operated as a top-three receiver in the Ravens offense and was set for a sizeable role prior to the injury. He was seeking multiple opinions on the injury as of Monday, but Zenitz now reports Lane is expected to have surgery on his wrist very soon. Zenitz adds that the hope is for the rookie to be able to return in a month. Injured reserve will be a consideration for Lane, which would be a four-game absence at the minimum.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: Ravens HC Jesse Minter said Ja’Kobi Lane will seek second and third opinions after suffering a fractured wrist in Week 1’s win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: It was reported Sunday night that Lane was likely to miss several weeks, but on Monday, Minter said Lane could be out a bit longer than expected. The rookie third-rounder caught 1-of-3 targets for 11 yards in his pro debut but was seeing a good amount of work before exiting. Lane’s 24 first-half snaps were the second-most of any Ravens receiver. We’ll likely have a better sense of how long Lane will be sidelined in the coming days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports that Ravens WR Ja’Kobi Lane suffered a fractured wrist and will undergo further testing to determine the full extent of the injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-lan.analysis: Garafolo’s colleague, Ian Rapoport, adds that Lane will be sidelined for “several weeks.” This is an unfortunate development for both the player and the team. Fellow Ravens WR Zay Flowers aggravated the hamstring injury he recently rehabbed as well. Expect rookie WR Elijah Sarratt to be active in Week 2 against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.headline: Jordan Davis (ankle) told reporters x-rays were negative on his ankle and he feels “OK” at this point.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.analysis: Davis is still a candidate to be limited in practice this week, but it doesn’t look like this injury is a major threat to send him to injured reserve or anything like that. Talking with the media after the game is a good sign for his future ability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.headline: Jordan Davis went to the locker room in the middle of Week 6 against the Panthers with a leg injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.analysis: Jordan Davis was at the bottom of a pile on a 3rd-down run in the fourth quarter and remained down on the field. He was slow to get up and did leave the field under his own power, but he was moving very gingerly as he walked into the locker room. It’s unclear right now if the injury is to his ankle or his knee, but we should get an update after the game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.headline: Eagles signed DT Jordan Davis to a three-year, $78 million extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.analysis: The deal includes a whopping $65 million in guaranteed money. Davis is now tied to the Eagles through the 2029 season after becoming the highest-paid nose tackle in NFL history with the extension. The former No. 13 overall pick in 2022 notched the second most solo tackles in 2025 amongst defensive linemen and also contributed five sacks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.headline: Eagles DT Jalen Carter (heel) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.analysis: On the plus side, fellow DT Jordan Davis (shoulder) continues to practice in full and LG Landon Dickerson (ankle) at least remained limited rather than experiencing a downgrade. Hopefully, this is just a pre-planned rest day for Carter, who sat out in the Eagles’ Week 6 upset loss to the Giants. The G-Men ran the ball aggressively, totaling 172 yards and four touchdowns on 48 carries. The Vikings could employ a similar game plan with RB Jordan Mason if Carter is again out this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.headline: Eagles DT Jordan Davis lost 26 pounds this offseason and is expecting to play more snaps.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.analysis: Davis now tips the scales at 330 pounds. This is the lightest he’s been since his sophomore year at Georgia, per PHLY Eagles’ Zach Berman. Davis has functioned as a rotational player since the Eagles drafted him in the 2022 NFL Draft’s first round. A well-conditioned Davis on the field for all three downs could take a step forward in his fourth season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.headline: Eagles exercised the fifth-year option for DT Jordan Davis.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.analysis: After Eagles general manager Howie Roseman declined to say whether the team would pick up Davis’ option just two weeks prior, the team made the call after Davis played his second straight 17-game season for the dominant Philly front seven. Davis, who has 3.5 sacks and five tackles for loss over his past two seasons, was graded by Pro Football Focus as 2024’s 40th-best defensive tackle. He will make $12.9 million in the 2026 season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.headline: Eagles GM Howie Roseman declined to disclose if the team would pick up Jordan Davis’ fifth-year option.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.analysis: “The absence of a decision on Davis logically suggests the Eagles are still weighing their options ahead of the May 1 deadline,” writes The Athletic’s Brooks Kubena. Perhaps the Eagles are leaving their options open because of certain draft scenarios, but Davis has been a fine rotational player for the Eagles in his first three seasons. Davis has generated a 70.9 or better PFF grade in all three of his seasons to date, but has yet to play more than 561 snaps for the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.headline: Jordan Davis (hamstring) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.analysis: Davis being added to the injury report on Thursday is a bit concerning, but the fact he was able to log a limited session is still encouraging. We’ll see how he fares in Friday’s practice, but for now, we’d expect him to suit up for Week 8 against the Commanders. In addition to Davis, the Eagles also added CB James Bradberry (ankle) and LB Zach Cunningham (ankle) to the practice report. Both were listed as limited participants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.headline: Eagles declared DE Robert Quinn, QB Ian Book, CB Josh Jobe, RB Trey Sermon, G Josh Sills, and G Sua Opeta inactive for Week 13 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.analysis: Quinn injured his knee in practice, and the pass rusher was declared out on Friday. It’s a blow for the Eagles’ ability to get to the passer. However, the Eagles will have DT Jordan Davis, who is returning from injured reserve. bolstering the interior of the defensive line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.headline: Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni said he’s hopeful DT Jordan Davis (ankle) can play in Week 13 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jordan-dav.analysis: Philadelphia’s rush defense has been horrendous with Davis sidelined since Week 8. Only six defenses have allowed a higher EPA against the rush than the Eagles since Davis suffered his ankle injury. Davis practiced this week and should return just in time to face Derrick Henry and the run-heavy Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jalen Hurts “will be out an estimated three months as he undergoes treatment” for blood clots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.analysis: This would effectively end Hurts’ season, as a three-month absence would have him on track to return some time in late-January/early-February. In a statement released by Hurts’ agent, Nicole Lyyn, she said further tests revealed “deep vein thrombosis as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli.” She said that Hurts is stable and is not expected to have any “functional limitations” and that his treatment to resolve his blood clotting issues “should only involve anticoagulation [i.e., ‘blood thinners’].” As a result, Hurts will not be permitted to engage in football activities and will not be allowed to resume them until he is off his blood thinners. The good news here is that Hurts is expected to make a full recovery, and the doctors do not believe this will have a long-term effect on him moving forward. Hurts threw for 933 yards, eight touchdowns, and three interceptions this season while completing 57.8 percent of his passes — his lowest mark since his rookie season. He ran for another 107 yards and one touchdown as he and the Eagles struggled in his first five starts under offensive coordinator Sean Mannion. He remains under contract through the 2028 season, but Hurts has faced his fair share of scrutiny since leading the Eagles to a Super Bowl title in 2024. Hurts’ contract situation would suggest his job is more than secured for the foreseeable future, but this is the same Eagles front office that used a 2020 second round pick to select him as the heir apparent to Carson Wentz, who signed a four-year extension with the team in 2019. While we fully expect Hurts to be back with the Eagles next season, we can’t rule out the team using an early draft pick on a quarterback in a draft that is projected to be one of the more QB-rich drafts in recent memory.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.headline: Eagles placed Jalen Hurts (blood clots) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.analysis: Whelp, that reversed course quickly. It was reported earlier Saturday that the team was not planning on placing their franchise quarterback on injured reserve, with the team going back on those comments less than seven hours later. Although not yet fully evident, it appears as if additional information was ascertained during the day. There is no telling how long Hurts will be away from the team, with most recent reporting simply labeling it an “indefinite” absence. Tanner McKee steps into the starting role and could be worthy of deep league consideration as a QB2, for the foreseeable future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Eagles aren’t planning to place QB Jalen Hurts (blood clot) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.analysis: While Hurts still has no timetable to return, the Eagles haven’t even discussed the possibility of placing him on injured reserve, according to Schefter. That could change as there’s still a possibility Hurts could wind up on injured reserve if that’s where the medical information leads them. Most blood clots are treated with anticoagulants (blood thinners), which would sideline Hurts for a minimum of six weeks, according to Schefter’s sources. The best-case scenario, according to Schefter, seems to be if the blood clot is minor enough that doctors could begin treatment with anti-inflammatories. Two team doctors that Schefter polled also speculated that the 28-year-old quarterback could miss six weeks. Tanner McKee is in line to start at least a few games while Hurts is out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Eagles will decide whether to place Jalen Hurts (blood clot) on short-term injured reserve on Saturday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.analysis: Fowler reportedly spoke to “some people who are hopeful” that Hurts can avoid injured reserve. He described the situation as being “very much touch and go” and said Tanner McKee will “probably” start multiple games. The Eagles go on bye in Week 10, so if Hurts does land on injured reserve, the Eagles’ Week 11 game against the Steelers would be his earliest possible return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.headline: Speaking on the Pat McAfee Show, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said he “would describe” Jalen Hurts’ (blood clot) status as being “out indefinitely.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.analysis: Hurts’ blood clot was initially a superficial issue in his calf. Unfortunately, the clot has moved and the situation now appears to be quite serious and, per Rapoport, “scary.” Rapoport said Hurts will now undergo treatment, “which, a lot of times, is blood thinners.” If that treatment option is deemed necessary, Hurts would not be allowed to play. Rapoport believes Hurts will be sidelined in Week 6 “and likely beyond.” Tanner McKee is his replacement.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Tanner McKee will start for the Eagles until Jalen Hurts’ (superficial blood clot) “medical situation is solved.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.analysis: McKee, 26, is a towering pocket passer (6'6/231) with 97 career dropbacks. He has two career starts and has made appearances in two other contests, averaging 6.8 yards per attempt and a 73.8 percent adjusted completion rate. McKee was the subject of trade rumors last offseason, but luckily, the Eagles kept him. He faces a Panthers secondary missing its two starting perimeter cornerbacks, though he has almost exactly 72 hours to get himself ready and the Eagles’ pass-catching corps is banged up. He is a viable QB2 in superflex formats, but he offers a wide range of potential outcomes. McKee is backed up by rookie Cole Payton. NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo thinks the team could reunite with Andy Dalton, whom they released last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo believes the Eagles could re-sign Andy Dalton.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.analysis: Dalton is “an option” for the Eagles, who are down to two available quarterbacks this week, Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton, with Jalen Hurts having been ruled out preemptively due to a superficial blood clot in his calf. The Eagles released Dalton last week. A few teams have reportedly checked in with Dalton since his release, “though there’s familiarity and a clear role in Philly for him if he decides to return.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.headline: Jalen Hurts has a “superficial blood clot” and will not play in Week 6 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.analysis: The Eagles released an official statement announcing the news. Per their statement, Hurts took a cleat to the calf in Week 4. He went in for treatment the following Thursday and an ultrasound revealed the blood clot. Doctors ultimately cleared him to play in Week 5. He continued to receive treatment over the next two days. After practice on Wednesday (yesterday), a follow-up ultrasound revealed movement in the small blood clot. The team has now ruled him out for Week 6 as they determine the next course of action. They didn’t comment on how long Hurts will be out, but it’s possible this is a long-term issue for the veteran quarterback. Tanner McKee will draw the start versus Carolina.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.headline: Jalen Hurts completed 21-of-40 passes for 220 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ 19-17, Week 5 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.analysis: Hurts added a grand total of two yards on the ground. The Eagles even seemed afraid to use him for tush pushes, opting for a shotgun handoff on an early fourth-and-one. The bulk of Hurts’ production through the air came on a single deep shot to Darius Cooper. Hurts’ pass was actually a bit off the mark, but Cooper adjusted well and sprinted into the end zone for a 62-yard touchdown. Hurts had Dontayvion Wicks wide open for his second long score of the day late in the third quarter, but an all-out blitz forced him to throw off his back foot and he overshot the attempt. A field goal with eight seconds left on the clock still should have been enough to win the game. Philly’s kick coverage unit then got burned by Ameer Abdullah, setting up a walk-off kick from Cam Little. The Philly offense is as lifeless as they come. Even if DeVonta Smith returns for Week 6 versus the Panthers, Hurts will fail to crack the top-12 at quarterback for the first time in years.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.headline: Jalen Hurts (calf) is not on Philadelphia’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-hurt.analysis: Hurts popped up with a calf injury on Friday, but practiced in full and seems to be expected to play. Tanner McKee, now the only game in town after Andy Dalton’s release, would take over if necessary on Sunday. It doesn’t sound like anything to be overly worried about at this point, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.headline: Falcons released Cooper Rush.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.analysis: Rush’s release came after the Falcons signed Andy Dalton. Rush had a rough stretch with the Falcons, throwing for 229-1-4 in his two starts while completing 56.4 percent of his passes. Once regarded as one of the better backup quarterbacks in the league, Rush has struggled mightily in his two seasons away from the Cowboys, going 0-4 in his starts since 2024 while throwing one touchdown to eight interceptions. He could catch on elsewhere as a practice squad option in the coming days, but he seems like a long shot to start another game in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.headline: Falcons declared Cooper Rush, QB Jack Strand, CB Malcom DeWalt IV, CB Roger Longerbeam, DE Jared Iven, and OL Ethan Onianwa inactive for Week 4 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.analysis: Rush will serve as the emergency quarterback over Jack Strand. LB Samsom Ebukam, who came into the weekend listed as questionable, will play against the Saints. The Falcons look to move into a tie atop the NFC South against their divisional opponent after beating the Packers in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.headline: Falcons declared QB Cooper Rush, QB Jack Strand, CB Malcolm Dewalt, CB Robert Longerbeam, EDGE Samson Ebukam and OT Ethan Onianwa inactive for Week 3 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.analysis: Rush sits ahead of Strand on the depth chart and has been labeled as this evening’s emergency third quarterback. Hopefully, it doesn’t come to that. Week 3 marks QB Michael Penix’s return to action following last year’s season-ending knee injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.headline: Speaking Monday, Falcons HC Kevin Stefanski did not commit to naming a starting QB for Week 3’s game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.analysis: With the Falcons set to play on Thursday night, Stefanski will have little time to prepare his starter for the week. It’s hard to imagine the team going back to Cooper Rush after back-to-back disastrous starts to open the season, which could pave the way for rookie UDFA Jack Strand to make the start of Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) and Michael Penix Jr. (knee) still aren’t ready to go. Strand completed 8-of-15 passes for 59 yards and an interception in his first taste of NFL action. Stefanski did say he had a “decent idea” of who he thinks he will be starting this week, so we’ll likely have our answer soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.headline: Cooper Rush completed 10-of-17 passes for 86 yards and two interceptions before being benched in the third quarter of the Falcons’ Week 2 game against the Panthers
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.analysis: Rush opened the game with a lost fumble on Atlanta’s first offensive play of the day. Things somehow got worse from there. He was intercepted twice and nearly threw a third, but it went through the hands of Panthers linebacker Bobby Okereke. Rush was arguably the worst starter in the league in Week 1 and nothing changed in Week 2. With Michael Penix expected to make his 2026 debut next week, Rush may have just finished his final career start. Jack Strand will close this game out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.headline: Falcons QB Cooper Rush will start in Week 2 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.analysis: It was reported earlier that Rush was expected to draw the start, but with Michael Penix Jr. (knee) officially ruled out, it will be Rush getting the ball against the Panthers. Rush struggled in last week’s game against the Steelers, throwing for 143 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions on 22 attempts. Drake London shouldn’t be viewed as anything more than a WR2 in fantasy this week with Rush under center, while Kyle Pitts profiles as a boom-or-bust TE1 after putting up zero fantasy points in Week 1. Jack Strand will serve as Rush’s backup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Cooper Rush is expected to start in Week 2 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.analysis: Rush is taking all of the first-team reps with the Falcons in Friday’s practice, and according to Rapoport, sources familiar with the situation expect Rush to get the nod on Sunday. With Rush under center, all Falcons pass-catchers receive a substantial downgrade after he struggled to move the ball in Week 1 against the Steelers. Fantasy managers hoping Drake London and Kyle Pitts can be of some value against a Panthers defense that allowed 269 yards and two passing TDs to the Bears last week should approach both players with caution. London is best trusted as more of a WR2, while Pitts, who saw one target on 21 routes last week, shouldn’t be viewed as anything more than a boom-or-bust TE2 in what figures to be a run-heavy game for the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.headline: Falcons QB Cooper Rush (back) is practicing in full for Week 2 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.analysis: Rush told reporters that he and QB Michael Penix (knee) split first-team reps, though the coaching staff already said Penix is not yet ready to take the field on game day. Rush or rookie QB Jack Strand will likely start, with QB Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) ailing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.headline: Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski said QB Cooper Rush is getting treatment for a back injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.analysis: Stefanski on Wednesday wouldn’t rule out any of his four quarterbacks of the apocalypse, including rookie QB Jack Strand, who flashed in preseason action against second and third-team defenses. Rush as abysmal in the Falcons’ Week 1 loss to the Steelers. He was 10.5 percent below his expected pass rate, throwing for 143 yards, one touchdown, and two picks. There’s almost no way Strand would be a downgrade for Week 2 if he gets the nod. Michael Penix (knee) will continued to be sidelined and Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) is questionable at best. Strand should be picked up in superflex leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Tua Tagovailoa (oblique) is dealing with a strain and is day-to-day.
