https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cooper-rus.analysis: But, Rapoport added, that doesn’t necessarily mean he’ll play this week. “Generally, for a throwing position, it’s not usually one week,” Rapoport added. Cooper Rush could be awaiting the Panthers in Week 2, and based on how Rush played in Week 1, that means the Panthers defense could go from allowing 59 points to being a streamable defense in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andy-dalto.headline: Falcons signed Andy Dalton, formerly of the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andy-dalto.analysis: Dalton had a chance to re-sign with the Eagles after being let go by them earlier in the week, but he spurned them to sign with Atlanta. The 38-year-old vet will presumably serve as the Falcons’ third-string QB for now, but could be one injury away from seeing playing time. Dalton threw for 293-1-1 on 37 pass attempts for the Panthers last season and has not started more than five games in a season since 2022.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andy-dalto.headline: NBC Sports’ Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio reports that Andy Dalton declined an offer to re-sign with the Eagles and will sign with another team “as soon as tomorrow.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andy-dalto.analysis: The Eagles released Dalton less than two weeks ago. According to Florio, the Eagles reached out to Dalton with an offer after Jalen Hurts’ superficial blood clot moved in his calf, resulting in an indefinite sidelining, and Dalton told the Eagles, “no, thank you.” Florio did not reveal where Dalton plans to sign, but we should get word on that before long.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andy-dalto.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Tanner McKee will start for the Eagles until Jalen Hurts’ (superficial blood clot) “medical situation is solved.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andy-dalto.analysis: McKee, 26, is a towering pocket passer (6'6/231) with 97 career dropbacks. He has two career starts and has made appearances in two other contests, averaging 6.8 yards per attempt and a 73.8 percent adjusted completion rate. McKee was the subject of trade rumors last offseason, but luckily, the Eagles kept him. He faces a Panthers secondary missing its two starting perimeter cornerbacks, though he has almost exactly 72 hours to get himself ready and the Eagles’ pass-catching corps is banged up. He is a viable QB2 in superflex formats, but he offers a wide range of potential outcomes. McKee is backed up by rookie Cole Payton. NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo thinks the team could reunite with Andy Dalton, whom they released last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andy-dalto.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo believes the Eagles could re-sign Andy Dalton.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andy-dalto.analysis: Dalton is “an option” for the Eagles, who are down to two available quarterbacks this week, Tanner McKee and rookie Cole Payton, with Jalen Hurts having been ruled out preemptively due to a superficial blood clot in his calf. The Eagles released Dalton last week. A few teams have reportedly checked in with Dalton since his release, “though there’s familiarity and a clear role in Philly for him if he decides to return.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andy-dalto.headline: Eagles released Andy Dalton.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andy-dalto.analysis: Dalton was demoted to the QB3 spot after throwing an end zone interception while Jalen Hurts was going through a concussion check in Week 3. Someone will take his spot on the active roster. We just don’t know who that will be. Eagles general manager Howie Roseman is making moves. Expect more to follow.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andy-dalto.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Tanne McKee is the Eagles’ backup quarterback for Week 4 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andy-dalto.analysis: The Eagles demoted Andy Dalton after his end zone interception in Week 3. He took over for Jalen Hurts while the latter was being evaluated for an injury and immediately gave the ball away in scoring position. McKee has two career starts since being drafted in 2023.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andy-dalto.headline: The Athletic’s Zach Berman reports Tanner McKee’s No. 2 quarterback spot “doesn’t appear secure.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andy-dalto.analysis: To say the least, it’s going to be hard for the Eagles to recoup major draft capital in a trade for McKee if he can’t beat out an Andy Dalton who looked extremely washed last offseason. The backup quarterback battle updates in July will continue until morale improves.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andy-dalto.headline: Eagles acquired QB Andy Dalton from the Panthers in exchange for a seventh-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andy-dalto.analysis: It was previously reported that the Panthers were getting calls for Andy Dalton. The team then went out and signed Kenny Pickett, making it clear they were moving on from Dalton this offseason. Getting even a seventh-round pick in return for Dalton is mildly impressive for Panthers GM Dan Morgan. After the trade, NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo insisted, “Tanner McKee firmly locked into the No. 2 spot behind Jalen Hurts.” That would be a bit odd given that the Eagles just sought out Dalton, though they did carry three quarterbacks on their roster last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andy-dalto.headline: ESPN’s David Newton reports the Panthers “plan” to move on from Andy Dalton.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andy-dalto.analysis: Newton adds “even if it means releasing Dalton and leaving $3.83 million in dead cap money.” Things really crashed down hard from the Andy Dalton Combine “getting calls” experience. Dalton, who turns 39 in October, likely proved that he just wasn’t a good enough backup last year in his start against the Bills to keep paying a premium on. It wouldn’t be surprising if the Panthers cut him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andy-dalto.headline: Speaking on the Pat McAfee Show, Panthers GM Dan Morgan said “I haven’t talked to any teams about a trade (for Andy Dalton).”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/andy-dalto.analysis: This comes a day after ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported the Panthers had been receiving calls about Dalton for a potential trade. Morgan said he “would talk to Andy” about any requests for a trade that may come through, but it’s hard to imagine the 38-year-old signal-caller being in high demand with free agency and the draft still to go. Dalton has one more year remaining on his current deal with the Panthers, and could make for a nice bridge for a team bringing in a younger quarterback, but wouldn’t be viewed as anything more than a one-year option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-ball.headline: Colts fired GM Chris Ballard.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-ball.analysis: The team announced its decision to move on from Ballard early Monday morning. The Colts opted to retain Ballard for a 10th season earlier this offseason despite a monumental collapse in the second half of last season that saw the team finish 8-9 after getting off to an 8-2 start. Ballard was hired as the Colts GM in 2017 and leaves with just two postseason berths and zero division titles to his name. The abrupt retirement of Andrew Luck before the start of the 2018 season presented an early challenge for Ballard to suddenly find a new QB, which often resulted in short-term answers to solve a long-term problem. After the likes of Philip Rivers, Matt Ryan, and Carson Wentz passed through the organization, the Colts finally selected Anthony Richardson in the first round of the 2023 NFL Draft in hopes of landing their guy. When it became apparent Richardson wasn’t the answer, the team signed Daniel Jones, who turned in a solid 2025 campaign and was rewarded with a two-year, $88 million contract earlier this offseason. Among the multiple missteps by Ballard during his Colts tenure is the trade for cornerback Sauce Gardner, whom he acquired in exchange for the team’s 2026 and 2027 first-round picks. Few GMs get the leash that Ballard was provided with by the Colts, but this felt like a move that was destined to happen now or at the end of the season. Now, the Colts can get a head start on their next GM search in what is shaping up to be another rough season. The team announced that head coach Shane Steichen will remain in his role for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-ball.headline: Colts announced they will retain HC Shane Steichen and GM Chris Ballard.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-ball.analysis: After falling from 8-2 to out of the playoffs it’s a mild surprise that both will return. The Colts would probably be hardpressed to do better than Steichen as an offensive mind, so that part makes some sense even if he hasn’t made the playoffs yet. But Ballard’s trade for Sauce Gardner has left the franchise without a first-round pick in 2026 or 2027 and has almost forced them to look into retaining Daniel Jones off a torn Achilles. Ballard hasn’t won a playoff game since 2018. Principal owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon will speak with the media tomorrow.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-ball.headline: The Athletic’s Zak Keefer reports “Jim Irsay has decided to retain coach Shane Steichen and general manager Chris Ballard for the 2025 season.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-ball.analysis: The Colts’ 2024 season was filled with mild highs and myriad lows but Steichen and Ballard will evidently get another shot at turning things around. Their futures beyond 2025 are likely tied directly to Anthony Richardson’s performance. Hopefully, the talented dual-threat quarterback can produce consistently positive results next year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-ball.headline: Colts GM Chris Ballard told reporters that he’ll do “whatever it takes” to trade up in the draft if there’s a quarterback the Colts really want.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-ball.analysis: Good Degrassi reference, Chris. Unrevealed is whether or not the Colts actually like any of these quarterbacks enough to move up from No. 4 to No. 1 (or possibly to No. 3, assuming the Texans are taking a quarterback at No. 2), and which quarterback that would be if so. The Colts have taken on an aura of desperation over the past year, with Jim Irsay micromanaging the organization’s decisions, and it is well within reason that they’ll trade up to No. 1 to try to settle a position that has been rough sledding since Andrew Luck retired.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-ball.headline: Colts owner Jim Irsay said in an interview with ESPN that Chris Ballard will return as general manager in 2023, while interim head coach Jeff Saturday’s return is being strongly considered.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-ball.analysis: This news shouldn’t come as much of a shock, as Irsay was already on record in November saying he expects Ballard to be retained as general manager. His affinity for Saturday isn’t lost on anybody, but a full slate of coaching candidates is expected to be interviewed before the team decides on a new head coach for 2023. In his brief tenure with the team, Saturday has led the Colts to a 1-4 record and played a role in the Vikings setting an NFL record for the largest comeback in league history when they overcame a 36-0 halftime deficit to down the Colts 39-36 in Week 15. Saturday’s qualifications to coach at the NFL level came under fire when Irsay opted to hire him after letting go of Frank Reich after Week 9. More qualified coaching candidates are almost certain to pass through Irsay’s office this upcoming offseason, but whether or not they can move him off his love for Saturday is anybody’s guess.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-ball.headline: Speaking Monday night, Colts owner Jim Irsay said GM Chris Ballard will return for the 2023 season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-ball.analysis: Take it with a grain of salt, as just last week Irsay committed to both Ballard and coach Frank Reich, and then Reich was fired Monday following the Week 9 blowout loss to the Patriots. Ballard has drafted relatively well in his six years at the helm for the Colts, but he’s whiffed time and again in his pursuit of a quarterback ever since Andrew Luck’s abrupt retirement. All in all, Ballard is probably a pretty solid GM, but he really needs to find an answer under center. And he needs to do it ASAP. Sam Ehlinger isn’t the solution.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-ball.headline: Speaking at the Owner’s Meetings, Colts owner Jim Irsay said that the Colts explored a trade for a young quarterback that would have cost two first-round picks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-ball.analysis: This was, of course, before they acquired Matt Ryan. The Colts were on the periphery of the Deshaun Watson talks before the Texans shut them out, but perhaps Chris Ballard had his eye on a different young quarterback as well. The trade never materialized and the Colts instead pivoted to Ryan.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-ball.headline: Colts extended GM Chris Ballard and HC Frank Reich through 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-ball.analysis: Ballard was hired in 2017 and Reich was hired as head coach the following season. Ballard has overseen several strong draft classes, and Reich has coached the Colts to a 28-20 record, including last season’s 11-5 playoff team. Ballard and Reich have shown an ability to quickly adapt at the quarterback position. In 2021 a new quarterback will be under center in Indianapolis for the fourth consecutive season, as Ballard continues to search for a long-term solution in the post-Andrew Luck era. Bringing in Carson Wentz this offseason was a bold move, and one that appears to have resonated with ownership.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-ball.headline: Chiefs director of football operations Chris Ballard won’t interview for the 49ers’ open general manager position.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-ball.analysis: He wasn’t interested in cleaning up the 49ers’ mess. Ballard has a strong relationship with GM John Dorsey and clearly doesn’t want to leave a great situation in Kansas City. The Chiefs won 12 games during the regular season, their most since 2003.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-ball.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the 49ers have requested an interview with Chiefs director of football operations Chris Ballard for their open general manager position.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-ball.analysis: Ballard has been a hot general manager candidate in recent years, and he interviewed with the Titans for their top spot last January. He will likely draw interest from other teams as the carousel revs up to full speed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Savion Williams caught all four targets for 32 yards in the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys, adding nine yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Williams was immediately asked to fill the WR3 role for an offense missing its top two slot receivers. Even so, he finished fifth on the team in targets and carries little fantasy value for as long as the team’s top three options in Christian Watson, Matthew Golden, and Tucker Kraft remain healthy. That doesn’t change ahead of a matchup with the Lions in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Savion Williams (ankle/PUP) is questionable for Green Bay’s Week 6 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Williams was limited in practice all week, making it seem like he could wait another week on the PUP list. When he does come back, the WR3 role would seem to be wide open for him after Jayden Reed’s injury. He remains a decent fantasy football stash if you have extra injured reserve spots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Savion Williams (ankle/IR) will not play in Green Bay’s Week 5 game against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Williams isn’t a half-bad IR stash though with almost all of the offense flowing through Christian Watson and Matthew Golden right now. The WR3 room has been thinned with injuries and Jayden Reed (neck) won’t return this year. Williams could play a major role once activated from IR; this is just the first week of his 21-day window where he was designated to return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Packers GM Brian Gutekunst said WR Savion Williams (ankle/IR) has a high-ankle sprain.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Williams was placed on IR at last cuts without an explanation of the injury, so here it is. Gutekunst said he thinks Williams will be ready when the four-week mandatory stay on IR is over.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Packers placed WR Savion Williams on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Williams, 24, was a non-factor for Green Bay in 2025 with 10 catches for 78 yards; although he did a solid job as a kick returner with 717 yards on his 28 attempts. The 2025 third-round pick has the athleticism to be a helper in 2026, but fantasy managers in redraft leagues shouldn’t count on it .

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Packers WR Matthew Golden (wrist) is not on Green Bay’s final Week 16 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Despite his first useful fantasy game (3/55) in some time last week against Denver, we’d caution against starting Golden in Week 16 as Christian Watson seems likely to play. Savion Williams (foot) is also off the injury report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Packers WR Jayden Reed (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Reed returned from foot and shoulder injuries to play in Week 14, getting four targets on the day. He saw a sizeable role, running over 60 percent of available routes; the Packers will limit his practice workload to start the week. Also limited were fellow wide receivers Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) and Savion Williams (foot). Wicks played through the ankle injury in Week 14 while Williams did not practice all of last week. Reed is still trending to play and is the best receiver out of the three, while Wicks is worth a speculative deep league dart throw and Williams is not fantasy relevant.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Packers WR Dontyavion Wicks (ankle) is not on Green Bay’s final Week 14 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: We’d be surprised if he did anything close to what he did on Thanksgiving against the Bears, but perhaps the 24-year-old has turned over a new leaf with this offense. He’s still a FLEX play at best. The Packers also ruled out WR Savion Williams (foot), who did not practice all week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Savion Williams (foot) did not practice Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: He played through the foot listing last week, generating zero yards on his lone touch. Non-dynasty managers don’t have to worry about Williams this season between his lack of progress and Green Bay’s lack of interest in throwing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Packers WR Romeo Doubs (wrist) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Nearly the entire Packers pass-catching group was either limited or not practicing on Wednesday. Doubs was listed as a limited participant with a wrist injury, along with three other Packers wideouts listed as limited and Savion Williams (foot) listed as a non-participant. Doubs is the current lead receiver in an offense that does not have a definitive No. 1 receiver. If he were to miss time, Christian Watson would be first up for a bump, followed by the rookie Matthew Golden. Stay tuned to Doubs and the rest of the Green Bay receivers’ statuses this week; the Packers’ fantasy hierarchy could see a shake-up if multiple receivers cannot play Week 12 against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 5-of-8 targets for 37 yards in the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Kraft was forced from the game in the second quarter after taking a scary hit to his thigh area that generated torsion on his knee while his foot was still planted. It was the opposite knee to the one he injured a season ago and the veteran tight end would miss only one drive before returning to the game after the half, providing a collective sigh of relief for fantasy managers that have tasted the despair of a major knee injury already. Kraft could be busy in Week 7 against the defense allowing the most fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends when the Packers face off against the division rival Lions in a potential shootout.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 5-of-5 targets for 64 yards in the Packers’ Week 5 win over the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: The five-catch effort was Kraft’s second straight after previously having zero. His 54 yards were also his most since Week 1. His 46-yard reception in the third quarter was his longest of the season. All of that is good, though it was still somewhat disappointing amidst a 367-yard Jordan Love outburst where Christian Watson and Matthew Golden both eased by 100 yards. Kraft is averaging a pedestrian six targets. He’s going to need both more looks and big plays to remain a higher-end TE1. It will nevertheless be impossible to bench him for Week 6 against the Cowboys’ shaky defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 6-of-7 targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Packers’ Week 4 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Jordan Love made it a point to get Kraft going in this game, peppering him with easy-button targets throughout the contest. Kraft led the team with a 23 percent target share. His six grabs also led the team and are a new season high. He found the end zone with an impressive toe-dragging catch at the goal line. Kraft is still looking for the explosive play, but the team is getting him more involved every week. He is back in the TE1 ranks after a slow couple of weeks to start the season. Kraft will look to stay hot versus the Bears next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 4-of-8 targets for 26 yards in the Packers’ Week 3 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Kraft has not yet looked himself after recovering from a torn ACL suffered in 2025, this time committing two drops for the first time in his career. To add additional context, Kraft has never had more than three drops in an entire season entering his fourth year in the league. The game plan clearly consisted of getting Kraft involved early to circumvent the offensive line struggles, but the connection with Jordan Love was off throughout. Kraft appears likely to need time to get back to full speed for the Packers, although his snaps and route participation rate were back to normal for the second consecutive week. Fantasy managers are likely forced to ride through the turbulence considering the state of the tight end position throughout the league, but he is a shaky start ahead of a Week 4 matchup with the Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 2-of-3 targets for 15 yards in the Packers’ Week 2 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: The good news is that Kraft played 52 of the team’s 53 snaps and ran a route on 32 of their 34 dropbacks. The bad news is that he wasn’t commanding targets, and he also fumbled one of his catches, but the replay review couldn’t determine for sure who recovered it, so the Packers were able to maintain possession. Perhaps we should have been a little less aggressive in expecting Kraft to return from tearing his ACL less than a year ago and go right back to being himself at the start of the season. His role remains elite, but it may take another couple of weeks before he’s physically able to play like we’re used to seeing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft caught 3-of-6 targets for 65 yards in the Packers’ Week 1 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Kraft, who tore his ACL in Week 9 last year, told reporters he would not be on a snap count in Week 1. He was. Kraft ran 20 routes to Jonnu Smith’s 18. The good news is that Kraft looked as explosive as ever, racking up gains of 30, 23, and 12 yards. Even with the weak route rate, this goes down as a win for a player whose game is built around big plays. His route rate should climb in the coming weeks, keeping him in the TE1 mix versus the Jets next Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Packers signed TE Tucker Kraft to a four-year, $75 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: The news was first reported by ESPN’s Adam Schefter. Kraft’s deal, which runs through the 2030 season, has a maximum value of $92 million and includes a $26.5 million signing bonus. He’s now the NFL’s highest-paid tight end. Kraft had 32 receptions, 489 yards and six touchdowns before tearing his ACL in Week 9 last year. Not on the injury report for Week 1, Kraft is a surefire TE1 even in a tough matchup against the Vikings defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: The Milwaukee Journal Sentinel’s Tom Silverstein reports that the Packers and TE Tucker Kraft are unlikely to agree on a contract extension before the season opener.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Silverstein believes the deal’s total value likely isn’t as important to the Packers as the structure. Kraft is still likely to reset the tight end market, but since he is returning from a season-ending ACL tear and has “yet to show he’s picked up where he left off last year, it may take some time for the deal to come together.” In the meantime, as long as he takes the field, Kraft can be treated as a TE1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Tucker Kraft (knee) is not on the injury report ahead of his Week 1 game against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Kraft has been trending toward playing in Week 1 for a long time. Not appearing on the injury report in any capacity means he is good to go. Kraft may still have somewhat of a pitch count for his first game back from a 2025 torn ACL, but Matt LaFleur will be sure to get him the ball when he is on the field. Kraft is a fantasy TE1 for the Packers’ Week 1 game against Minnesota.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.headline: Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst said he expected TE Luke Musgrave (neck) to play at some point in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tucker-kra.analysis: Musgrave is coming back from a neck injury with no clear timeline for a return to action. The Packers last week signed Jonnu Smith, who will play behind Tucker Kraft to start the regular season. Smith could be an interesting waiver add if Kraft — returning from a major knee injury — misses any time in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.headline: Pierre Strong rushed 11 times for 28 yards in the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys, adding 39 yards on five receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.analysis: Strong’s 17 opportunities handily led the backfield on a night MarShawn Lloyd was in and out of the game due to an early injury scare. Even so, he managed only 2.8 yards per carry that was overshadowed by the looking return of lead back Josh Jacobs, the latter of whom is expected to be activated from the commissioner exempt list Monday. Strong, Lloyd, and Kaleb Johnson can safely be returned to the waiver wire from whence they came.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.headline: Pierre Strong rushed five times for seven yards in the Packers’ Week 5 win over the Bears, adding three receptions for 11 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.analysis: Making his Packers debut, 27-year-old journeyman Strong slid into Chris Brooks’ (ankle, injured reserve) vacated role. Although it’s a potential concern for MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson — any new face in this makeshift backfield would be — it appears to be a bigger issue for Johnson, as Strong was playing ahead of him until garbage time. Ominous for Johnson managers, though Strong has little shot at carving out 12-team league value of his own.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.headline: Packers released Pierre Strong.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.analysis: Strong was released right after it was reported that the team was acquiring Kaleb Johnson from the Steelers. He spent the 2025 season on the Packers’ practice squad and was elevated for two games. Strong will likely find work on another practice squad once rosters are settled.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.headline: Packers RB Chris Brooks took first-team reps to begin 11-on-11 drills at organized team activities on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.analysis: Brooks opened team drills as the Packers’ starting running back on Wednesday. Fellow backup RB Pierre Strong then subbed in, taking first-team reps as well. Starting RB Josh Jacobs was arrested on Tuesday for domestic abuse and was not present. Presumed RB MarShawn Lloyd practiced on Tuesday, but was limited to individual drills for an undisclosed reason on Wednesday. Injuries derailed Lloyd’s first two NFL seasons, so his absence is worth monitoring.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.headline: Packers RB MarShawn Lloyd (undisclosed) sat out during team drills at organized team activities on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.analysis: It’s possible this is just a maintenance-related coaching decision, but it is still slightly concerning. Injuries have limited Lloyd to just 10 offensive snaps through two NFL seasons. Packers starting RB Josh Jacobs was arrested on Tuesday and was not present on Wednesday, allowing the backups to take first-team snaps. Per ESPN’s Rob Demovsky, Lloyd “took part in team drills during Tuesday’s closed session but did only individual work Wednesday.” Packers RB Chris Brooks began team drills with the first-team offense before subbing out for RB Pierre Strong. The Packers had the day off on Thursday and will resume practicing tomorrow. The Packers “remain optimistic that the powerful and speedy Lloyd can repay the team for their patience,” but he needs to retake the field soon if he hopes to prove his reliability. Hopefully, Lloyd is back in action.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.headline: Releasing Josh Jacobs would result in a $6.25 million dead cap hit for the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.analysis: Jacobs this week was arrested in Wisconsin on domestic abuse chargers. The 28-year-old back was booked in jail for battery, criminal damage to property, disorderly conduct, strangulation and suffocation, and intimidation of a victim. Jacobs denies the allegations. If the Packers were to release Jacobs — who has two years and $25 million remaining on his current deal — they would absorb a doable $6.2 million hit to the salary cap for 2026. Jacobs could be facing team and/or league discipline in the coming months, and could miss part of the regular season if the NFL’s investigation into the domestic abuse allegations warrants a suspension. Other running backs on the Packers depth chart include Chris Brooks, MarShawn Lloyd, and Pierre Strong.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.headline: Packers signed K Lucas Havrisik, OT Brant Banks, DL Dante Barnett, OG Karsen Barnhart, DL Anthony Campbell, TE McCallan Castles, OT Dalton Cooper, TE Drake Dabney, DL James Ester, CB Tyron Herring, LB Jamon Johnson, RB Damien Martinez, S Mark Perry, WR Will Sheppard, RB Pierre Strong Jr. and TE Messiah Swinson to reserve/futures contracts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.analysis: Havrisik hit 4-of-4 field goals and 7-of-9 extra points this year, and the Packers seemed to be developing him as kicker of the future — whatever that means in the NFL — while letting him stay on the practice squad. With Brandon McManus’ job officially under scrutiny, it’s possible he eventually gets the Packers kicker gig.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.headline: Packers added RB Emanuel Wilson (illness) to the injury report Saturday with a questionable designation.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.analysis: The team elevated RB Pierre Strong from the practice squad in an associated move, which comes as both Josh Jacobs and Wilson are listed as questionable. Stay tuned ahead of the team’s inactives Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.headline: Packers K Brandon McManus (quad) is inactive for Week 7 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.analysis: Also inactive for the Packers are RB Pierre Strong Jr., G Donovan Jennings, T Anthony Belton, TE Ben Sims, DL Lukas Van Ness, and DL Devonte Wyatt. McManus will miss another game due to his quad issue, meaning Lucas Havrisik will kick for Green Bay against the Cardinals. Strong was elevated from the practice squad, but with Josh Jacobs (calf/illness) active, he is inactive this week. Meanwhile, Van Ness will miss this game due to a foot issue that kept him out of practice all week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.headline: Browns released RB Pierre Strong Jr.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pierre-str.analysis: This move is a bit surprising with Quinshon Judkins still unsigned. Perhaps that signing is just around the corner, or the team just feels good about Jerome Ford and Dylan Sampson. In two preseason games, Strong rushed 18 times for 18 yards and caught 5-of-6 targets for 28 yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Jake Ferguson caught 2-of-3 targets for 13 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 6 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: Ferguson has now been out-targeted by the team’s WR3, Ryan Flournoy, in five of six games, even being out-targeted by fellow tight end Brevyn Span-Ford in this one. The latter caught 4-of-5 targets for 35 yards on a night quarterback Dak Prescott attempted 54 passes. Any fleeting fantasy value is quickly evaporating as the fourth option, at best, through the air. Ferguson can safely be left on fantasy benches ahead of a Week 7 meeting with the Eagles on the road.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Jake Ferguson caught 3-of-6 targets for 19 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 5 loss to the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: Ferguson committed two uncharacteristic drops against the Buccaneers, the second of which resulted in a game-sealing interception to push the Cowboys to 2-3 ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Packers. Now held to 43 yards or fewer in five consecutive games, Ferguson is relegated to a touchdown-dependent TE2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Jake Ferguson caught 3-of-4 targets for 11 yards in Dallas’ Week 4 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: He was chipping a bunch against Texans’ EDGE tandem, so the line isn’t super surprising. He did manage a key fourth-down catch on Dallas’ go-ahead final drive of the game. He’ll look to regain his low-end TE1 juice next week against the Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Jake Ferguson caught 3-of-5 targets for 23 yards and a touchdown in Week 3’s loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: Ferguson continues to make the most of his limited targets. Despite seeing just nine targets in his last two games, the veteran tight end has turned three of those into scores. Ferguson hauled in a 19-yard touchdown catch from Dak Prescott in the third quarter against the Ravens, but was otherwise held to just four yards on his other four targets. The touchdowns are encouraging, but we will need to see more targets before we can elevate Ferguson into TE1 territory. He’ll be a boom-or-bust TE2 next week against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Jake Ferguson caught 4-of-4 targets for 43 yards and two touchdowns in the Cowboys’ Week 2 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: Ferguson connected with Dak Prescott for a 10-yard touchdown in the second quarter when he broke free in the secondary for an uncontested score. After a recovered fumble by the Cowboys in the third quarter,, he and Prescott would link up again for a 12-yard score to put the Cowboys up 27-13 in a game where their team never trailed. This was a far more encouraging outing for Ferguson, who posted a disappointing 2-6-0 line in Week 1 against the Giants. He’ll be on the TE2 radar in Week 3’s game against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Jake Ferguson caught both targets for six yards in the Cowboys’ Week 1 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: The Cowboys were dominated in both time of possession and total offense on a night the Giants converted 9-of-10 third downs, resulting in the poor showing in the box scores for the veteran tight end. Ferguson’s stark fantasy splits when both CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens are healthy remain a concern for fantasy managers that invested a middle-round pick in his services, something that a home matchup against a forgiving Commanders defense could remedy. Even so, Ferguson is nothing more than a middling TE2 in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Cowboys restructured TE Jake Ferguson’s contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: According to ESPN’s Todd Archer, the Cowboys now have $33.2 million in salary cap space this year. They also reworked DT Kenny Clark and CB DaRon Bland’s deals. Ferguson’s $7.25 million base salary was turned into a signing bonus. For fantasy purposes, this does not alter Ferguson’s standing. The front office could have a personnel move in mind, though. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Jake Ferguson caught 1-of-2 targets for five yards in the Cowboys’ Week 18 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: None of the Cowboys’ starters were asked to do much today, but Ferguson was targeted once in the red zone on a play that he dropped. He’ll end the season with 82 catches on 102 targets for 600 yards and eight touchdowns. The eight touchdowns and 82 catches were career-highs for Ferguson, and his 102 targets tied his career high. Ferguson came up big for Dallas when CeeDee Lamb was out with an injury and totaled six touchdowns in four weeks from Weeks 4-7. Ferguson just recently agreed to a contract extension with Dallas, so he’ll be back next season and could be a TE1 option in fantasy depending on what the Cowboys do with impending free agent George Pickens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Cowboys TE Jake Ferguson (calf) is not on Dallas’ final Week 18 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: Ferguson probably isn’t in line for major work in the finale as he has just 10 targets in his last three games, but the calf injury he tweaked in Week 17 won’t hold him out here. Ferguson would be a low-end TE1 if we could count on four quarters of Dak Prescott. Since we can’t, he’s probably in the TE2 range.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.headline: Cowboys TE Jake Ferguson (calf) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jake-fergu.analysis: Ferguson aggravated his old calf injury during his team’s Week 17 game and was unable to practice yesterday. He now has a chance to play in Week 18. Whether the Cowboys allow him to play is a separate issue. The 26-year-old tight end is under contract through 2029.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught 7-of-9 targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 6 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: While the yardage totals continue to remain modest for the third-year receiver, his emergence as a trusted WR3 in the offense has led to him out-targeting tight end Jake Ferguson in five of six games through the first third of the season. That’s a role that can return usable FLEX production in the right matchups in the typically high-powered Cowboys offense, adding to his high-end handcuff value. Fantasy managers can continue to stash FLournoy ahead of a Week 7 meeting with the division rival Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught 3-of-4 targets for 90 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 5 loss to the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: Flournoy continues to operate as the clear WR3 behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens, typically incapable of returning viable fantasy production in their shadows. He hit for a 48-yard reception at the end of the second quarter to set up a go-ahead field goal entering the break, otherwise remaining about as quiet as we would expect. This was the first game in 2026 over a modest 37 yards for Flournoy, who could be tasked with additional emphasis in the immediate future after Lamb departed with a quad injury in the fourth quarter. He could be worth a speculative add ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the reeling Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught 4-of-5 targets for 37 yards in Dallas’ Week 4 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: Flournoy has been held to exactly 22 or 23 yards in each of his first three games of the season, but the trend of Dallas passing more is pretty good for him. He’s got 21 targets over his last three games. It’s not anything beyond FLEX production yet but Thursday night games can be weird and that’s where Dallas will be next week against the Buccaneers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught 2-of-4 targets for 22 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 1 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: The veteran receiver inked a one-year contract extension this offseason to retain his supporting role in the high-powered Dallas offense, but the early returns were less than inspiring. Flournoy played 41 of 58 snaps, nearly every-down work, but the Cowboys just didn’t get enough play volume to let him spike a ceiling week. It’ll be hard for Flournoy to return consistent fantasy production for as long as both CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens remain healthy. He’ll be a boom-bust WR4 in a plus matchup against the Commanders in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Cowboys signed Ryan Flournoy to a one-year, $6 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: Flournoy is now under contract through the 2027 season. The 26-year-old receiver caught 40 passes for 475 yards and four touchdowns last season, while finishing third among Cowboys receivers in routes run (273) and fourth on the team in targets. It was reported earlier this summer that he was seeing more snaps in the slot, but it’s hard to imagine Flournoy making enough of an impact to be fantasy-relevant as long as CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, and Jake Ferguson are healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: ESPN’s Todd Archer reports Ryan Flournoy “has worked in the slot more” this offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: Archer mentioned Flournoy as the biggest surprise for the Cowboys so far this offseason. The third-year receiver totaled 40 catches for 475 yards and four touchdowns last season, and played 34.4 percent of his snaps in the slot. The Cowboys ran the fourth-most plays from 11 personnel last season, per TruMedia. While it’s possible that Flournoy’s increased slot role leads to more production, fantasy managers should take this with a grain of salt. As long as CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens, and Jake Ferguson are healthy, Flournoy will face an uphill climb to improve on the 3.8 targets per game he averaged last season. That said, if either Lamb or Pickens were to miss time, Flournoy could have some streaming upside in deeper leagues after he posted a few 100-plus yard games last season in games where either Pickens or Lamb were sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said he really thinks WR Ryan Flournoy “is taking the next step.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: Schottenheimer believes the 2024 sixth-round pick “has a chance to be a terrific receiver in this league.” He currently projects as the Cowboys’ WR3 and will likely carry that distinction into the regular season. Flournoy is a worthwhile best ball pick right now, but it remains to be seen whether he will warrant consideration in 12-team re-draft leagues late in August. Flournoy posted a 40/475/4 receiving line last season, while upping his yards per route run average from 1.06 to 174. It will be difficult for him to be anything more than a volatile WR5/WR6, but he will deliver a few spiked weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: The Athletic’s Jon Machota believes Ryan Flournoy will be Dallas’ No. 3 receiver in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: In other words, he expects Flournoy to confine KaVonate Turpin to a gadget role. Flournoy produced in his limited chances last year and, if a surprise George Pickens trade comes to fruition, could have real fantasy upside in 2026. As is, he’ll have WR5/WR6 appeal in what profiles as the third or fourth option (alongside tight end Jake Ferguson) in a good passing offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Ryan Flournoy caught 5-of-7 targets for 68 yards in a Week 18 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: With the Cowboys leaning heavily on their backups in this one, Flournoy led the team in targets and receiving yards. In fact, he was the only player who had more than three targets in this one. That will end a solid season for the 26-year-old, who had 40 catches on 56 targets for 475 yards and four touchdowns. He had a few big games for the Cowboys when CeeDee Lamb was forced to miss time with injuries and figures to be somebody the Cowboys look to retain this offseason. Flournoy will be a restricted free agent, so Dallas’ ability to hold onto him will depend on whether or not any other team falls in love with him in the offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.headline: Cowboys WR Ryan Flournoy (knee) is not on Dallas’ final Week 18 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ryan-flour.analysis: He’ll get some work in with Dak Prescott in the finale. Flournoy has showcased some big play ability and nearly had a two-touchdown game against the Chargers in December before leaving with an injury. He’s a potential WR4/WR5 play this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 9-of-18 targets for 70 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 6 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb was targeted relentlessly against the match-zone-based Green Bay defense but suffered through a failing connection with quarterback Dak Prescott on his way to middling fantasy returns. The Cowboys managed under 100 yards in the first half and were victimized by two Prescott interceptions deep in Green Bay territory, leading to a game environment that required 55 Prescott dropbacks. Even with a second consecutive middling-to-poor performance from a fantasy first round pick, Lamb is still pacing for a 1,500-yard, 11-touchdown season, plenty to provide a solid return on investment for fantasy managers that used their top pick on his services. Lamb could be busy again in Week 7 against the inside-funnel nature of the Philadelphia defense, where he will once again be a fantasy WR1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb (quad) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb played through a quad bruise last week but exacerbated the issue and left the game late in the fourth quarter. The injury is not believed to be serious and a full practice today means Lamb isn’t at risk of missing Week 6. Despite burning fantasy managers with two catches for nine yards last time around, Lamb remains one of the best fantasy football wideouts in play this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports CeeDee Lamb’s quad injury is not believed to be serious after Week 5’s loss to the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb was on the field for a few more plays in Thursday’s loss to the Buccaneers after his injury was announced. Rapoport reports that Lamb is believed to be dealing with a quad bruise, which is not believed to be serious. Lamb and the Cowboys now have over a week to rest up before facing the Packers on Sunday Night Football in Week 6. Barring an unexpected development, we would expect Lamb to be good to go for next week’s game against the Packers at Lambeau Field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: Cowboys WR CeeDee Lamb (quad) is questionable to return to Week 5 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb departed in the fourth quarter with a quad injury. He tried to return but managed one snap before making his way back to the sideline, coming back on the field later in the drive for a two-point attempt. He was shown on the sideline in visible discomfort following the additional two snaps. Lamb managed to catch just 2-of-5 targets for nine yards prior to departing. Fantasy managers will want to track his status in the coming week, although the additional recovery time could allow him to avoid any missed games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 17-of-21 targets for 189 yards and a touchdown in Dallas’ Week 3 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: He simply could not be stopped the way the Texans were playing defense. Lamb feasted on the sideline and against zone coverages — his longest catch went just 30 yards — and he had the go-ahead touchdown with less than 30 seconds left that had FOX’s Greg Olsen wondering why any defense would play him that way when he’d been that productive over the course of the game. He’d never managed more than 17 targets in a game before today. Obviously he won’t do this again, but Lamb has delivered for those who lucked into him in the late first-round mix and will again be a plug-and-play alpha WR1 against the Bucs on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 7-of-8 targets for 112 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 3 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: That makes it back-to-back games of 100-plus yards for Lamb. Lamb didn’t officially find the end zone on this one, but he did come up with a catch on a two-point reception in the third quarter to cut the Ravens’ lead to 24-21. He came up with a few big plays in the fourth quarter, with his biggest being a 49-yard reception on a drive that ended with a KaVontae Turpin rushing touchdown to briefly give the Cowboys the lead. Despite being out-targeted 11 to 8 by George Pickens in this one, Lamb has looked like the unquestioned WR1 for the Cowboys through the first three weeks. He’s totaled 15 receptions for 265 yards and two touchdowns over the last two weeks and is a high-end WR1 in next week’s game against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 8-of-9 targets for 153 yards and two touchdowns in the Cowboys’ Week 2 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Lamb caught three passes on the Cowboys’ opening drive, picking up gains of 15 and 23 yards before connecting with Dak Prescott on a three-yard score. Lamb gave the Commanders fits all day, but strung together another massive drive late in the fourth quarter when he hauled in a 35-yard pass from Prescott, who went right back to him five plays later for a 24-yard touchdown on a pass Lamb had to fight to come down with. Lamb has now scored in each of his first two games this season and will be firmly on the WR1 radar in next week’s game against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: CeeDee Lamb caught 5-of-8 targets for 44 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 1 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Although he lead the team in both targets and receiving, Lamb got off to a slow start while committing an early drop. He would score from one yard out in the second quarter after a Javonte Williams touchdown was ruled short of the goal line and also draw a defensive pass interference penalty in the second half that would lead to a Williams score, but the Cowboys simply had problems creating the chunk plays that ruled the roost in 2025. Better days are likely ahead for the perennial WR1, which starts in a Week 2 home showdown against another divisional opponent in the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: ESPN’s Ben Solak believes Dak Prescott could throw for 5,000 yards in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Solak’s prediction was among his bold predictions for the 2026 NFL season. Prescott having a shot at 5,000 yards, Solak said, would hinge on the Cowboys remaining a fast-paced offense in 2026. Last season the Cowboys led the league in play clock remaining at the snap and offensive plays per game, leading to 600 passes for Dak — a career high. The wideout duo of George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb won’t hurt matters for Prescott, who has eclipsed 4,500 passing yards three times in his NFL career. Pickens’ downfield ability was reflected in Prescott finishing sixth in deep ball accuracy last season. “The volume will be there for Prescott to not just lead the league in passing in 2026 but to once again challenge for the 5,000-yard milestone,” Solak said. Quarterbacks have thrown for more than 5,000 yards just 14 times in league history.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.headline: Cowboys will restructure contracts of QB Dak Prescott, WR CeeDee Lamb and OG Tyler Smith, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ceedee-lam.analysis: Restructuring the contracts of Prescott, Lamb and Smith will create $66 million in cap space. Schefter also passes along that Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said the Cowboys will rework the contracts of DTs Kenny Clark, Quinnen Williams and Osa Odighizuwa, who are scheduled to count around $63 million against the cap. With the new cap set at $301.2 million, the Cowboys had negative-$56.1 million in cap space. These moves help Dallas become compliant and have money to work with this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 11 times for 41 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 6 loss to the Packers, adding nine yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: Williams has now been held to 3.8 yards per carry or fewer in five of six games and 45 yards on the ground or fewer in four of six games, with seven combined touchdowns keeping his fantasy value afloat through the first third of the regular season. Furthermore, Williams has now seen 12 or fewer carries in four of six contests to start the year. The good news is that the Cowboys have no choice but to keep riding Williams until the wheels fall off considering the general lack of depth in the backfield, meaning there are likely to be better days ahead for the veteran back. He gets another middling matchup on the ground against the division rival Eagles in Week 7, where he will be a volume-driven RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 12 times for 45 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 5 loss to the Buccaneers, adding 17 yards on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: Williams has now averaged 3.8 yards per carry or fewer in four of five games, keeping his fantasy value afloat via six combined touchdowns through five weeks. While the touchdown equity is solid in one of the league’s most potent offenses, we’re liable to see more down weeks like the one he put forth against the Buccaneers unless, or until, the Cowboys can fix their woes on the ground. Williams did see all but one running back opportunity in this one, keeping him in the top six in backfield opportunity rate through Week 5. Consider Williams a volume-aided and touchdown-aided RB2 ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the reeling Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 19 times for 62 yards and three touchdowns in the Cowboys’ Week 4 win over the Texans, adding five catches for 21 yards on his only five targets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: Williams had a very easy rushing score — his first one where he only had to beat one defender to the outside after a pair of pulls. He also had a very hard one, where he dragged several Texans defenders into the red zone. The Cowboys didn’t run the ball much, but when they did it was effective. Williams was averaging 5.1 yards per tote before the second half, where he simply lived in the goal-to-go set. He’ll be on the low-end RB1 line in Week 5 against a Jalon Daniels-led Bucs outfit on Thursday night.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 19 times for 98 yards and one touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 3 loss to the Ravens, adding two receptions for five yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: The Cowboys drew up a lot of carries for Williams early in this one. The 26-year-old back totaled seven carries for 45 yards on his team’s first two possessions, and punched in a two-yard score late in the fourth quarter to put the Cowboys up 10-0. Williams would mostly be bottled up by the Ravens after his score, but he did break free for a 22-yard run in the third quarter that helped set up a Brandon Aubrey field goal — which was blocked. This is undoubtedly the best game of the season for Williams, who hadn’t gone for more than 41 yards in either of his first two games. That said, he still struggled at times to get going on the ground, as seven of his carries went for two or fewer yards. His volume remains reliable enough to keep him in the RB2 conversation for next week’s game against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 12 times for 30 yards in the Cowboys’ Week 2 win over the Commanders, adding three receptions for 20 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: The Cowboys dominated through the air on Sunday, but the same can’t be said of their efforts on the ground. Washington bottled up Williams all afternoon, with his biggest play coming on a nine-yard run on the Cowboys’ final drive. Williams has just 71 rushing yards on 24 attempts (3.0 YPC), but has also seen nine targets in his first two games. He remains the unquestioned leader of the Cowboys’ backfield and will be a volume-based RB2 in next week’s game against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Javonte Williams rushed 12 times for 41 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys’ Week 1 loss to the Giants, adding five receptions for 31 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: Williams understandably operated as a clear workhorse for a Cowboys team with little depth at the position following Malik Davis’ season-ending injury earlier in the week. His two second half scores and five receptions masked poor rushing efficiency on a night the Cowboys ran only 52 offensive plays, although a robust 32.7 percent total opportunity share foreshadows the potential for continued elite counting stats for the remainder of the regular season. Fantasy managers can continue to start Williams as a volume-driven RB1 as the team prepares to host the Commanders in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said RB Jaydon Blue and RB Phil Mafah “are going to get a bunch of work” in the preseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: Per Schottenheimer, Blue and Mafah “are in a tight battle for the backup running back spot.” Blue has received positive reports for some time now. His speed and receiving ability make him an ideal complement to starting RB Javonte Williams, who “probably won’t get a whole lot of run” in the preseason. If Blue can secure the role, he could warrant FLEX treatment on a weekly basis. Mafah (6'/234) is a burly rusher. Were he to win the RB2 job, he may be ill-suited to playing on passing downs, which could benefit Williams. We’ll see how things shake out in the preseason. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: The Athletic’s Jon Machota believes Jaydon Blue is “the ideal fit” to be a complementary option to Javonte Williams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: Machota noted Blue’s pass-catching ability as the biggest reason for him to potentially see some work behind Williams. Blue caught 42 passes for 368 yards and six scores during his final season at Texas. He then flopped as a rookie, seeing just one catch and 38 carries in total. The bulk of his opportunities came in a meaningless Week 18 game. Still, Dallas did nothing to address their backfield depth this offseason and head coach Brian Schottenheimer has talked up Blue’s work ethic this time around. With a strong training camp, Blue could cement himself as a change-of-pace option for the Cowboys, putting him on the menu for fantasy drafters in deeper leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said the team recently held RB Javonte Williams out of team drills to give RB Jaydon Blue and RB Phil Mafah more work.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: Reporters noticed Williams was not participating in organized team activities last week. The Cowboys hosted their three-day mandatory minicamp this week, and it sounds like Williams was either limited or held out again today. Schottenheimer was asked whether this was due to Williams’ shoulder injury from last season or simply veteran maintenance. Fortunately, Schottenheimer said Williams is “in a great spot” and “looks great.” His absence was “more about getting the young guys some reps in this last full-speed practice.” It seems like the Cowboys are hoping that one of Blue or Mafah can step up and be a reliable backup. If one separates from the other, he will be a worthwhile late-round pick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.headline: Cowboys RB Javonte Williams (undisclosed) was not present at organized team activities on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/javonte-wi.analysis: ESPN’s Todd Archer advises that readers not to get carried away with any of today’s observations. It’s a reasonable preface. There is no reason to think Williams’ absence is concerning. The Cowboys are still conducting voluntary workouts, so he is not compelled to be there. Mandatory minicamp is scheduled for June 16-18. Archer adds that RBs Phil Mafah, Jaydon Blue and Malik Davis split first-team reps, with Mafah notably taking the first snap.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: Dak Prescott completed 34-of-54 passes for 258 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the Cowboys’ 23-13, Week 6 loss to the Packers, adding seven yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: Prescott and the Cowboys were completely unable to get anything going prior to the half, managing just 92 yards of total offense while taking a 17-point deficit into the break. They would force a three-and-out to start the third quarter and follow it up with a touchdown drive to get on the board, but a punt and two turnovers on downs left them trailing by 16 until a late score inside of two minutes remaining in the final frame. Prescott’s two interceptions occurred deep in Green Bay territory in the second quarter, removing much needed points from the scoreboard in what was then a tight game. The loss drops the Cowboys to 2-4 and looking up at the Giants for the division lead through a third of the regular season. Prescott will be a back-end QB1 on the road against the division rival Eagles in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: Dak Prescott completed 24-of-42 passes for 316 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions in the Cowboys’ 24-16, Week 5 loss to the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: The two interceptions on Dak’s ledger were both in-and-out of his receivers’ hands, the second of which hit tight end Jake Ferguson in the face mask to allow the Buccaneers to ice the game in the fourth quarter. The first “pick” bounced off the hands of Ryan Flournoy to allow the Buccaneers to establish an 11-point lead at the beginning of the third quarter, a deficit the Cowboys would be unable to overcome. That said, Prescott wasn’t at all at his sharpest, missing numerous throws wide in addition to a few badly under-thrown balls in the second half. To make matters worse, alpha wide receiver CeeDee Lamb departed the game in the fourth quarter with a quad injury. The Cowboys fall to 2-3 and find themselves looking up at both the Giants and Eagles ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Packers at Lambeau. Prescott returns to QB1 status in what has become a soft matchup, pending the health of Lamb.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: Dak Prescott completed 32-of-45 passes for 335 yards and one touchdown in the Cowboys’ 34-30, Week 4 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: He had just 87 passing yards at halftime, but the Cowboys turned up in a major way in the second half by peppering CeeDee Lamb with targets and getting George Pickens matched on Kamari Lassiter to their benefit. Prescott was surgical against the blitz and led a game-winning drive after C.J. Stroud briefly put the Texans up 30-27, leading the Cowboys 74 yards in 1:43 by brutalizing the Texans’ zone coverage. Dak should remain in the QB1 ranks next week against the woeful Buccaneers on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: Dak Prescott completed 25-of-40 passes for 276 yards and one touchdown in the Cowboys’ 34-31, Week 3 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: Dak and the Cowboys came out with a run-heavy approach early, but Prescott was efficient through the air when given the chance. He was able to get both CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens involved in this one, with the two receivers combining for 14 receptions for 194 yards on the day. Prescott’s lone touchdown pass came on a 19-yard strike to Jake Ferguson in the third quarter to cut the Ravens’ lead to 24-21, but on the Cowboys’ final drive in the fourth quarter, he would go 3-of-6 passing for 36 yards while adding another nine yards on the ground to help set up a game-tying field goal by Brandon Aubrey. A literal last-second field goal moments later would give the Ravens the win, but Prescott and the Cowboys have now gone for 30-plus points in back-to-back weeks. He’ll be a fringe QB1/QB2 in next week’s game against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: Dak Prescott completed 26-of-31 passes for 279 yards and four touchdowns in the Cowboys’ 37-20, Week 2 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: Dak and the Cowboys faced little resistance from the Commanders’ defense in this one. The Cowboys came out firing from the start, as Prescott orchestrated a 10-play, 66-yard opening drive that ended with a three-yard touchdown pass to CeeDee Lamb, who had three receptions on the drive. Prescott threw his second touchdown of the game to Jake Ferguson, who broke free in the end zone for a 10-yard score, and in the third quarter, the two connected again for a 12-yard score. Dak found Lamb for a 24-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter to set the Cowboys’ franchise record for career touchdown passes (249), putting the finishing touches on what was an impressive day. Prescott will be a fringe QB1/QB2 in next week’s game against the Ravens in Rio De Janeiro.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: Dak Prescott completed 22-of-34 passes for 175 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Cowboys’ 28-20, Week 1 loss to the Giants, adding 14 yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: A first half in which Prescott was victimized by drops and penalties from his supporting cast was completely overshadowed by a defensive performance that saw the Giants go 9-of-10 on third down and amass 394 yards of total offense. The Cowboys saw the ball only twice in the second half, scoring touchdowns on both drives, but it was ultimately not enough as they fell to 0-1 for the second consecutive season. Prescott’s lone interception came on a prayer ball down the sideline on third down at the end of the first half, eventually leading to a go-ahead touchdown for the Giants as they took a 14-7 deficit into the break, one they would not overcome. The Cowboys now turn the page to Week 2 as they prepare to host another division opponent in the Commanders in what has quickly become a near must-win game for both teams. Prescott will look to return to the QB1 ranks in a plus matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: ESPN’s Todd Archer reports that the Cowboys “had high interest” in former Texas Tech QB Brendan Sorsby when he shared plans to enter the NFL Supplemental Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: Archer cites multiple sources on this one. Sorsby’s gambling issues were reportedly not enough to dissuade the Cowboys from considering him as a potential long-term replacement for QB Dak Prescott, who turns 33 next week and is signed through 2028. In the end, the NFL declined to hold a supplemental draft this year, preventing the Cowboys from potentially drafting him at “a lower-than-expected price.” Perhaps they will revisit the idea next offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: ESPN’s Ben Solak believes Dak Prescott could throw for 5,000 yards in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: Solak’s prediction was among his bold predictions for the 2026 NFL season. Prescott having a shot at 5,000 yards, Solak said, would hinge on the Cowboys remaining a fast-paced offense in 2026. Last season the Cowboys led the league in play clock remaining at the snap and offensive plays per game, leading to 600 passes for Dak — a career high. The wideout duo of George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb won’t hurt matters for Prescott, who has eclipsed 4,500 passing yards three times in his NFL career. Pickens’ downfield ability was reflected in Prescott finishing sixth in deep ball accuracy last season. “The volume will be there for Prescott to not just lead the league in passing in 2026 but to once again challenge for the 5,000-yard milestone,” Solak said. Quarterbacks have thrown for more than 5,000 yards just 14 times in league history.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said Dak Prescott will be limited in team drills because of a sore knee.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: Schottenheimer said it’s “nothing to be concerned about.” We mostly agree, but every once in a while these situations become more serious or linger for a bit. Prescott figures to be a top-15 fantasy quarterback this year, though he won’t quite have the game scripts he had last year if Dallas’ defense can improve from “abysmal” to “regular bad” unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.headline: The Cowboys will host the Eagles for their annual Thanksgiving afternoon game this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dak-presco.analysis: The Cowboys will play host to their division rival, the Eagles, in front of a national audience this Thanksgiving. The Cowboys downed the Kansas City Chiefs in a high-scoring 31-28 affair last season, and have won their last four Thanksgiving Day contests. The league has now announced two Cowboys games ahead of its full schedule release, as they are also set to take on the Giants on Sunday Night Football in Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed nine times for 42 yards in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals, adding two receptions, 18 yards and one touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum got the Rams’ second drive all to himself before re-entering the game on the fourth drive and splitting reps with Kyren Williams thereafter. Rams coach Sean McVay seemingly rewarded Corum for powering through contact on a third-down conversion from the Cardinals’ 19-yard line by allowing him to remain on the field for the scoring-position sequence. Two plays later, Corum was scampering upfield for a 15-yard receiving score after hauling in a pass in the flats. He ran hard the rest of the way, but the Rams got off just 20 rushing attempts today, surprisingly playing in a trailing game script for the entire second half, as the Cardinals achieved victory via voluminous field goals. Corum is an RB3/FLEX against the Raiders next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed five times for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 5 loss to the Bills, adding 53 yards on three receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum provided a much needed spark in relief of lead back Kyren Williams, contributing three clutch receptions that kept drives alive in addition to a third quarter touchdown. That said, his modest volume continued while Williams turned in a third straight game with 20 or more opportunities, including 28 total targets in that stretch. Corum remains a top fantasy handcuff but is unlikely to return useful fantasy weeks for as long as Williams is healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed five times for 14 yards in the Rams’ Week 4 win over the Eagles, adding a seven-yard reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum was employed as a pure breather back this afternoon, as he got out-touched 26-6 by Kyren Williams. Four of Corum’s handles came on one first quarter series. With the 1-2 Rams staring down the barrel of 1-3 as they trailed by two scores for several quarters, they circled the wagons around their most established players, and that does not yet include Corum. The third-year pro will undoubtedly pop up for more 10-12 carry afternoons, but he’s fading from FLEX relevance as Williams gets re-established in the low-end RB1 mix.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes the Rams need more from Blake Corum in the coming weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Atkins believes Puka Nacua’s (groin) impending return will lighten the box, in turn making life easier on the run game and preventing the opposition from blitzing as frequently as the Broncos did last week. Corum has not established himself as a reliable weekly contributor in fantasy. Perhaps positive impacts from Nacua’s return trickle down to the Rams’ No. 2 running back. Kyren Williams remains a locked-in starter. Keep Corum stashed for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 15 times for 88 yards in the Rams’ Week 3 loss to the Broncos, adding 70 yards on six receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Williams’ 70 yards through the air were a career-high mark in receiving for a single game, returning yet another RB1 fantasy performance despite sharing backfield work with Blake Corum. Corum managed only 15 yards on six carries and caught two passes for zero additional yards. Furthermore, Corum has still not seen a carry inside the red zone through three games of the 2026 season. Williams remains a surefire RB1 ahead of a difficult matchup against the Eagles in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed 12 times for 79 yards in the Rams’ Week 2 win over the Giants, adding 13 yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum was kept out of the end zone for the second straight game to open the 2026 season but continues to display elite per-touch efficiency. The scoring woes could persist considering the robust red zone role of cohort Kyren Williams, the latter of whom found pay dirt for the second consecutive game to open the season. Corum continues to be a difficult weekly start outside of deeper leagues for as long as he is taken off the field where it matters most to fantasy production, and will remain a borderline FLEX start when the Rams face the Broncos in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Blake Corum rushed 10 times for 54 yards in the Rams’ Week 1 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum was unable to find the end zone while Kyren Williams did, but Corum was the more efficient tailback between the 20s with Williams only tallying 41 yards. He was also a non-factor in the passing game, but the Rams were basically a non-factor in the passing game with Matthew Stafford struggling to figure out the 49ers’ defense. Corum could see more touches in Week 2 against the Giants, but there’s no guarantee.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Kyren Williams believes Blake Corum is “a lot leaner” heading into 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: “I would say he’s a lot leaner for sure, he looks a lot more explosive,” was Williams’ exact quote. The Rams’ in-house reporters claim “that explosiveness has been on display all camp.” A disappointing 2024 rookie, Corum successfully earned a 1B role as a sophomore and is pushing for more. It’s still difficult to believe he could crack the top 24 at running back in fantasy, but it is possible he continues to cut into Williams’ top-18 value. Williams and Corum’s workload split will be one of September’s most intriguing early-season storylines.

https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: Rams HC Sean McVay said Blake Corum will “be a big factor” in the offense this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Corum took a nice leap in his second season as a pro, posting a 145-746-6 rushing line over 17 games while competing with Kyren Williams for touches every step of the way. Like Corum, Williams was also healthy for 17 games, but that didn’t stop Corum from popping up for a few top-24 PPR finishes last season. Corum’s 9.4 opportunities per game weren’t enough to make him a reliable option in start/sit leagues, as he managed only one double-digit PPR performance from Weeks 1-12, but his production could pave the way for a more even split with Williams this season. It may take some time to determine whether or not we can view Corum as a player who has standalone value this season, but he remains one of the best handcuffs in fantasy playing in an elite offense that could feature him in a high-volume role should Williams ever miss time.
