https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes Rams RB Blake Corum “could push for his first 1,000-yard rushing season this year.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/blake-corum/00.analysis: Back on May 1st, Atkins predicted Rams coach Sean McVay would deploy starting RB Kyren Williams and Corum in a 50-50 split, with Williams operating as the “primary third-down back and between-the-tackles runner,” while Corum functions as “a change-of-pace option with explosive capabilities.” With spring workouts complete, Atkins is doubling down with minor clarifications. Corum has made strides as a pass protector and receiver, and could “earn more playing time in an offense that wants to blur the run and the pass,” but Williams still remains the superior passing game player and should out-snap Corum because of this. Williams’ “consistency and short-yardage skills” could also keep him on the field in goal-line situations. Williams posted a 259/1,252/10 rushing line while Corum went for 145/746/6. Atkins thinks the two backs could split carries almost 50-50, which would seemingly make a 1,000-yard season doable for Corum. However, Corum’s ceiling outcome is limited if Williams indeed remains the primary player on passing downs and in goal-line situations.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 10 times for 50 yards in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals, adding three receptions for 17 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Williams played for the duration of the first and third drives, ceding the second to Blake Corum, who played well right out of the gate. The duo rotated during drives thereafter. Williams looked like his normal, capable self, showcasing a slick spin move off contact on the Rams’ fourth drive. Unfortunately for him, Corum fought hard to convert a first down just inside the red zone and coach Sean McVay kept him out there for the scoring-position sequence, which ended in a 15-yard receiving score for Corum. Williams quietly continued his high-end receiving involvement, earning six targets against the Cardinals today. Williams belongs in the RB1 tier next week against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 16 times for 49 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 5 loss to the Bills, adding 27 yards on six receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Williams has yet to see more than the 16 carries he saw against the Bills this season but the team’s recent pass-heavy nature has left the veteran lead back with six or more receptions in three straight games, including 27 total targets in that span. The elite-level aerial volume made it three consecutive games with 20 or more opportunities for Williams, who continues to return RB1 fantasy weeks while playing in one of the league’s top offenses. Williams remains a middling RB1 ahead of a Week 6 divisional showdown against the Cardinals at home.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 16 times for 80 yards in the Rams’ Week 4 win over the Eagles, adding 10 receptions for 66 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Williams’ 10 receptions were a new career high, while his 26 touches were tied for his seventh most. This, as Blake Corum handled the ball only six times. With Matthew Stafford having trouble against a stout Eagles defense in the rain, he focused on Williams checkdowns, and the strategy actually paid off as the Rams erased a 20-10 halftime deficit. Williams now has 47 touches over the past two weeks after that number was 28 for Weeks 1 and 2. With the Rams off to a shaky start, it’s not surprising they’ve started concentrating touches on their most established weapons. Corum is going to hang around as a nuisance, but Williams has returned himself to the low-end RB1 mix ahead of a likely Week 5 shootout with the Bills.

Kyren Williams remains a locked-in starter. Keep Corum stashed for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 12 times for 85 yards in the Rams’ Week 2 win over the Giants, adding 12 yards and a touchdown on two receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Williams has opened the season with touchdowns in consecutive games after hitting pay dirt 15 times or more the previous two seasons. The difference this season is that he’s doing it while Blake Corum has been much more involved in the weekly game plan. Williams continues forward with an elevated weekly floor due to his robust red zone role, albeit with a shakier ceiling than in recent years due to the presence of Corum. He remains a back-end RB2 when the Rams travel to Colorado to face the Bronco in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.headline: Kyren Williams rushed 11 times for 41 yards with a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 1 loss to the 49ers while adding three catches for 24 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Williams’ day was salvaged with a short-yardage score. He finished with one more rushing attempt than Blake Corum, but Corum did look spryer with 54 yards on those attempts. The Rams’ offense just didn’t have it in the Australian showdown, and Williams should see a better box score in Week 2 against the Giants; even if Corum remains a fantasy adversary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyren-will.analysis: Atkins still expects Williams to be the starter. Playing on third down and in the two-minute drill gives running backs an edge in PPR formats. Atkins did not specify which back will play in the latter scenario, but we imagine Williams will get the first crack at the gig. If Williams is also set to be the interior runner, it likely means he gets the first chance in the red zone. He out-snapped No. 2 RB Blake Corum in the red zone, 26-6, during the playoffs last year. That said, losing touches to the point of a 50-50 split hurts his upside.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Tyler Higbee caught 4-of-4 targets for 22 yards and one lost fumble in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Higbee was simply outplayed by fellow TE Colby Parkinson in this one. Higbee also had the ball ripped from his possession by LB Cody Simon while trying to fall forward for extra yards on the Rams’ seventh drive, further reducing his fantasy output. With Parkinson playing well, Higbee is a shakier, low-end TE1 against the Raiders next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Davis Allen (foot) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Allen remains out, and Parkinson (shoulder) remains limited. Tyler Higbee has played productively in the Rams’ No. 1 tight end role, and he should be expected to do so again this week against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Tyler Higbee caught 5-of-6 targets for 83 yards in the Rams’ Week 5 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Higbee continued to operate as the primary pass-catching tight end against the Bills, something that must please fantasy managers considering Colby Parkinson returned from a one-game absence. Furthermore, the team carried only three tight ends on the active game-day roster after being at either four or five through the first month of the 2026 season. Higbee is a middling TE2 in fantasy circles ahead of a juicy matchup against the divisional rival Cardinals in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Colby Parkinson (knee/shoulder) practiced in full on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Parkinson is unlikely to be startable as a TE1 if he plays on Monday night, but his return will likely reduce Tyler Higbee’s snap share. Higbee has been TE1-viable in each of the last two weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Colby Parkinson (shoulder) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Parkinson has a chance to return for the Rams’ Monday Night Football game against the Bills. If this is the case, he would hurt Tyler Higbee’s snap share, threatening the latter’s TE1 viability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Tyler Higbee caught 5-of-6 targets for 67 yards in the Rams’ Week 4 victory over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: One of only two healthy Rams tight ends, Higbee was the Rams’ clear-cut No. 3 passing-game weapon behind a returning Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. There’s a huge gulf between the Rams’ wideouts and Higbee, but he should be able to provide TE2 streamer value for the next several weeks, including Week 5 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Rams HC Sean McVay said TE Terrance Ferguson (ankle) will likely miss Week 4 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Ferguson briefly departed after injuring his ankle in the team’s Sunday Night Football loss to the Broncos, returning for two snaps prior to departing again after his lone reception of the evening. The ankle injury now appears likely to cost the talented young tight end at least one game, with the potential for the absence to linger if the sprain is “more high than low.” McVay also relayed that fellow tight end Colby Parkinson suffered an AC sprain and is considered day-to-day. Veteran Tyler Higbee would be in line to operate as the primary receiving tight end after amassing 62 yards and a touchdown on eight receptions in Week 3, should both miss. Higbee should be added in all formats as a potential TE1 in the immediate future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Tyler Higbee caught 8-of-11 targets for 62 yards and a touchdown in the Rams’ Week 3 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Higbee’s first quarter touchdown got the scoring started for the Rams, but it wasn’t until Terrance Ferguson departed with an ankle injury that his volume truly took off. From that point forward, Higbee was one of the primary options through the air, finishing two targets behind Davante Adams for the team lead. Fantasy managers will want to monitor Ferguson’s status closely in the coming week as Higbee could become a legitimate waiver target should Ferguson miss time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: Tyler Higbee caught both of his targets for 12 yards in the Rams’ Week 1 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Higbee ended up leading the Rams’ tight ends in targets and receptions, as Davis Allen had just one catch before exiting with a head injury, and Terrance Ferguson didn’t catch his only opportunity. Ferguson still seems like the tight end to roster going forward, but one could argue Higbee has the higher floor because he’ll see more snaps because of his blocking ability. That’s not a ringing endorsement, if it’s not obvious. The Rams will try and get it going against the Giants in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes Terrance Ferguson “has some of the best breakout potential of current Rams players who haven’t done so yet.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tyler-higb.analysis: Atkins added, “The ideal outcome for him is to lead their tight ends in catches and yards.” He noted that the coaching staff was focused on bringing Ferguson along incrementally in 2025. Now they will have the chance to move him into a more prominent role for his second season. Ferguson only caught 11 passes as a rookie, but he parlayed a seam-stretching role into 231 yards and three scores despite the low reception total. Atkins sees Ferguson as a de facto No. 3 receiver for the team, with Colby Parkinson and Tyler Higbee both fulfilling the role of a traditional inline tight end. Rookie Max Klare will also be in the mix for snaps, but will likely be brought along slowly as well. With an ADP that barely even registers in early best ball drafts, Ferguson is worth a look as a high-upside TE3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson caught 5-of-6 targets for 31 yards and one touchdown in the Rams’ Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson played effectively against the Cardinals’ zone coverage this afternoon. He bagged a first down after finding a soft spot downfield on the Rams’ fourth drive, and deftly hurdled a defender on a one-yard gain a few plays later. His touchdown occurred on the Rams’ final possession and required post-catch effort, barreling through contact and extending for the score. Parkinson is a touchdown-dependent TE2 against the Raiders in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Davis Allen (foot) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: He got in a limited session and the Rams apparently trust him to play despite a pair of missed practices on Wednesday and Thursday. Colby Parkinson (shoulder) also avoided the final report. Tyler Higbee is the Rams tight end you should be using at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Davis Allen (foot) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Allen remains out, and Parkinson (shoulder) remains limited. Tyler Higbee has played productively in the Rams’ No. 1 tight end role, and he should be expected to do so again this week against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Davis Allen (foot) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Allen is dealing with a foot injury and is listed as a DNP on the Rams’ estimated practice report. Fellow tight end Colby Parkinson (shoulder) was listed as limited, though he has been dealing with the shoulder injury for a few weeks now and the Rams are likely managing his workload. Parkinson is trending to play. Allen’s potential absence may lead to the Rams activating rookie Max Klare to play alongside Parkinson and fantasy streaming option Tyler Higbee in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (knee/shoulder) practiced in full on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson is unlikely to be startable as a TE1 if he plays on Monday night, but his return will likely reduce Tyler Higbee’s snap share. Higbee has been TE1-viable in each of the last two weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (shoulder) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson has a chance to return for the Rams’ Monday Night Football game against the Bills. If this is the case, he would hurt Tyler Higbee’s snap share, threatening the latter’s TE1 viability.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Rams declared TE Colby Parkinson, WR CJ Daniels, QB Ty Simpson, CB Jaylen Watson, DT Aaron Donald, OL Bill Murray and CB Cam Lampkin inactive for Week 4 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson’s absence with knee and shoulder issues at least comes as Puka Nacua returns, though the Rams are somehow down to only two healthy tight ends. Parkinson appears to be genuinely day to day, so we would assume he has a decent chance of returning for Week 5 against the Bills. Improbably, the Rams’ injury issues have made Tyler Higbee a legitimate streaming option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Colby Parkinson (knee/shoulder) is questionable for Los Angeles’ Week 4 game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: He didn’t practice at any point this week with an AC sprain suffered after he had already been questionable with the knee ailment heading into Week 3. Tyler Higbee should be a reasonable TE2 option against the Eagles this week even if Parkinson is healthy; it doesn’t seem like he is.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Rams HC Sean McVay said TE Terrance Ferguson (ankle) will likely miss Week 4 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Ferguson briefly departed after injuring his ankle in the team’s Sunday Night Football loss to the Broncos, returning for two snaps prior to departing again after his lone reception of the evening. The ankle injury now appears likely to cost the talented young tight end at least one game, with the potential for the absence to linger if the sprain is “more high than low.” McVay also relayed that fellow tight end Colby Parkinson suffered an AC sprain and is considered day-to-day. Veteran Tyler Higbee would be in line to operate as the primary receiving tight end after amassing 62 yards and a touchdown on eight receptions in Week 3, should both miss. Higbee should be added in all formats as a potential TE1 in the immediate future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay said Colby Parkinson (knee) is “trending in the right direction” for Week 3 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/colby-park.analysis: Parkinson did not practice once this week because of the knee issue, so it’s a bit of a surprise that McVay sounds optimistic about him suiting up today. The team may have kept him out of practice as a precaution. He will handle an inline tight end role while Terrance Ferguson handles de facto WR2 duties with Puka Nacua out. Ferguson remains in the TE1 mix while Parkinson is a touchdown-or-bust TE2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught 1-of-3 targets for four yards in the Ravens’ Week 6 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews ran 11 more routes than rookie tight end Josh Cuevas but was out-targeted by Cuevas 5-to-3. Andrews continues to underwhelm in the passing game and has now failed to surpass 28 yards in four straight games. He can be left on waivers ahead of Week 7’s game against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught 4-of-6 targets for 28 yards in the Ravens’ Week 5 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews dropped a would-be touchdown on the team’s opening possession on a ball that went through his hands in the end zone. He would then fumble on the following possession, which Jessie Bates returned for a touchdown to force the Ravens into catch-up mode for the remainder of the game. Luckily for him, late heroics from Tyler Huntley and Derrick Henry had the team escaping with a victory. Andrews has not looked great to start the 2026 season, having not eclipsed 50 yards through five games. He’ll remain a shaky fantasy start in Week 6 when the Ravens host the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews (hand) is practicing in full for Week 5 against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews practiced in full with the hand injury last week before posting a 5/27/1 receiving line. He should be good to go again this week, though he is a low-end TE1, with backup QB Tyler Huntley likely starting in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught 5-of-6 targets for 27 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 4 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews continues to see most of his work come in the short area of the field. He’s gone for less than 30 yards in each of his last two games, but did manage to haul in a three-yard score in the second quarter of Sunday’s win for his first touchdown of 2026. Lamar Jackson also missed Andrews in the end zone on a high throw earlier in the game, but he remains a very touchdown-dependent option as far as fantasy is concerned. He’s a boom-or-bust play in Week 5 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews (hand) is practicing in full for Week 4 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: The Ravens seemingly forgot about Andrews when they first posted their injury report, only noting his injury and status in a post 40 minutes after the initial run. In their defense, Andrews has been pretty forgettable this year, catching 13 passes for 122 scoreless yards. The hand injury shouldn’t be an issue this week, but he’s still stuck in the TE2 ranks versus Tennessee.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught 3-of-5 targets for 24 yards the Ravens’ Week 3 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews missed part of this game with a hand injury but returned to catch two passes for a total of 15 yards in the second half. Andrews has yet to find the end zone this season and hasn’t gone for more than 49 yards in a game. There’s not much for fantasy managers to rely on here heading into next week’s game against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews (hand) returned in the third quarter of Week 3’s game against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews returned to the field midway through the quarter. He saw three targets before leaving the game in the first half, but it seems unlikely he will see many more targets at this point. The Ravens have attempted just 11 passes through nearly three full quarters of play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews (hand) is questionable to return in Week 3 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: We’re not quite sure what happened here, but Andrews was not on the field for the Ravens’ fifth drive of the game, with the team announcing soon after that he would be questionable to return. The veteran tight end caught 1-of-3 targets for nine yards before exiting.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Mark Andrews caught 6-of-7 yargets for 49 yards in the Ravens’ Week 2 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Andrews was targeted four times on the Ravens’ first four possessions, with his biggest play coming on a 10-yard reception to start a drive that ended with a Derrick Henry touchdown. Andrews caught a 14-yard reception on the Ravens’ final drive of the game as they tried to mount a comeback, but the drive ended on an interception by Lamar Jackson three plays later. Andrews has caught 10 passes for 98 scoreless yards on 13 targets through his first two games. It’s decent production for a tight end, but he continues to look like a shell of the player he once was. He’ll be a boom-or-bust TE2 in Week 3 against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.headline: Ravens WR Zay Flowers (hamstring) is doubtful to play in Week 2 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mark-andre.analysis: Flowers entered the season at the tail end of a rehab program for the hamstring strain he suffered on August 31st. He logged two full practice sessions before dominating the Colts early on in Week 1. Unfortunately, Flowers balled too hard, aggravating the hamstring injury in the process. He is unlikely to play this week, but his return to practice today is a great sign for his Week 3 availability. The Ravens placed WR Ja’Kobi Lane (wrist) on injured reserve this week. This means WRs Rashod Bateman, Elijah Sarratt and Devontez Walker could be asked to step up, although TE Mark Andrews will probably serve as the team’s top pass-catching option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaleel-mcl.headline: Jaleel McLaughlin rushed nine times for 41 yards in the Browns’ Week 6 win over the Ravens, adding four receptions for 14 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaleel-mcl.analysis: McLaughlin operated as the Browns’ lead back with Quinshon Judkins and Dylan Sampson both sidelined. The 26-year-old back saw six of his carries go for four or more yards, and he was the only Browns running back to see a target. If either Judkins or Sampson are able to return in Week 7 against the Titans, McLaughlin will likely return to his role as a lightly used backup. If Judkins were to miss another game, McLaughlin could be in line for double digit touches, but he would be a risky bet as far as fantasy is concerned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaleel-mcl.headline: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaleel-mcl.analysis: Judkins suffered a potentially serious ankle injury in Week 5 and could miss Week 6 against the Ravens if he’s unable to practice in the next couple days. That could leave Jaleel McLaughlin as the Browns’ lead back against Baltimore. Dylan Sampson (knee) could also suit up if he’s able to practice after a four-week stint on IR.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaleel-mcl.headline: Browns head coach Todd Monken said Quinshon Judkins is considered day-to-day with an ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaleel-mcl.analysis: Monken was spotted in a walking boot after Sunday’s loss to the Jets, but Monken said his RB1 will have a chance to play in Week 6 against the Ravens. Judkins rushed 14 times for 44 yards last week and has a rushing line of 73-221-1 for the season, along with 18 receptions for 102 additional yards. Judkins’ practice status will be one to monitor throughout the week. If he’s not able to play, Raheim Sanders would likely handle the early-down work, with Jaleel McLaughlin mixing in as well.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaleel-mcl.headline: Browns signed RB Jaleel McLaughlin to their active roster.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaleel-mcl.analysis: He gets the elevation after the Browns place Dylan Sampson on injured reserve. McLaughlin and Raheim Sanders will be behind Quinshon Judkins in Week 2. McLaughlin’s career shows him as a more reliable pure runner than Sanders, but we’re unsure of how the split behind Judkins will go from here.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaleel-mcl.headline: Browns signed RB Jaleel McLaughlin to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaleel-mcl.analysis: Outside of Quinshon Judkins, Dylan Sampson and Raheim Sanders are also in front of McLaughlin. The 25-year-old back has landed in a nice enough spot though considering none of these backs outside of Judkins has proved all that much yet. Also joining the Browns practice squad are: CB Myles Bryant. DE Logan Fano. T KT Leveston. P Wes Pahl. CB D’Angelo Ross. DT Tyreak Sapp. DE Khordae Sydnor. S Zion Washington. LB Nathaniel Watson and WR Kole Wilson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaleel-mcl.headline: Broncos waived RB Jaleel McLaughlin.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaleel-mcl.analysis: McLaughlin could return to the Broncos as a practice squad player. The Broncos also waived DT Israel Antwine, CB Brent Austin, wide receiver Michael Bandy, LS Luke Basso, CB Sean Fresch, DB Ricardo Hallman, OT Reid Holskey, TE Justin Joly, WR Kolbe Katsis, WR Dane Key, WR Joseph Manjack, OLB Dasan McCullough, DT Jordan Miller, OT Tyler Miller, LB Red Murdock, OL Gavin Ortega, S Parker Robertson, WR Cameron Ross, WR Kyrese Rowan, RB Cody Schrader, S Miles Scott, OLB Ron Stone Jr., CB Reese Taylor, OLB Johnny Walker Jr., DT Kristian Williams and LB Taurean York. The Broncos waived LB Drew Sanders with an injury designation. The Broncos released LS Mitchell Fraboni, TE Lucas Krull, FB Adam Prentice, OT Foster Sarell, C Lecitus Smith and OG Calvin Throckmorton. The Broncos placed DT Frank Crum and TE Caleb Lohner on injured reserve with a designation to return, and OG Nick Gargiulo on the reserve/physically unable to perform list. Those three players must miss at least four games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaleel-mcl.headline: The Denver Post’s Luca Evans believes Tyler Badie and Jaleel McLaughlin are battling for one roster spot in training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaleel-mcl.analysis: Badie probably has the edge given his versatility on special teams and third-down work. McLaughlin’s path to a roster spot “looks dicey” per Evans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaleel-mcl.headline: Broncos re-signed RB Jaleel McLaughlin to a one-year, $1.145 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaleel-mcl.analysis: Weeks after opting not to tender an offer to McLaughlin, the 25-year-old back will return to the Broncos on a one-year deal with a chance to battle for a roster spot. McLaughlin will enter camp as the RB3 behind J.K. Dobbins and R.J. Harvey, but his familiarity with Sean Payton’s offense should give him the inside edge on winning a camp battle. McLaughlin made the Broncos as a rookie UDFA in 2023 and has totaled 226-1,093-3 on the ground while adding another 59-263-4 through the air. He’s a solid depth piece but is unlikely to carry any immediate fantasy value in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaleel-mcl.headline: Broncos non-tendered RB Jaleel McLaughlin.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaleel-mcl.analysis: It’ll make him a free agent. Entering his age-26 season, McLaughlin has averaged 4.8 yards per rush and caught 59-of-69 targets for 263 yards over three years in the league. McLaughlin is built like a third-down back and will likely resurface elsewhere to attempt to snag that role for a new team.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaleel-mcl.headline: Broncos ruled out RB J.K. Dobbins (foot) for the AFC Championship Game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaleel-mcl.analysis: Dobbins is not yet ready to resume playing. He remained limited throughout all three practices this week after the Broncos opened his 21-day practice window on Monday. With Dobbins out, rookie RB RJ Harvey will again lead the backfield. He totaled 11 touches last week. Broncos RB Jaleel McLaughlin handled four and RB Tyler Badie had one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: NBC Sports’ Pro Football Talk’s Mike Florio reports that there is “growing buzz” that the Chargers could fire OC Mike McDaniel “soon,” and potentially replace him with pass game specialist Adam Gase.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: According to Florio, Gase “is expected to take over if McDaniel is fired.” The Chargers go on bye in Week 7, so this is the best time to install a new offense if they really intend to do so. Gase previously served as head coach of the Jets and Dolphins, though those stints are hardly reassuring. His offenses have frequently fallen short of expectations. The 0-6 Chargers are searching for answers, though, and the McDaniel-Justin Herbert pairing does not seem to be working out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: When asked if Chargers OC Mike McDaniel is going to continue calling plays, coach Jim Harbaugh said the team is “going to look at everything.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: Harbaugh made clear that his team has to “address everything,” especially the offense, and acknowledged that the Chargers aren’t scoring enough points. He added that the plan is to watch today’s game tape and “get with our offensive coaches” to figure things out. Although McDaniel could end up losing play-calling duties, Harbaugh owned the team’s offensive woes, saying it “starts” with him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said he doesn’t plan to intervene in the offense if it continues to struggle.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: When asked if he had any plans of intervening, Harbaugh offered his endorsement of offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, saying, “No. We trust Mike. We believe in Mike.” The 0-3 Chargers have struggled mightily out of the gate to start the season, failing to score more than 16 points in a game while also turning the ball over six times. Even in a game where the Chargers forced five turnovers off of Josh Allen and the Bills and registered four sacks, they were unable to capitalize on multiple opportunities to take the lead in the 24-16 defeat. We’ll see how long Harbaugh can go continuing to let McDaniel run the show, but it wouldn’t be surprising if the team decided to make a change if things continue in this direction.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: Chargers hired Max McCaffrey as their new running backs coach.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: McCaffrey is a former undrafted free agent NFL wide receiver who spent time with five different NFL teams. He joined the college coaching ranks as a wide receivers coach at Northern Colorado in 2020. He added offensive coordinator to his title in 2021 and held both roles for two seasons. McCaffrey joined the NFL coaching ranks as a member of former Dolphins head coach Mike McDaniel’s coaching staff in 2023, serving as an offensive assistant through the 2025 season. McCaffrey’s new role reunites him with McDaniel, who was hired as the Chargers’ offensive coordinator in January. 49ers RB Christian McCaffrey and Commanders WR Luke McCaffrey are Max’s younger brothers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: Chargers hired former Dolphins HC Mike McDaniel as offensive coordinator.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: McDaniel continued to entertain head coaching offers even after it was rumored he would join the Chargers. Now, after much deliberation, McDaniel is officially joining the Chargers to pair with Justin Herbert and company. McDaniel’s offense finished 11th or better in points scored in two of his four seasons with the Dolphins, but his final two seasons proved forgettable as Tua Tagovailoa’s limitations became apparent and defenses took advantage. McDaniel gets a top-flight QB and talent young playmakers in Ladd McConkey and Omarion Hampton to help guide his offense into 2026. All will make for enticing fantasy picks, and Herbert should enjoy a bounce back if his offensive line can stay healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports former Dolphins HC Mike McDaniel is “still in the mix” for the Raiders’ head-coaching vacancy.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: According to Rapoport, McDaniel is ultimately expected to take the Chargers’ offensive coordinator role, but until the Raiders officially rule him out as a candidate, he will remain an option for the Silver and Black. McDaniel most recently canceled his interview with the Bills on Friday and withdrew his name for consideration for the Browns before that. McDaniel has made several rounds this coaching cycle to speak with teams, but the Chargers seem like the most likely fit barring a team sweeping in to hand him a head coaching gig.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: NFL Insider Jordan Schultz reports former Dolphins HC Mike McDaniel canceled his interview with the Bills to discuss the team’s head coaching position on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: While the Bills are just beginning their search for a new head coach after dismissing Sean McDermott earlier this week, McDaniel has already withdrawn his name from the Browns head coaching search and interviewed for multiple offensive coordinator positions before agreeing to sign on with the Chargers. Schultz says McDaniel and the Bills remain in contact for a potential interview, but there’s a “strong possibility” he moves forward with the Chargers. McDaniel’s presence in Los Angeles would be massive as fantasy managers could expect the 42-year-old coach to get the most out of Justin Herbert and the rest of the Chargers’ offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: Bills are expected to interview former Dolphins HC Mike McDaniel for their head-coaching vacancy on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: McDaniel is expected to take the job as the Chargers’ offensive coordinator, but he’ll still take time to speak with the Bills about their head-coaching opening before settling for a coordinator role. McDaniel withdrew his name from the Browns’ head-coaching search earlier this week in favor of the Chargers’ job, but having the chance to lead a team with one of the best quarterbacks in the game in Josh Allen could be too much for McDaniel to pass up should the opportunity present itself. The Bills are early in their head-coaching search and still have other potential suitors to meet over the weekend, but for now, McDaniel is in the mix.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports former Dolphins head coach Mike McDaniel is “expected to become” the Chargers’ new offensive coordinator.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: The Chargers have won the Mike McDaniel sweepstakes, expecting to hire the former Dolphins head coach to their open offensive coordinator role. Several teams were in on the 42-year-old, who was interviewing for both head coaching and offensive coordinator roles. According to Schefter, McDaniel is informing teams they are out and staying in Los Angeles for the evening with the expectation he is the next Chargers’ offensive coordinator. For fantasy purposes, we are in for a faster-paced offense under Justin Herbert. Omarion Hampton is in line for more opportunity in the passing game while the wide receiver room gets better opportunities in McDaniel’s offense when compared to former offensive coordinator Greg Roman’s passing game concepts. Fantasy managers can expect to be more bullish on Herbert and the Chargers offense for 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.headline: Former Dolphins head coach Mike McDaniel informed the Browns he’s withdrawing from their head coaching search.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mike-mcdan.analysis: McDaniel, who is no sure-fire shot to get a head-coaching job though he’s still a candidate with the Ravens and Raiders, is interviewing for the Chargers offensive coordinator job today. It doesn’t look great for the Browns that they couldn’t convince McDaniel to come in for a second interview given the fact that he may be looking at settling into an offensive coordinator spot. Still on the Browns list for second interviews are: Jaguars OC Grant Udinski, Rams passing-game coordinator Nate Scheelhaase, former Ravens OC Todd Monken and Chargers DC Jesse Minter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Noah Gray caught all three of his targets for 53 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: The Chiefs used more two tight end sets with Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton sidelined. Gray ran a route on around half of KC’s drop backs and matched Travis Kelce with 53 yards. If Kelce struggles to play through the ankle injury he picked up against the Bolts, Gray could step in as the team’s TE1 in Week 7 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Noah Gray caught 3-of-5 targets for 30 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 18 loss against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: Gray led the Chiefs in targets for 30 receiving yards in another miserable offensive outing for the Mahomes-less KC offense. It was a season-best game for Gray, who once again played behind Travis Kelce and had just five games with more than 20 receiving yards. He had 21 receptions for 178 yards in 2025. Gray, 26, is signed through the 2027 season and could have an increased role in the team’s passing offense if Kelce retires this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Noah Gray (concussion/shoulder) practiced in full on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: Gray missed last week’s game with the concussion. The shoulder issue is a new addition to his practice report, though a full practice means it won’t stop him from suiting up this week. Gray isn’t on the fantasy radar for Week 14 but does bring plenty to the table as an extra blocker and a backup tight end for the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Chiefs TE Noah Gray (concussion) has been ruled out for Week 13 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: Gray sustained a head injury last week against the Colts and entered the league’s concussion protocol. He won’t suit up on a short week. It could mean a slight target bump for TE Travis Kelce. Gray had five receptions on seven targets over his past two games as a rotational tight end in the KC offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Chiefs TE Noah Gray (concussion) did not practice on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: Gray has slowly seen his role in the passing game grow over the past month, accumulating 12 targets in Kansas City’s last four games. It looks very unlikely he’ll be up for Thursday’s game against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Noah Gray caught a two-yard pass in the Chiefs’ Super Bowl LIX loss to the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: Gray’s short grab was his lone target in a blowout loss. Coming off back-to-back solid seasons as the Chiefs’ No. 2 seam stretcher, Gray signed a new three-year deal on the eve of Week 1 and proceeded to post a career-best slash of 40/437/5 as Travis Kelce continued to decline. Gray’s five scores tied for ninth amongst tight ends, though his modest eight red zone targets suggest that number was a fluke. It was still an encouraging campaign for the 25-year-old with Kelce looking like a retirement candidate. Were that to transpire, Gray would suddenly be in the lower-end TE1 mix for a Chiefs skill corps that remains undermanned despite its continued Super Bowl appearances.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Noah Gray caught 1-of-1 targets for one yard and rushed once for negative-four yards in the Chiefs’ Week 18 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: Gray logged just four total snaps in this one, indicating the Chiefs value him as a capable passing-game contributor. Most skill position starters rested in this one though some, like Gray, remained active in a reserve capacity. Gray could be an interesting leverage option in playoff DFS tournaments.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Chiefs declared Travis Kelce inactive for Week 18 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: The Chiefs listed numerous healthy, core players as doubtful to play this week with Kelce of course among them. His deactivation was fully expected. Backup tight end Noah Gray is an intriguing, if volatile, dart throw. The fourth-year veteran is having a career-best season and the Chiefs could use the opportunity to see what they have in Gray for the long-term. It is possible Andy Reid already views Gray as an important passing-game contributor though so he may have a limited role, with the playoffs in mind.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Travis Kelce caught 5-of-7 targets for 30 yards in Kansas City’s Week 16 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: Not the line you wanted, but certainly the line you’re used to. Since Week 12, Kelce has gone over eight targets just once and hasn’t done better than 68 yards in a game or scored. Kelce has become a low-end TE1. Noah Gray (1/10 on one target) gets tagged on to this post because he somehow managed to not score a touchdown. Neither player is an exciting start in Week 17 against the Steelers, though we can understand riding with Kelce’s volume.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.headline: Noah Gray caught 2-of-5 targets for 21 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 15 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/noah-gray/.analysis: Gray’s fifth score of the season was also his fifth in as many games. Today snapped a string of four straight four-catch performances, but Gray continues to lack ceiling, while his floor is still struggling to crack the top 18 in fantasy. Especially with Patrick Mahomes’ (ankle) health now up in the air, Gray isn’t a compelling Week 16 streamer against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.headline: Cyrus Allen caught both of his targets for 27 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.analysis: Rashee Rice’s absence didn’t translate into more playing time for Allen, who logged a mere five pass routes against the Chargers. He can remain on waiver wires until his playing time increases, which is unlikely if Rice is able to return in the coming weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.headline: When asked about Chiefs WR Cyrus Allen, WR coach Chad O’Shea said rookie wide receivers are “always a work in progress.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.analysis: You don’t say, Chad. Allen was the talk of Chiefs training camp. Beat reporters celebrated his ability to beat man coverage and win over the middle of the field — two aspects that help wide receivers thrive in fantasy. Unfortunately, Allen has logged just four offensive snaps this season. O’Shea adds that Allen is improving every day, both “fundamentally and schematically.” Good for him. The once-intriguing rookie is droppable in 12-team formats, though an in-season breakout remains possible. Theoretically.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.headline: Chiefs OC Eric Bieniemy said the team is going to continue building up WR Cyrus Allen to a bigger workload “the right way.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.analysis: Apparently, that means barely using him on game day, at least in the short term. Allen played one snap in the Chiefs’ season opener, despite starting WRs Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy combining for a just 5/37/1 stat line. Bieniemy also said that Allen is “going to be a part of our success moving forward. I guarantee that.” Given Allen’s Week 1 usage, becoming fantasy-relevant could take quite some time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.headline: Cyrus Allen caught 1-of-2 targets for 12 yards in the Chiefs’ preseason game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.analysis: The Chiefs let most of their starters take the field in this game and Allen wasn’t among them. He didn’t see a snap until after Rashee Rice, Xavier Worthy, and Tyquan Thornton had all left the contest. His first target didn’t come until the third quarter, and it was a drop on a high throw. The rookie rebounded with a 12-yard gain for a first down on the very next play. After playing well into the second half of the team’s final preseason game, Allen is, at best, the Chiefs’ WR4 entering the season. Despite the strong training camp, he shouldn’t be in starting fantasy lineups for Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.headline: ESPN’s Nate Taylor reports that Chiefs WR Cyrus Allen’s “ability to be a quality route runner should make him one of the Chiefs’ top answers” against man coverage.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.analysis: Taylor stops short of declaring Allen a starter in three-wide receiver sets, so he is likely still stuck in the No. 4 wide receiver spot. The fifth-round rookie has at least carved out a role for himself, and Taylor dubs him “the biggest winner in camp.” Allen is a worthwhile late-round pick at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.headline: Cyrus Allen caught 3-of-5 targets for seven yards in the Chiefs’ preseason loss to the Buccaneers on Saturday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.analysis: Allen saw action through the first three quarters of play. His 29 snaps were the third-most of any Chiefs receiver, while his 23 routes run were the second-most on the day. All three of his catches came in the short areas of the field, as evidenced by the -1.7 ADOT he averaged on his three receptions, per TruMedia. One of the most hyped players of this training camp season, the rookie fifth-rounder has a 5-27-0 receiving line on 10 targets in his two preseason games thus far.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.headline: Chiefs WR Tyquan Thornton suffered a hamstring strain at practice on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.analysis: Thornton headed into the medical tent and was subsequently carted to the locker room at Tuesday’s practice. Now it’s been revealed that he suffered a hamstring strain. It’s unclear how long Thornton might be out, but his injury further opens the door for camp standout Cyrus Allen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.headline: Cyrus Allen caught 2-of-5 targets for 20 yards in Kansas City’s first preseason game.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.analysis: The good news is that Allen worked with the starters in the slot. The bad news is that he worked well into the second half in the first preseason game while leading the team in targets. He’s clearly the highest-upside stash receiver of the group, but playing deep into the first preseason game isn’t a great sign for his chances of early playing time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.headline: Cyrus Allen (shin) returned to practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.analysis: Allen has been sidelined since Saturday after he suffered a shin injury during a collision with a teammate. The flashy fifth-round rookie has made a name for himself in the early part of training camp and is now back on the field following his brief injury scare. Allen’s recent training camp hype has made him an interesting dart throw in the later rounds of drafts, but it will likely take a few things breaking in his favor for him to make a meaningful fantasy impact this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that Chiefs WR Cyrus Allen is “very much part of the offensive plan.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cyrus-alle.analysis: According to Breer, Allen “might’ve been the best receiver in camp before bruising his shin.” Internally, the team apparently sees some similarities to Stefon Diggs in Allen’s “physical profile and play style.” Year after year, a Chiefs youngster soars up draftboards after turning in a promising showing in training camp. The results haven’t always matched the hype, though, particularly in recent seasons. Only time will tell if Allen is worthy of the praise he’s received — and only those willing to take the ADP plunge will benefit. He is not without risk, but Allen’s upside is worth chasing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Emmett Johnson had three rushes for six yards in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: It was another Ken Walker explosion game (128 yards, two touchdowns on the ground) with Johnson serving as the breather back. Johnson should be rostered as a high-upside contingency option in case Walker misses any time in the coming weeks or months.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Emmett Johnson rushed six times for 17 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 3 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Johnson was not targeted in the passing game. His six carries were nothing to sneeze at on an afternoon where the Chiefs were limited to 49 total plays, but that was compared to 20 Kenneth Walker touches. Johnson will have some pop-up standalone value behind workhorse Walker, but he is primarily a contingency option heading into the meat of the fantasy campaign.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said RB Emmett Johnson “will continue to get more snaps.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Johnson has turned 14 touches into 103 scrimmage yards thus far. Evidently pleased with his fifth-round rookie, Reid wants to keep “allowing Emmett to grow,” in turn taking “a little bit of load off” starting RB Kenneth Walker. Reid notes that Walker wants the ball on every play and is not asking for a lighter workload, but Reid is seeking “a nice balance with those two in there,” which “keeps them even more fresh as the season goes on.” Walker, of course, remains an elite RB1. Johnson, however, should be rostered in all 12-team leagues as a high-upside bench stash that could return standalone value before long.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Chiefs waived RB Emari Demercado.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Demercado’s departure leaves rookie RB Emmett Johnson and second-year RB Brashard Smith to back up starting RB Kenneth Walker. The Chiefs also waived DE Vincent Anthony, LB Kam Arnold, WR Andrew Armstrong, WR Wesley Bissainthe, DT Cole Brevard, WR Jason Brownlee, WR Jacob De Jesus, OT Ethan Driskell, WR Omari Evans, OT Chukwuebuka Godrick, LB Cam Jones, WR Xavier Loyd, S Tanner McCalister, DT Amari McNeill, C Pete Nygra, RB Jaydn Ott, DT Damon Payne, CB D’Arco Perkins-McAllister, TE Mason Pline, S DeShon Singleton, CB Melvin Smith, EDGE Tyreke Smith, OG Josh Thompson, CB Zelmar Vedder, TE Tre Watson and WR Jeff Weimer. The Chiefs released LB Cole Christiansen, CB Kaiir Elam, CB Kader Kohou and EDGE Emmanuel Ogbah. The Chiefs placed DT Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) on the reserve/physically unable to play list and WR Jimmy Holiday on injured reserve. The Chiefs also waived OG C.J. Hanson, QB Chris Oladokun and RB EJ Smith with injury designations.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Emmet Johnson rushed seven times for 39 yards in the Chiefs’ preseason game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Johnson added two catches for 15 yards and had another chunk gain through the air called back because of a penalty. Kenneth Walker didn’t play in this contest, allowing Johnson to draw the start with some of KC’s first-team offense on the field. Johnson split reps with Emari Demercado over the team’s first three drives, then left the game for good. He looks like the team’s No. 2 back, though all three backs have been the next man up behind Walker at some point during the preseason. Johnson isn’t guaranteed the backup job, but he’s now the favorite, putting him in the mix as a late-round flyer in deeper fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Emmett Johnson was “one of the positives coming out of” their first preseason game.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Johnson had 12 carries for 59 yards and three catches for 10 yards against the Rams. While we’ve seen a little camp buzz about Johnson, The Athletic’s Jesse Newell presents this as a step forward for Johnson who “has been running with the fourth-string offense most of training camp.” He’s still probably the best back to have rostered in the event of a Kenneth Walker injury, but this isn’t such an important role that the backup necessarily needs to be rostered in standard redraft leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that Chiefs RB Emmett Johnson “is swiftly earning a role as an explosive, decisive runner.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Breer refers to RB Kenneth Walker as an “every-down” player, says RB Brashard Smith “has already shown he can be a weapon in space,” and notes RB Emari Demercado adds depth. Perhaps taking on a change-of-pace rushing role is in play for Johnson this season. The rookie back has pass-catching experience as well, but Smith and Demercado could offer more in that department at the moment. Johnson could be the next player up if Walker were to miss time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: ESPN’s Dan Graziano believes Emmett Johnson “has a shot” to be Kansas City’s No. 2 back.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: The currently-murky situation behind Kenneth Walker includes the rookie Johnson, veteran receiving back Emari Demercado, and Player Who Is Nominally A Running Back Brashard Smith. The fifth-round pick sure seems like the best play here over the long-term, but if Johnson can win the No. 2 role out of camp, he’d hold some stash fantasy value behind Walker.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: A to Z Sports’ Charles Goldman believes Emari Demercado “is closer to RB2 in Kansas City than any other prospect.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Goldman added that the team is “very high” on Demercado before noting his spot as the No. 2 back in every drill of note during OTAs. The Chiefs signed Demercado to a one-year deal this offseason to back up Kenneth Walker. They also added Emmet Johnson in the fifth round of the draft, but it sounds like the veteran has the inside track to backup duties right now. Demercado could also operate as the team’s primary back on passing downs, giving him some extra juice in PPR formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.headline: Chiefs signed rookie RB Emmett Johnson to a four-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/emmett-joh.analysis: Chiefs front office officials said last week that they were shocked Johnson was still available in the fifth round of the 2026 NFL Draft. KC traded up to take Johnson, 22, who had 1,823 total yards in 2025 at Nebraska. Johnson enters the NFL with a 100th percentile college dominator rating along with a 99th percentile college target share. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid recently said he was impressed with Johnson’s pass catching and compared him favorably to LeSean McCoy. With a solid offseason Johnson could function as the Chiefs’ lead back if Ken Walker misses time in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Jalen Nailor caught 1-of-4 targets for nine yards in the Raiders’ Week 6 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: After missing Week 5’s game against the Patriots due to a concussion, Nailor was back on the field this week to face the Bills. Unfortunately for the 2026 free-agent signee, the results looked all too familiar. Nailor managed only one reception for nine yards and is now sitting on a 6-61-0 receiving line through his first five games of the season. Fantasy managers shouldn’t be counting on him to provide anything in next week’s game against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Jalen Nailor (concussion) will play in Las Vegas’ Week 6 game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: This per coach Klint Kubiak, so we assume Nailor has passed protocol. He’s only a FLEX play at this point as it’s hard to trust any weapons in the Vegas offense beyond Brock Bowers, even in a good matchup against a struggling Bills defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Jalen Nailor (concussion) resumed practicing in a red non-contact jersey.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor will likely end up being listed as a limited participant today. He has a chance to play in Week 6 against the Bills, but his odds would be better if he had returned yesterday. If active, Nailor would only be a boom-bust WR5/FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Jalen Nailor (concussion) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor suffered a concussion in the Raiders’ Week 4 loss to the Chiefs, missing Week 5 against the Patriots while still in the protocol. He starts out the week not practicing, indicating he is not close to clearing protocol. Though he still has a chance to play this week, Nailor does not need to be stashed for fantasy purposes amid a murky wide receiver corps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Raiders ruled out Jalen Nailor (concussion) for Week 5 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: The Raiders entered the season with a thin wide receiver corps, and the unit just got thinner. Tre Tucker will continue functioning as the team’s top wide receiver and second pass catcher, backed up by Cody White (ankle) and rookie Malik Benson. Nailor does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Raiders WR Jalen Nailor (concussion) did not participate in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor will almost assuredly sit out the Raiders’ Week 5 game against the Patriots. Fellow WR Dont’e Thornton (hamstring) is practicing in full, and WR Cody White (ankle) remains limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Raiders WR Jalen Nailor (concussion) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor suffered a concussion against the Chiefs in Week 4 and starts out the week not practicing. This indicates he is on the wrong side of questionable for Week 5 against the Patriots. Fellow WR Cody White (ankle) was limited as well, though Dont’e Thornton (hamstring) returned to practice, giving the Raiders some reinforcement with Nailor still in concussion protocol.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Jalen Nailor (concussion) will not return in Week 4 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor took a hard hit from Chiefs S Nohl Williams in the second quarter and was forced to go to the sideline to be evaluated. The team has now announced that Nailor will not be returning for Sunday’s game. Nailor will end the day with zero receptions on zero targets and will need to clear concussion protocol if he hopes to return in Week 5 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Jalen Nailor caught 1-of-3 targets for 16 yards in the Raiders’ Week 3 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor picked up on first down on the Raiders’ opening drive after going in motion and running a crossing route. Raiders QB Kirk Cousins was off-target on his other two throws to Nailor. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.headline: Jalen Nailor caught 1-of-3 targets for nine yards in the Raiders’ Week 2 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jalen-nail.analysis: Nailor caught three passes for 27 yards on five targets last week. His role shrank this time around with Tre Tucker erupting for 119 yards and a score. It will be hard for him to see more work in Week 3 if Brock Bowers is back. He is buried in the WR6 ranks ahead of the Raiders’ upcoming game versus the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy caught all seven of his targets for 73 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: The Chiefs, with Rashee Rice (hamstring) sidelined, made every effort to force feed Worthy near the line of scrimmage in this one. That resulted in Worthy leading the KC offense in both targets and receiving yards, with a long reception of 19 yards. Most of his Week 6 touches were of the gadget variety. Increased usage should give Worthy a sturdy PPR floor for now. He should be considered a flex play next week against the tough Seattle secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Rashee Rice (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Rice appeared to have a good chance at suiting up for Week 6 when Andy Reid spoke about it after Week 4’s win over the Raiders. Reid only said he “tweaked” his hammy. Even with a bye week to rest, it looks like Rice is now on the wrong side of questionable for Week 6. With Tyquan Thornton on IR, Xavier Worthy may be tasked with WR1 duties this week. He totaled four catches for 70 yards in his last outing and would be a solid FLEX play versus the Chargers if Rice can’t go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy caught 4-of-7 targets for 70 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 4 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Worthy saw a season-high seven targets in this one after Rashee Rice (hamstring) exited just a few plays into the game. Worthy came up with a handful of key plays for the Chiefs, with his biggest coming on a 41-yard reception that put the Chiefs in position for a short touchdown pass to Tyquan Thornton a few plays later. The Chiefs now head into their Week 5 bye, but they could be down multiple receivers, with Rice and Thornton (ankle) both suffering injuries in this one. While we don’t yet know the extent of Rice’s injury, Thornton’s ankle injury looked like a potential season-ender. Worthy could well be worth a stash in leagues where he is still available, as he could soon be the top receiver for the Chiefs when they return in Week 6 to face the Chargers. Second-year receiver Jalen Royals, who ran 21 routes in this game, could also see an expanded role in the coming weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy caught 2-of-2 targets for 20 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 3 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Worthy was also shaken up by a big hit but was never announced with an injury. Patrick Mahomes attempted only 24 passes this afternoon, but that’s still a disappointing target total for the third-year pro. 23-year-old Worthy is now sitting on just 10 catches for 63 yards through the Chiefs’ first three games. Even with this offense showing major year-over-year improvement, it’s getting harder to keep the WR4 faith with Worthy. The Raiders are a plus Week 4 matchup in Vegas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy caught 5-of-7 targets for 25 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 2 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Worthy’s score came from one yard out on a fourth-down play at the end of the second quarter. The play followed three consecutive failed rush attempts from Kenneth Walker from one yard out, with the veteran receiver leaking to the flat on a Mahomes bootleg for his first score of the young season. Worthy remains a shaky WR5 ahead of a cake matchup with the Dolphins in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Xavier Worthy caught 3-of-6 targets for 18 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 1 win over the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: The entire Kansas City pass offense appeared stuck in the mud, with little ability to attack deep against one of the league’s best defenses. Worthy struggled to gain separation on targets beyond five yards of the line of scrimmage, something the Chiefs have struggled with the previous two seasons. Further hampering their downfield pass game was an inconsistent and adjusting Patrick Mahomes in his first game since tearing his ACL. The return of offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy saw the Chiefs lean on new running back Kenneth Walker, who out-gained the entire Denver offense on his own, leaving little in the way of additional motivation to air the ball out. Worthy enters a Week 2 matchup with the Colts as a low-upside WR5, likely best left on fantasy benches, for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Chiefs WR Xavier Worthy (shoulder) is practicing in full for Week 1 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Worthy’s range of potential outcomes remains quite wide. The team attributed his lackluster 2025 season to the significant shoulder injury he suffered in Week 1. He missed time in training camp with a shoulder issue as well. He can be treated as a volatile FLEX playing in a top-tier offense against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Chiefs WR Xavier Worthy (shoulder) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: On Monday, Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Worthy should resume practicing at some point this week. The Chiefs have another practice tomorrow, so Worthy technically still has 24 hours to prove Reid right, but his continued absence is slightly concerning regardless. Last Saturday, Worthy sprained the same shoulder that was surgically repaired this offseason. He dislocated his right shoulder in Week 1, causing a full labral tear and badly impacting his season. It would be great to see him resume practicing fully tomorrow or early next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Chiefs HC Andy Reid said Xavier Worthy is dealing with a sprained shoulder and should return to practice later this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: This news comes after Worthy was carted from the field during Saturday’s practice. The third-year receiver is hoping to put last year’s disappointing season behind him when he caught just 42 passes for 432 yards and one touchdown while missing some time with a dislocated shoulder. Despite the early scare over the weekend, this recent injury doesn’t appear to be all too concerning.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.headline: Chiefs WR Xavier Worthy (shoulder) was carted from practice Saturday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/xavier-wor.analysis: Worthy was taken via cart from the practice field Saturday, although beat reporters said he was sitting in the front seat and “didn’t seem distressed as he exited.” Even so, fantasy managers don’t like seeing “Worthy” and “shoulder” together in the same sentence after the speedy third-year receiver dislocated his shoulder in Week 1 of the 2025 season and never fully looked himself. That leaves his status as a situation to monitor moving forward. Per ESPN’s Nate Taylor, Worthy made “an impressive deep catch against two defenders in which he fell to the turf near the end zone.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 25-of-33 passes for 222 yards and two touchdowns in the Rams’ 16-18, Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: The Cardinals’ pass rush was disruptive, hitting Stafford seven times and sacking him twice. Stafford lost a fumble on a two-point conversion, but the box score only shows a failed two-point try, evidently saving fantasy managers two fantasy points. Stafford later fumbled after getting spooked by a pass-rushing ghost. A Rams lineman recovered it, but it derailed an otherwise effective, tempo-based drive. Stafford nearly hit Nacua for a wide-open 65-yard touchdown at one point, but a QB hit altered Stafford’s trajectory and the pass fell incomplete. Nacua almost hauled in a diving 45-yard catch later on, but blatant DPI prevented it. Stafford engineered a touchdown drive at the tail end of the game, connecting with Nacua on a 42-yarder and a 16-yarder, before Colby Parkinson barreled into the end zone for the score. Stafford should return to the QB1 tier against the Raiders in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 40-of-54 passes for 383 yards and three touchdowns in the Rams’ 37-34, Week 5 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: It was the third consecutive game in which Stafford attempted 51 passes or more in what has become the most voluminous passing offense in the league. The two powerhouses felt each other out throughout the first half as only 20 combined points per scored before the break. Things would get aggressive for the final 30 minutes as seven combined touchdowns were scored on nine second half possessions, four of which were accounted for by the Rams. Stafford directed a whopping 24 targets toward alpha wide receiver Puka Nacua, who set a career high with 17 receptions in a short-area role. The reigning MVP returned an instant classic performance against the 2024 MVP, ultimately coming up short in overtime following a blocked field goal attempt from Harrison Mevis. The Rams fall to 2-3 ahead of a home matchup against the more forgiving Cardinals in Week 6. Stafford is once again a fantasy QB1 in that matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 32-of-51 passes for 316 yards, zero touchdowns and two interceptions in the Rams’ 24-20, Week 4 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: Stafford put the Rams behind the eight ball with a pair of first half interceptions but was better after the break as the Rams slowly erased a 20-10 deficit. Not that he was amazing, but with the Eagles finishing an inconceivable 0-12 on third down, Stafford needed to make just enough plays, and that’s what he did despite leaving some meat on the bone. It was forgivable on a rainy day in Philly, though Stafford now has at least one interception in all four of his starts. In fact, he has as many scores (six) as picks. Hopefully that trend reverses with Puka Nacua back in the lineup, though the schedule is not lightening up with the Rams hosting the Bills for Monday Night Football in Week 5. That should nevertheless be a fantasy football bonanza.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 30-of-55 passes for 390 yards, two touchdowns, and two interceptions in the Rams’ 30-26, Week 3 loss to the Broncos, adding 13 yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: The Rams stormed out to a 16-0 lead they would take into the break but two unanswered scores and two-point conversions from the Broncos saw the game knotted at 16 heading into the fourth quarter, which is where the scoring really took off. Stafford and the Rams appeared to be in control of the game until a Talanoa Hufanga pick-six off Stafford, making 33 career pick-sixes thrown to give him a record he would otherwise not like to have on his ledger. Stafford answered on the following possession on a 48-yard strike to Konata Mumpfield, only for the Broncos to answer back with a Bo Nix rushing score with 47 seconds left to play. Stafford worked more magic to get the team into the red zone, marching the field with only one timeout with a chance to win on the final play of the game. Hufanga ultimately won the play with his second interception off Stafford, sending the Rams to a 1-2 record. Stafford also became the first quarterback in NFL history to throw for 20,000 yards for two different franchises in the loss. Stafford remains a locked-in QB1 in fantasy circles ahead of a Week 4 showdown with the Eagles on the road.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Rams head coach Sean McVay said he’s “not sure” if Puka Nacua (groin) will play in Week 3.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: McVay said he’s “hopeful” Nacua, who missed Monday night’s game against the Giants, will be able to suit up against Denver next week. The Rams offense was fine without Nacua on Monday against an injury-ravaged Giants team. LA had the week’s fourth highest EPA per play on the way to a 28-6 win. Another game with Nacua sidelined will mean more target domination for Davante Adams and more involvement for Terrance Ferguson, who caught 6-of-9 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown against New York.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 22-of-31 passes for 327 yards, four touchdowns, and one interception in the Rams’ 28-6, Week 2 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: It was an inspiring effort from the 38-year-old quarterback while playing without his top option through the air in Puka Nacua. Stafford locked onto Davante Adams, the latter of whom turned 10 targets into eight receptions for 195 yards and two touchdowns, on his way to a 22nd career game with four touchdown passes. He also moved into sixth on the all-time passing touchdown leaderboard, overtaking Philip Rivers with the four-touchdown performance. The Rams shook off their travel woes in convincing fashion to move to 1-1 ahead of road meeting with the Broncos in Week 3, where Stafford will remain a locked-in QB1 in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Matthew Stafford completed 15-of-25 passes for 155 yards with an interception in the Rams’ 27-7, Week 1 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: Stafford didn’t get much time to enjoy Australia, and likely won’t leave this contest with fond memories. He completed just 4-of-11 passes in the first half and didn’t do much better in the final 30 minutes, and outside of a 41-yard connection with Puka Nacua, he just couldn’t get the ball downfield. He was also stuffed on a fourth-and-goal run at the goal line to cement the poor day. Credit the 49ers’ defense, but it’s fair to call this a disappointing season debut for the reigning MVP. Expect a rebound in Week 2 against the Giants in a Monday Night Football contest.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Rams QB Matthew Stafford said retiring from football will be a ‘year-to-year’ decision.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: Stafford discussed retirement rumors on Chris Long’s podcast, Green Light . He said a retirement decision would be “year-to-year...committing to more than that feels a little bit daunting and I think a little bit unfair to the team and myself.” The 38-year-old is looking only to the short-term, knowing he is “ready to play this year.” Stafford is not looking to make long-term decisions at this stage of his career without knowing how his body will feel after a season of play. The veteran also mentioned he has talked to Tom Brady and Drew Brees about playing into his 40s and is open to the prospect of doing so. However, Stafford is only focusing on the upcoming season for now; the Rams will be in Super Bowl contention between his return and the addition of Myles Garrett on defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins reports that the Rams plan to manage QB Matthew Stafford’s training camp reps.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: Stafford’s degenerative back issue cost him almost all of training camp last year, yet he “returned and cast those fears aside with the best season of his life.” The Rams have reportedly realized how well the time off served Stafford, as a “critical form of load management,” and plan to do some of that again this year. Per Atkins, this has been the plan for some time, and it explains why the Rams tried to sign veteran QBs like Jimmy Garoppolo and Kirk Cousins, “and why they valued the backup role enough to help justify spending the No. 13 pick on QB Ty Simpson.” In other words, don’t be alarmed if we see Simpson taking a few first-team reps this summer. Stafford remains a locked-in QB1. However, we will, of course, track all of his notable offseason developments here at Rotoworld.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.headline: Rams coach Sean McVay revealed that the team almost placed QB Matthew Stafford (back) on short-term injured reserve to begin the 2025 season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/matthew-st.analysis: Stafford aggravated a disc injury between the offseason workout program and training camp last year. He did not practice until August 18th. Reports on the injury ran the gamut. At one point, The Athletic’s Jourdan Rodrigue reported that the Rams “aren’t worried” about the injury, before later reporting that the back injury “is going to be a thing” all year. Ultimately, time spent in an Ammortal chamber outside the Rams’ facility helped Stafford get ready for an NFL MVP season. Injury risk is, of course, present. But Stafford remains one of the rare pocket passers capable of producing an elite QB1 season. Draft him accordingly.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Theo Wease caught 2-of-3 targets for 21 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs.
