https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Wease ran a route on 28 of the team’s 45 drop backs while the Chargers struggled with a spate of wide receiver injuries. Wease could see some playing time when the Chargers come back from their Week 7 bye if Ladd McConkey (head) remains sidelined. Wease had one reception headed into Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Theo Wease caught his only target for 63 yards and a touchdown in the Dolphins’ Week 17 win over the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Wease connected with fellow rookie Quinn Ewers for the first career touchdown of both of their careers. He got behind the Bucs secondary on busted coverage and took the pass to the endzone for a 63-yard score. The 24-year-old undrafted rookie free agent had just two catches heading into this game and now adds a touchdown to his pedigree. Wease seemingly has the boom-or-bust deep ball role in the Dolphins offense once occupied by healthy scratch Nick Westbrook-Ikhine.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Dolphins signed RB Jeff Wilson to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: With Brian Robinson now in San Francisco, Wilson probably felt better about his chances of being elevated off Miami’s practice squad. The Dolphins also signed TE Greg Dulcich, CB BJ Adams, CB Cornell Armstrong, LB Quinton Bell, OL Braeden Daniels, WR AJ Henning, DT Alex Huntley, LB Derrick McLendon, K Riley Patterson, OL Josh Priebe, TE Hayden Rucci, S John Saunders Jr., TE Theo Wease Jr., S Jordan Colbert to their practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Dolphins signed Missouri WR Theo Wease.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Wease (6’3/200) is a sixth-year prospect who spent four seasons at Oklahoma before transferring to Mizzou in 2023. He appeared in 63 games during his college career, but his production was often inconsistent. Wease surpassed 600 receiving yards just twice, and was seldom viewed as anything more than a serviceable WR2 wherever he played. Wease was never a target dominator, and has a career TPRR of 0.205, though some of this can be attributed to the fact that he played alongside productive college talents like Marvin Mims and Luther Burden. Wease has the ideal size to play on the outside, which is where he lined up on 87.8 percent of his career snaps, per PFF. To his credit, Wease saved his best performance for last, totaling 60 receptions for 884 yards and four touchdowns in 2024, leading all Missouri pass catchers in receiving yards. He makes up for his subpar athleticism (4.27 RAS) with his ability to win contested catches (56.3 contested catch rate 2023-2024), but Wease will need an impressive training camp if he hopes to stick on a 53-man roster. He’s a prime candidate to start his career on the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Oklahoma redshirt sophomore WR Theo Wease (foot) returned to practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Wease (6'2/200) entered the transfer portal the day after Lincoln Riley left for USC, but pulled his name out shortly thereafter when Oklahoma HC Will Venables brought in former Ole Miss OC, Jeff Lebby, to run the offense. “The turning point I would definitely say was Coach Lebby, just his philosophy and how real he made me feel,” Wease said. “It was just a family-like feel I got from him.” The former five-star talent will have Dillon Gabriel throwing balls to him out of the slot with Marvin Mims stretching the sideline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Oklahoma sophomore WR Theo Wease takes his name out of the transfer portal.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: This is big news for Brent Venables and the Sooners. They have seen their four top pass catchers all hit the transfer portal with Jadon Haselwood and Austin Stogner finding new homes in the SEC. Being able to keep Wease (6'2/200) will be huge for new offensive coordinator Jeff Leddy as he gets settled in. Wease should be a major factor in Leddy’s offense which relies on RPO’s, screens, and deep concepts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Oklahoma sophomore WR Theo Wease (leg) was a participant in warmups ahead of Saturday’s game against Iowa State.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Wease (6'2/200) being dressed out and going through warmups is a positive development for the Sooners, who are expected to be without Drake Stoops. After starting all 11 games last season, Wease has yet to appear in a game season due to the leg injury that he suffered in a September practice. The sophomore caught 37 passes for 530 yards and four touchdowns in 2020.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Oklahoma sophomore WR Theo Wease (leg) is still not fully participating in practice and is unlikely to play this week against Baylor.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Wease (6'2/200) sustained the leg injury in practice back in early September and has been gradually trying to return to the field. Though he is making progress, when HC Lincoln Riley was asked about Wease’s availability for Baylor, he expressed skepticism saying “Too early to say... probably a bit of a reach right now.” His return would be a welcomed boost to a rejuvenated Oklahoma offense under freshman starting QB Caleb Williams, as Wease caught 37 passes for 530 yards and four touchdowns last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Oklahoma sophomore WR Theo Wease (leg) is expected to make his return at some point this season according to HC Lincoln Riley.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Wease (6'2/200) sustained the leg injury in Week 1 against Tulane and was expected to miss several weeks. The exact phrasing used by HC Lincoln Riley is that he expects him to return “sometime this year.” Though that timeframe doesn’t exactly crystalize when he will be available, it’s at least confirmation that the sophomore wideout will return in 2021. Wease, who missed the spring game due to a leg injury, caught 37 passes for 530 yards and four touchdowns last season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Oklahoma sophomore WR Theo Wease is expected to miss a “few weeks” after suffering a lower leg injury in a recent practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Just how much time Wease (6'2/200) will miss remains unknown, as the wide receiver still has to undergo MRI and X-ray scans. According to All Sooners, the expectation is that he’ll miss at least a “few weeks,” so Wease won’t be available when Oklahoma takes on Tulane Saturday afternoon. Wease, who missed the spring game due to a leg injury, caught 37 passes for 530 yards and four touchdowns last season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.headline: Charlies Kolar caught 3-of-5 targets for 20 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/charlie-ko.analysis: Kolar ran 28 routes on the day while Oronde Gadsden II ran 24 routes and also had five targets from Justin Herbert. The division of pass-catching duties for LA’s tight ends make both guys unplayable for fantasy outside the deepest formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.headline: Kimani Vidal had seven rushes for 21 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs, adding three catches for 19 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.analysis: Vidal got much of his work in the first quarter before Omarion Hampton worked into the backfield later in the game. Hampton ended up leading the Bolts backfield in both routes and targets, with Vidal a close second in both categories. When the Chargers return from the bye week, Vidal could see an increased role as the team looks elsewhere for production. He should be rostered in most deep formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.headline: Omarion Hampton had seven rushes for 18 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs, adding four catches for 21 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.analysis: Hampton was his usual plodding self in this one, with a long rush of four yards in another depressing outing for the LA offense. Kimani Vidal, meanwhile had seven rushes for 21 yards and got much of his work in the first quarter. Keaton Mitchell had just two carries and did not catch his lone target. Hampton led the backfield in routes and targets on the day. His diminishing role and his lack of efficiency has made Hampton nothing more than a touchdown-dependent desperation flex option this year. The Chargers have a bye in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.headline: Kimani Vidal rushed eight times for 57 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.analysis: Vidal showed off his potential to be a big-play back on a 42-yard touchdown that gave the Chargers a 17-10 lead. The 25-year-old did nothing outside of that carry, but in a game where offense was limited — limited is putting it nicely — it stood out. Vidal was more effective than Omarion Hampton (33 yards on 14 carries) and Keaton Mitchell (11 on six) but still seems likely to be behind both for Week 6 against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.headline: Kimani Vidal caught two passes for 11 yards and a touchdown while rushing four times for 16 yards in the Chargers’ Week 4 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.analysis: Vidal took a flip pass from Justin Herbert for a touchdown to get the Chargers to within two scores. The 25-year-old saw plenty of reps as Los Angeles is clearly committed to the committee approach — no running back had more than ten carries — but outside of that score, he didn’t do much with them. The Chargers take on the Broncos in Week 5 and Vidal remains off the fantasy radar.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.headline: Chargers RB Keaton Mitchell rushed three times for minus-one yard in Thursday’s preseason game against the 49ers, adding one reception for 11 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.analysis: Mitchell’s box score would have looked a lot better if his 21-yard reception on a route out of the backfield had not been called back due to a penalty. Chargers starting RB Omarion Hampton played all three snaps on the opening drive before giving way to Mitchell, who played 10-of-10 snaps on the second and third drives. Fellow backup RB Kimani Vidal took the field as the Chargers’ kick returner to begin the game. He made his first appearance on offense on the Chargers’ fourth drive. Mitchell could return standalone FLEX value with big-play upside in this role. He reportedly visited the blue medical tent, but was allowed to return to the sideline. Hopefully, this is a non-issue.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.headline: Chargers RB Kimani Vidal rushed five times for eight yards in Thursday’s preseason game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.analysis: Vidal stayed in for two drives and did not catch his only target. Tonight’s start suggests Vidal is behind RB Keaton Mitchell on the depth chart. Mitchell did not play, nor did starting RB Omarion Hampton. Vidal is a proven, capable fill-in starter, but he should only be drafted as the Chargers’ RB3 at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.headline: Speaking on NFL Daily about his backfield rotation, Chargers OC Mike McDaniel said, “if a player is playing really well, I’m not going to take them out.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.analysis: Earlier this week, McDaniel said he plans to employ a hot-hand approach at the running back position and plans to “use all three of those guys probably every game.” NFL Daily co-hosts Gregg Rosenthal and Jourdan Rodrigue helpfully followed up on those comments, specifically regarding their fantasy football implications. McDaniel encouragingly prefaced his response by saying, “no one has to worry,” adding that benching productive players is “bad business.” If you were already bullish on one or more of Omarion Hampton, Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal, these comments can be taken positively. Reading between the lines, if Hampton, the starter, proves his value as the team’s RB1, he should receive a fantasy-friendly workload.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.headline: Chargers OC Mike McDaniel said “I’ll use all three of those guys probably every game” when asked about the backfield.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.analysis: Speaking to reporters Monday, Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel said that all three of Omarion Hampton, Keaton Mitchell, and Kimani Vidal will be featured in the backfield this season. “Good news is I see all three of those guys performing at a very high level,” McDaniel said. “Kinda play hot hand once you’re into games.” While that’s not the best news for fantasy managers that invested second round picks into Hampton, the opportunity for the Chargers to turn heads on the scoreboard could result in a case of “a rising tide raises all ships.” McDaniel famously, and recently, made two backs top-six producers in fantasy points per game in the same season, with both Raheem Mostert and De’Von Achane finishing 2023 in that range. Whether a similar situation transpires in Los Angeles remains to be seen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.headline: Chargers OC Mike McDaniel said he could use all three RBs in a game and that usage may depend on who has the “hot hand.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.analysis: It’s the kind of thing fantasy managers hate to hear. When speaking about his running backs on Monday, McDaniel said, “I see all three producing at a very high level,” while saying the workload for each back could depend on the opponent and who has the “hot hand.” While it’s certainly concerning on the surface, we feel pretty confident in Omarion Hampton having the safest role as far as fantasy is concerned, while Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal could prove a bit more volatile. Their volatility has been baked into their ADP all offseason, as Mitchell is often going in the 12th or 13th round of drafts while Vidal often goes undrafted. It may take some time to get a good sense of McDaniel’s plans for the backfield, but we would expect a clear-cut RB1 and RB2 to emerge this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.headline: The Athletic’s Daniel Popper expects Keaton Mitchell to beat out Kimani Vidal for Chargers’ RB2 role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/kimani-vidal/0.analysis: Per Popper, the Chargers really like Mitchell’s ability to “press the edge and get explosives to the outside.” That said, Popper believes Vidal will “give Mitchell a push” for the role. He also believes that both players will make the final roster, regardless. If this is how the depth chart shakes out, one wonders whether Vidal could sneak onto the field in certain passing situations, potentially reducing Mitchell’s standalone viability. Mitchell was seen working in the passing game last week, though — something he rarely did in Baltimore — so it is too early to tell.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden II caught 3-of-5 targets for 17 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Both Gadsden and Charlie Kolar had five targets on the day (Kolar caught three of those targets for 20 yards). Gadsden logged 28 pass routes to 24 for Kolar. The split-up tight end role will make it next to impossible for either guy to be fantasy relevant without catching a touchdown. The Chargers are on bye next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden failed to haul in his only target in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Gadsden had another disappointing outing for the Chargers and his fantasy managers on Sunday. He’s now been held without a catch in two of his last three games and has yet to exceed 36 receiving yards in any game this season. Playing in one of the worst offenses in the league certainly doesn’t help things, but Gadsden can’t be trusted by fantasy managers at this point and won’t be on the fantasy radar in Week 6 when the Chargers visit the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden II caught 5-of-8 targets for 36 yards in the Chargers’ Week 4 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Gadsden did make a spectacular catch on fourth down to set up a touchdown, but oustide of that, the tight end — while finishing tied for the most catches on the day with Keaton Mitchell — was unable to find any room against the Seahawks’ defense. The 23-year-old was more involved than he has been in previous weeks, but that’s less compliment to this effort than insult to the first few. He’ll be back at it in Week 5 against another tough defense in the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Chargers TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) won’t play in Los Angeles’ Week 4 game against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: He did rejoin practice today, making it plausible he’ll be up for the Chargers’ Week 5 game against the Broncos. Second-year receiving TE Oronde Gadsden was unable to seize the moment with Kolar and TE David Njoku (knee) sidelined last week, catching 0-of-3 targets. The once-promising youngster must do something on Sunday if he wishes to remain re-draft-relevant in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden didn’t catch any of his three targets in a Week 3 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Gadsden’s first target of the day was on a third-down pass that hit off his hands and landed on the grass. Neither of his other two targets was particularly close to being caught. He did play on 39 of the team’s 69 snaps, more than any other tight end, and ran a route on 31 of their 43 dropbacks, which was the third-most of any player on the Chargers. We guess you can talk yourself into his role based on those numbers, but the results weren’t there, and the Chargers look discombobulated on offense. It’s hard to trust Gadsden in fantasy going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: ESPN’s Kris Rhim reports that Chargers TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) will not be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Kolar’s surgery earlier this week reportedly changed his prognosis. Kolar was expected to land on short-term injured reserve and miss at least four games. Apparently, the team expects him back sooner than that. Backup TE Oronde Gadsden is still set to start, given Kolar and TE David Njoku’s (knee) injuries, but Gadsden’s audition window has evidently shrunk. He remains a worthwhile add and can be started by TE-needy fantasy managers in what should be a productive game environment against the Bills this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden caught both of his targets for 18 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers’ Week 2 loss to the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: David Njoku left the game early with a knee injury and Charlie Kolar followed him to the locker room much later because of a forearm injury. As a result, Gadsden’s route rate jumped from 14 percent in Week 1 to 48 percent today. He still managed just two catches, but Gadsden at least found the end zone for the first time this year. The Chargers offense has looked defunct through two weeks, so even a full-time role for Gadsden could result in middling fantasy numbers. Still, he is worth a look off the waiver wire for teams in need of tight end production.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Chargers OC Mike McDaniel said the team plans on utilizing TE Oronde Gadsden’s skillset.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: McDaniel was asked why Gadsden only played eight snaps in Week 1. The Chargers’ offensive coordinator said he expected Gadsden to get more involved last week, but the game “didn’t play out” that way. McDaniel closed by saying he expects Gadsden “to be more involved outside of an unforeseen situation where the game and the parameters with which you’re playing change — and therein lies the problem. Gadsden is not a full-time player. Projecting his weekly usage will be challenging. He is currently not worth starting in 12-team leagues, though that could change if McDaniel decides to feature him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.headline: Oronde Gadsden II caught both of his targets for 32 yards in the Chargers’ Week 1 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/oronde-gadsden.analysis: Gadsden hardly saw the field against Arizona. He ran just seven pass routes while David Njoku logged 17 routes and caught all five of his targets. Gadsden is clearly an afterthought in the Chargers passing offense for now. He should remain on waiver wires ahead of the Bolts’ Week 2 game against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston caught 1-of-3 targets for 57 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston’s lone catch was a fantastic grab over tight coverage in the fourth quarter. He nearly scored on the play. Even with Ladd McConkey out with a head injury, Johnston did not function as the Chargers’ top wideout, as DeAndre Lambert-Smith led the team with ten targets. Johnston will be nothing more than a deep league flex option going forward. He should not be rostered in most 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Stark difference from last week’s limited-limited-rule out. Jim Harbaugh would not commit to putting it on the record that Johnston would be on a snap count. Playing through the injury with Los Angeles’ sad sack offensive line would seem to have Johnston as more of a sketchy FLEX play than a WR3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston is on track to play, but this wide receiver corps is very banged up. KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring) and Brenen Thompson (quad) remained limited as well. Marquez Valdes-Scantling (ribs) upgraded to full.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston, KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring), Brenen Thompson (quad), and Marquez Valdes-Scantling (rib) were all limited Wednesday. Lambert-Smith currently has his practice window for return from IR open while the others are dealing with a varying level of ailments. Johnston is the best fantasy option out of this group, but he is only worth FLEX consideration in the deepest of leagues. With Ladd McConkey (foot) also limited, the Chargers have several “maybes” ahead of a Week 6 matchup against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Quentin Johnston (chest) will “probably be limited this week like last for the practice.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: “We’ll see where he’s at the end of the week,” Harbaugh added. Johnston practiced on both Thursday and Friday so he likely has the best chance of being active among Los Angeles’ main three wideouts. Unfortunately this passing game is in rough shape, and even a higher volume, healthy load probably wouldn’t get Johnston above the FLEX line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) won’t play in Los Angeles’ Week 5 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston got in limited sessions on Thursday and Friday, so it was surprising to see him sent straight to “not playing.” Tre’ Harris figures to step in as Los Angeles’ top outside receiver by snaps this week and is a worthwhile FLEX play, even against a formidable Broncos defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston and TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) both remained limited today, though WR Brenen Thompson (quad) downgraded. He did not practice, nor did Ladd McConkey (foot). Tre’ Harris could end up being the Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver, but he would only be a FLEX against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Chargers WR Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: In addition to Johnston, TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) and WR Brenen Thompson (quad) were also limited. Johnston has played in every game this season, but pops up on the practice report with a chest issue on Wednesday. He is not yet in danger of missing Week 5, barring setbacks later in the week. Neither Thompson nor Kolar have played since Week 2 but both have a chance to return this week against the Broncos. With Ladd McConkey (foot) not practicing, Johnston may have fantasy value as the Chargers’ No. 1 wideout this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston caught 1-of-2 targets for 44 yards in the Chargers’ Week 4 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston at least made the most of his only catch, as it was on 4th-and-7 and kept the Chargers in the game. He also saw a redzone target, but Justin Herbert overthrew him. Johnston simply cannot be trusted even with the potential to make big plays in Week 5 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.headline: Quentin Johnston caught 3-of-6 targets for 40 yards in a Week 3 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/quentin-jo.analysis: Johnston also had a really bad drop on a 3rd-and-10 pass in the fourth quarter with the Chargers trailing. The ball hit him directly in the hands about three yards past the sticks, and he dropped it. Still, Johnston played on 60 of the team’s 69 snaps and ran a route on 37 of their 43 dropbacks, so he remains the clear second receiver by playing time. After Week 3, it wouldn’t be a surprise to see Tre Harris start to cut into Johnston’s workload.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell had two rushes for four yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: Mitchell did not catch his only target on the day. He was third among Bolts running backs in pass routes, behind Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal. The sad state of the Chargers offense and injuries to the team’s offensive line make it nearly impossible for Mitchell to post fantasy relevant numbers for now. The Chargers are on bye in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell rushed 6 times for 11 yards in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos while adding three receptions for 18 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: The only positive here was that Mitchell was somewhat involved in the pass game, but it was all of the check-down variety. The injuries to the Los Angeles offensive line just won’t open many holes right now, and even if Mitchell has looked more spry than Omarion Hampton, there’s more risk than reward having him in a lineup right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel said he has not lost “any faith” in Omarion Hampton.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: “I don’t see any change in terms of the depth chart at all. I felt I was underutilizing a strength,” McDaniel said about the increased usage of Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal. McDaniel’s statement is good for Hampton in the sense that we know Hampton will retain a reasonable role. And it’s bad because McDaniel is all but confirming the pecking order will remain the same. Expect more low-end RB2/FLEX nonsense from Hampton.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell rushed 10 times for 39 yards while catching five passes for 24 yards in the Chargers’ Week 4 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: Mitchell, Omarion Hampton and Kimani Vidal were both equally involved in the rushing attack, and that’s not really a compliment to anyone in this group.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell (foot) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 4 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: He practiced all three days this week, upgrading to full on Friday, and should be a lower-end FLEX option against a tough Seahawks run defense. The good news for Mitchell is that the proof-of-concept of “the Chargers can’t run block so they should just use someone fast” worked in Week 3. He should see a reasonable amount of touches in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell (ankle) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: The Chargers’ speedy RB2 was seen wearing a walking boot after practice on Wednesday, but that didn’t keep him from practicing today. Mitchell scored a touchdown on a red zone carry last week and could continue rotating in against the Seahawks this week. He should be rostered in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: ESPN’s Kris Rhim reports Keaton Mitchell was wearing a walking boot on his left foot after practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: He was eventually added to the injury report as “limited” with an ankle issue. Per Rhim, Mitchell told reporters in the locker room he was okay. Mitchell was not initially on the injury report. This obviously flared up during practice but he didn’t have it looked at until after the report was posted. We will get more clarity on the situation tomorrow. Mitchell’s role grew in Week 3 with 11 touches, but a foot or ankle injury would likely limit any further progress.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell rushed eight times for 52 yards in a Week 3 loss to the Bills, adding three catches and a receiving touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: Mitchell’s touchdown was on a “pass” from Justin Hebert that was really a jet sweep where Herbert let go of the ball, and Mitchell rushed it in off the edge. Regardless, it was a nice run by Mitchell, who made Deone Walker miss in the backfield and is a clear example that the Chargers want to get him the ball in space. Mitchell did see about half as many carries as Omarion Hampton, but he played just three fewer snaps and ran a route on nine more dropbacks. Considering he was also seeing some work in the red zone, Mitchell needs to be rostered in all formats right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell rushed five times for 24 yards in the Chargers’ Week 2 loss to the Raiders, adding one catch for 145 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: The Chargers deployed Mitchell sparingly once again. He touched the ball four times in his LA debut last week and that number only improved to six this time around. Omarion Hampton logged 23 carries and two catches today. On the other hand, Hampton coughed up a game-losing fumble, so the Chargers may want to see more from Mitchell next week versus the Bills. He is buried in the RB5/6 ranks for now, but fantasy managers can hold onto him for at least one more week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.headline: Keaton Mitchell had four rushes for nine yards in the Chargers’ Week 1 loss to the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/keaton-mit.analysis: Omarion Hampton led the LA backfield with ten carries. Hampton scored a short rushing touchdown and lost a fumble in the first half. Mitchell logged 13 pass routes and one target against the Cardinals while Hampton ran 17 routes and was not targeted. Mitchell’s Week 1 involvement could lead to some fantasy usefulness at some point this season. For now he’ll remain a big-play reliant flex play in deeper formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chad-rylan.headline: Chad Ryland converted 6-of-6 field goals in the Cardinals’ Week 6 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chad-rylan.analysis: Ryland attempted and converted a season-high six field goals today, including two between the 20-29-yard lines, three between the 30-39-yard lines and one from 40-plus. He’s attempted fewer than three field goals in 3-of-6 games thus far, and coach Mike LaFleur said post-game that he “never” wants to see Ryland attempt six kicks again, unless they are extra points. Ryland should probably not be counted on for high-end K1 results next week against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chad-rylan.headline: Cardinals waived K Joshua Karty.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chad-rylan.analysis: Karty produced a 67 percent field goal conversion rate and an 88 percent extra point conversion rate with the Cardinals last year. He was slated to compete with K Chad Ryland this offseason. It appears as though Ryland is the victor.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chad-rylan.headline: Cardinals re-signed K Chad Ryland to a one-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chad-rylan.analysis: Ryland has spent the last two seasons with the Cardinals, converting on 81.5 percent of his field goal attempts over that span while going 10-of-14 from 50-plus yards. The 26-year-old kicker was 6-of-10 from that distance in 2025 and also made all 36 of his extra point attempts. The decision to bring back Ryland was a no-brainer for head coach Mike LaFleur, although he’ll likely face competition for the kicking job after the Cards brough in Josh Karty last December.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chad-rylan.headline: Cardinals signed K Joshua Karty off the Rams’ practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chad-rylan.analysis: Will we get a Chad Ryland release move here, or will the 2025 Cardinals create some sort of two-kicker abomination scenario with their remaining time? There are so many questions to ask, and so little that we know. And so little of it that feels like it matters. Someone will kick and be a decent option against the Bengals in Week 17.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chad-rylan.headline: Chad Ryland converted one of two field goal attempts in the Cardinals’ Week 14 loss against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chad-rylan.analysis: Ryland has now missed one field goal in four straight games. On the season he has missed six of his 25 field goal tries while making all 29 of his extra points. Attached to an Arizona offense that rarely has the benefit of neutral and positive game script — allowing for field goal attempts throughout the game — Ryland is not a reliable fantasy play. He should not be rostered in Week 15 against Houston.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chad-rylan.headline: Matt Prater (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chad-rylan.analysis: Prater, 40, remains on injured reserve, and the Cardinals will need to activate him shortly if he has any chance in playing in Week 18 against the 49ers. If Prater can’t go, the Cardinals will have Chad Ryland handle the kicking duties.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chad-rylan.headline: Cardinals K Matt Prater (knee) will not play in Week 16 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chad-rylan.analysis: Prater will remain on injured reserve for at least one more week. Chad Ryland will continue to kick for the Cardinals. Facing a Carolina defense that should allow Arizona to move the ball with ease, Ryland is a solid streaming option this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chad-rylan.headline: Cardinals opened the 21-day practice window for K Matt Prater (knee).
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chad-rylan.analysis: Prater will practice with the Cardinals this week and has a chance to suit up in Week 16 against the Panthers. Chad Ryland would continue kicking for Arizona if Prater, who suffered a knee injury in October, needs another week of practice before returning to action. The Panthers are allowing the fourth most field goal tries this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chad-rylan.headline: Cardinals HC Jonathan Gannon said he expects Matt Prater (knee) to play again this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chad-rylan.analysis: Prater has been on injured reserve since October 15th. He’s not eligible to return until Week 12, meaning there’s still plenty of time for him to recover from his injury before the team can even consider activating him. Prater’s replacement, Chad Ryland, has converted on 10-of-11 field goal attempts this season and has two field goals of 50-plus yards to his name. His emergence could put the Cardinals in a tough decision once Prater is healthy enough to be activated.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chad-rylan.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Cardinals K Matt Prater (knee) is not expected to play in Week 6 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chad-rylan.analysis: Prater missed Week 5 with the knee issue and is listed as questionable for Week 6. Practice squad kicker Chad Ryland will take his spot in the lineup. Ryland went 3-of-4 on field goals last week and connected on his only PAT attempt.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keandre-lamber.headline: KeAndre Lambert-Smith caught 5-of-10 targets for 32 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keandre-lamber.analysis: With Ladd McConkey out with a head injury, Lambert-Smith led the Chargers in pass routes and targets. He didn’t do much with the opportunity. The flurry of Chargers wideout injuries could leave the team with no choice but to give Lambert-Smith significant snaps when they return from their Week 7 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keandre-lamber.headline: KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring) is questionable for Los Angeles’ Week 6 game against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keandre-lamber.analysis: With Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston suiting up this week, any chance of Lambert-Smith returning to real fantasy value looks quashed. For this week, anyway. He did get in a full session today. If activated off injured reserve ahead of the contest, he can be ignored until after the Week 7 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keandre-lamber.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keandre-lamber.analysis: Johnston is on track to play, but this wide receiver corps is very banged up. KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring) and Brenen Thompson (quad) remained limited as well. Marquez Valdes-Scantling (ribs) upgraded to full.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keandre-lamber.headline: Quentin Johnston (chest) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keandre-lamber.analysis: Johnston, KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring), Brenen Thompson (quad), and Marquez Valdes-Scantling (rib) were all limited Wednesday. Lambert-Smith currently has his practice window for return from IR open while the others are dealing with a varying level of ailments. Johnston is the best fantasy option out of this group, but he is only worth FLEX consideration in the deepest of leagues. With Ladd McConkey (foot) also limited, the Chargers have several “maybes” ahead of a Week 6 matchup against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keandre-lamber.headline: Chargers activated KeAndre Lambert-Smith’s (hamstring) 21-day practice window.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keandre-lamber.analysis: The lanky downfield wide receiver could return to find himself seriously competing for a starting role. Lambert-Smith caught 5-of-12 targets for 51 yards and one touchdown as a rookie last year, yet drew praise from film analysts around the industry. The Chargers are desperate for offensive contributions. Lambert-Smith can be stashed in 14-team leagues, though his low odds of producing make him a tougher pickup in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keandre-lamber.headline: Chargers placed WR KeAndre Lambert-Smith on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keandre-lamber.analysis: He’ll miss at least the next four games. Lambert-Smith played in two special teams snaps in the opener and the days of him and Trey Lance hooking up for deep passes at the Hall of Fame game feel like they happened five years ago instead of in 2025. The Chargers added Gary Jennings off the practice squad to fill the void.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keandre-lamber.headline: KeAndre Lambert-Smith did not play in the Chargers’ Wild Card loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keandre-lamber.analysis: A hamstring injury suffered in Week 18 kept the situational deep threat sidelined against the Patriots. He caught 5-of-12 targets for 51 yards and one touchdown in his rookie season. Lambert-Smith will get the chance to earn a spot on the game-day roster this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keandre-lamber.headline: Chargers WR KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring) won’t play in Los Angeles’ Wild Card game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keandre-lamber.analysis: He didn’t practice all week. The rookie would enter next week with a questionable tag if the Chargers survive in New England.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keandre-lamber.headline: Chargers WR KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keandre-lamber.analysis: Lambert-Smith is now on the wrong side of questionable, having missed the last two practices. The speedy rookie has not yet established himself as a reliable pass catcher, but he would be nice to have available on game day. The Chargers’ offense has been hit hard with injuries this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keandre-lamber.headline: Chargers WR KeAndre Lambert-Smith did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keandre-lamber.analysis: Lambert-Smith left the Chargers’ Week 18 game against the Broncos with an apparent hamstring injury and now starts out the week not practicing. The rookie 23-year-old is low on the pass-catching depth chart and finished the 2025 regular season with five receptions for 51 yards and a touchdown. Lambert-Smith’s absence on kick returns will have more of an impact if he cannot go in the Wild Card against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 5-of-7 targets for 97 yards and two touchdowns in the Raiders’ Week 6 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Tucker found the end zone on an 11-yard touchdown pass from Kirk Cousins in the fourth quarter to tie the game at 23-23. Later in the game, with the Raiders down by 10, Tucker found himself on the receiving end of a Kirk Cousins moon ball in the end zone, which he hauled in for a 44-yard touchdown to cut the Bills’ lead to 33-30 with just over a minute left in the game. Tucker is the closest thing the Raiders have to a fantasy-viable wide receiver, and he has proven to be a volatile player throughout his four-year career. Fantasy managers shouldn’t view him as anything more than a boom-or-bust WR4 in next week’s game against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 4-of-5 targets for 41 yards in the Raiders’ Week 5 loss to the Patriots, adding two rushes for -7 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Tucker’s two rushing attempts were blown up in the backfield. He was third on the team in targets, trailing Brock Bowers and Ashton Jeanty. Tucker, who usually operates as the team’s primary downfield option, should have some appeal in Week 6 against Buffalo in what could be a high-scoring game. He has at least four receptions in four of five games this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 4-of-8 targets for 44 yards in the Raiders’ Week 4 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Tucker’s longest catch came on a 23-yard reception late in the fourth quarter as the Raiders looked to drive and tie up the game. Had the replay officials called for a review of the play in time, the catch likely would have been overturned, but the play was upheld, much to the disappointment of the Chiefs and head coach Andy Reid. The eight targets Tucker saw in this one set a new season high. He’s totaled 44 or fewer yards in three of four games this season and will be hard to trust as anything more than a dart-throw WR4 in Week 5 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 4-of-4 targets for 43 yards in the Raiders’ Week 3 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Tucker had a bigger impact in real life than he did in fantasy. On the plus side, he helped set up a field goal and a touchdown, first by finding the soft spot in the Saints’ zone coverage in the two-minute drill. Later, his 15-yard gain on a deep crossing route helped set up the Raiders. He also committed a holding penalty, which erased a short gain for RB Ashton Jeanty. Tucker is a WR4/FLEX against the Chiefs next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 5-of-7 targets for 119 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 2 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Kirk Cousins got the deep ball going in this game after settling for mostly check-downs in Week 1. Tucker caught two passes of 40+ yards, the first of which was a second-quarter touchdown. He also tied Ashton Jeanty with a team-high seven targets, so it wasn’t just a one-off deep shot for the veteran wideout. Brock Bowers is expected to return next week, meaning Tucker’s target share should take a hit the next time we see him. Even if he is relegated to field-stretching duties in Week 3, Tucker will remain a high-ceiling FLEX bet versus the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Tre Tucker caught 2-of-4 targets for 27 yards in the Raiders’ Week 1 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Despite receiving clear-cut No. 1 wide receiver treatment late in the preseason, Tucker was not the clear-cut No. 1 wide receiver in Week 1. He nabbed a nice 21-yard gain and had another downfield pass broken up by DPI, but Raiders coach Klint Kubiak didn’t have a focal target here. Treat Tucker as a boom-bust FLEX against the Chargers next week, in what should be a back-and-forth game environment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said the team is still trying to find a wide receiver who is “accountable and can help us on Sunday.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: He punctuated his point by saying only, “still looking.” Kubiak’s ambiguous phrasing could suggest that the Raiders are seeking a wide receiver via trade, but it can also be read simply as an indictment of players like Jalen Nailor, Jack Bech and Malik Benson. None of the three turned in a great game last night, while Tre Tucker was given the night off. Tucker makes for a boom-bust FLEX option in an underwhelming position group.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Raiders WR Jalen Nailor caught 1-of-3 targets for 22 yards in Thursday’s preseason game against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: Both Nailor and WR Jack Bech played tonight while WR Tre Tucker took the night off. Bech failed to earn a target and played into the fifth drive. Nailor called it a night after the third drive. The Raiders’ top-three wide receivers appear to be Tucker, Nailor and Bech, in that order. Tucker might warrant matchup-based FLEX treatment in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: Raiders WR Malik Benson operated as the team’s WR2 with WR Jalen Nailor and WR Dont’e Thornton “nicked up” on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: The depth chart placement is a tad curious because it suggests Benson ran ahead of either WR Tre Tucker or WR Jack Bech. Benson has been rotating in with the first-team offense for more than a week, so this isn’t groundbreaking news, but one wonders if he can use the opportunity to make a compelling case for a starting role in three-wide receiver sets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.headline: ESPN’s Ryan McFadden reports that Raiders WR Malik Benson is taking reps with the first-team offense.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tre-tucker.analysis: The Raiders are reportedly rotating five different wide receivers through team drills, including Tre Tucker, Jack Bech, Jalen Nailor and Dont’e Thornton. Tucker is the most proven player of the bunch and should be expected to secure a starting role. Things are fluid beyond that. McFadden named Benson, a sixth-round rookie, his “biggest surprise” of spring practices. He reportedly fostered a strong connection with QB Fernando Mendoza. Given his draft capital, Benson is likely a long shot to earn a starting role, but he also possesses intriguing upside as a field stretcher. Don’t bank on a breakout, but keeping an eye on him this summer is worthwhile.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught 7-of-9 targets for 95 yards in the Raiders’ Week 6 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: This is the second time in three weeks that Mayer has popped up for a big performance. With Brock Bowers blanketed for much of the first half, Mayer stepped up to catch five passes for 52 yards in the first half, and he ripped off an impressive 28-yard reception in the second half on a drive that ended with a Matt Gay field goal. Playing behind Bowers continues to make Mayer a risky fantasy bet, but he’s averaging 6.7 targets in his last three games, which is buoyed by this week’s nine-target game and a 10-target outing in Week 4 against the Chiefs. With a few reliable tight ends on bye in Week 7, Mayer could have some viability as a dart throw next week against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught his lone target for two yards in the Raiders’ Week 5 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Mayer and the rest of the Vegas pass catchers took a backseat to Brock Bowers, who had a team-leading ten targets for 110 yards and a touchdown before the Raiders pulled their starters in the fourth quarter of this blowout loss. Mayer was fresh off an 82-yard outing (on ten targets) against Kansas City. He should remain on waivers ahead of Week 6’s game against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught 8-of-10 targets for 82 yards in the Raiders’ Week 4 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Mayer’s 10 targets were just one fewer than what Brock Bowers (11) saw on the day. Mayer made the most of his opportunities, racking up 82 yards—the second most in his career and saw four of his receptions come on the Raiders’ first four drives of the game. On the Raiders’ fourth drive, Mayer hauled in passes of two, seven, and 17 yards, with his longest catch setting up a 48-yard field goal just before halftime to put them up 13-10. We shouldn’t expect this level of production from Mayer on a weekly basis, but the Raiders’ underwhelming WR corps could pave the way for more opportunities for Mayer going forward after this solid outing. There’s a lot to like here, but Mayer will be a boom-or-bust TE2 next week against the Patriots until we see reliable target totals on a more consistent basis, while he shares the field with Brock Bowers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught 3-of-3 targets for 32 yards and one touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 3 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Mayer scored with just under six minutes left in the first half. Coach Klint Kubiak sent Brock Bowers in motion, back and forth across the formation, behind the line of scrimmage, before Kirk Cousins executed the play-action fake. Mayer ran an out route from the slot and shook Saints defender Justin Reid on the cut before quickly hauling in the pass. Mayer’s other two catches both went for double-digit yardage gains. He will be a viable TE2 moving forward, with defenses focused on stopping Bowers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught 3-of-4 targets for 23 yards in the Raiders’ Week 2 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Brock Bowers missed his second game of the year while recovering from a mensicus trim procedure, giving Mayer another opportunity to start. He led the Raiders in routes but failed to make a big impact in the box score, logging a measly 14 percent target share. Mayer is generally in the TE2 mix when Bowers is out, but even then he isn’t a particularly high-upside option. With Bowers expected to return next week, Mayer can be sent back to the waiver wire on the upcoming waivers run.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Michael Mayer caught 6-of-7 targets for 32 yards in the Raiders’ Week 1 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Mayer was seemingly set for a sizable workload, going 3-of-3 for 21 yards on the Raiders’ first drive. He caught his fourth pass on the second drive, which was punched out and recovered by the Dolphins, but the play was overturned. For his part, Mayer looked good on short in-breakers and out routes, and his six receptions tie for a team-high. The Raiders simply got up to a 10-0 lead early in the second quarter and controlled the game thereafter, leaving the passing offense to take a backseat role to the Raiders’ ground game. Mayer can be started as a TE1 again next week against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Raiders signed TE Michael Mayer to a three-year, $45 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: The deal was first reported by NFL Insider Ian Rapoport. Mayer’s deal includes $30 million guaranteed and his $15 million average annual value is third among tight ends. The Raiders selected Mayer in the second-round (35th overall) of the 2023 NFL Draft. He had 300 yards as a rookie and the Raiders drafted Brock Bowers 13th overall the following year. Mayer is firmly on the fantasy radar for Week 1 against the Dolphins with Bowers (knee) sidelined, but his value is unstable as the Raiders’ second tight end.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: Raiders ruled out TE Brock Bowers (knee) for Week 1 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Earlier today, Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said he was initially optimistic that Bowers could play in Week 1, even after undergoing a recent meniscus trim, which is surprising. Kubiak, however, declined to discuss an updated return timeline for his star tight end. We do not yet know when he is expected back. In the meantime, Michael Mayer is a TE1 this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Raiders TE Michael Mayer’s “role now is expected to grow” with TE Brock Bowers (knee) sidelined.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Mayer, 25, immediately vaults into the TE1 tier, especially with a matchup against the Dolphins’ defense upcoming in Week 1. Mayer banked two top-five finishes last season, notably catching 9-of-10 targets for 89 yards in Week 17 with Bowers on injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Raiders TE Brock Bowers is expected to miss “a game or two” after undergoing a meniscus trim on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-ma.analysis: Raiders No. 2 TE Michael Mayer should be added wherever available. On the plus side, this does not appear to be a long-term absence, but missing Bowers for a couple of games is obviously concerning. According to Schefter, Bowers “got banged up ‘a little in camp’ and the injury was diagnosed last week.” With any luck, fantasy managers can expect to get their TE1 back for the Raiders’ Week 3 game against the Saints. Mayer is a TE1 in the meantime.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: Ken Walker had 19 rushes for 128 yards and two touchdowns in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers, adding two catches for 11 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: The Chiefs once again leaned hard on the rushing attack, running the ball 24 times while attempting 30 passes on the day. Walker breezed through a lifeless LA defense from start to finish. On many of his carries Walker was not touched until he was five or six yards beyond the line of scrimmage. Walker, who accounted for 19 of the team’s 24 rushing attempts, is perhaps the most important player in fantasy football through Week 6. He’ll be an RB1 in Week 7 against his former mates in Seattle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: Kenneth Walker rushed 22 times for 177 yards and two touchdowns in the Chiefs’ Week 4 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: Walker found the end zone twice in 19 seconds in this one. After scoring on a two-yard run in the fourth quarter, Walker then broke free for a 22-yard run on his next play after the Chiefs recovered a fumbled kickoff by the Raiders. Walker’s longest run of the game was an explosive burst down the right sideline that saw him pick up 76 yards, but he was tackled at the Raiders eight-yard line and lost out on a scoring opportunity two plays later when Tyquan Thornton came down in the end zone with an eight-yard reception. Walker has now scored multiple touchdowns in three of four games this season and has 621 yards from scrimmage and seven total touchdowns. He’s been more than fantasy managers could have hoped for through the first four weeks, but they will have to manage without him next week as the Chiefs enter their bye week. He’ll be firmly in the RB1 mix in Week 6, however, when the Chiefs play host to the winless Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: Kenneth Walker rushed 18 times for 70 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 3 win over the Dolphins, adding two receptions for three yards and a second score.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: The two-touchdown outing was Walker’s second in three games as a Chief after he had only one such effort for the Seahawks last season. His 20 touches were a rather remarkable total seeing as the Chiefs were limited to 49 plays with the Dolphins attempting to play keep away. He was not efficient, but Patrick Mahomes was. That’s the new reality for defenses facing the Chiefs, as this is no longer a stop Mahomes at all costs team. You now have to pick your poison, which is going to lead to many more blow-up efforts for KWIII. Perhaps that will include Week 4 in Vegas against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said RB Emmett Johnson “will continue to get more snaps.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: Johnson has turned 14 touches into 103 scrimmage yards thus far. Evidently pleased with his fifth-round rookie, Reid wants to keep “allowing Emmett to grow,” in turn taking “a little bit of load off” starting RB Kenneth Walker. Reid notes that Walker wants the ball on every play and is not asking for a lighter workload, but Reid is seeking “a nice balance with those two in there,” which “keeps them even more fresh as the season goes on.” Walker, of course, remains an elite RB1. Johnson, however, should be rostered in all 12-team leagues as a high-upside bench stash that could return standalone value before long.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: Kenneth Walker rushed 24 times for 117 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 2 win over the Colts, adding 61 yards on six receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: Walker has now notched 178 combined yards or more in each of his new team’s first two games to start the season. In addition to the gaudy yardage numbers, Walker saw 10 targets on 47 Patrick Mahomes pass attempts in the overtime victory, while accounting for all but four running back opportunities. His backfield opportunity share, touchdown equity, and pass game involvement make Walker a top-tier fantasy asset for those that invested a second-round pick in his services this offseason. The only micro-blemish on his record against the Colts was a sequence of carries at the end of the second quarter in which he was stuffed from the one-yard line on three straight plays, with the team eventually scoring on fourth down via a touchdown pass to Xavier Worthy. Walker remains a top-tier RB1 ahead of a road date with the much more forgiving Dolphins in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: Kenneth Walker rushed 23 times for 173 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 1 win over the Broncos, adding 18 yards and a touchdown on three receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: Walker single-handedly out-gained the entire Denver offense on the evening as he was the clear point of emphasis in Patrick Mahomes’ first game back after tearing his ACL in 2025. He was fed seven carries on the team’s first nine offensive plays run from scrimmage, a drive that would result in a 15-yard Mahomes rushing touchdown on the team’s first possession. The highlight of the game for the explosive back was a 60-yard touchdown run on fourth-and-one, in which he bounced the football outside and dusted the secondary on his way to the end zone. He would add a receiving score on a “Kansas City Special” later in the game, taking a Mahomes shuttle pass to the end zone from two yards out to further bolster his counting stats. What’s more, walker played all but five offensive snaps in the first half with the game still within reason, highlighting a massive ceiling for the remainder of the season. Walker is a locked-in RB1 ahead of a Week 2 matchup against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: The Athletic’s Jesse Newell reports the Chiefs view Kenneth Walker as a potential three-down back.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: What is clear in the wake of the Chiefs waiving Emari Demercado is that they don’t really have another player that qualifies as a passing-down back besides Walker without squinting. The other backs they kept are Emmett Johnson, a Day 3 rookie, and Brashard Smith, a gadget player without enough size to really block. Perhaps the Chiefs will address this in street free agency ahead of the season, but as things stand, it certainly seems like Walker will be involved on all three downs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: ESPN’s Nate Taylor reports that the Chiefs are counting on RB Kenneth Walker to help build a “more potent offense” this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: Chiefs coach Andy Reid and QB Patrick Mahomes believe last season’s run game failed to make defenses respect their play-action run fakes. With Walker now on board, the Chiefs believe both the run game and play-action game will improve. The staff has catered to Walker by installing more plays from under center, which Walker prefers to shotgun. “One way Walker can help transform the offense,” per Taylor, “is by becoming a true dual-threat player.” Reid believes Walker’s “receiving skills and ability to make defenders miss” will allow Reid to incorporate “one of his favorite passing concepts: the variety of plays where a play-action fake to the running back is executed before a short screen pass is thrown back to the same running back.” Walker should be expected to handle a high-end, dual-threat workload. He is a locked-in RB1 with immense upside.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: Chiefs coach Andy Reid said Kenneth Walker’s shoe caused some swelling around his ankle, but he will be fine.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: Walker was held out of practice recently because of the issue, but this seems to be as minor as it gets. It’s safe to assume Walker will be back at practice soon, likely without any limitations. Walker has been going at the top of the second round of fantasy drafts. This little injury scare shouldn’t move that ADP in the slightest. He remains a strong RB1 bet this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.headline: Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker (foot) is not participating in practice on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-wa.analysis: This probably isn’t a major cause for concern — if you’ve ever drafted Kenneth Walker before, you know he misses plenty of practice time — the Chiefs are likely just taking it easy on the man expected to be their bellcow back this season. But the more practice he misses, the more serious we’ll take it. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 23-of-30 attempts for 272 yards and one interception in the Chiefs’ Week 6 win against the Chargers, adding five rushes for 16 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Mahomes had multiple touchdown tosses in every game this season headed into Week 6. Kansas City’s offense didn’t have to do much against a sleepy Chargers offense that could barely move the ball once again on Sunday. The Chiefs leaned on Ken Walker, who went for 128 yards and two touchdowns on the day. With Rashee Rice and Tyquan Thornton out, Mahomes relied heavily on Xavier Worthy and Travis Kelce. Until Rice is back and fully healthy, Mahomes will be more of a top-15 option. He gets the Seahawks in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 15-of-30 passes for 225 yards and two touchdowns in the Chiefs’ 30-27, Week 4 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Mahomes was under duress throughout this one. He took multiple hits and was sacked twice, but managed to come up with just enough plays to pull off the road win against a spry Raiders team. Mahomes threw his first touchdown of the day in the first quarter, finding Tyquan Thornton for a two-yard score, then connected with Thornton again in the fourth quarter for an eight-yard touchdown near the back of the end zone. Mahomes’ longest play of the game also went to Thornton, when the speedster broke free down the left sideline to make a 55-yard catch. Unfortunately, Thornton exited the game with a gruesome ankle injury after the play, but he did set up Kenneth Walker for a two-yard touchdown run on the ensuing play. Mahomes and the Chiefs are now 4-0 as they enter their Week 5 bye week. They’ll play host to the Chargers, who are 0-4 when they return in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 20-of-24 passes for 246 yards, two touchdowns and an interception in the Chiefs’ 24-10, Week 3 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: With the Dolphins playing ball-control offense, the Chiefs were limited to just 49 total plays, but Mahomes and company compensated with extreme efficiency. That included long catch-and-run gains to Travis Kelce and Rashee Rice, with Mahomes also finding the former for an end zone score. Mahomes has now posted multiple passing scores in each of his first three starts. It took him seven games to accomplish that feat last year. There was a scary moment when Mahomes got “body weighted” by DL Chop Robinson, but Mahomes shook it off as Robinson was flagged for roughing. Currently averaging 8.3 yards per attempt after that number was 7.1 a year ago, Mahomes is looking at home in this “new look” Chiefs attack once again coordinated by Eric Bieniemy. He has another soft Week 4 matchup in the Raiders before the Chiefs head on early-season bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 32-of-47 passes for 382 yards and three touchdowns in the Chiefs’ 33-30, Week 2 win over the Colts, adding 17 yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Mahomes looked much more like himself against the Colts than he did against the Broncos in Week 1, with his typical mobility in the pocket on full display as he extended plays. He even escaped the pocket twice to pick up crucial first downs with his legs in key situations, looking closer to how he did before tearing his ACL in 2025. Mahomes managed to complete two passes greater than 30 yards, one to Tyquan Thornton and one to Rashee Rice, an area of his game that he has not excelled in over the previous two seasons. Even so, it took the Chiefs two possessions in overtime to finally sneak by the tenacious Colts, moving to a 2-0 record ahead of a road date with the Dolphins in Week 3. Mahomes has returned to weekly QB1 status, although the team could look to continue its dominance on the ground against a week opponent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes (knee) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Mahomes ran the ball seven times for 23 yards and one touchdown last week before practicing in full this week. Both factors are encouraging. The Chiefs’ star quarterback warrants QB1 treatment against the Colts in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes (knee) is practicing in full for Week 2 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Rashee Rice (knee) is also practicing in full. Both players underwent offseason knee procedures and had slow ramp-ups during the summer. Both players were active for Week 1 and found the end zone. Mahomes did so on the ground, putting the notion that he would be hampered by the knee issue to rest. The passing attack still looked shaky in Week 1, but there are no health concerns for either player. Mahomes will be a low-end QB1 versus the Colts, and Rice will hold a spot in the WR2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Patrick Mahomes completed 15-of-27 passes for 184 yards, two touchdowns, and one interceptions in the Chiefs’ 31-10, Week 1 win over the Broncos, adding 23 yards and a touchdown on seven carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: A rushing score on the team’s first possession appeared to calm fantasy owners’ nerves as that was the area of Mahomes’ game most in question coming off the injury, but concerns grew as he completed just two of his first 12 pass attempts in his first start since suffering a torn ACL in 2025. A passing score to Rashee Rice at the end of the first half elevated his counting stats further before a shuttle pass touchdown to Kenneth Walker after the break took him into fantasy QB1 territory. Even so, the outing was far from perfect as Mahomes missed numerous open receivers on his way to a paltry 6.8 yards per pass attempt. Mahomes’ lone interception was a badly overthrown ball on a miscommunication in the third quarter that could have been much more damning had the Kansas City defense not held the Broncos to a field goal on the resulting possession. With games against the Colts, Dolphins, and Raiders on tap the next three weeks, the Chiefs could continue to lean on Walker after the recent addition out-gained the entire Denver offense by himself in Week 1. Mahomes will be difficult to trust until he proves to be more accurate through the air.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes (knee) is practicing in full for Week 1 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Earlier this week, Chiefs coach Andy Reid said there is a “good chance” that Mahomes starts in Week 1. At this point, we would be surprised if he didn’t. The Chiefs’ quarterback is coming off season-ending ACL and LCL tears and will likely scramble less frequently than he did last year, potentially hurting his expected fantasy football output. He is a borderline QB1/2 against the Broncos’ elite defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said “there’s a good chance” Patrick Mahomes will start Week 1’s game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: We would be very surprised if Mahomes didn’t start Week 1 given how this has trended this offseason, but Reid left it in some doubt, adding “Most likely, he’ll be the guy that’s out there.” Justin Fields would be the starter if Mahomes couldn’t go, we doubt we’ll be talking about that possibility seriously on Friday or Saturday ahead of Kansas City’s MNF opener.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.headline: ESPN’s Nate Taylor reports that the Chiefs are counting on RB Kenneth Walker to help build a “more potent offense” this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/patrick-ma.analysis: Chiefs coach Andy Reid and QB Patrick Mahomes believe last season’s run game failed to make defenses respect their play-action run fakes. With Walker now on board, the Chiefs believe both the run game and play-action game will improve. The staff has catered to Walker by installing more plays from under center, which Walker prefers to shotgun. “One way Walker can help transform the offense,” per Taylor, “is by becoming a true dual-threat player.” Reid believes Walker’s “receiving skills and ability to make defenders miss” will allow Reid to incorporate “one of his favorite passing concepts: the variety of plays where a play-action fake to the running back is executed before a short screen pass is thrown back to the same running back.” Walker should be expected to handle a high-end, dual-threat workload. He is a locked-in RB1 with immense upside.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: Khalil Shakir caught 4-of-6 targets for 34 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 6 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: Shakir didn’t have an overly productive day through the air in this one, but he did manage to find the end zone for his first touchdown of the season. Shakir scored on a nine-yard screen pass in the second quarter to put the Bills up 13-7. Shakir has now gone for double-digit PPR points in three straight games but will be hard to trust as anything more than a WR4/WR5 in Week 8 when the Bills return from their bye to face the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: Khalil Shakir caught all three targets for 80 yards in the Bills’ Week 5 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: Shakir’s modest target total was primarily a product of a ground-heavy approach from the Bills, who were playing without both DJ Moore and Joshua Palmer. His quiet fantasy outing was quickly remedied through a 57-yard, catch-and-run reception on the team’s second possession of overtime to set up the game-winning, Tyler Bass field goal. Shakir remains a shaky fantasy bet ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: Khalil Shakir caught 7-of-8 targets for 82 yards and a fumble in the Bills’ Week 4 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: Shakir served as Josh Allen’s safety blanket for much of the first half, but he was quiet for much of the second half. Most of his production came on a 51-yard catch-and-run, where he broke a few tackles and got the Bills into the red zone. On another catch-and-run opportunity, he had the ball punched out by two Patriots defenders for a crucial fumble. Shakir and Allen were also not on the same page on a key third-down pass that led to a punt. The Bills are going to need more from Shakir if DJ Moore (Shoulder) misses any time, but Shakir did play the second-most snaps of any receiver and ran the most routes, so his role is still there.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: Khalil Shakir caught 1-of-3 targets for six yards in the Bills’ Week 3 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: The Bills’ offense was totally out of sorts in this game, and Shakir was hurt by their inability to get anything going through the air. Still, he played on 45 of their 62 snaps and ran a route on 23 of their 33 dropbacks, the second-most of any wide receiver. He’ll be in for a better game against the Patriots next week, but he remains just a desperation FLEX play right now unless the Bills are headed for a shootout.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: Khalil Shakir caught 3-of-6 targets for 38 yards in the Bills’ Week 2 win over the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: Shakir continued in a gadgety role for the Bills, primarily working the short areas of the field in addition to receiving snaps out of the backfield. That could change in the immediate future after lead receiver DJ Moore departed in the second quarter with what appeared to be a significant shoulder injury. Even so, Shakir is best left on the waiver wire in all but the deepest fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: Khalil Shakir caught 4-of-6 targets for 50 yards in Buffalo’s Week 1 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: The good news is he was healthy enough to play after he was seemingly sidelined towards the end of training camp with something the Bills never disclosed. He played 30-of-57 snaps. The bad news is that if Dalton Kincaid is going to be this involved, it’s not likely that Shakir will be targeted enough to crack the WR3 ranks. A lot can change — and Kincaid isn’t known for his durability — but it was a “meh” debut for Shakir as he fell behind Kincaid and DJ Moore in the passing pecking order.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: The Athletic’s Joe Buscaglia reports that Bills WR Khalil Shakir (undisclosed) is on the practice field on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: This is good news. Shakir has been sidelined for multiple weeks, rehabbing an undisclosed injury. His return today puts him on track to play in Week 1 against the Texans’ top-tier defense. Whether Shakir can be a reliable FLEX with WR DJ Moore now in Buffalo and TE Dalton Kincaid reportedly set to take on a larger role remains to be seen. Getting back on the field is the first step, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports “there’s currently optimism” from the Bills that Khalil Shakir will play in Week 1 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: Shakir has been held out of practice for multiple weeks with an undisclosed injury. He has gotten some work off to the side, though it’s becoming more concerning with each day he fails to work in with the team. According to Zenitz, the team is simply being cautious with Shakir. We’ll learn more about his ailment when the first official injury report comes out next week. Like the Bills, fantasy managers should take a cautious approach with Shakir in the final week of drafts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: Khalil Shakir (undisclosed) did not practice on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: Neither did Ty Johnson (knee), with both players still having plenty of time to get back before next Sunday’s Week 1 game against the Texans.
