It’s hard to tell how seriously to take these because Joe Brady has been a brick wall on injury questions, but we’ll get a better indication next week when injury reports start to hit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.headline: Khalil Shakir has been sidelined from Bills practice this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/khalil-sha.analysis: Shakir was sidelined from Tuesday’s special practice at Highmark Stadium and hasn’t suited up since. Coach Joe Brady did not divulge the nature of the injury. Like most ailments this time of year, it’s probably a minor issue where the team is opting for caution, but it’s good to “timestamp” these things, so to speak. Barely going in the WR5 range, 26-year-old Shakir could easily outproduce his ADP, though probably not to the extent he cracks the top 36.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.headline: Trey McBride caught 7-of-9 targets for 53 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 6 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.analysis: McBride’s first target ended up being a Quentin Lake interception, but Jacoby Brissett went right back to his star tight end on the following drive. McBride made a contested catch on a quick in route, spun off contact and took off downfield for a 26-yard gain. McBride’s day largely consisted of out routes and catches in the flats after that, but he was given two opportunities to score a touchdown from inside the Rams’ 25-yard line on the Cardinals’ seventh drive. On 2nd-and-1 from the Rams’ 21-yard line, McBride caught a pass in the flats and rumbled through contact for a short first-down gain. Three plays later, on 3rd-and-goal from the Rams’ seven-yard line, Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur dialed up a screen pass for him, but the Rams blew it up, resulting in a yardage loss. It wasn’t McBride biggest outing, but a 7/53 is hardly unusable. McBride remains an elite TE1 against the Broncos next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.headline: ArizonaCardinals.com’s Darren Urban believes Carson Beck won’t start in the “immediate future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.analysis: Cardinals fans appear to be pining for the team to bench Jacoby Brissett and start the rookie in the coming weeks as another season circles the drain for Arizona. Beck so far has been the Cards’ emergency third quarterback. Urban said there remains a “chance Beck is made the backup this week or next and allow him to come on in relief if the situation presents itself. I don’t see Beck starting in the immediate future, but it does feel his time grows closer, and if the offense continues to sputter, that would be understandable.” Brissett this season ranks 15th in passing yards. He’s thrown nine touchdowns to five interceptions and ranks 30th out of 37 qualifying QBs in adjusted yards per attempt. He won’t be a viable fantasy play this week against a tough Rams coverage unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.headline: Trey McBride caught 9-of-10 targets for 66 yards and one touchdown in the Cardinals’ Week 5 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.analysis: McBride looked like his normal, dominant self, carving up defenders on out routes and in-breakers. Unfortunately, hearts were also broken when Jacoby Brissett fired a touchdown pass right past McBride, running wide open inside the Lions’ five-yard line, to backup TE Teagan Quitoriano, also running wide open in the back of the end zone. Fortunately, McBride was able to haul in a juggling, falling and contested touchdown catch late in the fourth quarter to boost his final stat line. McBride is an elite TE1 against the Rams next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.headline: Trey McBride caught 7-of-12 targets for 31 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 4 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.analysis: It was another compiling-based statistical performance for the Cardinals’ dominant seam stretcher, but the PPR check clears all the same. Amazingly, seven catches were actually a new season low. McBride is going to keep stacking volume efforts, but he has now been out-targeted 30-23 by Michael Wilson over the past two weeks, not that a single soul is concerned about 23 targets in two games. Potentially more concerning is the negative chatter arising around Jacoby Brissett’s play. Either way, McBride has a Week 5 smash spot in the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.headline: Trey McBride caught 9-of-11 targets for 75 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 3 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.analysis: McBride had a big receiving day, though penalties prevented it from being more productive. His first reception was called back due to offensive pass interference while he drew defensive pass interference in the endzone on a 4th-and-1 play. He continues to be the Cardinals’ most effective target on immediate routes, slashing through the 49ers defense for 75 yards. Not much more nuance is needed here, McBride is a fantasy TE1 for Week 4 against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.headline: Trey McBride caught 8-of-10 targets for 41 yards and one touchdown in the Cardinals’ Week 2 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.analysis: McBride is unbelievably good at getting open on short-to-intermediate crossers and out routes. Even the Seahawks’ elite defense had trouble capping his receptions total, although they did prevent him from producing a double-digit gain. McBride’s second-quarter touchdown pulled the Cardinals even with the Seahawks, 7-7. It was a daring, smart call by coach Mike LaFleur, who called McBride’s number via a short out route on 4th-and-goal from the Seahawks’ three-yard line. McBride remains an elite TE1 against the 49ers next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.headline: Cardinals TE Trey McBride (rest/back) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 2 against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.analysis: McBride is good to go for the Cardinals’ matchup against the Seahawks and can be treated as a shoo-in TE1, per usual. The Seahawks are without S Ty Okada (hamstring), theoretically making life a little easier for McBride. Fellow S Nick Emmanwori (hip/ankle) is questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.headline: Cardinals TE Trey McBride (rest/back) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.analysis: McBride should be considered good to go for the Cardinals’ Week 2 game against the Seahawks. It took a while for the team to let us know what was going on yesterday. Although there is something at play here with the back listing, the fact that the team labeled it a rest day is great to see. He’s an elite TE1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.headline: Cardinals TE Trey McBride (rest/back) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.analysis: No need to panic after McBride was seen working off to the side Wednesday; the Cardinals listed him as DNP with a rest/back designation. Despite the back being added to the designation, it does not seem like a serious injury worry with the Cardinals also giving him the “resting player” tag. This reads as a rest day for McBride. He is still good to go for Week 2 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.headline: Cardinals TE Trey McBride was seen working off to the side on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trey-mcbri.analysis: This could simply be a veteran rest day after the 26-year-old tight end posted a 9/95/1 receiving line against the Chargers in Week 1. Teams frequently allow star players to sit out during the week’s first official practice. The official injury report should come out soon. Until then, there is no reason to panic.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid caught 7-of-8 targets for 38 yards in the Bills’ Week 6 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid did nearly all of his damage in the short area of the field, but his fantasy managers will take any kind of volume they can get after a three-week stretch where Kincaid saw a dismal seven combined targets. Kincaid’s eight targets led all Bills pass-catchers in this one, and were it not for an 18-yard touchdown taken off the board by a holding penalty, he could have been in line for a much bigger day. It’s far too early to say that Kincaid is “back,” but fantasy managers can at least be happy with a decent day of production. The Bills are now entering their bye week, but Kincaid will be boom-or-bust TE1 in Week 8 against the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid (ribs) returned in the fourth quarter of Week 6’s game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: With the game tied at 23-23, Kincaid returned to the field with the Bills attempting to take the lead. Whatever he’s dealing with appears to be minor at this point, so he’ll likely attempt to gut out the remainder if this one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid (ribs) is questionable to return in Week 6’s game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid exited in the third quarter and went to the blue medical tent before eventually heading for the locker room. Kincaid could be seen holding his ribs while running a route earlier in the game and was in the midst of a good performance. We will check back in with any updates we receive.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid caught 1-of-2 targets for seven yards in the Bills’ Week 5 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: The Bills clearly came into this one intent on establishing the run, attempting 37 rushes to just 19 Josh Allen pass attempts in a game played without both DJ Moore and Joshua Palmer. Kincaid has now seen three or fewer targets in each of his last three games after erupting for 225 yards through the air in the first two weeks. The ceiling was never in question, but fantasy managers have to be reeling after three consecutive down performances for the enigmatic tight end. Kincaid remains an upside TE1 ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Bills head coach Joe Brady said he wants to find a way to get more targets for Dalton Kincaid.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid had just two targets in Sunday’s loss to the Patriots after seeing three looks last week against the Chargers. He’s cooled off considerably after a hot start to the 2026 season. “There’s no reason Dalton Kincaid should have two targets, especially with the flow of the game and how that goes,” a visibly frustrated Brady said after Buffalo’s Week 4 loss. “Gotta find a way to get the ball in his hands and do a better job of that.” Against the Patriots Kincaid was targeted on just 8 percent of his routes. He’ll look to bounce back next week against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid caught 1-of-2 targets for seven yards in the Bills’ Week 4 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: The Bills’ offense was struggling to move the ball during this game, and DJ Moore left early with a shoulder injury, so it’s almost inexcusable that Kincaid wasn’t used more often. Kincaid played one fewer snap than Dawson Knox but ran 22 routes to Knox’s 10. Still, Josh Allen dropped back to throw 40 times, and Khalil Shakir ran a route on 34 dropbacks, so there is no reason for Kincaid to run 12 fewer than that over the whole game. He ran fewer routes than Josh Palmer and only six more routes than Moore, who only played one and a half quarters. The Bills will need to find a way to get Kincaid back into their plans before Monday night’s game against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid caught 2-of-3 passes for 38 yards and a fumble in the Bills’ Week 3 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid almost had another big catch over the middle of the field for another 15 or more yards, but he was lit up by a safety and dropped the ball at the end of the play. It was the type of hit where you’re just happy that he wound up healthy and able to stay in the game. The 26-year-old later made a nice catch and broke three tackles as he moved closer to the Chargers’ end zone, but the ball was poked out from behind by a chasing defender. Kincaid still ran the second-most routes of any receiver on the Bills and remains a TE1 in fantasy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid caught 7-of-8 targets for 95 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 2 win over the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid truly did it all in this one, routinely in the middle of the blocking scrum on long James Cook runs in addition to his work through the air. His 95 yards handily paced the team, with his first touchdown of the young season coming from 16 yards out near the end of the second quarter. Kincaid remains one of the most efficient pass-catchers in the league on a per-route basis and has worked his way into the upper echelon of fantasy assets at the position. He remains a locked-in TE1 when the Bills host the Jets in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler said there are no snap restrictions for Dalton Kincaid this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid, according to Fowler, “could be the real key to elevating Josh Allen and the Buffalo offense this season.” Fowler added “multiple people with the team told me Kincaid is healthier than he was this time last year and is on no snap restrictions.” This is further confirmation that Kincaid won’t see the highly restrictive usage of the Sean McDermott era in Buffalo. Head coach Joe Brady is keen on using Kincaid both as an intermediate threat and a downfield option. Kincaid in Week 1 against the Texans led all tight ends in air yards (94) and ran a route on nearly 70 percent of the Bills’ drop backs. He could be an elite every-week option going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.headline: Dalton Kincaid caught 5-of-6 targets for 130 yards in Buffalo’s Week 1 win over the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dalton-kin.analysis: Kincaid was the recipient of many of Josh Allen’s biggest throws of the game, including a 35-yarder to put him over 100 yards on Buffalo’s final non-kneeldown drive. Kincaid played 42-of-57 snaps, a 73 percent rate he never came close to hitting in any game last year. It sure seems like there’s no reason for the Bills to not target him if he can stay healthy; so it will be hard to not recommend him as a TE1 against the Lions on TNF.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman caught 4-of-6 targets for 59 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 6 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman’s six targets tied for second-most on the Bills with Khalil Shakir, who also found the end zone in this one. Coleman scored on an impressive 12-yard play by Josh Allen, who appeared ready to take off and run with the ball before spotting Coleman open in the end zone and flipping a shovel pass to him for the score. Coleman has now scored in three straight games and has been targeted six or more times in two of his last three. With the Bills now heading into their Week 7 bye, Coleman could face more target competition when they return in Week 8 against the Ravens if DJ Moore (shoulder) is active. Moore was questionable entering this week and ruled out 90 minutes before kickoff, so it wouldn’t be surprising if he was a full-go after the bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman caught 1-of-2 targets for seven yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 5 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman was largely erased by the lockdown corner play of the Rams but had a receiving line also heavily influenced by a ground-heavy game plan from a Bills team that attempted only 19 passes in almost 70 minutes of football. It was quite the letdown fantasy performance for managers looking to take advantage of the absences of both DJ Moore and Joshua Palmer. Coleman is a borderline FLEX play in Week 6 against the Raiders, pending the status of Moore.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Joshua Palmer (shoulder) was added to the injury report on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Palmer seemingly injured his shoulder in practice today. The Bills may already be without WR DJ Moore (shoulder) on Monday night. While Palmer is not relevant in 12-team leagues, his potential absence would improve Keon Coleman’s stock.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 5 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman should be good to go for the Bills’ Monday Night Football game against the Rams this week. He had a career day in Week 4, with a 6/116/1 receiving line. We have seen Coleman produce solid outings in the past, so caution is advised if one is to consider believing the hype. That said, he rose to the occasion last week and could do so again in what should be a high-scoring game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman caught 6-of-7 targets for 116 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 4 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: This was the best game we’ve seen from Coleman in a long time. Not only did he show up in the box score, but two of his catches were unbelievable sideline grabs that showed the type of hands that made him an intriguing draft pick out of Florida State. He played on 46 of the team’s 59 snaps and ran a route on 31 of their 40 dropbacks. With D.J. Moore leaving this game with a shoulder injury, Coleman is a priority add on waiver wires before next week’s game against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said WR Keon Coleman (ankle) “should be good to play” for Buffalo’s Week 4 game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman was limited on Thursday after a Wednesday DNP and apparently will avoid a questionable tag. He was questionable last week and played through the injury, though he doesn’t draw enough targets to be fantasy-relevant outside of the deepest leagues at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman missed two practices last week before getting in a limited session on Friday. He still suited up and caught one of his two targets for a 37-yard gain. He will likely see a very limited number of reps in practice again this week. Coleman is not on the fantasy radar for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman caught 1-of-2 targets for 37 yards in the Bills’ Week 3 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman was questionable to play with an ankle injury, but he was out there for 32 of the team’s 66 snaps, which was the third-most among wide receivers. His lone catch was a busted coverage down the sideline where a better throw from Josh Allen could have led to a touchdown. Coleman is playing better football this season, but he remains just an end-of-bench flyer if either DJ Moore or Khalil Shakir were to suffer an injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Keon Coleman (ankle) is active for Week 3 against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Coleman was iffy headed into the weekend with an ankle injury he sustained last week against the Lions. Last week Coleman caught all six of his targets for 63 yards with DJ Moore sidelined with a shoulder issue. Moore is active for Week 3, meaning Coleman should remain on fantasy benches for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.headline: Bills declared WR Skyler Bell, OL Jude Bowry, OL Ar’maj Reed-Adams, DL T.J. Sanders, OLB Mike Danna, and S Jalon Kilgore inactive for Week 3 against the Chargers
https://www.nbcsports.com/keon-coleman/0.analysis: Both DJ Moore (shoulder) and Keon Coleman (ankle) were listed as questionable on the final injury report, but both of them will suit up to play. There’s a chance that they could have their snap share managed as they play through injuries, but we’d have to assume they’re both relatively healthy if the Bills are going to put both of them on the field in an early-season matchup. You may just see a little more Khalil Shakir and Josh Palmer usage than normal. Moore remains the receiver with the most fantasy upside and could be a low-end WR2 with Shakir also being a solid WR3 in PPR formats given his role as a lower aDOT target-earner.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.headline: Kendrick Bourne caught 5-of-8 targets for 47 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 6 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.analysis: Bourne got going with a 15-yard catch-and-run on the Cardinals’ third drive. He earned a third-down end zone target from the Rams’ three-yard line, running an out route just inside the goal line, but he was unable to secure the pass, resulting in a close incompletion. He later bagged a tight-window catch on the Cardinals’ first drive after halftime, helping the offense down the field for one of their six field goal drives. The crafty veteran remains a PPR FLEX starter against the Broncos next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.headline: Kendrick Bourne caught 5-of-8 targets for 70 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 5 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.analysis: Bourne looks like a viable FLEX starter for those in need. His 70 receiving yards were a team high, and his eight targets trailed only Trey McBride (10). The journeyman receiver delivered two 20-plus-yard gains via post routes, the first coming on the Cardinals’ first drive and the second on the seventh. Jacoby Brissett tried to force another downfield shot to Bourne on the latter drive, but it didn’t work out. Bourne is running high-value routes in the center of the field, playing for a garbage-time team with a cannon-armed quarterback. The results could be volatile at times, but he is worth starting in the FLEX against the Rams next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.headline: Kendrick Bourne caught 2-of-3 targets for 22 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 3 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.analysis: Bourne operated as the Cardinals’ No. 3 wide receiver, seeing just three targets in a high-volume passing day. The team’s pass-catching hierarchy seems to have settled in, with Michael Wilson and Marvin Harrison operating as the top wide receivers and Trey McBride the top tight end. Bourne will get some looks behind this group but won’t be fantasy relevant without an injury ahead of him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.headline: Kendrick Bourne caught 2-of-3 targets for 11 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 2 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.analysis: Bourne earned his first target on the Cardinals’ fourth drive. The throw was a tad late, and Bourne’s hesitated while running his route, so the pass glanced off his hands in the flats. He caught the next two, but barely cleared double-digit yardage. Bourne does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.headline: Kendrick Bourne caught all eight of his targets for 75 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 1 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.analysis: Bourne led all Arizona wideouts in targets, catches, and yards. He ran a route on 82 percent of Cardinals dropbacks. Jacoby Brissett found Bourne in the short and intermediate areas throughout the first half — averaging a meager five air yards per target — while Michael Wilson and Marvin Harrison Jr. worked mainly downfield. Bourne could be an interesting waiver add this week in deeper PPR formats if his usage keeps up.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.headline: Cardinals agreed to terms with WR Kendrick Bourne, formerly of the 49ers, on a two-year, $10 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.analysis: The deal has a max value of $12 million. Bourne has been a consistent depth receiver throughout his career, most recently catching 37 passes for 551 yards for the 49ers in 2025. He has cracked 500 yards three times in nine seasons, profiling best as WR3 or lower on the depth chart. He’ll be exactly that for the Cardinals, who are fortifying the pass-catchers behind Marvin Harrison Jr. and Michael Wilson as they figure out their quarterback plans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.headline: Kendrick Bourne failed to catch either of his two targets in San Francisco’s Divisional Round loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.analysis: Bourne went for 142 yards in Week 4, 142 yards in Week 5, and 180 yards from Weeks 7-18. It was a fun ride. Bourne enters free agency as a respectable outside depth receiver, but he hasn’t cracked 600 yards since 2021 and will need extreme circumstances to be fantasy-relevant going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.headline: Demarcus Robinson caught 3-of-4 targets for 24 yards in San Francisco’s Week 18 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.analysis: He played 37-of-42 snaps and out-targeted Kendrick Bourne four to one in San Francisco’s finale. Assuming Ricky Pearsall is able to play in the Wild Card round, this won’t matter much. But it is worth noting that Robinson could be the DFS punt we’re interested in — rather than Bourne — if Pearsall is sidelined again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.headline: Demarcus Robinson caught both targets for 23 yards and a touchdown in the 49ers’ Week 16 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.analysis: The offense was focused heavily on George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey throughout, likely invoked by the heavy Cover-3 rates of the Indianapolis defense in the absence of Sauce Gardner. Robinson snuck in an early touchdown as the two teams traded blows in the first half before disappearing into irrelevancy once more. Fellow role-playing wide receiver Kendrick Bourne caught 3-of-5 targets for 27 yards while playing more offensive snaps than Robinson, earning a sizable $500,000 bonus for going over 500 yards on the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.headline: Kendrick Bourne caught his only target for 19 yards in the 49ers’ Week 10 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendrick-b.analysis: We miss the Mac Jones/Kendrick Bourne friendship. Since going for exactly 142 yards in back-to-back games in Week 5 and Week 6, Bourne has managed a total of 111 yards in four games, with just nine targets. If you were holding on to him hoping that Mac Jones would eventually get back to his main man, you can let go of those dreams. It looks like it will take injuries to make that happen again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson caught 4-of-7 targets for 32 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 6 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Wilson’s day would have looked a lot different if a would-be 36-yard touchdown pass from Jacoby Brissett had not glanced off Wilson’s fingertips while he dove for it in the end zone. He had another 30-yarder go off his hands on the following drive, and had a five-yard catch overturned by a penalty. The disappointing box score results could allow fantasy managers to send a successful buy-low offer. Wilson is a WR2/3 next week against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: ArizonaCardinals.com’s Darren Urban believes Carson Beck won’t start in the “immediate future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Cardinals fans appear to be pining for the team to bench Jacoby Brissett and start the rookie in the coming weeks as another season circles the drain for Arizona. Beck so far has been the Cards’ emergency third quarterback. Urban said there remains a “chance Beck is made the backup this week or next and allow him to come on in relief if the situation presents itself. I don’t see Beck starting in the immediate future, but it does feel his time grows closer, and if the offense continues to sputter, that would be understandable.” Brissett this season ranks 15th in passing yards. He’s thrown nine touchdowns to five interceptions and ranks 30th out of 37 qualifying QBs in adjusted yards per attempt. He won’t be a viable fantasy play this week against a tough Rams coverage unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson caught 4-of-7 targets for 30 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 5 loss to the Lions, adding one pass for seven yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Wilson almost scored a passing touchdown via an end-around trick play on the Cardinals’ opening drive, but his receiver, Jacoby Brissett, was stopped two yards shy of the end zone. Heartbreak struck again two drives later, when Wilson only got one foot in bounds along the sideline on a would-be 19-yard catch. Brissett went right back to him on the following play, but the contested pass edged past Wilson’s outstretched hands. Wilson tacked on a couple of short gains before snagging a 17-yard pass on the Cardinals’ ninth drive, and he nearly bagged a 47-yard touchdown down the left sideline on the 10th drive, but his coverage defender effectively contested it, resulting in an incompletion. Wilson should handle a WR2-level workload against the Rams in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson caught 7-of-13 targets for 95 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 4 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Wilson is now up to a staggering 30 targets over the past two weeks after that number was “just” 14 across Weeks 1 and 2. He is managing to drew more looks than one of the biggest target sponges in the league Trey McBride, though the seam man still has 23 targets the past two weeks. Wilson and McBride have turned this offense into a two-man affair, with No. 3 Marvin Harrison Jr. now a distant role player. That’s all good and well in fantasy for the time being, but Jacoby Brissett has quietly been amongst the most ineffective QBs in the league. The rebuilding Birds may decide to get a look at Carson Beck sooner rather than later. Either way, that won’t be before next week’s potential shootout with the Lions. Wilson is now a weekly WR3 pushing for top-24 status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson caught 11-of-17 targets for 89 yards and a touchdown in the Cardinals’ Week 3 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Wilson saw season-highs across the board as the Cardinals played catch-up against the 49ers for much of the day. He operated as the team’s No. 1 wide receiver, seeing over three times the opportunities as Marvin Harrison Jr. Catching much of the outside passes and intermediate crossers for the day, Wilson scored on a five-yard Jacoby Brissett pass in the third quarter. It’s clear he is Brissett’s top target in the offense, especially when the team is playing from behind. Wilson ranks as a high-end fantasy WR3 heading into Week 4 against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson caught 2-of-7 targets for 18 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 2 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Wilson had a brutal day. The Seahawks prevented two receptions by committing defensive pass interference, and QB Jacoby Brissett prevented at least two more with a pair of overthrows. One led to an interception. The other led to a dropped interception. Wilson remains WR3/FLEX-viable against the 49ers in Week 3, coming off consecutive seven-target games. He is stuck in a tough situation, but the opportunities to score fantasy points should be there next week. Not every defense is as well-designed and talented as Seattle’s.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Michael Wilson caught 5-of-7 targets for 56 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 1 win against the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Wilson nearly came down with a couple deep shots from Jacoby Brissett. He was clearly favored — as he was last season — over Marvin Harrison, Jr., who ended the game with just one grab for 33 yards. Wilson, who signed a huge contract extension with the Cards before the season opener, has a good shot of operating as Arizona’s No. 1 wideout this season. Brissett’s willingness to go downfield even against tight coverage will give Wilson weekly chances to emerge as a matchup-tilting wideout in fantasy football. Wilson will be a WR3 play in Week 2 against a tough Seattle secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: Cardinals signed Michael Wilson to a three-year, $75 million extension through 2029.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Per ESPN’s Adam Schefter, the deal includes $47 million in guarantees, with a max value of $78 million. Wilson was set to enter a contract season in a week. Instead, he’ll be under contract with Arizona through the 2029 season. He broke out in the second half of the 2025 season and finished the year with his first 1,000-yard campaign. He compiled 775 of those yards in the final eight games of the year. Even if he can’t replicate those numbers over 17 weeks, Wilson took a massive step forward, and receivers aren’t cheap on the open market. It makes sense for Arizona to lock him up long-term instead of letting him test the waters of free agency next offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: ESPN’s Josh Weinfuss reports “there’s been movement on Michael Wilson’s negotiations with the Cardinals.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Weinfuss adds that “something could come down in the next day or so.” Wilson has been in line for an extension this offseason and despite an effort, the Cardinals have yet to reach an agreement. It seems the sides are at least making progress, with Weinfuss hearing about “movement” in negotiations. Wilson was the team’s No. 1 wide receiver and downfield target for Jacoby Brissett after Kyler Murray went to the bench last season. An extension for the 26-year-old may be coming prior to Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Cardinals have “attempted” to sign Michael Wilson to a contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/michael-wi.analysis: Wilson emerged as the team’s clear No. 1 receiver in 2025 once Kyler Murray was benched in favor of Jacoby Brissett, who has the arm strength to get the ball downfield to Wilson. Wilson was 18th among all wideouts in receiving yards and tenth in air yards last year. Fowler said “the likeliest path for Wilson is to enter Week 1 on the final year of his rookie deal. Perhaps the team finds a way to get a deal done, but sources indicate he’s likely to be a key free agent.” Wilson, 26, could make Alec Pierce money in 2027 if the Cardinals don’t re-sign him in the coming months.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Jacoby Brissett completed 24-of-35 passes for 218 yards and one touchdown in the Cardinals’ 18-16, Week 6 win over the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: Brissett threw an interception to Rams S Quentin Lake while targeting Trey McBride on the Cardinals’ third play from scrimmage but managed to play mistake-free, and touchdown-free, football from there on out. Brissett took zero sacks for the first time this season and linked up with four different players for explosive gains. That said, the box score results obviously disappoint. Brissett nearly linked up with Michael Wilson for a 36-yard touchdown on the Cardinals’ seventh drive, but the ball glanced off Wilson’s fingertips as he dove for it in the end zone. The drive ultimately resulted in a field goal, as did five others. Brissett will be a high-end QB2 against the Broncos in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: ArizonaCardinals.com’s Darren Urban believes Carson Beck won’t start in the “immediate future.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: Cardinals fans appear to be pining for the team to bench Jacoby Brissett and start the rookie in the coming weeks as another season circles the drain for Arizona. Beck so far has been the Cards’ emergency third quarterback. Urban said there remains a “chance Beck is made the backup this week or next and allow him to come on in relief if the situation presents itself. I don’t see Beck starting in the immediate future, but it does feel his time grows closer, and if the offense continues to sputter, that would be understandable.” Brissett this season ranks 15th in passing yards. He’s thrown nine touchdowns to five interceptions and ranks 30th out of 37 qualifying QBs in adjusted yards per attempt. He won’t be a viable fantasy play this week against a tough Rams coverage unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Jacoby Brissett completed 29-of-47 passes for 292 yards, three touchdowns and one interception in the Cardinals’ 21-45, Week 5 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: Brissett also rushed twice for 19 yards and nearly scored on a trick play via a seven-yard reception. He was stopped at the Lions’ two-yard line. Brissett guided the Cardinals to a 14-play scoring drive on their first possession, which he capped off with a two-yard touchdown strike to backup TE Teagan Quitoriano. The bottom dropped out after that. The Cardinals racked up five straight drives ending a punt, with Brissett only managing to break the dreary streak by throwing an interception. Brissett managed to salvage his box score with another Quitoriano score, and a juggling touchdown catch secured by Trey McBride. Brissett also coaxed a few big plays out of fellow backup TE Elijah Higgins. Apparently, the veteran quarterback is ready to target more towering pass catchers with Marvin Harrison Jr. now a Texan. Brissett is a borderline QB1/2 with a shaky floor in Week 6 against the Rams. Coach Mike LaFleur said post-game that he is not considering a quarterback change.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Jacoby Brissett completed 21-of-35 passes for 166 yards, two touchdowns and three interceptions in the Cardinals’ 36-24, Week 4 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: Brissett added four carries for 18 yards. Entering the proceedings with just one pick through three starts, Brissett tossed two in the first half before “adding” a walk-off pick-six on the game’s final play. Trailing 30-24, the Cardinals had a 4th-and-goal from the Giants’ four-yard line. Then a pressured Brissett threw it right to Deonte Banks after Michael Wilson cut off his route in the end zone. It was a brutal end to a brutal game, one where Brissett took a pair of sacks in addition to his giveaways. He did find the beleaguered Marvin Harrison Jr. for a 12-yard score against man-to-man coverage on the game’s opening drive, but that opening drive score went down as MHJ’s only reception. The duo did draw a late DPI to set up their ill-faded goal-line series. Averaging a miserable 4.7 yards per attempt on 115 throws over his past three starts, Brissett could get the Carson Beck chatter going in the desert sooner rather than later. That being said, the Lions are a plus Week 5 matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Jacoby Brissett completed 38-of-52 passes for 280 yards and two touchdowns in the Cardinals’ 36-30, Week 3 loss to the 49ers, adding four carries for four yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: Brissett and the Cardinals offense had difficulty navigating penalties and finishing drives in the first half, playing catch-up for much of the second half. The offense wore down the 49ers’ banged-up defensive line over time, with Brissett tossing a pair of touchdowns and sneaking in another from the one-yard line to bring the Cardinals close in the fourth quarter. Though he couldn’t complete the comeback, Brissett’s fantasy production with 52 passing attempts is a good sign for Cardinals pass-catchers moving forward. However, they won’t be in as much of a pass-happy game script against the Giants in Week 4; Brissett is a fantasy QB2 for next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Cardinals qB Jacoby Brissett (hip) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 3 against the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: Brissett practiced fully all week, despite the hip injury. Brissett is not quite hitting the peaks he produced last year and is too tough to trust in 12-team leagues. Consider him a QB2 against the 49ers this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Cardinals QB Jacoby Brissett (hip) was a full practice participant on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: Brissett seemingly dealt with an injury in the Cardinals’ Week 2 loss against the Seahawks, but played through it. He opens the week listed with a hip injury but was a full practice participant. Though Brissett seems to have a hip issue ailing him, it does not seem like it will keep him from playing. The veteran remains in the low-end QB2 conversation for Week 3 against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Jacoby Brissett completed 17-of-28 passes for 95 yards, one touchdown and one interception in the Cardinals’ 7-31, Week 2 loss to the Seahawks, adding one rush for seven yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: Brissett was seemingly dealing with some sort of thigh issue against the Seahawks. Between the Cardinals’ eighth and ninth drives, Brissett was seen briefly meeting with the training staff, who applied a heating pad to one of his legs. He tried walking after a while, but shook his head and took a seat on the bench until it was time for the Cardinals’ offense to retake the field. The veteran quarterback was constantly under pressure, though he only took two sacks. Brissett threw an interception via a bad overthrow on the Cardinals’ seventh drive, and later had a would-be interception dropped on the Cardinals’ eighth drive. The leg issue seemingly impacted his ability to drive the ball downfield, which could keep him as a mid-to-low QB2 against the 49ers in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: Jacoby Brissett completed 27-of-37 attempts for 277 yards and a touchdown in the Cardinals’ Week 1 win against the Chargers, adding six rushes for 14 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: Brissett outperformed Justin Herbert in every statistical category in what proved to be an easy victory for the underdog Cardinals. Brissett continued attacking downfield in this one, connecting with Marvin Harrison, Jr. for a 33-yard gain and Trey McBride for a 28-yarder. Brissett narrowly missed Michael Wilson on a couple first half deep shots. Arizona took its foot off the gas in the fourth quarter with the Chargers offense clearly out of answers and unable to move the ball with Ladd McConkey (chest) sidelined. Brissett’s aggressive style and his highly talented group of pass catchers should make him viable as a streaming option in Week 2 against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler believes Jacoby Brissett “could be a trade candidate at midseason” if he is playing well and the Cardinals are losing games.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jacoby-bri.analysis: Fowler notes that the Cardinals likely want to see what they have in Carson Beck before the season ends. Of course, if the Cardinals are winning games, they will stick with what is working. Brissett put up strong counting stats last year, throwing for 281 yards per game across his 12 starts. That, however, did not result in any success for the Cardinals, who went 1-11 with Brissett under center. A similar season would make the veteran a viable backup or injury fill-in at that trade deadline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton had seven rushes for 18 yards in the Chargers’ Week 6 loss to the Chiefs, adding four catches for 21 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Hampton was his usual plodding self in this one, with a long rush of four yards in another depressing outing for the LA offense. Kimani Vidal, meanwhile had seven rushes for 21 yards and got much of his work in the first quarter. Keaton Mitchell had just two carries and did not catch his lone target. Hampton led the backfield in routes and targets on the day. His diminishing role and his lack of efficiency has made Hampton nothing more than a touchdown-dependent desperation flex option this year. The Chargers have a bye in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton rushed 14 times for 33 yards in the Chargers’ Week 5 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Webster’s defines plodding as whatever this was. Hampton picked up a literal third of his yards on one 11-yard carry, and while much of the blame goes to the sheer lack of bodies on the offensive line, it was still mightily unimpressive. Hampton is at best a dart-throw FLEX for Week 6 against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel said he has not lost “any faith” in Omarion Hampton.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: “I don’t see any change in terms of the depth chart at all. I felt I was underutilizing a strength,” McDaniel said about the increased usage of Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal. McDaniel’s statement is good for Hampton in the sense that we know Hampton will retain a reasonable role. And it’s bad because McDaniel is all but confirming the pecking order will remain the same. Expect more low-end RB2/FLEX nonsense from Hampton.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton rushed nine times for 45 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers’ Week 4 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Hampton’s late touchdown that still left the Chargers down by 10 in the middle of the fourth quarter is the only positive of the day. Los Angeles clearly isn’t enamored with the second-year tailback — or at the very best, is concerned about keeping him healthy — right now, and he was clearly in a timeshare again with Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal. He’s at best a FLEX play for Week 5 against the tough Denver defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton rushed 15 times for 56 yards in a Week 3 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: The Chargers were missing two starting interior linemen and decided that running up the gut was not going to work for them. Understandably so. Hampton was held to just 3.7 yards per carry and didn’t seem to break any tackles in the interior of the Bills’ defensive line. Mike McDaniel decided to use Keaton Mitchell on the perimeter at the start of the game, but the Bills adjusted to take that away. At the end of the day, Hampton had 15 carries to Mitchell’s eight, but Hampton played 29 snaps, while Mitchell played 26 and ran a route on double the amount of dropbacks that Hampton did. This is a problematic timeshare in an offense that doesn’t look very good right now. Hampton remains a low-end RB2 who is touchdown dependent, which means he’s probably an RB3 next week against the Seahawks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton rushed 23 times for 94 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers’ Week 2 loss to the Raiders, adding two catches for 21 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Hampton was a workhorse in this game, picking up what was blocked but not much more. He had a solid outing going until late in the fourth quarter when Nakobe Dean knocked the football out of his hands and into the waiting arms of Jeremy Chinn. A lengthy return put the Raiders in scoring position and all but ended the game. Fantasy managers won’t be too bothered by the blunder today, but it could result in the team giving more work to Keaton Mitchell, who only touched the ball six times. Hampton will be near the top of the RB2 ranks for Week 3 versus the Bills despite seeing an RB1 workload today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Omarion Hampton had 12 rushes for 43 yards and a touchdown in the Chargers’ Week 1 loss against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Hampton got away with it thanks to a first half touchdown plunge before the LA offense imploded following Ladd McConkey’s chest injury. Hampton was not targeted on 17 pass routes while Keaton Mitchell saw one target on 13 routes. Mitchell had four rushes on the day. Mike McDaniel’s offense collapsed immediately after the Bolts marched downfield on their first drive of the game, making it hard to tell exactly how Hampton (and Mitchell) will be used in neutral game script. That the Chargers were dominated by the Cardinals could be a bad sign for everyone in the Chargers offense, including Hampton. He’ll be a top-20 option next week against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Keaton Mitchell (hamstring) is active for Week 1 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Mitchell, a limited participant in practice for much of the week, will suit up for the Bolts’ season opener against Arizona. He should see a handful of designed touches in Mike McDaniel’s offense while Omarion Hampton functions as the team’s lead back and Kimani Vidal mixes in here and there. Mitchell can be used as a second flex option for now. Chargers declared S RJ Mickens, CB Deane Leonard, OL Logan Taylor, OL Alex Harkey, and OL Trevor Penning inactive for their season opener.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: The Athletic’s Daniel Popper said a top-five season for Chargers RB Omarion Hampton is “realistic.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Popper fielded a question about Hampton’s top-10 chances as a guest on the Locked On Chargers show. The metrics for measuring this feat were left undefined, but rushing yardage or scrimmage yardage are the two most likely baselines. While OC Mike McDaniel has teased a potential hot-hand approach, Popper has remained steadfast in his stance that Hampton is set for bellcow duties thanks in part to speed, physicality and scheme versatility. He warrants RB1 treatment right out of the gate.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.headline: Chargers RB Keaton Mitchell rushed three times for minus-one yard in Thursday’s preseason game against the 49ers, adding one reception for 11 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omarion-ha.analysis: Mitchell’s box score would have looked a lot better if his 21-yard reception on a route out of the backfield had not been called back due to a penalty. Chargers starting RB Omarion Hampton played all three snaps on the opening drive before giving way to Mitchell, who played 10-of-10 snaps on the second and third drives. Fellow backup RB Kimani Vidal took the field as the Chargers’ kick returner to begin the game. He made his first appearance on offense on the Chargers’ fourth drive. Mitchell could return standalone FLEX value with big-play upside in this role. He reportedly visited the blue medical tent, but was allowed to return to the sideline. Hopefully, this is a non-issue.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty rushed 10 times for 22 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 6 loss to the Bills, adding four receptions for 36 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Jeanty, who is dealing with a foot/ankle injury, wasn’t effective on the ground, but that didn’t stop him from scoring his first rushing touchdown of the season. Jeanty punched in a one-yard score in the first quarter of Sunday’s game to give the Raiders an early 7-3 lead, but averaged a disappointing 2.2 YPC overall. He did manage a solid 4-36-0 receiving line on six targets, with two of his four receptions coming on the Raiders’ third drive of the game. Jeanty appeared on 15 more snaps than Mike Washington and out-touched him 14 to 10. While he continues to struggle from an efficiency standpoint, Jeanty’s volume will make him a low-end RB1 next week against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty (foot) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 6 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: The Raiders’ starting running back is good to go for what should be a fantasy-friendly game environment. The Raiders encouragingly stopped listing Jeanty with an ankle injury this week. Hopefully, his remaining plantar fasciitis issue subsides before long as well. Jeanty is a low-end RB1 in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty (foot) said he is feeling “great” and “ready to go” for Week 6 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: The quotes read a tad bit more enthusiastically than Jeanty did while speaking to media members at his locker, but this is still good to hear. Jeanty has been dealing with an ankle injury for a long time, but the team took that injury off the weekly practice report this week. He is now listed only with the foot injury after experiencing “a flare-up of plantar fasciitis” last Friday. Jeanty is a low-end RB1 against the Bills this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty (foot) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Jeanty’s previous ankle designation was removed from the injury report and he was a full practice participant on Wednesday. His practice participation lines up with Raiders coach Klint Kubiak saying the 22-year-old running back was starting to “feel a lot better.” Though there were rumors of the Raiders resting Jeanty for a week, he is trending to play in Week 6 against the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Ashton Jeanty (foot/ankle) is starting to “feel a lot better.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Kubiak also shot down the idea of the Raiders resting Jeanty for a week, despite it being reported earlier today that the Raiders were considering giving him a week off to recover at some point. Jeanty has been dreadfully inefficient this year, averaging a meager 3.3 yards per carry, though the team’s subpar offensive line also deserves some of the blame. For fantasy purposes, his workload has been the big draw. He is averaging 22 touches per game through five weeks. Even if the foot and ankle injuries continue to bother him, Jeanty has to be treated as a mid-range RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty had 10 rushes for 27 yards in the Raiders’ Week 5 loss to the Patriots, adding three catches for 50 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Most of Jeanty’s production against New England came on a 31-yard catch and run in the third quarter. Battling through foot and ankle injuries, Jeanty looked hobbled from the start and struggled to break tackles or outrun Patriots defenders to the edge. Most Raiders starters rested in the fourth quarter of a lopsided loss. Jeanty still doesn’t have a rushing touchdown on the season and hasn’t had 100 rushing yards in a game since Week 1 against the Dolphins. Until Jeanty is fully healthy he probably won’t provide much in the way of upside, including next week against a decent Buffalo run defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty (ankle, foot) is active for Week 5 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Jeanty will play through his foot and ankle injuries against New England. It wouldn’t be surprising if he cedes some backfield work to a healthy and much more explosive Mike Washington, however. Jeanty should be considered a top-24 option this week while Washington is a desperation flex. Raiders declared WR Jalen Nailor, QB Aidan O’Connell, S Tristin McCollum, RB Roman Hemby, S Dalton Johnson, OL Trey Zuhn, and DT JJ Pegues inactive against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Ashton Jeanty (foot/ankle) is “hopeful” to play in Week 5 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Per Rapoport, Jeanty had a flare-up of plantar fasciitis last week to go along with his ankle injury. He added that Jeanty will work out before today’s game to see how he’s feeling. If he can’t go, Mike Washington Jr. would see the bulk of the backfield touches. Washington has been an explosive complement to Jeanty this year, averaging five yards per carry on 24 attempts. He would jump to the top of the RB2 ranks if Jeanty can’t go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Ashton Jeanty (foot/ankle) is questionable for Las Vegas’ Week 5 game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Kubiak didn’t get into real specifics about the injury when asked. Mike Washington just found his way into real contingency value and is a worthwhile stash/hedge anywhere he was dropped. Jeanty did not practice Friday after a limited session (and the addition of a foot tag) on Thurdsay, so this certainly doesn’t appear to be heading in the right direction. That said, we knew Jeanty would be managing something after the preseason ankle injury and the Raiders have given out rest days on Friday quite a bit already this year. Jeanty is likely something close to truly questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.headline: Ashton Jeanty (ankle/foot) was not spotted at Friday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ashton-jea.analysis: Jeanty has been dealing with the ankle injury throughout the week, but the foot injury was added after Thursday’s practice. Jeanty was officially listed as limited on Thursday, but the Raiders’ RB1 was absent from the media portion of Friday’s practice. We will receive final word on his Week 5 availability soon, but rookie Mike Washington could be in line for a busy day against the Patriots if Jeanty is unable to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: James Cook rushed 22 times for 95 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 6 win over the Raiders, adding three receptions for 58 additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: Cook had a much-needed bounce-back game in Sunday’s win over the Raiders. A week after he fumbled twice in an overtime win over the Rams, Cook secured the football for all four quarters and broke off multiple explosive plays while handling 22 of the Bills’ 24 running back carries. His lone rushing touchdown came on a three-yard run in the fourth quarter, and came one play after Cook ripped off a 26-yard reception on a third-and-three to keep the chains moving. Concerns about ball security may follow Cook for the remainder of the season, but his role in the Bills’ offense continues to provide valuable production in both real and fantasy football. He will be locked in as an RB1 in Week 8 against the Ravens when the Bills return from their Week 7 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: Bills coach Joe Brady said James Cook needs to protect the ball or he’s going to get fewer carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: “At some point, there has to be consequences,” Brady said about his lead back, who has fumbled four times in five games this season, including twice on Monday night. Cook has played 67.3 percent of the team’s snaps, and this probably isn’t a threat to his lead back status, but it wouldn’t be surprising if he sat on the bench for a spell if he fumbled in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: James Cook rushed 25 times for 111 yards and two touchdowns in the Bills’ Week 5 win over the Rams, adding seven yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: Cook’s elite rushing line was overshadowed by two fumbles, the second of which was a lost fumble on the team’s first possession of overtime, placing the Rams in position to complete the comeback and steal away the victory. A blocked field goal on what would have been the game-winning kick breathed new life into the Bills, who demonstrated confidence in their lead back by throwing him right back out there on the following possession to eventually win the game. The 26 touches go down as a season high for the veteran back, who found paint for the fourth consecutive game in the thrilling overtime win. Cook remains a top-tier RB1 for fantasy purposes ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Raiders in Las Vegas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: James Cook rushed 12 times for 75 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 4 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: He added two catches for either yards. This game was never more than a one-score game, so it’s pretty shocking that Cook only had 14 touches. The Patriots did a good job containing him early in the game, apart from his touchdown run, but the Bills simply moved away from the running game too quickly. Cook was gaining huge chunk yards in the second half and should have been fed more carries during the game. With the Bills having their second straight mediocre offensive performance, you have to wonder if they will make it a point to lean on Cook more next week against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: James Cook rushed 24 times for 154 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 3 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: Cook was the only running back to get a carry on the day, and he ripped off over six yards per rush. He got the Bills down inside the two-yard line twice but watched as Josh Allen ran it into the end zone each time. On the third trip deep into the red zone, Cook rushed it in from four yards out. With Ty Johnson back, Cook did cede some passing game work; however, Cook also played 42 of the team’s 62 snaps, compared to just 15 snaps for Johnson. The lack of receiving may prevent Cook from being a top-five running back, but he’s a clear RB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: James Cook rushed 21 times for 135 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 2 win over the Lions, adding four yards on one reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: Cook jumped out to a scorching start on the ground, reaching the century mark in rushing before the half. Still, fantasy managers were left scratching their head as they watched Josh Allen account for three touchdowns from inside the five, two on the ground and one through the air. It wasn’t until a 22-yard carry that was down at the one late in the fourth quarter that the team rewarded Cook with a short-yardage touchdown, finally allowing fantasy managers their first taste of sweet touchdown copium from their first-round draft pick on the young season. Cook is likely to remain busy when the Bills host the Jets in Week 3, where he will remain a locked-in RB1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Bills “want to get that running game recharged” in Week 2 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: Bills RB James Cook totaled 57 yards on just 13 rushing attempts last week, adding three catches for 12 yards. Per Fowler, the Bills plan to use him a lot more in primetime this evening. Cook can be treated as a locked-in RB1 in what should be a fantasy-friendly game environment on Thursday Night Football. The Bills notably elevated RB Frank Gore Jr. from the practice squad, which could indicate that RB Ty Johnson (hamstring) will be inactive tonight.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: James Cook rushed 13 times for 57 yards in Buffalo’s Week 1 win over the Texans, adding three catches for 12 yards on four targets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: Cook had twenty yards on the game’s first drive, but the game eventually skewed pass-heavy for the Bills and Josh Allen had the game’s only two rushing touchdowns. Per PFF’s early charting data, Cook had 41 of the 57 snaps and almost all the work ahead of Ray Davis and Frank Gore Jr. Assuming Ty Johnson remains out on a short week against the Lions in Week 2, Cook will remain a touch-dominator on the RB1 line and will have a chance for a better touchdown runout.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: Bills RB Ty Johnson (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: It sure looks like the hamstring strain that Johnson suffered more than a month ago is going to keep him sidelined for the Bills’ season opener against the Texans. Starting RB James Cook was expected to play a larger role in the passing game this year. With Johnson sidelined, Cook could hog passing down snaps.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.headline: Bills RB Ty Johnson (hamstring) was not present during the portion of practice open to the media.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/james-cook.analysis: Johnson went down while running a route on August 9th. He resumed running roughly two weeks ago, but has not yet rejoined his teammates in drills. Although Johnson is not on the fantasy radar himself, he has hogged passing down snaps in recent seasons. Starting RB James Cook has been expected to take on a larger receiving role this season, and Johnson’s potential absence adds credence to that idea.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Kirk Cousins completed 23-of-41 passes for 313 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Raiders’ 33-30, Week 6 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: Cousins and the Raiders strung together a handful of nice drives in Sunday’s loss to the Bills, but they needed to be just about perfect to slow Buffalo’s offensive attack. With Brock Bowers bottled up for most of the evening, Cousins connected with tight end Michael Mayer seven times for 95 yards, with his lone touchdown passes coming on passes of 11 and 44 yards to Tre Tucker in the fourth quarter. The 44-yard touchdown pass to Tucker came inside of two minutes and with the Bills up by 10, but Cousins and Tucker took advantage of a struggling Bills’ defense to complete the long score and keep things interesting in the waning seconds. Now losers of three straight games, the Raiders will hope to avoid a fourth straight loss next week when they host the suddenly 2-4 Rams. Cousins continues to enjoy a career revival under Klint Kubiak and has now thrown for 1,582-14-5 in his first six games. He’ll be in the QB2 mix for next week’s game against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Kirk Cousins is the starter “but if Fernando [Mendoza]'s number is called we have confidence in him.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: No real surprise after Mendoza’s mop-up appearance in Week 5. It doesn’t appear that he’s taken a major step towards unseating Cousins — who has played well — just yet. But it remains a reasonable bet to happen in the near future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Kirk Cousins completed 19-of-28 attempts for 243 yards and a touchdown in the Raiders’ Week 5 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: Cousins didn’t play poorly, but didn’t do much beyond connecting with Brock Bowers for some long gains in the first half. The Patriots avalanched the severely overmatched Raiders in the third quarter. Cousins was sacked three times while narrowly avoiding a few other big losses, as the Vegas offensive line struggled to protect him throughout. His muted showing comes after 11 touchdown tosses over the season’s first four games in Klint Kubiak’s offense. Cousins will look to bounce back in Week 6 against the Bills in what should be a high-scoring affair.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Kirk Cousins completed 31-of-52 passes for 365 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Raiders’ 30-27, Week 4 loss to the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: Cousins and the Raiders did everything they could to remain undefeated, but came up just short in a game that came down to the wire against their division rivals. Cousins led the Raiders right down the field on their opening drive and capped it with a 27-yard touchdown pass to Ian Thomas, who was wide open for an easy score. After leading multiple drives that ended in field goals, Cousins came up big for the Raiders in the fourth quarter when he avoided a sack in the pocket and stepped up to find Brock Bowers in the back of the end zone for a 20-yard touchdown. A successful two-point conversion play to Cody White cut the Chiefs’ lead to 30-27, but with the Raiders driving in the final seconds of regulation, Cousins would throw the game-ending interception to hand the Chiefs their fourth-straight win of the season. Cousins and the Raiders proved to be legit in this one, as they went blow-for-blow with the Chiefs to the very end. Now sitting with a 3-1 record, the Raiders will look to rebound in Week 5 against the Patriots. Cousins has thrown multiple touchdowns in every game this season and has now thrown for 11 TDs to four INTs. He’ll be in the mix as a strong QB2 next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Kirk Cousins completed 22-of-33 passes for 248 yards and three touchdowns in the Raiders’ 35-27, Week 3 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: Cousins had a few off-target passes in this one, but he certainly loves having Brock Bowers in the lineup. The duo linked up 10 times on the day, which opened things up for the rest of the offense as the game progressed. Coach Klint Kubiak sent Bowers in motion inside the green zone on a play-action play seemingly designed for Michael Mayer, who got open with ease on a short out route and hauled in the score. Cousins fumbled while being hit late in the game, but a teammate recovered, preserving his turnover-free outing. He warrants borderline QB1/2 treatment against the Chiefs next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Kirk Cousins completed 19-of-29 passes for 253 yards, three touchdowns, and an interception in the Raiders’ 26-14, Week 2 win over the Chargers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: Cousins was intercepted on the Raiders’ opening drive of the game, but no one was necessarily at fault. Cousins threw a well-timed ball to Tre Tucker on an in-breaking route and the speedy receiver slipped while cutting, leaving the pass to sail into enemy hands. The veteran passer needed a few more drives to get in rhythm but eventually began to pick apart the LA defense. He completed four passes of 20+ yards, something he managed just once in Week 1. Cousins remains more of a ball distributor than anything else, but he has looked good in that role through two weeks. There are worse Superflex options for Week 3 when Cousins takes on the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Kirk Cousins completed 21-of-30 passes for 160 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions in the Raiders’ 27-13, Week 1 win over the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: The Raiders’ first punt occurred with just over 14 minutes left in the fourth quarter. Cousins was only asked to manage this game, and he did so moderately effectively. Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty scored two of Cousins’ passing touchdowns on catch-and-run plays via routes out of the backfield. Cousins deserves credit for hitting WR Jack Bech in stride on a 15-yard score, but he also deserves blame for both interceptions. One was an overthrow; the other was late. Cousins is a QB2 next week against the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Raiders named Kirk Cousins as the team’s Week 1 starter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: With input from Tom Brady, head coach Klint Kubiak will put the 38-year-old Cousins under center for the season opener against the Dolphins. Fernando Mendoza, the No. 1 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft, will serve as Cousins’ backup. How long this arrangement will last is anyone’s guess. A good start to the regular season could delay Mendoza’s first NFL start for a couple months but he’s almost certain to take over as the Vegas starter at some point in 2026. Mendoza should be stashed in most superflex formats and Cousins profiles as a decent QB2 in such formats for Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak said he’s talking with Tom Brady “multiple times per week” about the team’s starting quarterback situation.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: An NFL head coach consulting with an NFL announcer on who his team should start under center is a brave new world for the league. It looks like the Raiders are set on Kirk Cousins to start Week 1 against the Dolphins after Fernando Mendoza’s spotty preseason play and struggles in training camp. Look for Cousins to target his short-area pass catchers relentlessly, like he did last year in Atlanta. It won’t be long before Mendoza gets a shot at starting duties. He should be rostered in most superflex leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Raiders QB Kirk Cousins is expected to be named the starter eventually.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kirk-cousi.analysis: Appearing on NFL Live Friday afternoon, Fowler said that people inside the Raiders’ building and around the league still expect Cousins to be named the starter. Raiders HC Klint Kubiak declined to name a starting quarterback Friday morning. Following the loss of Thursday’s preseason game against the 49ers, Kubiak said rookie Fernando Mendoza needs another three preseason games before going as far as mentioning that Mendoza’s practice reps will decline once the regular season begins. While Kubiak continues to drag his feet when it comes to the official announcement, all signs still point to Cousins being named the starter at some point eventually.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 23-of-33 passes for 255 yards and two touchdowns in the Bills’ 33-30, Week 6 win over the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: The Raiders did their part to keep Allen in the pocket in this one. He managed just one rushing yard on five carries, but did plenty of damage through the air to put the Bills in position to pull out their fifth win of the season. Allen threw his first touchdown of the day to Khalil Shakir in the second quarter on a nine-yard screen pass, and flipped an impressive shovel pass to Keon Coleman in the third quarter for his second touchdown pass of the day. Allen and the Bills have scored 30-plus points in four of their first six games this season, with Allen totaling four touchdowns in his last two games. The Bills punted just twice in this one, and Allen led his team on three straight scoring drives to start the game. While there’s plenty to figure out on defense, Allen and the offense are clicking on all cylinders even with DJ Moore (shoulder) sidelined. The Bills now head into their Week 7 bye week and will return in Week 8 to play host to the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 12-of-19 passes for 210 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Bills’ 37-34, Week 5 win over the Rams, adding 121 yards and a touchdown on 10 carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: The two teams mustered only 20 combined points in the first half as they felt each other out. There were only two punts after the break between the two sides, who combined for seven touchdowns on nine combined possessions including five straight touchdowns in the fourth quarter to send the game to overtime. Allen and the Bills took the ball first in the extra frame and quickly found themselves deep in enemy territory following a 57-yard, catch-and-run pass to Khalil Shakir. A James Cook fumble on the next play appeared to shatter Allen’s chances of earning his first career win in overtime, but a blocked 48-yard field goal attempt from Harrison Mevis gave the ball back to the Bills with a chance to win. Two Josh Allen scrambles set up a game-winning, 45-yard field goal for Tyler Bass. Allen ended with the second most yards on the ground of his career as the Bills moved to 4-1 with the wild win. Allen remains the top overall quarterback in fantasy circles ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Raiders on the road.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 23-of-33 passes for 253 yards, one touchdown, and one interception in the Bills’ 29-26 Week 4 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Allen did score a rushing touchdown, but he had just four rushing yards on five carries, making this the second straight game that he was contained as a rusher. Every time Allen rolled out, the Patriots had a defender in the lane, and Allen wasn’t able to make his usual big plays with his arm. Once D.J. Moore left the game with a shoulder injury, it felt like none of the Bills’ receivers were able to create space with their defenders, much like we saw for all of 2025. Allen’s interception was an egregious decision on the final drive of the game, where he made an impressive spin move to avoid a sack and then chucked an unnecessary Hail Mary into double coverage. You’re still starting Allen in fantasy leagues, but it’s a bit concerning that we’ve seen the Bills’ offense look scattered and out of sync for two straight games. It won’t get easier on Monday against the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 16-of-26 passes for 204 yards and two interceptions in the Bills’ 24-16, Week 3 win over the Chargers, adding 22 yards rushing and two touchdowns on the ground.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Allen certainly wasn’t good in this one, but he wasn’t alone. The Bills turned the ball over five times, committed 10 penalties, and allowed four sacks and somehow won this game. His first interception was on a truly bad read over the middle of the field. The second was on a deep pass into coverage when Allen thought he had drawn an offside. The pass managed to hit the safety in the back and then land in his stomach when he rolled over after hitting the ground. Allen would also fumble on a sack later in the game. The Chargers did a good job of taking Allen’s scrambles away, and this entire Bills team was in disarray, so nobody was consistently open down the field.
