That being said, Allen’s two rushing touchdowns give him 85 for his career, which means he’s now tied with former Bill Marshawn Lynch for 17th on the NFL’s all-time list. The Bills and Allen will look to get things straightened out against the Patriots next week, and Allen will clearly be in your lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 20-of-31 passes for 248 yards and three touchdowns in the Bills’ 41-31, Week 2 win over the Lions, adding 69 yard and two touchdowns on 14 carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Was it ever a doubt that Super Josh would make an appearance in the franchise’s first game in their new stadium? To the utter dismay of James Cook fantasy managers, Allen accounted for three touchdowns from inside the five against the Lions, two with his legs and one with his arm, extending his NFL-record for games with multiple rushing touchdowns and multiple passing touchdowns to 10 in the process. The unquestioned overall QB1 in fantasy circles continues to prove the doubters wrong as the Bills surge to 2-0 atop the AFC ahead of a home meeting with the Chargers in Week 3. Allen remains a top-tier fantasy asset until pigs fly.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Josh Allen completed 20-of-29 passes for 334 yards and two touchdowns in the Bills’ 36-31, Week 1 win over the Texans, adding 23 yards and two touchdowns on the ground.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Some had suggested you might want to bench Josh Allen against the Texans defense this week. Instead, Allen absolutely decimated last year’s top defense with a game-winning stick throw to the post for Josh Palmer to take a late five-point lead. He did his typical witchcraft out of structure, the best of which was probably a floater in his own end zone with a man in his face that landed directly on Dalton Kincaid’s hands. He also owned the ground game in the red zone. It was the first Bills win in Houston since the JP Losman Era. Allen, as always, will be in the QB1 overall discussion against the Lions in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: The Athletic’s Joe Buscaglia said he would not be surprised if DJ Moore is “on the field constantly and for [Josh] Allen to default to looking his way.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Buscaglia called Moore, who was acquired from the Bears this spring, the “crown jewel of the offseason” for the Bills front office. “Moore’s contributions to the offense within training camp were immediate and obvious,” Buscaglia said. “Allen routinely pushed the ball downfield to Moore, making a concerted effort all summer to build on-field chemistry with the Bills’ new No. 1 receiver. ... The days of ‘everybody eats’ seem to be in the rearview mirror.” It’s a bullish report — one that could mean Moore is among the best values in redraft leagues this season even after being among the NFL’s most inefficient wideouts in 2025. Moore should be in all 12-team lineups for Week 1 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports Josh Allen and “most Bills starters” will sit for Saturday’s preseason game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: After a good week of joint practices against the Browns, the Bills are expected to sit most of their starters while giving their depth players a chance to show what they have. Veteran QB Kyle Allen will draw the start on Saturday, with backup Shane Buechele also expected to see work. The Bills’ decision to sit their starters should come as good news for Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson, who are still battling for the QB1 job, with Sanders in line to start with the first-team offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: The Athletic Football Show’s Dave Helman believes Bills WR Skyler Bell could be “Ja’Marr Chase lite” in the NFL.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Taken by Buffalo with the 125th pick in the 2026 draft, Bell — a hyper-productive wideout at UConn — joins DJ Moore, Khalil Shakir, Josh Palmer, and Keon Coleman in an underwhelming receivers room. Bell, Helman said, enters the NFL with a multifaceted skill set that is highly valued among most NFL front offices. “This is probably the most reckless thing I’ll say on this show,” Helman said. “This is Ja’Marr Chase lite. He’s a freak athlete, he’s explosive, but he’s very powerful and strong. And watching him, I was just like, obviously, he’s not Ja’Marr Chase ... but he does all that type of stuff. He can take it to the house. He can just body people out of the way. He can high point the ball. If I was trying to get Ja’Marr Chase’s skillset on late day two or even into day three, I’m all the way in on this guy.” Helman wasn’t alone in his praise of Bell, who last season was second among all college wideouts in yards per route run. Ryan Fowler of NBC Sports Philadelphia said in March that Bell, 23, was close to a Round One prospect. The Bills took him late on the third day of the draft.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.headline: Bills HC Joe Brady said Josh Allen (foot) is “good to go” to participate in the team’s offseason program.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/josh-allen.analysis: Allen underwent surgery to repair a broken bone in his foot, but two months post-op, the Bills’ QB1 appears to be in good shape. The Bills went out and traded for WR DJ Moore this offseason to give Allen a much-needed weapon in the passing game, and with Allen trending in the right direction, he should have plenty of time to build with Moore before training camp ramps up earlier this summer. Allen has finished as the QB1 in fantasy points per game in four of his last six seasons and projects as a high-end QB1 again this upcoming season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.headline: Ted Hurst caught 3-of-6 targets for 40 yards in the Bucs’ Week 6 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.analysis: Hurs tied his season highs in catches and yards today. He also drew a defensive pass interference call that netted Tampa Bay 22 yards. Emeka Egbuka would score on the very next play. Hurst is looking like a solid field-stretcher, but the Bucs’ offense isn’t set up to support more than one fantasy-relevant pass-catcher. With Emeka Egbuka decisively taking that role, Hurst is buried in the WR6 ranks going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.headline: Ted Hurst was not targeted in the Buccaneers’ Week 5 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.analysis: Hurst has seen his role eaten into by downfield threat Tez Johnson as the season has progressed, clearly not yet ready to take on a full workload in the offense as he enters the second month of his rookie season. Hurst brings the size and physicality to grow into a consistent producer at the NFL level, something fantasy managers could have to be patient with in the coming weeks. Hurst safely remains a bench stash ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.headline: Ted Hurst caught 2-of-3 targets for 25 yards in the Bucs’ Week 4 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.analysis: Hurst was the only Bucs pass-catcher to gain more than 20 yards on a single play. The passing game was otherwise relegated to intermediate throws and check-downs in Jalon Daniels’ first start. With Jalen McMillan on IR, Hurst has locked up a starting role. That simply is worth much for fantasy managers with a backup quarterback under center. Hurst will be a desperation FLEX play when he takes on the Cowboys next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.headline: Ted Hurst caught his lone target for 40 yards and a touchdown in the Bucs’ Week 3 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.analysis: Hurst caught a perfectly-placed 40-yard score down the seam in the first half and did not see another look from Baker Mayfield. It wasn’t a lack of playing time that limited Hurst: He ran a route on 39 of the team’s 43 drop backs on the day. His downfield profile will make Hurst a volatile weekly play in 12-team leagues. He should probably stay on benches next week against the Dolphins if Mayfield (hand) is sidelined, however.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.headline: Ted Hurst caught 1-of-5 targets for 21 yards in the Bucs’ Week 2 loss against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.analysis: Hurst was overthrown by Baker Mayfield a few times in the second half. It could have been a big day for the speedy rookie if his quarterback weren’t struggling so mightily with deep throws. Hurst had a solid role though, running a route on 29 of the team’s 37 drop backs. He will be a high-variance flex play for Week 3 against the Vikings if Mayfield can find a little accuracy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Jalen McMillan (knee) is expected to play in Week 2 against the Browns, but not in a “full-time role just yet.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.analysis: The Bucs are going to ease McMillan back into the lineup after he missed Week 1 with the knee injury. McMillan will take rookie Ted Hurst’s spot in the lineup once healthy, but that might not happen until Week 3. Until we see what their split looks like, neither Hurst nor McMillan should be in fantasy lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.headline: Jalen McMillan (knee) is practicing in full on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.analysis: McMillan missed Week 1 due to a knee issue, despite getting in three limited practices during the week. He was listed as doubtful and the team ruled him out ahead of kickoff. It seems like the team was taking a cautious approach with his return from the training camp injury, and he should be good for Week 2. McMillan is expected to take rookie Ted Hurst’s spot in the lineup at X. Hurst managed just three catches for 36 yards in the role. In his first game of the season, McMillan will be buried in the WR5 ranks for fantasy purposes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.headline: Ted Hurst caught 3-of-3 targets for 36 yards in the Bucs’ Week 1 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.analysis: Hurst’s first NFL reception was a sure-handed grab against tight coverage as he went to the ground. Pro Football Focus charted Hurst as playing 43-of-57 snaps. That’s an extremely strong mark for a rookie third-rounder, though it will only last as long as Jalen McMillan is on the shelf with his knee injury. The Bucs declined to formally rule McMillan out until this morning, so there is a chance he is back for Week 2 against the Browns. For now, Hurst remains waiver wire fodder in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.headline: Jalen McMillan (knee) is inactive for Week 1 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.analysis: As is Sean Tucker (hamstring). McMillan’s immediate absence will force the Bucs to dig in to their young receiving depth earlier than they would have liked, but rookie Ted Hurst is not a bad fall-back option for the club. For fantasy managers, however, Hurst is not yet an option even in 14-team leagues. Also inactive for the Bucs are OT Justin Skule, CB Ayden Garnes, DL DeMonte Capehart, DL Elijah Simmons and OG Billy Schrauth.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.headline: Bucs listed Jalen McMillan as a starting receiver on the team’s Week 1 depth chart.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/ted-hurst/.analysis: It’s McMillan, not rookie WR Ted Hurst III, who’s listed as a starter alongside Chris Godwin and Emeka Egbuka ahead of Tampa’s Week 1 game against the Bengals. Hurst, the tallest of the Bucs wideouts, has by all accounts impressed Bucs players and coaches throughout the offseason and should have some kind of role in the team’s passing attack to start the year. It could be a while before Hurst takes on a more prominent role, however. Bucs general manager Jason Licht said last week that Hurst, 22, has “proven to us throughout camp, even OTAs, practice every day that he’s been very, very steady...it’s kind of evolved into okay, we can use him this year and he’s going to play a role.” Hurst can be stashed in deeper fantasy formats for now. McMillan is unlikely to be a factor in the Tampa offense after once again struggling with injuries this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor caught 4-of-6 targets for 33 yards in the Jets’ Week 6 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor is now up to 7/57 in two games since returning from his thumb injury. First-round rookie Kenyon Sadiq, who missed most of Week 5 with a concussion, is 3/15 during the same timespan. This Jets tight end targets battle figures to oscillate back and forth, but Taylor is the preferred option for the time being. It’s still not resulting in more than desperation TE2 value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Kenyon Sadiq remains in the league’s concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: The good news is that Sadiq was able to practice in a limited capacity on Wednesday. Sadiq suffered the head injury in Week 5 against Cleveland and did not return to action. Mason Taylor led the team’s tight ends with a 59 percent route rate against the Browns, catching all three of his targets for 23 yards. If Sadiq remains in the protocol tomorrow, he would be a long shot to play in Week 6. Taylor in that case would be a desperation streaming option in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor caught 3-of-3 targets for 24 yards in the Jets’ Week 5 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Active for the first time since Week 2, Taylor caught the second most balls on the team as Kenyon Sadiq departed with a third quarter concussion. Those are awful developments for Sadiq managers, but almost certainly not enough to create TE2 value for Taylor, even if Sadiq misses Week 6 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Jets TE Mason Taylor (thumb) is practicing in full for Week 5 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor’s return could be problematic for rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq. Sadiq posted a 7/105/1 receiving line two weeks ago before goose-egging last week. Taylor is not a serious receiving threat, but he can eat into Sadiq’s snap share. Sadiq likely remains a viable TE1, but his volatility just increased a tad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Breece Hall (quad) will not play in Week 4 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Hall was initially mentioned as being week-to-week when he was diagnosed with his quad injury, so he was never really considered a candidate to play in Week 4 despite the team waiting until the end of the week to rule him out. With Hall out, the Jets will look to Braelon Allen to handle most of the backfield duties. Allen will profile as a solid RB2 candidate with a chance for more upside in what could be a high-volume day against the Bears. In addition to Hall, the Jets also ruled out OG Dylan Parham (knee), TE Mason Taylor (thumb), and LB Kiko Mauigoa (quad) for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor (thumb) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor was sidelined all of last week and, so far, all of this week with the thumb injury. He’d need to mount a major comeback on Friday to get on to the questionable line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor (thumb) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor missed Week 3 with the thumb issue and is currently considered week-to-week. A DNP today puts him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 4. Assuming he is out, Kenyon Sadiq, coming off a breakout performance versus the Lions, will be in line for a larger role once again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor (thumb) will not play in Week 3 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Head coach Aaron Glenn said on Friday morning that Taylor would miss Sunday’s game after being sidelined in practice throughout the week. It was reported on Tuesday that Taylor would be week-to-week with his injury, so it isn’t all to surprising to learn that he will be sidelined for this one. Taylor has -2 yards on two receptions this season and wouldn’t have been on the fantasy radar even if he was active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor (thumb) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: He’s considered week-to-week and didn’t practice on either of the first two days of the week. Taylor will likely be ruled out on Friday, opening the door for Kenyon Sadiq to see a workload elevation against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.headline: Mason Taylor (thumb) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/mason-tayl.analysis: Taylor, according to head coach Aaron Glenn, will “be just fine.” That could mean he’ll be ready for the Jets’ Week 3 game against the Lions. Through two games Taylor leads the team in tight end routes while rookie Kenyon Sadiq leads in tight end targets. Sadiq, being targeted on 17 percent of his routes, would be a nice streaming play in Week 3 if Taylor is sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq caught 1-of-3 targets for 12 yards in the Jets’ Week 6 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Although there was an injury-shortened appearance mixed in, Sadiq now has just three catches for 15 yards over his past three games. This, as Mason Taylor has caught nine balls for 57 yards over the past two weeks. Sadiq’s big-play ability is going to come back into play sooner rather than later, but he is unsurprisingly maxing out as a zero-floor TE2 in fantasy for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) is active for Week 6 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Sadiq made quick work of the league’s concussion protocol, for better or worse. With Omar Cooper Jr. also active vs. the Pats, Sadiq isn’t much more than a low-end TE2 prayer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Sadiq left Week 5 with a concussion. He was upgraded to a full practice on Friday and seemingly cleared the league’s concussion protocol over the weekend. With Mason Taylor and Omar Cooper Jr. back for Week 6, there will likely be fewer targets to go around in a Jets offense that has regressed heavily over the past two weeks. Sadiq is a low-end TE2 for his date with New England.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) is questionable for New York’s Week 6 game against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: He did upgrade to a full practice and Aaron Glenn told reporters he expects Sadiq to play. Sadiq’s fantasy upside is well-known, but with Mason Taylor back and Omar Cooper Jr. also pushing to play, his target volume has shrunk quite a bit from some of the early-season scenarios we’ve seen. He’s likely a TE2 at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq (concussion) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: He has been limited twice and doesn’t look close to clearing concussion protocol. It’s become rarer for players to launch a Friday comeback to get off protocol, but it’s not unprecedented. Sadiq looks like he’s on the doubtful side of questionable heading into Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq remains in the league’s concussion protocol.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: The good news is that Sadiq was able to practice in a limited capacity on Wednesday. Sadiq suffered the head injury in Week 5 against Cleveland and did not return to action. Mason Taylor led the team’s tight ends with a 59 percent route rate against the Browns, catching all three of his targets for 23 yards. If Sadiq remains in the protocol tomorrow, he would be a long shot to play in Week 6. Taylor in that case would be a desperation streaming option in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq suffered a concussion in the Jets’ Week 5 game against the Browns and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: To make matters worse, Sadiq suffered the injury in the process of losing a fumble. Targeted on a 3rd-and-9 near the goal line in the third quarter, Sadiq was short of the first down and got “Peanut punched” for the giveaway. With neither side getting anything going in rainy New Jersey conditions, Sadiq had just two receptions for three yards before going down, getting out-produced by a returning Mason Taylor in the process. Now highly questionable for Week 6 against the Patriots, Sadiq will not be on the streamer radar if given the go-ahead.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Jets TE Mason Taylor (thumb) is practicing in full for Week 5 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: Taylor’s return could be problematic for rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq. Sadiq posted a 7/105/1 receiving line two weeks ago before goose-egging last week. Taylor is not a serious receiving threat, but he can eat into Sadiq’s snap share. Sadiq likely remains a viable TE1, but his volatility just increased a tad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq did not catch any of his three targets in the Jets’ Week 4 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: A week after breaking out with 105 yards on seven catches against Detroit, Sadiq came up empty. He ran a route on 12 of the Jets’ 20 drop backs on a miserably low volume day for the New York offense. Sadiq split routes with Jeremy Ruckert, a less-than-bullish sign for the rookie’s involvement in the Jets offense moving forward. Sadiq will have some streaming appeal in Week 5 against the Browns if Mason Taylor remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.headline: Kenyon Sadiq (back) is questionable for New York’s Week 4 game against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenyon-sad.analysis: He did get in another limited session today, his third in a row, which would suggest he has a strong chance of playing. Sadiq will get a rankings boost with Breece Hall, Adonai Mitchell, and Mason Taylor all ruled out. He’s a fringe TE1, but one with an extremely high ceiling after last week’s 7/105/1 line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Kenneth Gainwell rushed two times for 17 yards in the Bucs’ Week 6 loss to the Steelers, adding one catch for seven yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: There isn’t much to say here. Gainwell has topped out at five carries in a single game this year, and that came all the way back in Week 1. He hasn’t caught more than three passes in a game either, so even the PPR scam that he operated in Pittsburgh has been shut down. Gainwell isn’t in the fantasy conversation headed into Week 7 versus Carolina.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Kenneth Gainwell rushed three times for five yards in the Bucs’ Week 4 loss to the Packers, adding two catches for 22 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Gainwell wasn’t awfully involved in the Bucs’ game plan, but he took the field for almost as many routes as Bucky Irving and cashed in with a 10-yard score in the second half. It was his first touchdown as a Buccaneer. Gainwell is still averaging just 5.3 touches per game, but this performance could earn him more work going forward, specifically on passing downs. He will be a low-end RB4 for Week 5 against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Buccaneers OC Zac Robinson said game flow and productivity have limited RB Kenny Gainwell’s usage.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: The Buccaneers are 0-3, so if trailing game scripts aren’t the ideal setup for a receiving specialist, we aren’t sure what is. Robinson said he would like to get Gainwell more involved, but also added that Gainwell has to earn those reps by being more productive. Robinson said he also wants to get RB3 Sean Tucker more involved during the same presser. It sounds like this backfield still belongs to starting RB Bucky Irving, who is dealing with a glute injury, but changes are at least being considered.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Buccaneers OC Zac Robinson said he wants to get RB Sean Tucker going.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Robinson described Tucker as being “special with the ball in his hands,” and said that it’s on the coaching staff to find spots to mix him in. Whether this impacts starting RB Bucky Irving basically comes down to how and when — and if — the Buccaneers get Tucker involved. Taking a few snaps away from RB2 Kenneth Gainwell would be no big deal. Utilizing Tucker in the red zone would be consequential for Irving. Hopefully, Robinson provides more insight before his team’s Week 4 game against the Packers. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles said Bucky Irving “is not on the team’s injury report” after Week 3.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Irving was spotted on the sideline for the majority of the fourth quarter. It’s possible that Irving just did something that irked Bowles rather than actually suffering an injury, but given how Irving’s injuries quickly manifested last season, we’re going to want to see that on the official injury report on Wednesday before we dial the status down to “unconcerned.” This news does seem to leave Kenny Gainwell as a lower-priority waiver claim.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Kenny Gainwell had three rushes for -4 yards in the Bucs’ Week 3 loss to the Vikings, adding two catches for 14 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Gainwell was once again inefficient with his limited opportunities. He operated as the team’s lead back, however, when Bucky Irving exited with a lower body injury. If Irving misses any time, Gainwell would profile as a top-24 PPR option, even if he loses touches to Sean Tucker. Tampa could be without Baker Mayfield (thumb) for a while. That would dampen the prospects of everyone in the offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Kenneth Gainwell had two rushes for ten yards in the Bucs’ Week 2 loss against the Browns, adding three catches for five yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Gainwell saw some pass-catching involvement once the Bucs fell behind Cleveland, but it was once again Bucky Irving who worked as Tampa’s clear No. 1 back, seeing 19 touches, including most of the early-down opportunities. Irving’s domination of the Bucs backfield through two weeks means Gainwell is nothing more than a bench stash in 12-team formats for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Kenny Gainwell rushed five times for 15 yards in the Bucs’ Week 1 loss to the Bengals, adding a three-yard reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Shockingly, Gainwell got out-targeted 7-1 by Bucky Irving, though Pro Football Focus did chart Irving’s snaps advantage at a far more modest 35-26. Gainwell was out there. He simply wasn’t a focal point when it came to getting the ball. It was a bizarre contest with sacks and fumbles derailing the Bucs’ offense, but we would have thought this kind of comeback game script would have led to far more Gainwell receptions. Maybe it was just a fluke, but Irving is a safe RB2 heading into Week 2 while Gainwell is now a more uncertain FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Buccaneers RB Sean Tucker (hamstring) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles said earlier this week that Tucker will be a game-time decision for Week 1 against the Bengals. His continued absence from practice is discouraging, but it bodes well for RB Bucky Irving and RB Kenneth Gainwell. Tucker is not expected to be a high-volume offensive contributor at this point, but adding even a couple of touches to each player’s workload is helpful

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.headline: Bucky Irving rushed three times for 14 yards in the Buccaneers’ preseason Week 2 game against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kenneth-ga.analysis: The starting offense played two series consisting of eight plays before giving way to the second unit, wherein Irving saw a carry on the first three plays from scrimmage before Gainwell entered the game. Gainwell received his lone carry on the following play, with neither back seeing another opportunity before departing. Previous talk surrounding this backfield hinted at more of a “1A-1B” situation than what was seen in their first preseason action, widening the range of outcomes of Irving in a fantasy setting for the coming season. That leaves potential room for upside considering Irving’s No. 55 overall aggregate ADP across all platforms, particularly considering how much the coaching staff has talked up his receiving chops this offseason. Consider Irving an interesting upside bet in the fifth round.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Cade Otton caught 1-of-2 targets for four yards in the Bucs’ Week 6 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: Otton had caught between three and five passes in every game this year until today, so this goes down as his first true bust of the season. On the other hand, he has peaked at five catches and 56 yards with zero touchdowns thus far, so the ceiling has been nonexistent. Otton could increase his production once Baker Mayfield is back in the lineup, but it doesn’t look like that will happen next week. He is barely in the TE2 conversation as long as Jalon Daniels remains under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Cade Otton caught 4-of-6 targets for 37 yards in the Bucs’ Week 4 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: Otton’s 37 yards were somehow enough to lead Tampa Bay, though that largely speaks to the ineffective nature of the team’s passing attack. With Jalon Daniels under center, there simply wasn’t much production to go around. He was intercepted twice and threw for just 148 yards. With Daniels likely to make his second start of the year on Week 5, Otton is a low-end TE2 for his upcoming matchup with Dallas.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Cade Otton caught 3-of-6 targets for 56 yards in the Bucs’ Week 3 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: As usual, Otton led the Bucs in pass routes and was second on the team in targets behind Emeka Egbuka. Most of Otton’s production came on a 37-yard catch in the first half. Baker Mayfield narrowly missed the tight end for another long gain later in the contest. Otton’s route involvement should keep him in deep league lineups next week against the Packers, unless Mayfield (hand) is sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Cade Otton caught 5-of-6 targets for 38 yards in the Bucs’ Week 2 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: Otton led the Bucs in targets while running nearly every route. This has been Otton’s role for quite some time. You know what you’re getting if you use Otton in fantasy lineups: He’s something of a PPR cheat code when the Bucs hit a negative game script. He’ll be a deep league option in Week 3 against the Vikings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Cade Otton caught 3-of-5 targets for 26 yards in the Bucs’ Week 1 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: This is about a standard Otton statline, though this one came on a day where Baker Mayfield attempted fewer than 30 passes. With Jalen McMillan sidelined, Otton probably would have exceeded five catches had the Bucs not kept killing drives with sacks and turnovers, alas. Otton is always good for a few PPR points on the back end of the TE2 ranks, but that appears to be his ceiling heading in to his age-27 campaign.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Buccaneers TE Cade Otton said there is “a lot of play action” in new OC Zac Robinson’s scheme.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: This is the kind of thing we like to hear for QB Baker Mayfield and his pass catchers. Robinson did not feature play action during his two seasons as the Falcons’ offensive coordinator, nor did former Buccaneers OC Josh Grizzard, so Otton’s comments are reassuring. Per PFF, NFL offenses averaged 7.76 yards per pass play with play action and just 6.72 without it. Upping the play action rate should help the Buccaneers run a more efficient offense in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Bucs and Chargers are hosting Georgia TE Oscar Delp for top-30 pre-draft visits.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: Delp last week made pre-draft visits with the Vikings, Patriots, and Ravens. Delp at Georgia was a little-used tight end who totaled 65 receptions for 793 yards and seven touchdowns over his final three collegiate seasons. He was targeted on a meager 13 percent of his pass routes over those three years. Delp, 23, profiles as a rotational tight end to start his NFL career, though he has some upside if he lands in the right spot. In LA he would compete with Oronde Gadsden II for tight end snaps and routes, and in Tampa he would compete with Cade Otton, who recently re-signed with the Bucs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Buccaneers re-signed TE Cade Otton to a three-year, $30 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: Otton, 26, will remain with the Bucs for the foreseeable future on a new deal that guarantees him $20 million. The former fourth-round pick has gone for 500-plus yards in each of his last two seasons, and caught 59 passes for 572 passes and one touchdown last season. A versatile tight end who can play in line, out wide, and in the slot, Otton has finished second in receptions each of the last two seasons for the Buccaneers. He’ll be a decent plug-and-play tight end for the upcoming fantasy season but is unlikely to have consistent TE1 value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Cade Otton caught 7-of-9 targets for 94 yards and a touchdown in the Buccaneers’ Week 18 win over Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: Calling Otton the top target for Tampa Bay in the passing game is quite the understatement; as no other receiver had 40 yards. The 26-year-old tight end not only had a touchdown, but picked up what was essentially a game-clinching first down late in the game on a connection with Baker Mayfield. Amazingly it was the first touchdown of the season for Otton, but outside of those lack of scores it was a solid season for the fourth-year player. Otton will head to free agency after the season. He could get a chance to find the end zone again in the playoffs, but they’ll need the Saints to upset the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.headline: Cade Otton caught all four of his targets for 33 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 17 loss to the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cade-otton.analysis: Otton has a fixed role as the TE1 in the Bucs’ offense. This meant the sixth-most targets on the team against the Dolphins, mostly in the short area and over the middle of the field. With Chris Godwin and Jalen McMillan also taking many of Baker Mayfield’s targets between the sticks, Otton barely has TE2 utility heading into Week 18.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson caught 4-of-6 targets for 44 yards in the Jets’ Week 6 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson’s second quietest effort of the season came as he dealt with Christian Gonzalez’s stingy coverage and first-round rookie teammate Omar Cooper Jr. returned from his ankle injury. With Adonai Mitchell (finger) likely — hopefully — soon returning from his marathon absence, Wilson is set to have a lot more target competition in the Jets’ receiver corps, but those extra bodies should also create more space for the Jets’ No. 1. Wilson remains a high-end WR2 heading into next week’s plus matchup with the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson caught 7-of-11 targets for 104 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 5 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: The 100-yard effort was Wilson’s second in three weeks. It was no easy feat on a rainy afternoon in Jersey where Geno Smith completed only 17 passes. Wilson’s score was a 32-yarder where he spun out of a tackle for a catch-and-run house call. In addition to the 100-yard efforts, Wilson now has a score in three of his past four appearances. It’s like Wilson’s lost 2025 never happened, which is exactly what the Jets and fantasy managers were hoping for. A weekly fixture in the low-end WR1 ranks, Wilson has a Week 6 date with the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson caught 3-of-4 targets for 27 yards in the Jets’ Week 4 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: No one on the Jets offense got home for fantasy purposes as the Bears held on to the ball for several long drives in the second half. The Jets possessed the ball for just 17 minutes on the day. Wilson’s four targets led the New York offense, as Geno Smith was limited to a mere 15 pass attempts. Wilson continues to dominate air yards and targets in the Jets offense and should remain in all lineups next week against Cleveland.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Jets coach Aaron Glenn said Garrett Wilson was evaluated for a concussion and was cleared to return in the Jets’ Week 3 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson took a hard hit late in the fourth quarter and was slow to get up. The Jets turned the ball over on the next play, so we never got to see Wilson return, but it sounds like he would have been back on the field had the game gone to overtime. Wilson ended the day with 10 catches for 107 yards and a touchdown on 13 targets. He found the end zone on an incredible circus catch late in the fourth quarter to tie the game up. As expected, Wilson was the focal point of the Jets’ passing attack with Adonai Mitchell sidelined. Even if Mitchell returns next week versus the Bears, Wilson will be moving up the WR2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson caught 5-of-7 targets for 57 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 2 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson saw five fewer targets than Adonai Mitchell, but played more snaps and ran more routes. Mitchell simply sees more quick-hitter looks close to the line of scrimmage, while Wilson is used more over the middle of the field. The Packers also frequently sent safety help over to Wilson’s side, but the 26-year-old was still able to make a few big catches when they mattered. He should be in for a bigger day against the Lions next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson caught 6-of-7 targets for 79 yards in the Jets’ Week 1 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: With the Jets in the unusual position of dominating a game from whistle to whistle, new QB Geno Smith dropped back just 24 times. Translation, Wilson coming away with seven targets was actually a pretty good outcome. The Jets’ blocking appeared much improved, but this was not a true test, even if it came on the road. That will come in Week 2 for the Jets’ home opener against the Packers. Wilson will remain a solid WR2 whose high floor will hopefully be accompanied by more ceiling efforts this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich said he’s been “so impressed” with Geno Smith’s play.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Reich has reportedly added wrinkles to the offense he deployed as head coach of the Colts and Panthers. At both of those stops his offenses were near the bottom of the league in most basic offensive metrics. Smith, meanwhile, has looked sharp as the team’s starting quarterback throughout training camp and in limited preseason snaps. He’ll look to bounce back from a nightmarish statistical 2025 season in Vegas. Jets players, including Garrett Wilson, told The Athletic that they have enjoyed the “player empowerment” that comes along with Reich’s coaching style and his offensive scheming, which leaves room for improvisation. The Jets offense could be functional as long as Smith, 35, is healthy and upright.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Garrett Wilson said his knee has felt “great” at practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Wilson’s knee injury cost him 10 games last season, but the star receiver is in a good spot this offseason. Wilson is participating in OTAs and also had praise for his quarterback, Geno Smith, who he said throws a “friendly ball.” It’s an encouraging sign for the 25-year-old receiver who posted three-straight 1,000-yard seasons to start his career before his 2025 season was derailed. He’s the unquestioned WR1 on the Jets’ depth chart and is surrounded by unproven talent in Adonai Mitchell and rookie Omar Cooper Jr. Wilson will have high-end WR2 upside this season with a chance to crack the top-12 at his position in fantasy in a new-look offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: SNY’s Connor Hughes reports the Jets are “open to dealing & listening.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: The reports comes off the heels of New York swapping Jermaine Johnson for T’Vondre Sweat. Hughes made it clear the Jets aren’t having a fire sale, though it’s hard to see this as anything else. They sent most of their big names packing at the trade deadline last year, with Sauce Gardner, Quinnen Williams, and Michael Carter all traded. At this point, the Jets are running out of players to deal, even if they want to keep making moves. Justin Fields is expected to be released, but a team looking to sign him could guarantee his services by trading for him. Garrett Wilson was also the subject of trade rumors last year, though the Jets just inked him to a long-term deal and didn’t seem interested in moving him at the deadline.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.headline: Jets HC Aaron Glenn said Garrett Wilson (knee) will not return this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/garrett-wi.analysis: Glenn had been reluctant to say in recent weeks whether Wilson would return this season, but he has finally confirmed that his WR1 will be shut down for the remainder of the season. Wilson suffered a knee sprain in Week 6 against the Broncos and re-aggravated that same injury in Week 11. The Week 11 injury landed Wilson on injured reserve, meaning he wouldn’t be eligible to return until Week 15. With the Jets in the final weeks of another lost season, there was little reason to force Wilson back on the field and risk another injury. Wilson caught 36 passes for 395 yards and four touchdowns in the seven games he appeared in this season while averaging 8.4 targets per game. This will mark the first time in his four-year career that Wilson failed to go for 1,000 yards, but there’s little reason to believe he won’t be ready to bounce back next season. The Jets have a lot to figure out this offseason, especially at the quarterback position following the failed Justin Fields experiment. Despite the question marks in the team’s QB room, Wilson should profile as a high-upside WR2 in fantasy next season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin caught 4-of-8 targets for 37 yards in the Bucs’ Week 6 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: Godwin’s eight targets today go down as a season-high, but he failed to make much of his opportunities, per usual. The veteran wideout hasn’t hit 50 receiving yards in a game this year and is still looking for his first touchdown of the season. With Emeka Egbuka pulling away as the team’s WR1, there isn’t much volume headed Godwin’s way. With Jalon Daniels likely to make another start next week, Godwin is tumbling down the WR4 ranks ahead of Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin caught all three targets for 37 yards in the Buccaneers’ Week 5 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: Godwin’s three targets finished tied for fourth on the team behind Emeka Egbuka, Cade Otton, and Kenny Gainwell on a night backup quarterback Jalon Daniels attempted only 25 passes. Week 5 now marks the fourth game in five tries in which Godwin was held to four targets or fewer, leaving the veteran wide receiver completely unusable in a fantasy setting, for the time being. He can safely be stashed on benches ahead of a Week 6 meeting with the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin caught 6-of-7 targets for 31 yards in the Bucs’ Week 4 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: UDFA rookie Jalon Daniels made his first career start and leaned on Godwin for some easy completions. Godwin led the team in catches and targets, though Cade Otton surprisingly led the way in yards with 37. Godwin set new season highs in targets and catches. The Bucs are operating an incredibly low-wattage offense without Baker Mayfield, but Godwin could continue to see enough work to return WR4 numbers in PPR leagues. He will put that to the test versus the Cowboys in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin (ankle) is not on Tampa Bay’s final Week 4 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: Godwin was a full participant for two straight days after a Wednesday DNP. The insertion of Jalon Daniels makes him (well, makes every Buccaneers player) hard to trust for Week 4, but Godwin is probably still in the FLEX conversation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin (ankle) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: Godwin should be expected to play in Week 4 against the Packers at this point, although he has mostly underperformed thus far. Buccaneers OC Zac Robinson said earlier that Godwin Jr. “is a stud and will continue to do his thing. The ball will find him.” That might be harder than one imagines with an undrafted free agent rookie at quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin (ankle) returned to practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: It will likely go down as a limited session for the veteran wideout, but Godwin should be on track to play in Week 4. The bad news is that he will do so with UDFA rookie Jalon Daniels as his quarterback. Godwin was already off to a slow start, and things aren’t likely to improve with a backup quarterback under center. He is low-wattage FLEX play for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin (ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: Godwin’s history of lower-leg injuries makes this a little bit concerning. The veteran wide receiver is already set to catch passes from a backup quarterback. If active, he may be playing on an injured ankle. He can only be viewed as a boom-bust FLEX at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin caught 3-of-4 targets for 25 yards in the Bucs’ Week 3 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: Godwin had a long touchdown grab called back on a holding penalty in the second half — a deflating moment for the Bucs in their comeback attempt against the elite Minnesota defense. Godwin was third on the team in targets on a low-volume day for the Tampa offense. Godwin, who has ten receptions over three games this year, won’t have much fantasy appeal going forward if Baker Mayfield’s hand/thumb injury proves to be of the long-term variety.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin caught all three of his targets for 46 yards in the Bucs’ Week 2 loss against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: The Bucs main slot receiver saw some early involvement but was invisible for most of the second half as the Bucs pushed the ball downfield. Godwin, who now has 86 yards on seven grabs through two games, is a WR4 option in a struggling Tampa offense. Until Baker Mayfield improves, Godwin should stay on benches in most fantasy formats, especially against the formidable Minnesota defense in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.headline: Chris Godwin caught 4-of-4 targets for 40 yards in the Bucs’ Week 1 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-godw.analysis: With sacks and turnovers short-circuiting the Bucs’ offense, Godwin and company were limited to 52 total plays. Godwin was out-targeted 6-4 by Emeka Egbuka, but was on the field for 49-of-57 snaps in Jalen McMillan’s absence. Not that we would expect McMillan to cut into Godwin’s playing time upon his return. One of Godwin’s grabs produced a vicious stiff arm. He’s looking like a legitimate WR3 heading into Week 2 against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarvion-.headline: Cowboys declared LB DeMarvion Overshown, CB Cobie Durant, S Alijah Clark, RB Emari Demercado, OLB James Houston, T Drew Shelton, and WR Camden Brown inactive for Week 6 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarvion-.analysis: Overshown remains absent with his hamstring injury. Recent acquisition Joey Porter Jr is active after missing Week 5 with an illness. The Cowboys look to shake off an ugly Week 5 loss against the surging Packers on Sunday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarvion-.headline: Cowboys declared LB DeMarvion Overshown, CB Cobie Durant, CB Caelen Carson, RB Emari Demercado, OL James Houston, OL Ajani Cornelius, and WR Camden Brown inactive for Week 4 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarvion-.analysis: Every player on here was ruled out before the weekend. The Cowboys continue have lost several key defenders through the early part of the season and will now have to find a way to slow a Houston offense that will have Nico Collins back for the first time in two weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarvion-.headline: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring) will not play in Week 4 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarvion-.analysis: Overshown will miss a third straight game with his hamstring injury, and has “a little ways to go” before returning to the field. Overshown was injured in the Cowboys’ Week 1 game against the Giants. We’ll see if he can get on the field for Week 5’s game against the Buccaneers, but with that game being on a Thursday night, it wouldn’t be a surprise if we learned Overshown would miss a fourth straight game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarvion-.headline: Cowboys declared LB DeMarvion Overshown, CB Cobie Durant, S Malik Hooker, RB Emari Demercado, OG Ajani Cornelius, and WR Camden Brown inactive for Week 3 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarvion-.analysis: Durant, Hooker, and Overshown were all ruled out before the weekend, so there’s nothing surprising here. The Cowboys are down four key players on the defensive side of the ball, which could make for a big day for Lamar Jackson and the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarvion-.headline: Cowboys ruled out LB DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring) for Dallas’ Week 3 game against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarvion-.analysis: No surprise, as he was expected to be ruled out following Wednesday. The Cowboys also ruled out CB Cobie Durant, S Malik Hooker and S P.J. Locke, each of whom are dealing with long-term ailments.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarvion-.headline: Cowboys LB DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring) is not expected to travel to Brazil for Week 3 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarvion-.analysis: Overshown will now, apparently, miss his second game this season. He will be missed. The Cowboys’ defense is tasked with stymying the Ravens’ top-tier rushing attack, led by RB Derrick Henry and QB Lamar Jackson.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarvion-.headline: Cowboys declared LB DeMarvion Overshown, CB Caelen Carson, S Malik Hooker, RB Tyler Goodson, LB James Houston, OL Ajani Cornelius, and WR Camden Brown inactive for Week 2 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarvion-.analysis: Nothing surprising here, as Overshown and Hooker were both ruled out before the weekend, leaving the Cowboys without two starters on the defensive side of the ball. The Cowboys and Commanders are both looking to pick up a win this weekend to avoid starting 0-2 what projects to be a tough NFC East.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarvion-.headline: DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring) is not expected to play in Week 2 against the
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarvion-.analysis: The Cowboys are already without fellow starter Malik Hooker because of a broken bone in his wrist. Overshown is expected to miss a week or two with a hamstring strain. After getting decimated by Jaxon Dart in Week 1, the Cowboys will now have to face the Commanders without two of their starters on defense. This is as good as bounce-back spots get for the Washington offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarvion-.headline: Cowboys declared WR Ryan Flournoy (knee) inactive for Week 17 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarvion-.analysis: Flournoy is dealing with a knee injury he suffered in Week 16 against the Chargers. He failed to get in a full practice on a short week and is now ruled out, making KaVontae Turpin the Cowboys’ No. 3 wide receiver for the week. The Cowboys also declared LB DeMarvion Overshown, CB Caelen Carson, RB Jaydon Blue, DT Jay Toia, and DT Perrion Winfrey inactive for Week 17 against the Commanders. Overshown is out with a concussion suffered in Week 16.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarvion-.headline: Cowboys activated LB DeMarvion Overshown (knee) from the PUP list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/demarvion-.analysis: It was the last day the Cowboys could conceivably activate him after designating him to return three weeks ago, so we don’t know if Overshown is actually game-ready yet. The Cowboys were on bye this past week, and Overshown was still picking up limited practices ahead of their Week 9 game against the Cardinals. Dallas also activated rookie CB Shavon Revel (knee) from the non-football injury list — he faces much the same uncertainty. Both of these players should be boosts for a beleaguered Cowboys back seven. When they’ll actually debut is a question we don’t have an answer for yet.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.headline: Isaiah Davis rushed seven times for 16 yards in the Jets’ Week 6 loss to the Patriots, adding a 10-yard reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.analysis: This was by far Davis’ biggest workload during Breece Hall’s (quad) ongoing absence, though Braelon Allen continued to dominate snaps and touches. Hall has to be getting close to a return, but even if he remains for Week 7 against the Dolphins, Davis has not shown earn to merit second FLEX treatment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.headline: Isaiah Davis rushed two times for eight yards in the Jets’ Week 5 win over the Browns, adding a nine-yard reception.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.analysis: Davis at least touched the ball after his Week 4 doughnut, but Pro Football Focus charted him as getting out-snapped 60-10 by fill-in No. 2 Braelon Allen. Decisive, to say the least. Even if Breece Hall (quad) is forced to miss his third straight game in Week 6, Davis hasn’t shown enough to warrant a 12-team league looksee.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.headline: Braelon Allen rushed four times for 14 yards in the Jets’ Week 3 loss to the Lions, adding three catches for three yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.analysis: Breece Hall suffered a thigh injury late in this game and did not return, leaving Allen as the lead back for the Jets’ final two drives. He touched the ball six times on the pair of drives. Fellow backup Isaiah Davis did not touch the ball once. His role would likely grow if Hall misses time, but Allen is the clear target in his backfield on waivers. Allen would push for an RB2 ranking if Hall is sidelined for Week 4 against the Bears.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.headline: ESPN’s Rich Cimini reports Jets RB Breece Hall (groin) said he is “good to go and can handle a full workload, if necessary.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.analysis: It’s unclear whether Hall added the “if necessary” bit or if Cimini did, but regardless, this is good to hear. Hall is practicing in full leading up to the Jets’ Week 1 game against the Titans and can be treated as an RB1. Jets RB3 Isaiah Davis (knee) is also practicing fully.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.headline: Jets HC Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall suffered a strained groin in Monday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.analysis: Glenn said he doesn’t believe Hall’s injury “was a big deal,” but said the star RB will be evaluated. It sounds like Hall avoided anything too serious, but given the nature of these types of injuries, it wouldn’t be surprising if Hall was sidelined for at least a few days. With Hall and Isaiah Davis (knee) both sidelined, the Jets are relatively thin at RB at the moment. Braelon Allen will slide into RB1 duties until Hall can return, and remains an intriguing late-round pick as the handcuff for Hall in fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.headline: The Athletic’s Zack Rosenblatt believes Isaiah Davis is the “early favorite” for the Jets’ backup running back job.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.analysis: Rosenblatt led his breakdown by noting that Davis and Braelon Allen will both get snaps, so there isn’t likely to be a clear winner behind Breece Hall. Allen missed most of the 2025 season with a knee injury. In his absence, the Jets leaned on Davis as a pass-catcher to give Hall the occasional breather. He was targeted 28 times and brought down 21 of them for 186 yards. Davis has also been effective between the tackles, averaging 5.6 yards per carry through two seasons compared to 3.7 for Allen. The Jets’ backup job could have some appeal in deeper fantasy leagues, but it sounds like fantasy managers will want to get more info from training camp before placing their bets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.headline: Jets coach Aaron Glenn said he’s planning to use Breece Hall, Braelon Allen, and Isaiah Davis as a “three-headed monster” this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.analysis: Glenn reportedly wanted to use his backfield in a similar fashion last season before Allen went down in Week 4, according to an article published by ESPN. This would be potentially brutal news for fantasy managers eyeing Breece Hall in drafts, although it is worth pointing out that in the three complete games both Hall and Allen played together, Hall appeared on 59 percent of the team’s snaps while Allen played on 29 percent of snaps, and Davis just 15 percent. Hall also had 51 total opportunities over that span, while Allen and Davis combined for 22 opportunities. Time will tell if Glenn and offensive coordinator Frank Reich really do lean into this “three-headed monster” idea, but it’s hard to imagine Hall, who recently signed a three-year, $43.5 million contract, losing enough work to be forced out of the mix as a fringe RB1/RB2 given his three-down skillset. That said, both Allen and Davis could serve as viable late-round handcuffs for Hall should he ever miss time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.headline: Braelon Allen said he is up to 250 pounds and is the biggest, strongest, and fastest he has ever been.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.analysis: Despite adding 15 pounds since entering the NFL, Allen said this is the lowest his body fat percentage has ever been. Allen missed most of the 2025 season with a knee injury that eventually required surgery. At this point, it sounds like his recovery is complete. Head coach Aaron Glenn talked up his potential in the passing game, though he said that he views Breece Hall, Allen, and Isaiah Davis as a “three-headed monster.” Allen could have some minor stand-alone value as a short-yardage back this year, but the presence of Davis will likely prevent him from making much of an impact on the redraft fantasy landscape.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.headline: Jets RB Breece Hall (knee) is questionable to play in Week 18 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.analysis: When asked if Hall will play, Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said, “we’ll see.” Glenn has played coy with most start-sit decisions in the Jets’ 3-13 season. No reason to stop now. Hall logged just two limited sessions to close the week. He is scheduled to enter free agency at the end of the season. Preserving his health for free agency could be the smart move. He may wish to put his stamp on the season with a strong showing, though. It would be difficult to project his playing time if he is active. Treat him as a volatile RB2 if he suits up. His backup, RB Isaiah Davis (concussion), has been ruled out, leaving Kene Nwangwu (quad) and Khalil Herbert behind Hall.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.headline: Jets RB Isaiah Davis (concussion) won’t play in New York’s Week 18 game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-dav.analysis: Davis never really had a sustained run where he looked to potentially be the lead back in his second season, finishing with a 43/236/1 line on the ground and never crossing the 10-carry threshold. It’s likely that if Breece Hall isn’t brought back, Davis will remain behind Braelon Allen (knee) on the depth chart to open 2026. Davis could grow into a bigger receiving role if Hall leaves, making him a potential Kenny Gainwell-type player next year and someone who could be on the draft radar in what, well, doesn’t look like a very good team at the moment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.headline: Packers declared OL Aaron Banks, CB Benjamin St-Juste, OL Jager Burton, and OL Donovan Jennings inactive for Week 6 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.analysis: No real surprises from the Packers as they look to continue their recent momentum forward as they chase the Vikings and Bears in the competitive NFC North. The team also appears set to get back franchise running back Josh Jacobs for Week 7 after it was reported the veteran back will be removed from the commissioner exempt list Monday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.headline: Packers declared OG Aaron Banks, OL Jacon Monk, DL Anthony Campbell, and RG Kevin Zeitler inactive for Week 4 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.analysis: Banks missed Week 1 with the knee issue. He suited up in Week 2 but aggravated the injury and has been out ever since. He is also dealing with a toe injury, per the injury report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.headline: Packers declared CB Benjamin St-Juste, OL John Williams, OL Travis Glover, DT Warren Brinson, and DT Javon Hargrave inactive for Week 2 against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.analysis: That means that starting left guard Aaron Banks (knee) will be back on the field after missing Week 1 against the Vikings. In a game that figures to be played in constant rain, having a fully healthy offensive line will be a nice boost for Marshawn Lloyd and the Packers’ offense. Javon Hargrave (concussion) remains out for Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.headline: Packers declared OG Aaron Banks, LB Ty’Ron Hopper, OL Travis Glover, WR J. Michael Sturdivant, DT Warren Brinson, and DT Anthony Campbell inactive for Week 1 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.analysis: Banks is dealing with knee tendinitis. He was limited in practice throughout the week before being listed as questionable. Rookie Jager Burton is expected to start at left guard.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.headline: Packers restructured OG Aaron Banks’ contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.analysis: According to ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler, this “simple restructure” will reduce Banks’ 2026 cap hit down to $24.8 million. Banks, who was drafted in the second round by the 49ers back in 2021, signed a four-year contract with the Packers last offseason and is under contract through 2028. The five-year vet started 14 of the 15 games he appeared in for the Packers in 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.headline: Packers declared K Brandon McManus, DL Devonte Wyatt, OT Anthony Belton and CB Kamal Hadden inactive for Week 6 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.analysis: The Packers signed K Lucas Havrisik on Saturday, with McManus nursing a quad injury. Havrisik will kick in McManus’ stead. Green Bay received great news regarding the offensive line’s health. LT Rasheed Walker (quad), LG Aaron Banks (groin/knee), RT Zach Tom (oblique/back) and backup OG/C Jacob Monk are all active this week. The talented unit should keep QB Jordan Love upright against the Bengals. Starting CB Nate Hobbs (concussion) is not on the inactives list, indicating he successfully passed the NFL’s concussion protocol.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.headline: Packers LT Rasheed Walker (quad) is questionable for Week 6 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.analysis: Packers LG Aaron Banks (groin/knee), RT Zach Tom (oblique/back), backup OG/C Jacob Monk (hamstring) and CB Nate Hobbs (concussion) are questionable. On the plus side, backup LT Jordan Morgan (knee) will be active. Packers backup OT Anthony Belton (ankle) is out. The Packers are 2-1-1 despite the lengthy offensive line injury list. If the unit can get healthy later this year, this team will be a force to be reckoned with.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.headline: Packers RB Josh Jacobs (ankle) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.analysis: Jacobs should handle another high-end RB1 workload against the Cowboys this week. The Packers will be without both RT Zach Tom (oblique) and his direct backup, RT Anthony Belton, who is on the injury report with an ankle injury. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said Tom injured his knee on Wednesday. It is worth noting that high-ankle sprains and MCL sprains often share the same injury mechanism. Packers LG Aaron Banks (groin) is doubtful to play. On the plus side, TE Tucker Kraft (knee/elbow) will play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.headline: Packers LG Aaron Banks (groin) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.analysis: Jordan Morgan looks like a candidate to get a full game at guard with Banks injuring himself in Week 3 and not practicing in either of the first two sessions of the week. It won’t keep you away from any Packers — this is the Cowboys defense we’re talking about — but it might make their rushing effectiveness go down a bit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.headline: Packers LG Aaron Banks (groin) left Green Bay’s Week 3 game against the Browns and did not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-bank.analysis: He played 31 snaps before leaving at halftime, which kicked Jordan Morgan inside and got Green Bay’s other right tackles on the field to replace the similarly-departed Tom. We wouldn’t be surprised if Banks spent some time on the injury report this week at the very least. Green Bay’s offensive line injuries helped contribute to a disappointing loss against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: Darenll Washington caught 4-of-6 targets for 25 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 6 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: Washington got in the end zone for the third time this year via an RPO toss from Rodgers near the goal line. His six targets were double the total of Pat Freiermuth, who was laboring through a calf injury in this contest. Muth should be healthier and earn more looks next week, making this minor spike game from Washington rather unsustainable. Washington will be a touchdown-or-bust TE2 for his Week 7 date with the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: Pat Freiermuth caught 3-of-5 targets for 17 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 4 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: Freiermuth found the end zone late in the fourth quarter for his second touchdown of the season, tying fellow tight end Darnell Washington for fourth on the team with five targets. Washington managed to corral just two of his five targets but eclipsed the yardage total of Freiermuth with 27 yards while also adding a touchdown of his own. Both tight ends appear unlikely to contribute viable counting stats considering neither has seen more than five targets in a game during the first month of play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Steelers are going to use Jaylen Warren “a lot” while frequently utilizing two-tight end sets in Week 4 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: It sounds like Warren is belongs on the RB1/2 border with Rico Dowdle (toe) sidelined again this week. The Steelers will try to control the line of scrimmage by frequently deploying TEs Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington, both in the run game and as receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: Darnell Washington caught 3-of-4 targets for 67 yards in the Steelers’ Week 3 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: No, Washington can’t be trusted in fantasy, but he sure is fun when he gets a full head of steam. Washington caught a season-high three passes in Sunday’s win over the Bengals and led the Steelers in receiving yards, thanks largely to the 47-yard play he made in the fourth quarter. A true man among boys with the ball in his hands, Washington rumbled through and past multiple defenders on his way to the big gain. While he’s always good for an exciting play or two, Washington can be left on waivers for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: The Athletic’s Mike DeFabo believes TE Pat Freiermuth will be the Steelers’ “go-to pass-catching tight end” this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: The Steelers notably signed TE Darnell Washington to a four-year, $42 million contract extension this offseason, but DeFabo believes Freiermuth is still the team’s TE1. He expects Washington to continue operating as a receiving threat, “especially in the red zone,” but he is apparently stuck in the TE2 role. Washington’s profile is certainly more intriguing, but he may be best viewed as a boom-bust backup option in best ball for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: Steelers signed TE Darnell Washington to a four-year, $42 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: Washington’s contract includes $21 million in guaranteed money. A third-round pick in the 2023 NFL Draft from Georgia, he’s been as advertised so far in his pro career. Washington has only 57 catches, 625 yards and two touchdowns in three seasons, but is a tremendous blocker and extremely difficult to tackle when he has the ball. Listed at 6-foot-7 and 264 pounds, he’s one of the most physically imposing players in the NFL. With a $10.5 million average annual value, Washington is 12th in AAV among tight ends. That level of commitment could be a sign the Steelers plan to use a good amount of two tight end sets with Washington and Pat Freiermuth in head coach Mike McCarthy’s first season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: Steelers TE Darnell Washington had surgery to repair his broken arm.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: Washington underwent surgery Monday and won’t return to the Steelers this season, even if they manage to beat the Ravens in Week 18 and make the playoffs. Washington ends the 2025 season with 31 receptions on 43 targets for 364 yards and one touchdown. He was third among Pittsburgh tight ends in catches, as Jonnu Smith and Pat Freiermuth remains involved in Arthur Smith’s tight end-heavy offensive scheme. With Washington sidelined, Freiermuth would seem to be the main beneficiary. Both Smith and Freiermuth have a 48 percent route participation rate through Week 17.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: Steelers HC Mike Tomlin said Darnell Washington suffered a broken arm in Week 17’s loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: Washington was ruled out shortly after leaving the field in the second quarter of Sunday’s game. The hulking tight end won’t be available for Week 18’s must-win game against the Ravens that will decide the winner of the AFC North, which further hurts a passing game that will already be without DK Metcalf. Both Pat Freiermuth and Jonnu Smith could benefit from an uptick in targets with Washington sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: Darnell Washington (forearm) has been ruled out for the remainder of Week 17’s game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: Washington went down in the second quarter and attempted to come back in for a play. After his lone attempt to gut it out, he left for the sidelines and was ruled out shortly after leaving the field. Washington’s day ends with two receptions for 15 yards on two targets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.headline: Calvin Austin (hamstring) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darnell-wa.analysis: Austin left Week 16’s game with the hamstring injury. He went down in the second half and was listed as questionable to return but never did. A DNP today stacks the odds against him to suit up on Sunday. With DK Metcalf suspended for the remainder of the regular season, Adam Thielen is seemingly the team’s top wideout for Week 17. Aaron Rodgers will also lean heavily on his tight ends versus the Browns, putting Darnell Washington and Pat Freiermuth in the TE2 mix.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Braelon Allen rushed 17 times for 78 yards in the Jets’ Week 6 loss to the Patriots, adding two receptions for 26 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Allen ceded a little more work to Isaiah Davis than he did the past two weeks during Breece Hall’s (quad) ongoing absence, but he still cleared 100 yards from scrimmage for the second consecutive week. Allen was thundering around the field, handing out some nasty stiff arms and broken tackles. Never placed on injured reserve and out for the past three contests, Hall has to be getting close to a return, but we thought the same thing heading into Week 6 before Adonai Mitchell missed his fourth consecutive contest with a finger injury. The Jets don’t seem particularly great at this roster management thing. Allen will remain a high-end RB2 if Hall sits against the lowly Dolphins in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Breece Hall (quad) will not play in Week 6 against the Patriots
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Things have been trending in this direction for Hall all week. The 25-year-old back was a DNP on both Wednesday and Thursday, and will now miss a third straight game as a result of his injury. Braelon Allen will again lead the Jets’ backfield this week against the Patriots and has handled 44 of the Jets’ 48 running back opportunities since Week 4. Allen will be a volatile RB2 against a Patriots defense that ranks 18th against running backs in fantasy scoring this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: ESPN’s Rich Cimini reports that Breece Hall (quad) is working with trainers on the side field on Thursday, yet remains week-to-week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: This is a small but positive update. Hall typically works on his quad rehab program elsewhere or simply observes practice. Today’s return to the side field will still result in him being listed as a non-participant, but as Cimini says, this is measurable “progress” for the Jets’ top running back. Braelon Allen will undoubtedly get the start this week, but perhaps Hall has a chance to return in Week 7 against the Dolphins. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Jets coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) remains week-to-week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Hall will not practice today, and it sounds like he will not practice on Thursday or Friday either. Braelon Allen has played productively in his stead, most recently rushing 24 times for 116 yards and a touchdown against the Browns. Allen is a locked-in RB2 until Hall returns from his upper-leg injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Braelon Allen rushed 24 times for 116 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 5 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Allen surprisingly added just one catch for zero yards on four targets. Not ideal, though Allen’s rushing output nearly doubled his previous career high of 59. It was exactly what the Jets and fantasy managers needed during Breece Hall’s second straight absence with a quad injury. Allen contributed runs of 10, 17, 11 and 22 yards, with that final rush finding the end zone. He also had a 13-yarder called back by holding. In other words, he was both grinding out tough yards and providing longer gains. Isaiah Davis mixed in for only cursory breather back work. With Hall yet to resume practicing, Allen should have another plug-and-play RB2 setup in Week 6 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Breece Hall (quad) will not play in Week 5 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Braelon Allen will once again be in line to lead the Jets’ backfield with Hall sidelined for a second consecutive week. Hall did not practice on Wednesday or Thursday and will presumably be a DNP again on Friday, now that he has been ruled out ahead of practice.
