Allen saw 100 percent of the Jets’ running back opportunities last week, rushing 14 times for 59 scoreless yards while adding two receptions for an additional eight yards on two targets. He’ll be a fringe RB1/RB2 in what should be another high-volume day for the third-year back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) is still “week to week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: It doesn’t look like Hall will practice this week as he recovers from the injury he sustained in Week 3. That would mean Braelon Allen, who saw all 14 running back rushes for New York in Week 4, will again function as the team’s workhorse in Week 5 against the Browns. Allen should still be considered a top-24 option despite the Jets’ immense offensive struggles last week against Chicago. The Browns’ defense is allowing the sixth-highest EPA per rush this season. Hall was officially a non-participant on Wednesday’s injury report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Braelon Allen had 14 rushes for 59 yards in the Jets’ Week 4 loss to the Bears, adding two catches for eight yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Allen accounted for every running back rushing attempt for New York with Breece Hall (quad) sidelined. He also ran a route on 14 of the team’s 19 drop backs on a low-volume day for the Jets offense. It’s fantastic usage, even if it didn’t amount to much in the lopsided affair. Allen should remain in lineups next week against the Browns if Hall remains out. His pass game involvement could give Allen plenty of weekly upside for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Breece Hall (quad) will not play in Week 4 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Hall was initially mentioned as being week-to-week when he was diagnosed with his quad injury, so he was never really considered a candidate to play in Week 4 despite the team waiting until the end of the week to rule him out. With Hall out, the Jets will look to Braelon Allen to handle most of the backfield duties. Allen will profile as a solid RB2 candidate with a chance for more upside in what could be a high-volume day against the Bears. In addition to Hall, the Jets also ruled out OG Dylan Parham (knee), TE Mason Taylor (thumb), and LB Kiko Mauigoa (quad) for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.headline: Breece Hall (quad) did not practice Wednsday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/braelon-al.analysis: Hall went down with a quad injury on Sunday against the Lions and did not return to the game. Braelon Allen took over as the Jets’ lead back, a role he’ll likely continue to occupy in Week 4 against the Bears’ gettable rush defense if Hall is sidelined. Allen should be rostered in all leagues and could be a top-20 option in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Devin Singletary rushed four times for 14 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the Saints, adding one reception for 19 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: Singletary saw 31 snaps on the day, leading Giants running backs in a pass-happy game script. It’s unclear what the Giants backfield will look like moving forward, but it’s a messy committee for now. Singletary and Tyrone Tracy seem to be the preferred options for passing down snaps, though Tracy is the preferred choice for more high leverage situations. Singletary is worth a waiver claim but fantasy managers should stay tuned to wade through the coach-speak and see what this Giants backfield looks like for Week 7 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Giants declared S Jason Pinnock, RB Devin Singletary, CB Nikko Reed, DT Bobby Jamison-Travis, OT J.C. Davis, and QB Jake Haener inactive for Week 5 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: Singletary is once again a healthy scratch as the Giants will roll with Cam Skattebo, Najee Harris, and Tyrone Tracy as their top three backs. J.J. McCarthy will serve as the QB2 behind Jameis Winston in what figures to be a messy game in the elements in Washington this afternoon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Giants declared RB Devin Singletary, S Ar’Darius Washington, CB Nikko Reed, DL Jihad Ward, OL J.C. Davis, TE Thomas Fidone, and DT Bobby Jamison-Travis as inactive for Week 4 against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: This is the second-straight week that Singletary has been made a healthy scratch for the Giants. Najee Harris and Tyrone Tracy will serve as the backups to Cam Skattebo. It’s also worth noting that QB J.J. McCarthy, who was acquired from the Vikings earlier this week, is active for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Giants declared RB Devin Singletary, TE Thomas Fidone II, OL J.C. Davis, DL Josh Tupou, DL Bobby Jamison-Travis, CB Deonte Banks, and S Tyler Nubin inactive for Week 3 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: Singletary is a healthy scratch this week. Najee Harris and Tyrone Tracy are the backup running backs for New York. Singletary had nine carries and four catches in the first two weeks of the year. His absence could be a slight boost to Cam Skattebo, though Singletary’s touches may just be distributed to the other backups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Cam Skattebo rushed 18 times for 81 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 1 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: Although Skattebo was not targeted in the pass game, his 18 carries handily led the team. Furthermore, presumed backup Tyrone Tracy lost a fumble on one of his two carries, resulting in Devin Singletary taking over primary backup duties for the remainder of the game. Those two variables should keep Skattebo’s weekly volume high after showing no ill effects of the devastating ankle injury suffered in 2025. His touchdown now gives him eight total scores in nine professional appearances despite only six of those being starts, a rate that will keep Skattebo in the weekly borderline RB1 discussion moving forward. Tracy managed just two snaps to Singletary’s 25, leaving Singletary as the primary backup for the moment. It’s possible Najee Harris gets into this discussion after being a healthy scratch in Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Tyrone Tracy Jr., Najee Harris and Devin Singletary are all listed as co-No. 2 backs on New York’s unofficial Week 1 depth chart.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: We can’t endorse relying on anyone in this backfield as a surefire bellcow in the event that Cam Skattebo gets hurt or is ineffective enough to lose playing time. It seems like it will be hard to rely on Tracy to have a major role this year with Harris in town.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: ESPN’s Jordan Raanan says Najee Harris “was brought in under the premise that he’s going to be a significant contributor” for the Giants this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: It’s worth noting that Cam Skattebo continues to be the first running back up in practice, but it sounds like the Giants could have a vision for Harris, who signed with the team on a one-year, minimum-salary deal, per Raanan. Harris is returning from a torn Achilles that ended his 2025 season in Week 3, but there’s plenty of room for him to earn snaps behind Skattebo once he gets up to speed. A blown pass-blocking assignment by Tyrone Tracy in the team’s first preseason game against the Vikings raised immediate questions about whether or not the Giants will trust Tracy in pass-blocking situations this season, and Harris has proven to be a capable pass-blocker in the past. At this point, it’s hard to imagine Harris having any standalone fantasy value in a healthy Giants backfield, but he could be worth a handcuff to Skattebo in deeper leagues based on these latest reports.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: SNY’s Connor Hughes said it’s “clear Cam Skattebo is the top back” for the Giants in training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: According to Hughes, Skattebo is “the first up in almost every running drill,” and he has also handled the majority of carries in practice. While it’s certainly an encouraging sign for Skattebo’s usage, Hughes also notes that the preferred options in the passing game are Tyrone Tracy and Devin Singletary. If the Giants were to dial back Skattebo’s role in the receiving game, it could deal a bit of a blow to his fantasy stock. He was on a 17-game pace to catch 51 passes last season, and his work in the passing game made up 43.7 percent of his fantasy scoring in PPR leagues last year. Skattebo’s role as an early-down grinder and goal-line back should be more than enough to satisfy fantasy managers this season, but a reduced role in the passing game would put a bit of a cap on his ceiling.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Giants restructured RB Devin Singletary’s contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: Singletary’s job with the Giants is safe, for now. The 28-year-old back has been relegated to backup duty in each of his last two seasons with the Giants, totaling 874 yards and nine touchdowns on 232 carries while appearing in 232 games. The Giants are reportedly going to be big players in the running back market once free agency kicks off next week, and could also eye a high-end rookie in the draft. Any major additions could put Singletary’s spot on the 53-man roster in jeopardy, especially if Cam Skattebo is healthy for the start of next season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.headline: Devin Singletary rushed nine times for 25 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 18 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/devin-sing.analysis: The 28-year-old will finish the season with 119 carries for 436 yards and five touchdowns in 17 games. He also added 18 catches on 19 targets for 151 yards and served primarily as the red zone option whenever either of Tyrone Tracy Jr. or Cam Skattebo was injured. Singletary is under contract for $5 million next season, but the Giants could opt out of that deal and take on a $1.25 million dead cap. Whomever they hire as head coach will likely play a big role in deciding that.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth caught 2-of-3 targets for 11 yards in the Steelers’ Week 6 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: The Muth was clearly limited by his nagging calf injury in this game. He was added to the injury report over the weekend and played through the issue despite being hit with a late questionable tag. He was spotted hobbling to the sidelines at least once during this game, though he ultimately gutted it out and played through the issue. He and Darnell Washington each played 54 of 76 offensive snaps. Better days should be ahead for Freiermuth once he’s healthy, but it will be hard to trust him as anything other than a TE2 flyer for his Week 7 game against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth (calf) is active for Week 6 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Muth was a late addition to the injury report, with the Steelers adding him on Saturday and listing him as questionable. With multiple starting receivers out this week, Muth will be asked to take on more work as a pass-catcher, moving him up the TE2 ranks. Inactive for the Steelers are WR Ben Skowronek, QB Drew Allar, QB Will Howard, CB Sean Murphy-Bunting, RB Eli Heidenreich, CB Terell Smith, and DL Kevin Jobity Jr.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Steelers are “optimistic” Pat Freiermuth (calf) will play in Week 6 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Freiermuth was added to the injury report on Saturday. The team listed him as questionable for Week 6. A last-minute addition to the injury report is never a good sign, so we wouldn’t be surprised if his snaps are limited even if he is active. On the other hand, with Roman Wilson and Michael Pittman out, the Steelers may have no choice but to play a banged-up Muth more than expected. He will be a high-risk TE2 if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth (calf) is questionable for Week 6 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Freiermuth popped up on the injury report Saturday afternoon with a calf injury. He’s questionable for this weekend against the Buccaneers. Freiermuth would’ve been in line for a sizable workload with the Steelers down multiple wide receivers. Coming off a two touchdown performance in Week 5, fantasy managers need a backup plan in case Freiermuth is ultimately ruled out against Tampa Bay.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth caught 5-of-7 targets for 44 yards and two touchdowns in the Steelers’ Week 5 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Freiermuth ran 27 routes on 38 dropbacks, which was a distant third behind DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard; however, Aaron Rodgers is far more effective when targeting the intermediate and middle areas of the field, which makes Freiermuth a more consistent target than either of the wide receivers. With Michael Pittman (foot) and Roman Wilson (finger) both hurt, Freiermuth could be a fringe TE1 next week against the Bucs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth caught 3-of-5 targets for 17 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 4 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Freiermuth found the end zone late in the fourth quarter for his second touchdown of the season, tying fellow tight end Darnell Washington for fourth on the team with five targets. Washington managed to corral just two of his five targets but eclipsed the yardage total of Freiermuth with 27 yards while also adding a touchdown of his own. Both tight ends appear unlikely to contribute viable counting stats considering neither has seen more than five targets in a game during the first month of play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Steelers are going to use Jaylen Warren “a lot” while frequently utilizing two-tight end sets in Week 4 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: It sounds like Warren is belongs on the RB1/2 border with Rico Dowdle (toe) sidelined again this week. The Steelers will try to control the line of scrimmage by frequently deploying TEs Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington, both in the run game and as receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth caught 2-of-4 targets for 30 yards in the Steelers’ Week 3 win over the Bengals
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Aaron Rodgers narrowly missed Freiermuth on a 20-plus-yard throw in the third quarter that could have been a touchdown if they had connected. Freiermuth has been targeted 14 times through the first three weeks but has just one meaningful fantasy line (5-45-1) thus far. Fantasy managers can find better options than Muth in Week 4’s game against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Pat Freiermuth caught 4-of-5 targets for 32 yards in the Steelers’ Week 2 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Freiermuth has a hold on the Steelers’ TE1 role, getting much of Aaron Rodgers’ short-yardage looks in the flat and middle of the field. The Steelers were not in the red zone all that much, so we have yet to see the 27-year-old’s utilization there. Regardless, he is consistently a top-four pass-catching option for the team, he’s just stuck in the low-ceiling Pittsburgh offense. Freiermuth is a touchdown-dependent fantasy play and will be in the low-end TE2 ranks for Week 3 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.headline: Steelers WR Michael Pittman (foot) is questionable to play in Week 2 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/pat-freier.analysis: Pittman did not practice at all this week. If he plays, he could be fairly limited. We tentatively expect him to be inactive on game day, though. Steelers TE Pat Freiermuth had a solid role last week and could take on No. 2 pass-catcher duties if Pittman indeed cannot play. Steelers WR DK Metcalf will almost assuredly take on a larger role, operating as the team’s receiving focal point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Kyle Williams caught a 12-yard pass in the Patriots’ Week 6 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Romeo Doubs departed early in the proceedings with a shoulder injury, but Williams was still held under two receptions for the fifth time in six appearances. We know Williams can pop up for big plays like a northeastern Isaac TesLaa, but the Patriots’ coaching staff doesn’t trust him for anything else. He’s off the radar in all but the deepest of formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Kyle Williams caught all three of his targets for 91 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Williams caught a beautifully thrown 49-yard score from Drake Maye, who had four touchdown passes to go along with 376 yards through the air in the blowout victory. Williams ran a route on 19 of the team’s 42 drop backs with Mack Hollins on injured reserve. He also came down with a long grab in the second half that put the Pats in position to take a four-score lead. A.J. Brown’s eventual return to the New England offense — as soon as this week against the Jets — will further limit Williams’ snaps and routes. He won’t be playable in most formats going forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Kyle Williams caught his lone target for 34 yards in the Patriots’ Week 3 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Williams logged a pass route on 16 of the Patriots’ 29 drop backs on the day and had one of the longest plays of the game for a struggling New England passing attack. Williams will need more playing time if he’s going to be viable for fantasy purposes. For now Mack Hollins appears to be the top wideout in the Patriots offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: DeMario Douglas caught 1-of-2 targets for nine yards in the Patriots’ Week 2 win over the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Douglas made the first catch of the game for the Patriots, but was silent the rest of the day. The 25-year-old is a low-yardage slot receiver who tends to get schemed targets when he is on the field. Douglas tallied the third-most snaps of all Patriots wide receivers on the day but will find it hard to achieve fantasy relevancy in an offense that utilizes multiple receivers in several different ways. Second-year receiver Kyle Williams also saw a pair of targets, catching one for 10 yards. Neither Williams or Douglas are anything more than deep league dart throws for Week 3 against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: The Athletic’s Chad Graff believes getting WR Kyle Williams more involved will help the Patriots generate explosive plays.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The issue is that Williams “didn’t display much craftiness in his route running during training camp this summer.” He ended up “buried on the depth chart” and played just 12 snaps in the opener. Still, Graff notes, Williams has shown an ability to “release off the line of scrimmage with ease, and run straight, deep routes for big completions.” Getting Williams more involved makes sense, but the Patriots have been reluctant to do so thus far in his career. He can be stashed on deep-leagues benches for a week or so, but positive results are not guaranteed.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Patriots WR Kyle Williams caught 2-of-2 targets for 55 yards and one touchdown in Thursday’s preseason game against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: This is the performance Williams needed to have following WR Kayshon Boutte’s trade to the Texans. The Patriots still have a crowded wide receiver room, but at least one competitor has been removed from the equation. Williams delivered a 10-yard catch on a curl route on the Patriots’ third play from scrimmage. Three plays later, he shook his defender at the line of scrimmage and took off down the left sideline. He hauled in the pass from QB Tommy DeVito in stride and waltzed into the end zone for a 45-yard score. Williams does not yet need to be drafted in 12-team leagues, vying for the third wide receiver spot on the Patriots’ depth chart. He could be a worthwhile waiver wire add early on, though.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: The Athletic’s Chad Graff believes Kyle Williams is “going to have a role” in the Patriots’ offense this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: It’s hard to imagine Williams having a fantasy-relevant role given the fact that the Patriots went out and added A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs this offseason, but Graff believes the second-year receiver will have some sort of role in the offense this season. As a rookie, Williams caught 10 passes for 209 yards and three touchdowns, and he went for 2-37-1 on three targets in last week’s preseason game against the Colts. Williams’ role in the offense could be worth monitoring in-season, but there’s no reason to rush to add him to your draft day plans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Patriots WR Kyle Williams hopes to improve his play over the middle of the field this offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Williams also focused on building lower-body strength this offseason, adding five to eight pounds in the process. He believes this strength could help him develop as a centerfield target, which is the primary thing to note for fantasy purposes. A 2019 Rotoworld study showed that targets thrown over the middle, 10-plus yards downfield, are more valuable than those thrown along the sideline at an equivalent depth. Williams went 0-for-5 on centerfield targets as a rookie. Improving his play over the middle will help him challenge for a role in the Patriots’ starting three-wide receiver set. Williams also said he hopes to be more consistent, build chemistry with QB Drake Maye and master the playbook this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Kyle Williams caught 1-of-2 targets for seven yards in the Patriots’ Super Bowl LX loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: A third-round rookie hype merchant in an offense many were expecting to be better, Williams ended up struggling to get on the field, catching just two passes across his first nine games. He was more involved down the stretch, but still finished the regular campaign with all of 10 grabs. He turned that limited work into more than 20 yards per catch and three touchdowns, but Williams was a strict role player in an offense that has fellow field-stretchers Mack Hollins and Kayshon Boutte. With both those wideouts likely back for 2026, Williams could have a difficult time commanding a bigger role. He turns 24 in November, making him a lower-upside hold in dynasty leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Kyle Williams caught 3-of-5 targets for 20 yards in the Patriots’ Week 17 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: With Kayshon Boutte out for the week and Mack Hollins on IR, Williams was tasked with WR1 duties in New England this week. He led the team in routes and logged a respectable 20 percent target share. Williams didn’t do much with the extra opportunities and even committed one egregious drop. The misplay broke Drake Maye’s completion streak at 11 to open the game. Boutte should be back next week. He will reclaim the No. 1 wideout role once cleared, meaning Williams won’t be on the fantasy radar for Week 18.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Efton Chism was held without a catch in the Patriots’ Week 6 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Coming off a two-game stretch where he surprisingly popped up for 99 combined yards, Chism was held under two receptions for third time in five 2026 appearances. This, as A.J. Brown returned to the lineup. Romeo Doubs (shoulder) did depart, but Chism is never going to have the advantage on Pop Douglas for slot/short-area looks. He is not a realistic consideration in 12-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Efton Chism caught 5-of-6 targets for 57 yards in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Chism came down with some big catches to keep the chains moving. He seems to have earned the trust of the Patriots coaching staff and Drake Maye in recent weeks. Even so, his route participation has been limited and his role could shrink next week if A.J. Brown returns from his high ankle injury. For now he’s an OK stash in deeper fantasy leagues in case he carves out a bigger role in the rejuvenated New England passing offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Efton Chism III caught 2-of-4 targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 4 win over the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Chism III’s touchdown was a spectacular diving one-handed touch in tight coverage that gave the Patriots a late lead over the Bills. It was an unreal grab on a third-down play in the biggest moment of the game. His only other catch was also on a third-and-long to keep a drive alive. With Mack Hollins (calf) leaving this game early, Chishm III played on 30 of the team’s 70 snaps and ran a route on 18 of their 43 dropbacks. The 24-year-old came into today with just five career catches, but he could be in for a bigger role in Week 5. He is still not a priority add in fantasy leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Patriots declared WR Efton Chism, CB Kobee Minor, OLB Bradyn Swinson, OT Marcus Bryant, G Caedan Wallace, TE C.J. Dippre and QB Tommy DeVito inactive for Super Bowl LX against the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Chism, an undrafted free agent rookie, was active in the Divisional Round and Wild Card Round but did not play in the AFC Championship Game. He caught 3-of-3 targets for 75 yards and one touchdown in the regular season and caught his lone postseason target for a 20-yard gain. DeVito will serve as the Patriots’ emergency third quarterback today.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Drake Maye completed 17-of-29 targets for 268 yards, one touchdown, one interception and lost one fumble in the Patriots’ 16-3, Wild Card win over the Chargers, rushing 10 times for 66 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Maye led the team in rushing, but he got the most out of RB Rhamondre Stevenson, efficiently linking up with him three times via the passing game for 75 yards. Maye was nearly on the receiving end of an explosive pass play, but rookie WR Efton Chism overthrew him, wide open, running down the right sideline. Chism made up for it with a 20-yard reception. Maye’s 37-yard scramble on the Patriots’ final drive before halftime was the longest rush of the game. He connected with TE Hunter Henry for a 28-yard, third-quarter touchdown against Chargers S Derwin James. The Patriots face the winner of the Texans-Steelers game tomorrow night. Maye’s elite fantasy upside remains intact no matter the opponent, though the Steelers field a far more fantasy-friendly defense than the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Efton Chism caught both of his targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in the Patriots’ Week 17 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Chism hasn’t played much this year after surprisingly making the Pats’ roster after a strong training camp. New England was without Kayshon Boutte and Mack Hollins this week, giving Chism an opening. He took the opportunity and ran with it, pulling in his first grab of the day for 30 yards and his second for a 10-yard score. Boutte should be back next week, meaning Chism isn’t guaranteed a spot on the gameday roster for Week 18. Still, his Week 17 spike should earn him more playing time in the long run.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said DeMario Douglas (hamstring) is questionable for New England’s Week 17 game against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: If Douglas doesn’t play, New England’s only three healthy wideouts on the roster will be Stefon Diggs, Kyle Williams, and Efton Chism. Chism would fit best in the slot, so he may get a chance to have a moment against the Jets if Douglas is ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Patriots declared QB Tommy DeVito, LB Robert Spillane, OT Marcus Bryant, TE CJ Dippre, and WR Efton Chism inactive for Week 16 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: All of Carlton Davis, Marcus Jones, Harold Landry, and Christian Barmore are active for the Patriots after coming into the weekend listed as questionable. Tommy DeVito will continue to serve as the emergency quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Patriots declared WR/KR Efton Chism III, OLB Bradyn Swinson, TE C.J. Dippre, OT Marcus Bryant, DT Eric Gregory, and QB Tommy DeVito inactive for Week 15 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: No real surprises here. The Patriots come into this game relatively healthy, except for defensive tackle Milton Williams being on the IR.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Patriots declared WR/KR Efton Chism III, TE C.J. Dippre, DT Joshua Farmer, G Caedan Wallace, QB Tommy DeVito, and LB Jahlani Tavai inactive for Week 12 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: No huge surprises here; however, with Chism out for the game, the Patriots may turn to TreVeyon Henderson or Terrell Jennings to return kicks

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: Kalif Raymond caught both of his targets for 18 yards in the Bears’ Week 6 win against the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: Raymond ran a pass route on 18 of the Bears’ 45 drop backs and didn’t see a target until the second half. He has been mostly phased out of the team’s passing offense since profiling as Chicago’s de facto WR1 over the first couple games of the season. Raymond, who has just 30 receiving yards over his past three games, can be left on the waiver wire ahead of Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: Kalif Raymond caught 3-of-4 targets for six yards in the Bears’ Week 5 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: Raymond’s fast start to the season has now been erased to the tune of just five catches for 12 yards over the past two weeks. Even with Caleb Williams (hamstring) looking likely to return for Week 6 against the Falcons, Raymond’s brief moment in the 2026 fantasy sun has come and gone.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: Kalif Raymond caught 6-of-7 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in the Bears’ Week 3 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: Raymond has now led the Bears in receiving in two of the team’s first three games, with Week 3 his best performance yet on the back of a 41-yard touchdown through busted coverage. It isn’t likely the career role player will lead the team in receiving throughout the season, but the early returns on investment must have fantasy managers ecstatic for those that either drafted him in the final round or scooped him off the wire following Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: Kalif Raymond caught 5-of-5 targets for 40 yards in the Bears’ Week 2 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: For whatever reason, Raymond again lead the Bears’ receiver corps in production, though Luther Burden did out-target him on fewer snaps. Cold comfort. Although Raymond out-snapped Burden, he was on the field 16 fewer plays than Rome Odunze. Pro Football Focus’ Nathan Jahnke charted Raymond as seeing more time in “12" personnel than his sophomore teammate. We would like to say this is bound to change going forward, but coach Ben Johnson had no problem featuring veteran Olamide Zaccheaus in 2025. Raymond is struggling to create WR4 value of his own, but he is certainly hampering Burden and Odunze’s production ahead of Week 3 against the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: Kalif Raymond caught 8-of-9 targets for 89 yards in the Bears’ Week 1 win against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: Raymond, who ran a route on 23 of 40 Caleb Williams drop backs, led the Bears in targets, catches, and receiving yards, while Colston Loveland went catchless and Luther Burden was an afterthought. Raymond’s route participation suggests he’ll be a rotational player in the run-first Chicago offense. That should make him a risky option in any sort of fantasy league. Even so, it’s clear Raymond has taken something similar to the D.J. Moore role and could be useful in fantasy this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: The Chicago Tribune’s Sean Hammond reports that Bears WR Rome Odunze exited practice early on Thursday after suffering an apparent leg injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: Per Hammond, Odunze “came up hobbling during an install period at the start of practice,” with what appeared to be a right leg injury. Apparently, Odunze “wasn’t overly concerned” and tried to continue practicing, but Bears trainers removed him from the field. That last bit is encouraging. Hopefully, Odunze’s Week 1 availability has not been jeopardized. Bears TE Colston Loveland and WR Luther Burden would benefit if Odunze cannot play. Odunze is backed up by WR Kalif Raymond.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: The Athletic’s Kevin Fishbain believes the “expectation” is that Kalif Raymond will be the team’s No. 3 receiver.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: Jahdae Walker could position himself as the No. 3 with a second-year jump, and third-round pick Zavion Thomas is also in the mix. This room will probably split the snaps enough to make them unappealing from a fantasy perspective, but it’s possible someone emerges as a WR4-type.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: Bears signed WR Kalif Raymond, formerly of the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: Raymond was mostly a role player and a special teams standout during his five years in Detroit. Last season Raymond had 24 receptions for 289 yards and a touchdown while drawing three starts for the run-heavy Lions. In Chicago, Raymond — entering his age-32 season — will likely function as a role player in Ben Johnson’s run-centric offense. He could see starter’s snaps if the Bears struggle with receiver injuries in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: Isaac TeSlaa caught his only target for 18 yards in the Lions’ Week 18 win over the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: TeSlaa emerged as a primary option for the Lions in Week 13 after Amon-Ra St. Brown departed with injury, finishing off the back half of his rookie season as the clear WR3 for the Lions. That effectively shifted Kalif Raymond into a situational role, something likely to carry forward into the 2026 season. TeSlaa ends his rookie year with 16 catches for 239 yards, flashing abilities in the red zone through six touchdowns. Although unlikely to immediately see his role grow while playing alongside St. Brown and Jameson Williams, TeSlaa appears likely to step into a bigger role when one of the main receivers goes down. That gives him legitimate best ball upside considering he will be playing for an offense that has finished in the top five in scoring in each of the previous four seasons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.headline: Kalif Raymond caught 4-of-5 targets for 62 yards and a touchdown in the Lions’ Week 16 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kalif-raym.analysis: Raymond and Isaac TeSlaa split the No. 3 role this week. Both players topped 50 yards and scored. TeSlaa did so on seven targets compared to five for Raymond. Jared Goff compiled 364 yards in a failed comeback bid, allowing multiple ancillary pieces to get home this week. That shouldn’t be the case next week. We don’t recommend starting Raymond or TeSlaa in the fantasy football finals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: Malachi Fields caught 2-of-8 targets for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: Fields saw a season-high eight targets, but caught just two of those passes for 19 yards. The Giants passing game behind Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely isn’t productive for fantasy purposes. Darnell Mooney had a carry for 20 yards while Charlie Jones caught 2-of-3 passes for 66 yards. Fields is the best option past Nabers and Likely, but he can be left on fantasy benches for Week 7 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: Malachi Fields caught 2-of-3 targets for 52 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 4 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: Fields has now caught exactly two passes in each of his first four NFL appearances. His 12-yard touchdown was the first of his career. Jameis Winston was flushed from the pocket and found Fields on the run. The duo later connected on a similar play for a non-scoring 40-yard grab. Today was the first time Winston showed any signs of life in place of Jaxson Dart, though Fields is still going to be a tough sell WR4 in this depressed offensive environment.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: Malachi Fields caught both of his targets for 19 yards in the Giants’ Week 3 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: Fields hasn’t caught more than two passes in a game this year. He finished third on the team in targets in Week 3. Fields is on the field plenty, he just isn’t earning that many opportunities. He is not a viable fantasy option for Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: Malachi Fields caught 2-of-6 targets for 30 yards in the Giants’ Week 2 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: Fields struggled alongside the rest of the Giants in a game played mostly with backup quarterback Jameis Winston under center. Jaxson Dart departed after the team’s first possession with what looked like an MCL sprain based on the mechanism of the injury, something that could force missed contests from the normal starter. That would position Fields in a difficult spot to return usable counting stats in the short term. He gets the struggling Titans in Week 3, where he’ll be best left on fantasy benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: Malachi Fields caught 2-of-4 targets for 25 yards in the Giants’ Week 1 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: The rookie wide receiver showcased a polished all-around skillset, reinforcing offseason reports that he had locked down the WR2 role opposite Malik Nabers. His 6'4, 220-pound frame was on full display as he was continually utilized as both a down-blocker and blocker in the second level on runs, something that should allow him to continue to operate as the clear-cut WR2 for the Giants throughout his rookie campaign. That said, the box scores highlights the obvious distinction that his snap rate — he led all Giants wideouts with 50 — won’t always translate to fantasy production while playing alongside Nabers and tight end Isaiah Likely, the latter two of whom commanded 17 targets on 29 Jaxson Dart pass attempts. The good news is that he played well ahead of veterans Darnell Mooney and Odell Beckham Jr., with Mooney having 39 snaps and Beckham just 11. Fantasy managers are best off viewing Fields as a high-end stash at the end of benches for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: ESPN’s Jordan Raanan believes WR Malachi Fields “will likely start as the Giants’ No. 2 receiver opposite Malik Nabers.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: This isn’t the first time Raanan has suggested Fields could have the inside edge as the Giants’ WR2. Earlier this month, he said the rookie third-rounder was making an “early claim” for the role, which doesn’t come as much of a surprise given the thin receiving corps the Giants are currently working with. The 6-foot-4, 220-plus-pound receiver has an excellent catch radius and made a name for himself with his ability to haul in contested targets during his days at Virginia and Notre Dame. It seems highly unlikely that Fields would make enough of an impact to be considered a reliable fantasy contributor, but he could be worth a late-round/stash in drafts to see how things unfold for him in the weeks to come.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: Malachi Fields caught 3-of-3 targets for 34 yards and a touchdown in the first week of the preseason against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: It’s a game that The Athletic’s Dan Duggan says “strengthened his push for the No. 2 receiver job.” His touchdown pass was from Jaxson Dart, but he was one of several receivers getting first-team snaps. It’s hard to believe Fields will be relevant early in 12-team redraft leagues unless Malik Nabers suffers a setback, but he’s squarely on the fantasy radar after a big camp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: The Athletic’s Dan Duggan believes Giants WR Malachi Fields “has made an early claim for the No. 2 receiver spot” in camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: The Giants traded up to select Fields with the No. 74 overall pick in this year’s draft, adding him to a receiver room that is noticeably thin behind Malik Nabers. This isn’t the first time Fields has garnered praise from the media, as ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reported in late July that the Giants were “highly impressed” by the hulking receiver who made a name for himself as a contested catch specialist. It’s highly unlikely that Fields will make enough of an impact as a rookie to be a viable fantasy option, but he could prove valuable as a big target in and around the end zone for the Giants this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Giants have been “highly impressed” by WR Malachi Fields.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: Fowler goes so far as to say there are “shades” of former Giants WR Plaxico Burress “as far as style.” This is, perhaps, technically a true statement, but almost assuredly hyperbolic. Fields, a third-round rookie, landed on a depth chart chock-full of speedy role players. He brings a unique skill set with his 6'4/218 frame and jump-ball abilities. Carving out a role this season is possible, but not a given.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.headline: Giants signed third-round pick WR Malachi Fields to a four-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/malachi-fi.analysis: Giants GM Joe Schoen recently said Fields will be the “power forward” in the team’s wide receiver corps, jumping for contested catches and blocking on the perimeter. Fields has a chance to play in year one, with speedster WR Darius Slayton coming off another sub-600-yard season. Fields warrants final-round consideration in best ball formats. Expectations must be tempered.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Corey Kiner rushed 11 times for 57 yards in the Patriots’ Week 6 win over the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Even with Rhamondre Stevenson active and TreVeyon Henderson surprisingly playing through his ankle injury, Kiner was called on as the Patriots’ “closer,” with all 11 of his handles coming in the final 16:30 of the contest. The Patriots were winning, but the game was still in doubt. Kiner responded by continually turning his short-yardage opportunities into first downs, while he ended up leading the team in rushing. It wasn’t easy to see that one coming, but it might be difficult for coach Mike Vrabel to un-see it as neither Stevenson nor Henderson impress in their No. 1 or 2 jobs. Kiner is worth an end-of-bench stash in 14-team leagues but is not yet 12-team league relevant.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) will miss multiple weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Henderson suffered his latest ankle injury in Week 5 against the Raiders. Schefter said Henderson is “regarded as a quick healer, so the Patriots are hoping his return is sooner rather than later.” Still, he could be sidelined for the next few weeks, leaving Rhamondre Stevenson as the team’s clear lead back. Corey Kiner, meanwhile, appears to be in line as the Patriots’ RB2 after seeing seven touches last week against the Raiders. Kiner should be stashed in most 12-team fantasy leagues for now. Stevenson profiles as a top-12 play until Henderson returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Corey Kiner had six rushes for 52 yards in the Patriots’ Week 5 win against the Raiders, adding one catch for seven yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Kiner’s seven touches came after TreVeyon Henderson went down with what could be a serious ankle injury in the second quarter. While much of his work came in garbage time, Kiner could work as the Patriots’ No. 2 back behind Rhamondre Stevenson if Henderson is sidelined in Week 6. Kiner is worth a look on waiver wires this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Corey Kiner rushed six times for 11 yards in the Patriots’ Week 1 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Kiner served as Rhamondre Stevenson’s backup with TreVeyon Henderson out this week. He was the only other Pats running back to see a carry in this game, though practice squad call-up Lan Larison was targeted twice, both of which he caught. Kiner did not see a look through the air. As a backup running back without any pass-catching value, Kiner is not on the fantasy radar heading into Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Mike Reiss reports that Patriots RB TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is not present for the media-access portion of practice on Sunday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The injury has sidelined Henderson since August 24. The Patriots face the Seahawks on Wednesday. At this point, Henderson must be considered questionable to play. Even if he were active, he would be slated for No. 2 duties behind starting RB Rhamondre Stevenson, and it is fair to wonder if the team would keep Henderson on a snap count. Reiss reported this morning that RB Lan Larison and/or RB Hassan Haskins would likely be elevated from the practice squad if Henderson cannot play, joining Stevenson and backup RB Corey Kiner on game day.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Patriots acquired RB Corey Kiner from the Cardinals in exchange for a seventh-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The trade was first reported by ESPN’s Adam Schefter. The draft pick going to the Cardinals is a seventh-round pick in 2028. Kiner was buried on the depth in Arizona, but should immediately step in as the RB3 behind Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson with the Patriots. A former UDFA who appeared in four games with the Cardinals last year, Kiner is only worth a stash in deeper formats and has no standalone fantasy value.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Emari Demercado rushed five times for 30 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 16 loss to the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Demercado failed to snag his only target and he was out-touched 6-to-5 by fellow backup RB Corey Kiner. Cardinals RB Michael Carter is the clear-cut starter and Kiner’s presence reduces Demercado’s bench-stash value. This looks like a three-player committee with one FLEX-viable player.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cardinals signed RB Corey Kiner off the Vikings’ practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Cardinals released RB Jermar Jefferson in a related move. We’d love to say this doesn’t matter, but sadly, all Cardinals running back news is real news. Kiner spent time with the 49ers in training camp before getting hurt, he was a priority UDFA signing this offseason. It’s possible he may be fantasy-relevant at some point given how banged up the Cardinals RB room is.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: 49ers HC Kyle Shanahan said RB Patrick Taylor (shoulder) will miss a couple of weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Taylor exited Saturday’s preseason game against the Raiders with the injury and did not return to the field. Rookie UDFA Corey Kiner also exited with a high-ankle sprain and is expected to miss a couple of weeks. The 49ers are already dealing with injuries to Isaac Guerendo (shoulder) and rookie Jordan James (knee). Behind Christian McCaffrey is journeyman Ke’Shawn Vaughn and the recently re-signed Jeff Wilson, who rushed for 8-16-1 against the Raiders while adding another catch for 16 yards. Both Vaughn and Wilson could spell McCaffrey in Week 1 against the Seahawks if Guerendo, James, and Taylor are all sidelined. That said, none of these players carry much fantasy upside.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: 49ers RB Corey Kiner was carted from the field in Saturday’s preseason game due to an ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Kiner is a UDFA from Cincinnati who has been impressing in Niners camp. The rookie broke off a 19-yard run in the second quarter and remained down after the play, only to later be carted from the field. While he’d typically be considered a long shot to make the roster, Kiner may have had an opening given the current state of the 49ers’ backfield. We’ll hopefully know more on his injury soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 6-of-11 targets for 99 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely scored his fifth touchdown of the season and third over the last two games. He also caught a two point conversion, with all his scoring coming in the fourth quarter from J.J. McCarthy. The pass-heavy game script helped Likely salvage his fantasy day late in the game as he saw double-digit targets for the third straight game and fourth time this season. Now averaging 9.8 targets per game, Likely is squarely in the fantasy TE1 ranks heading into a tough Week 7 matchup against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely (foot) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Theo Johnson has a neck injury and was limited in practice. Both tight ends should be able to suit up on Sunday. Coming off a career-high in targets (13), Likely is looking more like a top-five fantasy tight end every week. He should be in every fantasy lineup for his Week 6 date with the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 11-of-13 targets for 94 yards and two touchdown in the Giants’ Week 5 tie with the Commanders
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely set a new career-high with 11 receptions in this one, and came up with two clutch touchdowns in the process. His first score came on a three-yard strike from Jameis Winston on a third-and-goal play that the Giants needed to stay in the game, cutting the Commanders’ lead to 19-13. Then, in the fourth quarter and with the Giants facing a fourth-and-eight, Likely turned an eight-yard reception upfield for a 17-yard touchdown that nearly looked like a fumble and turnover at the goal-line. Likely has been targeted 25 times in his last two games and has now gone for 66 or more yards in three of five games to start the season. He’s starting to show good chemistry with Jameis Winston and will be on the TE1 radar in next week’s game against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely (knee/groin) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 5 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: The Giants’ passing offense is tethered to Jameis Winston’s scattershot arm, but Likely has a favorable matchup against the Commanders’ defense this week. He can be started as a low-end TE1 in this divisional showdown.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely (knee/groin) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely is on track to face the Commanders’ fantasy-friendly defense in Week 5. Ideally, we will see him upgrade to full participation tomorrow. The Giants’ starting tight end warrants TE1 treatment thanks to his workload and plus matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely (knee/groin) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely evidently got a little banged up while handling a second-high 12 targets last week. His early-week participation puts him on track to face the Commanders in Week 5, but new injuries are worth keeping an eye on. He is a TE1 if active this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 7-of-12 targets for 66 yards in the Giants’ Week 4 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely’s 12 targets were a new season high as fill-in QB Jameis Winston finally got a little something going through the air. That included two heinous interceptions, but we were beginning to wonder if Winston was ever going to complete another pass. That he did stabilizes Likely’s low-end TE1 value, though we have no doubt the giveaways will stick in the coaching staff’s mind. This is still an offense that is going to work to hide the quarterback and potentially start trade acquisition J.J. McCarthy at some point this fall. Those variables limit Likely’s upside even if the floor is now looking a little better heading into Week 5 against the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 2-of-5 targets for 13 yards in the Giants’ Week 3 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Likely’s yardage total came back to Earth last week with just 33 despite seeing 10 targets. It fell further today, as did the target total. On the plus side, he finished second on the team in receiving opportunities and finished with a 23 percent target share. Likely remains the team’s de facto No. 2 receiver behind Malik Nabers. That simply wasn’t worth much in terms of fantasy points today. He remains a solid TE1 bet for Week 4 against the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught 5-of-10 targets for 33 yards in the Giants’ Week 2 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Although fantasy managers are thrilled with the team-leading 10 targets, the nature of those targets is cause for concern considering the uneven play from backup quarterback Jameis Winston. Starter Jaxson Dart was forced from the game with a knee injury on the team’s first possession and it would not be shocking to see him miss games considering the mechanism of his injury, leaving the offense in the hands of the inconsistent Winston. Even so, fantasy managers will be thrilled to start Likely in a plus matchup against the Titans in Week 3, particularly considering the multitude of injuries at the position throughout the league.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.headline: Isaiah Likely caught all eight targets for 78 yards and two touchdowns in the Giants’ Week 1 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/isaiah-lik.analysis: Making his debut for a new team, Likely didn’t wait long to prove he can be a featured tight end for the Giants, scoring on the final possession of the first half and first possession after the break. His first score highlighted his athleticism as he escaped coverage to the corner of the end zone from 15 yards out while his second trip to paint was reminiscent of a Nagy design for Travis Kelce in which the veteran tight end shed a chip-block in the flat for an easy score from two yards. Likely looks every bit of a fantasy TE1 but gets a difficult matchup against the Rams in Week 2. Even so, you’re starting him if you got him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers caught 12-of-15 targets for 165 yards in the Giants’ Week 6 loss to the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Nabers was once again heavily involved in the Giants’ passing game, getting the first offensive touch for New York. He saw 15 targets and tallied 165 scoreless yards on the day, with over half of this yardage coming with J.J. McCarthy in the fourth quarter. It’s the third straight 100-yard game for Nabers, who is now fully ramped up from his torn ACL last year. The Giants may be debating between Jameis Winston and J.J. McCarthy as the starting quarterback for next week. Regardless of the starter, Nabers sees enough volume to be a borderline WR1 for Week 7 against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers caught 11-of-20 targets for 121 yards and one touchdown in the Giants’ Week 5 tie with the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Nabers saw 15 of his targets come in the second half after the Giants opted to abandon a mostly useless ground game in a game they trailed for most of the afternoon. Nabers came up with multiple big plays as the Giants mounted their comeback attempt, with his biggest coming on a leaping 17-yard touchdown in the end zone to tie the game at 27-27 with under two minutes to go in the game. Nabers had a key drop on a screen pass in overtime that had a chance to set up a big gain, but he made up for it later in the game with a 28-yard gain as the Giants were trying to position themselves for a potential game-winning field goal attempt. Nabers has now gone for 100-plus yards in back-to-back weeks and has found the end zone in both of those games. He seems to finally be hitting his stride after a slow start to the season, and will profile as a high-end WR2 in next week’s game against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Giants coach John Harbaugh said Malik Nabers (knee) will be “ready to play” on Sunday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: It was presumed that Nabers would play after sitting out Wednesday with soreness in his surgically repaired knee. Though this is just our speculation, the Giants may take it easier on their star receiver this week after he hauled in 6/112/1 against the Cardinals in Week 4. He remains on the WR2 line in what has been (when not facing the Cardinals) a rough offense with Jameis Winston under center.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers (knee) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Nabers is currently going through route running drills with his position group, putting him on track to play in Week 5 against the Commanders. Nabers sat out yesterday, citing extra soreness in his surgically repaired knee, but told ESPN’s Jordan Raanan that he usually feels better as the week progresses. A WR1 finish is in play this week, assuming he is active. He was later listed as limited on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers (knee) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Earlier today, The Athletic’s Dan Duggan reported that Nabers sat in the rehab section, speaking with the team’s head trainer during individual drills before seemingly going through some sort of rehab routine. ESPN’s Jordan Raanan then reported that Nabers said he was feeling “more sore than usual,” and “did as much as he could at practice.” When asked whether this could affect his ability to play in Week 5 against the Commanders, Nabers said, “we’ll see,” adding that it usually gets better as the week progresses. We tentatively expect Nabers to play, though this is worth monitoring closely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers caught 6-of-7 targets for 112 yards and a touchdown in the Giants’ Week 4 win over the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Nabers’ first 100-yard game of the season almost didn’t happen after he re-injured his shoulder on a soaring first quarter reception, his first catch of the afternoon. He thankfully shook it off and went on to score his first touchdown, as well, a 25-yarder in the second quarter. He got matched up 1-on-1 with LB Mack Wilson, and Jameis Winston did not miss. It was a desperately needed outing for fantasy managers who were beginning to wonder if Nabers would even produce WR2 returns, let alone WR1. The top 12 is probably still a little far fetched, but this was an encouraging outing heading into next week’s road date with the Commanders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers caught 5-of-6 targets for 26 yards in the Giants’ Week 3 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: The good news is that Nabers didn’t appear bothered by his shoulder injury and led the Giants with a 27 percent target share. The bad news is everything else. With Jameis Winston under center, the Giants took the air out of the ball and ran 33 times compared to just 22 pass attempts. Winston also stuck mostly to check-down duties, taking any chance of a big play for Nabers off the table. The Giants should be forced to throw more next week, but this isn’t going to be an exciting offense without Jaxson Dart under center. Nabers is likely stuck in the WR2 ranks for Week 4 versus the Cardinals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers is not on New York’s final Week 3 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: It sure didn’t seem like he had great chemistry with Jameis Winston on Monday night, leaving Nabers feeling more like a mid-range WR2 than someone you’d really want to count on to carry you to victory in what will be a windy Week 3 game against the Titans. Still, he’s fully healthy and got in full practices in each of the last two days of the week to clear the injury report.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Malik Nabers (shoulder) said his shoulder feels good and x-rays came back with positive results.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Nabers speaking to the media is likely also good news for his availability on Sunday. The 23-year-old wideout is practicing and upgraded to full today, so he’s likely to be good to go and has a chance at avoiding a questionable tag on Friday altogether.

https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.headline: Giants WR Malik Nabers (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s walkthrough.
https://www.nbcsports.com/malik-nabers/0.analysis: Nabers hurt his shoulder in the Giants’ Week 2 loss to the Rams, staying in the game and catching zero passes after the injury. The Giants had a walkthrough practice on Wednesday, listing Nabers as limited. When asked if the 23-year-old had X-rays done, head coach John Harbaugh gave his usual vague answer, saying, “I don’t know.” A limited practice listing indicates Nabers is not dealing with a major issue, but his practice status is worth monitoring leading up to Week 3 against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Jaylen Warren rushed 14 times for 50 yards in the Steelers’ Week 6 win over the Bucs, adding two catches for 28 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: Warren and Rico Dowdle, who was active after missing three games with a toe injury, split the backfield carries for the majority of this game. Warren finally pulled away from Dowdle late in the fourth quarter and overtime. Over the final 20 minutes of the contest, Warren out-carried Dowdle 7-2. He held a modest 7-5 carries advantage through three quarters. Dowdle was more efficient on the ground, but the Steelers clearly trust Warren more in all situations when push comes to shove. Warren will be in the RB2 mix when he takes on the Saints next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Rico Dowdle (toe) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: Dowdle has been out since Week 2 because of the toe issue. In the meantime, Jaylen Warren has looked like one of the league’s most dynamic backs on the ground and through the air. While his gargantuan workload will return to normal with Dowdle back, Warren should still operate as the team’s unquestioned RB1. Dowdle is just a mid-range FLEX play for his first game back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said “there’s a number you’d like to continue to give [Jaylen Warren],” even after Rico Dowdle (toe) returns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: “He’s produced, so it’s been heavy. It’d be great to get Rico back this week, too. ... Having him as a one-two punch was the vision of this offense, but Jaylen’s crushing it right now. He’s been awesome for us,” McCarthy continued. That’s a very telling “but.” Warren has to be regarded as the chair of a committee at this point rather than in a backfield split, and Dowdle probably doesn’t belong in the FLEX conversation coming off his injury until we see a good workload for him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Jaylen Warren rushed 15 times for 101 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 5 win over the Colts, adding six catches for 87 yards and another touchdown through the air.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: Warren got the Steelers on the board with an 80-yard catch-and-run, where he simply beat the Colts defenders down the sideline. He also ripped off a 50-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. The Steelers only had one other play go for longer than 17 yards on the day. Since Rico Dowdle has been out with a toe injury, Warren has emerged as a true RB1 in fantasy football. Even when Dowdle returns, you have to think that the Steelers have seen enough that they need to give Warren the lion’s share of the work.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Steelers declared RB Rico Dowdle, QB Will Howard, QB Drew Allar, CB Jamel Dean, RB Eli Heidenreich, CB Terell Smith, and DT Kevin Jobity Jr. inactive for Week 5 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: It was reported earlier in the day that Dowdle was unlikely to suit up due to his ongoing foot injury, so this doesn’t come as a major surprise. We could be looking at a big game for Jaylen Warren against an underperforming Colts defense. With Keenan Allen back for the Colts, the injury to Jamel Dean is a bit of a blow to this Pittsburgh secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said Rico Dowdle is making progress in his attempt to return from a toe injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: McCarthy said he expects Dowdle and Jaylen Warren to be a “one-two punch” once Dowdle returns to the field. Warren has totaled 34 rushes over the last two weeks while rushing for 220 scoreless yards, but had a 21-89-0 line during the first two weeks of the season when Dowdle was active. Both backs will likely fall in the RB3/FLEX range if Dowdle suits up for Week 5’s game against the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Jaylen Warren rushed 17 times for 93 yards in the Steelers’ Week 4 loss to the Browns, adding 33 yards on three receptions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: Warren’s six targets combine with his 17 carries to give him his second consecutive game with more than 20 opportunities in the absence of Rico Dowdle, seeing all but two running back opportunities in the process. More impressive was the fact that he once again maintained elite efficiency on the ground through the additional touches, averaging 5.5 yards per attempt against a solid Browns run defense. The veteran back appears likely to revert to a strict timeshare with Dowdle expected back for Week 5 after the long week, bringing him back to the RB3 range for a meeting with the Colts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Steelers are going to use Jaylen Warren “a lot” while frequently utilizing two-tight end sets in Week 4 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: It sounds like Warren is belongs on the RB1/2 border with Rico Dowdle (toe) sidelined again this week. The Steelers will try to control the line of scrimmage by frequently deploying TEs Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington, both in the run game and as receivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports there is a “pretty good chance” Rico Dowdle (toe) returns in Week 5 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: Dowdle did not practice this week and was ruled out for Thursday’s game against the Browns. Rapoport called him day-to-day. The mini-bye between today’s game and Pittsburgh’s Week 5 date with Indy at home should be enough rest to get Dowdle back on the field. Jaylen Warren will see almost the entirety of the backfield tonight before returning to committee duties once Dowdle is healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.headline: Rico Dowdle (toe) will not play in Week 4 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylen-war.analysis: Dowdle did not practice once this week before being ruled out for Thursday’s game against the Browns. The mini-bye ahead of Week 5 may help him get back on the field, but his status for next week’s contest is very much up in the air. Jaylen Warren will see the bulk of the backfield work versus Cleveland. he ran 17 times and caught three passes in Week 3. With an elite workload versus a middling Cleveland defense, Warren is a high-end RB2 this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard rushed 19 times for 76 yards in the Titans’ Week 6 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard was targeted only once, finishing without a reception. Pollard has somewhat surprisingly banished No. 2 Tyjae Spears to pure breather back status, but the Titans’ overall play volume and touchdown opportunities are so limited that he is still struggling to achieve weekly RB2 status. He has nevertheless shored up his RB3/FLEX floor. That is where you will find him in the Week 7 ranks against the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard rushed 14 times for 52 yards in Tennessee’s Week 5 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard looks like he could be a legitimate NFL running back somewhere, but it sure can’t happen on this offense. He’s cleared 14 carries and 48 yards in each of his last four games and has just one touchdown to show for it. It’s fringe low-end RB2 land for Pollard, as usual, against the Colts next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard (foot) is not on Tennessee’s final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard will take on the 0-4 Texans, who have had some trouble handling the run, and should be a viable low-end RB2 this week. He continues to get Wednesday vet days while dealing with this foot injury, but doesn’t seem to be in any real danger of missing time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard (foot) resumed practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: During Weeks 3-4, Pollard took Wednesdays off, rehabbing an ankle injury. He would resume practicing on Thursday and suit up on Sunday. Now, with his new foot issue, he appears to be on the same practice plan. Expect him to play in Week 5 against the Texans. Pollard was a full participant on Thursday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard (foot) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: The Titans have given Pollard Wednesday off in back-to-back weeks. He was removed from the injury report entirely on Friday both times. This week should be no different. Pollard has 39 touches over the past two weeks. Even on a struggling Titans offense, that’s enough work to put him on the RB2/3 border for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard rushed 16 times for 48 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ Week 4 loss to the Ravens, adding two catches for two additional yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Pollard was wildly inefficient in this one, but saved his fantasy day when he scored a three-yard touchdown in the first quarter to give the Titans their first points of the day. It was the first touchdown of the season for Pollard, who continues to serve as the Titans’ primary back, but there’s not much fantasy upside to be had here. Pollard will be a boom-or-bust RB3 next week against the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter believes Tony Pollard “fits the profile” of a player who could be traded ahead of the deadline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Schefter didn’t cite any sources telling him that Pollard could be on the move, but he did connect a few key dots. Pollard is in the final year of his contract and the Titans are going nowhere fast. If they don’t plan on re-signing him next offseason, they might as well get something in return for him in the middle of another lost season. His departure would also clear the way for rookie Nick Singleton to see more work.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard (ankle) is not on the injury report and will play in Week 4 against the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: With Titans RB2 Tyjae Spears (ankle) questionable to play, Pollard could end up handling a big workload. Unfortunately, the Titans field an unproductive offense and face the Ravens this week. He can only be viewed as a moderate FLEX starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard (ankle) practiced in full on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: The full practice keeps him as a potential RB2/FLEX option against the Ravens for Week 4. Pollard dominated reps in Week 3 with Tyjae Spears active as a game-time decision. Spears looks to be a little better this week, but Pollard should be at the head of the committee still in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.headline: Tony Pollard (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tony-polla.analysis: Neither did Tyjae Spears, who is also dealing with an ankle issue. Both backs played through their injuries last week and head coach Robert Saleh said today that he isn’t concerned about either of them missing Week 4. The Titans held them out of last Wednesday’s practice as well, so this seems to be the new norm for the backfield tandem. Pollard remains a volume-based RB3 after seeing 21 touches last week. Spears is nothing more than a backup right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: Aaron Rodgers completed 33-of-49 passes for 253 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Steelers’ 26-19, Week 6 overtime win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: Rodgers and the Steelers couldn’t get anything going through three quarters. They had just three points on the board and Germie Bernard check-downs were their only method of moving the ball. Even that was barely working. Running out of options, Rodgers simply started forcing the ball to DK Metcalf. He targeted Metcalf 12 times in the fourth quarter and overtime. The Steelers scored 16 points in the fourth quarter and another seven in the extra frame. Rodgers now has at least 230 yards and multiple touchdowns in four straight games. The Steelers’ pass-crazed approach under Mike McCarthy has kept him in the QB2 mix so far, and it will do so again when he faces the Saints next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: Aaron Rodgers completed 22-of-31 passes for 235 yards and three touchdowns in the Steelers’ 34-22, Week 5 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: The Steelers seemed worried about the Colts’ pass rush today, so there were a lot of quick-hit passes from Rodgers. The vast majority of them went to running backs or tight ends. Only nine of Rodgers’ 22 completions went to wide receivers, and 80 of his 235 passing yards came on a short pass to Jaylen Warren that the running back took up the sideline for a long touchdown. That’s not to say Rodgers didn’t play well. He did a good job avoiding sacks and not taking negative plays, but the Steelers’ offense didn’t look very potent outside of two explosive plays from Jaylen Warren. They may find things a little bit tougher against the Bucs next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.headline: Aaron Rodgers completed 22-of-40 passes for 299 yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions in the Steelers’ 27-24, Week 4 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aaron-rodg.analysis: Rodgers was under constant pressure from an unrelenting Cleveland pass rush, taking five sacks while throwing two interceptions in the loss. The offense struggled to maintain consistent efficiency as the Steelers fell into a 21-7 hole in the second quarter, eventually requiring more Rodgers fourth quarter heroics to knot the game at 24 with under two minutes to play. That would be enough time for Deshaun Watson to get the Browns into field goal range for the go-ahead kick with 10 seconds remaining. With just one timeout in hand, the Steelers were forced into downfield aggression on the final play of the game, which resulted in the second of two Rodgers interceptions. The Steelers have now been involved in three one-score games through four weeks, something both Steelers fans and those familiar with head coach Mike McCarthy are all too familiar with - two of those games resulted in wins. Up next for Rodgers and the Steelers are the reeling Colts in Week 5, against whom Rodgers will remain a middling QB2 in fantasy circles.
