https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: The Titans’ offense looked dead on arrival with 34 yards on their six first-half drives. They opened the game with four consecutive three-and-outs and didn’t get on the board until late in the fourth quarter, when Ward tossed a short touchdown to Wan’Dale Robinson. It looked like Ward was getting in rhythm late in the game, but he ended the contest with a ghastly interception directly into the hands of Jevon Holland, who was standing in the end zone waiting for the ball. Ward took care of the ball until the game-ending throw, but this was a one step forward, two steps back showing from the young passer. That has unfortunately been the case for the better part of the last three weeks. Ward is not on the fantasy radar for Week 4 against the Ravens, and his poor play is making all of the team’s fantasy options largely irrelevant.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cam Ward completed 13-of-20 passes for 183 yards in the Titans’ 24-20, Week 2 loss to the Eagles, adding four rushes for seven yards and two touchdowns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ward’s two scores on the ground doubled his previous career total, though he is now sitting on one passing touchdown through eight quarters. He is at least not turning the ball over, and has taken “just” five sacks. He has been so far unable to heat up his connections with offseason additions Carnell Tate and Wan’Dale Robinson, but he found Elic Ayomanor for two critical gains vs. Philly. Cutting out the negative plays was an absolutely essential first step for Ward, but he has yet to supplement them with big gains or consistent chain-moving. That included botching a Hail Mary in the fourth quarter this afternoon. Ward won’t be much of a superflex option for next week’s road date with the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Cam Ward completed 19-of-32 passes for 140 yards and a touchdown in the Titans’ 23-10, Week 1 loss to the Jets, adding four rushes for 21 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Ward also took three sacks for 13 yards. His touchdown was a too little, too late 11-yard strike to Elic Ayomanor with the Titans trailing 23-3 at the 2:42 mark of the fourth quarter. As was the case down the stretch last season, Ward did a good job of avoiding turnovers, but he struggled to generate positive plays of any kind. He was besieged by pressure, but he just wasn’t making anything happen. That could come in time — there’s a new experienced play-caller in Brian Daboll and several new weapons in the skill corps — but this was a highly discouraging start to the year at home vs. a not-exactly-amazing Jets defense. It was certainly confirmation that Ward is on the outside looking in of top-24 status in superflex leagues for the time being. The Eagles are a rough Week 2 matchup, even if the Titans are at home.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Titans offensive coordinator Brian Daboll said the team’s downfield passing attack has to improve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Cam Ward’s preseason has been as bad or even worse than his rookie campaign. Ward in last week’s preseason game against Seattle completed eight of his 12 attempts for 69 yards. His average depth of target on completed passes this preseason sits at a meager 1.2 . Carnell Tate, meanwhile, has been targeted five times on his 23 preseason routes and does not have a reception to show for it. Daboll has been somewhat defensive this month when asked about Ward’s immense struggles after working on basic fundamentals with the second-year QB in the offseason. Ward, one of the most inaccurate passers in recent NFL history, is unlikely to support more than one fantasy-viable pass catcher in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 5-of-7 targets for 60 yards and two touchdowns in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts was one of the beneficiaries of a pass-heavy second half for a Falcons offense that was forced to abandon the run game facing a multi-touchdown deficit. Pitts took advantage of single coverage a couple times, including on his first touchdown grab. He now has three touchdowns over his past two games as Michael Penix brings some stability to the Atlanta offense. Pitts, who ran a route on 26 of the team’s 38 drop backs against Chicago, will be a viable play in Week 7 against the Niners.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 5-of-6 targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 5 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts remained largely confined to short area work with his game-long reception going for only 13 yards. A second quarter touchdown from five yards out gave the veteran tight end his first trip to paint through five games and his five receptions doubled that of his previous four appearances. Pitts remains a difficult weekly start for as long as Drake London and Bijan Robinson remain healthy. A Week 6 meeting with the Bears in Atlanta should see him remain in the TE2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught all three targets for 47 yards in the Falcons’ Week 4 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts played just one snap on the team’s first two possessions before seeing modest usage the rest of the game. His counting stats were padded in the second half with a 28-yard, catch-and-run reception on a play action pass out of the flat. Pitts isn’t getting the snaps or route participation to return consistent fantasy production and is best left on fantasy benches for as long as Drake London remains healthy. That won’t change ahead of a Week 5 meeting with the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 1-of-2 targets for five yards in the Falcons’ Week 3 win over the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts was the recipient of Michael Penix’s first completion of the 2026 season, with the latter making his season debut following ACL surgery. The return of his starting quarterback was not enough to give Pitts his first fantasy-relevant performance of the season as he watched blocking tight end Austin Hooper score the lone receiving touchdown of the evening from five yards out in the second quarter. Fantasy managers are stuck in the constant hype cycle with Pitts with very little to show for it through three games, making Pitts a difficult start on the road against the Saints in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts caught 1-of-3 targets for 15 yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Cooper Rush was a disaster once again, tanking the fantasy prospects of every Falcon. Pitts narrowly avoided his second straight bagel with a lone catch late in the second quarter. He failed to catch his only target last week. There’s not much to say about Pitts and the entire offense when Rush simply shuts down all production from the jump. Pitts will reclaim a spot in the TE1 ranks if Michael Penix is back for Week 3. He is not on the fantasy radar if Rush is under center once again.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowlers reports Michael Penix (knee) is “not yet ready for live game action.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Fowler said Penix, still recovering from his 2025 ACL injury, “wants to be fully confident before stepping onto the field. And my understanding is the Falcons are leaving the comfort level part of his recovery up to him.” “Penix is coming off his third ACL reconstruction, which is a lot of ACL reconstructions,” ESPN’s Dan Graziano added. “I believe it takes a lot of mental work to convince yourself it’s OK to go back out there and play. If Penix needs more time, I’m sure the Falcons will give it to him, though I believe we will see him on the field at some point this season.” That would leave Tua Tagovailoa as the team’s presumed starter if Tua can play through the oblique strain that sidelined him in Week 1 against the Steelers. If Tua can’t go, the Falcons could be forced to start Cooper Rush for another game or two. Rush, who had the lowest drop back EPA of any QB in Week 1, makes Drake London and Kyle Pitts iffy starts in 12-team fantasy formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Kyle Pitts Sr. had no catches on one target in a Week 1 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts owes most of this to a poor performance by Cooper Rush under center. Pitts played on 39 of the team’s 61 snaps and ran a route on 22 of their 29 dropbacks. He simply wasn’t a factor with Rush struggling to move the ball down the field. We should note that the Falcons were very run-heavy with Rush at quarterback, and Charlie Woerner played 38 snaps and was on the field for 22 run-blocking snaps to just 16 for Pitts. If the Falcons are going to continue to be so focused on rushing the ball, that could cut into some of Pitts’ snaps and usage.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Falcons TE Kyle Pitts caught 3-of-3 targets for 59 yards in Friday’s preseason game against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Pitts ripped off multiple double-digit gains, moved well and looked tough to bring down. He delivered a 37-yard catch on the Falcons’ first drive, securing the pass on a quick out route from bunch formation before taking off down the right sideline. He later had a 16-yard gain on a sort crossing route, where he again chewed up yards after the catch. Pitts is a mid-tier TE1 entering the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports “Falcons people on the ground” believe Kyle Pitts is moving better than he has in years.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: Fowler settles on Pitts being a “certified first or second option in the passing game.” Pitts sets up as a potential high-end TE1 on an offense that loves to use the tight end, and the fact that he finished second in fantasy points among TEs last year is proof of concept that he was already playing better in 2025. With his contract taken care of, perhaps this will be the year Pitts ascends to the top of the tier, the writer said forgetting any of the last five years had happened.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.headline: Falcons signed TE Kyle Pitts to a three-year, $54 million extension with $36 million in guaranteed money.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kyle-pitts.analysis: The Falcons had previously waffled a bit on potentially making Pitts available after “President Of Football” Matt Ryan took over, but must have liked what they saw in the early offseason. Pitts currently looks to be slated for the No. 2 receiver role in Atlanta behind Drake London and should be a fantasy-viable TE1 this year. (Words that have never come back to bite anyone.) Pitts settles for slightly below George Kittle’s $19.1 million per year and Trey McBride’s $19 million per year and will remain in Atlanta for the near future.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 3-of-6 targets for 19 yards in the Eagles’ Week 6 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Despite not lighting up the box score, Lemon was third on the team in targets and finished fourth in receptions. Initial reports had him playing on 52 of the team’s 64 snaps and running a route on 47 of their 52 dropbacks. That was the most routes of any receiver on the team. Some of this was because the team seemed to be easing DeVonta Smith back from injury, and Dontayvsion Wicks briefly left the game with an injury scare, but we also wouldn’t be surprised to see Lemon get more work in what is looking like a bit of a lost season in Philadelphia.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 5-of-7 targets for 43 yards in the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: The good news is that Lemon set new season highs in targets, catches, and yards. The bad news: All of that resulted in a measly 9.3 PPR points. Lemon will hopefully continue to earn more opportunities as the season progresses, but DeVonta Smith’s return could just as easily stall the rookie’s progress. Lemon will be a WR4/5 if Smith remains out for Week 6 against the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Dontayvion Wicks (hamstring) was added to the injury report on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Wicks was listed as a limited participant today, indicating that he strained his hamstring during Thursday’s practice. With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) still sidelined, rookie WR Makai Lemon could be the de facto top receiver, though the team has struggled to use him effectively thus far. Hollywood Brown (ankle) also remains sidelined.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 3-of-6 targets for 27 yards in the Eagles’ Week 4 loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon moved up a spot in the targets pecking order with DeVonta Smith sidelined, but it resulted in the same quiet box score he posted the first three weeks of his career. The No. 20 overall pick is now sitting on 10 receptions for a scoreless 65 yards through his first four NFL appearances. There has yet to be any light at the tunnel with regards to either his usage or the Eagles’ overall offensive environment. Even with byes beginning and injuries mounting, Lemon is not a recommended WR4 heading into Week 5 against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 3-of-4 targets for 29 yards in the Eagles’ Week 3 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon was the target on the team’s first play from scrimmage, gaining a first down on a first down play for the Eagles for the first time all season. The offense would sputter throughout the game on their way to only 47 offensive plays run from scrimmage, capping the fantasy upside of all involved in the process. Lemon has yet to live up to his lofty draft capital through the first three games of his professional career, but he could be called on for heavier work with tight end Dallas Goedert nursing an MCL sprain. Things don’t get any easier with a matchup against the Rams on deck for Week 4, where Lemon can safely be left on fantasy benches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught a 14-yard pass in the Eagles’ Week 2 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon also “added” a -5 yard rush. Lemon’s first quarter catch ended up going down as his only target of the afternoon. He’s now stuck on four catches for nine yards through his first two NFL contests, and is getting soundly out-targeted by Dontayvion Wicks. That’s with Darius Cooper mixing in. The Eagles are calling plays like Lemon has to be manufactured his touches. Two games is not a large sample size, but it is enough to know we can’t rely on Lemon as a WR4 for Week 3 in Chicago.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Makai Lemon caught 3-of-4 targets for negative -5 yards in the Eagles’ Week 1 win over the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: It’s possible things could’ve gone worse for Lemon in his debut, but not much worse. The rookie first-rounder saw two of his four targets come at/behind the line of scrimmage, with his longest target coming eight yards downfield. Lemon’s 28 routes run were good for third-most among Eagles receivers in this one, but we would expect him to see a little more work downfield going forward. Lemon remains a bench stash heading into Week 2’s game against the Titans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: ESPN’s Tim McManus believes “expectations should be tempered early” for Eagles WR Makai Lemon.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: It’s a reasonable assessment for a rookie who missed valuable spring and summer practice reps due to a recurring hamstring strain. Lemon reportedly admitted that he should have been “more professional off the field” regarding the injury, and Eagles WR coach Aaron Moorehead eventually told him to do “whatever” WR DeVonta Smith did during his own hamstring rehab program. Per McManus, “coaches say Lemon attacked the mental part of the game with high intensity as he waited to get healthy.” McManus believes Lemon should get playing time right away, but Smith and WR Dontayvion Wicks will “receive the bulk of targets while the rookie gets his footing.” Lemon must be safely stashed on benches at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Eagles WR Makai Lemon caught 3-of-5 targets for three yards in Friday’s preseason game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon had a rough night, but tonight’s outcome does not make him any less of a top-tier prospect. The first-round rookie was sidelined by a recurring hamstring injury for much of the spring and summer, so a rusty first showing is understandable. Lemon took the blame, on the field, for QB Tanner McKee’s interception, although it is fair to note that McKee’s pass arrived late. Lemon had broken inward, off his stem, and an open window was available to the Eagles’ backup quarterback. Unfortunately, Lemon was forced to slow down and leap for the pass, accidentally batting it backward as he attempted to high-point it. Bengals CB Tacario Davis snagged it and that was that. Davis also broke up a pass intended for Lemon on a corner route 20 yards downfield earlier in the game. He had a good night. Lemon may need to ramp up for another couple of weeks, but he remains a smart draft pick in 12-team leagues. Lemon later went back into the game to field a punt, but went nowhere with it.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.headline: Eagles WR Makai Lemon said he believes he will be ready to play in Week 1 against the Commanders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/makai-lemo.analysis: Lemon returned to practice last week and was seen running with the first-team offense on Monday. Speaking with the media after Monday’s practice, Lemon confirmed that the hamstring injury he had been dealing with was in the same leg that had given him problems earlier this offseason. He’s missed a lot of time, but the rookie first-rounder has just under three weeks to get up to speed and be ready for the season opener, so we’ll see if he can get there. Lemon is worth a late-round pick in fantasy drafts, but shouldn’t be put in lineups until we see how he’s used in game situations.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.headline: Kendre Miller rushed 20 times for 70 yards in the Saints’ Week 6 win over the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.analysis: Milles led the Saints backfield in snaps and touches, adding two receptions for zero yards to his 70 scoreless rushing yards. He is the clear lead runner for the Saints and was tackled at the one-yard line on two separate drives, coming up just short of a touchdown to salvage his fantasy day. Miller’s lack of involvement in the passing game caps his fantasy ceiling but rushing volume makes him a low-end RB3 for Week 7 against a solid Steelers defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.headline: Kendre Miller rushed 10 times for 30 yards in the Saints’ Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.analysis: Miller led the backfield in carries, giving up three to Alvin Kamara and two to CJ Donaldson. Kamara saw the most targets at two, but Donaldson led the way in snaps. This is a true three-headed monster of a backfield, but Miller has at least settled in as the primary early-down option. With game script likely on his side versus the Giants in Week 6, Miller will be a low-end RB3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.headline: Alvin Kamara (back) was not seen practicing on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.analysis: Kamara briefly left the Saints’ Week 4 game against the Falcons to deal with a knee injury. Today, he is sidelined by a back injury. It’s perhaps unsurprising for a 31-year-old player who has clearly lost a step at this point in his career. He is backed up by Kendre Miller and CJ Donaldson. Either player can be stashed in 12-team formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.headline: Saints placed Travis Etienne on injured reserve with a hamstring injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.analysis: This is a tough break. The Saints’ high-priced free agent signee will be sidelined for at least four games. Their Week 8 bye makes him eligible to return in Week 9. Veteran RB Alvin Kamara is the next man up, followed by RB Kendre Miller. Both should be rostered in 12-team leagues. Kamara will likely get the first crack at the starting job, but he has struggled to play efficiently this season, and coach Kellen Moore gave RB CJ Donaldson the backfield’s first green zone touch last week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore said Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) “will miss time” and that a timeline for his return has not yet been determined.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.analysis: It’s unclear how much time Etienne will miss, but it wouldn’t be surprising if this became an injured reserve stint. Alvin Kamara could find himself in a more elevated role next week, perhaps with Kendre Miller joining him in a committee. Etienne exited Week 3’s loss to the Raiders with the injury after rushing for 57 yards on 13 carries. It had already been a tough scene for Etienne-reliant fantasy managers this year just based on how the results on the field were going; this won’t help.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.headline: Kendre Miller rushed four times for 14 yards in the Saints’ Week 3 loss to the Raiders, adding two receptions for five yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.analysis: Miller dealt with an illness this week, but today’s performance can hardly be called sick. Miller had a chance to carve out a role after Travis Etienne aggravated his hamstring injury, but he didn’t do much with the opportunity. If Etienne cannot play, Miller will be a touchdown-dependent FLEX.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.headline: Kendre Miller (illness) is not on New Orleans’ final Week 3 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.analysis: He returned to practice today and practiced in full after missing Thursday to an illness. That’s not exactly a guarantee he’ll play; he was a healthy scratch last week behind Alvin Kamara.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.headline: Saints RB Kendre Miller (illness) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.analysis: Illnesses very rarely sideline players on game day, though this is worth tracking. Saints committee leader, RB Travis Etienne, remains limited by a hamstring injury. Saints RB2 Alvin Kamara could log a decent touch count this weekend against the Raiders, though he is a fairly inefficient player at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.headline: Saints RB Travis Etienne (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.analysis: Etienne remains limited, which keeps him in the questionable camp for the Saints’ Week 3 game against the Raiders. Saints RB3 Kendre Miller was sidelined by an illness, but those rarely impact NFL players’ availability on game day. Veteran RB Alvin Kamara should be rostered wherever he is available.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.headline: Saints RB Travis Etienne (hamstring) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kendre-mil.analysis: Etienne begins the week with a limited session, which is either good or bad, depending on when the injury occurred. If this is a lingering issue from Sunday, Etienne should be considered likely to play. Limited practices early in the week are generally a good sign. However, if he suffered the injury during today’s practice, his Week 3 availability would be in jeopardy. Veteran Saints RB Alvin Kamara would likely get the start, but RB Kendre Miller would be FLEX-viable if Etienne sits.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (head) was ruled out in Week 6 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey exited the game after a 17-yard reception in the first quarter and was seen entering the blue medical tent before being helped to the locker room. The quickness with which he was ruled out could mean the injury is on the severe side. The Chargers are down to their fifth and sixth wideouts on the depth chart. Justin Herbert likely won’t be fantasy relevant for the rest of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (foot) is not on Los Angeles’ final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said he did not know if McConkey or Quentin Johnston would be on snap counts on Sunday. Cool. What we do know is that the Chargers desperately need a win and McConkey is their best receiver, so the incentives are certainly aligned to get McConkey into the fantasy WR3 discussion even with a pitch count.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (foot) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey is on track to once again be active on game day, but it is unclear how involved he will be. Two limited sessions are a good sign, but it would be great to see him practice fully tomorrow. In that instance, starting him as a WR2 would be far more palatable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said he expects Ladd McConkey (foot) to practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: We, in turn, expect McConkey to be listed as a limited participant. An update will be provided if he practices in full. The Chargers’ No. 1 wide receiver was an emergency active last week, goose-egging in the box score. His early-week return to practice puts him on track to play in Week 6 against the Chiefs, but it would be great to see him practice in full by the end of the week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said it’s “possible” that Ladd McConkey (foot) is “working back in this week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey was active last week but an emergency-only player and played zero snaps. With the Chargers having a Week 7 bye, we’d be surprised if they pushed McConkey to play unless they really needed him. Unfortunately, since he was already active last week, we know that they may really need him. His status is up in the air ahead of Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Ladd McConkey (foot) is not expected to play in Week 5 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey did not practice at all this week but was still given a questionable tag on Friday. He was always a long-shot to play after aggravating his foot injury in Week 4. With Quentin Johnston out this week as well, Tre’ Harris will be Justin Herbert’s No. 1 receiver. That puts him in the WR3 mix despite the Chargers’ dismal offensive performance through four weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (foot) is questionable for Los Angeles’ Week 5 game against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey did not practice all week — though they might tack something on in the non-media period on Friday to make it look better — and is clearly just trying to gut it out at this point. He’ll likely be on a snap count if he does play. But Denver’s cornerback room is severely banged up, so McConkey likely remains in low-end WR2 range this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Ladd McConkey (foot) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: McConkey is firmly on the wrong side of questionable at this point, and unfortunately, the rest of the Chargers’ wide receiver corps is fairly banged up. The Chargers are on bye in Week 7. Hopefully, McConkey’s foot injury is not serious enough to keep him out until Week 8. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Chargers WR Ladd McConkey (foot) did not participate in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: Though head coach Jim Harbaugh ambiguously said we would get McConkey in practice, the 24-year-old is officially listed as a non-participant on Wednesday. Harbaugh also previously stated McConkey will be day-to-day after he re-aggravated the foot injury in Week 4. Ultimately, it’s unclear if McConkey will play this week given he generally pushes through injuries with little practice time, but a re-aggravation could lead to a game missed this time around. Stay tuned for practice reports later in the week to provide clarity on his Week 5 status.

https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Ladd McConkey (foot) will be at practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/ladd-mcconkey/.analysis: The phrasing is slightly ambiguous, but we believe he is saying McConkey will be present and participating in some capacity — likely as a limited participant. Harbaugh told reporters yesterday that McConkey was considered day-to-day after aggravating his foot injury in Week 4 against the Seahawks. Getting in a limited session to begin the week gives him a chance to play in Week 5 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. caught 6-of-7 targets for 103 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 6 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Active for the first time since Week 1, the No. 30 overall pick shook off his ankle issue by recording the first 100-yard outing of his now two-game career. It was a much needed effort with No. 1 Garrett Wilson getting tangled up in Christian Gonzalez’s coverage. The highlight was a 48-yard touchdown where Cooper got behind the entire defense then came back to an underthrown deep ball for six. This was after he had a shorter touchdown called back by a dubious Tim Patrick OPI penalty. Now firmly in the mix for No. 2 status even when Adonai Mitchell comes back from his seemingly never-ending finger injury, Cooper is worth rostering in a majority of fantasy leagues with injuries mounting and bye weeks raging. The Jets have a plus Week 7 matchup in the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper (ankle) is active for Week 6 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Up for the first time since Week 1, Cooper should immediately slide in as the Jets’ No. 2 wideout with Adonai Mitchell (finger) still somehow on the shelf. He’s a dart throw WR4 for a contest where the Jets should be playing from behind. Joining Mitchell on the shelf for Gang Green are RB Breece Hall, CB Nahshon Wright, LG Dylan Parham, DT Jack Heflin and EDGE Joseph Ossai.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. will play in Week 6 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Cooper had his 21-day practice window opened earlier this week, but is officially set to return after logging a full practice on Friday. The rookie receiver could step into an immediate role for the Jets with Adonai Mitchell (finger) out for at least one more week, but he could still be a few weeks away from fantasy relevance. Cooper played on just five snaps in Week 1 before his injury, but did catch one pass for 30 yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Jets opened the 21-day practice window for Omar Cooper (ankle).
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Cooper has been on injured reserve since sustaining a high ankle sprain in Week 1. He could return as soon as this week against the Patriots, though he could see his snaps and routes limited. Cooper can be rostered in deeper 12-team formats. Garrett Wilson’s domination of the New York passing offense makes it tough for anyone else to post fantasy-relevant numbers for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Jets placed WR Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: The news was first reported by NFL Insider Ian Rapoport. Cooper is going on injured reserve for an ankle sprain. He’ll be sidelined for at least four games with a designation to return. Rapoport mentions that Cooper should be back “shortly.” Cooper could still make an impact in the second half of his rookie season, but he isn’t worth holding in most fantasy formats at this point.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper (ankle) will not play in Week 2 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: This was always expected to be the case, but head coach Aaron Glenn said on Friday, while speaking with the media, that Cooper, RB/KR Kene Nwangwu (back), S Minkah Fitzpatrick (groin), and EDGE Joseph Ossai (foot) will all miss Sunday’s game against the Packers. It was reported earlier this week that the Jets are hoping to have Cooper back “within the next four weeks,” so it wouldn’t be surprising if he also missed Week 3’s game against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) is “week to week, with the hope that he returns within the next four weeks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: The phrasing at the end of that sentence makes it clear the Jets are pondering not sending him to injured reserve. Fantasy managers who took the plunge in non-dynasty leagues do not necessarily have to hold on to Cooper through the early weeks if something catches their eye on the wire.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports that Jets WR Omar Cooper is believed to have suffered a high ankle sprain in Week 1 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Pelissero also reported that Cooper will undergo an MRI to further assess the injury on Monday, confirming NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport’s report from earlier this evening. Cooper could be looking at a multi-week absence, but only time will tell. Hopefully, it is just a mild injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Jets WR Omar Cooper’s (ankle) X-rays were negative, and he will now undergo an MRI.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: Cooper got hurt at the end of a 30-yard catch-and-run against the Titans, when another player rolled up on his right ankle. Cooper helped bring his offense to the Titans’ four-yard line. It was his only time touching the football. For now, we wait and see what the diagnosis is, but the fact that he needs more imaging is a little discouraging.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.headline: Omar Cooper Jr. suffered an ankle injury in the Jets’ Week 1 game against the Titans and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/omar-coope.analysis: The maligned first-round rookie had a rugged, 30-yard catch-and-run to the Titans’ four-yard line on the Jets’ opening series, but got his right ankle rolled up on in the process. He required the assistance of a cart, but the Jets claimed he might still return. He was then ruled out at halftime. It’s a brutal blow for a first-rounder who supposedly had a rough summer. Despite the delayed ruleout, Cooper should definitely be considered on the wrong side of questionable for Week 2. If he is occupying one of your final bench spots, he will be a shaky hold during this week’s all-important waivers run.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Germie Bernard caught 11-of-12 targets for 87 yards and a touchdown in the Steelers’ Week 6 win over the Bucs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: Bernard began the game with a potentially catastrophic blunder by moving the chains on first down, only to run back behind the sticks in search of more yards. He was taken down behind the line to gain for a turnover on downs. Instead of banishing him to the bench, Aaron Rodgers continued to lean on the rookie throughout the contest for easy completions underneath. He tied DK Metcalf for a team-high in catches. Per the broadcast, it was the most catches by a rookie receiver of Rodgers since the grizzled veteran entered the league. Bernard went from a PPR scam to a full-blown breakout in overtime by extending the ball for a game-winning touchdown with two defenders draped over him. Bernard has 21 targets over the past two weeks. He also has at least 80 yards in back-to-back games. He is looking at a WR3 ranking for his Week 7 matchup with the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said Ben Skowronek (leg) has been ruled out for Week 6.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: We weren’t exactly worried about Skowronek siphoning many targets away, but with him out of the pecking order entirely Germie Bernard should be a wheels-up WR3 for Week 6 now that both Skowronek and Roman Wilson have been ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Germie Bernard caught 6-of-9 targets for 80 yards in the Steelers’ Week 5 win over the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: Michael Pittman (foot) was ruled out earlier in the week, and then Roman Wilson dislocated his finger during the game, so there wasn’t a lot of competition for Bernard and DK Metcalf. The rookie from Alabama played the same number of snaps as Metcalf and ran a route on 35 of the team’s 38 dropbacks. This isn’t an explosive passing attack, but Bernard looks like the WR2 in Pittsburgh now and is more of an intermediate and short-area target than DK Metcalf, which could lead to decent fantasy value over the next few weeks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Roman Wilson has been ruled out for the remainder of Week 5 against the Colts with a dislocated finger.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: Wilson had just one target in the first half. He pinned the reception to his hip, but the ball was ripped loose by a defender, which not only made the pass incomplete but also seemed to dislocate Wilson’s finger. With Michael Pittman Jr. also hurt, we should continue to see a lot of Germie Bernard in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said Michael Pittman re-aggravated his foot injury and will miss multiple weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: McCarthy told reporters the team is evaluating Pittman’s roster spot, meaning they could place him on injured reserve. He would miss at least four weeks while on IR. Pittman tried to play through the foot injury but only made it two weeks before aggravating the issue. He was spotted using a scooter to support his foot in the locker room on Wednesday. We suspect the Steelers will place him on IR to give Pittman enough time to fully recover. Germie Bernard will now operate as the team’s permanent WR3, with Roman Wilson taking on more work as the clear No. 2 receiver. Both players will be decent FLEX options for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Michael Pittman (foot) is questionable for Pittsburgh’s Week 3 game against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: He was limited in practice all three days this week with a foot injury that kept him out of Week 2. We’d say Pittman is on the optimistic side of questionable based on his participation status. If he’s out again, it would likely be Germie Bernard picking up the slack, as he did in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Michael Pittman (foot) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: Pittman didn’t practice once last week, so a limited session today is a big step in the right direction. Germie Bernard took his spot in the lineup on Sunday and caught four passes for 35 yards, but he also coughed up a drop that was then intercepted by New England. The mistake all but guarantees his return to the bench once Pittman is healthy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Germie Bernard caught 4-of-8 targets for 35 yards in the Steelers’ Week 2 loss to the Patriots
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: Bernard saw increased opportunity with Michael Pittman ruled out for Week 2. He caught all four of his receptions on one drive in the second quarter but ended as the second-most targeted receiver on the team. Bernard seemed to lose much of the trust he earned with a rough bobble on an Aaron Rodgers screen pass that led to an interception in the fourth quarter. The rookie second-round pick will find fantasy relevance while Pittman is out, but is no more than a fantasy WR5 for Week 3 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: Steelers WR Germie Bernard caught 1-of-2 targets for 13 yards and one touchdown in Thursday’s preseason game against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: Bernard started alongside other Steelers backups this evening, indicating he has not yet earned a starting role in three-wide receiver sets. That said, he looked good. Bernard found the end zone via a screen pass on the Steelers’ second drive, shaking a defender immediately after the catch before muscling past another as he crossed the plane. He nearly scored again on the following drive, but QB Will Howard overthrew him in the end zone. The Steelers’ top-two WRs, DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman, are just getting over injuries, and No. 3 WR Roman Wilson should not be considered insurmountable in-house competition. Bernard could work his way into the lineup early in the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.headline: ESPN’s Benjamin Solak reports Germie Bernard “ran almost exclusively with the second-stringers” during 11-on-11s and “struggled with some of the finer details of the playbook.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/germie-ber.analysis: Not a glowing review. Combine Bernard’s struggles with the idea that the Steelers might remain run-heavy this year (also espoused by Solak) and it feels like Bernard might just be a deep-league bench option this year. It should be noted that the overwhelming majority of the drumbeat about Bernard this offseason has been positive, so perhaps this was just an off-day.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: Dameon Pierce rushed 12 times for 35 yards and a touchdown in the Eagles’ Week 6 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: With Saquon Barkley, Tank Bigsby, and Will Shipley all hurt, and Carson Steele getting injured early in this game, Pierce took every single carry for the Eagles on Sunday. He also played on 61 of the team’s 64 snaps. However, that wasn’t able to amount to much on the ground with all of Philadelphia’s injuries. Pierce was also asked to pass block a lot, which means he only ran a route on 15 of the team’s 52 dropbacks. That’s going to limit his fantasy value, and he looks like a TD-dependent FLEX play while he remains the starter. The upside is that there doesn’t seem to be anybody coming for his job until Barkley (hamstring) returns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: Eagles ruled out RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring) for Week 6 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: It was pretty clear that this was where things were headed when Barkley was unable to practice on Wednesday and Thursday. We do not yet know Barkley’s official Friday practice participation level, but he was not seen practicing during the portion of practice open to the media. Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele and practice squad player Jaydon Blue will likely split touches this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: Barkley is firmly on the wrong side of questionable for his team’s Week 6 game against the Panthers, potentially leaving Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele and practice squad player Jaydon Blue to split touches. Hopefully, reports clarify whether Pierce would handle a sizable workload as the de facto starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: Dameon Pierce rushed 11 times for 14 yards in the Eagles’ Week 5 loss to the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: Pierce “added” two catches for -2 yards. He took over as the Eagles’ lead back after Will Shipley went down with a foot injury in the first half. Carson Steele did not see the field for a single offensive snap. Pierce would presumably in line for a workhorse role in Week 6 if Shipley and Saquon Barkley are both out, but his efficiency today speaks for itself. This isn’t an offense capable of opening running lanes, nor is Pierce a back who can make a lot out of a little. Pierce is a low-priority waiver wire add for Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: Will Shipley (foot) will not return to the Eagles’ Week 5 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: Shipley suffered the foot injury in the second quarter and was initially listed as questionable to return. He will now miss the remainder of the contest. Dameon Pierce is the only other running back on the roster with a touch today. Carson Steele is also active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: Will Shipley (foot) is questionable to return in Week 5 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: Shipley got stuffed on a carry in the second quarter and was checked out by trainers after the play. He went to the locker room after a brief trip to the blue medical tent. Dameon Pierce will be the next man up if Shipley’s day is over. Carson Steele is the only other back on the roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: Barkley will likely be listed as a non-participant on today’s official injury report. He is unlikely to play in Week 5 against the Jaguars. Aside from Barkley, the Eagles have RBs Will Shipley and Dameon Pierce on the active roster. Shipley will probably lead the backfield in touches this week, but it could be a messy workload split.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: Eagles activated RB Dameon Pierce to the team’s active roster.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: Pierce will probably operate as the team’s No. 2 back behind Will Shipley this week against the Jaguars, one of the league’s best rush defenses. Tank Bigsby and Saquon Barkley are sidelined, leaving the Eagles scraping bottom for backfield depth. Look for Pierce to get some early-down work against the Jaguars. Shipley, who had six carries for 23 yards last week, is the only viable fantasy option of the two, though head coach Nick Sirianni heaped praise on Pierce Wednesday. “He’s an NFL starting running back,” Sirriani said of Pierce. “Maybe wouldn’t have said that when he was on our practice squad publicly, because of the fear of losing him. But he’s an NFL starting running back.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Tank Bigsby will have core muscle surgery and be placed on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: Rapoport reports there are hopes that Bigsby will be back “in six weeks or shorter.” The 24-year-old back will be required to miss at least four games now that he’s headed for an IR stint. With Saquon Barkley (hamstring) also at risk of missing at least one game, third-string RB Will Shipley could be in line for a busy day in Week 5 against the Jaguars. Shipley rushed six times for 23 yards in Sunday’s loss to the Rams, but could be a sneaky option in PPR leagues given his pass-catching profile during his days at Clemson, when he caught 85 passes over three seasons. It also wouldn’t be surprising if Dameon Pierce or Jaydon Blue were promoted off the practice squad and saw early down touches while Shipley serves in more of a third-down role. There’s a lot to figure out here over the next few days.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.headline: Eagles signed RB Dameon Pierce to the practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dameon-pie.analysis: The news was first reported by ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler. Pierce was released by the Eagles on Sunday with the team keeping Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley to backup Saquon Barkley. Pierce will head to the practice squad and be the next running back up if an injury arises.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 3-of-5 targets for 87 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson, whose season-high yardage coming into the week was 54 — his total in both of the past two weeks — got loose a couple times in this one, mostly when the Falcons ditched their usual run-heavy offense in favor of a fast-pace pass-heavy approach while facing a multiple touchdown second half deficit. Running a route no 32 of the Falcons’ 38 drop backs, Dotson led the team in receiving yards thanks largely to a 41-yard grab. Dotson could be a deep league play in Week 7 against the Niners.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-4 targets for 54 yards in the Falcons’ Week 5 loss to the Ravens.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson’s 54 yards finished second on the team behind alpha Drake London but his four targets finished behind London, Kyle Pitts, and Bijan Robinson. His status as the starting wide receiver opposite London likely means little in the wake of modest volume games that continue to stack up. He can safely be left on, or returned to, the waiver wire.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-3 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Falcons’ Week 4 win over the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson continues to operate as the team’s WR2 opposite Drake London but remains unlikely to return consistent fantasy production in an offense heavily concentrated on its top two options in London and Bijan Robinson. Dotson’s touchdown came in the fourth quarter with the team cruising, pushing the lead to 21 points with under 10 minutes to play. Fantasy managers can safely keep Dotson on the bench ahead of a Week 5 meeting with the Ravens in Atlanta.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 2-of-4 targets for 11 yards in the Falcons’ Week 2 loss to the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson saw four targets for the second week in a row. He went for 19 yards on one catch last week and didn’t look any different this time around. Dotson is the team’s No. 2 receiver by routes, but there aren’t enough targets to go around after Drake London, Kyle Pitts, and Bijan Robinson all get theirs. Dotson is not on the fantasy radar for Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson caught 1-of-3 targets for 19 yards in a Week 1 loss to the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson actually operated as the second receiver for the Falcons in this one, running a route on 20 of the team’s 29 dropbacks. He also played 38 snaps, while Olamide Zaccheaus played just 18. That didn’t amount to much, but it’s something for fantasy managers in deeper leagues to keep in mind when Michael Penix eventually gets back onto the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: ESPN’s Marc Raimondi believes Falcons WR Zachariah Branch could start the season as a “gadget guy,” before later earning a starting role.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Branch was a screen game dominator in college, with speed to spare. Raimondi thinks the Falcons will attempt to replicate his Georgia game early on, but Branch has a chance to become “the No. 3 guy, maybe even the No. 2 guy at some point.” Falcons WRs Jahan Dotson and Olamide Zaccheaus sit in those two spots. Branch is unlikely to contribute meaningfully in fantasy early in the year, but he is worth keeping an eye on in-season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: The Athletic’s Josh Kendall believes that if the Falcons make a “random offseason move,” it might come at wide receiver.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: The Atlanta depth chart at wideout is sparse even after we account for third-round pick Zachariah Branch in the draft. The No. 2 receiver right now might be Jahan Dotson. Olamide Zaccheaus is also in the picture. The Falcons still have $27 million in cap space but we’ve rarely heard them mentioned by national reporters as interested in the Stefon Diggs/Deebo Samuel/Keenan Allen best veteran free agent wideout tier. Those guys aren’t mentioned in this report either, but they do make plenty of sense from a roster standpoint.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: The Athletic’s Josh Kendall believes Jahan Dotson “may be” Atlanta’s No. 2 receiver this year.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: The Falcons released Darnell Mooney and KhaDarel Hodge, leaving them with a depth chart behind Mooney of Olamide Zaccheaus, Casey Washington and Deven Thompkins. The Falcons, who lost their first-round pick in the ill-fated James Pearce trade, also don’t have many draft picks this year and could be less likely than most teams to draft a wideout that could challenge Dotson for a role. We’re not quite at “sleeper” status here, but we’re at least late-round Best Ball curious.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Falcons signed WR Jahan Dotson, formerly of the Eagles, to a two-year contract worth $15 million.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Dotson could see starter’s snaps in Atlanta after the Falcons parted ways with Darnell Mooney. Dotson was stuck behind DeVonta Smith and A.J. Brown over the past couple seasons in Philadelphia with no real way to see consistent routes or targets in the Eagles’ ultra run-heavy offense. Dotson managed just 37 catches and one touchdown over 34 regular season games with the Eagles. In Atlanta he will be a distant WR2 at best in Kevin Stefanski’s offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.headline: Jahan Dotson was held without a catch in the Eagles’ Wild Card loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jahan-dots.analysis: Finishing up his second year as the Eagles’ sparingly-used No. 3 wideout, Dotston was sporadically productive in a dysfunctional passing attack. Headed to free agency after Philly declined his fifth-year team option, Dotson could end up back with the Eagles on a non-guaranteed contract. The 2022 draft bust’s two years in the Eagles’ system probably make him worth more to Philly than anybody else. That being said, we doubt Dotson would be a candidate to ascend to No. 2 status if A.J. Brown is traded.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller did not have a catch on two targets in the Panthers’ Week 6 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: Initial reports have Waller playing on 36 of the team’s 79 snaps and running a route on 21 of their 46 dropbacks. Tommy Tremble, the other tight end, ran a route on 14 dropbacks, so Waller is technically the primary option in the passing game of the two. However, Tremble scored two touchdowns this week. We don’t recommend chasing either guy in fantasy right now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller (toe) is not on Carolina’s final Week 6 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: He upgraded to a full practice today. Waller will be a low-end TE2 with Jalen Coker (quad) playing in Week 6 against a Jalen Hurts-less Eagles outfit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller (toe) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: He appears to be trending towards playing, though Waller is old enough that we probably shouldn’t count it as a sure thing that he’ll get off the questionable line. Waller would be a reasonable TE2 if he plays against the Eagles on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller (toe) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: The Panthers should have their veteran receiving tight end on the field when they take on the Eagles this week. Waller remains a viable TE1, albeit as a somewhat volatile producer. We expect him to be practicing in full by the end of the week, coming off a restful bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller caught 3-of-6 targets for 36 yards in the Panthers’ Week 4 win over the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: Waller saw minimal involvement as quarterback Bryce Young leaned into his top option through the air, feeding Tetairoa McMillan 16 targets on 41 pass attempts in the absence of both Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette. Fantasy managers that scooped Waller off of waivers following his two-touchdown game in Week 2 are surely left disappointed in the recent returns, making Waller a potential drop candidate as the Panthers head to their bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller caught 5-of-8 targets for 51 yards in the Panthers’ Week 3 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: With Xavier Legette (knee) sidelined and Jalen Coker (quad) joining him, Panthers tight ends Waller, Tommy Tremble and Mitchell Evans combined for 11/128. It was Waller’s most prolific receiving day of the season even though he didn’t find the end zone. Waller is undoubtedly providing valuable real-life reps for the Cats, but with 10 total receptions through three contests, he is looking like too much of a role player to rise above TE2 streamer status heading into Week 4 against the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller caught all three of his targets for 33 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers’ Week 2 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: Waller saw as many targets as Tommy Tremble and Mitchell Evans combined. Unlike the other Carolina tight ends, Waller is still an explosive pass-catcher and a de facto wide receiver. When Bryce Young looked his way, it was for a big play. He made good on the minor role with his first two touchdowns as a Panther. Waller only has five targets through two weeks. He will make the occasional big play, but it’s hard to get him in fantasy lineups with such a limited role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Darren Waller caught both of his targets for 28 yards in the Panthers’ Week 1 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: Waller had a short touchdown grab called back on offensive pass interference while rotating snaps and routes with Tommy Tremble. Both Panthers tight ends ran 19 routes on the day and saw two targets from Bryce Young. Waller will continue as a touchdown-reliant TE2 option in Week 2 against the Falcons.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Panthers declared TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, WR John Metchie, QB Haynes King, S Zakee Wheatley, OT Albert Reese, OLB Patrick Jones II, and DT Cam Jackson inactive for Week 1 against the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: Sanders, who worked through a lingering ankle injury this offseason, won’t suit up for the team’s season opener. That leaves Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble as the Panthers’ top two tight ends against Chicago. Waller will be a touchdown-dependent TE2 option who probably won’t run many routes in the run-first Carolina offense. Tremble should remain on waiver wires.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.headline: Panthers TE Darren Waller practiced on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/darren-wal.analysis: Waller looked “big and fast” in Monday practice, per head coach Dave Canales, and reportedly hit 20 MPH on one of his routes. The veteran tight end was seen catching passes from Bryce Young and could have a chance to suit up for the Panthers’ Week 1 game against the Bears. It’s still too early to know how significant a role Waller will have in Canales’ offense, but he could have some fantasy viability as a streaming option in what is a very thin tight end room in Carolina.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith completed 20-of-30 passes 252 yards, one touchdown and an interception in the Jets’ 26-19, Week 6 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: Smith was missing Adonai Mitchell for the fourth consecutive contest, but he found returning rookie first-rounder Omar Cooper Jr. for a sizzling 6/103/1 on seven targets. That was a necessary development with Garrett Wilson being limited to 4/44 as he was hounded by Christian Gonzalez. The 252 yards were Smith’s second most of the season, though his first interception of 2026 was a dreadful, costly mistake in the fourth quarter. He threw it in Keyon Sadiq’s direction, but Charles Woods ran the rookie tight end’s route for him. Disappointing, though we now have six games of evidence that Smith isn’t the bottom-three QB he appeared to be amidst the Raiders’ 2025 fiasco. Things could also get better if Mitchell soon returns and forms a legit trio with Wilson and Cooper. Smith won’t rise above mid-range QB2 status even for premium matchups, but he does have a primo Week 7 spot in the Dolphins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith completed 17-of-30 passes for 182 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ 17-12, Week 5 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: Smith “added” five carries for seven yards. He also lost a fumble. Coming off a generationally bad Week 4 clunker against the Bears, Smith was hardly outstanding in rainy MetLife Stadium conditions, though he was superior to Deshaun Watson. Not that you would have noticed in real time. Smith fumbled “just” once compared to Watson’s four, also taking “only” four sacks to Watson’s staggering eight. Like Watson, Smith also lost a key pass catcher to a concussion, with Kenyon Sadiq going down in the third quarter. Both before and after Sadiq’s injury, the Jets mostly rode the run, with Braelon Allen turning his 24 carries into a strong 116 yards. Smith has predictably faded a bit after his relatively “hot start,” while he now has a tough Week 6 road test in the reviving Patriots. Smith’s decent weapons — which will hopefully include Adonai Mitchell next week — keep him in the QB2 mix, but only as a low-end option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith completed 8-of-15 attempts for 119 yards and a touchdown in the Jets’ Week 4 loss to the Bears.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: The Jets had the ball for a mere 17 minutes, as the Tyson Bagent-led Chicago offense dominated time of possession from start to finish. Smith, who had a combined 58 pass attempts over his past two outings, struggled against consistent pressure from the Bears front seven. His only highlight of the day came on a 58-yard touchdown strikes to Isaiah Williams in the fourth quarter. Smith should be a superflex option next week against the Browns. The return of Adonai Mitchell (finger) would boost Smith’s ceiling.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith completed 31-of-37 passes for 321 yards and three touchdowns in the Jets’ 31-24, Week 3 loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: Smith also ran for 12 yards and completed one of his two two-point conversion attempts. The sacks, of which he took five, were an issue, but it was an otherwise flawless game from the veteran passer. He got particularly hot in the second half, getting points on the board in three of his four drives after the break. Smith was unfortunately sacked and lost the football on the final drive of the game, giving Detroit the win. The Jets don’t look like a team that is going to win many games this year, but it’s not because of Geno. Smith will be a viable Superflex option when he takes on the Bears next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith completed 27-of-41 passes for 247 yards and a touchdown in New York’s 20-17, Week 2 loss to the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: The Jets weren’t able to make many big plays in this one. Geno’s longest completion was a 43-yard connection to Breece Hall that Hall caught three yards beyond the line of scrimmage. There was not another pass completion longer than 17 yards on the day. That being said, Geno didn’t make many bad decisions and took what the Packers’ defense was giving him. The offensive line provided no push in the running game, so the Jets may need to let Geno play more aggressively if they’re going to put up more points. That could start in Week 3 against a Lions team that figures to score a lot of points.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Geno Smith completed 19-of-24 passes for 215 yards in the Jets’ 23-10, Week 1 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: Smith “added” six rushes for seven yards. Although it was not a productive day in fantasy football, it was a highly encouraging one in “real life.” At least for one game, the Jets’ blocking was 10x better than what Smith experienced in Las Vegas last season, and he took advantage by taking zero sacks and hitting several down-field passes to his talented skill corps. Three different receivers generated gains of 30-plus yards, but Omar Cooper Jr.'s was more of a catch-and-run. Unfortunately, the rookie injured his ankle in the process. Smith is going to be a “highs and lows” quarterback in even the best of years, but there is now reason to believe 2026 will not be all lows like 2025 was with the Raiders. The Packers will be a tougher opponent for the Jets’ home opener in week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Cade Klubnik will be the team’s QB2 to start the regular season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: What this means is that Geno Smith has plenty of job security. Klubnik in the preseason completed 21 of 34, passes for 190 yards, no touchdowns, and one interception while taking four sacks. Klubnik would be a marked downgrade from Smith if the veteran misses time in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich said he’s been “so impressed” with Geno Smith’s play.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: Reich has reportedly added wrinkles to the offense he deployed as head coach of the Colts and Panthers. At both of those stops his offenses were near the bottom of the league in most basic offensive metrics. Smith, meanwhile, has looked sharp as the team’s starting quarterback throughout training camp and in limited preseason snaps. He’ll look to bounce back from a nightmarish statistical 2025 season in Vegas. Jets players, including Garrett Wilson, told The Athletic that they have enjoyed the “player empowerment” that comes along with Reich’s coaching style and his offensive scheming, which leaves room for improvisation. The Jets offense could be functional as long as Smith, 35, is healthy and upright.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: SNY’s Connor Hughes reports Geno Smith (foot soreness) will start Friday’s preseason game against the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: Smith will undoubtedly only play a series or two, but it’s confirmation he’s over the “soreness” that held him out last weekend. Smith would have reportedly played through the “injury” during the regular season, so it was never believed to be serious. Any injury is worth noting for a 35-year-old player coming off a rough, rough year, but this one is in the rear-view mirror.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.headline: Jets QB Geno Smith (foot soreness) will not play in Friday’s preseason game against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/geno-smith.analysis: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports that the team is not concerned about Smith’s foot soreness, writing, “if this was a regular-season game, he’d be a go.” Smith has reportedly been pushing the ball downfield in practice. Those hoping to catch a glimpse of the Jets’ passing attack will have to check back next week to see if the foot issue has been resolved. Rookie QB Cade Klubnik gets the start tonight.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: Tommy Tremble caught all four of his targets for 46 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers’ Week 6 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: The Panthers seemed a little concerned about the Eagles’ pass rush since Tremble played on 54 of the team’s 79 snaps. He also was on the field for more than half of their dropbacks, but a large chunk of those were in pass-blocking situations. Still, he was schemed wide open on both touchdown passes, which led to a great fantasy day. It’s just not something we would recommend chasing next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: The Athletic’s Joseph Person believes the Panthers could target TE Kenyon Sadiq in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: Person said the Panthers, who hold the 19th pick in the 2026 draft, could target two Oregon players: Sadiq, who had 51 receptions for 560 yards and eight touchdowns in his final collegiate season, and safety Dillon Thieneman, one of the most sought-after secondary options in this year’s draft. The team would likely have to trade up to make sure they have a shot at Sadiq, who would join Tommy Tremble and Ja’Tavion Sanders in the Carolina tight end room if he lands with the Panthers. The Panthers in 2025 targeted the tight end position at a 21 percent clip, the seventh lowest mark in the NFL. “Could that change with Brad Idzik taking over the play calling and the addition of offensive specialist Darrell Bevell, who was in Seattle with Canales when the Seahawks traded for All-Pro tight end Jimmy Graham?” Person said. “Possibly.” Sadiq, who ranks 11th in yards per route run among tight ends in the 2026 draft class, would probably be a rotational player in Carolina.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: Tommy Tremble caught 3-of-3 targets for 22 yards in Carolina’s Wild Card Round loss to the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: The Panthers failed to establish a full-time TE1 for most of this year, with Tremble only going over 75.4 percent of the snaps in the final two games of the regular season. He played 54-of-67 snaps versus the Rams. Tremble caught more than one ball in six of his 18 games played this season. He’s low-end TE2 fodder at best entering the final year of his contract.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: Tommy Tremble caught 3-of-4 targets for 38 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 18 loss to the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: Tremble caught a touchdown pass early from Bryce Young to get the Panthers within a score at 10-7. The former Notre Dame tight end finished with just two touchdowns in 2025, and remains much more effective as a blocker than as a receiver. The Panthers didn’t really showcase any of their tight ends this year, making it hard to trust any of them in fantasy leagues. Ostensibly they’d like Ja’Tavion Sanders to be their main receiving tight end, but he just can’t stay healthy. Tremble could get a playoff game next week if the Falcons beat the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: Tommy Tremble caught his lone target for zero yards in the Panthers’ Week 7 win against the Jets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: Tremble logged 12 routes on the day while Ja’Tavion Sanders ran 14 routes and did not catch either of his targets. Neither Tremble nor Sanders are fantasy relevant unless one of the tight ends misses time. Tremble had been a viable streaming option while Sanders was sidelined with an ankle injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: Tommy Tremble caught 4-of-4 targets for 39 yards in the Panthers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: He added one Liu Kang flying kick against a Cowboys defender in the open field, though nothing was called. Tremble appears and disappears from the Panthers passing game depending on the matchups, and when Ja’Tavion Sanders comes back he’ll likely lose most of his pure passing-game snaps. He can be left on waiver wires heading into Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: Tommy Tremble caught 5-of-8 targets for 42 yards and a touchdown in the Panthers’ Week 4 loss to the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: Tremble entered the game with only six targets all year but was needed for more with Ja’Tavion Sanders sidelined and provided some volume. His score was a seven-yarder to cap the Panthers’ opening drive. The Panthers would then give up 42 unanswered points before Tremble took a massive hit to bring them to the one-yard line with 2:20 remaining. He was shaken up but said afterward he was fine. The Panthers are so low on quality targets that Tremble could stick in the top 24 for however long Sanders is sidelined, but it is difficult to recommend anyone in this awful overall offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: Ja’Tavion Sanders caught 2-of-2 targets for 11 yards in the Panthers’ Week 3 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: Sanders’ usage came back down to earth after a nine-target Week 2 put him on fantasy radars. The 22-year-old didn’t get his first target until the second half, when he caught a Bryce Young pass and hurdled a defender for a seven-yard gain. The Panthers offense is a difficult one to project for consistent fantasy points, but he will have better days in a more pass-heavy game script. Fellow tight end Tommy Tremble caught both of his targets for 16 yards on the day. Sanders is a deep league streamer option at tight end for Week 4 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: Panthers TE Tommy Tremble (back) is not on the injury report and will play in Week 1 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: Tremble underwent back surgery in May and opened training camp on the PUP list. He returned to practice and was activated from PUP last week. J’Tavion Sanders should slot in as the Panthers’ starting tight end heading into his second season, but Tremble will pitch in for blocking reps and some work in 12-personnel looks. Tremble’s return to the lineup will keep Sanders off the tight end streaming radar for now.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.headline: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said TE Ja’Tavion Sanders “has really improved as a pass catcher.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tommy-trem.analysis: The Associated Press’ Steve Reed adds that it “sort of sounds like he will be the primary pass receiver at that position,” but he notes nothing is “etched in stone.” Sanders has decent odds of etching it in stone if his improved play translates to early-season success. Tommy Tremble, Sanders’ primary competition at the position, “hopes” he will be ready for Week 1 but has not yet returned to practice after undergoing back surgery in May. Sanders is a worthwhile dart throw, who can be paired with a reliable, if unexciting, veteran option in drafts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 6-of-9 passes for 86 yards in the Panthers’ Week 6 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan saw a lot of Quinyon Mitchell in tight coverage on Sunday, but he had a solid day that could have been much better after a fourth-quarter pass went off his hands in the end zone. It would have been a difficult catch with Mitchell draped all over him, but it was a catchable pass. More importantly, it shows that McMillan remains a key piece of this passing game, and he did run the most routes of any receiver on the team.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 14-of-16 targets for 192 yards and two touchdowns in the Panthers’ Week 4 win over the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan set career highs in both receptions and yardage in the first half with nine catches for 147 yards before the break. He operated as the clear alpha in a pass attack without both Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette, routinely dusting everyone the Lions had at their disposal in an injury-ravaged secondary. While the receiving line surely turns heads, fantasy managers were left even more ecstatic about the way in which he was utilized, with the second-year receiver catching six passes for 94 yards and both touchdowns while aligned in the slot. Offensive coordinator Brad Idzik is providing structure, sequencing, and situational tendencies unlike anything fans had grown accustomed to when head coach Dave Canales was helming the offense, resulting in quarterback Bryce Young leading the league in passing while averaging more than 30 points per game through the first month of play. McMillan’s ceiling remains sky-high as a legitimate WR1 when the Panthers square off against the Eagles fin Week 6 following their bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 2-of-5 targets for 17 yards in the Panthers’ Week 3 loss to the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: By far McMillan’s quietest outing of the young season came with Jalen Coker departing midway through with a quad injury. No. 3 Xavier Legette didn’t even suit up as he battled a knee issue. That allowed the Browns’ defense to key in on T-Mac, and key they did. Fill-in No. 2 Brycen Tremayne took advantage with four receptions for a team-leading 83 yards. Heinous stuff for McMillan managers, but he has an immediate Week 4 bounce-back spot in the defense-less Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.headline: Tetairoa McMillan caught 5-of-10 targets for 101 yards in the Panthers’ Week 2 win over the Falcons.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/tetairoa-m.analysis: McMillan took a backseat to Jalen Coker last week. The opportunities were distributed more evenly this time around. McMillan led the team with 10 targets and a 28 percent target share. Coker wasn’t far behind with nine targets. McMillan easily led the team in yards, though Coker caught eight balls and Darren Waller popped up for a two-score game.
