Moses signed a three-year, $24 million contract with the Patriots this offseason and said he’s “just pacing things out” when asked about his limited participation in OTAs thus far. For now, this seems like a non-issue as training camp nears, but it will be something worth monitoring if the 34-year-old continues to be limited late into the summer.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/morgan-mos.headline: Patriots agreed to terms with OT Morgan Moses, formerly of the Jets, on a three-year, $24 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/morgan-mos.analysis: Per NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo, the deal is worth up to $28.5 million. The Patriots fielded arguably the worst offensive line in the league last year, so it’s no surprise to see them spending big to improve that unit. Protecting Drake Maye has to be a priority for the rebuilding Pats this offseason. Even at 34 years old, Moses is a solid right tackle option for a team desperate to improve both bookends to their offensive line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/morgan-mos.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Jets OT Morgan Moses “was given a clean bill of health from the Jets’ medical staff.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/morgan-mos.analysis: As Garafolo notes, Moses played through a Grade 2 MCL sprain last year. Moses missed some time early in the year because of the injury but ultimately pushed through it for much of the remainder of the season. Moses will officially be a free agent next week unless the Jets make a last-second move to keep him around. Even at 34 years old, the career right tackle should have some suitors on the open market.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/morgan-mos.headline: Jets declared CB Michael Carter II, DL Phidarian Mathis, LB Jamin Davis, S Jaylin Sampson, OL Morgan Moses, EDGE Braiden McGregor, and CB Jarrick Bernard-Converse inactive for Week 18 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/morgan-mos.analysis: The Jets face a Dolphins team that can get into the playoffs with a win and a Broncos loss to the Chiefs. Aaron Rodgers is also making what may be the final start of his career, and only one touchdown pass shy of 500 for his career. It’s the end of another tumultuous season for the Jets, who are looking at a number of major changes this offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/morgan-mos.headline: Jets declared OT Morgan Moses, LB CJ Mosley, DE Braiden McGregor, DT Leonard Taylor, CB Jarrick Bernard-Converse, and RB Izzy Abanikanda inactive for Week 4 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/morgan-mos.analysis: Moses in Week 3 went down with a knee injury and is expected to miss some time, though he avoided injured reserve. Losing Moses is a blow for a Jets offensive line that Pro Football Focus grades as the league’s 19th best pass-blocking unit.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-ocon.headline: Raiders declared QB Aidan O’Connell, S Tristin McCollum, S Dalton Johnson, DE Cian Stone, OG Bryce Cabeldue, and DT Tonka Hemingway inactive for Week 6 against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-ocon.analysis: The Raiders didn’t have any players listed as questionable entering this one. Hemingway, who is dealing with a concussion, was ruled out before the weekend and will look to return in Week 7 against the Rams if he can clear concussion protocol.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-ocon.headline: Raiders HC Klint Kubiak said “all three (QBs) deserve first team reps” this week after Thursday’s preseason game against the Cardinals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-ocon.analysis: Kubiak didn’t come right out and say Mendoza could see more first-team reps, but it feels like things are trending that way. His response came after he was asked if Mendoza specifically deserved more first-team reps after a nice outing in his first taste of preseason action, to which Kubiak said the team will put together a plan to ensure all three QBs get first-team reps, which feels somewhat evasive and unrealistic, given that we know career backup Aidan O’Connell isn’t contending for a starting job in camp. Kubiak went on record after Thursday’s game, saying that the battle for QB1 remains Kirk Cousins’ to lose. It wouldn’t be surprising if Mendoza did see more first-team reps in the coming days, but we would be surprised if O’Connell began working in with the first team. That said, it will be worth monitoring Mendoza’s first-team reps going forward, as he could still push Cousins for the starting role before Week 1.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-ocon.headline: The Athletic’s Sam Warren believes “the door is open” for the Raiders to move Aidan O’Connell.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-ocon.analysis: Yes, well, the door has been open for almost two years now. O’Connell, entering the final year of his rookie contract, played only in the Week 18 finale with Geno Smith hurt and Kenny Pickett self-combusting. It’s clear the front office doesn’t want much to do with him. He’s a plausible trade or release candidate at last cuts as the Raiders look likely to roll with Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza on the active roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-ocon.headline: Raiders general manager John Spytek said, “the best guy will play” when asked about starting a rookie quarterback immediately.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-ocon.analysis: It’s no secret the Raiders are more than likely going to select Indiana’ Fernando Mendoza No. 1 overall in the 2026 NFL Draft. However, the question has been lingering on whether the Raiders will start Mendoza out of the gate or let him sit for a bit first. Las Vegas signed Kirk Cousins as a veteran presence in the locker room and still have Aidan O’Connell as quarterback depth. Spytek implied that a competition between Cousins, O’Connell, and Mendoza could shake out the Week 1 starter. Mendoza would be the franchise quarterback, but there is a good chance Cousins (or even O’Connell) start in the interim while the rookie gets better prepared for the long-term.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-ocon.headline: Aidan O’Connell completed 6-of-12 attempts for 65 yards in the Raiders’ Week 18 win against the Chiefs, adding one rush for seven yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-ocon.analysis: O’Connell entered the game in relief of Kenny Pickett, who was yanked in the first half after a rough start. It was the first game action of 2025 for O’Connell, who missed most of the season with a wrist injury. Signed through the 2026 season, O’Connell will likely return to the Raiders as a backup or third-string quarterback.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-ocon.headline: Kenny Pickett completed 1-of-4 passes for three yards and an interception in Las Vegas’ Week 18 win over the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-ocon.analysis: Pickett appeared to be benched after throwing a first quarter interception on an intermediate pass attempt, but he did return at one point as the Raiders split snaps between Aidan O’Connell and Pickett. Pickett enters free agency without much on his side other than youth. Pickett played for four teams in four seasons of his rookie contract and is a candidate to be a backup in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-ocon.headline: Raiders coach Pete Carroll declined to say whether Kenny Pickett or Aidan O’Connell will start against the Chiefs in Week 18.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-ocon.analysis: Has anyone tried asking the Raiders to be normal? We’re just asking questions here. Carroll said both players would play. Neither player is worth rostering in superflex leagues in Week 18. O’Connell has probably performed like a better quarterback but spent all season buried on the depth chart for reasons that defy rational explanation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-ocon.headline: Raiders head coach Pete Carroll said Geno Smith (ankle) will not play Week 18 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-ocon.analysis: It appears as though Smith’s season is over. Earlier today, Vegas Nation’s Vincent Bonsignore reported that the Raiders will use “a combination of Kenny Pickett and Aidan O’Connell” this week. Neither player should be in starting lineups, in what sounds like some sort of game-day platoon. In his first season with the Raiders, Smith completed 302-of-448 passes for 3,025 yards, 19 touchdowns and 17 interceptions, while rushing 41 times for 109 yards. He is under contract through 2027, though he is owed no money that season. If the Raiders were to cut him this offseason, it would cost them $18.5 million in dead money while saving them $8 million.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-ocon.headline: Vegas Nation’s Vincent Bonsignore believes the Raiders will use “a combination of Kenny Pickett and Aidan O’Connell” in Week 18 against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-ocon.analysis: Bonsignore seems to imply both players will take reps in Week 18. Pickett has been the first player off the bench, so we assume he will get the start. Should the Raiders actually employ a two-quarterback game plan, neither player should be anywhere near a re-draft or DFS lineup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-ocon.headline: Raiders declared WR Jack Bech, RB Raheem Mostert, WR Phillip Dorsett, S Terrell Edmunds, RB Chris Collier, DT Brodric Martin and QB Aidan O’Connell inactive for Week 17 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/aidan-ocon.analysis: Bech injured his back on Friday. Although the Raiders’ (2-13) season is lost, a Week 17 absence could be consequential for Bech down the road. This was an opportunity for the underwhelming rookie to put a positive performance on film. He produced career highs in targets (six), receptions (six) and receiving yards (50) in Week 14. Hopefully, he can get healthy enough to play in Week 18 against the Chiefs.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) is inactive for Week 6 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Moore was considered legitimately questionable entering the weekend after logging only one practice. He will now miss a second straight game with the shoulder injury he suffered in Week 4, paving the way for Keon Coleman to again see significant snaps. While Moore is out, Josh Palmer, who was questionable with his own shoulder injury, is active. The Bills declared DT Ed Oliver, LB Mike Danna, and OG Ar’ma Reed-Adams inactive for Sunday’s game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) is questionable to play in Week 6 against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: The Athletic’s Joe Buscaglia notes that Moore resumed practicing today after sitting out on Wednesday and Thursday. He did the same thing last week before being labeled questionable and ultimately ruled out on game day. It looks like he’s a game-time decision again this week. If active, he can be started as a WR2, but re-injury remains a risk.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: It looks like the Bills could again be without their No. 1 wide receiver on game day. Josh Allen and Co. take on the Raiders this weekend, in what should be a fantasy-friendly game environment. Hopefully, Moore resumes practicing soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Moore aggravated a shoulder injury in Week 4 and only practiced with a non-contact jersey on Saturday of last week. After missing Week 5, Moore starts out as a non-practice participant in the Bills’ Wednesday walk-through. He will need at least a limited practice before fantasy managers can start considering him for Week 6 lineups.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: Bills WR DJ Moore (shoulder) is inactive for Week 5 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Moore’s absence leaves only Keon Coleman, Khalil Shakir, Greg Dortch, and Skyler Bell as healthy wide receivers on the active roster with Joshua Palmer also sidelined. Expect heavy snap rates for Coleman and Shakir alongside tight end Dalton Kincaid, with the possibility the team elevates their 12-personnel rates through the inclusion of Dawson Knox. Also inactive for the Bills are WR Joshua Palmer, OL Jude Bowry, OL Ar’maj Reed-Adams, DL Ed Oliver DL, Landon Jackson, and NCB Dee Alford.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: Bills WR DJ Moore (shoulder) is questionable for Week 5 against the Rams.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Moore failed to practice until Saturday after aggravating a shoulder injury in Week 4, returning to the field in a limited capacity while wearing a red non-contact jersey. That was apparently enough to keep the door open for an appearance on Monday Night Football against the Rams, although he certainly appears to be on the wrong side of the questionable tag. Fantasy managers would be wise to seek alternate options considering the timing of the game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: Bills WR DJ Moore (shoulder) practiced with a non-contact jersey Saturday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: This is the first time Moore has returned to the practice field after aggravating a shoulder injury in Week 4. Still no word on his game-day injury status, which will come later in the afternoon, but it a small step in the right direction for the veteran receiver. Fantasy managers likely want to continue the search for alternatives with the Bills playing on Monday Night Football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) did not practice on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: The Bills’ No. 1 wide receiver is on the wrong side of questionable for his team’s Monday Night Football game against the Rams. Moore sprained the AC joint in his left shoulder in Week 2. He aggravated it in Week 4 with a hard fall and was unable to continue playing. If active, Moore will be a risk-reward WR2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore (shoulder) was not spotted in the media-viewing portion of practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Joe Brady is quoted as saying that if Moore feels he’s healthy enough to play, he “owes it to the WR to let him be out there.” It’s not exactly a quote that inspires a lot of confidence in Moore’s availability for Monday night’s matchup with the Rams after he left Week 4’s game due to landing on the shoulder. We would regard Moore as on the doubtful side of questionable at this point, but there’s time to turn that around on Friday and Saturday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.headline: DJ Moore is doubtful to return to Week 4 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dj-moore/5.analysis: Moore landed on his left shoulder while trying to make the catch on a pass in the second quarter. It’s the same shoulder that he injured in the Week 2 win over the Lions. Obviously, the fact that it’s the same shoulder is not a great sign, as is Moore’s long injury history. We should get an update at halftime, but Keon Coleman figures to step into a larger role for the remainder of the game. Moore had just one catch for 11 yards before leaving with his injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nolan-smit.headline: Nolan Smith has been ruled out of Week 6 against the Panthers with a concussion.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nolan-smit.analysis: Smith was on a pass rush rep, coming off the edge, when he got hit hard under the chin on a chip block by Chuba Hubbard. There was no helmet-to-helmet contact, but Smith went down hard and was immediately evaluated for a concussion. He was later ruled out for the remainder of the game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nolan-smit.headline: Eagles EDGE Nolan Smith was arrested for speeding and reckless driving in Georgia.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nolan-smit.analysis: The Georgia Gazette noted Smith was booked on May 15th for speeding in excess of maximum limits and reckless driving. The 25-year-old was driving 137 miles per hour in a 70 mile-per-hour zone in his home state of Georgia, where he also attended the University of Georgia to play college football. It is still undetermined if the NFL or the Eagles have some form of punishment for Smith, but he is set to enter a pivotal year with the Eagles picking up his fifth-year option last month.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nolan-smit.headline: Eagles exercised the fifth-year option for LB Nolan Smith.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nolan-smit.analysis: The Eagles selected Smith with the 30th overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft. The fourth-year linebacker has totaled 10.5 sacks and 10 TFLs in his first three seasons with the team while racking up 91 tackles, and was instrumental in the team’s Super Bowl championship run, where he totaled four sacks in four postseason games. Smith is now under contract through the 2027 season and could be in line for an extension before his new deal is up if he’s able to string together a breakout campaign in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nolan-smit.headline: Eagles activated LB Nolan Smith ahead of Week 11’s game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nolan-smit.analysis: Smith suffered a triceps injury in Week 3’s win over the Rams and has been sidelined ever since. The third-year pro totaled 10 tackles and one forced fumble in the three games he appeared in this season, and totaled a career-high 6.5 tackles last season. He should immediately slot into his normal role on Monday night against the Packers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nolan-smit.headline: Eagles OLB Nolan Smith (triceps) is practicing in full for Week 10 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nolan-smit.analysis: The Eagles activated Smith’s 21-day practice window on Tuesday, and he appears to be on track to retake the field on Monday night. In late September, Smith re-injured the same triceps muscle he tore in Super Bowl LIX. Fortunately, he rehab plan has evidently gone according to plan, as a return “around” the Eagles’ Week 9 bye was the goal.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nolan-smit.headline: Eagles placed OLB Nolan Smith on injured reserve.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nolan-smit.analysis: Smith reportedly re-injured the triceps muscle that he tore during Super Bowl LIX. He underwent surgery to repair the torn tissue this offseason. The Eagles believe Smith will not require surgery and hope to have him back “around” their Week 9 bye. Players placed on injured reserve are eligible to return after missing four games. The Eagles also placed CB Jakorian Bennett and WR Darius Cooper on injured reserve with undisclosed injuries. Both players are likewise expected to avoid surgery and are expected to return around Week 9. The Eagles signed S Marcus Epps, TE Cameron Latu, and CB Parry Nickerson to the active roster, and LB Lance Dixon, DB Eli Ricks, and WR Quez Watkins to the practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nolan-smit.headline: Eagles EDGE Nolan Smith suffered a torn triceps in the team’s Super Bowl LIX victory.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nolan-smit.analysis: The second-year first-round pick out of Georgia evidently played through the injury in the second half. He went under the knife Wednesday and is expected to be ready for Week 1. More than likely, he will be good to go for training camp. 2024 was a nice leap for Smith after he made zero rookie starts. He played roughly 70 percent of the Eagles’ snaps and tallied 6.5 sacks. That does not include the four QB takedowns he logged during the postseason. Heading into his age-24 campaign, Smith could make another big leap.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nolan-smit.headline: Eagles signed No. 30 overall pick EDGE Nolan Smith to a four-year contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nolan-smit.analysis: Smith is one of several Georgia Bulldogs who will now suit up for the Eagles this season. Smith is an elite defender who played a key role on Georgia’s national championship-winning teams. He brings elite athleticism and a solid production profile to a defense that could use him all over the field, and will likely work his way into an every-down role.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nolan-smit.headline: Eagles selected Georgia EDGE Nolan Smith with the No. 30 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nolan-smit.analysis: A former number one overall rated recruit from the 2019 prep cycle according to 247Sports, the IMG Academy product has been a fixture on the vaunted Georgia defense since arriving on campus in 2019. An ace closer, Smith (6’22/238) only missed eight tackle attempts in his four years as a Bulldog and is almost impossible to beat to the sideline on outside runs. Despite being undersized by traditional standards, his bend, get off and ability to flatten after blowing away tackles with his blinding speed are rare, even in a loaded edge class. Smith’s 4.39s 40 is the second fastest time ever run by an edge defender while his blistering 1.47s 10-yard split is a 100th percentile score that portrays the limitless athletic traits Smith possesses. He was limited to just 188 snaps in 2022 but produced 19 pressures in that span while meaning a pristine 90.6 rush defense grade in 2021. His outrageous physical gifts and high-end production bode well for Smith’s transition to the next level as an omnipresent standup 3-4 linebacker who never comes off the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nolan-smit.headline: The Athletic’s Dane Brugler has Georgia senior EDGE Nolan Smith second in his 2023 NFL draft edge rankings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nolan-smit.analysis: The top spot belongs to Will Anderson who is one of the best pass rushers we have seen in years. The second spot was a question but Brugler believes it to be Smith (6'3/235). He cites his twitchy athleticism as his best trait, something he uses to get to the quarterback and to stop the run. If he can improve his play strength, that will go a long way in securing a spot at the top of his edge rankings come April.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught 5-of-7 targets for 44 yards in Jacksonville’s Week 6 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: The Jaguars did have a tight end touchdown, but unfortunately for fantasy managers it went to Nate Boerkircher on a ridiculous one-handed stab on a pop pass at the goal line. Strange has now gone for 23 targets in three games and appears to be crowding out Brian Thomas Jr. He’s a reasonable low-end TE1, albeit one on bye next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught 7-of-8 targets for 68 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 5 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: After a quiet three games to start the year, Strange has heated up over the past two weeks. He led the team with seven catches last week and did so again today in London. Strange had seven catches in his first three games combined. He can’t be expected to pace the Jags in receiving, but Strange is back on the TE1/2 border for his Week 6 date with Houston.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught 7-of-8 targets for 95 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 4 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Strange was Trevor Lawrence’s primary target against a Bengals defense that has struggled against tight ends. Many of his targets were middle-of-the-field intermediate passes as he tallied 95 total receiving yards on the day. The Jaguars offense has a variety of pass-catchers that can find success based on defensive matchup. The game environment aligned perfectly for Strange, who rarely came off the field with 53 total snaps. The Eagles are a tougher matchup for tight ends, but Strange is a good streamer option in the high-end TE2 territory for a Week 5 matchup in London.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught 3-of-5 targets for 32 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers dominated looks from Trevor Lawrence on a low-volume day for the Jacksonville offense. Strange played his usual role as a check down option for Lawrence, rumbling for yards after the catch on two of his three grabs. Strange, with seven catches on the year, could be a streaming play in Week 4 against the Bengals if the game turns into a shootout.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught both of his targets for 17 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 2 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Strange ran a pass route on 30 of the team’s 36 drop backs but was invisible for most of the game. For now Strange can be treated as a desperation streamer in 12-team formats ahead of the Jags’ Week 3 matchup against the Patriots. He should remain on waiver wires in 10-team leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Brenton Strange caught 2-of-3 targets for 23 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 1 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Strange operated as the Jaguars’ primary receiving tight end, seeing three targets on the day. In a loaded passing attack, he still found opportunity in what was a very fantasy-friendly offense. Strange caught a 14-yard touchdown in the second quarter and was mostly quiet in a second half where the Jaguars were already up by four scores. The Jaguars wide receivers will take much of Lawrence’s targets but Strange has a role over the middle of the field; he profiles as TE2 for Week 2 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Jaguars signed Brenton Strange to a three-year contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Per NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo, the deal is worth “up to” $48 million. A chunk of that figure is presumably based on incentives. The contract includes $25 million guaranteed. Strange posted a minor breakout in 2024 with 411 yards on 40 grabs. He upped the ante in 2025 to 46 catches for 540 yards despite missing five games. Strange was heading into the final year of his rookie deal before this extension and the team spent multiple draft picks on tight ends, making it look like they were considering letting him walk next offseason. Instead, Nate Boerkircher and Tanner Koziol will primarily see the field for heavy offensive looks, something the team talked about after the draft. Strange will sit on the TE1/2 border in early fantasy drafts.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes Brenton Strange will be a “key piece of everything the Jaguars do on offense” in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Shipley said the Jaguars drafting Texas A&M TE Nate Boerkircher and Houston TE Tanner Koziol in the 2026 draft does not mean the Jaguars coaching staff has a smaller role planned for Strange, who last season 46 catches, 540 yards, and three touchdowns as the team’s TE1. Shipley expected Strange’s pass game involvement to grow as the Jaguars deploy more tight end-heavy offensive sets. The Jaguars, Shipley said, are “clearly hoping that injecting the [tight end] room with talent should allow Strange to produce at an even higher level than before.” Last season Strange was targeted on 21 percent of his routes, which ranked 25th out of 58 qualifying tight ends. Though he’ll likely be the team’s third or fourth option in the passing game, Strange should be a viable fantasy option in 12 and 14-team leagues this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: ESPN’s Michael DiRocco reports the Jaguars have had preliminary discussions about extensions for WR Parker Washington, TE Brenton Strange, and EDGE Travon Walker.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: It was pointed out by John Shipley a few days ago that Wan’Dale Robinson’s free agent contract might be a starting point for the Washington extension. Walker is entering his final season under his rookie contract’s fifth-year option. Strange and Washington are both on the final year of their rookie contracts. The Jaguars have been uncharacteristically (and probably smartly, given their success last year) quiet in free agency, so perhaps they’re just focusing on locking up their core.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes the Jaguars could target a tight end in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/brenton-st.analysis: Shipley refers to Jaguars starting TE Brenton Strange as “maybe the most underrated tight end in the entire NFL” and says the team knows “just how important he is to everything they do.” Sounds like Strange’s role is safe. Shipley believes TE Quintin Morris could have true TE2 potential, but Morris caught just 6-of-7 targets for 55 yards and one touchdown after signing with the Jaguars in free agency last year. His position on the depth chart sounds less secure. Strange can be viewed as a low-end TE1 candidate at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: Travis Hunter caught 4-of-4 targets for 59 yards and a touchdown in Jacksonville’s Week 6 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: In London, where Travis Hunter’s best games live, Hunter both caught a touchdown and picked off C.J. Stroud (his first of the season), becoming the first player to do both in the same game since Brian Dawkins in 2002. Hunter did all this on just nine offensive snaps. The skill is there to do this on offense, but the Jaguars have really been defense-first with his snaps this year. Depending on the post-bye buzz, Hunter could be a reasonable pick-up in fantasy leagues ahead of Week 8’s games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said the Jaguars are “looking at continuing to find different ways” to get Travis Hunter involved.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: Coen talked about getting Hunter involved more on both sides of the ball, so it’s unclear how much of an uptick in offensive snaps we can expect in Week 3. Hunter has a 58 percent snap share on defense and a pitiful nine percent snap share on offense through two games. Even if he isn’t likely to hit the fantasy radar anytime soon, it would be shocking for the No. 2 overall pick to play this infrequently every week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: Travis Hunter caught his lone target for eight yards in the Jaguars’ Week 1 win over the Browns, adding one carry for three yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: Hunter saw just four offensive snaps to 39 defensive snaps against the Browns. With a good wide receiver room, Hunter was not playing offense as much and his utilization overlapped with Jakobi Meyers. It’s unlikely the 23-year-old achieves much fantasy relevancy without an injury to Meyers moving forward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley reports that Travis Hunter “is expected to be the Jaguars’ No. 1 cornerback in Week 1 and beyond.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: Shipley leaves the light on for offensive contributions, entertaining the idea that Hunter can chip in “a few hundred yards and a few touchdowns” this season as well. That said, the early indications for Hunter’s FLEX viability in managed leagues are pretty bleak. Stash him if you wish, but understand that starting him in Week 1 against the Browns could result in zero points.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley reports that Jaguars CB/WR Travis Hunter has taken reps “almost exclusively at cornerback” for the last two weeks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: Shipley estimates that Hunter has logged fewer than 10 reps at wide receiver in team drills during that span. Shipley said, “it seems like” the Jaguars are treating Hunter like their CB1. He also still thinks “there will be games where he logs 50 percent of the offensive snaps,” though. The biggest takeaway is that Hunter has an extremely wide range of potential outcomes, and he cannot be counted on to be FLEX-viable at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: ESPN’s Mike DiRocco reports that Jaguars WR Brian Thomas Jr. and CB/WR Travis Hunter “have shared reps” in 11 personnel packages.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: To be clear, Thomas is the starting X-receiver and Hunter is rotating in behind him. Hunter has also been taking more defensive snaps lately, so if he is going to maintain an offensive role, a simplified downfield role makes sense. Regarding Thomas, DiRocco adds that he “was arguably the best player on the field” during organized team activities, has had a “great” training camp and is “showing some of the toughness and ball security that seemed to be missing last season.” With all of that in mind, losing snaps in three-wide receiver sets is a bit surprising. Thomas is extremely talented, but obvious questions remain as to his usage in the upcoming season. A boom-bust WR3 season could be on the way.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: Travis Hunter took zero 11-on-11 reps on offense on Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: It was suggested by Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley that the Jaguars could be “tipping their hand” here, as he writes “it is clear the Jaguars believe they need to devote more practice time with Hunter before Week 1 at cornerback, which could be the biggest signal yet that the majority of his snaps against the Cleveland Browns on Sept. 13 will be at cornerback.” Hunter will likely still be involved in the offense — he has worked with the offense every day before this — but it is notable that there was a shift here. Hunter will likely be just a dart throw WR5/WR6 in most standard leagues this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe believes Brian Thomas Jr. will play the X receiver role in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: That would mean Thomas is set to play on the outside at the line of scrimmage. Parker Washington will presumably play in the slot with Jakobi Meyers and Travis Hunter fighting for flanker duties. As Wolfe notes, Liam Coen learned last year that going over the middle of the field and taking hits isn’t BTJ’s thing. Instead, he will likely be tasked with winning deep and beating man coverage. Wolfe noted Liam Coen’s roots in the Rams’ offense and compared BTJ’s role to that of Brandin Cooks and Sammy Watkins when they played in LA. Cooks topped 1,200 receiving yards in his first season with the Rams but fell below 600 in his second and final season with the team. Watkins, meanwhile, played just one season in LA and was also held under 600 yards. All signs point to Washington being the team’s No. 1 receiver this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said, “He will do it,” when asked if Travis Hunter would play offense and defense in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: Talking with Peter Schrager on his podcast, Coen almost laughed at the idea that Hunter might play exclusively on one side of the ball this year. Early offseason reports suggested Hunter might play primarily on defense after suffering a season-ending injury during his rookie season. Every subsequent report from local beats and all the quotes from the coaching staff have made it clear that Hunter remains a two-way player. Coen did note that they are still determining how much he will play on both sides of the ball, but it sounds like a part-time role on offense is the floor. Given the barrage of information suggesting Hunter will play on offense, a WR57 price tag for last year’s No. 2 overall continues to look absurdly cheap.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.headline: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports Jaguars WR/CB Travis Hunter (knee) will be a “full go” for training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/travis-hun.analysis: Hunter is working his way back from a 2025 knee injury and is expected to be a full go for the beginning of training camp, according to Wolfe. The 23-year-old is still going to play both sides of the ball, though Wolfe stated Hunter can be “unleashed” as a starter on defense and “the goal is to eventually have him play nearly all the snaps on defense in a particular game.” The Jaguars seem to like Hunter much better as a cornerback but he will still play offense with his wide receiver snaps fluctuating depending on the game. Hunter is attending meetings for both sides of the ball and will presumably practice both sides come training camp. He is expected to be healthy and ready to go by the time Jags veterans report to training camp in late July.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 4-of-11 targets for 64 yards in Jacksonville’s Week 6 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: A lot of these incompletions were balls Washington got a hand on but couldn’t quite reel in as was breaking to the sideline. Washington displayed his speed and shiftiness on a 27-yard catch-and-run in the second quarter where he cut through both Texans linebackers for a big gain. He is a fantasy WR2 as the Jaguars enter their bye week. Washington is #onpace for a near-1,200 yard season with 14 touchdowns even after this dud.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 6-of-9 targets for 124 yards and two touchdowns in the Jaguars’ Week 5 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Coming off a pair of quiet weeks, Washington paid off for fantasy managers early with a 51-yard score in the first quarter. It was somehow nowhere close to his best play of the day. Washington scored his second touchdown on a falling, one-handed grab in the end zone from 27 yards out near the end of the game. The grab was reminiscent of Odell Beckham’s famous touchdown catch. Washington remains the most talented and most involved receiver on the Jags. He will be a high-end WR2 versus the Texans next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 1-of-3 targets for 7 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 4 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Washington also added three yards with one carry on the ground. After a hot start to the season, Washington was relatively quiet against the Bengals. The Jaguars receivers combined for just 11 of Trevor Lawrence’s 23 targets and Washington saw three of those. His first reception came in the fourth quarter on a 40-yard catch-and-run that would have sealed the game, but was called back after replay showed he stepped out of bounds after seven yards. Game script and the Bengals’ tight end weaknesses played a factor in this game, with Brenton Strange the primary target on the day. Washington should still be the Jaguars’ No. 1 receiver and is a fantasy WR2 for Week 5 against the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: It’s Washington’s second touchdown in the Jags’ first three games of the season. Washington caught his touchdown against the Patriots after having an acrobatic touchdown grab called back on a penalty. Having established himself as the team’s clear-cut WR1 — well ahead of Brian Thomas, who had one target in Week 3 — Washington will have a rock solid weekly floor with ceiling to spare in shootout game scripts. Washington should remain in all lineups next week against a middling Bengals defense, in what could be a high-scoring affair between two potent offenses.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 8-of-12 targets for 98 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 2 loss against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Trevor Lawrence, as always, targeted Washington heavily, as no other Jacksonville pass catcher saw more than eight targets on the day. Washington came within half a yard of a touchdown in the first half after scoring in Week 1 against the Browns. Clearly the team’s No. 1 wideout, Washington should have a rock-solid weekly floor with upside to spare, especially when the Jaguars have to operate a more pass-heavy offense. Washington will be a top-15 play next week against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington caught 5-of-6 targets for 83 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 1 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Washington saw elite usage in the first half, making the first Jacksonville catch of the game and ending the Jaguars’ first drive with a diving 30-yard touchdown reception. He followed it up with a one-handed sideline catch on the second drive and tallied five receptions in the first half. His usage was that of a legitimate No. 1 wide receiver for the Jaguars’ fantasy-friendly offense. The game was out of hand in the second half, leading to no more receptions the rest of the day, but fantasy managers will be happy with Washington’s utilization and production as he adds to his elite box scores from the end of last season. Washington is a fantasy WR2 heading into Week 2 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports the Jaguars are “unlikely” to extend Parker Washington before Week 1.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Per Wolfe, the Jags explored a deal similar to that of Michael Wilson, who just landed a three-year, $75 million extension. The two sides couldn’t agree to terms, and Washington will now start his contract year. It’s a highly risky move for a largely unheralded player who caught lightning in a bottle at the end of last year. Washington caught 29 passes for 507 yards and three touchdowns in his final five games, including one postseason appearance. If he repeats anything close to those numbers over a full season this year, Washington will make far more than Wilson as a free agent next offseason.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Jaguars HC Liam Coen said Parker Washington will “absolutely” be the team’s punt returner to start the season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Coen also noted that Washington is “the guy right now,” suggesting that his role as the returner could change at some point in the year. Washington returned 25 punts for the Jaguars last season and racked up 341 return yards and two touchdowns on those returns. Coen said the Jaguars will hope to get Travis Hunter involved as the punt returner at some point, but Washington will start the season in the role. Washington profiles as a solid WR2 to start the fantasy season after going for 58-847-5 last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Parker Washington said his contract talks with the Jaguars “are continuing.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Jags GM James Gladstone said last week that the team was open to an in-season extension with Washington, who is set to hit free agency next offseason. Both sides want to get a deal done, but they are clearly still at odds over the details of the contract. Even if it takes longer than expected, it does look like Washington will sign an extension before he gets to test the waters of free agency. Coming off an outstanding training camp, Washington should be treated as a fantasy WR2 for the Jags’ Week 1 date with the Browns.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.headline: Jaguars general manager James Gladstone said the team would be open to negotiating an extension with WR Parker Washington in-season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/parker-was.analysis: Washington, 24, is entering a contract year, coming off the best season of his career. He is reportedly expected to be the team’s No. 1 wide receiver. If Washington plays up to that standard, he will unquestionably be able to raise his asking price. Signing him to a deal right now could save the team money in the long term, but the front office evidently wants to see how he fares early in the year. Although this route could be costly, having a true No. 1 wide receiver affirm his financial value with top-tier play is a good problem to have.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) is questionable to return to Week 6 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Phillips came into this game questionable with a hamstring injury but was able to suit up. Unfortunately, he got hurt early in the first quarter and is unlikely to return. Considering he had the bye week to heal and is not 100 percent, it seems likely that the EDGE rusher will miss some time with the injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Taylor Moton (blood clots) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Moton is tentatively on track to make his return from injured reserve this week. Meanwhile, RT Monroe Freeling (knee) sat out on Wednesday. Panthers DT Tershawn Wharton (neck) is practicing in full, while EDGE Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) was limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said he is “hopeful” Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) will be able to play in Week 6 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Phillips went down with a hamstring injury late in Sunday’s game against the Lions and didn’t return to the field. For a player with Phillips’ injury history, there were immediate concerns regarding the severity of the injury, but with a Week 5 bye on tap, the hope is Phillips won’t miss much time, if any. Phillips has totaled two sacks in his first four games of the season. In addition to Phillips, the team is also hopeful that OT Monroe Freeling (knee) will be able to return in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Devin Lloyd (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Lloyd was one of the Panthers’ premier free agent additions this offseason, and he’s already proven to be worth the investment. Lloyd terrorized the Falcons in Week 2 with a sack and two interceptions, one of which was a pick-six. Fellow free agent acquisition Jaelan Phillips was also absent from practice today. He is dealing with a back injury. Though the Browns aren’t a particularly good offense right now, it would still be a massive boon for them if Lloyd and Phillips are out for Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Panthers agreed to terms with EDGE Jaelan Phillips, formerly of the Eagles, on a four-year, $120 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the deal includes an eye-popping $80 million guaranteed. The Eagles were reportedly working to retain the 27-year-old (in May) pass rusher, but got outbid by the typically free-spending Panthers. A former Dolphin who flourished during his eight-game trade cameo for the Eagles last season, Phillips finally stayed healthy last year after an injury marred 2023-24 run. That’s a concern going forward, but Phillips is a pass-rushing difference maker when on the field.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports “Philly isn’t done trying” to re-sign Jaelan Phillips before the legal tampering period begins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: It sounds like the Eagles are making a push to re-sign Phillips before the legal tampering period begins on Monday. Phillips, whom the Eagles acquired at last year’s trade deadline, totaled 28 tackles, two sacks, and one fumble recovery in his eight games with the team last season, and is believed to have a strong market should he become available. While the soon-to-be 27-year-old dealt with two serious injuries in 2023 and 2024, he managed to play in all 17 regular season games in 2025 and is a clear difference maker for any defense he’s on.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports Odafe Oweh, Jaelan Phillips, Trey Hendrickson and Boye Mafe are on Dallas’ “radar” in the coming days.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: The Cowboys lost out on the Maxx Crosby trade sweepstakes and will have to pivot — they reportedly had some interest in Hendrickson at the deadline. Oweh probably makes more sense as a younger upside swing, and this is the third of four NFC East teams in on Jaelan Phillips that we’ve heard about.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: ESPN’s Tim McManus believes the “expectation” is the Eagles will make a push to re-sign EDGE Jaelan Phillips.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Phillips came over in a midseason trade from Miami and had a great half-year in Philadelphia, posting a 77.1 PFF defensive grade in nine games. The Eagles stand to net a high compensatory pick if Phillips leaves, but it seems like they’d rather just keep the player.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Eagles DT Jalen Carter (hip) is not on Philadelphia’s final Wild Card injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Carter, Nakobe Dean (hamstring), Marcus Epps (concussion), and Jaelan Phillips (ankle) all were taken off the final injury report and will play against the 49ers. EDGE Azeez Ojulari (hamstring/IR) is questionable, but practiced in full today and looks likely to join them. The Eagles will summon all the defensive firepower they have against the 49ers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.headline: Eagles DT Jalen Carter (hip) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaelan-phi.analysis: Eagles LB Nakobe Dean (hamstring), S Marcus Epps (concussion), OLB Azeez Ojulari (hamstring) and OLB Jaelan Phillips (ankle) are all practicing fully. Carter’s continued participation is a good sign. Hopefully, he upgrades to full participation on Friday. The Eagles face the 49ers on Sunday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers caught 5-of-10 targets for 83 yards in Jacksonville’s Week 6 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: It’s his highest target total of the season and the first time Meyers has managed 10 targets since Week 14 of the 2025 season. No touchdown here, but Meyers is a fine real-life third receiver who has mostly been left to the FLEX life in Jacksonville. He enters the bye as someone who can be dropped in shallow leagues in a roster crunch, but also someone solidly in the top 50 wideouts in the league on a good offense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers caught 2-of-3 targets for 37 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 5 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers has been held to two and three catches over his past two games. It’s probably not a coincidence that Brenton Strange leads the team with 14 catches during Meyers’ two-game slump. Meyers is still operating as the Jags’ WR2, but his role will come down to matchup nuances on a week-to-week basis. He is sliding back into the WR5 fantasy ranks ahead of his Week 6 matchup with the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers caught 3-of-4 targets for 33 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 4 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers continues to see the most snaps among all Jaguars wide receivers as Liam Coen utilizes him as both an outside target and willing blocker. He was second in targets against the Bengals as Trevor Lawrence threw just 23 passes on the day. Meyers now seems to be ahead of Brian Thomas Jr. on the wide receiver pecking order and is WR3 fantasy play for a London game against the Eagles in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) is not on Jacksonville’s final Week 4 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: He should be trusted as a low-end WR3/FLEX play against the Bengals. Meyers has cleared the injury report with this thumb listing three times in three weeks, though he was questionable in Week 2. It clearly isn’t bothering him enough to impact his play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: No real surprises here; Meyers has played through this thumb listing in two consecutive weeks and will likely be removed from the injury report on Friday.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers has been playing through the thumb issue all year and that won’t change in Week 4. With Brian Thomas Jr.'s role disappearing, Meyers has quietly emerged as the No. 2 receiver on one of the league’s best offenses. He remains a solid FLEX play for his Week 4 date with the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers caught 7-of-8 targets for 64 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers made the most of his opportunities in a revenge game against his former team. After totaling three catches for 68 yards in his first two games of the season, Meyers led the Jaguars in targets and grabs against New England, catching one of Trevor Lawrence’s three touchdown throws. Meyers entered the game with a meager six percent target share and a 11 percent air yards share. He could have some flex viability in Week 4 against a middling Bengals secondary that gave up a big day to Steelers pass catchers in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) is active for Week 3 against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers was able to practice late in the week and will suit up as the team’s WR3 against a tough New England coverage unit. It’s a revenge game for Meyers, who through Week 2 has a 6 percent target share and a 12 percent air yards share while running a route on 76 percent of the Jaguars’ drop backs. Jaguars declared WR CJ Williams, S Jalen Huskey, LB Jack Kiser, OL Daniel Faalele, DE Wesley Williams, and DT Albert Regis inactive against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) isn’t on Jacksonville’s final injury report for Week 3.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: He will play against the Patriots. Meyers got in his first full practice since suffering the thumb injury and should be a reasonable FLEX play against New England.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.headline: Jakobi Meyers (thumb) remained limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jakobi-mey.analysis: Meyers played through this thumb listing last week and was limited in back-to-back sessions to start the week; he should be considered likely to play against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez rushed 11 times for 55 yards in Jacksonville’s Week 6 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: He failed to catch his only target. Rodriguez was churning out success rate on the regular in the first half. The Jaguars curiously went away from him in the second half, as he played just 21-of-70 snaps and had only one carry after halftime. He’s not a must-hold through the bye week, but this game is the proof-of-concept that he can be an effective weapon for the Jaguars if they want to use him as a between-the-tackles pounder.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez rushed two times for five yards in the Jaguars’ Week 5 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez was all but phased out of the rotation in this game. His most notable touch was a goal line carry which he was stuffed on and then fumbled the ball away. He was called down on the field. Even though replay clearly showed him losing the ball, there was no clear recovery and the refs didn’t bother overturning the non-fumble. Rodriguez may still be the occasional touchdown vulture, but his role has been reduced to the point where fantasy managers can safely cut ties with him on the next run of waivers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez rushed six times for 35 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 4 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez entered the game frequently when the Jaguars entered Bengals territory. He has a hold on short-yardage opportunities while also getting some red zone looks, but Bhayshul Tuten is the clear lead back. Rodriguez was out-snapped 36-to-15 but salvaged his fantasy day with a 25-yard rushing touchdown in the fourth quarter. He is a handcuff for fantasy purposes heading into Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez had eight rushes for 37 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez remained the second option in the Jaguars backfield behind Bhayshul Tuten, but stole a short score from Tuten in the blowout victory. Through three games Rodriguez has been a between the tackles option who has next to no involvement in the passing game. He would only be fantasy viable if Tuten misses time this season. For now C-Rod is a decent stash as a contingency option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Jaguars HC Liam Coen said he “fully anticipates” more snaps for LeQuin Allen on third down.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Allen played on just one offensive snap in last week’s win over the Browns, but led the Jaguars in third-down snaps (146) last season. Despite all the snaps he saw on third down as a rookie, Allen never materialized into a viable fantasy option. Whether or not that changes this season is to be determined, but any additional snaps he receives on third down would come at the expense of Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez, after Rodriguez led the way with five third-down snaps last week. While Allen seeing additional work in these situations could be problematic for fantasy managers, they shouldn’t let that deter them from starting Tuten in Week 2 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Chris Rodriguez Jr. rushed six times for 23 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 1 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Rodriguez was the Jaguars’ second running back in the game, but equaled Bhayshul Tuten’s touches on the first drive. He was used both in the red zone and short-yardage situations early on; Rodriguez tied for the lead in backfield snaps in the first half. The game was out of reach in the second half, with Ameer Abdullah taking on garbage time carries and Rodriguez finishing the game second in backfield snaps. Fantasy managers will like the high-leverage utilization but a lack of receiving upside caps Rodriguez’ ceiling. He is firmly in the RB4 range for Week 2 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said RB LeQuint Allen (hip) is a game-time decision for Week 1 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: As expected, Allen did not practice Wednesday. It’s not that fantasy managers were eager to start Allen this week, but his absence would open up more routes and potential targets for Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez, who are listed as co-starters on Jacksonville’s Week 1 depth chart. Both C-Rod and Tuten would be slightly better options if Allen is sidelined this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes neither Bhayshul Tuten nor Chris Rodriguez will emerge as the lead back in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Shipley hedges a bit by noting that there’s a chance that one back simply carries the momentum early in the season forward and never lets up, but ultimately falls on the idea that neither back is likely to hit 1,000 rushing yards in 2026. “I think there is a more likely chance we see both running backs hit 750+ yards than one of them hit 1,000,” Shipley writes. Such a split would probably lean towards Rodriguez at the goal line, making him slightly more fantasy-valuable on a weekly basis barring big plays from Tuten. If this prediction comes true, both backs might have trouble cracking the weekly RB2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said he would be “pleasantly surprised” if LeQuint Allen Jr. (soft tissue) played in Week 1 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Coen talked up Ameer Abdullah as a potential replacement for Allen’s duties in pass protection. He also singled out Chris Rodriguez’s abilities in pass pro. Pass protection duties aren’t a direct source of fantasy value, but it usually means that player will be on the field for the two-minute drill, which can generate plenty of receptions for running backs. Bhayshul Tuten not getting those reps would be a notable ding to his fantasy outlook. Allen himself isn’t on the fantasy radar, healthy or not.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.headline: Jaguars RB LeQuint Allen (soft tissue) will miss the rest of training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/chris-rodr.analysis: Allen suffered a soft tissue injury during Monday’s practice and the Jaguars announced Tuesday morning that he’ll miss the rest of training camp. It’s unclear if he’ll be ready for the start of the regular season. While Allen doesn’t have standalone fantasy value, he seemed destined for a legitimate role as the primary receiving back in this offense. If Allen misses time in the regular season, it would boost receiving opportunities for Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-steele/.headline: Carson Steele left Week 6 against the Panthers with a shoulder injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-steele/.analysis: Steele caught a screen pass in the flats and lowered his head to try and run over the defender. He came up holding his shoulder and had to have the shoulder immobilized as he walked into the locker room with his pads off. It had the look of a dislocation, which would mean Dameon Pierce and Jaydon Blue are the only two healthy running backs for the Eagles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-steele/.headline: Eagles ruled out RB Saquon Barkley (hamstring) for Week 6 against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-steele/.analysis: It was pretty clear that this was where things were headed when Barkley was unable to practice on Wednesday and Thursday. We do not yet know Barkley’s official Friday practice participation level, but he was not seen practicing during the portion of practice open to the media. Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele and practice squad player Jaydon Blue will likely split touches this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-steele/.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-steele/.analysis: Barkley is firmly on the wrong side of questionable for his team’s Week 6 game against the Panthers, potentially leaving Dameon Pierce, Carson Steele and practice squad player Jaydon Blue to split touches. Hopefully, reports clarify whether Pierce would handle a sizable workload as the de facto starter.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-steele/.headline: Will Shipley (foot) is questionable to return in Week 5 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-steele/.analysis: Shipley got stuffed on a carry in the second quarter and was checked out by trainers after the play. He went to the locker room after a brief trip to the blue medical tent. Dameon Pierce will be the next man up if Shipley’s day is over. Carson Steele is the only other back on the roster.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-steele/.headline: Eagles released RB Carson Steele.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-steele/.analysis: The news was first reported by Ryan Fowler of NBC Sports Philadelphia. Steele signed a futures deal with the Eagles in January after spending most of last season on the Chiefs practice squad. He was facing an uphill battle to make the team with Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley backing up Saquon Barkley in the Eagles backfield. Steele will head to the open market in search of his next organization.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-steele/.headline: Eagles signed FB Carson Steele to a reserve/futures contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-steele/.analysis: Steele hung on the Chiefs practice squad for most of last season and will now get a chance to stick in Philadelphia. With Will Shipley and Tank Bigsby under contract, it’s hard to see Steele making any sort of fantasy noise without injuries ahead of him.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-steele/.headline: Chiefs signed RB Clyde Edwards-Helaire to their practice squad.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-steele/.analysis: It’s been done. He’ll be joined by QB Chris Oladokun, FB Carson Steele, WR Hal Presley, OT Chu Godrick, OL C.J. Hanson, DT Coziah Izzard, DT Brodric Martin, CB Melvin Smith Jr, CB Kevin Knowles and FS Mike Edwards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-steele/.headline: Chiefs waived RB Carson Steele.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-steele/.analysis: We’ll always have Week 3 of 2024 — Steele fits as a hybrid RB/FB and Kansas City’s depth chart was weak enough last year that Steele rumbled for 72 yards on 17 carries against the Falcons. He lost two fumbles in his first four appearances and was banished to spot duty after Week 6. Steele had a 47.8 PFF grade in 41 preseason snaps but could resurface elsewhere if he’s not asked on to the Kansas City practice squad.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-steele/.headline: Carson Steele was held without a touch in the Chiefs’ Super Bowl LIX loss to the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-steele/.analysis: An UDFA out of UCLA, Steele ended up a fullback who wasn’t, primarily playing traditional running back. Limited to 63 uninspiring touches despite Isiah Pacheco’s nine-game absence with a broken leg, Steele seemed to lose the coaching staff’s trust on offense after losing two fumbles across his first four appearances. Although he remains eight months shy of his 23rd birthday, Steele did not demonstrate enough rookie upside to guarantee his 53-man roster spot for 2025.

https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-steele/.headline: Carson Steele rushed eight time for 25 yards and caught 2-of-2 targets for two yards in the Chiefs’ Week 18 loss to the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/carson-steele/.analysis: Steele was unable to make magic happen in this one despite leading the Chiefs in touches. Steele has proven himself as a capable ball carrier with Patrick Mahomes under center but playing well in an offense led by Carson Wentz is a far different ask. Steele will not be fantasy-relevant following the Chiefs’ first-round bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten rushed 12 times for 39 yards in Jacksonville’s Week 6 loss to the Texans, adding four catches for 48 yards and two touchdowns on his only four targets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: The Jaguars looked like they were in control with their run game early in this one, but Tuten sputtered out in the second half, where he managed just six carries for 18 yards with the Jaguars curiously going away from Chris Rodriguez Jr. Tuten played 40-of-72 snaps with Rodriguez having a big day on the ground. It feels good that his “down” games are like this, and he also had a rushing touchdown pulled off the board after what appeared to be a phantom holding flag was thrown. Tuten enters the Week 7 bye as an RB2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten rushed 22 times for 72 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 5 win over the Eagles, adding two catches for 24 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: The Jags’ offense struggled to execute at a basic level in this game, and Tuten may have been hurt the most by errors. Their first goal line sequence of the day started with a Chris Rodriguez near-fumble. After two incomplete passes, Liam Coen dialed up a jet sweep for Tuten that was blown up for a loss of six yards. The Jags’ next goal line sequence featured a pair of delay of game penalties followed by an incomplete pass on fourth down. Tuten got the full workhorse treatment in this game, ceding just two carries and one catch to his backups. He unfortunately could not make much of the touches. Tuten will be a high-end RB2 if this role persists into his Week 6 matchup versus the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten rushed 17 times for 73 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 4 win over the Bengals, adding two receptions for 18 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten continued to operate as the Jaguars’ lead back, ripping off a 15-yard carry to open the game. He found success running to the outside edges of the Bengals defense, tallying 91 total yards on the day. However, fantasy managers will be frustrated with the results as Tuten had touchdowns of 44 yards and three yards get called back due to holding penalties while Chris Rodriguez scored late in the game. The good news is Tuten out-snapped Rodriguez 36-to-15 on the day. He is still the lead back, though he cedes short-yardage and clear passing-down opportunities to Rodriguez and LeQuint Allen. Tuten gets enough opportunities to be squarely in the fantasy RB2 range on a weekly basis, he is a top-20 play for Week 5 against the Eagles in London.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Chris Rodriguez had eight rushes for 37 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Rodriguez remained the second option in the Jaguars backfield behind Bhayshul Tuten, but stole a short score from Tuten in the blowout victory. Through three games Rodriguez has been a between the tackles option who has next to no involvement in the passing game. He would only be fantasy viable if Tuten misses time this season. For now C-Rod is a decent stash as a contingency option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten had 15 rushes for 73 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots, adding two catches for 17 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten has taken control of the Jaguars backfield over the past couple weeks. Against the Patriots he out-carried Chris Rodriguez 15 to eight, with much of Rodriguez’s opportunity coming after the game had been decided. Tuten split pass-catching duties with LeQuint Allen, who also had two grabs on the day. Tuten probably won’t be a 20-touch back most weeks, but he should be a solid RB2 option going forward, including in Week 4 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten had 13 rushes for 65 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 2 loss against the Broncos, adding two catches for -3 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten more than doubled the workload of Chris Rodriguez, who had six rushes for 13 yards and did not record a reception. Tuten looked like the far more explosive backfield option for the Jags. He nearly broke a couple big runs and had one long carry called back on a penalty. Last week Tuten had 88 total yards against the Browns. The second-year back is looking more reliable as a fantasy option in what was regarded as a shaky situation ahead of the season. He should be seen as a top-24 play in Week 3 against the Patriots.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Jaguars HC Liam Coen said he “fully anticipates” more snaps for LeQuin Allen on third down.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Allen played on just one offensive snap in last week’s win over the Browns, but led the Jaguars in third-down snaps (146) last season. Despite all the snaps he saw on third down as a rookie, Allen never materialized into a viable fantasy option. Whether or not that changes this season is to be determined, but any additional snaps he receives on third down would come at the expense of Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez, after Rodriguez led the way with five third-down snaps last week. While Allen seeing additional work in these situations could be problematic for fantasy managers, they shouldn’t let that deter them from starting Tuten in Week 2 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Bhayshul Tuten rushed 15 times for 66 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 1 win over the Browns, adding one reception for 22 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Tuten started the game for the Jaguars, getting the first two carries of the game. His utilization was mixed, tying Chris Rodriguez for snaps in the first half. Tuten was rotated out for early red zone and short-yardage snaps, though he saw some of those opportunities later in the game. He held up well in pass-protection and took a screen pass 22 yards for his first reception. With the game out of hand in the second half, Tuten ultimately saw the highest snaps out of the backfield, tallying 28 on the day. He showed good burst and the ability to fight through contact, but Rodriguez will continue to be a thorn in his side for utilization. Tuten profiles as a high-end RB3 for Week 2 against the Broncos.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said RB LeQuint Allen (hip) is a game-time decision for Week 1 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: As expected, Allen did not practice Wednesday. It’s not that fantasy managers were eager to start Allen this week, but his absence would open up more routes and potential targets for Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez, who are listed as co-starters on Jacksonville’s Week 1 depth chart. Both C-Rod and Tuten would be slightly better options if Allen is sidelined this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes neither Bhayshul Tuten nor Chris Rodriguez will emerge as the lead back in 2026.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/bhayshul-t.analysis: Shipley hedges a bit by noting that there’s a chance that one back simply carries the momentum early in the season forward and never lets up, but ultimately falls on the idea that neither back is likely to hit 1,000 rushing yards in 2026. “I think there is a more likely chance we see both running backs hit 750+ yards than one of them hit 1,000,” Shipley writes. Such a split would probably lean towards Rodriguez at the goal line, making him slightly more fantasy-valuable on a weekly basis barring big plays from Tuten. If this prediction comes true, both backs might have trouble cracking the weekly RB2 ranks.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 24-of-41 passes for 306 yards, four touchdowns and one interception in Jacksonville’s 34-31, Week 6 loss to the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: It could have been more, had Liam Coen not settled for a game-tying field goal on fourth-and-short with less than four minutes left in the game. It also could have been more had Lawrence not thrown an end-zone pick to Calen Bullock. At the end of the day, the screen day was dealing and Lawrence was hitting all sorts of in-breakers against a beleaguered Texans secondary. He enters the bye week as a sure-fire QB1 with 1,174 passing yards and 10 throwing touchdowns in his first five games. Last year’s rushing touchdowns appear to have vanished as the Jaguars have gotten better in the red zone, but Lawrence is still playing exceptional football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 24-of-39 passes for 331 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in the Jaguars’ 19-17, Week 5 win over the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: Lawrence gave fantasy managers what they needed with a solid box score, but he was not the reason the Jags won this game. Lawrence struggled under pressure, throwing one ugly interception while putting the ball on the ground twice via sack-fumbles. Both were recovered by the Jags. The offense was also a catastrophe in the red zone, though a series of penalties and bizarre play calls are largely to blame there. Down by one with eight seconds left, it looked like the team’s struggles on offense would be too much to overcome. Instead, Ameer Abdullah returned a kickoff 53 yards to set up a walkoff field goal from Cam Little. If the Jags can clean things up after an uncharacteristically sloppy game, Lawrence will remain a mid-range QB1 for Week 6 versus the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 18-of-23 passes for 227 yards and one touchdown in the Jaguars’ 22-17, Week 4 win over the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: The Jaguars offensive operation was far from clean against the Bengals; the team as a whole tallied 10 penalties for 100 yards by halftime. Lawrence was sacked four times behind a struggling offensive line but still put together an efficient game. He found Brian Thomas Jr. for the game’s first touchdown as time wound down in the first half and found tight end Brenton Strange for seven of his 18 completions. Despite a relatively pedestrian showing, Lawrence comes away with zero turnovers and the win. He will be a top-12 fantasy option for Week 5 against the Eagles in London.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 19-of-29 attempts for 182 yards and three touchdowns in the Jaguars’ Week 3 win against the Patriots, adding four rushes for 25 yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: Lawrence’s big statistical day could have been bigger if he hadn’t inexplicably taken a knee at the one yard line on a QB rush with about eight minutes left in the fourth quarter. Bhayshul Tuten would go on to score a rushing touchdown a few plays later. Lawrence picked apart of the New England secondary with very little pressure in his face, targeting former Patriots WR Jakobi Meyers heavily and connecting with three different pass catchers for touchdowns — including Parker Washington, who had another score called back. Lawrence, with one of the highest weekly floors in the game, will again be a top-12 QB option in Week 4 against Bengals in what should be a high-scoring game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 17-of-29 attempts for 189 yards and one interception in the Jaguars’ Week 2 loss against the Broncos, adding two rushes for six yards.
