https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: The Jaguars were relatively run-heavy against Denver a week after the Broncos were shredded by Ken Walker and the Chiefs. Lawrence mostly checked down in this one, targeting Parker Washington a team-high 12 times. Brian Thomas, Jr., meanwhile, had two untimely drops, one that appeared to frustrate Lawrence. Lawrence’s interception came on a poor throw to Washington near the sideline. He’ll look to bounce back next week against a stingy New England secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Trevor Lawrence completed 18-of-23 passes for 245 yards and four touchdowns in the Jaguars’ 34-10, Week 1 win over the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: It was a monstrous offensive showing from the Jaguars, led by Lawrence and his four passing touchdowns. He opened scoring with a 30-yard touchdown throw to Parker Washington in the first quarter, tossing two more scores in the first half. Lawrence flexed his mobility with a lob on the run to Jakobi Meyers for a 32-yard touchdown in the third quarter. With a comfortable lead, Lawrence rested in the fourth quarter, finishing with a whopping 0.72 EPA per play. Nick Mullens tallied three kneel-downs in relief. Liam Coen’s offense will generate many fantasy opportunities across the board, especially when operating as efficiently as it did Week 1. Lawrence built upon his solid 2025 season with an all-star showing Week 1 against the Browns and should be a low-end fantasy QB1 for Week 2 against a tougher Broncos defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Jaguars QB Trevor Lawrence said he is more confident in his “progressions, adjustments, when to kill a play and what to call instead.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: According to ESPN’s Michael DiRocco, Lawrence’s offseason “was about gaining a graduate-level understanding” of coach Liam Coen’s offense. Last season, Lawrence was rehabbing an injury while attempting to change his footwork and adjust to a new play caller. He is now calmer and “can play more freely the way he did in the second half of last season.” Lawrence was the overall QB1 in total scoring from Weeks 9-18. If Lawrence and his pass catchers can carry the momentum into 2026, Lawrence can once again finish as an elite QB1, this time from Week 1 onward.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Jaguars HC Liam Coen said he is “trending toward” playing the starters in Friday’s preseason game against the Panthers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: The Jaguars didn’t play any starters in last week’s preseason game against the Saints, but Coen said that because they couldn’t do a padded practice on Monday with the Panthers, he may consider playing his starters a bit on Friday in order to get some “good (players) on good (players)” facing one another. If the Jaguars do play their starters this week, it will be their only taste of preseason action, as Coen has already said he won’t be playing them in the third preseason game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Jaguars coach Liam Coen said he is “pleased” with QB Trevor Lawrence’s performance in spring practices.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: Specifically, Coen said Lawrence “did a really nice job taking care of the football,” perhaps throwing fewer than five interceptions across organized team activities and mandatory minicamp. Lawrence also performed well when “running the whole operation, managing the protections and some of the concepts on the field.” With a year of experience in Coen’s system now under his belt, Lawrence said he feels more confident going through his progressions and is doing “a lot less thinking” as plays are unfolding. Jaguars OC Grant Udinski has been impressed with Lawrence’s recall and his ability to guide teammates through concepts that the team hasn’t practiced in quite a while. Positive reports on the Jaguars’ offense continue to roll in. Lawrence warrants QB1 treatment in 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes the chemistry between QB Trevor Lawrence and WR Jakobi Meyers “has taken a leap” this offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/trevor-law.analysis: The Jaguars acquired Meyers via trade in Week 10 last year. He then led the Jaguars in targets (63) and receptions (43) until their season came to a close with a Wild Card Round loss to the Bills. Fellow Jaguars WRs Parker Washington and Brian Thomas Jr. have generated buzz in recent weeks, but Meyers should not be overlooked. He still has a chance to repeat as the team’s target leader this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/foster-mor.headline: Foster Moreau caught 2-of-2 targets for seven yards and two touchdowns in Houston’s Week 6 win over the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/foster-mor.analysis: Sure. One of them was even a beautiful one-handed snag as the game drew near halftime. Moreau out-paced Dalton Schultz (4-of-6 targets, 33 yards) in the fantasy streets even if not on the snap count spreadsheets. You know better than to chase the low-snap high-touchdown outlier.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/foster-mor.headline: Dalton Schultz caught 3-of-3 targets for 30 yards in Houston’s Week 3 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/foster-mor.analysis: Schultz told the CBS booth before the game that he “hopes to not have stat lines” like he had in Week 2, an anecdote they related as he had just one catch in the fourth quarter. Sounds like news that fantasy managers wish they had heard yesterday. He didn’t have a catch in the first half and yielded a red zone touchdown to spoiler Foster Moreau. Schultz has low-end TE1 status in a classic #RevengeGame against the Cowboys in Week 4.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/foster-mor.headline: Texans agreed to terms with TE Foster Moreau, formerly of the Saints, on a two-year, $7.3 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/foster-mor.analysis: $6.3 million is guaranteed. The two sides were reportedly in discussions earlier in the day, with the Texans ultimately deciding Moreau was a good fit. He’ll join a roster with holdovers Dalton Schultz, Cade Stover, and Brevin Jordan, with Harrison Bryant also an unrestricted free agent. Moreau’s 2025 season ended on injured reserve due to an ankle injury after his 2024 season ended early due to a knee injury. Now entering his age-29 season, Moreau’s fantasy value is far from appealing in all formats.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/foster-mor.headline: New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill reports TE Foster Moreau is “in talks” with the Houston Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/foster-mor.analysis: Moreau has shown some versatility in the past, catching up to 33/420/2 in his time with the Raiders, but was targeted just 10 times in 253 offensive snaps with the Saints after coming back from a late-season knee injury in 2024. He’ll turn 29 in May.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/foster-mor.headline: Saints placed TE Foster Moreau on injured reserve with an ankle injury.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/foster-mor.analysis: A knee injury ended Moreau’s 2024 season and kept him sidelined this year in Weeks 1-4. He appeared in 11 games this season, catching 7-of-10 targets for 70 yards. He turns 29 this summer and is an impending free agent. Even if he signs with a team this summer, he does not need to be considered in re-draft formats next year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/foster-mor.headline: Juwan Johnson (ankle) is active in Week 5 against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/foster-mor.analysis: With Foster, Mauro and Tyson Hill also both active, the Saints will have their top three tight ends all active for the same game for the first time this season. What that means for all of their usage remains to be seen, but it’s hard to start any of them with confidence this week until we see how the Saints deploy them. The Saints declared OG Cesar Ruiz, CB Isaac Yiadom, DE Chase Young, DT Khristian Boyd, OT Xavier Truss, and RB Devin Neal inactive.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/foster-mor.headline: Saints activated TE Foster Moreau (knee) form the Physically Unable to Perform list.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/foster-mor.analysis: The team also activated Taysom Hill, setting the stage for both to make their season debuts against the Giants. It could not have come at a better time considering fellow tight end Juwan Johnson is listed as questionable with an ankle injury.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/foster-mor.headline: Saints QB/TE Taysom Hill (knee) and TE Foster Moreau (knee) are questionable for New Orleans’ Week 5 game against the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/foster-mor.analysis: It’s a good sign for both that they practiced all week without setbacks. If Juwan Johnson (ankle) is down in Week 5, one of them could walk in to a big role right away in Kellen Moore’s offense. It’ll probably be Saturday before we know if that’s the case, as each would need to be officially activated off the PUP list. Hill obviously has some fantasy upside if healthy, but he’s also a 35-year-old coming off a serious knee injury. Tread carefully.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/foster-mor.headline: Saints QB/TE Taysom Hill (knee) and TE Foster Moreau (knee) were both limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/foster-mor.analysis: They maintain the same status. We don’t yet know if Hill or Moreau will be active for Week 5 — either could cut deeply into Juwan Johnson’s fantasy value if officially activated from the PUP list after being designated to return on Monday. The Saints have a 21-day window from Monday to do it, so there’s not necessarily an urgency to activating Hill or Moreau for Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/foster-mor.headline: Saints TE Foster Moreau (knee) was limited on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/foster-mor.analysis: Moreau and Taysom Hill (knee) both returned to practice today, while Weeks 1-4 starting TE Juwan Johnson (ankle) was sidelined. It is too early to tell if Moreau will be active for the Saints’ Week 5 game against the Giants, though Moreau really does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues at this time.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. caught 3-of-4 targets for 34 yards in Houston’s Week 6 win over the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: It tied his season-high for receptions in four games with Arizona. Harrison played just 12 snaps. The Texans do seem dedicated to giving him the ball — as you’d hope after he was acquired for a second-round pick — and we imagine he’ll be in the FLEX conversation next week against the Giants after a full week to hone trust with the coaching staff. His first two catches were on in-breaking routes.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said Marvin Harrison Jr. will play in Week 6 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: It’s a slightly short turnaround for MHJ, who was traded to the Texans on Sunday, and a weird travel schedule with Houston flying to London to take on the Jags. On the other hand, a week is still more than enough time to get Harrison Jr. installed at least as a part-time player. He isn’t much of a fantasy option this week, but a week or two of practice reps could get him in the FLEX mix if Houston proves to be a better fit for the former No. 4 overall pick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Texans acquired WR Marvin Harrison Jr. from the Cardinals in exchange for a 2027 second-round pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Harrison, 24, gets a fresh start partway through his third NFL season. The former first-round pick has averaged just 47.8 receiving yards per game in 33 career games. Adjusting to a new scheme on the fly could be challenging, and Harrison has not proven himself to be a reliable fantasy contributor. It could be tough sledding for fantasy managers, but if Harrison quickly adjusts to his new team, he has a clear runway to No. 2 wide receiver duties next to Nico Collins. He should be rostered in 12-team leagues. The Cardinals are also sending a 2027 seventh-round pick to the Texans in exchange for a 2027 sixth-round pick.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Cardinals declared Marvin Harrison Jr., QB Carson Beck, CB Starling Thomas, Andrew Wingard and DL Andrew Billings inactive for Week 5 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Life continues to be rough for fantasy managers rostering Harrison. The soon-to-be ex-Cardinal will not participate in what should be a fantasy-friendly game against the porous Lions defense. Bummer. Still no definitive word on where he will end up next week. Trey McBride, Michael Wilson and Kendrick Bourne benefit from his absence. The Cardinals will be without Wingard, one of two starting safeties, but will have DT Walter Nolen (calf) available to them.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Cardinals are finalizing a deal to trade WR Marvin Harrison Jr., reports ESPN’s Adam Schefter.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: The Cardinals informed Harrison this morning that he will be inactive for Sunday’s game against the Lions as the details of the trade are finalized, according to Schefter. While it’s unclear where Harrison is headed, Schefter mentions the Houston Texans as one team known to have interest. The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reported this morning that the Cardinals could be seeking a second-round pick and a mid-round pick in return. Harrison has just five catches for 85 yards and one touchdown in four games this year. According to Schefter, no Harrison trade will be completed until after Sunday’s games. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Cardinals would want a second-round pick and more to consider trading WR Marvin Harrison Jr., reports the Ringer’s Tom Pelissero.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Pelissero says the Cardinals would want a second-pick and perhaps a mid-round pick in exchange for Harrison. The 24-year-old receiver was drafted fourth overall two years ago, but under new coach Matt LaFluer he has 85 yards in four games this year. Pelissero points to Harrison’s decision to hire an agent last month as evidence he could be preparing for a trade. While Harrison has obviously been a disappointment in fantasy this year, he should find his way into some starting lineups against the Lions secondary in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. caught a 12-yard touchdown in the Cardinals’ Week 4 loss to the Giants.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Harrison capped the Cardinals’ opening drive with a beautiful 12-yard end zone grab against Deonte Banks’ 1-on-1 coverage. It was the best possible start to the beleaguered wideout’s day. It would also prove to be a false start, as he caught zero other passes on three scattered targets. Admittedly, that does not include a late DPI that set the Cardinals up at the Giants’ four-yard line as they desperately sought a potential game-winning touchdown. Good, but nowhere close to enough for all involved. MHJ has now been out-targeted 30-9 by Michael Wilson over the past two weeks. That is to say nothing of Trey McBride. The Lions are a plus Week 5 matchup, but Harrison Jr. remains more waiver wire fodder than potential upside FLEX option.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports teams are “doing their due diligence” on Marvin Harrison Jr.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Schefter noted that the Cardinals aren’t “enthralled” with the idea of trading Harrison Jr. He also said point-blank that “it would not be a surprise” for MHJ to be traded. As much as the Cardinals may not want to admit it, this experiment needs to come to an end. The team has Michael Wilson and Trey McBride locked up on long-term contracts and MHJ has done nothing this year. He has four catches for 73 scoreless yards this year. At this point, it’s likely in the best interest of both sides for Harrison Jr. to find a new home.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: Marvin Harrison Jr. caught 3-of-5 targets for 40 yards in the Cardinals’ Week 3 loss to the 49ers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: Harrison finished the day with a modest 3/40 receiving line, though that represents a small share of the Cardinals’ offensive output on the day. His first target was a declined offensive pass interference on third down and his first reception came in the second quarter. Harrison did make a clutch catch on third-and-long in the fourth quarter but he ultimately saw just five targets on a day where Jacoby Brissett threw 52 passes. Michael Wilson looks like Brissett’s preferred wide receiver while the deep looks Harrison can excel at are not easily obtainable in this iteration of the Cardinals offense. Harrison is a low-end fantasy WR4 at best against the Giants next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.headline: The Arizona Republic’s Theo Mackie reports Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur “met [the] idea” of manufacturing touches for Marvin Harrison “with skepticism.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/marvin-harriso.analysis: “I know it’s like, ‘Well, just get some easy completions to get going,’” LaFleur told Mackie. “And that’s fine. You also have Trey McBride, who’s one of the best underneath guys in the world. And there’s only about 60, 65 plays a game. And you’ve gotta run the ball. And you’ve got Kendrick, who works underneath pretty well too. So everyone’s kind of got their role.” In other words; don’t look for LaFleur to bail your Harrison fantasy pick out. If Harrison does get cooking this year it’ll be in the normal flow of their offense. So far that has yielded just four targets in two games.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins caught 3-of-5 targets for 76 yards in Houston’s Week 6 win over the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: He added a long defensive pass interference penalty drawn on Travis Hunter to set up Houston’s second third-quarter touchdown. Collins also took an end around in the red zone for five rushing yards. Close, but ultimately not the line that fantasy managers were hoping for. Collins will remain in the low-end WR1 region against the Giants in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins caught 5-of-7 targets for 56 yards in Houston’s Week 5 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: He went for 3/45 in the first half and was mostly managed down with the Texans not really threatened in a major way after he sealed a block for their first touchdown in the third quarter. Collins took a hard fall after a leaping grab and did look a little worse for the wear on the sideline. We wouldn’t be surprised if he saw injury report time this week. That said, he looked good and the Texans simply didn’t need to throw the ball much late in this one. It’s back to the low-end WR1 line next week against the Jaguars.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins caught 7-of-8 targets for 118 yards and two touchdowns in Houston’s Week 4 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: He immediately busted out of the gates with a 45-yarder, caught a touchdown to end that drive, then found the end zone a second time in the second half when he worked to the other side of zone coverage and C.J. Stroud was able to find him on an improvised throw. Pretty good player. Collins handled 36-of-53 snaps, highest on the team. He’ll be a low-end WR1 against the Titans in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins (hamstring) is not on Houston’s final Week 4 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: He got in a full session and will escape the line. Collins doesn’t play the same amount of snaps that most of the league’s top wideouts play anyway, so even if he is managed a bit, he can be trusted as a low-end WR1 in what looks to be a smash spot against a bad Cowboys pass defense, though one that is integrating new trade acquisition Joey Porter Jr. against Collins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins (hamstring) was seen practicing on Friday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: We’re still waiting for the final injury report to drop, but Collins appears set to return in Week 4 after missing the last two games with a hamstring injury. Collins was listed as limited in Wednesday’s and Thursday’s practices and has been trending in the right direction all week. We’ll check back in when the Texans officially confirm Collins’ status ahead of the weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: The Houston Chronicle’s Jonathan M. Alexander reports that Nico Collins (hamstring) was “optimistic” about playing in Week 4 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: Alexander caught up with Collins after the Texans’ star player logged his second consecutive limited practice. Collins should probably still be treated as sitting somewhere in the questionable-to-probable range, but this is great to hear. Collins is a WR1, as usual, if active.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: Another limited session keeps Collins in the questionable column as he attempts to return from a multi-week hamstring strain. The Texans would surely like to have their star wide receiver back for what could be a back-and-forth game environment against the Cowboys this week, but balancing short-term and long-term needs is critical. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Nico Collins (hamstring) returned to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reported over the weekend that Collins had a “decent chance” to return in Week 4. Even a limited practice today is a big step in the right direction. The winless Texans desperately need a playmaker on offense and Collins is their only option. While he could be on a pitch count in his first game back, Collins has to be in fantasy lineups the moment he is cleared to play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports there is a “decent chance” Nico Collins (hamstring) returns for Week 4 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: Collins injured his hamstring in practice last week and has already been ruled out for the second game in a row. He did not practice this week, so the Texans’ first injury report of Week 4 will be telling. Dalton Schultz will continue to vacuum up targets in the meantime. He saw 14 targets last week and caught 12 of them for 140 yards.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.headline: Texans ruled out WR Nico Collins (hamstring) for Week 3 against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/nico-colli.analysis: Collins will miss his second consecutive game with yet another hamstring strain. Last week, the passing offense ran through TE Dalton Schultz, who earned 13 targets. Fellow Texans WR Xavier Hutchinson was next with eight targets, but he caught just three, making for a shaky FLEX option this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylin-noe.headline: Jaylin Noel caught 4-of-4 passes for 107 yards and a touchdown in Houston’s Week 6 win over the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylin-noe.analysis: Noel has scored in all of Houston’s wins this year; that’s analytics. The underlying numbers are more annoying — he played 31-of-63 snaps and was not one of Houston’s top targets in what has been a frustrating room. Still, it’s very clear he’s the second-most talented player in this receiving corps, even if Marvin Harrison Jr. is cutting in. Noel has some FLEX viability in Week 7 against the Giants.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylin-noe.headline: Jaylin Noel caught 5-of-5 passes for 41 yards and a touchdown in Houston’s Week 5 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylin-noe.analysis: Noel added a one-yard carry that made him the team’s leader in wideout touches. His touchdown came as C.J. Stroud extended the play by spinning backwards out of the pocket and floated towards the end zone before delivering a strike to Noel. He still played just 30 of 65 snaps, but there’s a commitment to touches for Noel that seems fantasy-interesting, at least ahead of any Marvin Harrison Jr. news on Monday. He’s a FLEX possibility next week against the Jaguars in London.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylin-noe.headline: Tank Dell (knee) won’t play in Houston’s Week 5 game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylin-noe.analysis: He did not practice on Friday and was ruled out. The Texans reportedly pushed hard on Dell in full pads on Thursday’s practice despite the questionable listing, it seems his body did not react as they’d hoped. This leaves Jaylin Noel in a potential FLEX-useful spot against a rough Titans secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylin-noe.headline: Jaylin Noel caught 3-of-3 targets for 85 yards in Houston’s Week 4 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylin-noe.analysis: Noel and C.J. Stroud connected on a 52-yard downfield catch that Noel barely had to let up on. He did play 34 snaps, the highest amount he’s had since Week 2, in a telling sign for how the offense is trending. Still, Noel is probably best approached as a deep league boom/bust FLEX play at this point. He’s continually played the game of one step forward, one step back.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylin-noe.headline: Kayshon Boutte caught 2-of-2 targets for 21 yards in Houston’s Week 3 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylin-noe.analysis: Boutte played 35-of-52 snaps, and if that sounds low, it actually lead the team in Nick Caley’s absolutely bizarre WR platoon situation where it seems like he is trying to find someone who he trusts. Boutte looks the best of the bunch, but we can’t recommend trying to eat these non-existent fantasy points. Jaylin Noel (2/17 on two targets) and Jared Wayne (1/20 on four targets including an inexcusable drop) continue to haunt the situation.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylin-noe.headline: Jared Wayne caught 2-of-7 targets for 33 yards in Houston’s Week 2 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylin-noe.analysis: Jaylin Noel outsnapped him 44-to-36 for the Texans No. 3 receiver role but Wayne beat Noel out by one catch, two yards, and two targets. “Man starts over again everyday, in spite of all he knows, against all he knows,” Emil Cioran once wrote. And these are the readings C.J. Stroud should get familiar with as he endures another week of this receiving corps in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylin-noe.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said he “would not be surprised” if Texans WR Jaylin Noel is more involved in Week 2 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylin-noe.analysis: Rapoport adds that Noel is “really talented.” We agree, but the Texans have consistently played WR Xavier Hutchinson ahead of him. Noel, 24, is an explosive player, and the Texans will be looking for playmakers to contribute with WR Nico Collins (hamstring) sidelined this week. Noel is officially on the boom-bust FLEX radar in Week 2 against the Bengals.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylin-noe.headline: Kayshon Boutte caught 1-of-2 targets for 21 yards in Houston’s Week 1 loss to the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylin-noe.analysis: Boutte managed just 36-of-79 snaps, third-most among Texans wideouts, as they ran weird platoons that had Jared Wayne, Jaylin Noel, and Xavier Hutchinson all on the field for at least 24 snaps. Until someone conclusively wins this job, or at least we start getting some juice that someone might win the job, it’ll be hard to start any of these receivers in fantasy football.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylin-noe.headline: Jaylin Noel (hamstring/finger) returned to practice on Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylin-noe.analysis: A real “call an ambulance, but not for me” situation here as it was reported that Noel would be out for a few weeks on Sunday. He’s likely only participating in practice in a reduced role based on that. At this point Noel is likely just a bench dart throw in most leagues despite playing objectively well last year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylin-noe.headline: Texans WR Jaylin Noel (hamstring/finger) will be out for “a few weeks” after suffering “a little bit of a setback.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/jaylin-noe.analysis: NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson noted earlier today that Noel was not participating in practice due to a finger injury, which he suffered in July, and a recent hamstring injury. It turns out Noel’s recent hamstring injury is actually a re-injury. Fellow second-year WR Jayden Higgins has the inside track to the WR2 role. Noel was set to compete with Xavier Hutchinson and WR Tank Dell for the WR3 gig. Instead, he is losing valuable preseason reps. Noel might be best viewed as an early-season waiver wire add.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks rushed 15 times for 56 yards in Houston’s Week 6 win over the Jaguars, adding two catches for 25 yards on three targets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: Marks was mostly bottled up, though he did manage 9/41 in the second half behind a few reasonably big runs to become the first back all year to hit 40 rushing yards against the Jaguars. He played 49-of-63 snaps. The Texans run game is still bad, but against the Giants in Week 7 Marks should probably be on the RB2 line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Texans ruled out David Montgomery (groin) for Week 6 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: We already knew that Montgomery was considered week-to-week, so this is unsurprising. Woody Marks will start for however long Montgomery is sidelined. The Jaguars field one of the NFL’s best run defenses, but Marks ceded just one snap to Dare Ogunbowale last week. Theoretically, he should remain in a near-full-time role, elevating him to the RB2/FLEX tier despite the tough matchup.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Texans head coach DeMeco Ryans said David Montgomery will be week-to-week with the groin injury he suffered in Week 5 against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: Ryans said Woody Marks “will carry the load” for the team while Montgomery is sidelined. It’s been a tough start to the season for Montgomery, who scored three times in Week 1 but has been locked out of the end zone ever since while averaging a career-low 3.5 yards per touch. Marks has been slightly more efficient than Montgomery this season, but the Texans’ running game as a whole has left much to be desired. Marks’ expected workload makes him worth a waiver wire claim where available, but fantasy managers shouldn’t expect anything more than RB3 levels of production at this time. The Texans will take on the Jaguars in London in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks rushed 15 times for 62 yards in Houston’s Week 5 win over the Titans, adding four catches for 23 yards on four targets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: He had a 20-ish yard touchdown taken off the board on what appeared to be a ticky-tack holding penalty. The more important story here is that David Montgomery (groin) went down mid-game and the Texans gave Marks a full workload. He had 56-of-65 snaps and no other back received a carry or touch. Marks won’t get that kind of workload next week against the Jaguars, but if Montgomery is destined for a long absence, he should threaten 70 percent of the snaps and a majority of the workload, making him one of the day’s bigger fantasy winners.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks rushed six times for 22 yards and a touchdown in Houston’s Week 4 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: His touchdown came on a two-minute play where the Cowboys line wasn’t even set, aka the only way any Texans runner can advance the football. Still, he’s faster than David Montgomery and that’s really all the Texans have in their backfield. He’s a FLEX option against the Titans in Week 5.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks rushed five times for 15 yards and a touchdown in Week 3’s loss to the Colts, adding one catch for six yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: Marks managed just 20 snaps to David Montgomery’s 32 in a game where there was only one hurry-up drive that got off the ground for the Texans, but at least he cashed in with a one-yard touchdown plunge. He remains a volatile FLEX next week against the Cowboys.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks rushed eight times for eight yards against the Bengals in Week 2, adding five catches for 27 yards on six targets.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: At least he found a PPR scam role here, but this was ugly stuff as far as production. Marks has battled David Montgomery to a near 50/50 split through two weeks. All that’s really done for fantasy purposes is make neither of them all that interesting. Marks will be on the FLEX radar against the Colts in Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Woody Marks rushed nine times for 42 yards in Houston’s Week 1 loss to the Bills, adding one catch for minus-2 yards on his only target.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: Marks was a change-up back and also worked two-minute drives — this is a pretty solid runout for him based on how it looked at times this offseason, but it’s going to be hard for him to deliver standalone value with David Montgomery monopolizing the red zone touches. Marks isn’t completely unstartable but is probably more of a what-the-heck FLEX against the Bengals in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: The Houston Chronicle’s Jonathan M. Alexander believes the rushing workloads for Texans RB David Montgomery and RB Woody Marks “might not be 50-50, but it will be close.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: According to Alexander, the Texans have utilized both running backs nearly evenly throughout camp. Texans OC Nick Caley “doesn’t typically go away from what’s working,” which could result in a hot-hand approach on game day. For now, Montgomery should be treated as the starter, but Marks looked good in last week’s preseason game and should be stashed on benches in 12-team leagues at the very least.

https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.headline: Texans RB Woody Marks rushed four times for 37 yards and one touchdown in Thursday’s preseason game against the Raiders, adding one reception for six yards.
https://www.nbcsports.com/joquavious-mar.analysis: The Texans gave RB David Montgomery the night off, so Marks got the start alongside QB C.J. Stroud. The second-year running back played 10-of-10 first-team snaps before retiring for the evening. Marks looked good tonight, particularly on his 20-yard touchdown run, which required him to weave through traffic and bounce off would-be tacklers twice. The fact that Marks played while Montgomery rested could suggest Montgomery is the clear-cut starter rather than a 1A to Marks’ 1B. The young running back is still worth drafting as a bench stash, with potential standalone FLEX viability

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: C.J. Stroud completed 24-of-34 passes for 312 yards, three touchdowns and one interception in Houston’s 34-31, Week 6 win over the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: The Texans running game was mostly abandoned until the fourth quarter, leaving Stroud to wail on an overmatched Jaguars secondary. His best throw was probably on Houston’s final possession of the first half, as he dotted a 50-yard throw with a defender in his face to Jaylin Noel, eventually setting up (checking notes) Foster Moreau’s second touchdown of the day. Stroud has now thrown for six touchdowns and gone over 260 yards in each of his last three games; he’s suddenly in the high-end QB2 competition with bye weeks hitting as the Texans host the Giants in Week 7.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: C.J. Stroud completed 26-of-34 passes for 261 yards and a touchdown in Houston’s 26-3, Week 5 win over the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: He added a rushing touchdown on a goal-to-go red zone keeper. The Texans offense continues to bog down with penalties and bad runs — they went into half with four field goals — but Stroud was able to pilot the ship well enough to keep things reasonable until the Titans defense broke in the second half. He’ll head to London next week to face the Jaguars, yet another team that should keep him throwing given how good their run defense is, so he’ll be a mid-range QB2 for that one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: C.J. Stroud completed 21-of-31 passes for 347 yards and two touchdowns in Houston’s 34-30, Week 4 loss to the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: Well, hard to blame much of this on him. Stroud was turnover-free for the third time in four games and peppered the returning Nico Collins with targets while also finding a 52-yarder to Jaylin Noel and several chunk gains to the tertiary receivers. The Texans had a 30-27 lead at the two-minute warning. For once, the defense gets to pick up the slack. The Texans have the mother of all get-right games in an 0-4 bowl against the Titans next week. Given how poorly the run offense is going, Stroud may continue to let it rip here and could be on the high-end QB2 line.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: Texans coach DeMeco Ryans said he is open to leaning more into the passing game.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: “The thing for me about offensive football is you have to make sure you move the ball and try to score as many points as possible,” Ryans is quoted as saying by the Houston Chronicle. “How that looks to me, it really doesn’t matter. You can think or want to be a certain thing. But if you’re shown that that’s not the case and it’s not getting done, then you have to adjust. That’s where we are.” The Texans already abandoned the run against the Bengals in Week 2, throwing the ball 55 times. Perhaps Nico Collins’ return this week will raise all ships, but if it was as simple as the Texans needing to throw more, they probably would have scored more than six points against the Bengals. C.J. Stroud has a streamable matchup against the Cowboys this week if it all comes together.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: C.J. Stroud completed 16-of-27 passes for 167 yards and a touchdown in Houston’s 19-17, Week 3 loss to the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: It was turnover-free football despite three sacks. Simply put: The Texans just don’t look like an NFL offense right now. Two of Stroud’s three deep balls in this game could have been intended for any of four different receivers, one of them hit off Jaylin Noel’s hands. Nobody has taken the reins. Texans OC Nick Caley deserves to be on the hot seat. Stroud passes the eye test when you watch these games, but the design of this offense — especially the run offense — is brutal. Stroud is near the bottom of the superflex QB2 ranks against the Cowboys next week, though the potential return of Nico Collins merits some consideration that better things could happen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: C.J. Stroud completed 30-of-55 passes for 353 scoreless yards in Houston’s 20-6, Week 2 loss to the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: Stroud looked pretty good in this game, but he had no one to throw to, the Texans had no running game (Stroud lead the team in rushing with 29 yards), and they scored six points. Other than that, Mrs. Lincoln... Xavier Hutchinson failed to reel in several passes that hit him in the hands, including a would-be touchdown in the waning moments. It’s clear that without Nico Collins there’s just not enough talent on the field here to support a dead running game, and that’s what happened today. The Texans will look to rebound against the Colts in Week 3, a game where Stroud is probably on the QB2 radar for in superflex leagues.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: C.J. Stroud completed 26-of-38 passes for 274 yards and two touchdowns in Houston’s 36-31, Week 1 loss against the Bills.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: The buried news from the traditional stat line is that Stroud fumbled twice and the Texans recovered neither of them, including a back-breaker inside the Buffalo 20 on Houston’s final drive. The hard truth is that this offensive line is still not good. But, overall, it’s hard to fault the Texans offense for this one — if the 2025 Texans defense showed up, they win the game. Stroud looked competent-if-not-stellar in leading a touchdown drive in the two-minute drill of the first quarter. This is a good result for his superflex QB2 prospects — the Texans defense being as bad as they were in this one would also be welcomed news for fantasy managers. Stroud will get an (on-paper) easier roll against the Bengals in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: Texans and QB C.J. Stroud will pause contract discussion until after the 2026 season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: The two sides worked diligently to get a deal done before the start of the regular season but will now pause discussions until after the year. Stroud was reportedly offered a substantial deal earlier in the offseason but turned it down, now forced to “bet on himself” as he plays out the final year of his rookie deal, minus the fifth-year option. Stroud has been unable to rekindle his rookie year magic while playing under two different offensive coordinators, something he’s looking to remedy in his second season under Nick Caley.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Texans are “prepared to put CJ Stroud in what it feels is a strong place among the 12 quarterbacks in the $50 million club.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: Houston GM Nick Caserio recently said the team would not negotiate a new deal with Stroud once the regular season begins, putting a hard and fast deadline on Stroud’s ability to secure a longer-term contract with the team that drafted him. His immense and nationally-televised struggles down the stretch last season — including his playoff meltdown against the Patriots — could factor into the team’s decision to go all in on him as a long-term franchise quarterback. Fowler said Stroud “can let an exploding quarterback market do the work for him if he waits an additional six to eight months” and explore free agency in 2027. Stroud over the past three seasons ranks 22nd out of 40 qualifying QBs in adjusted EPA per drop back, alongside Bo Nix and Trevor Lawrence. He ranks 24th in drop back success rate, just behind Mac Jones.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.headline: Texans GM Nick Caserio said there were “productive talks” on a contract extension for QB C.J. Stroud and that if a deal isn’t done before the start of the season, they’ll pick it up next offseason.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/c-j-stroud.analysis: There’s really no reason for Stroud to want to negotiate off last year’s end-of-season performance, so we’re not stunned that there’s been no extension. It does sound like the Texans are at least laying the groundwork for next offseason. The general NFL expectation has been that Stroud will go into the year without an extension. The Houston Chronicle’s Jonathan Alexander reported that league sources believe the Texans and Stroud’s camp “are not far off on what they think Stroud’s contract terms should look like and how much he should be paid per year.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.headline: Reed Blankenship (concussion) was ruled out of Houston’s Week 6 game against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.analysis: Blankenship suffered the concussion near the end of the first half and was carted off with a towel over his head. MJ Stewart took over at safety for a suddenly-ordinary Texans defense.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.headline: Texans agreed to terms with S Reed Blankenship, formerly of the Eagles, on a three-year, $24.8 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.analysis: Blankenship made the Eagles’ roster as a UDFA in 2022. He served as a backup during his rookie season before earning a starting role in 2023. Blankenship never gave up that job and went on to start 46 reglar season games plus five postseason contests during his time in Philly. Blankenship broke up four passes and intercepted one in 2025. He will slot into a starting role on an elite Houston defense this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.headline: Eagles CB Darius Slay (concussion) returned to practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.analysis: Slay missed Week 13 with the concussion after failing to return to practice at any point in the week. Even a limited session on Wednesday would put him on track to return for Week 14. Safety Reed Blankenship suffered a concussion of his own on Sunday and did not practice today. He will likely miss Philly’s upcoming matchup with the Panthers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.headline: Eagles S Reed Blankenship suffered a concussion in Week 13 against the Ravens and will not return.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.analysis: Blankenship was ruled out at the end of the third quarter after heading to the locker room with the brain injury. The veteran safety signed a one-year extension in the offseason and has been giving the Eagles their money’s worth and then some. He has three interceptions, five pass breakups, and a fumble recovery this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.headline: Eagles signed S Reed Blankenship to a one-year contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.analysis: Blankenship was in the final year of his deal but will now be under contract through 2025. The former UDFA from the 2022 class has appeared in 25 games for the Eagles over the last two years and started in all 15 games he appeared in last season. In his brief career, Blankenship has totaled four interceptions and one fumble recovery and earned a PFF coverage grade of 78.0 last season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.headline: Eagles S Reed Blankenship (groin) is not participating in Saturday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.analysis: Blankenship is in danger of missing the Eagles’ Wild Card game against the Buccaneers with a groin injury. He missed practice on Saturday and head coach Nick Sirianni said he would be a game-time decision. If Blankenship cannot go, Avonte Maddox is likely to step up in his place.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.headline: Eagles S Reed Blankenship (concussion) is questionable to return to Week 14 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.analysis: Blankenship took the brunt of an attempted tackle attempt to the head in the second quarter of the team’s Week 14 game against the Cowboys. He was removed from the game by the independent neurologist and was ruled questionable to return.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.headline: Eagles S Reed Blankenship (ribs) will not play in Week 7 against the Dolphins.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.analysis: Cornerback Bradley Roby is also set to miss Week 7. The Eagles’ defense has fallen from grace this year and a nightmare run of injuries in their secondary has been one of the biggest culprits. Expect Mike McDaniel and the Dolphins to pick on Philly’s backups in the secondary this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.headline: Eagles CB James Bradberry (concussion) will not play in Week 1 against the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.analysis: Safety Reed Blankenship is also out for Week 2. Though the injuries to Philly’s secondary should make life easier for Kirk Cousins, he is entering Thursday Night Football with a banged-up offensive line and is facing one of the league’s most terrifying-front sevens. It could still be a long night in primetime for Cousins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.headline: Eagles DT Fletcher Cox (ribs) did not practice Monday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/reed-blank.analysis: Safety Reed Blankenship and running back Kenneth Gainwell also missed practice with a rib injury, while LB Nakobe Dean (foot) and CB James Bradberry (concussion) were held out with various ailments. The Eagles host the Vikings on a quick turnaround when the two teams square off on Thursday Night Football in Week 2.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.headline: Panthers declared OT Monroe Freeling, TE Ja’Tavion Sanders, QB Haynes King, RB AJ Dillon, OG Torricelli Simpkins, OT Albert Reese, and DT TeRah Edwards inactive for Week 6 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.analysis: The good news is that offensive tackle Taylor Moton is active for the first time this year. He missed the first month of the season while recovering from treatment for a blood clot. He will start at right tackle in place of Freeling.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.headline: Monroe Freeling (knee) is doubtful for Carolina’s Week 6 game against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.analysis: The rookie got in back-to-back limited sessions, but they must have indeed been quite limited for him to wind up with the rarely-used doubtful tag. It’s very unlikely he plays this weekend. Taylor Moton (blood clot) is questionable after three full practices and would seem to be the favorite to start at right tackle.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.headline: Monroe Freeling (knee) was limited in Thursday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.analysis: It’s an upgrade from a Wednesday DNP. Freeling played 64 percent of the snaps in Week 4 and looks to be trending in the right direction for Week 6 after the Week 5 bye.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.headline: Taylor Moton (blood clots) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.analysis: Moton is tentatively on track to make his return from injured reserve this week. Meanwhile, RT Monroe Freeling (knee) sat out on Wednesday. Panthers DT Tershawn Wharton (neck) is practicing in full, while EDGE Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) was limited.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.headline: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said he is “hopeful” Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) will be able to play in Week 6 against the Eagles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.analysis: Phillips went down with a hamstring injury late in Sunday’s game against the Lions and didn’t return to the field. For a player with Phillips’ injury history, there were immediate concerns regarding the severity of the injury, but with a Week 5 bye on tap, the hope is Phillips won’t miss much time, if any. Phillips has totaled two sacks in his first four games of the season. In addition to Phillips, the team is also hopeful that OT Monroe Freeling (knee) will be able to return in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Monroe Freeling (concussion) will play in Week 4 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.analysis: The Panthers entered the season down both of their starting tackles. They will also be without left guard Damien Lewis this week. Getting Freeling back is a big win for Bryce Young and the offense. Freeling has struggled in pass protection so far but is serviceable in the run game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.headline: Xavier Legette (knee) will not play in Week 4 against the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.analysis: Legette will miss a second straight game with his knee injury. He has caught just two passes for 64 yards on six targets this season and wouldn’t be on the fantasy radar even if he were active. In addition to Legette, the Panthers also ruled out OG Damien Lewis (elbow) for Week 4 against the Lions while OT Monroe Freeling (concussion), DT Lee Hunter (foot), and DT Cam Jackson (knee) were all listed as questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.headline: Panthers RT Monroe Freeling (concussion) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.analysis: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reported earlier this week that stud Panthers LG Damien Lewis (elbow) will be out “a few weeks.” The Panthers have a fantasy-friendly matchup against the Lions this week, but Freeling’s health is worth tracking.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.headline: Panthers placed RT Taylor Moton on the reserve/non-football injury list with blood clots.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.analysis: He’s joined by CB Jaycee Horn, who cut his foot while running and required stitches. Horn’s injury is expected to be a minor one. Moton, on the other hand, is expected to miss the start of the season and the “belief” is he’ll play in 2026. The Panthers later clarified that Moton is hopeful to return from clotting in his lung at “mid-season.” Rookie first-round tackle Monroe Freeling figures to step in for Moton early.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.headline: Panthers selected Georgia OT Monroe Freeling with the No. 19 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/monroe-fre.analysis: The giant Freeling will be blocking for the diminutive Bryce Young in Carolina. The Panthers offensive line in 2025 were graded by PFF as the league’s 17th best pass blocking unit. Freeling (6’7/315) enters the 2026 NFL Draft as one of the most physically gifted offensive linemen in the class, boasting rare movement skills and length for the position. The Bulldogs tackle brings a prototype frame at roughly 6-7, 315 pounds with nearly 35-inch arms, pairing that length with elite athletic traits highlighted by a freakish 9.99 Relative Athletic Score, including a 4.93s forty, 33.5-inch vertical and 9’7” broad jump. Freeling’s athleticism shows up consistently on tape, showing advanced movement capabilities in space, executing reach blocks, lead assignments and screen duties while displaying the quick feet to mirror edge rushers in pass protection. After a developmental sophomore season, Freeling made a major leap in 2025, posting an 86.1 PFF pass-blocking grade while allowing just two sacks and eight total pressures across 469 pass-blocking snaps. His length, quick redirect ability and fluidity passing off twists make him particularly effective against speed rushers and stunts. However, Freeling can struggle to maintain leverage and hand placement at times, with inconsistent run-blocking landmarks and occasional balance issues when he leans into contact.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/azeez-al-s.headline: Azeez Al-Shaair left Houston’s Week 6 game against the Jaguars to be evaluated for a concussion.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/azeez-al-s.analysis: The Jaguars have been able to impose their will on the Texans in the run game in the first half, and this won’t help matters. Al-Shaair left after Jacksonville scored their first touchdown in the second quarter and was spotted walking to the locker room.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/azeez-al-s.headline: Texans declared LB Azeez Al-Shaair, DE Chris Braswell, OG Febechi Nwaiwu, OT Nate Thomas, and TE Marlin Klein inactive for Week 4 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/azeez-al-s.analysis: The Texans are at near full strength and welcome back wide receiver Nico Collins, who was removed from the team’s injury report on Friday. Collins’ return comes at a time where Houston is seeking its first win of the season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/azeez-al-s.headline: Texans signed LB Azeez Al-Shaair to a three-year, $54 million contract extension.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/azeez-al-s.analysis: Al-Shaair was set to play out the final year of his current contract this season. Instead, Houston keeps him locked in with a long-term deal. Al-Shaair has been with the Texans for two years, starting all 27 regular season games he has been active for. In 2025, Al-Shaair totaled two interceptions, one forced fumble, and a team-high 103 combined tackles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/azeez-al-s.headline: Fort Worth Star-Telegram’s Nick Harris reports that the Cowboys are discussing potential trades for Dolphins LB Jordyn Brooks and Texans LB Azeez Al-Shaair.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/azeez-al-s.analysis: Harris isn’t the only reporter who believes that the Cowboys are still on the hunt for new defenders. In a report from earlier today, ESPN’s Todd Archer mentions Brooks and Al-Shaair as well, while also bringing up Steelers LB Patrick Queen as a possibility. Harris disagrees on the latter player, saying on social media that the Cowboys have “pivoted off Queen,” though he believes the inside linebacker position “gets addressed in the trade market.” In a mock draft published today, Harris links LSU CB Mansoor Delane to the Cowboys at pick No. 12 and Clemson EDGE T.J. Parker at pick No. 20. Brooks totaled 125 solo tackles and 19 TFLs. Al-Shaair totaled 74 solo tackles and five TFLs. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/azeez-al-s.headline: Texans CB Kamari Lassiter (ankle/knee) won’t play in Houston’s Week 18 game against the Colts.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/azeez-al-s.analysis: That will unlock some of Indianapolis’ wideout options should Riley Leonard be able to aim the ball in their direction. Derek Stingley (oblique) is off the injury report, as is linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair. It doesn’t sound like Lassiter would be resting if this were a win-and-in game for the Texans.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/azeez-al-s.headline: Texans CB Kamari Lassiter (ankle/knee) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/azeez-al-s.analysis: Lassiter got hurt in Week 17 against the Chargers, but was able to return later in the game. Thus far, he has missed both practices in Week 18. Fellow starting CB Derek Stingley (oblique) resumed practicing today, as did LB Azeez Al-Shaair (knee/shoulder). The Texans (11-5) have secured a playoff spot, yet trail the Jaguars (12-4) in the AFC South standings. If the Jaguars lose to the Titans this week, the Texans can steal the division title by beating the Colts. The outcome seems unlikely.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/azeez-al-s.headline: Texans CB Derek Stingley (oblique) is questionable for Houston’s Week 16 game against the Raiders.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/azeez-al-s.analysis: He got in a limited session to get on to the questionable line after missing Wednesday and Thursday practice. Azeez Al-Shaair was limited on Thursday, but did not participate in Wednesday or Friday practice for the Texans. Both players should be considered true question marks for Week 16’s action against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/azeez-al-s.headline: Texans restructured LB Azeez Al-Shaair’s contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/azeez-al-s.analysis: The restructuring of Al-Shaair freed up $6.26 million in cap space for the upcoming season. Al-Shaair is perhaps most known for his illegal hit on Trevor Lawrence that saw the league levy a three-game suspension against him. Al-Shaair joined the Texans on a three-year, $34 million deal and is under contract through 2026. Last season he totaled 70 tackles and two sacks in 11 games while earning a PFF defensive grade of 68.9.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/azeez-al-s.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Joe Mixon (ankle) will play in the Texans’ Divisional Round against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/azeez-al-s.analysis: Rapoport reports that linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair (knee) will also play after being listed as questionable on Friday. Mixon suffered his ankle injury on Wednesday and was a DNP on Thursday, so we don’t know much about the severity of his injury other than it’s not believed to be “a major injury,” according to a report from Friday. It sounds like the Texans will be able to lean on Mixon in his normal role on Saturday as the Texans hope to top the Chiefs and make a trip to the AFC Championship Game next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/azeez-al-s.headline: Texans listed Joe Mixon (ankle) as questionable for Saturday’s AFC Divisional Round game against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/azeez-al-s.analysis: This is one worth watching. After popping up as limited following an ankle injury he sustained in Wednesday’s practice, Mixon was a DNP on Thursday and officially carries a questionable designation into the weekend. It’s possible Mixon was sidelined on Thursday out of precaution, but his status will be one to monitor until the team officially confirms his availabilty. In addition to Mixon, LB Azeez Al-Shaair (knee) and WR Robert Woods (hip) are also listed as questionable.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dan-quinn/.headline: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Commanders owner Josh Harris “would love” for Dan Quinn to remain the team’s head coach.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dan-quinn/.analysis: Garafolo says this as if Harris is simply a bystander watching Quinn bumble his way through another season. Garafolo did add that “anything is on the table” if the Commanders get blown out by the 49ers on national television on Monday. They are currently 7.5-point underdogs on most sportsbooks. With a bye week on deck after San Francisco, the Commanders could see Week 7 as the best time to pull the plug on Quinn.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dan-quinn/.headline: ESPN’s John Keim reports Dan Quinn “wanted a different offensive identity and spoke often with his staff of wanting a better run-pass balance.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dan-quinn/.analysis: ‘Bill’ Croskey-Merritt and restricted free agent Chris Rodriguez would stand to gain fantasy value if the Commanders focused on a more run-focused approach, as they seem like a team that has limited resources to dedicate to the running back position this offseason. It’s hard to speculate on who the Commanders could bring in to install a scheme that’s akin to what Quinn desires just based on the idea of more run-pass balance, but the search to replace Kliff Kingsbury looks destined to bring in someone with a more buttoned-up run game.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dan-quinn/.headline: The Athletic’s Dianna Russini reports Commanders head coach Dan Quinn “is expected back” for the 2026 season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dan-quinn/.analysis: Russini adds that “changes to the offense and the defense remain possible.” Quinn took over defensive play-calling in November. Replacing DC Joe Whitt seems plausible. The team has also reportedly “had conversations about potentially moving on from [OC Kliff] Kingsbury even if he doesn’t get a head-coaching job.”

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dan-quinn/.headline: Commanders HC Dan Quinn said he will take over as defensive coordinator.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dan-quinn/.analysis: After becoming the first team to lose four-straight games by 20-plus points since the 2002 Cardinals, Quinn decided something must be done. The Commanders’ defense has been abysmal all season, but their struggles have become more noticeable as they enter the more difficult portion of their schedule. Since Week 7, the Commanders have allowed 38.5 points per game and 451.3 yards per game. Quinn’s defenses as a head coach have never been the stellar units we’ve grown accustomed to seeing when he was a defensive coordinator, so this isn’t exactly new territory. We’ll see if this change leads to better results as the Commanders now prepare for a Week 11 game game in Spain against the Dolphins who are fresh off an upset win over the Bills.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dan-quinn/.headline: Commanders GM Adam Peters said the team is “far from [their] answer” when it comes to deciding what to do with the No. 2 pick.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dan-quinn/.analysis: The Commanders appear to be taking an open-minded approach with the No. 2 overall pick, which will presumably be used on a quarterback. In addition to saying they are willing to hear calls for offers to trade the No. 2 pick, head coach Dan Quinn has also said it’s “ fair to envision ” the team drafting a quarterback early in next month’s draft. Given the strength of this year’s class and the position that they’re in, it’s hard to imagine the Commanders not taking a shot on a franchise quarterback with a new regime in place and a need at the position.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dan-quinn/.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Commanders are hiring Cowboys DC Dan Quinn as their head coach.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dan-quinn/.analysis: Quinn brings six years of head coaching experience to Washington. The former Falcons head coach went 43-42 during his time with the team, making the playoffs in two of those seasons while also being on the receiving end of a loss to Tom Brady and the Patriots in Super Bowl LI in the infamous “28-3" game. The Commanders enter the 2024 offseason holding the most cap space of any team in the league and the No. 2 overall pick, which will presumably be used on a franchise quarterback. As a defensive coach, Quinn never quite put the pieces together on the defensive side of the ball in Atlanta, as the Falcons boasted only one top-10 defensive unit in his six seasons. He and newly-hired GM Adam Peters have the money and assets to get Washington’s rebuild off the ground, now the real work begins.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dan-quinn/.headline: Cowboys DC Dan Quinn conducted a second interview for the Commanders’ head-coaching vacancy Tuesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dan-quinn/.analysis: We already knew the sides were talking, but it’s taken on greater meaning with the surprise news that Lions OC Ben Johnson, for some reason, doesn’t want the job. Quinn could be a decent turnaround artist from the perspective that he’s a player’s coach who should handle his side of the ball. He would also seem extremely unlikely to be the man to complete the gut-job rebuild Washington is embarking on.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dan-quinn/.headline: Fox Sports’ Ralph Vacchiano reports the Commanders have second interviews with five different head coaching candidates over the next two days.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dan-quinn/.analysis: Detroit’s Ben Johnson remains the odds-on favorite to land Washington’s head coaching gig, but the team is also set to speak with Ravens assistant head coach Anthony Weaver and defensive coordinator Mike Macdonald, along with defensive coordinators Dan Quinn and Aaron Glenn. With so many interviews on tap, the Commanders’ search isn’t quite over yet, but we’d expect them to come to a decision sometime this week. In addition to the five coaches they have to meet, the Commanders have already conducted second interviews with Texans OC Bobby Slowik and in-house candidate Eric Bieniemy.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dan-quinn/.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Commanders will have a second in-person interview with Cowboys DC Dan Quinn early next week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dan-quinn/.analysis: Quinn had a second interview with the Seahawks on Thursday and is clearly a finalist to land either of the two gigs. Only three head coaching vacancies remain in the league, one of which is the Falcons — Quinn’s old stomping grounds. The Seahawks have long been considered the favorite to land Quinn, but the Commanders are clearly interested in his services. Washington currently holds the No. 2 pick in this year’s draft and has over $70 million in cap space. Coupled with those things is the fact that Washington is also under new ownership, making it an enticing destination for whoever receives an offer for the position.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dan-quinn/.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that the Seahawks are scheduled to have a second interview with Cowboys DC Dan Quinn on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/dan-quinn/.analysis: Quinn’s past connection to the Seahawks has made him a top candidate to fill the void left by Pete Carroll. Quinn served as the Seahawks assistant head coach and defensive line coach from 2009 to 2010 and returned in 2013 and 2014 as their defensive coordinator before taking the head coaching gig in Atlanta. Quinn is scheduled to meet with other teams in the coming days, but it wouldn’t be surprising to see an offer come from the Seahawks before he leaves the building.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that “no change is imminent” at head coach for the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.analysis: Saints owner Gayle Benson said earlier this week that the team’s 1-4 record is “not acceptable.” Rapoport noted that she came to practice in a “show of support” for Moore and company, though it felt equally like a show of force from the outside. Rapsheet also stressed several times that the team needs to start winning games. While a change at head coach might not happen next week, it does sound like Moore won’t survive the season if things don’t turn around soon.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.headline: Saints owner Gayle Benson said in a speech that the team’s 1-4 record “is not acceptable to me.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.analysis: It appears that Kellen Moore and GM Mickey Loomis are on the hot seat after a surprisingly bad start and a no-show on the 20th anniversary of the return to the dome. We’d be a little surprised if Moore were fired in only the second year of his tenure, without even being given a chance to pick his own franchise quarterback. But most ownership groups would not say something like this out loud, so it’s worth noting.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore plans to call plays for the offense this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.analysis: This was expected to be the case, but Moore confirmed it at his introductory press conference on Thursday. The first-time head coach made a name for himself as an offensive play-caller and is fresh off leading the Eagles’ offense to 33 points in the team’s Super Bowl win over the Chiefs. Moore and the Eagles leaned heavily into the ground game last season, but during his 2023 campaign with the Chargers and his four-year run with the Cowboys (2019-2022), his offenses were ranked in the top-15 in early-down pass rate. How Moore decides to run his offense with the Saints could depend on how their off-season goes. While Alvin Kamara isn’t getting any younger, it’s hard to imagine any coach trusting Derek Carr to lead a high-volume passing attack.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Eagles quarterbacks coach Doug Nussmeier is a “strong candidate to have a big role” on the New Orleans offensive staff under Kellen Moore.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.analysis: “Perhaps offensive coordinator,” Rapoport adds. Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni has made some noise about blocking assistants from leaving today but with an elevation, he’d have no way to block Nussmeier moving to the Saints. Nussmeier has been Moore’s quarterbacks coach with the Cowboys, Chargers, and Eagles. He has not been a candidate for any prominent external jobs that we’ve written about since interviewing for the Ravens offensive coordinator gig in 2023.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports 49ers assistant head coach Brandon Staley is a “leading candidate” to become Saints defensive coordinator.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.analysis: New Saints head coach Kellen Moore reportedly has strong interest in bringing in Staley as the team’s defensive coordinator. Staley flamed out as Chargers head coach after three seasons, going 24-24 and heading one of the NFL’s worst defenses. Staley spent the 2024 season as an assistant to Niners head coach Kyle Shanahan. As head of the Saints defense, Staley would take over a unit that last year ranked 19th in EPA allowed and 18th in offensive success rate allowed. The Saints pressured the passer at the 11th lowest rate in 2024.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.headline: Saints hired Eagles offensive coordinator Kellen Moore as the team’s head coach.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.analysis: Two days after Moore and the Eagles dominated the Chiefs in the Super Bowl, Moore, 36, gets his first crack at a head coaching gig. The Eagles reportedly expected Moore to be a short-term OC, especially if he had immediate success with Jalen Hurts and the Philly offense. He did just that in 2024: The Eagles were eighth in total yards and seventh in points, ranking sixth in EPA per play and first in rush EPA thanks to Saquon Barkley’s massive campaign. In New Orleans, Moore will have to figure out how to make it work with Derek Carr at the helm and an aging Alvin Kamara in the backfield. Moore’s ability to manipulate defenses and create space for his playmakers will be put to the test in 2025 and beyond.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.headline: The Athletic’s Mike Silver “expects” Kellen Moore to have “strong interest” in Brandon Staley as a defensive coordinator.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.analysis: The Moore-Saints partnership is not actually, as an NFL national reporter would say, “officially official” yet. But all signs have been pointing that way for some time. Staley took on assistant head coach duties for the 49ers last year after washing out of Los Angeles in 2023. Given how poorly San Francisco’s defense played last year, he wouldn’t exactly be an inspiring defensiv coordinator hire for Moore. But Staley had a good track record on that side of the ball prior to 2023 and a Kliff Kingsbury-esque bounceback could definitely happen.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.headline: Speaking Sunday, Eagles owner Jeffrey Lurie said “Unfortunately, we’re gonna have to wish (Kellen Moore) the very best with New Orleans.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.analysis: This comment came shortly after the team’s Super Bowl LIX victory over the Chiefs, when Lurie was asked if he expects the team to lose Moore to the Saints this week. Lurie simply responded with “I do” before proceeding to praise the coordinator who was fresh off leading the Eagles to their second championship in eight seasons. The ink has long felt dry on Moore’s contract with the Saints, even though nothing has been made official yet. We’d expect the official word to come down any day now, but Lurie’s recent comments are about as definite as it gets.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter confirms Eagles OC Kellen Moore is expected to be named the Saints’ next head coach following Super Bowl LIX.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.analysis: The NFL’s worst kept secret keeps inching closer to becoming official. Moore’s hiring would be the Saints’ first leap outside the Sean Payton coaching tree in two decades, and would follow on the heels of an excellent “bounce-back campaign” for Moore after a trying 2023 with the Chargers. A methodical coaching riser who has overseen strong offenses most everywhere he’s been, Moore would address the Saints’ desperate need for fresh ideas when it comes to scoring points.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.headline: NFL Network’s Tom Pelissero reports the Saints plan to meet with Eagles OC Kellen Moore for their head coaching vacancy after the Super Bowl.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/kellen-moo.analysis: Moore has already interviewed with the Saints twice. As Pelissero notes, a third meeting can’t happen until after the Super Bowl, hence the timing. The Super Bowl is also conveniently located in New Orleans, making an in-person visit a small ask for Moore. It’s been reported multiple times that Moore is the favorite to land the Saints opening. A third meeting all but confirms that. Dolphins DC Anthony Weaver and Giants OC Mike Kafka have both had multiple interviews with the Saints and are still in the mix.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler Jr. (ankle) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: JPJ was downgraded to a limited participant in Friday before being hit with the questionable tag, causing some concern about his Week 6 availability. It looks like the light practice session may have been a precaution. The newly-minted Cowboys should be good to go versus Green Bay.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) is questionable for Dallas’ Week 6 game against the Packers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Porter downgraded from full to limited on Friday and wound up with this status despite practicing all three days this week. Peculiar. Matthew Golden and Christian Watson would be better off on Sunday if Porter wasn’t able to go.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Cowboys declare CB Joey Porter, LB DeMarvion Overshown, CB Cobie Durant, OLB James Houston, OG Ajani Cornelius, OT Drew Shelton and WR Camden Brown inactive for Week 5 against the Buccaneers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Porter’s bumpy 2026 campaign takes another surprising turn. The Cowboys’ new cornerback was set to expand his involvement this evening, but he is evidently unable to play due to an illness. Fortunately for the Cowboys, the Buccaneers’ offense is hamstrung by Baker Mayfield’s (thumb) absence.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Joey Porter (back/conditioning/contract) is not on the injury report for Week 4 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones said on Friday, “we actually think Joey Porter will get snaps.” ESPN’s Todd Archer notes that prior to the mid-week trade, Porter was ruled out of Thursday’s game between the Steelers and Browns, saying his back was tight. He practiced the last two days “without issue.” Porter might be on a snap count this week, but it looks like he will play.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports there is “a chance” that Joey Porter Jr. (back/conditioning/contract) plays in Week 4 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Porter Jr. missed the first three games of the year with a back issue. The Steelers also listed conditioning under his name on the injury report and even took the back injury off entirely at one point. All of that is to say that his absences were ultimately contract-related, which everyone knew in the first place.
