He was ruled out for Thursday’s game by Pittsburgh, but is eligible to play for the Cowboys this week if they can get him up to speed on the playbook ahead of Sunday’s game. He will likely play on specific packages if he does suit up, but that would still be an upgrade for a banged-up Dallas secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports the Cowboys “will not be immediately extending Joey Porter Jr.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Schultz added that the plan is to have him play first and “the contract will take care of itself from there.” That’s not exactly what Porter Jr. was looking to get out of this move, but it also points to the fact that his relationship with the Steelers was simply fractured beyond repair. Pittsburgh’s somewhat archaic rules around contract negotiations drove a wedge between them and their star corner. They don’t extend players during the season and, with rare exceptions, they do not guarantee money beyond the first year of a new deal. If Porter Jr. suits up next week and puts a few good games on tape, we suspect the Cowboys will feel comfortable giving him the contract he wanted from the Steelers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Tom Pelissero of The Ringer reports that the Cowboys have acquired Joey Porter Jr. in a trade with the Steelers.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: In exchange for Porter, the Cowboys will send the Steelers a second-round selection in 2028 as well as a conditional sixth-round pick. Pelissero noted in his blog that trade talks between Dallas and Pittsburgh had picked up over the past few weeks, and the deal will soon become official. Porter has yet to play a snap in 2026 as he has dealt with a back injury, and also a contract dispute. The 26-year-old is one of the more talented corners in football, and Dallas has struggled considerably to stop the pass over the first three weeks. Assuming good health, Porter should be a vast improvement over what the Cowboys have gotten out of their corners to begin 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Jalen Ramsey (wrist) is questionable for Week 4 against the Browns.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Ramsey was listed as limited for all three practices this week. He is attempting to play through a broken wrist and will likely wear a cast or brace if he is active. As expected, Joey Porter Jr. remains out this week admist his contrat dispute with the team.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr. (NIR/conditioning) was a full participant in Tuesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Though Porter has been listed on the injury report with a back issue to start the season, he was listed for “conditioning” to open this week. It’s no secret Porter is in a contract dispute and the Steelers have been getting trade calls on the 26-year-old. However, he is practicing fully ahead of a Week 4 Thursday matchup against the Browns and could certainly play. When asked if Porter will play, head coach Mike McCarthy said, “We hope so.” With Jalen Ramsey dealing with a broken wrist, Porter’s help will be welcome in the secondary.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.headline: Joey Porter Jr. (back) will not play in Week 3 against the Bengals.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joey-porte.analysis: Who could have seen this coming? Porter has yet to suit up for a game this season, and it’s due to either a back issue, his current contract situation, or a mixture of the two. Teams have inquired about his availability via trade, but no deal appears on the horizon for the 26-year-old corner. In addition to Porter, the Steelers also declared RB Rico Dowdle, QB Drew Allar, QB Willi Howard, RB Eli Heidenreich, DE Kevin Jobity Jr., and DE Gabe Rubio inactive for Week 3.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Tyler Shough has two broken bones in his non-throwing hand.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Both Shough and Kellen Moore have given non-answers when asked about the quarterback’s left hand. Per Schefter, the injury could take a couple of months to heal, but it will not cost him any playing time. Shough injured his hand versus the Falcons in Week 4 and wore a protective glove in Week 5. He is coming off his two worst games of the year, though we don’t suspect the hand is to blame. Things get much easier this week with the Giants on tap. Shough will get another shot at a QB1 finish in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Saints coach Kellen Moore, asked directly if Tyler Shough’s non-throwing hand is broken, said “it got banged two weeks ago and he’s just wearing some protective layers there.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: So, probably, then. The hand hasn’t really been a contributing factor to New Orleans’ decline so much as the Saints offensive line has just been in the blender for two weeks against Atlanta and Minnesota’s fronts, but it sure looks like Shough is managing through something and we should probably break ties against him in the rankings.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough completed 16-of-25 passes for 96 yards and two interceptions in the Saints’ 23-13, Week 5 loss to the Vikings.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Shough had been coasting on extreme play volume over the first month of the fantasy season. Brian Flores and the Vikings’ hyper-aggressive defense had no issues shutting down that approach. The Saints had five drives in the first half. Only one lasted longer than three plays. Of their four second-half drives, two ended with interceptions. A fumbled kickoff coming out of the break didn’t help the team’s play volume either. Shough has ultimately been a better fantasy quarterback than a real-life passer this year and the Vikings’ defense exposed that truth for the better part of four quarters. He will look to rebound against a far worse Giants unit in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough (hand) is not on New Orleans’ final Week 5 injury report.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: As expected, he’ll start and be on the QB1/QB2 borderline against an extremely pesky and attacking Vikings defense that has held down quarterback scoring quite well so far this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough (hand) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: As a right-handed quarterback, Shough should be fine despite his surprise appearance on the injury report. Even in a blowout loss on Monday, the second-year passer racked up 286 yards and a touchdown on 48 attempts. As long as the volume is there, Shough is good for low-end QB1 numbers. He will remain inside the top 12 at his position for Week 5 against Minnesota.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough completed 30-of-48 passes for 286 yards and one touchdown in the Saints’ 45-24, Week 4 loss to the Falcons, adding five yards on two carries.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Shough and the Saints stayed true to recent form as they quickly fell into a 14-point hole in the first quarter, with the team now averaging an almost eight point deficit at the half since head coach Kellen Moore took over to start the 2025 season. The team was unable to reproduce the second half magic they so frequently muster behind an overmatched offensive line. Shough needed a late touchdown toss to Devaughn Vele with less than two minutes to play to give fantasy managers something of value. Moore and Shough have their work cut out for them with Brian Flores’ relentless defense coming to town in Week 5, where Shough will be on the QB1/2 border in fantasy circles.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough completed 29-of-42 passes for 255 yards, four touchdowns and one interception in the Saints’ 27-35, Week 3 loss to the Raiders, adding one rush for 36 yards and two lost fumbles.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Shough funneled four touchdown passes to Saints TEs Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant, bringing the game’s total to six tight end touchdowns, which tied a league record. The Saints’ quarterback played well overall, though his interception was due to a poor throw. Both fumbles were caused by Raiders pass rushers, and Shough had a third fumble reversed by an illegal contact penalty on the Raiders. Regardless, he can be trusted to throw the ball voluminously while adding a little extra with his legs. He warrants low-end QB1 treatment against the Falcons next week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough completed 27-of-34 passes for 252 yards and one touchdown in the Saints’ 24-17, Week 2 win over the Ravens, adding nine carries for 23 yards and a touchdown.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Shough played mistake-free football all afternoon, chipping away at the Ravens’ defense before leading his team to 15 unanswered points in the fourth quarter to secure the win. Shough repeatedly connected with Chris Olave all afternoon, and he found the star receiver uncontested in the end zone for his lone touchdown. Shough punched in a one-yard score on a QB sneak with 1:21 left to put the Saints up 24-17 and complete the upset of the Ravens on the road. It wasn’t an overly flashy outing by Shough, but he was efficient against a stout Ravens defense, which still managed three sacks on the day. He’s now strung together two strong fantasy performances and will be on the radar as a high-end QB2 next week against the Raiders.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: Tyler Shough completed 35-of-56 passes for 410 yards, three touchdowns, and two interceptions in the Saints’ 30-31, Week 1 overtime loss to the Lions.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Shough was nearly seeing ghosts in the first half. The Saints had zero points and their longest drive resulted in 36 yards with a punt. Then, in the second half, Shough turned the ball over on each of his first two drives. The game looked truly over at this point, but Shough battled back and got points on the board on each of his next four drives. Detroit played passively on defense and Shough routinely punished them with long throws to Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele. Shough nearly won the game with a touchdown pass to Noah Fant in overtime. Kellen Moore went for two and Shough was unable to find his target in the back of the end zone. With the first-half rust hopefully shaken off, Shough will be a high-end QB2 versus the Ravens.

https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.headline: New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill believes Saints WR Jordyn Tyson’s route running strengths fit well with QB Tyler Shough’s passing preferences.
https://www.nbcsports.com/college-footba.analysis: Underhill compared Tyson’s best routes with Shough’s highest-targeted areas of the field and declared, “it’s the same diagram.” Coincidentally, Tyson’s route tree closely overlaps with that of No. 1 WR Chris Olave. Underhill believes that this dynamic will allow coach Kellen Moore to use Tyson and Olave interchangeably. They will both line up in the perimeter and in the slot. Underhill believes Olave will remain the team’s top pass catcher “for the near future,” but eventually both he and Tyson will work as two “top receivers.” Tyson missed most of spring practices with a hamstring injury, but Underhill said he will not worry about the issue unless Tyson misses training camp. Underhill closed the segment by saying a 55/700/5 receiving line on 90 targets is a “safe projection” for Tyson’s rookie season, though he believes Tyson is capable of doing more. The “safe” stat line equates to 155.0 PPR points and would have made him the WR40 last season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Joe Alt (neck) is expected to “ramp up” this week.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.analysis: Pre Rapoport, Alt received good news after seeing a specialist for his neck injury earlier this week. Alt missed last week’s game with the issue and has already been ruled out for Week 6, but this is still a positive turn of events, all things considered. With a Week 7 bye on deck, Alt could be back as soon as the following week when the Bolts take on the Rams.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.headline: Joe Alt (neck) will not play in Los Angeles’ Week 6 game against the Chiefs.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.analysis: Alt was off to see a specialist, per Jim Harbaugh, on Monday. He did not practice. At this point an IR stint seems more likely than not. The four rookie line should be intact for the Chargers this week with Kayode Awosika also ruled out.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.headline: Joe Alt (neck) did not practice on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.analysis: Chargers OG Kayode Awosika (fibula), S Derwin James (hamstring) and CB Donte Jackson (hamstring) also remained sidelined. The Chargers take on the division-rival Chiefs this weekend.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.headline: Joe Alt (neck) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.analysis: Alt missed Week 5 after not practicing last week and opens up Week 6 as a non-participant. Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Tuesday that Alt would visit a specialist for his neck injury. G Kayode Awosika (fibula) is also still sidelined. Justin Herbert’s offensive line looks like it will still be missing both players this week; the Chiefs’ defensive line will have a good day against the inexperienced depth that will start for the Chargers.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said OT Joe Alt (neck) will see a specialist.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.analysis: Last week’s offensive line in front of Justin Herbert featured four rookies and Cole Strange. It doesn’t look like it’s getting much better in Week 6.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Chargers OT Joe Alt (neck) is expected to miss Week 5 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.analysis: An already disappointing season continues to tumbler for the Chargers. LT Rashawn Slater (ankle) is already out this week and Alt will join him on the injury report. Neither starting tackle has been able to stay healthy over the course of their careers, making life difficult for QB Justin Herbert. Though Alt is expected to miss this week against the Broncos, Rapoport adds that there are “no plans” for him to go on injured reserve.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.headline: Joe Alt (neck) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.analysis: In true Chargers fashion, their once-promising offensive line has been scattered to the winds by injuries. Left tackle Rashawn Slater won’t play this week because of an ankle injury. Now their right tackle could also be put on ice. Already one of the most disappointing offenses of the year, there’s almost no hope for the Bolts to turn things around this week.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said RT Joe Alt (neck) is still being evaluated after Los Angeles’ Week 4 loss to the Seahawks.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.analysis: Alt suffered the injury in Week 4 when Nick Emmanwori slammed into him from behind while trying to down Justin Herbert. It sounds like there’s a real chance that he misses Week 5. Somehow, the 2025 Chargers offensive line has returned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said Joe Alt (ankle) and Rashawn Slater (knee) have been medically cleared for the start of training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.analysis: Harbaugh didn’t say exactly how much either player would participate in the opening practices of camp and even noted that the whole team is starting off in a “ramp-up” stage. Alt suffered two high-ankle sprains last year, the second one requiring season-ending surgery. Slater did not play at all in 2025 because of a ruptured patellar tendon. Though it would make sense for both players to be limited during the first few practices of training camp, it doesn’t sound like any player will have any lingering issues heading into 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.headline: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh said it, “It looks that way,” when asked if Joe Alt (ankle) and Rashawn Slater (knee) will be ready for training camp.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/joe-alt/14.analysis: Chargers GM Joe Hortiz said both players were ahead of schedule when asked about them a week before the NFL Draft. Slater suffered a season-ending ruptured a patellar tendon last August and did not play a snap in 2025. Alt was unable to recover from a high-ankle sprain during the season and finished the year on injured reserve. All signs point to the Chargers having their elite tackle duo healthy for the start of the year. With an improved offensive line and Mike McDaniel on the headset, this is truly a make-or-break year for Justin Herbert.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Abdul Carter (groin) is expected to play in Week 6 against the Saints.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: Carter got in one limited practice to close the week before being listed as questionable. That would normally make him a coin-flip at best to play today, head coach John Harbaugh was optimistic about Carter’s health early in the week. He is good to go, as is left tackle Andrew Thomas, who is dealing with a groin injury. He has played through the groin issue several times already and will do so again versus the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: Andrew Thomas (groin) was seen working off to the side on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: Thomas, the Giants’ left tackle, RT Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) and EDGE Abdul Carter (calf) were all seen without jerseys, working on the side field with the training staff today. Expect to see all three listed as non-participants. Thomas has played through a couple of injuries this season, and seemingly has a good chance of suiting up in Week 6 against the Saints.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: Abdul Carter (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: Giants coach John Harbaugh said Carter is doing well, so it doesn’t seem like he’s at much risk of missing Week 6. Rookie corner Colton Hood, on the other hand, is in concussion protocol and didn’t practice today. He will likely miss Week 6 while he works his way through the protocol.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: Giants HC John Harbaugh said Abdul Carter’s ankle injury doesn’t appear to be too serious.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: Speaking after Monday’s minicamp, Harbaugh said Carter suffered a twisted ankle but downplayed any notion that it would be a serious injury. The Giants and their fans can breathe an early sigh of relief after the former No. 3 overall pick was seen limping off the field early in the first day of the team’s three-day minicamp.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: Giants beat writer Pat Leonard reports Abdul Carter suffered an apparent foot injury at Monday’s minicamp and could be seen limping to the sideline.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: We’ll likely get an update on this soon, but it’s a concerning development for the second-year pass rusher who is hoping to build on a rookie season that included 43 tackles, four sacks, and seven TFLs. According to Leonard, Carter eventually made his way indoors and was seen leaving the field without his shoe. ESPN’s Jordan Raanan later reported that the “initial belief” is that Carter is okay, but we will provide an update when we receive one.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: Giants EDGE Abdul Carter (illness) is not on the injury report for Week 18 against the Cowboys.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: Carter returned to practice on Friday, logging a limited session. Giants DL Dexter Lawrence (illness) was also removed from the injury report, though he did not resume practicing. We tentatively expect both players to be on the field for Week 18, but projecting their snap counts is tough. The Giants and Cowboys have both been eliminated from playoff contention.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: Giants EDGE Abdul Carter (illness) was not seen practicing on Thursday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: Carter’s absence is unsurprising. The coaching staff reportedly sent him and others home yesterday. The Athletic’s Dan Duggan noted DL Dexter Lawrence was also absent on Thursday. He believes Lawrence is “also in the illness category.” Both players have a chance to face the Cowboys this week, though the team notably kept TE Theo Johnson (illness) sidelined in Week 17, and he has not yet resumed practicing.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: Giants EDGE Abdul Carter (illness) did not practice on Wednesday.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: Three Giants players “were sent home or not at practice as they deal with illnesses.” Carter is, unfortunately, among them. The Giants’ stud rookie has been playing very well as of late. An absence would make life far easier on the Cowboys this week. Stay tuned.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Giants EDGE Abdul Carter “vehemently denied Tuesday that he slept through a walk-through practice last week.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: The No. 3 overall pick was benched for a series on Sunday after reports surfaced that he slept through practice last week. Carter says the Giants changed their practice schedule and he was getting treatment while he was supposed to be at the walk-through. The young defender still owned up to his mistake but wanted to clear the air on exactly what happened. Between the Carter benching and a loss to the Packers in Week 11, it has been a rocky start for interim head coach Mike Kafka. Things won’t be getting any better in Week 12 when the Giants travel to Detroit to take on the Lions.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.headline: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Giants EDGE Abdul Carter (hamstring) is a game-time decision for Week 7 against the Broncos.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/abdul-cart.analysis: Carter was added to the injury report on Friday as a limited participant before being listed as questionable. That likely means he suffered the hamstring issue in practice. Per Rapoport, he will go through some work before inactives before the team makes a final decision on his status. The rookie has 24 pressures and .5 sacks this year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-william.headline: Jaguars declared WR CJ Williams, CB Montaric Brown, S Jalen Huskey, LS Ross Matiscik, DE Wesley Williams, and DT Albert Regis inactive for Week 6 against the Texans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-william.analysis: Jones was the only Jaguar with a questionable tag headed into this contest. Brown and Matiscik were ruled out earlier in the week and the rest are healthy scratches.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-william.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley believes WR Josh Cameron would be the fill-in starter if a Jaguars starting wide receiver misses time.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-william.analysis: This might not matter, but it is worth noting. The Florida Times-Union recently reported that Jaguars WR Jakobi Meyers ( thumb ) is sidelined, as is WR Brian Thomas (shoulder). Both picked up minor injuries recently, but according to Shipley, the team does not “seem overly concerned” about either issue. Cameron and fellow sixth-round rookie WR CJ Williams have had good training camps. Cameron is evidently the name to know for waiver wire purposes in-season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-william.headline: Sports Illustrated’s John Shipley reports that Jaguars WR CJ Williams “has already become a favorite target for most of the backup quarterbacks.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-william.analysis: Good for him. Do we expect Williams to contribute meaningfully in re-draft formats this year? No. But, the No. 203 overall pick in this year’s draft seemingly has strong odds of securing a spot on the final roster. Williams is a name to know for dynasty, and currently profiles as the Jaguars’ WR5 for 2026.

https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-william.headline: Jaguars selected Stanford WR CJ Williams with the No. 203 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/cj-william.analysis: Williams is listed at 6-foot-1, 205 pounds on Stanford’s website, but we don’t have an official measurement on him because he didn’t test at the Combine and didn’t seem to be on the draft industrial complex’s radar. He did measure in at 6'0/203 at Stanford’s Pro Day, where he somehow managed a 5.76 RAS. Not exactly emblematic of a future NFL wideout. Neither NFL.com’s Lance Zeirliein nor The Athletic’s Dane Brugler wrote him up, to say nothing of our own Eric Froton. Williams started his career at USC in 2022 before transferring to Wisconsin then ending up in Palo Alto. He did manage 59 receptions in 2025, leading the team and producing 749 yards and six scores. Maybe he’s good. We frankly couldn’t tell you. We are told he was an 81 OVR on EA Sports College Football 26. Jaguars GM James Gladstone is hoping he’s pulled a fast one on the league, but it’s just as likely he’s playing himself.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.headline: Texans declared TE Marlin Klein, S Jalen Pitre, RB David Montgomery, DE Sebastian Harsh, IOL Febechi Nwaiwu, OT Braden Smith, and OT Nate Thomas inactive for Week 6 against the Jaguars.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.analysis: Klein remains a healthy scratch. David Montgomery was ruled out on Friday after missing all three practices this week because of a groin injury. Woody Marks will handle the lion’s share of the backfield touches versus the Jags.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.headline: Texans declared TE Marlin Klein, CB Collin Wright, DE Chris Braswell, LB Aiden Fisher, OG Febechi Nwaiwu and OT Nate Thomas inactive for Houston’s Week 5 game against the Titans.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.analysis: The Texans had five questionable players, including three offensive linemen with illnesses. All three of those linemen will play, and Kayden McDonald and M.J. Stewart were activated off injured reserve to make their season debuts as well as the Texans try to avoid an 0-5 start.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.headline: The Houston Chronicle’s Jonathan M. Alexander reports that Texans TE Marlin Klein “will have some sort of role” this season.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.analysis: Alexander also lists Klein behind TE1 Dalton Schultz and apparent TE2 Foster Moreau, so this isn’t exactly a ringing endorsement. Klein has efficiently caught 4-of-5 targets for 62 yards thus far in the preseason, and OC Nick Caley unpromptedly complimented Klein’s run blocking. The latter aspect is likely Klein’s ticket to game-day snaps this season. Schultz is a trusted veteran. Klein will likely be a non-factor in fantasy this year, but perhaps he can gain some ground in-season and force the Texans to get him involved late in the year.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.headline: The Houston Chronicle’s Jonathan M. Alexander believes the Texans “will likely utilize a lot more 12 personnel packages in 2026 than they did last season.”
https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.analysis: Injuries thinned the Texans’ tight end depth last season. This offseason, the front office signed TE Foster Moreau and drafted TE Marlin Klein, who is currently sidelined by a hamstring injury. Starting TE Dalton Schultz should continue to play a lot of snaps, though he is likely just a high-end TE2. Increasing 12 personnel sets decreases the number of snaps available to the wide receiver position, which could be a problem if the coaching staff decides to employ a rotation at the WR2 spot.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.headline: Texans TE Marlin Klein was sidelined this week after injuring his hamstring at organized team activities.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.analysis: Klein’s hamstring injury is not expected to be a long-term issue. The athletic second-round rookie caught 37 passes for 351 yards and one touchdown over his final two college seasons. The Texans have a decent group of backup tight ends, though many of the veterans have fairly extensive injury histories. Klein may have a chance to earn the TE2 role this season.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.headline: Texans signed No. 59 overall pick TE Marlin Klein to a four-year, $8.184 million contract.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.analysis: An elite athlete at the position, Klein didn’t begin playing football until high school, but totaled 37 passes for 371 yards and one touchdown in his last two seasons at Michigan. While he should still see plenty of playing time in his rookie season, we wouldn’t expect him to contribute much from a fantasy perspective with Dalton Schultz still with the team. Klein is an interesting stash in dynasty leagues but he can be left on the waiver wire in redraft leagues for the time being.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.headline: Texans selected Michigan TE Marlin Klein with the No. 59 overall pick in the 2026 NFL Draft.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.analysis: Klein began playing football in Germany before moving to the United States in high school. Because he was late to football, his numbers at Michigan aren’t much to write home about. Over Klein’s last two seasons, he caught 37 passes for 351 yards and one touchdown. He stands 6’6/248 and ran a 4.61-second 40 at the NFL Scouting Combine. Add in strong burst numbers and he left Indy with a 9.05 RAS. Klein is also a strong blocker despite his lack of reps. His receiving game needs work, but the athletic profile gives him a considerable ceiling. He will get to learn behind Dalton Schultz for a year before potentially taking over in 2027, when Schultz becomes a free agent.

https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.headline: Michigan received a verbal commitment from three-star 2022 TE Marlin Klein.
https://www.nbcsports.com/marlin-klein/0.analysis: Klein (6'6/215) became Michigan’s third verbal commitment in the Class of 2022 Tuesday morning, joining DT Alex VanSumeren and LB Tyler Martin. While he’s been used at both wide receiver and tight end at the high school level, Klein has been projected as a tight end once he arrives on campus. Currently attending Rabun Gap-Nacoochee School in Rabun Gap, Georgia, the three-star recruit is actually a native of Germany. Klein’s recruitment picked up during the summer as Power 5 programs such as Boston College, Florida State, Georgia, Louisville and Virginia Tech all tendered offers.
